2681	
2682	Custom working-indicator frames are rendered verbatim. If you want colors, add them to the frame strings yourself, for example with `ctx.ui.theme.fg(...)`.
2683	
2684	### Autocomplete Providers
2685	
2686	Use `ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider()` to stack custom autocomplete logic on top of the built-in slash-command and path provider. Set `triggerCharacters` for custom natural triggers such as `$`.
2687	
2688	Typical pattern:
2689	
2690	- inspect the text before the cursor
2691	- return your own suggestions when your extension-specific syntax matches
2692	- otherwise delegate to `current.getSuggestions(...)`
2693	- delegate `applyCompletion(...)` unless you need custom insertion behavior
2694	
2695	```typescript
2696	pi.on("session_start", (_event, ctx) => {
2697	  ctx.ui.addAutocompleteProvider((current) => ({
2698	    triggerCharacters: ["#"],
2699	    async getSuggestions(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, options) {
2700	      const line = lines[cursorLine] ?? "";
2701	      const beforeCursor = line.slice(0, cursorCol);
2702	      const match = beforeCursor.match(/(?:^|[ \t])#([^\s#]*)$/);
2703	      if (!match) {
2704	        return current.getSuggestions(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, options);
2705	      }
2706	
2707	      return {
2708	        prefix: `#${match[1] ?? ""}`,
2709	        items: [
2710	          { value: "#2983", label: "#2983", description: "Extension API for registering custom @ autocomplete providers" },
2711	          { value: "#2753", label: "#2753", description: "Reload stale resource settings" },
2712	        ],
2713	      };
2714	    },
2715	
2716	    applyCompletion(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, item, prefix) {
2717	      return current.applyCompletion(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol, item, prefix);
2718	    },
2719	
2720	    shouldTriggerFileCompletion(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol) {
2721	      return current.shouldTriggerFileCompletion?.(lines, cursorLine, cursorCol) ?? true;
2722	    },
2723	  }));
2724	});
2725	```
2726	
2727	See [github-issue-autocomplete.ts](../examples/extensions/github-issue-autocomplete.ts) for a complete example that preloads the latest open GitHub issues with `gh issue list` and filters them locally for fast `#...` completion. It requires GitHub CLI (`gh`) and a GitHub repository checkout.
2728	
2729	### Custom Components
2730	
2731	For complex UI, use `ctx.ui.custom()`. This temporarily replaces the editor with your component until `done()` is called:
2732	
2733	```typescript
2734	import { Text, Component } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
2735	
2736	const result = await ctx.ui.custom<boolean>((tui, theme, keybindings, done) => {
2737	  const text = new Text("Press Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel", 1, 1);
2738	
2739	  text.onKey = (key) => {
2740	    if (key === "return") done(true);
2741	    if (key === "escape") done(false);
2742	    return true;
2743	  };
2744	
2745	  return text;
2746	});
2747	
2748	if (result) {
2749	  // User pressed Enter
2750	}
2751	```
2752	
2753	The callback receives:
2754	- `tui` - TUI instance (for screen dimensions, focus management)
2755	- `theme` - Current theme for styling
2756	- `keybindings` - App keybinding manager (for checking shortcuts)
2757	- `done(value)` - Call to close component and return value
2758	
2759	See [tui.md](tui.md) for the full component API.
2760	
2761	#### Overlay Mode (Experimental)
2762	
2763	Pass `{ overlay: true }` to render the component as a floating modal on top of existing content, without clearing the screen:
2764	
2765	```typescript
2766	const result = await ctx.ui.custom<string | null>(
2767	  (tui, theme, keybindings, done) => new MyOverlayComponent({ onClose: done }),
2768	  { overlay: true }
2769	);
2770	```
2771	
2772	For advanced positioning (anchors, margins, percentages, responsive visibility), pass `overlayOptions`. Use `onHandle` to control focus or visibility programmatically:
2773	
2774	```typescript
2775	const result = await ctx.ui.custom<string | null>(
2776	  (tui, theme, keybindings, done) => new MyOverlayComponent({ onClose: done }),
2777	  {
2778	    overlay: true,
2779	    overlayOptions: { anchor: "top-right", width: "50%", margin: 2 },
2780	    onHandle: (handle) => {
2781	      handle.focus(); // focus this overlay and bring it to the visual front
2782	      // handle.unfocus({ target: editorComponent }); // release input to a specific component
2783	      // handle.setHidden(true/false); // toggle visibility
2784	      // handle.hide(); // permanently remove
2785	    }
2786	  }
2787	);
2788	```
2789	
2790	A focused visible overlay can reclaim input after temporary non-overlay custom UI closes. If you intentionally want another component to keep input while the overlay stays visible, call `handle.unfocus({ target })`. Passing `{ target: null }` releases the overlay without focusing another component.
2791	
2792	See [tui.md](tui.md) for the full `OverlayOptions` and `OverlayHandle` API and [overlay-qa-tests.ts](../examples/extensions/overlay-qa-tests.ts) for examples.
2793	
2794	### Custom Editor
2795	
2796	Replace the main input editor with a custom implementation (vim mode, emacs mode, etc.):
2797	
2798	```typescript
2799	import { CustomEditor, type ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
2800	import { matchesKey } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
2801	
2802	class VimEditor extends CustomEditor {
2803	  private mode: "normal" | "insert" = "insert";
2804	
2805	  handleInput(data: string): void {
2806	    if (matchesKey(data, "escape") && this.mode === "insert") {
2807	      this.mode = "normal";
2808	      return;
2809	    }
2810	    if (this.mode === "normal" && data === "i") {
2811	      this.mode = "insert";
2812	      return;
2813	    }
2814	    super.handleInput(data);  // App keybindings + text editing
2815	  }
2816	}
2817	
2818	export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) {
2819	  pi.on("session_start", (_event, ctx) => {
2820	    ctx.ui.setEditorComponent((tui, theme, keybindings) =>
2821	      new VimEditor(tui, theme, keybindings)
2822	    );
2823	  });
2824	}
2825	```
2826	
2827	**Key points:**
2828	- Extend `CustomEditor` (not base `Editor`) to get app keybindings (escape to abort, ctrl+d, model switching)
2829	- Call `super.handleInput(data)` for keys you don't handle
2830	- Factory receives `tui`, `theme`, and `keybindings` from the app
2831	- Use `ctx.ui.getEditorComponent()` before `setEditorComponent()` to wrap the previously configured custom editor
2832	- Pass `undefined` to restore default: `ctx.ui.setEditorComponent(undefined)`
2833	
2834	To compose with another extension that already replaced the editor, capture the previous factory before setting yours:
2835	
2836	```typescript
2837	const previous = ctx.ui.getEditorComponent();
2838	ctx.ui.setEditorComponent((tui, theme, keybindings) =>
2839	  new MyEditor(tui, theme, keybindings, { base: previous?.(tui, theme, keybindings) })
2840	);
2841	```
2842	
2843	See [tui.md](tui.md) Pattern 7 for a complete example with mode indicator.
2844	
2845	### Message and Entry Rendering
2846	
2847	Register a custom renderer for messages with your `customType`. Use message renderers for content that should participate in LLM context:
2848	
2849	```typescript
2850	import { Text } from "@earendil-works/pi-tui";
2851	
2852	pi.registerMessageRenderer("my-extension", (message, options, theme) => {
2853	  const { expanded, outputPad } = options;
2854	  let text = theme.fg("accent", `[${message.customType}] `);
2855	  text += message.content;
2856	
2857	  if (expanded && message.details) {
2858	    text += "\n" + theme.fg("dim", JSON.stringify(message.details, null, 2));
2859	  }
2860	
2861	  return new Text(text, outputPad, 0);
2862	});
2863	```
2864	
2865	Messages are sent via `pi.sendMessage()`:
2866	
2867	```typescript
2868	pi.sendMessage({
2869	  customType: "my-extension",  // Matches registerMessageRenderer
2870	  content: "Status update",
2871	  display: true,               // Show in TUI
2872	  details: { ... },            // Available in renderer
2873	});
2874	```
2875	
2876	For TUI-only content that should not be sent to the LLM, render custom entries instead:
2877	
2878	```typescript
2879	pi.registerEntryRenderer("my-card", (entry, options, theme) => {
2880	  return new Text(theme.fg("accent", JSON.stringify(entry.data)));
2881	});
2882	
2883	pi.appendEntry("my-card", { status: "done" });
2884	```
2885	
2886	### Theme Colors
2887	
2888	All render functions receive a `theme` object. See [themes.md](themes.md) for creating custom themes and the full color palette.
2889	
2890	```typescript
2891	// Foreground colors
2892	theme.fg("toolTitle", text)   // Tool names
2893	theme.fg("accent", text)      // Highlights
2894	theme.fg("success", text)     // Success (green)
2895	theme.fg("error", text)       // Errors (red)
2896	theme.fg("warning", text)     // Warnings (yellow)
2897	theme.fg("muted", text)       // Secondary text
2898	theme.fg("dim", text)         // Tertiary text
2899	
2900	// Text styles
2901	theme.bold(text)
2902	theme.italic(text)
2903	theme.strikethrough(text)
2904	```
2905	
2906	For syntax highlighting in custom tool renderers:
2907	
2908	```typescript
2909	import { highlightCode, getLanguageFromPath } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
2910	
2911	// Highlight code with explicit language
2912	const highlighted = highlightCode("const x = 1;", "typescript", theme);
2913	
2914	// Auto-detect language from file path
2915	const lang = getLanguageFromPath("/path/to/file.rs");  // "rust"
2916	const highlighted = highlightCode(code, lang, theme);
2917	```
2918	
2919	## Error Handling
2920	
2921	- Extension errors are logged, agent continues
2922	- `tool_call` errors block the tool (fail-safe)
2923	- Tool `execute` errors must be signaled by throwing; the thrown error is caught, reported to the LLM with `isError: true`, and execution continues
2924	
2925	## Mode Behavior
2926	
2927	| Mode | `ctx.mode` | `ctx.hasUI` | Notes |
2928	|------|------------|-------------|-------|
2929	| Interactive | `"tui"` | `true` | Full TUI with terminal rendering |
2930	| RPC (`--mode rpc`) | `"rpc"` | `true` | Dialogs and notifications via JSON protocol; `custom()` returns `undefined`. See [rpc.md](rpc.md) |
2931	| JSON (`--mode json`) | `"json"` | `false` | Event stream to stdout; UI methods are no-ops |
2932	| Print (`-p`) | `"print"` | `false` | Extensions run but can't prompt |
2933	
2934	Use `ctx.mode === "tui"` before TUI-specific features (`custom()`, component factories, terminal input). Use `ctx.hasUI` before dialog and notification methods that work in both TUI and RPC modes.
2935

17	### Lifecycle & Safety
18	
19	| Extension | Description |
20	|-----------|-------------|

183	## Key Patterns
184	
185	**Use StringEnum for string parameters** (required for Google API compatibility):
186	```typescript
187	import { StringEnum } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
188	
189	// Good
190	action: StringEnum(["list", "add"] as const)
191	
192	// Bad - doesn't work with Google
193	action: Type.Union([Type.Literal("list"), Type.Literal("add")])
194	```
195	
196	**State persistence via details:**
197	```typescript
198	// Store state in tool result details for proper forking support
199	return {
200	  content: [{ type: "text", text: "Done" }],
201	  details: { todos: [...todos], nextId },  // Persisted in session
202	};
203	
204	// Reconstruct on session events
205	pi.on("session_start", async (_event, ctx) => {
206	  for (const entry of ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()) {
207	    if (entry.type === "message" && entry.message.toolName === "my_tool") {
208	      const details = entry.message.details;
209	      // Reconstruct state from details
210	    }
211	  }
212	});

```text
## Scope

This analysis covers only `packages/server/src/server.ts` in `PiServer`. Behavior inside `ByteConnection`, `LiveSessionManager`, `ServerSnapshotPublisher`, listeners, and the protocol decoder is not visible.

## Ownership and state

### Server-owned global state

`PiServer` owns:

- `id`, generated with `randomUUID()` unless `options.serverId` is supplied.
- The listener collection in `listeners`.
- Frame and handshake limits: `maxFrameLength` and `handshakeTimeoutMs`.
- The active connection registry: `connections: Set<ConnectionState>`.
- The `LiveSessionManager` and `ServerSnapshotPublisher`.
- Lifecycle flags and promises: `closing`, `started`, `startPromise`, and `closePromise`.
- Optional error observation through `onError`.

`ServerSnapshotPublisher` receives the same `connections` set by reference, plus callbacks for `sendMessage`, `reportError`, and session metadata. It therefore observes server-wide connection and session state rather than maintaining an independent connection registry.

### Per-connection state

`accept()` creates one `ConnectionState` containing:

- A random connection `id`.
- The underlying `ByteConnection`.
- A `ClientMessageDecoder` configured with `maxFrameLength`.
- `sessionIds: Set`, initialized empty.
- `stage`, initially `awaitingHello`.
- `disconnected` and `handshakeComplete` flags.
- The handshake timer and, later, `handshake`.

`PiServer` does not directly read or modify `sessionIds` after initialization. Session association, ownership checks, and command semantics are delegated to `LiveSessionManager` through `executeCommand()` and `disconnect()`.

## Connection state machine

The visible stages are:

- `awaitingHello`
- `handshaking`
- `ready`
- `closing`
- `closed`

Transitions:

1. `accept()` creates an `awaitingHello` connection and adds it to `connections`.
2. `dispatchMessage()` requires the first decoded message to have type `hello`.
3. A valid first `hello` changes the stage to `handshaking` and starts `finishHandshake()`.
4. A successful handshake changes the stage to `ready`, sets `handshakeComplete`, and clears the timer.
5. Protocol failure or server shutdown changes the stage to `closing`.
6. `disconnect()` marks the connection `disconnected`, changes the stage to `closed`, removes it from `connections`, and invokes session cleanup.

A connection that arrives after `closing` has begun is closed immediately and receives a no-op handler; it is not registered.

The first-message rule is enforced by `dispatchMessage()`. A later `hello` is rejected regardless of whether the connection is still handshaking or already ready. Non-hello messages received during handshaking are deferred until `state.handshake` completes.

## Handshake behavior

`accept()` starts an unref’d timer. If it expires before completion, it invokes `failProtocol()` with an `invalid_request` error.

`finishHandshake()`:

1. Validates the protocol version with `isSupportedProtocolVersion()`.
2. Retrieves a snapshot through `snapshots.get()`.
3. Aborts if the server, connection, stage, or underlying transport is no longer usable.
4. Sends a `ServerHello` containing:
   - `PROTOCOL_VERSION`
   - The connection identifier
   - The snapshot
5. Marks the connection ready only if sending succeeded and the state is still handshaking.
6. If the snapshot revision changed during the handshake, retrieves the current snapshot and sends a `server_snapshot` event.

The version check is the only visible protocol-negotiation check. There is no visible authentication, authorization, capability negotiation, or client identity validation.

The deferred-message mechanism preserves handshake-before-request ordering, but there is no visible bound on how many decoded messages can accumulate while handshaking.

## Request concurrency and serialization

`receive()` decodes a chunk and iterates through all resulting messages. `dispatchMessage()` does not await request handling.

Once a connection is ready, each request invokes:

```text
void this.handleRequest(state, message)
```

Consequences:

- `PiServer` itself does not serialize requests per connection.
- Multiple `LiveSessionManager.executeCommand()` calls may run concurrently.
- Responses can complete and be sent out of request order.
- No per-connection request queue, mutex, or in-flight request limit is shown.
- `sendMessage()` has no visible per-connection write lock. Concurrent requests can therefore invoke `ByteConnection.send()` concurrently unless that lower layer provides serialization.
- A disconnect can occur while a command is running. Its eventual response is suppressed by `sendMessage()` if the connection has become disconnected or closed.

Whether session operations are serialized internally is unknown because `LiveSessionManager` is not included.

## Attach, detach, and session ownership

The listener’s `start()` callback supplies a `ByteConnection` to `PiServer.accept()`.

Attachment consists of:

- Creating `ConnectionState`.
- Installing `onData`, `onClose`, and `onError` callbacks.
- Adding the state to `connections`.

Detachment occurs in `disconnect()`:

- `disconnected` is set synchronously before awaiting anything.
- The stage becomes `closed`.
- The handshake timer is cleared.
- The state is removed from `connections`.
- `sessions.disconnect(connection)` is awaited.
- A snapshot broadcast is initiated if the connection completed its handshake and the server is not closing.

The synchronous `disconnected` check makes repeated `disconnect()` calls effectively idempotent. However, the underlying `ByteConnection.close()` operation has no equivalent visible deduplication or lock.

`sessionIds` strongly indicates per-connection session association, but this file does not prove how those IDs are populated, validated, or protected against cross-connection access. Those responsibilities belong to `LiveSessionManager` or the service.

## Events and snapshots

Visible server-to-client messages are:

- `hello`
- `hello_error`
- `response`
- `event` carrying `server_snapshot`

Snapshot publication occurs through:

- The `broadcastServerSnapshot` callback supplied to `LiveSessionManager`.
- `disconnect()` after a handshaken connection leaves.
- The revision check in `finishHandshake()`.

There is no general event subscription mechanism in this file. The snapshot publisher decides which registered connections receive broadcasts.

## Disconnect and cleanup paths

### Normal transport closure

`transportClosed()`:

- Calls `decoder.end()` unless the connection is already disconnected or closing.
- Reports decoder-finalization errors.
- Starts `disconnect()`.

It does not explicitly call the underlying transport’s close method because the transport has already reported closure.

### Transport error

The connection’s `onError` callback:

1. Reports the error.
2. Calls `closeConnection()`.
3. Calls `disconnect()` after the close promise resolves.

`closeConnection()` catches close failures and reports them, so transport-close errors do not prevent session cleanup.

### Protocol failure

`failProtocol()`:

- Ignores already closing, closed, or disconnected connections.
- Changes the stage to `closing`.
- Clears the handshake timer.
- Encodes a `hello_error` frame.
- Passes that frame as the final chunk to `ByteConnection.close()`.
- Disconnects afterward.

If encoding the error frame fails, the error is reported and the connection is closed without a final protocol frame. The same `hello_error` shape is used for decoder and protocol failures even after a connection may have reached `ready`.

### Server shutdown

`closeServerState()`:

1. Copies the current `connections` set.
2. Marks every copied connection `closing`.
3. Clears all handshake timers.
4. Closes every underlying connection.
5. Disconnects every connection.
6. Awaits `sessions.close()`.
7. Clears `connections`.

The server prevents new accepted connections by setting `closing` before shutdown work begins.

## Start and stop lifecycle

### Starting

`start()` rejects when:

- `started` is already true.
- `startPromise` already exists.
- `closing` is true.

`startInternal()` starts listeners sequentially. Only successfully completed listener starts are added to its local `started` list. After all listeners succeed, it sets `started = true`.

On startup failure:

- `closing` becomes true.
- Successfully started listeners are closed with `Promise.allSettled()`.
- `closeServerState()` runs.
- The original startup error is rethrown.
- Restart is impossible because `closing` remains true.

A listener that partially opens resources and then rejects from `start()` is not added to `started`, so this method does not guarantee cleanup for that partial-start case.

### Closing

`close()` is idempotent through `closePromise`. It sets `closing = true` immediately, preventing new connections and new starts.

`closeInternal()`:

- Waits for an in-progress `startPromise`, ignoring its rejection.
- Calls `close()` on every configured listener, not only listeners known to have started.
- Always invokes `closeServerState()` afterward.
- Sets `started = false` in its `finally` block.

If listener closure rejects, server-state cleanup still runs, but the close promise rejects. The same rejected promise is returned by later `close()` calls.

Calling `close()` before `start()` is allowed by this code and still invokes every listener’s `close()` method. Once closing begins, the instance cannot be started again.

## Error handling

`toProtocolError()` maps errors as follows:

- `InternalServerError`: reports its `cause` and exposes the fixed internal-error message.
- `PiServerError`: preserves its code and message, except `not_implemented`, which uses the fixed not-implemented message. Optional `details` are exposed.
- `ProtocolValidationError`: becomes `invalid_request`.
- Any other error: is reported and becomes a generic internal error.

`handleRequest()` converts command failures into unsuccessful `ResponseEnvelope` messages rather than closing the connection.

Errors from decoding, handshake processing, encoding, transport sending, closing, and internal conversion can reach `reportError()`. The configured `onError` callback is protected: exceptions thrown by the observer are swallowed.

Listener-close failures during the startup-failure `allSettled()` cleanup are not individually passed to `reportError()` by this file.

## Security and operational assumptions

The implementation visibly assumes that lower layers provide or enforce:

- Transport security such as TLS.
- Authentication and authorization.
- Correct listener admission policy.
- Safe session ownership and cross-connection access checks.
- Any required serialization of writes or session commands.

Protections present here include protocol framing limits, handshake deadlines, first-message validation, protocol-version checking, generic handling of unexpected errors, and cleanup on transport loss.

Not visible are:

- Connection-count limits.
- Request-count or concurrency limits.
- Handshake message-queue limits.
- Rate limiting.
- Authentication or authorization.
- Idle timeouts after handshake.
- Replay protection.
- Encryption.
- Backpressure management.
- Validation that externally supplied `serverId` is unique or suitably formatted.

`maxFrameLength` limits individual encoded or decoded frames, but no cumulative memory or workload limit is shown. Random UUIDs provide identifiers only; the code does not treat them as credentials. Snapshot contents and `PiServerError.details` may be exposed to clients according to the behavior of the service and session manager.
```

Based only on this file, the implementation defines an abstraction, not a complete protocol.

- **Connection premise:** The interface describes an already established, authorized, ordered byte stream. This is a stated assumption, not authentication or authorization logic.
- **Hello/authentication:** There is no hello message, credential validation, challenge, timeout handling, or authentication policy here. The state model implies an intended hello/handshake flow, but its rules are absent.
- **Ordering and concurrency:** `send` is asynchronous, but the file does not specify whether sends are serialized, whether inbound requests may run concurrently, or how responses are correlated or ordered.
- **Backpressure and limits:** A promise returned by `send` suggests completion can be awaited, but it does not define buffering, flow control, cancellation, write failure behavior, maximum frame size, maximum chunk size, or memory limits.
- **Framing and decoding:** Incoming data arrives as arbitrary byte chunks through `onData`. A client-message decoder is stored in the state, but framing, fragmentation, malformed-input handling, and decoder invocation are unspecified.
- **Session attachment:** The state stores a set of session identifiers. No attachment, detachment, ownership, authorization, duplicate handling, or cleanup policy is implemented here.
- **Cleanup and disconnect:** The state tracks disconnection and several lifecycle phases. The terminal predicate treats an explicitly disconnected connection or either shutdown phase as terminal. It does not itself close transports, clear sessions, resolve handshakes, or remove registry entries.
- **Errors and events:** Handlers receive data, closure, and an `Error`. The file does not define event ordering, whether errors imply closure, whether callbacks may throw, or whether duplicate close/error notifications are allowed.
- **Lifecycle details:** A handshake promise and required timeout are present, indicating expected handshake coordination and expiry. No transitions, timeout duration, cancellation, retry, or final-message behavior are defined.
- **Acceptor ownership:** The acceptor receives a byte connection and returns its handler; ownership responsibilities and invocation timing are unspecified.

Thus, the file establishes type-level state and callback shapes while leaving nearly all operational policy to the surrounding server implementation.

```text
## Coordinator model

- Two maps track state:
  - A live-session map holds each runtime, attached connections, subscription cleanup, operation count, readiness, terminal status, and disposal promise.
  - An opening map deduplicates simultaneous attempts to load the same session.
- A newly created session receives a server-generated UUID. Opening an existing session delegates to the service.
- Creation obtains a runtime, checks that its snapshot ID matches the requested ID, subscribes to runtime events, and only then publishes the live entry.
- If shutdown begins during acquisition, the runtime is disposed and acquisition fails.

## Attachment and locking

- A connection records attached session IDs, while each live session maintains the reverse connection set.
- Attach and detach are set operations, so repeating either action is effectively idempotent.
- Attaching broadcasts a current snapshot and updates the server-wide session view.
- Every live snapshot reports the runtime’s current phase, whether any client is attached, and a locked state.
- The locked field is informational in this coordinator; it does not serialize clients or commands.
- A terminal runtime rejects later acquisition. A runtime already disposing is awaited, then acquisition retries.
- There is no explicit ownership or single-client lock.

## Commands and concurrency

- Listing delegates to persistent service storage, then overlays live snapshots onto stored metadata and appends live sessions absent from storage.
- Create and attach return snapshots; prompt, steering, abort, and model/thinking changes require the caller to be attached.
- Detach only removes the relationship; it does not delete persistent data.
- Operations increment a counter, await the runtime call, return a refreshed snapshot, then decrement the counter.
- Concurrent commands are not queued by this file. They may run simultaneously, with the runtime responsible for handling such concurrency.
- An abort is simply delegated to the runtime; it does not itself remove the session or connection.

## Snapshots and events

- Runtime snapshots are the authoritative current state; the coordinator validates that the runtime ID never changes.
- Runtime phase and attachment information are added by the coordinator.
- Non-progress runtime events trigger snapshot broadcasts to all attached clients.
- Progress events are forwarded separately to attached clients.
- There is no revision number, sequence counter, replay buffer, or explicit event-ordering mechanism.
- Message sends are launched without awaiting them, so delivery completion and send failures are not coordinated here.

## Errors and termination

- A runtime error marks the session terminal, reports the error, unsubscribes from events, closes each attached transport, and disconnects those clients.
- Terminal sessions may be disposed even if their runtime phase is not idle.
- Acquisition, snapshot ID mismatches, unattached commands, closed connections, and non-live sessions produce protocol errors.
- Disposal failures are generally surfaced through the manager’s error reporter, though shutdown’s aggregate disposal path can itself reject.
- A runtime can become terminal between acquisition and attachment; the attachment check does not revalidate the live session’s terminal or disposing flags.

## Removal and cleanup

- Disposal occurs only when there are no connections, no active operations, and the runtime is idle, unless the session is terminal.
- Detach, operation completion, and runtime events all trigger cleanup checks.
- Disposal unsubscribes, disposes the runtime, removes the live-map entry, and refreshes the server-wide session list.
- The service’s persistent store is never explicitly deleted by this file; removal means removal from the in-memory registry after runtime disposal.
- Shutdown waits for pending openings, clears the live map, unsubscribes normal sessions, and disposes all runtimes.
- Shutdown suppresses ordinary automatic disposal until its own cleanup path runs.

## Main limitations

- No command serialization, revision tracking, replay, persistence writes, deletion API, or guaranteed message ordering is implemented here.
- Snapshot broadcasts can overlap, and stale snapshots could theoretically arrive after newer ones.
- Attachment and termination have small race windows because state checks and mutations are not transactionally synchronized.
```

### Bridge-relevant behavior

- **Authentication:** Not defined.
- **Transport:** Not defined. The frame-length and handshake settings imply protocol concerns, but no transport implementation or message format is supplied.
- **Sessions and persistence:** The service manages durable sessions. Creation receives an ID generated by the server, and the backing service is responsible for preserving it.
- **Commands:** A runtime accepts prompts, steering input, cancellation, model changes, and reasoning-level changes. Prompt and steering inputs derive from protocol commands while omitting command and session identifiers.
- **Events:** Clients can subscribe to snapshot, progress, and error notifications. Subscription returns an unsubscribe function.
- **Locking/concurrency:** A runtime represents exclusive acquisition. Conflicting operations are expected to fail instead of being queued. The types do not specify lock duration, fairness, or synchronization details.
- **Lifecycle:** The service creates or opens runtimes; each runtime can be observed and must eventually be disposed. Error reporting is available through the server-level callback and runtime error events.
- **Aliases:** `SessionRuntime` and `SessionRuntimeEvent` are compatibility aliases for the corresponding runtime types.

```text
## Security and permissions

- Default socket mode is `0600`, and newly created parent directories request `0700`.
- The configured path is a hard link to a private, hash-derived bind path, so both names refer to the same socket inode and permission changes apply to both.
- Callers can configure any mode from `000` through `777`; permissive settings therefore expose the socket to other local users.
- Existing parent directories are not repermissioned. Security consequently depends partly on their ownership and permissions.
- No authentication, encryption, peer-identity checks, or connection authorization appear in this file. Filesystem access is the primary security boundary.
- On Windows, permission-setting is skipped, so this file supplies no equivalent mode guarantee there.
- Empty and overlong paths are rejected. The maximum is 107 UTF-8 bytes on Linux and 103 elsewhere.

## Socket lifecycle

- Startup creates the parent directory, checks both the public and private names, binds the private name, verifies it is a socket, records device and inode, creates the public hard link, applies permissions, and only then reports the listener address.
- Startup failures attempt to close the server and remove owned paths.
- Starting twice or starting while closing is rejected.
- Closing is idempotent. It stops accepting, closes active connections, removes the public socket only when its recorded inode still matches, and removes the private bind name.
- Cleanup uses rename-before-delete, reducing the chance of unlinking a replacement at the public path.
- If replacement is detected during cleanup, the code preserves it and raises an error rather than deleting it.

## Stale socket handling

- Non-socket objects at either path are never removed.
- Existing sockets are probed before removal. A successful connection, or a one-second probe timeout, is treated as evidence that the socket is live.
- Specific connection failures such as refusal, missing path, broken pipe, and reset are treated as stale indications; other probe errors abort startup.
- Stale sockets are atomically renamed to a random temporary name, rechecked by inode, and then deleted.
- These checks address common replacement races, though filesystem operations can still encounter unusual concurrent changes after validation.

## Backlog, backpressure, and connection limits

- No accept backlog is supplied to `server.listen`; the effective backlog is therefore delegated to Node and the operating system rather than configured here.
- There is no maximum connection count, admission control, idle timeout, rate limit, or per-client quota.
- Outbound writes are serialized and copied before queuing.
- Each connection has a pending-outbound-byte ceiling, defaulting to four times the configured maximum frame size. Attempts beyond that limit are rejected.
- The implementation does not explicitly process the socket’s boolean backpressure result or wait for a drain event; its own pending-byte accounting is the main application-level control.
- The frame-size option is validated and used to derive the pending limit, but frame parsing or inbound-size enforcement is not performed in this file.

## Error handling and shutdown

- Server errors are delivered through the optional error callback; exceptions from that observer are suppressed.
- Socket errors are passed to the accepted connection handler and followed by socket destruction.
- Socket closure marks the connection closed and invokes the handler’s close callback.
- Active connections receive a graceful close opportunity, with a default five-second timeout before forced destruction.
- Server-close callback errors are reported but do not themselves reject shutdown.
- Exceptions thrown by the accept function or by handler callbacks are not wrapped here, so their effect depends on the surrounding event/runtime behavior.
- Cleanup failures can still reject `close`, and a path replacement detected during cleanup is intentionally left preserved rather than overwritten.
```

```text
# pi-gateway

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-Bun-black?logo=bun)](https://bun.sh)
[![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Dwsy/pi-gateway?style=social)](https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway)

The multi-channel AI gateway for pi coding agent. Connect your AI assistant to Telegram, Discord, Feishu, and WebChat with a single configuration.

---

## Why pi-gateway?

Direct use of OpenClaw requires managing RPC processes, message routing, and channel integrations yourself. pi-gateway handles all the infrastructure so you can focus on building intelligent agents.

```
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
|  Without         |     |  With            |     |  Your Benefit    |
|  pi-gateway      |     |  pi-gateway      |     |                  |
|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
| Manage RPC       |     |                  |     | Focus on agent   |
| processes        |     |  Automatic       |     | logic, not       |
|                  |     |  RPC Pool        |     | infrastructure   |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
| Build message    |     |                  |     | Zero boilerplate |
| routing          |     |  Session Router  |     | for multi-user   |
|                  |     |                  |     | scenarios        |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
| Handle channel   |     |                  |     | One config for   |
| differences      |     |  Unified API     |     | all platforms    |
|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
| Implement        |     |                  |     | Seamless pi      |
| from scratch     |     |  Plugin System   |     | skills support   |
|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
```

### Key Differentiator: Seamless pi Skills

pi-gateway is designed for pi users. All pi skills work out of the box:

```
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
|                 |       |                 |       |                 |
|  pi skills      |       |  pi-gateway     |       |  Result         |
|                 |       |                 |       |                 |
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
| send_message    |  -->  | Auto-route to   |  -->  | Message sent    |
| send_media      |       | active channel  |       | to Telegram/    |
| session_status  |       |                 |       | Discord/WebChat |
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
| cron            |  -->  | Isolated        |  -->  | Scheduled       |
|                 |       | execution       |       | tasks work      |
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
| message         |  -->  | Channel-aware   |  -->  | Reactions,      |
|                 |       | adapters        |       | edits, pins     |
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
| All pi skills   |  -->  | Transparent     |  -->  | Works anywhere  |
|                 |       | integration     |       | pi runs         |
+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
```

---

## Architecture

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                           pi-gateway                                    |
|                                                                         |
|  Telegram ----+                                                         |
|               |     +------------+     +-------------+     +-------+    |
|  Discord ------+--> |  Plugin    | --> |  Session    | --> |  RPC  |    |
|               |     |  System    |     |  Router     |     |  Pool |    |
|  Feishu ------+     +------------+     +-------------+     +-------+    |
|               |           |                  |                |        |
|  WebChat -----+      Hooks/Tools       Message Queue    pi --mode rpc  |
|                           |                  |                |        |
|                     +-----+-----+            |           +----+----+   |
|                     |           |            |           |         |   |
|                  Auth       Transform    Backpressure   JSON     stdin  |
|                                          Handling       Lines    stdout |
|                                                                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    v
                            +--------------+
                            |              |
                            |  pi agent    |
                            |  + skills    |
                            |              |
                            +--------------+
```

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| Plugin System | 14 hooks, 8 registration APIs. Extend without modifying core. |
| Session Router | Route to isolated agent instances: `agent:{id}:{channel}:{chat}` |
| Message Queue | Serialize per-session messages, prevent interleaving |
| RPC Pool | Manage subprocess pool with crash recovery and auto-scaling |

---

## Features

**Multi-Channel**: Telegram, Discord, Feishu (Lark), WebChat

**RPC Pool**: Isolated subprocess per session with configurable min/max/idle

**Session Isolation**: Deterministic routing for per-user/group contexts

**Message Queue**: Priority queue with backpressure handling

**Model Failover**: Automatic fallback chain with exponential backoff

**Cron Engine**: Scheduled tasks with isolated execution context

**Security**: DM policies (pairing/allowlist/open/disabled), SSRF guard

**Plugin Architecture**: Hot-reloadable plugins with full lifecycle management

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# Clone and install
git clone https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway.git
cd pi-gateway
bun install

# Configure
cp pi-gateway.jsonc.example pi-gateway.jsonc
export TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="your-bot-token"

# Start
bun run start

# Open http://localhost:52134
```

---

## Configuration

Minimal setup:

```jsonc
{
  "gateway": { "port": 52134 },
  "agent": { "model": "claude-sonnet-4" },
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "botToken": "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"
    }
  }
}
```

Key settings:

| Section | Purpose | Required |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `gateway.port` | HTTP/WS listen port | No (default: 52134) |
| `agent.model` | LLM model for agent | Yes |
| `agent.pool` | RPC pool size (min/max) | No |
| `channels.*.botToken` | Platform bot token | If channel enabled |

---

## Plugin System

```typescript
export default function myPlugin(api: GatewayPluginApi) {
  // Hook into agent lifecycle
  api.registerHook(["agent_end"], async (ctx) => {
    console.log(`Session ${ctx.sessionKey} completed`);
  });

  // Add HTTP endpoint
  api.registerHttpRoute("GET", "/health", async (req, res) => {
    res.json({ status: "ok" });
  });

  // Register slash command
  api.registerCommand("ping", async (ctx) => {
    await ctx.reply("Pong!");
  });
}
```

Available hooks:

| Hook | When |
|------|------|
| `before_agent_start` | Before agent starts |
| `agent_end` | After agent finishes |
| `message_received` | Message from channel |
| `message_sending` | Before sending (mutable) |
| `message_sent` | After sending |
| `before_tool_call` | Before tool execution |
| `after_tool_call` | After tool execution |
| `session_start` / `session_end` | Session lifecycle |
| `gateway_start` / `gateway_stop` | Gateway lifecycle |

---

## CLI Commands

```bash
pi-gw gateway [--port N] [--verbose]   # Start gateway
pi-gw doctor                            # Health check
pi-gw send --to <target> --message <m>  # Send message
pi-gw config show                       # Show config
pi-gw onboard                           # Interactive setup
```

Send command targets:

```
telegram:<chatId>                           # DM
telegram:<accountId>:<chatId>               # Specific account
telegram:<accountId>:<chatId>:topic:<tid>   # Topic in group
discord:<channelId>                         # Discord channel
```

---

## Security

| Policy | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `pairing` | Unknown sender gets 8-char code, admin approves |
| `allowlist` | Only configured user IDs can interact |
| `open` | Anyone can interact |
| `disabled` | Block all DMs |

```bash
# Approve pairing request
pi-gw pairing approve telegram ABCD1234
```

---

## Project Status

| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| Telegram | Stable |
| Discord | Stable |
| Feishu (Lark) | Beta |
| WebChat | Stable |
| Cron Engine | Stable |
| Plugin System | Stable |
| Hot-Reload | Planned |

---

## Requirements

- [Bun](https://bun.sh) >= 1.1.0
- [pi CLI](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) (`npm install -g @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`)
- LLM provider (API key or OAuth via `pi /login`)

---

## Common Issues

**Cannot connect to Telegram**

```bash
# Verify bot token
curl https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getMe

# Check environment variable
echo $TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
```

**RPC pool exhausted**

```jsonc
{ "agent": { "pool": { "min": 2, "max": 8 } } }
```

**Model rate limited**

```jsonc
{
  "agent": {
    "modelFailover": {
      "primary": "claude-sonnet-4",
      "fallbacks": ["gpt-4o", "gemini-pro"]
    }
  }
}
```

```text
# pi-gateway

Multi-platform chat bridge for pi — connect your AI agent to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. Real-time streaming, per-chat sessions, background tasks, and role-based access control.

> Fork of [0xKobold/pi-gateway](https://github.com/0xKobold/pi-gateway) with config-based UID allowlisting.

## Features

- **Multi-platform adapters** — Discord, Telegram, Slack, Twitch, WhatsApp, WebSocket
- **Real-time streaming** — responses appear token-by-token via live message editing
- **Per-chat sessions** — isolated conversations with configurable reset policies (daily / idle)
- **Background tasks** — spawn async work from chats, results delivered when ready
- **Allowlist security** — DB-based and config-file pre-approved UIDs, admin roles, tool access policies
- **Detached daemon mode** — `/gateway start -d` or `pi-gateway start -d` keeps the gateway alive after pi closes
- **HTTP + WebSocket API** — connect external clients, send prompts, receive streaming responses
- **pi-native** — runs as a pi extension with `/gateway` slash commands and registered tools

## Installation

Install from npm (recommended):

```bash
pi install npm:@gamalan/pi-gateway
```

Or clone and build manually:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/gamalan/pi-gateway.git
cd pi-gateway
npm install && npm run build
pi install .
```

Requires pi coding agent (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent >= 0.80.3`) and `@sinclair/typebox >= 0.32.0`.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Start the gateway
/gateway start

# Check status
/gateway status

# Stop
/gateway stop
```

The gateway starts on `http://localhost:3847` by default. See `/gateway config` for current settings. When detached mode is active, pi's footer shows `🟢 Gateway (daemon)` and automatically follows daemon start/stop changes.

## Configuration

Configuration lives at `~/.pi/gateway/config.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "port": 3847,
  "host": "localhost",
  "tokens": [],                    // Bearer tokens for API auth (empty = allow all)
  "corsOrigins": ["*"],
  "enableWebSocket": true,
  "enableHttp": true,
  "security": {
    "allowAll": true,              // false = enforce allowlist
    "requirePairing": false,
    "allowedUids": {},             // pre-approved users (see Security)
    "adminUids": {},              // users with full access (see Admin Users)
    "rateLimit": {
      "maxRequests": 60,
      "windowMs": 60000
    }
  },
  "sessions": {
    "resetPolicy": "idle",         // "daily" | "idle" | "both"
    "dailyHour": 4,                // hour (0-23) for daily reset
    "idleMinutes": 1440            // minutes before idle reset
  },
  "platforms": {
    "discord": {
      "enabled": true,
      "botToken": "your-token",
      "guildId": "optional-guild-id"
    },
    "twitch": {
      "enabled": true,
      "clientId": "your-client-id",
      "clientSecret": "your-secret",
      "channels": ["channel-name"]
    },
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "token": "your-bot-token",
      "webhookUrl": "https://..."  // omit for long polling
    },
    "slack": {
      "enabled": true,
      "webhookUrl": "https://...",
      "botToken": "optional-bot-token"
    },
    "whatsapp": {
      "enabled": true,
      "sessionPath": "~/.pi/whatsapp-session",
      "printQr": true
    }
  }
}
```

When the gateway starts for the first time with no config file, it
automatically seeds `~/.pi/gateway/config.json` from the default
template shipped with the package.  You can also find it at
`node_modules/pi-gateway/config/config.default.json`.

### Telegram: webhook vs long polling

The gateway auto-detects the mode based on whether `webhookUrl` is set:

| `webhookUrl` | Mode | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| Set | **Webhook** | Telegram POSTs updates to `/webhook/telegram` on the gateway's HTTP server. Lowest latency, requires a public URL. |
| Omitted | **Long polling** | The gateway opens a persistent connection to Telegram's `getUpdates` endpoint (30s timeout). Telegram holds it open and returns immediately when a message arrives — near-real-time, no public URL needed. |

Both modes are real-time. Long polling is NOT interval-based — it keeps one connection alive at all times.

## Security

### Allowlist (DB)

Manage users at runtime via `/gateway` commands:

```bash
# List allowlisted users
/gateway allow

# Add a user
/gateway allow discord 123456789

# Revoke a user (via tool or directly)
```

### Config-file pre-approved UIDs

Skip pairing entirely by listing UIDs in the `security` block of `config.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "security": {
    "allowAll": false,
    "allowedUids": {
      "discord": ["123456789", "987654321"],
      "telegram": ["1234567890"],
      "*": ["cross-platform-admin"]
    },
    "adminUids": {
      "discord": ["123456789"],
      "*": ["cross-platform-admin-uid"]
    },
    "rateLimit": {
      "maxRequests": 60,
      "windowMs": 60000
    }
  }
}
```

- Platform-specific keys match that platform only
- The `"*"` wildcard matches any platform
- Users in this list are auto-allowed on first contact — no pairing code needed
- `adminUids` grants full unrestricted access (bypasses all tool policies)
- All security settings live in the main `config.json` — no separate security file

### Admin Users

Admin users have **full unrestricted access** — they bypass all tool policies and can use every tool pi offers (bash, write, edit, subagent, etc.).

Admins can be set at runtime or via config's `security.adminUids` block:

```jsonc
{
  "security": {
    "adminUids": {
      "discord": ["123456789"],
      "*": ["cross-platform-admin-uid"]
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
# List all admins (DB + config)
/gateway admin list

# Grant admin to a user on a specific platform
/gateway admin add discord 123456789

# Grant admin on ALL platforms
/gateway admin add * 123456789

# Revoke admin
/gateway admin remove discord 123456789
```

Admin users are listed in the status panel and their messages carry a "FULL ACCESS" guard.

### Tool Policy

By default, external users are **restricted to read-only tools** when their messages reach pi: they can search code, inspect files, and ask questions, but cannot write files, execute shell commands, spawn subagents, or modify system state.

The policy is enforced via a system directive prepended to every forwarded message. It is tunable per platform, per user, or globally.

**Default allowed tools:** `read`, `web_search`, `fetch_content`, `fffind`, `ffgrep`, `module_report`, `read_symbol`, code search tools, `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_navigation`, `image_generate`, `gateway_*`

**Default denied tools:** `bash`, `write`, `edit`, `subagent`, `todo`, `goal_complete`, `mcp`, `ast_grep_replace`, `agent_browser`, `wait`, `intercom`, `wiki_*`, `lens_diagnostics`

#### Managing Policies

```bash
# List all explicit policies
/gateway tool-policy list

# See the default baseline
/gateway tool-policy defaults

# Allow bash for a specific user
/gateway tool-policy set discord U123456 bash allow

# Deny write for all users on Discord
/gateway tool-policy set discord * write deny

# Allow everything for an admin user (glob)
/gateway tool-policy set * admin-uid * allow

# Remove a policy by ID
/gateway tool-policy remove 3

# Reset all custom policies to defaults
/gateway tool-policy reset
```

Policies can also be managed from within pi sessions via the `gateway_tool_policy` tool.

**Resolution order** (highest wins): user-specific > platform-specific > global. Ties break deny-first (secure by default). The `*` glob matches any tool name. Admin users always bypass all restrictions.

> **Note:** All security configuration (allowlist, admin UIDs, rate limits)
> lives in the `security` block of `~/.pi/gateway/config.json`. There is
> no separate security config file. On first run, the gateway
> auto-seeds a complete default config so you don't have to write one
> from scratch.

### Pairing Flow

When `requirePairing` is enabled and a user is not in the allowlist:

1. User sends a message → blocked, receives a pairing code
2. Admin approves with `/gateway pair <code>`
3. User is added to the DB allowlist

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/gateway start [port]` | Start the gateway |
| `/gateway stop` | Stop the gateway |
| `/gateway restart` | Restart the gateway |
| `/gateway status` | Show running status, platforms, sessions |
| `/gateway pair [code]` | List pending codes or approve one |
| `/gateway allow [platform] [userId]` | List allowlist or add a user |
| `/gateway revoke <platform> <userId>` | Remove a user from the DB allowlist |
| `/gateway sessions` | List active chat sessions |
| `/gateway tasks` | List background tasks |
| `/gateway config` | Show current configuration |
| `/gateway admin list` | List admin users (DB + config) |
| `/gateway admin add <p\|*> <uid>` | Grant admin privileges |
| `/gateway admin remove <p\|*> <uid>` | Revoke admin |
| `/gateway admin list` | List admin users |
| `/gateway admin add <p\|*> <uid>` | Grant admin privileges |
| `/gateway admin remove <p\|*> <uid>` | Revoke admin |
| `/gateway tool-policy list` | List explicit tool policies |
| `/gateway tool-policy defaults` | Show default policy baseline |
| `/gateway tool-policy set <p> <u> <t> allow\|deny` | Add/update a tool policy |
| `/gateway tool-policy remove <id>` | Delete a policy |
| `/gateway tool-policy reset` | Clear all, back to defaults |

## HTTP API

Available when the gateway is running:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/api/status` | GET | Gateway status (running, adapters, clients, sessions) |
| `/api/sessions` | GET | Active sessions |
| `/api/background` | GET | Background tasks |
| `/api/allowlist` | GET | Allowlisted users |
| `/api/pairing` | GET | Pending pairing codes |

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` if tokens are configured.

## WebSocket API

Connect to `ws://localhost:3847`. Messages are JSON:

```jsonc
// Send a prompt
{ "type": "prompt", "data": { "message": "Hello" } }

// Start a background task
{ "type": "background", "data": { "sessionId": "...", "command": "..." } }

// Ping
{ "type": "ping" }
```

Receive responses, background task updates, and agent events as server-pushed messages.

## Registered Tools

The extension registers these tools for use in pi sessions:

- **`gateway_status`** — Check if gateway is running and which adapters are active
- **`gateway_sessions`** — List active chat sessions
- **`gateway_background_tasks`** — List and manage background tasks
- **`gateway_pairing`** — Generate or approve pairing codes
- **`gateway_tool_policy`** — Manage tool access policies for external users

## Sessions

Each chat gets an isolated session with configurable reset policies:

- **daily** — Session resets at a specific hour each day (default: 4 AM)
- **idle** — Session resets after N minutes of inactivity
- **both** — Whichever triggers first

Sessions persist across gateway restarts in `~/.pi/gateway/gateway-sessions.db`.

## Background Tasks

Long-running work is spawned in isolated background sessions. Results are delivered back to the parent chat when complete. Managed via `/gateway tasks`.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│  pi agent   │◄───►│        pi-gateway           │
│  (RPC)      │     │                             │
└─────────────┘     │  ┌─────────────────────┐    │
                    │  │ Platform Adapters    │    │
┌─────────────┐     │  │ Discord · Telegram   │    │
│ HTTP / WS   │────►│  │ Slack · Twitch       │    │
│ Clients     │     │  │ WhatsApp · WebSocket │    │
└─────────────┘     │  └─────────────────────┘    │
                    │                             │
                    │  ┌─────────────────────┐    │
                    │  │ Sessions Store      │    │
                    │  │ Background Manager  │    │
                    │  │ Security Layer      │    │
                    │  └─────────────────────┘    │
                    └─────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Platform adapters** translate incoming platform messages into a unified format
- **Sessions store** (`SQLite`) persists per-chat state with reset policies
- **Background manager** spawns async child processes, delivers results via chat
- **Security layer** checks allowlists, manages pairing codes, and enforces rate limits

## License

MIT

## Documented architecture

- A gateway accepts messages from Telegram, Discord, Feishu/Lark, and WebChat.
- Channel adapters feed a plugin layer, then a session router, message queue, and RPC process pool.
- Each RPC subprocess runs pi in RPC mode, communicating through JSON lines over standard input/output.
- Plugins can add lifecycle hooks, HTTP routes, commands, tools, and transformations. The page claims 14 hooks and 8 registration APIs.
- The gateway also documents cron jobs with isolated execution, model fallback with backoff, crash recovery, and configurable RPC-pool scaling.

## Transports

- External channels: Telegram, Discord, Feishu, and WebChat.
- Gateway access: HTTP and WebSocket are identified in the architecture and configuration.
- Agent transport: subprocess stdin/stdout carrying JSON-line RPC messages.
- CLI sending supports Telegram targets, including account, chat, and topic identifiers, plus Discord channel identifiers.

## Security

- Direct-message controls include pairing, allowlists, unrestricted access, and disabled mode.
- Pairing gives an unknown sender an eight-character code that an administrator must approve.
- The architecture also mentions authentication and an SSRF guard.
- The page does not describe credential storage, encryption, authorization for plugin routes, network binding defaults, or tenant isolation beyond session separation.

## Session mapping

- Routing is deterministic and isolates agent contexts by agent identity, channel, and chat.
- Group/topic routing is supported for Telegram.
- The stated goal is one isolated agent instance per relevant conversation context; exact lifecycle and persistence behavior are not specified.

## Queuing, streaming, attachments, and approvals

- Messages are serialized per session through a priority queue, with backpressure handling intended to prevent interleaving.
- Streaming behavior is not documented.
- Attachment handling is not documented. The skills diagram mentions media sending, but gives no supported formats, size limits, storage model, or transport details.
- Approval is documented for sender pairing only. There is no described tool-call, message, deployment, or human-in-the-loop approval workflow.

## Deployment

- Runtime requirement: Bun 1.1 or newer.
- The documented setup clones the repository, installs dependencies, copies an example JSONC configuration, sets a Telegram token environment variable, and starts the gateway with Bun.
- The default example exposes port 52134, with a local WebChat URL at that port.
- pi must be installed separately, and an LLM provider must be configured through credentials or pi login.
- Operational CLI commands cover gateway startup, health checks, outbound sending, configuration display, onboarding, and pairing approval.

## Version and activity

- No project version, release number, changelog, commit date, or maintenance cadence is provided.
- Listed channel status: Telegram, Discord, and WebChat stable; Feishu beta; cron and plugins stable; hot reload planned.
- A GitHub Stars badge is present, but the supplied content does not state a count or activity metric.

## Authority and caveats

This appears to be project-maintained README/documentation content, with links to the repository and deeper documentation, but the supplied page does not establish that it is a formally versioned or authoritative specification. Claims should therefore be checked against the repository, configuration schema, implementation, and release history. Several requested areas—streaming, attachments, detailed approvals, persistence, and deployment hardening—are absent or only briefly referenced.

## README-described behavior

### Architecture and transports

The README describes a Pi extension communicating with the agent through RPC. The gateway contains:

- Platform adapters for Discord, Telegram, Slack, Twitch, WhatsApp, and WebSocket
- HTTP and WebSocket client interfaces
- SQLite-backed session storage
- Background-task management
- Allowlist, pairing, rate-limit, and tool-policy enforcement

The default HTTP server is configured for `localhost:3847`. The WebSocket endpoint uses the same port.

### Session mapping

- Each chat receives an isolated session.
- Sessions are persisted in `~/.pi/gateway/gateway-sessions.db`.
- Reset modes are daily, idle, or both.
- Defaults are a daily reset hour of 4 and an idle timeout of 1,440 minutes.
- The precise platform-to-session-key mapping is not documented in the supplied material.

### Queue and background work

- Long-running work can run in isolated background sessions.
- Results are sent back to the originating chat.
- The README does not specify a general message queue, concurrency model, retry behavior, ordering guarantees, or backpressure handling.

### Streaming

- Platform responses are described as appearing incrementally through live message editing.
- WebSocket clients receive server-pushed responses, task updates, and agent events.
- The page does not document chunk formats, reconnection behavior, or delivery guarantees.

### Attachments

No attachment, file-upload, image-ingestion, or media-forwarding behavior is documented. WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and Twitch are listed as adapters, but their attachment capabilities are unspecified.

### Approvals and access controls

- Pairing can be required for users absent from the allowlist.
- A user receives a pairing code; an administrator approves it through a gateway command.
- Users may be preapproved by platform-specific or wildcard UIDs in configuration.
- Administrators may be configured or managed at runtime.
- External users are restricted to read-only tools by default.
- Tool policies can be set globally, per platform, or per user.
- Admin users bypass tool restrictions.
- API bearer authentication is available when tokens are configured.
- Rate limits are configurable.
- The example configuration defaults to permissive settings, including `allowAll: true`, empty API tokens, and wildcard CORS.

### Deployment

- Operates as a Pi extension with gateway slash commands and registered tools.
- Supports foreground operation and detached daemon mode.
- Telegram uses webhook mode when a webhook URL is set; otherwise it uses long polling.
- Platform credentials and options are configured in `~/.pi/gateway/config.json`.
- The README requires Pi coding agent version 0.80.3 or newer and TypeBox version 0.32.0 or newer.

The package metadata is presented as registry/package-page information. Architecture, streaming, task, security, and deployment details are README claims from the supplied page, not independently demonstrated evidence. 118	export function validateComboMetadata(metadata: unknown, id: string): ComboMetadata {

121	  }

123	  if (record.schemaVersion !== 1) throw new Error(`${id}: schemaVersion must be 1`);

125	  if (unknownKey) throw new Error(`${id}: unsupported combo.json field ${unknownKey}`);
126	  if (record.$schema !== undefined && typeof record.$schema !== "string") {

132	  }
133	  const launchArgs = validateLaunchArgs(record.launchArgs, id);
134	  const history = record.history;
135	  if (!history || typeof history !== "object" || Array.isArray(history)) {

139	  if (historyRecord.mode !== "isolated" && historyRecord.mode !== "shared") {

144	  if (unknownHistoryKey) throw new Error(`${id}: unsupported history field ${unknownHistoryKey}`);

152	    ? { mode: "shared", group: historyRecord.group as string }

174	      ? {}

273	export function validateLineage(combos: readonly Combo[]): Map<string, Combo> {
274	  const byId = new Map<string, Combo>(combos.map((combo) => [combo.id, combo]));
275	  for (const combo of combos) {
276	    const parentId = combo.metadata.derivedFrom;
277	    if (!parentId) continue;
278	    const parent = byId.get(parentId);
279	    if (!parent) throw new Error(`${combo.id}: parent combo ${parentId} does not exist`);
280	    if (parent.engine !== combo.engine) throw new Error(`${combo.id}: parent must use the same engine`);
281	  }
282	  const visiting = new Set<string>();
283	  const visited = new Set<string>();
284	  const visit = (id: string): void => {
285	    if (visiting.has(id)) throw new Error(`Lineage cycle detected at ${id}`);
286	    if (visited.has(id)) return;
287	    visiting.add(id);
288	    const parent = byId.get(id)?.metadata.derivedFrom;
289	    if (parent) visit(parent);
290	    visiting.delete(id);
291	    visited.add(id);
292	  };
293	  for (const combo of combos) visit(combo.id);
294	  return byId;
295	}

297	export async function comboDigest(combo: Combo): Promise<string> {
298	  const metadata: Partial<ComboMetadata> = { ...combo.metadata };
299	  delete metadata.$schema;
300	  delete metadata.derivedFrom;
301	  delete metadata.parentDigest;
302	  const agentDigest = await treeContentDigest(combo.agentDir);
303	  const hash = createHash("sha256");
304	  hash.update(JSON.stringify(stable(metadata)));
305	  hash.update("\0");
306	  hash.update(agentDigest);
307	  return `sha256:${hash.digest("hex")}`;
308	}

378	export function renderComboTree(combos: readonly Combo[]): string {
379	  const children = new Map<string | null, Combo[]>();
380	  for (const combo of combos) {
381	    const parent = combo.metadata.derivedFrom || null;
382	    const list = children.get(parent) || [];
383	    list.push(combo);
384	    children.set(parent, list);
385	  }
386	  for (const list of children.values()) list.sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
387	  const lines: string[] = [];
388	  const walkChildren = (combo: Combo, prefix: string): void => {
389	    const next = children.get(combo.id) || [];
390	    next.forEach((child, index) => {
391	      const last = index === next.length - 1;
392	      lines.push(`${prefix}${last ? "└─ " : "├─ "}${child.id} [${child.metadata.maturity}]`);
393	      walkChildren(child, `${prefix}${last ? "   " : "│  "}`);
394	    });
395	  };
396	  const roots = children.get(null) || [];
397	  roots.forEach((root) => {
398	    lines.push(`${root.id} [${root.metadata.maturity}]`);
399	    walkChildren(root, "");
400	  });
401	  return lines.join("\n");
402	}

467	function digestFileEntries(files: Readonly<Record<string, RuntimeSourceFile>>): string {
468	  const digest = createHash('sha256');
469	  for (const [relativePath, metadata] of Object.entries(files).sort(([left], [right]) => sortStrings(left, right))) {
470	    digest.update(relativePath);
471	    digest.update('\0');
472	    digest.update(metadata.sha256);
473	    digest.update('\0');
474	    digest.update(metadata.executable ? 'x' : '-');
475	    digest.update('\0');
476	  }
477	  return digest.digest('hex');
478	}

482	    Object.entries(files).map(([relativePath, metadata]) => [
483	      relativePath,
484	      { ...metadata, executable: false },
485	    ]),
486	  );
487	  return digestFileEntries(normalized);
488	}

490	/**
491	 * Scan a declarative agent tree without following links or accepting runtime state.
492	 */
493	export async function scanTree(root: string): Promise<ScannedRuntimeTree> {
494	  const absoluteRoot = resolveInputPath(root, 'source root');
495	  const rootStat = await lstatMaybe(absoluteRoot);
496	  if (rootStat === null) fail('PIA_SOURCE_MISSING', `Source directory does not exist: ${absoluteRoot}`);
497	  if (rootStat.isSymbolicLink()) {
498	    fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Source directory is a symbolic link: ${absoluteRoot}`);
499	  }
500	  if (!rootStat.isDirectory()) {
501	    fail('PIA_NOT_DIRECTORY', `Source root is not a directory: ${absoluteRoot}`);
502	  }
503	
504	  const entries: Array<[string, RuntimeSourceFile]> = [];
505	
506	  async function visit(directory: string, prefix: string): Promise<void> {
507	    const children = await fs.readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true });
508	    children.sort((left: Dirent, right: Dirent) => sortStrings(left.name, right.name));
509	
510	    for (const child of children) {
511	      const relativePath = prefix === '' ? child.name : `${prefix}/${child.name}`;
512	      validateRelativePath(relativePath, 'source path');
513	      const childPath = path.join(directory, child.name);
514	      const stat = await fs.lstat(childPath);
515	      if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
516	        fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Source path is a symbolic link: ${relativePath}`);
517	      }
518	      if (stat.isDirectory()) {
519	        await visit(childPath, relativePath);
520	        continue;
521	      }
522	      if (!stat.isFile()) {
523	        fail('PIA_NON_FILE_REJECTED', `Source path is not an ordinary file: ${relativePath}`);
524	      }
525	
526	      const { metadata } = await readOrdinaryFile(childPath, 'source path');
527	      entries.push([relativePath, publicSourceMetadata(metadata)]);
528	    }
529	  }
530	
531	  await visit(absoluteRoot, '');
532	  entries.sort(([left], [right]) => sortStrings(left, right));
533	  const files = Object.fromEntries(entries);
534	  return {
535	    root: absoluteRoot,
536	    digest: digestFileEntries(files),
537	    files,
538	  };
539	}

193	function textContent(content: unknown): string {
194	  if (typeof content === 'string') return content;
195	  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return '';
196	  const texts: string[] = [];
197	  for (const part of content) {
198	    if (isRecord(part) && part.type === 'text' && typeof part.text === 'string') {
199	      texts.push(part.text);
200	    }
201	  }
202	  return texts.join('\n');
203	}

205	function toolNames(content: unknown): string[] {
206	  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return [];
207	  const names: string[] = [];
208	  const seen = new Set<string>();
209	  for (const part of content) {
210	    if (!isRecord(part)) continue;
211	    const isCall = ['toolCall', 'tool_call', 'toolUse', 'tool_use'].includes(String(part.type));
212	    if (!isCall || typeof part.name !== 'string' || part.name.trim() === '') continue;
213	    const name = part.name.trim();
214	    if (!seen.has(name)) {
215	      seen.add(name);
216	      names.push(name);
217	    }
218	  }
219	  return names;

377	  const notes: string[] = [];

379	  if (truncated.size > 0) notes.push(`${truncated.size} retained block(s) truncated`);

382	    : '';

384	  const content = `${header}${omission}${renderedBlocks.length ? `\n\n${renderedBlocks.join('\n\n')}` : ''}\n`;

393	  return { ...block, body: truncateUtf8Head(block.body, bodyBudget, marker) };

407	    return {
408	      content: full,
409	      omittedBlocks: 0,
410	      retainedBlocks: blocks.length,
411	      truncatedBlocks: 0,
412	      totalBlocks: blocks.length,

414	  }
415	
416	  const included = new Set<number>();
417	  const truncated = new Map<ConversationBlock, ConversationBlock>();
418	  for (let index = 0; index < blocks.length; index += 1) {
419	    if (blocks[index].required) included.add(index);
420	  }
421	  const firstUser = blocks.findIndex((block) => block.kind === 'user');
422	  if (firstUser >= 0) included.add(firstUser);
423	  if (blocks.length > 0) included.add(blocks.length - 1);

425	  let result = renderSelection(header, blocks, included, truncated, maxBytes);
426	  while (utf8Bytes(result.content) > maxBytes) {
427	    const candidates = [...included]

429	      .sort((left, right) => utf8Bytes(renderBlock(right.block)) - utf8Bytes(renderBlock(left.block)));
430	    const candidate = candidates[0];
431	    if (!candidate) {
432	      fail('PIA_HANDOFF_LIMIT_TOO_SMALL', 'Handoff limit cannot preserve required conversation context');
433	    }
434	    const overflow = utf8Bytes(result.content) - maxBytes;
435	    const currentBytes = utf8Bytes(renderBlock(candidate.block));
436	    const next = truncateBlock(candidate.block, Math.max(96, currentBytes - overflow - 64));
437	    if (!next || utf8Bytes(renderBlock(next)) >= currentBytes) {
438	      fail('PIA_HANDOFF_LIMIT_TOO_SMALL', 'Handoff limit cannot preserve required conversation context');
439	    }
440	    truncated.set(blocks[candidate.index], next);
441	    result = renderSelection(header, blocks, included, truncated, maxBytes);
442	  }
443	
444	  for (let index = blocks.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
445	    if (included.has(index)) continue;
446	    const tentative = new Set(included);
447	    tentative.add(index);
448	    const next = renderSelection(header, blocks, tentative, truncated, maxBytes);
449	    if (utf8Bytes(next.content) <= maxBytes) included.add(index);
450	  }

453	  return { ...result, totalBlocks: blocks.length };
