1	# Changelog
2	
3	## [0.84.4] - 2026-08-28
4	
5	### New Features
6	
7	- **Terminal capability overrides** — Override detected terminal hyperlink, image, and truecolor support. See [Capability Overrides](docs/terminal-setup.md#capability-overrides).
8	- **Extension UI prompt events** — Integrations can distinguish active agent work from time spent waiting for `ctx.ui` prompts. See [Extension UI prompt events](docs/extensions.md#ui_prompt_start--ui_prompt_end).
9	- **RPC queue clearing** — Retrieve and clear queued steering and follow-up messages with `clear_queue`. See [RPC `clear_queue`](docs/rpc.md#clear_queue).
10	- **Fullscreen selection copy controls** — Disable automatic selection copying in fullscreen mode and use Ctrl+X to copy the active selection. See [UI & Display](docs/settings.md#ui--display).
11	- **DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision (experimental)** — Use the vision-capable model through the built-in DeepSeek provider. See [API Keys](docs/providers.md#api-keys).
12	
13	### Added
14	
15	- Added `ui_prompt_start` and `ui_prompt_end` extension events so host integrations can distinguish active agent work from waiting on user-facing `ctx.ui` prompts ([#8355](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8355) by [@cristinaponcela](https://github.com/cristinaponcela)).
16	- Added `detectSupportedImageMimeTypeFromFile()` to the public library exports ([#8600](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8600) by [@xl0](https://github.com/xl0)).
17	- Added inherited experimental vision-capable `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` model support.
18	- Added transcript usage notices for compaction and branch summaries when cache miss notices are enabled.
19	- Added RPC `clear_queue` to retrieve and remove queued steering and follow-up messages ([#8432](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8432)).
20	- Added environment variables and advanced settings for overriding auto-detected terminal hyperlink, image, and truecolor capabilities ([#8665](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8665)).
21	- Added `fullscreenCopyOnSelect` to disable automatic fullscreen selection copy; when disabled, `Ctrl+X` copies the active text selection before falling back to the last assistant message, while `/tree` still copies the selected message ([#7720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7720)).
22	
23	### Fixed
24	
25	- Fixed toggling thinking visibility clearing partial output from running Bash tools ([#8611](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8611)).
26	- Fixed Windows shell aborts crashing Pi when `taskkill.exe` is unavailable on `PATH` ([#6596](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6596)).
27	- Fixed resumed sessions corrupting the next appended entry when their JSONL file lacks a trailing newline ([#8345](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8345)).
28	- Fixed extension messages sent with `triggerTurn: false` while the agent is running being inserted between a tool call and its result, which made providers that validate message order reject the replayed history. They are now appended once the turn's tool results are in ([#8537](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8537)).
29	- Fixed compaction and branch summaries forcing `toolChoice: "none"` ([#8649](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8649), [#8638](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8638)).
30	- Fixed large tool results crossing the auto-compaction threshold being sent to the provider before compaction. Pi now compacts between tool execution and the next assistant response in the same run, and restores interactive progress when that run resumes ([#6879](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6879)).
31	- Fixed Google Vertex requests failing with `HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor` when the bundled Node.js runtime uses an HTTP(S) proxy ([#8610](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8610)).
32	- Fixed saving a default model from a non-empty model scope so it remains available in that scope.
33	- Fixed inherited `@` file autocomplete ranking to prefer direct and shallower matches over similarly ranked nested paths ([#8669](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8669)).
34	- Fixed inherited OpenAI-compatible streams serializing thinking signatures repeatedly during streaming ([#8671](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8671)).
35	- Fixed inherited main-screen rendering crashing when image-heavy output exceeded V8's string length limit ([#8028](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8028)).
36	- Fixed inherited fullscreen double-click word selection splitting paths and kebab-case tokens on `/` and `-` ([#8676](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8676)).
37	- Fixed inherited Cloudflare AI Gateway catalogs omitting supported `workers-ai/*` passthrough models.
38	- Fixed inherited OpenAI-compatible reasoning replay to merge consecutive streamed text and summary `reasoning_details` deltas.
39	- Fixed inherited OpenRouter reasoning controls so reasoning-mandatory models do not receive `effort: "none"` ([#8614](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/8614) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai)).
40	- Fixed inherited OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions ignoring an explicitly requested `toolChoice` when no tools are defined.
41	- Fixed inherited fragmented Mistral tool calls splitting when continuation chunks omit the tool-call ID ([#8387](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8387)).

43	## [0.84.3] - 2026-08-24
44	
45	### New Features
46	
47	- **PowerShell tool** — Use optional native PowerShell command execution on Windows. See [PowerShell Tool](docs/windows.md#powershell-tool).
48	- **Safer managed updates** — Stage, verify, and atomically activate updates for installer-managed installations. See [Install and Manage](docs/packages.md#install-and-manage).
49	- **Model and thinking controls** — Select thinking levels with `/thinking`, search defaults, keep selections session-scoped, and persist them explicitly with Ctrl+S. See [Models and Thinking](docs/keybindings.md#models-and-thinking).

52	
53	- Renamed the inherited `GoogleThinkingLevel` type to `GoogleApiThinkingLevel` and added `ResolvedGoogleThinkingLevel` for normalized adapter levels.

57	- Added an optional `powershell` tool for Windows, configurable through `defaultTools` and the SDK. See [PowerShell Tool](docs/windows.md#powershell-tool).
58	- Added a `/thinking` selector and searchable default choices to the model and thinking selectors; Ctrl+S saves the selected model as the global default. See [Models and Thinking](docs/keybindings.md#models-and-thinking).

66	- Added inherited provider-neutral `toolChoice` support to simple stream requests.

226	
227	### Breaking Changes
228	
229	- Renamed the inherited pi-ai `ModelsStreamTransforms` interface to `ModelsRequestTransforms` because its header transformation now applies to all authenticated provider requests.
230	- Changed JSON and RPC `message_update` events to emit only `assistantMessageEvent` deltas, removing the cumulative `message` and `assistantMessageEvent.partial` fields that caused quadratic output growth. Clients that need partial messages must assemble deltas between `message_start` and `message_end`; the latter remains authoritative ([#7290](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7290)).
231	- `ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders()` now returns `ProviderHeaders` with `string | null` values and preserves `null` header-deletion markers. Extensions that inspect returned headers must handle `null`; extensions forwarding them to pi-ai streams should pass them through unchanged. This prevents placeholder OpenAI credentials from being sent through Cloudflare AI Gateway ([#7030](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7030)).
232	- Changed `ModelRegistry.refresh()` to accept `ModelsRefreshOptions` and return `ModelsRefreshResult` instead of discarding cancellation and provider errors.
233	- Changed `ModelRuntime.setRuntimeApiKey()` to accept auth cancellation options rather than catalog refresh options. Call `refresh({ providers: [providerId], signal })` separately when remote freshness is required.
234	- Required config-form extension OAuth `refreshToken(credentials, signal)` callbacks to accept and honor a concrete abort signal.
235	- Replaced dynamic provider refresh context store access with the read-only `context.stored` snapshot and generation-checked `context.publish()` transaction.
236	
237	  **Providers built with `createProvider({ fetchModels })`:** no catalog-publication migration is required. Before and after, return the fetched models and register the resulting provider; `createProvider()` owns restoration, persistence, and in-memory publication.
238	
239	  ```ts
240	  // Before
241	  const beforeProvider = createProvider({
242	    // ...
243	    fetchModels: async ({ signal }) => {
244	      const response = await fetch(catalogUrl, { signal });
245	      return parseModels(await response.json());
246	    },
247	  });
248	  pi.registerProvider(beforeProvider);
249	
250	  // After: unchanged
251	  const afterProvider = createProvider({
252	    // ...
253	    fetchModels: async ({ signal }) => {
254	      const response = await fetch(catalogUrl, { signal });
255	      return parseModels(await response.json());
256	    },
257	  });
258	  pi.registerProvider(afterProvider);
259	  ```
260	
261	  **Handwritten native `Provider.refreshModels()`:** replace direct store access and pre-publication mutation with generation-guarded publications.
262	
263	  ```ts
264	  // Before
265	  refreshModels: async (context) => {
266	    const stored = await context.store.read();
267	    if (stored) currentModels = stored.models;
268	    if (!context.allowNetwork) return;
269	
270	    const refreshed = await fetchModels(context.signal);
271	    currentModels = refreshed;
272	    await context.store.write({ models: refreshed, checkedAt: Date.now() });
273	  },
274	
275	  // After
276	  refreshModels: async (context) => {
277	    if (context.stored) {
278	      const restored = context.stored.models;
279	      if (!(await context.publish({
280	        update: () => { currentModels = restored; },
281	      }))) return;
282	    }
283	    if (!context.allowNetwork) return;
284	
285	    const refreshed = await fetchModels(context.signal);
286	    if (context.signal.aborted) return;
287	    await context.publish({
288	      persist: { models: refreshed, checkedAt: Date.now() },
289	      update: () => { currentModels = refreshed; },
290	    });
291	  },
292	  ```
293	
294	  For the config-form `pi.registerProvider(name, { refreshModels })`, callbacks that only return models remain unchanged; pi publishes the returned list. If such a callback previously used `context.store` for custom persistence, read `context.stored` and call `context.publish({ persist: entry })`. In `publish()`, omit `persist` to leave storage unchanged, pass a `ModelsStoreEntry` to write it, or pass `persist: null` to delete it.
295	
296	- Replaced the inherited pi-agent-core harness session model with the v4 lane-based `Session`, `SessionStorage`, and `SessionRepo` APIs, including durable operation records, global facts, shared sequence numbers, and tree-scoped lane views.
297	- Promoted the inherited v2 session and `AgentHarness` API from pi-agent-core's experimental entrypoint to its default export and removed the experimental subpaths.
298	- Removed the inherited legacy JSONL and in-memory repository APIs. Use pi-agent-core's v4 `JsonlSessionRepo` or `InMemorySessionRepo`, both implementing the new `SessionRepo` contract.
299	- Added the inherited required pi-agent-core `FileSystem.renameFile()` operation for atomic JSONL publication; custom harness file-system implementations must provide same-filesystem replacement semantics ([#7707](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7707) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai)).
300	- Replaced experimental remote-session list summaries with durable `SessionMetadata`; `RemoteSession.sessions` no longer exposes runtime phase, model, thinking, attachment, or lock state, which remains available from acquired `SessionSnapshot` values ([#7708](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/7708)).

```text
## Architecture

- A Pi extension connects one Pi coding session to a Discord bot.
- Projects are separated into Discord text channels. The channel name is derived from the project’s working-directory name.
- Each Pi session normally receives its own thread within that project channel.
- Assistant output, optionally including tool activity and results, is sent to the session thread.
- Discord messages can be forwarded back to Pi, enabling two-way interaction.
- A stop reaction can abort the active turn.

## Setup

### Requirements

- Pi
- A Discord bot installed in the target server
- Bot permissions for:
  - Sending messages
  - Reading message history
  - Creating public threads
  - Managing threads
  - Adding reactions
  - Managing channels when automatic project-channel creation is enabled

### Installation

Recommended installation uses Pi’s package installer with `npm:pi-discord-bridge`. Alternatively, add that package to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`.

For a local checkout:

1. Copy the extension into `~/.pi/agent/extensions/discord-bridge`.
2. Run `npm install` there.
3. Reference it as `ext:discord-bridge` in Pi settings.

Copy `.env.example` to `~/.pi/.env`, fill in the values, and restart Pi. The configuration is global across projects.

## Environment configuration

The documented keys control:

- Enablement: `PI_DISCORD_ENABLED`
- Bot authentication: `PI_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`
- User authorization: `PI_DISCORD_USER_IDS`
- Routing mode: `PI_DISCORD_CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT`
- Fixed-channel routing: `PI_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID`
- Automatic-channel guild: `PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID`
- Live assistant updates: `PI_DISCORD_STREAM_MESSAGES`
- Per-session threads: `PI_DISCORD_CREATE_THREAD_PER_SESSION`
- Thread naming: `PI_DISCORD_THREAD_NAME_PREFIX`
- Tool-call display: `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_CALLS`
- Tool-result display: `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_RESULTS`
- User-input echoing: `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_USER_INPUT`
- Reasoning display: `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_REASONING`

Defaults documented by the page are:

- Disabled unless explicitly enabled
- Automatic project channels enabled
- Session threads enabled
- Thread prefix `pi`
- Tool calls, tool results, and user-input echo enabled
- Streaming edits and reasoning display disabled

Automatic channel creation requires a guild ID. Otherwise, the bridge can send everything to the configured fixed channel.

## Authorization and security

- Discord access is limited to the configured comma-separated user-ID allowlist.
- The bot token is the primary credential and must be supplied through configuration.
- Automatic channel creation requires channel-management permission, which is broader than ordinary message access.
- Showing tool output, user input, or reasoning can expose project or conversational data; reasoning display is off by default.
- The page does not document encryption, token rotation, audit logging, rate limits, role-based authorization, input validation, or handling of unauthorized users.

## Session, channel, and thread mapping

For each Pi start in a project:

1. The bridge finds or creates a text channel based on the working-directory name.
2. It creates a thread for the session unless that feature is disabled.
3. The thread receives a short identifier consisting of the configured prefix plus a five-character slug, such as `pi-a1b2c`.
4. Later sessions in the same project use the project channel but receive separate threads.

The page does not explain how channels are matched across renames, how name collisions are handled, or where mappings are persisted.

## Streaming and Discord UI

- Assistant streaming can either be suppressed until completion or represented by live message edits.
- Tool calls and tool results each have independent rendering switches.
- User messages can be echoed into Discord.
- Reasoning output is separately controlled and defaults to hidden.
- The bridge supports muting and unmuting Discord output.
- Users can interact through ordinary Discord messages, slash commands, and an abort reaction.
- The page does not specify message chunking, edit frequency, formatting rules, attachment handling, embed usage, or Discord size-limit behavior.

## Commands

### Discord slash commands

- `/session` — report session and thread details
- `/abort` — stop the current turn
- `/compact` — request context compaction
- `/new [args]` — begin another Pi session
- `/mute` and `/unmute` — control Discord output
- `/discord-status` — show bridge status and configuration
- `/discord-test [msg]` — send a test message
- `/discord-reconnect` — reconnect the bot

The bridge commands can be registered as native Discord slash commands. Natural-language messages are also forwarded to Pi.

### Pi commands

- `/discord-status`
- `/discord-test [msg]`
- `/discord-reconnect`
- `/discord-mute`
- `/discord-unmute`
- `/discord-arm`
- `/discord-launcher-status`

The last two expose in-process session replacement and HTTP-launcher status, but their mechanics are not described.

## Concurrency, queues, and lifecycle

- The page describes one thread per session and two-way message delivery.
- It provides no details about queues, ordering guarantees, simultaneous Discord inputs, concurrent tool calls, multiple Pi processes, backpressure, retries, or cancellation races.
- No subprocess, daemon, worker, or HTTP-server lifecycle is documented.
- Configuration takes effect after restarting Pi.
- Reconnection is exposed through a command, but retry policy, heartbeat handling, state restoration, and failure recovery are unspecified.
- No database or durable state mechanism is described; only reuse of project channels is documented.

## Limitations and documented gaps

- Per-project routing depends on a guild and channel-management access.
- Fixed-channel routing is available when automatic channel creation is disabled.
- Behavior for project-name collisions, deleted channels or threads, renamed directories, long names, missing permissions, offline Discord, and malformed configuration is unspecified.
- The page does not define logging, metrics, testing, deployment topology, version compatibility, or data-retention behavior.
- The project is identified as MIT-licensed.

```text
## Architecture

### Pi extension integration

Registers handlers for:

- `session_start`
- `session_shutdown`
- `input`
- `message_start`
- `message_update`
- `message_end`
- `tool_call`
- `tool_result`

Uses these Pi APIs:

- `pi.on`
- `pi.registerCommand`
- `pi.sendUserMessage`
- `pi.appendEntry`
- `pi.getCommands`
- `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId`
- `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries`
- `ctx.sessionManager.newSession`
- `ctx.isIdle`
- `ctx.abort`
- `ctx.compact`
- `ctx.hasUI`
- `ctx.ui.notify`

Locally registered commands:

- `discord-arm`
- `discord-status`
- `discord-test`
- `discord-reconnect`
- `discord-mute`
- `discord-unmute`
- `discord-launcher-status`

The code does not register or invoke Pi tools. It observes tool activity through `ToolCallEvent` and `ToolResultEvent`, then labels known tool-name patterns such as Bash, read, edit, write, web search, LSP, AST grep, and subagents.

Pi commands returned by `pi.getCommands()` are displayed for visibility only; arbitrary Pi command handlers are not dispatched from Discord.

### Discord authentication and authorization

- Bot authentication uses `PI_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, loaded from `~/.pi/.env` unless overridden by `PI_DISCORD_ENV_FILE`.
- Legacy token and user-variable names are disabled unless `PI_DISCORD_ALLOW_LEGACY_ENV` is enabled.
- Message and reaction input requires an exact author ID in `PI_DISCORD_USER_IDS` or `PI_DISCORD_USER_ID`.
- Bot-authored messages are ignored.
- Message input is accepted only from:
  - the configured fallback channel,
  - the current session thread,
  - channels remembered as project channels.
- Reaction-based abort additionally requires the reaction to be on a message authored by this bot and uses the stop emoji.
- Required Discord intents include guilds, guild messages, message content, direct messages, and reactions.

Important authorization gap: slash-command interactions are processed without checking the invoking user, guild, or channel. Registration is limited to configured guild IDs, but anyone able to invoke a registered command can potentially run bridge actions such as abort, mute, reconnect, test, or new-session operations.

Project-channel creation requires `PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID`. The bot needs suitable guild channel-fetch, channel-create, thread-create, send, edit, and reaction permissions, but the code does not explicitly verify those permissions.

### Inbound prompt handling

For ordinary Discord messages:

1. The message is filtered by channel and user ID.
2. Slash- or bang-prefixed bridge commands are handled first.
3. Otherwise the text is sent to Pi.
4. If Pi is idle, it uses a normal user message.
5. If Pi is busy, it uses `deliverAs: "steer"`.
6. The Discord message receives a success or queued reaction.

There is no application-level inbound queue, mutex, debounce, rate limit, or ordering guarantee. Multiple Discord events can call `pi.sendUserMessage` concurrently. Ordering therefore depends on Pi’s internal behavior and event scheduling.

### Outbound event streaming

Assistant output supports two modes:

- Non-streaming: one Discord message at `message_end`.
- Streaming: updates are buffered and periodically sent or edited.

The relay:

- splits content under Discord’s message-size limit,
- edits existing pages when possible,
- sends additional pages as needed,
- optionally renders reasoning,
- optionally posts local interactive input,
- posts tool-call embeds in running, successful, or failed states,
- reports summarized tool inputs, outputs, and durations,
- suppresses mentions and performs secret-pattern redaction.

Typing indicators are renewed periodically while assistant streaming or tool activity is active.

Limitations and race risks:

- Stream buffers are keyed only by message timestamp.
- `finalize` does not wait for an already-running `flush`, so edits and sends can overlap.
- Discord message edits are not serialized through the relay queue.
- Tool-result edits are also outside the send queue.
- Failed or muted finalization can leave stream state behind.
- Assistant messages without numeric timestamps are not relayed.
- Redaction is pattern-based and cannot guarantee removal of every secret.

### Session replacement and launching

`/new` has two paths:

1. If the local `discord-arm` command has armed the current session, it calls `ctx.sessionManager.newSession` and rebinds `lastCtx`.
2. Otherwise it launches a detached process using `PI_DISCORD_SPAWN_COMMAND`, defaulting to `pi`, plus configured arguments.

The armed state is tied to a session ID and is cleared when the active session changes. Spawned processes inherit the full environment, with only the launcher disabled in the child.

Notable limitations:

- Spawn errors emitted after process creation are not handled, so a failed launch may initially be reported as successful.
- Spawned sessions inherit the parent environment and current working directory implicitly.
- Spawn arguments support basic quoting but not escaping or robust shell parsing.
- Session state is global to the extension module, not isolated by session object.
- `lastCtx`, active channel, relay, and client references are process-wide; overlapping sessions or rapid replacement can target the wrong session.

### Persistence

The extension appends custom session entries for:

- relayed message timestamps,
- session-to-thread bindings.

On session start it restores both sets from the session manager. This prevents replaying already-relayed messages and restores known session threads.

Not persisted:

- project-channel mappings,
- mute state,
- Discord connection state,
- launcher state,
- active process ownership,
- tool-message state,
- in-memory stream buffers.

Project channels can be rediscovered by name after restart, but channel names derive only from the directory leaf. Different directories with the same final component can collide and reuse the same channel.

### Concurrency, locking, and cleanup

A promise chain serializes most outbound sends and thread creation, with a configurable delay between operations. It does not protect:

- inbound prompt submission,
- Discord edits,
- reactions and replies,
- interaction handling,
- session setup across concurrent starts,
- stream finalization versus flushing.

Reconnect and shutdown generally:

- wait for boot,
- stop typing,
- flush the send queue,
- destroy the Discord client,
- clear relay and REST state,
- stop the launcher on shutdown.

Potential lifecycle issues:

- Boot/reconnect/session-start operations share global mutable state.
- A shutdown during boot or channel creation can leave asynchronous work running.
- The launcher is stopped on `session_shutdown`, but detached child processes are not tracked or terminated.
- No explicit handling exists for Discord reconnect events beyond the manual reconnect command.
- A launcher port collision disables the HTTP endpoint for that instance.

### Unsafe defaults and operational concerns

- Discord bridging is disabled by default, which is appropriate.
- Per-project channel creation is enabled by default and requires guild configuration.
- The launcher is enabled by default.
- An empty launcher secret permits local `/new-session` requests without authentication. Binding to loopback limits exposure to the host, but does not authenticate local users or processes.
- The launcher accepts unrestricted request bodies and has no rate limiting.
- Slash registration is disabled by default, but if enabled, its handlers lack user/channel authorization.
- Status output includes project paths, IDs, and configured spawn arguments; spawn arguments could contain sensitive values and are not consistently redacted.
- Error replies from some Discord paths are not passed through the redaction function.
- Any allowlisted user can control every currently recognized project/session channel; there is no per-user project isolation or role distinction.
- The bot token itself is not printed, but environment-derived secret discovery and redaction are heuristic rather than comprehensive.

## Verification scope

The supplied page contains the repository README, but not the TypeScript source. Therefore, README-level claims can be summarized, while exact Pi APIs, hooks, locking code, and lifecycle behavior cannot be independently verified.

## Findings

- **Pi hooks and methods:** The README identifies the extension entry point as `src/bridge/index.ts` and exposes `/slk-bridge` commands. It does not name Pi hook registration APIs, event handlers, method signatures, or extension interfaces.
- **Slack admission and pairing:**
  - Requires a Slack app using Socket Mode.
  - Requires bot and app-level tokens.
  - First-time users receive a six-digit challenge displayed in the Pi terminal.
  - A user enters the code in Slack to become trusted.
  - Only one trusted Slack user is supported; `/slk-bridge releaseclaim` reopens claiming.
  - The README does not document whether pairing codes are persisted or how identity is stored internally.
- **Session and tmux ownership:**
  - Only one terminal session may own the Slack bridge at once.
  - A newly connected session takes ownership from the previous one.
  - tmux is used to create, resume, switch, and hand over Pi sessions.
  - Sessions are represented by separate Slack threads.
  - Supported operations include `new`, `resume`, `handover`, `optin`, and `optout`.
  - The README says handover and resumed sessions can replay prior conversation history.
- **Concurrency and locking:**
  - A single-instance guard prevents duplicate Slack connections.
  - The README mentions force-acquiring the connection by typing in the target session.
  - It provides no lock-file path, lease duration, atomicity guarantee, stale-lock recovery details, or race-handling behavior.
- **Persistence paths and permissions:**
  - Configuration: `~/.pi/slk-bridge.json`, mode 600.
  - Configuration directory: `~/.pi/`, mode 700.
  - Slack downloads: `~/.pi/slk-bridge-downloads/slack/`.
  - Handoffs: `~/.pi/slk-bridge-handoffs/`.
  - Environment variables override file configuration.
  - The README does not identify all persisted metadata, session files, or retention/deletion rules.
- **Reconnection and shutdown:**
  - The bridge connects after token configuration or on the next Pi launch when `autoConnect` is enabled.
  - Manual connection is available through `/slk-bridge connect`.
  - No reconnect retry policy, backoff, health checks, graceful shutdown procedure, signal handling, or Slack disconnect behavior is documented.
- **Tool approvals:**
  - Deterministic bridge commands are described as avoiding LLM calls.
  - No policy is documented for approving Pi agent tools, shell commands, file transfers, or actions initiated from Slack.
- **Security warnings:**
  - Treat both Slack tokens as secrets.
  - Remote Slack access can send prompts, receive files, and control session selection.
  - The single-user claim mechanism is the primary admission control described.
  - Required Slack scopes include messaging, file access, history, reactions, metadata, and user identification.
  - Challenge protection is stated as three attempts with two-minute expiry.
  - The README does not describe token encryption, audit logging, rate limiting, administrator roles, or file-content validation.
- **Compatibility:**
  - Targets the Pi coding-agent harness.
  - Requires tmux and `pi` available in `PATH` for handoff/session management.
  - Supports installation through Pi’s npm or local-path installer.
  - Requires a Slack app with Socket Mode and the listed permissions.
  - No supported Pi, Node.js, operating-system, Slack API, or tmux version ranges are specified.

 `https://github.com/zikolach/pirelay`

```text
## README-based verification

- **Pi integration:** The README identifies `extensions/relay/` as the Pi extension and says it listens to Pi lifecycle events, tracks task state, publishes routes, and injects authorized messenger input into the active session. It does **not** name specific Pi hook symbols, event types, or public API method names.
- **Pi commands:** The documented local command family is `/relay ...`, including setup, connection, diagnostics, approvals, status, file delivery, trust management, disconnection, and broker restart. The companion skill is at `skills/relay/SKILL.md`.
- **Broker model:** PiRelay uses a local broker for multi-session routing. One broker is shared by sessions with the same state directory, bot-token hash, and broker namespace. Clients register routes and periodically reconcile the complete route map. Transport health and route synchronization are reported separately.
- **Restart and recovery:** `/relay restart` replaces the shared broker; clients reconnect automatically. Partial recovery is tolerated, missing clients retry within bounded limits, and route repair normally occurs within about 30 seconds. A detached broker can be stopped manually during testing.
- **Messenger routing:**
  - Telegram: private bot chats, media, inline actions, Bot API progress signals, and multi-session selection.
  - Discord: DM-first operation, optional explicitly configured guild/channel routing, typing activity, and text commands prefixed with `relay`.
  - Slack: Socket Mode, App Home direct messages, optional channel/thread routing, reactions or ephemeral progress fallback, and an optionally installed native `/relay` command.
- **Pairing and authorization:** Local commands create short-lived, single-use pairing flows using QR/deep-link or PIN mechanisms. Pairing is tied to the selected Pi session and messenger. Allow-lists and local trust checks apply; unknown identities can be locally allowed, trusted, or denied before remote control is enabled.
- **Approvals:** Disabled by default. When enabled with explicit rules, sensitive operations from remote turns can pause for requester confirmation. The choices are one-time approval, session approval, or denial. Timeouts, revoked bindings, offline sessions, paused bindings, and delivery failures block gated actions by default.
- **Session persistence:** State is stored below `~/.pi/agent/pirelay/`; configuration is `config.json`. Resume with `pi --continue` can restore non-secret binding metadata. Tokens, signing secrets, prompts, tool internals, and transcripts are not persisted in relay state.
- **Concurrent sessions:** Multiple live Pi sessions can share a broker. Users can label sessions, list them with `/sessions`, select them with `/use`, or address one request with `/to`. Older offline sessions from the same workspace are hidden by default when a newer online session exists, but can be exposed with `/sessions all`.
- **Streaming and coalescing:** Progress supports `quiet`, `normal`, `verbose`, and `completion-only`. Updates are coalesced and deduplicated, with supported adapters editing a live progress message where possible. Tool activity is summarized using bounded safe labels and counts; raw output, file contents, transcripts, and arbitrary tool arguments are excluded.
- **Terminal delivery:** Final answers are chunked by platform limits, with paragraph-aware splitting and Markdown-file fallback where supported. Telegram additionally supports formatted Markdown, inline choices, and download or in-chat actions.
- **Limitations:** Native Slack slash commands may be stale or unavailable; Slack has no native typing bubbles. Discord requires Message Content Intent for ordinary text controls. Channel routing is opt-in, Telegram groups are not the default, file delivery is less capable on Discord and Slack, images require a vision-capable Pi model, image transfer is size/MIME constrained, and structured-answer detection is intentionally conservative.
```
</details></tool-use>

{"body":"## Summary\n\nTwo small, generic hardening changes would make PI WEB safer to operate behind a private reverse proxy while sharing canonical Pi session files with native clients:\n\n1. An exact request-boundary gate driven by `PI_WEB_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and `PI_WEB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, applied to both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades.\n2. Session admission control in `sessiond`, with a health/control surface that reports admission state, active sessions, and pending activations and can fail closed during updates or frontend handoffs.\n\nI implemented and tested bounded patches against `@jmfederico/pi-web` `1.202608.1` / commit `e3cd03aa18c9b677c45dc8f1992b3fe76816bafc`:\n\n- Host/Origin patch: 64 non-test added lines.\n- Admission patch: 99 non-test added lines and 4 deleted lines.\n- No session-storage or ownership rewrite.\n\n## Observed behavior\n\n- Approved loopback Host/Origin combinations succeed.\n- Unapproved Host and Origin values return `403`.\n- The same boundary applies to WebSocket upgrades.\n- Admission closes atomically and rejects new create/resume requests while allowing health/status inspection.\n- CLI/Web and Web/Web attempts to open the same canonical transcript fail closed under the corresponding Pi session-lease integration.\n- Distinct transcripts remain concurrently usable.\n- Gateway restart and a 180-second task/browser-disconnect scenario were exercised without transcript corruption.\n\n## Proposed shape\n\n- Keep proxy authentication external; these controls are defense in depth, not a replacement for it.\n- Treat an absent Host/Origin allowlist as current upstream behavior for compatibility, or gate strict behavior behind explicit environment configuration.\n- Keep admission logic generic and independent of any deployment manager.\n- Expose a small control API with at least `ok`, `version`, `piVersion`, `admissionClosed`, `activeSessions`, and `pendingActivations`.\n\nI can provide the two patch files or turn this into a focused PR if this direction fits the project.\n","comments":[],"createdAt":"2026-08-13T11:34:57Z","number":154,"state":"OPEN","title":"Add exact Host/Origin gates and session admission control","updatedAt":"2026-08-13T11:34:57Z","url":"https://github.com/jmfederico/pi-web/issues/154"}

56:## Quickstart
60:### A — Electron desktop app (no prerequisites)
72:On first launch a setup wizard walks you through mode selection (standalone vs. power-user), API key / OAuth sign-in, and [recommended extensions](#recommended-extensions). The standalone mode bundles Node.js and auto-installs pi + dashboard + openspec into `~/.pi-dashboard/` — **no terminal, npm, or Node.js required**.
87:### B — pi package (recommended for CLI users)
94:# open http://localhost:8000
107:🌐 Dashboard started at http://localhost:8000
110:Open **http://localhost:8000** in any browser. All active pi sessions appear automatically. See [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) for Node.js / build-tool requirements.
114:Windows has a few extra one-time setup steps. Run the following in an **Administrator** PowerShell session:
136:start http://localhost:8000
141:### C — From source (contributors)
169:To try the extension in a single pi session without registering it:
177:### D — Docker (self-contained, no host install)
179:Run the whole ecosystem — server, pi agent, code-server, zrok, tmux, terminals — in one container. No host install of pi, Node, or any tool.
185:# open http://localhost:8000
188:State persists in a named volume; API keys seed into `auth.json` on first run (or add providers later via the UI). Mount host projects at their identical absolute paths with `PI_WORKSPACES="/abs/a:/abs/b" ./up.sh` (auto-pinned on first run). The Electron desktop app can attach to a Docker-hosted server via the wizard's **Remote** mode — no local install. Full guide, volume performance profiles, dev mode, and external-gateway config: [`docker/README.md`](docker/README.md). For a disposable, fully isolated instance for manual browser QA (can't collide with a running host dashboard): [`docker/TESTING.md`](docker/TESTING.md).
192:## Features
195:- **Real-time session mirroring** — all active pi sessions with live streaming messages
199:- **Session spawning** — launch new pi sessions from the dashboard (headless by default, or via tmux)
200:- **On-demand session loading** — browse historical sessions with lazy-loaded content from pi session files
204:- **Workspace management** — organize sessions by project folder with pinned directories and drag-to-reorder
208:- **Local-image inlining + LaTeX math in chat** — agents can reference local screenshots inline as `![alt](/abs/path.png)` or `![alt](./relative.png)` and they render in chat (the bridge inlines bytes via a streaming-safe `pi-asset:<hash>` channel — each unique image's bytes ride exactly once per session, no matter how many streaming chunks repeat the token). Math expressions — inline `$x = \beta$` and display `$$\sum_i^n i$$` (block-level) — are typeset via KaTeX. PNG / JPEG / GIF / WebP / SVG / AVIF / BMP supported with a 5 MB-per-image, 20 MB-per-message cap; oversized or unreadable references render as a visible placeholder rather than a broken-image glyph. The dashboard server adds zero new HTTP routes.
212:- **PromptBus architecture** — unified prompt routing with adapters (TUI, dashboard, custom). Interactive dialogs (confirm/select/input/editor/multiselect) survive page refresh and server restart. Multiselect uses the bus-routed browser path exclusively (the dashboard `MultiselectRenderer` dialog) since pi 0.70's RPC mode has no working terminal-overlay primitive. First-response-wins semantics with cross-adapter dismissal.
213:- **Extension UI System (Phase 1)** — extensions can declare slash-command-triggered modal UIs as data, without authoring React or importing an SDK. Listen on `pi.events.on("ui:list-modules", probe)` and push descriptors into `probe.modules`; the dashboard renders `table` / `grid` / `form` views with row actions, optional confirm-dialog gates, and MDI icons. Modules survive reconnect via the server-side cache; in pure-pi mode descriptors stay dormant. See `openspec/specs/extension-ui-system/spec.md` for the protocol contract.
216:- **Browser-based provider auth** — sign in to Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity from Settings. Enter API keys for other providers. Credentials saved to `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` and live-synced to running sessions.
217:- **Custom LLM providers** — add OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, or Google Generative AI endpoints (Settings → Providers → LLM Providers). **Test** button verifies the base URL + API key before saving. Adding / editing / removing takes effect live in every running session — no restart.
218:- **Package management** — browse, install, update, remove, and **move** pi packages between global and project scopes from a single rich-row UI used in both Settings and Pi Resources. Install dialog exposes a Local/Global radio when launched from a per-folder context. Search the npm registry for pi-package extensions/skills/themes; install from npm or git URL. Active sessions auto-reload after changes.
219:- **MCP endpoint** — `POST /mcp` exposes dashboard sessions to MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor) once the server runs. Every request needs a bearer credential, including localhost. `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` gets a `pi-dashboard` entry automatically on first server start; external clients authenticate with a paired-device token. Local pi sessions need `pi-mcp-adapter >= 2.20.0`.
228:- **Zrok tunnel** — optional persistent public URL via reserved shares (see [Configuration → Tunnel](#tunnel-zrok))
232:## Chinese UI
234:PI Dashboard now includes a lightweight Simplified Chinese interface for the core operator workflow: onboarding, the session sidebar, chat composer, connection banners, Settings, provider setup, and package management.
246:## Prerequisites
253:| **pi-mcp-adapter ≥ 2.20.0** | Lets local pi sessions call the dashboard's `POST /mcp` endpoint | `pi ext update pi-mcp-adapter` |
261:| **tmux** | Spawn new pi sessions in a tmux window | When `spawnStrategy` is `"tmux"` |
262:| **[zrok](https://zrok.io/)** | Public tunnel with persistent URLs | When `tunnel.enabled` is `true` (default) |
266:## Configuration
272:### Precedence & keys
278:| `--port` | `PI_DASHBOARD_PORT` | `port` | `8000` | HTTP + browser WebSocket port |
279:| `--pi-port` | `PI_DASHBOARD_PI_PORT` | `piPort` | `9999` | Pi extension WebSocket port |
281:| `--no-tunnel` | — | `tunnel.enabled` | `true` | Disable zrok tunnel |
289:| — | `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` | `piSessionsDir` | `~/.pi/agent/sessions` | Pi sessions root the dashboard scans. See [Pi sessions directory](#pi-sessions-directory) |
291:The bridge also honours `PI_DASHBOARD_URL=ws://host:port` to point at a remote server instead of localhost.
293:#### Pi sessions directory
295:The dashboard is a separate process from pi, so it resolves **one** sessions root to scan. When pi's sessions live somewhere other than the default, point the dashboard at them via the following precedence (first match wins; blank values fall through, leading `~/` expands against `$HOME`):
298:2. `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` — pi's session-dir env var, if inherited by the dashboard process.
299:3. `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` + `/sessions` — pi's agent-dir relocation env var.
300:4. `~/.pi/agent/sessions` — built-in default.
302:Omit `piSessionsDir` (or leave it blank) to fall through to the env vars and default. Per-invocation `--session-dir` flags on other pi processes are not observable to the dashboard and are out of scope.
304:### Minimal `config.json`
326:### Authentication (optional)
328:OAuth2 authentication guards external (tunnel) access. Localhost is always unguarded.
332:  "auth": {
346:| `auth.secret` | No | JWT signing secret (auto-generated if omitted) |
347:| `auth.providers` | Yes | Map of provider → `{ clientId, clientSecret, issuerUrl? }` |
348:| `auth.allowedUsers` | No | Allowlist: usernames, emails, or `*@domain` wildcards. Empty = allow all |
352:**Callback URL:** register `https://<tunnel-url>/auth/callback/<provider>` in your OAuth provider settings. The tunnel URL is stable across restarts (reserved shares are auto-created).
354:> **Security note:** `/api/spawn-failures` is reachable to any caller on deployments without auth; entries contain `cwd` paths. Enable auth before exposing via tunnel.
356:### Tunnel (zrok)
358:The dashboard auto-connects a [zrok](https://zrok.io/) tunnel on start when `tunnel.enabled` is `true`. Install with `brew install zrok` (macOS) and run `zrok enable <token>` to enrol — the dashboard reads zrok's own config (`~/.zrok2/environment.json`), no keys are stored in the dashboard. Reserved shares provide persistent URLs across restarts.
360:### OpenSpec background polling
373:### Tool overrides
375:The dashboard resolves every external tool it calls (`pi`, `pi-coding-agent`, `openspec`, `npm`, `node`, `tsx`, `git`, `zrok`, `pi-dashboard`) through a single `ToolRegistry`. Each tool has an ordered strategy chain (override → managed install → bare-import / npm-global → PATH search), and every resolution records a diagnostic trail.
395:## Using the model proxy
401:export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1
412:**Auth:** proxy API keys only (`pi-proxy-*` prefix). Dashboard JWT is never accepted on `/v1/*`.
416:## Usage
418:### Auto-start (default)
424:**Debugging the Electron app via CDP.** The desktop app accepts an opt-in `--debug-cdp[=<port>]` CLI flag (and equivalent `PI_DEBUG_CDP` env var) that exposes Chromium's Chrome DevTools Protocol on a loopback-only port (default `9222`) so `agent-browser`, Playwright, Chrome DevTools, or any CDP client can attach to the *installed shell* — not just a separate browser pointed at `http://localhost:8000`. The flag wins if both flag and env are set. CDP is **off by default**, never binds beyond `127.0.0.1`, and logs a one-line `[debug-cdp]` warning to stderr when active. **Single-instance contract:** CDP must be enabled at first-instance launch; passing the flag to an already-running instance cannot enable CDP retroactively and only logs a warning — fully quit and relaunch. From this repo, `cd packages/electron && pnpm run dev:cdp` launches the dev Electron with CDP on. The bundled universal `browser` skill (shipped by the bridge extension) contains a worked-example recipe for attaching `agent-browser` to the Pi Dashboard app.
428:### Daemon mode
441:### Manual server start
449:### Graceful restart via API

457:curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/restart -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"dev":false}'

465:### Dev mode with production fallback
473:### Dev build on reload
481:> Blocks pi for ~2–5s during the build. The server shutdown affects all connected sessions — they auto-reconnect when one restarts the server.
483:### Session spawning
487:**tmux** — runs pi inside a tmux session named `pi-dashboard`, each spawned session as a new window:
497:### Slash commands (`/dashboard:*`) from a pi session
500:for driving the dashboard from any pi session without hand-writing curl.
509:  /dashboard:session-list          # table of every session
510:  /dashboard:session-info abc123   # all fields for a session (by id-prefix)
519:  /dashboard:session-tell abc123 please run the tests
520:  /dashboard:session-spawn          # new session in the current dir
521:  /dashboard:session-abort-all      # asks scope before aborting
528:### Keyboard shortcuts in chat input
530:Bash-style history recall and per-session draft persistence:
541:Drafts (typed-but-unsent text) are persisted per session in `localStorage` under `chat-draft:<sessionId>` and survive navigation (Settings, OpenSpec preview, diffs, …) and full page reloads. Drafts never leak between sessions.
545:## Recommended extensions
551:| `pi-anthropic-messages` | `git@github.com:BlackBeltTechnology/pi-anthropic-messages.git` | **required** | Tool calls on Claude-model Anthropic OAuth / 9Router `cc/*` / pi-model-proxy providers. Without it, tool calls fall back to Claude Code's built-in `bash_ide` sandbox and fail. |
557:Authoritative source: `packages/shared/src/recommended-extensions.ts`. Descriptions, versions, and installed-state are enriched live via `GET /api/packages/recommended` (offline fallback).
561:## Authoring a dashboard plugin
569:Then, from any pi session:
577:- **`new`** — scaffold a fresh `packages/<id>-plugin/` inside this monorepo. Pick which of the 10 React slots to claim (`session-card-badge`, `content-view`, `settings-section`, `tool-renderer`, …); the skill renders package.json (with `pi-dashboard-plugin` manifest), `src/client.tsx` with stubs, optional `src/server/index.ts`, optional `src/bridge/index.ts`, `configSchema.json`, and tests.
578:- **`augment`** — retrofit an existing pi-extension project on disk. The skill greps for TUI surface (`ctx.ui.*`, `pi.registerTool`, …), drives the agent through a canonical mapping table, asks per-callsite what to port, then injects a manifest field into `package.json` and adds `src/dashboard/`. Purely additive — your existing TUI keeps working in pure-pi sessions.
584:## Troubleshooting
586:### Dashboard server doesn't start
601:### Port already in use
607:### UI is empty or stuck after switching servers
609:Since the `safe-server-switch` release, switching servers via the header dropdown is **transactional**: the UI verifies the target through a short-lived staging WebSocket (5 s timeout) **before** clearing state or writing `localStorage`. If the target is unreachable, nothing changes — a toast appears and you stay on the previous server.
615:### Windows: sessions die when the dashboard restarts
617:Since the `consolidate-windows-spawn-and-platform-handlers` release, pi sessions on Windows **survive dashboard restart**, matching macOS/Linux behaviour. Previously, killing the dashboard process (Task Manager, Ctrl+C, `/api/restart`, crash) terminated every running pi session because the children were in the server's libuv kill-on-close Job Object. The fix uses `detached: true` so children are excluded from the parent's job.
619:If you previously relied on "closing the dashboard cleans everything up," use the per-session **Force Kill** action instead (or `POST /api/session/:id/force-kill`).
621:### Windows Terminal tab doesn't appear
623:Install Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) for tabbed interactive sessions — the dashboard prefers it over WSL tmux / headless when available. Windows 11 ships with it; on Windows 10 install from the Microsoft Store.
627:### Sessions don't group under my pinned folder
629:Since v0.3+, session grouping uses OS-aware path equality (`platform/paths.ts`). Sessions group correctly under a pinned folder even across trailing-separator, separator-style, or case differences (on Windows and macOS).
631:If you still see two entries for what should be one folder, the paths are likely on different Windows drives (`A:\Foo` and `B:\Foo` are different filesystems and never merge) — that's correct behaviour. If the paths really are the same filesystem, file an issue with both the pinned path (Settings → Tools → Export diagnostics) and the session `cwd` from `/api/sessions`.
633:### Tool not found (pi / openspec / npm / …)
637:### Recommended extensions: "Permission denied (publickey)"
639:`pi-flows` and `pi-anthropic-messages` install via SSH (`git@github.com:…`). If your system has no GitHub SSH key, set one up following [GitHub's SSH docs](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh), or substitute the equivalent HTTPS URL in the manifest if your fork is public.

```text
## Architecture
- A Go service sits between Pi’s session files and a browser-based PWA.
- Pi records conversations as JSONL under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
- The server reads those files, while `fsnotify` detects changes and pushes updates through SSE.
- Browser chat requests are handled by Pi processes running in RPC mode.
- Tailscale Serve can expose the local service over HTTPS on the tailnet.

## Pi RPC integration
- Installation registers `/web`, `/pi-web`, `/remote`, and `/refresh`.
- `/web` opens the active session, with SSH-aware behavior.
- `/refresh` imports messages created remotely into the terminal session.
- `/pi-web` controls the service and can check its status, restart it, or update it.
- Automatic session naming is handled by the web application, using either a local heuristic or a selected model.

## Session workers and persistence
- Browser-initiated work uses one RPC worker per session.
- Workers are removed after ten minutes without activity.
- Conversation persistence is file-based through Pi’s session JSONL files; no database is described.
- File watching enables near-real-time updates.
- The README does not specify session locking, recovery after worker failure, retention policies, or how simultaneous writers are reconciled.

## Web transport
- Local browser communication uses HTTP, with SSE for server-to-browser updates.
- The default address is `127.0.0.1:31415`.
- Tailscale provides the documented remote HTTPS path and MagicDNS-based access.
- The README does not describe WebSocket use, upload limits, SSE buffering, reconnection behavior, or API versioning.

## Authentication and network exposure
- A remote-access token can be supplied through `~/.config/pi-web/env`.
- Tailscale is the intended remote-access mechanism; it requires an installed, signed-in, and approved Tailscale client.
- Custom ports and non-loopback binding are supported according to the referenced installation documentation, but details are not included here.
- The README does not state whether authentication is mandatory, how tokens are validated, or whether local access is authenticated.
- It also omits rate limiting, CSRF protection, audit logging, role separation, and multi-user isolation.

## Concurrency and queues
- Per-session workers provide a basic isolation boundary.
- The README gives no explicit queue design, capacity limits, ordering guarantees, backpressure policy, cancellation semantics, or fairness rules.
- It is unclear whether multiple browser requests for one session are serialized or handled concurrently.

## Process lifecycle
- Installation places the binary under `~/.pi/agent/bin/pi-web` and configures login startup.
- Startup uses launchd on macOS, a user systemd service on Linux, and a Windows Run-key starter.
- The service exposes start, stop, restart, status, and update operations.
- RPC workers have a ten-minute idle reaping policy.
- Shutdown behavior, child-process cleanup, crash restart policy, health checks, and upgrade rollback are not documented.

## Permissions and limitations
- The design assumes access to the Pi session directory and the user’s home configuration paths.
- Installation modifies user-level startup configuration and Pi’s command integration.
- The README does not define filesystem permission requirements, privilege escalation behavior, sandboxing, or protection against other local users.
- The project is identified as beta, so behavior may change.
- Remote use depends on network reachability and, for the documented HTTPS workflow, Tailscale configuration.
```

A web chat interface for the [pi coding agent](https://pi.dev). The agent runs
**in-process** via the pi SDK and streams events to the browser over WebSocket:
thinking blocks, tool calls, file trees, a built-in terminal, model management,
theme switching, and a full settings panel — tuned for daily development.

> **Requirements** — Node.js ≥ 22.19 and a configured pi install.

## More from the author

> **Building with DSH?**
>
> [**dsh-ui-tools**](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/dsh-ui-tools) is the author's companion project for building and extending UI tools in the DSH ecosystem.

## ✨ Highlights

| 💬 **Chat that works like you do** | 🖼️ **Files & images** | 🧩 **Extensible by design** | 🔒 **Private by default** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Streaming replies, steer & follow-up queueing, slash commands, multiple conversations per project, edit-&-re-ask. | Attach files, paste images, ask about pictures (vision bridge), preview anything with GBK fallback. | Drop-in UI **plugins** (extra top-bar tabs + agent tools) and standalone **themes** — no rebuild, no restart. | Loopback-only, credential-safe: provider keys & headers never reach the browser. |

## Features

### 💬 Chat

- **Streaming agent chat over WebSocket** — the pi SDK runs in-process; events are pushed as snapshots (60 ms throttled) and the browser renders them.
- Thinking blocks, tool-call cards and bash outputs with live status (running → finished · waiting for the model · duration).
- **Steer (follow-up queueing)** — send a follow-up while the agent is replying; it is queued and injected as soon as the current turn's tool calls settle (the "Interrupt" equivalent of the pi CLI).
- **Slash commands** — `/` opens a command picker (built-in / extension / template / skill); built-ins include `/new /model /compact /cwd /thinking /resume`, plus `/help` (command list) and `/copy` (copy last reply).
- **Multiple conversations per project** — each conversation gets its own agent runtime and keeps running in the background after you switch away; the "Running conversations" list shows stream progress and lets you switch back.
- **Edit & re-ask** — fork any past question into a new branch and re-prompt; the original conversation stays untouched.
- Long threads auto-collapse messages older than 30 into lazy summary rows (click to expand).
- Question navigation — a floating rail plus per-question tags to jump between questions.

### 🖼️ Files, images & attachments

- Three attachment modes: `inline` (≤12 KB), `reference` (path only), `lines` (selected ranges) — over-limit ones degrade automatically.
- Paste / drag-drop / upload images — resized client-side and sent as image content when the model supports vision (warning otherwise).
- **Vision bridge** — when the current model is text-only, images are transcribed into text evidence by an auto-discovered vision model (cached per batch; model & on/off configurable in Settings).
- Attach arbitrary files without a workspace path — stored in a global uploads dir, inlined when small, referenced by absolute path otherwise.
- File preview — line numbers, click/drag/Shift selection (add to chat as `lines`), GBK fallback decoding, binary hex view, media preview over HTTP with Range support, and a download button.
- Live file tree — the server watches the listed directory (`fs.watch`) and re-lists on change; oversized directories show a truncation warning.

### 🖥️ Terminal & Git

- Built-in terminal (xterm.js + node-pty) with per-client PTY management; Windows auto-selects Git Bash (busybox fallback).
- **Source control (Git) panel** — status / branch / diff / untracked files via a hidden query terminal; commit, switch branch, push and pull run in the visible terminal and auto-switch to the terminal view.

### 🎛️ Models & settings

- Theme switching — pick a theme in the top bar; themes are pure `:root` palette overrides on top of the single layout stylesheet (default dark + bundled light/dark palettes). See [Themes](#themes) for how to add your own or contribute one.
- Model management — edit `models.json` in the UI and set per-provider API keys (keys/headers never leave the server).
- Thinking level per model (only the levels the model actually supports are shown).
- First-run setup wizard.
- Settings panel — system prompt (append or replace), toggle skills/extensions on/off with immediate effect, save/apply/delete settings presets, and vision-bridge model & switch.

### 🎯 Goal mode

- Goal bar — set a target with a review model, max rounds and a lock switch.
- Goal wizard (**AI Refine**) — turns a raw request into a concrete goal through a guided questionnaire.
- Automatic review loop — after each turn an independent review session checks the goal against the final text and `git diff HEAD`; on fail the feedback is injected as steer until it passes (or the round cap is hit).

### ⚙️ Background tasks

- Background-task panel — servers launched by the agent are detected via port snapshots and listed (port/pid/name); stop one or kill all.
- Tool watchdog — a tool call running over 20 minutes is aborted automatically.
- **Stop bash command only** — abort a running bash tool without killing the conversation.

### 🛡️ Safety & operations

- Loopback-only by default; set `PI_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0` for LAN / containers.
- WebSocket Origin/Host same-authority check — cross-origin pages are rejected (403); `PI_WEB_ALLOW_ORIGINS` whitelist for reverse proxies.
- Quiesce drain mode via a local control socket (`server status|quiesce|unquiesce`).
- Credentials stay server-side — provider headers are never sent to the browser.
- Sound alerts, Chinese/English UI, and a recent-projects list (click to switch workspace).

### 🚢 Deploy & update

- Foreground, global npm install, Docker (docker-compose), macOS launchd, Linux systemd, Windows Task Scheduler, and a desktop shortcut (`server shortcut`).
- In-app self-update — checks the npm registry, installs and auto-restarts the service.

## Install

```bash
npm i -g pi-web-ui            # global install (recommended)
npx pi-web-ui                 # or run without installing (latest, starts on :8787)
npm i -g .                    # or install the local checkout
```

**npm ≥ 12?** npm 12+ blocks dependency install scripts by default (you'll see
`npm warn install-scripts … blocked`). node-pty is a native module, so allow its
script (the other two packages it lists are harmless no-ops — allowing them just
silences the warning):

```bash
npm i -g --allow-scripts=node-pty,@google/genai,protobufjs pi-web-ui@latest
```


## Quick start

**Start**

```bash
pi-web-ui                                           # foreground, http://localhost:8787
PI_WEB_PORT=9000 PI_WEB_CWD=/path/to/project pi-web-ui     # custom port / workspace
```

**Stop**

- **Foreground**: press `Ctrl+C` in the terminal running it.
- **As a service**: `pi-web-ui server stop` (stops the instance; auto-start stays until `server uninstall`).

**Update**

```bash
npm i -g pi-web-ui@latest     # upgrade to the latest published version
pi-web-ui server restart      # restart the service to apply it (foreground: restart manually)
```

**Uninstall**

```bash
npm uninstall -g pi-web-ui
```

Uninstalling does **not** delete your chats — session data lives in
`<cwd>/.pi-web` (or `PI_WEB_DATA_DIR`) and survives uninstall/upgrade.


## System service

```bash
pi-web-ui server install --port 9000 --cwd /path/to/project   # install + start
pi-web-ui server status                     # running? auto-start?
pi-web-ui server restart                    # restart (applies config/version changes)
pi-web-ui server stop                       # stop (auto-start stays)
pi-web-ui server start                      # start again
pi-web-ui server uninstall                  # remove the service entirely
pi-web-ui server shortcut                   # desktop one-click launch icon
pi-web-ui server quiesce                    # drain: refuse NEW chats/messages, let running ones finish
pi-web-ui server unquiesce                  # reopen admission
```

`server status` also shows live stats via a local control socket (version,
PID, quiesce state, connected browsers, running conversations) — the same
socket drives `quiesce`/`unquiesce`.

- **macOS** → launchd agent (no sudo), logs to `/tmp/pi-web-ui.log` / `.err`
- **Linux** → systemd unit (`systemctl enable --now`), logs via `journalctl -u pi-web-ui -f`
- **Windows** → Task Scheduler logon task (hidden PowerShell window, no black console)

Options: `--port` (default 8787), `--cwd` (workspace), `--data-dir` (sessions),
`--name` (custom service name). Rerunning `server install` with new options
regenerates the config and restarts the service — that's how you change its
port/cwd.


## Plugins

Plugins are optional UI components (extra top-bar tabs backed by their own
client view, optionally with a server-side entry and agent tools). They live in
your **data-dir plugins folder** (`<dataDir>/plugins/<id>/`, default
`~/.pi-web/plugins/`) — a plugin is simply a directory containing
`manifest.json`, an optional server entry (`index.mjs`) and an optional view
entry (`client/entry.mjs`). No plugin directories = no plugins, nothing shows
up in the UI.

### Plugin catalog

These plugins ship in this repository (`dev/plugins/<id>/`) and can be installed
straight from GitHub:

| Plugin | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| 📬 [webmail](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/webmail) | IMAP inbox browsing / search / read / mark / delete + SMTP sending, new-mail notifications, and an optional "allow AI to manage my mailbox" switch (six `mail_*` agent tools). Auto-installs its npm deps on first activation. |
| 🗄️ [db-client](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/db-client) | Database workbench: connection manager + schema tree for MySQL / PostgreSQL / SQLite / SQL Server / MongoDB / Redis — table structure, paginated data with sorting, SQL editor, and row editing. Drivers auto-install on first use. |
| 📝 [vscode-editor](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/vscode-editor) | VS Code-like workbench: multi-root file tree (local + SSH hosts), CodeMirror multi-tab editor, Remote-SSH remote file browsing/editing, draggable multi-terminal panel (xterm.js), SFTP sync & upload/download to your computer. Auto-installs `ssh2`. |
| 📬 [demo-mailbox](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/demo-mailbox) | Minimal example plugin demonstrating the server entry + client view + two-way message protocol. Doubles as the plugin test fixture — start here if you want to write your own. |

Example — install the webmail plugin:

```bash
pi-web-ui install https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/webmail
```

Each plugin's directory in the repo has its own `README.md` with full feature
lists, configuration and per-plugin caveats.

### Installing

From GitHub (any of these source forms):

```bash
pi-web-ui install owner/repo                                  # shorthand
pi-web-ui install https://github.com/owner/repo               # full URL (.git optional)
pi-web-ui install https://github.com/o/r/tree/dev/sub/dir     # branch + subdirectory inside the repo
pi-web-ui install owner/repo#v1.2                             # pin a branch/tag (#suffix works on any form above)
pi-web-ui install /path/to/plugin-dir                         # local directory (for development)
```

Useful options:

- `--name <id>` — custom plugin id / directory name (defaults to the repo or
  subdirectory name; letters/digits/`-`/`_` only).
- `--force` — overwrite an existing installation. Your plugin's local
  `config.json` (credentials etc.) is preserved across upgrades.
- `--data-dir <dir>` — override the data dir (default `~/.pi-web`).

The CLI clones the repo (shallow; falls back to a tarball download without
git), locates the `manifest.json` (including inside subdirectories) and copies
the plugin into `<dataDir>/plugins/<id>/`.

**No git? No network?** You can also just copy a plugin directory into
`~/.pi-web/plugins/` by hand — same result.

### Updating

Re-run `install` against the same source with `--force`:

```bash
# example: update the webmail plugin to the latest version in the repo
pi-web-ui install https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins/webmail --force
```

- The upgrade preserves the plugin's local `config.json` automatically.
- Plugins that store other local state inside their directory (e.g. db-client's
  `db-connections.json`, vscode-editor's `ssh-hosts.json`) are **not** covered
  by that preservation — back those up before a forced reinstall.
- Refresh the browser afterwards; no server restart needed.

### Activating

If the server is running, just **refresh the browser** — new plugins are picked
up on attach without a restart. If it isn't, they load on next start. Each
plugin appears as a tab (🧩 or its own icon) in the top bar.

### Listing / disabling / uninstalling

```bash
pi-web-ui plugins             # list installed plugins (id / name / version / description)
pi-web-ui uninstall <id>      # remove a plugin
```

- To temporarily hide a plugin without uninstalling, use the **Settings panel
  (⚙) → UI plugins** switches — stored per client, purely visual, no restart
  needed. Re-enable any time.
- `uninstall` deletes the plugin directory; refresh the browser and its tab
  disappears. Plugin configuration written inside the plugin dir is removed
  too — back up `<dataDir>/plugins/<id>/config.json` first if you need it.


## Themes

Each theme is a **pure `:root` palette override** — a small CSS file that only sets CSS variables (see the `:root` block in `web/src/styles.css` for the full variable list: base colors `--bg/--accent/--term-*` plus derived colors like `--tooltip-bg/--code-bg/--notice-*`). The layout lives ONLY in the bundled `web/src/styles.css`; picking a theme overrides the variables, so every theme works with every build and layout changes never touch themes. Built-in themes are generated by `node make-light-theme.mjs`.

Built-in themes ship in the npm package (`themes/`, e.g. the bundled light theme). The theme picker lives in the top bar (🌞 icon); the current choice is stored per browser in `localStorage`.

### Using a theme

Just pick it in the top bar — built-in and user themes are merged in the same menu. User themes win over built-ins on the same id.

### Providing a theme locally (no GitHub needed)

Any CSS file dropped into your **data-dir themes folder** shows up in the theme menu automatically — no restart, no rebuild:

1. Find your data dir (default `~/.pi-web`, override with `PI_WEB_DATA_DIR`).
2. Create `<dataDir>/themes/` and drop your stylesheet in: e.g. `~/.pi-web/themes/my-theme.css`.
3. Reload the page and pick it in the top bar. The **file name (without `.css`)** is the theme id shown in the menu.

```
~/.pi-web/
└── themes/
    └── my-theme.css          # appears in the menu as "my-theme"
```

Easiest way to write one: copy a built-in palette (e.g. `themes/white.css` from the source repo) and change the `:root` colors — list every variable you want to override; unlisted ones fall back to the dark defaults in `styles.css`. Notes:

- The **terminal follows the theme** — set the `--term-*` variables (terminal ANSI palette + `--term-bg`) in your `:root` and both the xterm canvas and its padded container adapt automatically (see the defaults in `styles.css`).
- Syntax-highlight colors (`highlight.js`'s `github-dark.css` is bundled) must be overridden in your theme file or code will be unreadable on light themes — see the `.hljs` overrides at the bottom of `themes/white.css` for the pattern (dark themes can skip it).
- Theme ids must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (no dots/slashes — path-traversal guard on the server).

### Contributing a theme to the repository (GitHub)

Want your theme shipped to everyone? Open a pull request at [github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui):

1. Fork the repo and clone it.
2. Create your theme as `themes/<id>.css` — a pure `:root` palette. Copy `themes/white.css` (or `themes/cyberpunk.css` for a dark palette) as the starting template.
3. Verify locally: run `npm run dev`, then use the top bar theme picker — your theme must be listed and render correctly (chat cards, code blocks, tool-call cards, git/terminal panels).
4. Regenerate all built-in themes with `node make-light-theme.mjs` when you changed the variable list in `styles.css`.
5. Commit (`git add themes/<id>.css`) and open the PR. The `themes/` folder is already in the npm package `files` whitelist, so once merged and released, `npm i -g pi-web-ui` will ship your theme to everyone.

Rules for merged themes: the file must be a single CSS file, set the `--term-*` variables for a readable terminal, and override `.hljs` syntax colors for readable code on light themes.


## Security

- **Loopback-only by default** — the server binds `127.0.0.1` and is not
  reachable from the network unless you explicitly set `PI_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`
  (e.g. LAN access, Docker port mapping — the compose file sets it for you).
- **WebSocket origin check** — browser pages connecting to `/ws` must present
  an `Origin` whose hostname **and port** match the request `Host`;
  cross-origin pages are rejected with 403. Non-browser clients (no `Origin`)
  are unaffected. Add `PI_WEB_ALLOW_ORIGINS=http://your-host:port` for
  reverse-proxy setups.
- **Quiesce** — `server quiesce` refuses new prompts/forks/session resumes
  until you `server unquiesce`; in-flight runs finish cleanly (useful before
  upgrades/backups).
- **Credentials stay server-side** — provider `headers` (which may carry
  `Authorization` / API keys) are never sent to the browser; the model
  management UI edits everything else and the server preserves the headers.


## Reverse proxy (nginx)

Serve pi-web-ui behind nginx on the same host (it binds loopback only, so a
same-machine reverse proxy is the supported remote-access path — no
`PI_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0` needed):

```nginx
# pi-web-ui on 127.0.0.1:8787, exposed as https://your-host/pi/
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name your-host;
    # ssl_certificate ... / ssl_certificate_key ...

    # App entry at a sub-path (strips the /pi/ prefix)
    location /pi/ {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787/;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        # $http_host keeps the port — the server's origin check compares the
        # full authority (hostname AND port). $host would drop it and get 403.
        proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    # WebSocket — MUST forward Host identically or the upgrade is 403'd
    # (page loads, but chat/terminal keep reconnecting)
    location /ws {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
        proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
    }

    # Absolute-path assets/API the built frontend requests (root, not /pi/)
    location /assets/  { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; }
    location = /favicon.svg           { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; }
    location = /favicon-streaming.svg { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; }
    location = /api/file   { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; }
    location = /api/health { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8787; }
}
```

Key points:

- **`Host` must be `$http_host`** (keeps the port) on both `/pi/` and `/ws` —
  the origin check compares hostname **and** port. `proxy_set_header Host $host`
  or leaving it unset (defaults to the upstream `127.0.0.1:8787`) both fail with 403.
- **Same-origin works automatically**: as long as the browser's `Origin` equals
  the forwarded `Host` (it does through a plain proxy), no
  `PI_WEB_ALLOW_ORIGINS` is needed. Only set it when the browser origin differs
  from the Host the server sees (e.g. a TLS-terminating proxy that changes the
  port).
- **No `proxy_protocol` unless you really need real client IPs**: it makes
  nginx reject every connection that does not send a PROXY header, which
  breaks direct LAN access and any non-frp clients. With frp, drop
  `transport.proxyProtocolVersion` from the proxy config unless nginx listens
  with `proxy_protocol` too.
- **LAN access without a proxy**: just set `PI_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0` (and a
  firewall rule) — or put the whole server block above on port 80/443.

Full working example (with an frp tunnel): `deploy/nginx-subpath.conf`.


## Contribute

pi-web-ui is a small open-source project — **your contributions are what make it grow**. Code, plugins, themes, docs, translations, ideas: everything is welcome, and every merged PR ships to all users with the next `npm publish`. ❤️

| Way to contribute | How to get started |
| --- | --- |
| 🧩 **Write a plugin** | Build your own UI tab + agent tools. Copy `dev/plugins/demo-mailbox` as the minimal template (it doubles as the test fixture), develop locally, then either open a PR to ship it in the [catalog](#plugin-catalog) or [publish it standalone](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/tree/main/dev/plugins). |
| 🎨 **Contribute a theme** | Copy `themes/white.css` (light) or `themes/cyberpunk.css` (dark) as a pure-palette template, tweak the `:root` palette + `--term-*` + `.hljs`, verify with `npm run dev`, then open a PR — full walkthrough in [Contributing a theme](#contributing-a-theme-to-the-repository-github). |
| 💻 **Fix a bug / add a feature** | Look for [open issues](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/issues) or propose something new. Fork → branch → PR. Keep the code conventions in `AGENTS.md` (tabs, i18n keys in both languages, protocol changes in `server/protocol.ts`). |
| 📖 **Docs & translations** | Improve the READMEs, write plugin docs, fix typos, or help translate the UI / docs into more languages. |
| 💡 **Ideas & feedback** | Open an [issue](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/issues) or start a [discussion](https://github.com/xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui/discussions) — feature requests, bug reports, UI polish ideas, deployment experience reports. |

**Before opening a PR**, a quick sanity pass keeps reviewers happy:

- `npm run check:protocol` + `npm test` — protocol sync and unit tests.
- `npm run typecheck` — no type errors.
- `npm run build` — both frontend and backend compile.
- For protocol changes: add branches in both `server/index.ts` and `web/src/use-chat.ts` (see the "Protocol single source" note in `AGENTS.md`).

> Enjoying pi-web-ui? Give the repo a ⭐ — it helps others find it. And if you
> built something cool on top (plugin, theme, deployment recipe), tell us — we
> love showcasing community work.
