```text
### Topic propagation semantics

- A message’s topic can be changed through the message-edit endpoint; channel messages only.
- `propagate_mode` determines scope:
  - `"change_one"`: only the selected message; this is the default.
  - `"change_later"`: the selected message and subsequent messages.
  - `"change_all"`: every message in the topic.
- Content-only edits must use `"change_one"`.
- Topic resolution is implemented by renaming the topic with a checkmark and using `"change_all"`.
- Moving messages can also change their channel. Separate options control notifications in the former and new topic.

### Permission implications

Topic and channel moves are governed by organization settings, including permissions for resolving topics and moving messages within or between channels. Applicable time limits also restrict non-administrators and non-moderators; the API may reject a move when only part of a topic is eligible.

### Why a topic is not a stable session identity

A topic is mutable routing metadata, not an immutable object identifier. An edit may rename it, move one message, move a suffix, move the entire topic, or relocate messages to another channel. A session keyed only by topic name could therefore point to a different set of messages—or lose track of them—after another authorized edit. Use immutable message or server-issued identifiers for session identity, treating topic and channel as changeable attributes.
```
</details></tool-use>

2:   <img src="https://img.coly.cc/obs-img/2025/10/a3a76006fd9279cc3559b6854f9335fc.png" width="600" alt="piscord">
3: </p>
4: 
5: <h1 align="center">Piscord</h1>
6: 
7: <p align="center">
8:   <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/piscord"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/piscord" alt="npm version"></a>
9:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/l/piscord" alt="license">
10:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/node/v/piscord" alt="node version">
11:   <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-linux%20%7C%20macos%20%7C%20windows-blue" alt="platform">
12: </p>
13: 
14: A lightweight Discord gateway for [pi coding agent](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono). SQLite-backed queue, per-channel session isolation, crash recovery, abort support. One command to set up, runs as a daemon, never drops a message.
15: 
16: **Latest release:** see the npm version badge above and [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md) for details.
17: 
18: ```bash
19: npm install -g piscord
20: piscord setup                 # interactive wizard -- walks you through everything
21: ```
22: 
23: That's it. The setup wizard checks prerequisites, asks for your Discord bot token, lets you pick a channel policy, and optionally installs + starts a background service. Your bot is live in under a minute.
24: 
25: ## Prerequisites
26: 
27: - **Node.js** ≥ 20
28: - **Linux, macOS, or Windows**
29: - **[pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono)** ≥ 0.74.0 installed and on `PATH`, with login completed (`~/.pi/agent/auth.json`)
30: - **Discord bot token** — [create one here](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
31:   - Enable **Message Content Intent** under Privileged Gateway Intents
32:   - Bot permissions: `Send Messages`, `Read Message History`, `View Channels`, `Attach Files`
33: 
34: ## Features
35: 
36: - **Bridges to your existing `pi`** — shells out to the `pi` binary and reuses your login + model access
37: - **Per-channel sessions** — each Discord channel gets its own persistent conversation history
38: - **Per-channel working directories** — optionally override `PI_CWD` for specific channels without changing the global default
39: - **Channel access policy** — `open` (all channels), `open-trigger` (all channels, @mention required), or `allowlist` (manual registration only)
40: - **SQLite message queue** — survives crashes, auto-recovers stuck messages
41: - **Concurrency control** — per-channel serial processing + configurable global limit
42: - **DM auto-registration** — direct messages work out of the box
43: - **Discord slash commands** — `/pi status`, `/pi model`, `/pi thinking`, `/pi new`, `/pi stop`
44: - **Abort command** — `/pi stop` terminates the running task and clears queued messages
45: - **Attachment relay** — Discord file uploads are downloaded and passed to `pi` by local path so agents can inspect or convert any supported file type without flooding context
46: - **Message and file sending** — `piscord send` lets pi send plain text, files, or both to any Discord channel
47: - **Scheduled tasks** — cron or one-time tasks that trigger pi sessions on schedule
48: - **Archive auto-cleanup** — archived sessions are cleaned up after a configurable retention period
49: - **Cross-platform** — runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows with platform-aware defaults
50: - **Typing indicators** — shows "bot is typing" while `pi` processes
51: - **Message splitting** — handles Discord's 2000-character limit automatically
52: - **Daemon management** — systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS
53: - **Platform-aware paths** — XDG on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows
54: 
55: ## How It Works
56: 
57: ```
58: Discord ──discord.js──→ Gateway ──pi subprocess──→ Pi Agent
59:                            │                          │
60:                          SQLite                  Session dirs
61:                       (message queue)           (per channel)
62: ```
63: 
64: The gateway **does not embed or replace `pi`**. It finds and runs your installed `pi`:
65: 
66: 1. **Binary discovery** — uses `PI_BIN` config or finds `pi` in `PATH`
67: 2. **Auth reuse** — `pi` reads its own `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` when invoked
68: 3. **Model catalog** — the gateway imports the pi SDK to populate slash command autocomplete
69: 4. **Invocation** — each message is processed as `pi --session-dir <dir> --continue -p <message>`
70: 
71: ## Channel Policy
72: 
73: During setup you pick one of three policies. This controls how the bot interacts with server channels:
74: 
75: | Policy         | Behavior                                                               |
76: | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
77: | `open`         | All guild channels auto-register on first message. No @mention needed. |
78: | `open-trigger` | All guild channels auto-register, but only respond when @mentioned.    |
79: | `allowlist`    | Only manually registered channels are active.                          |
80: 
81: - DMs always auto-register when `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS=true` (the default).
82: - Use `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS` to block specific channels from auto-registration in `open` / `open-trigger` mode.
83: 
84: If you chose `allowlist`, register channels manually:
85: 
86: ```bash
87: piscord register [REDACTED:discord-client-id] "my-server #general" --no-trigger
88: piscord register [REDACTED:discord-client-id] "my-server #general" --cwd /srv/repos/app
89: ```
90: 
91: Re-running `piscord register` with `--cwd` updates that channel's working directory override. If no override is set, the gateway uses the global `PI_CWD`.
92: 
93: ## Slash Commands
94: 
95: The gateway registers a global `/pi` command on Discord:
96: 
97: | Subcommand        | Description                                                        |
98: | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
99: | `/pi status`      | Show model, thinking, working directory, session info, token usage |
100: | `/pi model`       | Set the channel's model (autocomplete from pi's available models)  |
101: | `/pi reset-model` | Clear the channel's model override                                 |
102: | `/pi thinking`    | Set thinking level: off / minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh    |
103: | `/pi new`         | Start a fresh session for this channel                             |
104: | `/pi stop`        | Abort the current task and clear queued messages                   |
105: 
106: `/pi model` reads the catalog from the configured `PI_BIN`, so it stays in sync when pi adds or removes models. It also honors pi's `enabledModels` setting (configured through `/scoped-models`), including model order and glob patterns. If no scope is configured, it shows all available models.
107: 
108: ## Tools for Pi
109: 
110: The gateway exposes two capabilities through its CLI that **pi itself can invoke**. You don't type these commands in your terminal — you just tell pi in Discord, and it handles the rest.
111: 
112: For example, you can say to pi:
113: 
114: > _"Create a daily task at 9am UTC that generates a summary report"_
115: > _"Send me report.pdf with a message saying here you go"_
116: > _"Set a one-time reminder for the 2pm meeting today"_
117: 
118: pi will run the appropriate `piscord task` or `piscord send` command behind the scenes.
119: 
120: ### Scheduled tasks
121: 
122: pi can schedule cron-based or one-time prompts through the gateway's scheduler. Tasks are injected into the normal message queue, so they use the channel's configured model, thinking level, and working directory.
123: 
124: Under the hood, pi runs commands like:
125: 
126: ```bash
127: piscord task add \
128:   --name "daily-report" \
129:   --schedule "0 9 * * *" \
130:   --channel dc:123456789 \
131:   --prompt "Generate today's summary report"
132: 
133: piscord task add \
134:   --name "meeting-reminder" \
135:   --schedule "2026-04-05T14:00:00Z" \
136:   --channel dc:123456789 \
137:   --prompt "Remind Colin about the 2pm meeting" \
138:   --once
139: ```
140: 
141: The `--schedule` value uses standard 5-field cron syntax (`minute hour day month weekday`). For one-time tasks, add `--once` and pass an ISO 8601 datetime.
142: 
143: **Task management** — also available via pi:
144: 
145: ```bash
146: piscord task list              # List all tasks
147: piscord task disable <id>      # Pause
148: piscord task enable <id>       # Resume
149: piscord task remove <id>       # Delete
150: ```
151: 
152: ### Sending messages and files to Discord
153: 
154: pi can send plain text messages, files, or both to any Discord channel using the gateway's built-in relay.
155: 
156: When you ask pi to send something, it runs commands like:
157: 
158: ```bash
159: piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --text "hello"
160: piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --file /path/to/report.pdf --text "Here's the report"
161: piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --file chart.png --file data.csv
162: ```
163: 
164: - `--text` works on its own
165: - Up to 10 files per message (Discord limit)
166: - Respects `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` per file
167: - Works independently — no running gateway daemon required
168: 
169: ## Daemon Management
170: 
171: The setup wizard offers to install a background service automatically. You can also manage it manually:
172: 
173: ```bash
174: piscord daemon install   # Generate + enable service
175: piscord daemon start     # Start
176: piscord daemon status    # Check status
177: piscord daemon logs      # Tail log output
178: piscord daemon stop      # Stop
179: piscord daemon uninstall # Remove the service
180: ```
181: 
182: - **Linux** — uses a systemd user service
183: - **macOS** — uses a launchd user agent
184: - **Windows** — daemon management is not yet supported; run `piscord start` in a terminal or use Task Scheduler manually
185: 
186: > **Headless Linux servers**: enable user lingering so the service runs without an active login session:
187: >
188: > ```bash
189: > sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER
190: > ```
191: 
192: ## Configuration Reference
193: 
194: Config file location depends on your OS (see Data Locations). On Linux: `~/.config/pi-discord-gateway/config.env`
195: 
196: Most users won't need to edit this file directly — `piscord setup` generates it for you. If you do want to tweak advanced settings, you can edit the file manually, or ask your pi to configure it for you. Run `piscord status` to see the config path on your system.
197: 
198: | Variable                     | Default                         | Description                                                                |
199: | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
200: | `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`          | _(required)_                    | Discord bot token                                                          |
201: | `PI_BIN`                     | `pi`                            | Path to pi binary                                                          |
202: | `PI_MODEL`                   | _(none)_                        | Default model override                                                     |
203: | `PI_THINKING`                | _(none)_                        | Default thinking level                                                     |
204: | `PI_CWD`                     | `$HOME`                         | Default working directory for pi; can be overridden per registered channel |
205: | `PI_EXTRA_FLAGS`             | _(none)_                        | Extra flags passed to pi                                                   |
206: | `TRIGGER_NAME`               | `pi`                            | Bot trigger name for @mentions                                             |
207: | `CHANNEL_POLICY`             | `open`                          | Channel access: `open`, `open-trigger`, or `allowlist`                     |
208: | `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS`          | _(none)_                        | Comma-separated channel IDs to exclude from auto-registration              |
209: | `MAX_CONCURRENCY`            | `3`                             | Max parallel pi invocations                                                |
210: | `MAX_SCHEDULED_CONCURRENCY`  | `1`                             | Max scheduled tasks enqueued per tick                                      |
211: | `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`           | `1000`                          | Queue poll interval (ms)                                                   |
212: | `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS`        | `15000`                         | Graceful shutdown timeout (ms)                                             |
213: | `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS`          | `true`                          | Auto-register DM channels                                                  |
214: | `ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS`     | `30`                            | Days to keep archived sessions (0 = never clean)                           |
215: | `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`       | `26214400`                      | Max size per attachment (0 = no limit)                                     |
216: | `MAX_TOTAL_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` | `52428800`                      | Max combined attachment size (0 = no limit)                                |
217: | `MEDIA_RETENTION_HOURS`      | `168`                           | Hours to keep downloaded attachment files for path-based agent access      |
218: | `SESSIONS_DIR`               | _(platform default)_/sessions   | Session storage directory (see Data Locations)                             |
219: | `DB_PATH`                    | _(platform default)_/gateway.db | SQLite database path (see Data Locations)                                  |
220: | `LOG_LEVEL`                  | `info`                          | Log level: debug/info/warn/error                                           |
221: 
222: After changing config, restart the service: `piscord daemon stop && piscord daemon start`
223: 
224: ## CLI Reference
225: 
226: ```
227: piscord setup [token]                         Interactive setup wizard
228: piscord start                                 Start gateway (foreground)
229: piscord status                                Show diagnostics
230: 
231: piscord channels                              List registered channels
232: piscord register <id> <name> [options]        Register a channel
233: piscord unregister <id>                       Unregister a channel
234: 
235: piscord send --channel <jid> [--text <msg>] [--file <path> ...]
236: 
237: piscord task add --name <n> --schedule <cron|iso> --channel <jid> --prompt <text> [--once]
238: piscord task list | remove <id> | enable <id> | disable <id>
239: 
240: piscord archive list                          List archived sessions
241: piscord archive cleanup [--dry-run]           Clean up expired archived sessions
242: 
243: piscord daemon install | uninstall | start | stop | status | logs
244: 
245: piscord help                                  Show help
246: ```
247: 
248: ### Register options
249: 
250: | Flag              | Effect                                        |
251: | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
252: | `--no-trigger`    | Respond to all messages (not just @mentions)  |
253: | `--main`          | Mark as main channel (implies `--no-trigger`) |
254: | `--folder <name>` | Custom session folder name                    |
255: | `--cwd <path>`    | Override `PI_CWD` for this channel only       |
256: 
257: ## Data Locations
258: 
259: Paths are platform-aware. Defaults by OS:
260: 
261: | Item     | Linux                                       | macOS                                                      | Windows                                     |
262: | -------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
263: | Config   | `~/.config/pi-discord-gateway/config.env`   | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/config.env` | `%APPDATA%\piscord-gateway\config.env`      |
264: | Database | `~/.local/share/piscord-gateway/gateway.db` | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/gateway.db` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\piscord-gateway\gateway.db` |
265: | Sessions | `~/.local/share/piscord-gateway/sessions/`  | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/sessions/`  | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\piscord-gateway\sessions\`  |
266: | pi auth  | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                     | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                                    | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                     |
267: 
268: ## Alternative Installation
269: 
270: ### npx (quick trial, no global install)
271: 
272: ```bash
273: npx piscord@latest setup
274: ```
275: 
276: ### From source
277: 
278: ```bash
279: git clone https://github.com/Crokily/pi-discord-gateway.git
280: cd pi-discord-gateway
281: npm install && npm run build
282: node dist/cli/index.js setup
283: ```
284: 
285: ## Troubleshooting
286: 
287: <details>
288: <summary><strong>pi not found in PATH</strong></summary>
289: 
290: `piscord status` shows "Pi binary: not found".
291: 
292: - Check `pi --version` works in the same shell
293: - Set `PI_BIN=/full/path/to/pi` in config.env
294: - Restart: `piscord daemon stop && piscord daemon start`
295: </details>
296: 
297: <details>
298: <summary><strong>Missing auth.json</strong></summary>
299: 
300: `piscord status` shows "Pi auth: missing".
301: 
302: - Run `pi` and complete the login flow
303: - Confirm `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` exists for the same user running the gateway
304: </details>
305: 
306: <details>
307: <summary><strong>Daemon service won't start</strong></summary>
308: 
309: - `piscord daemon status` — check for errors
310: - `piscord daemon logs` — see log output
311: - **Linux**: for headless servers, run `sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER`
312: - **macOS**: check `~/Library/Logs/piscord-gateway/` for launchd output
313: </details>
314: 
315: <details>
316: <summary><strong>Bot is online but doesn't respond</strong></summary>
317: 
318: - `open` policy: check `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS` doesn't include your channel
319: - `allowlist` policy: run `piscord channels` — at least one channel must be registered
320: - For trigger-only channels: mention the bot by name or use `@TriggerName`
321: - DMs auto-register when `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS=true`
322: </details>
323: 
324: ## Development
325: 
326: ```bash
327: npm install
328: npm run dev          # Start with tsx (no build needed)
329: npm run build        # Compile TypeScript
330: npm test             # Run Vitest suite
331: ```
332: 
333: ## Security
334: 
335: - Protect `config.env` — it contains your Discord bot token
336: - Anyone who can message a registered channel can spend your pi usage
337: - Review attachment size limits before exposing the bot
338: - Run the service as a normal user, not root
339:

25: /** Channels currently being processed (per-channel serial lock) */

29: const activeChannelControllers = new Map<string, AbortController>();

31: let running = false;
32: let pollTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
33: let stopPromise: Promise<void> | null = null;

39: export function abortChannelTask(jid: string): { aborted: boolean; cleared: number } {
40:   const controller = activeChannelControllers.get(jid);
41:   const aborted = Boolean(controller);

49: export function startProcessingLoop(): void {

51: 
52:   running = true;
53:   stopPromise = null;
54: 
55:   // Recover any messages stuck in 'processing' from a previous crash.
56:   const recovered = recoverStuckMessages();

59:   }

64: export function stopProcessingLoop(opts: { timeoutMs?: number } = {}): Promise<void> {
65:   if (stopPromise) {
66:     return stopPromise;

69:   running = false;

76: function schedulePoll(delayMs = config.pollInterval): void {

85: function clearPollTimer(): void {

164:     ]);

172: 
173:   let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;

189: async function processMessage(

206:   const typingLoop = createTypingLoop(jid);

208:   try {

210: 
211:     logMessage(jid, 'user', content);
212: 
213:     const effective = computeEffectiveChannelSettings(channel);
214: 
215:     const result = await invokeAgent(channel.folder, prompt, {
216:       model: effective.rawModelRef || undefined,
217:       thinking: effective.hasManagedThinking ? effective.effectiveThinking : undefined,
218:       cwd: effective.effectiveCwd,
219:       signal,
220:       attachments,
221:     });
222: 
223:     if (signal.aborted) {
224:       markMessageFailed(rowid);
225:       logger.info({ jid, rowid }, 'Message abandoned: shutdown interrupted processing');
226:       return;
227:     }
228: 
229:     if (result.ok) {
230:       const sent = await sendResponse(jid, result.text);
231:       if (!sent) {

234:         return;
235:       }
236: 
237:       logMessage(jid, 'assistant', result.text);
238:       markMessageDone(rowid);
239:       logger.info({ jid, responseLen: result.text.length }, 'Message processed');
240:       return;
241:     }
242: 
243:     const errMsg = `⚠️ Agent error: ${result.error?.slice(0, 300) || 'unknown error'}`;
244:     await sendResponse(jid, errMsg);
245:     markMessageFailed(rowid);
246:     logger.warn({ jid, error: result.error }, 'Agent returned error');
247:   } catch (err: any) {
248:     if (signal.aborted) {
249:       markMessageFailed(rowid);
250:       logger.info({ jid, rowid }, 'Message abandoned: shutdown interrupted processing');
251:       return;

253:

261:   } finally {

266: function createTypingLoop(jid: string): { stop: () => Promise<void> } {
267:   let typingAlive = true;
268:   let cancelTypingDelay = () => {};
269: 
270:   const loop = (async () => {
271:     while (typingAlive) {
272:       await setTyping(jid);
273:       if (!typingAlive) break;
274: 
275:       const delay = cancellableSleep(8000);
276:       cancelTypingDelay = delay.cancel;
277:       await delay.promise;
278:       cancelTypingDelay = () => {};
279:     }
280:   })();
281: 
282:   return {
283:     stop: async () => {
284:       typingAlive = false;
285:       cancelTypingDelay();
286:       await loop;
287:     },
288:   };
289: }
290: 
291: function cancellableSleep(ms: number): { promise: Promise<void>; cancel: () => void } {
292:   let finished = false;
293:   let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
294:   let resolvePromise: () => void = () => {};
295: 
296:   const promise = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
297:     resolvePromise = () => {
298:       if (finished) return;
299:       finished = true;
300:       if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
301:       resolve();
302:     };
303: 
304:     timer = setTimeout(resolvePromise, ms);
305:   });
306: 
307:   return {
308:     promise,
309:     cancel: resolvePromise,
310:   };
311: }

43: export async function invokeAgent(
44:   channelFolder: string,
45:   userText: string,
46:   opts?: {
47:     model?: string;
48:     thinking?: string;
49:     cwd?: string;
50:     signal?: AbortSignal;

58:   // `--session` expects a session *file* path. We want a dedicated directory per
59:   // Discord channel and to keep reusing the most recent session inside it.
60:   const args: string[] = ['--session-dir', sessionDir, '--continue'];
61: 
62:   // Model
63:   const model = opts?.model || config.piModel;
64:   if (model) args.push('--model', model);
65: 
66:   // Thinking
67:   const thinking = opts?.thinking || config.piThinking;
68:   if (thinking) args.push('--thinking', thinking);

70:   // Extra flags
71:   if (config.piExtraFlags) {

73:   }
74: 
75:   let attachmentPrompt = '';

77:   // Download attachments to disk and pass *paths* to the agent instead of using

79:   // request; that is convenient for small text files but unsafe for binary or
80:   // structured files (docx/xlsx/pdf/images) because it can flood the context
81:   // window with raw bytes. Path-based handoff keeps the prompt small and lets
82:   // pi decide which tools/converters to use for each file type.
83:   if (opts?.attachments) {
84:     try {

88:       attachmentPrompt = buildAttachmentPathPrompt(downloaded);

180: export function buildAttachmentPathPrompt(downloaded: DownloadedFile[]): string {

183:   const lines = downloaded.map((file, index) => {

189:       `  size: ${file.size} bytes`,
190:     ].join('\n');
191:   });
192: 
193:   return [
194:     '<attachments>',

196:     'Do not assume their contents are loaded into context. Use tools to inspect or convert these paths when needed.',
197:     ...lines,

202: function readLatestAgentErrorFromSession(channelFolder: string): string | undefined {
203:   const sessionFile = resolveLatestChannelSessionFile(channelFolder);
204:   if (!sessionFile || !existsSync(sessionFile)) return undefined;
205: 
206:   let lines: string[];
207:   try {
208:     lines = readFileSync(sessionFile, 'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/u);
209:   } catch {
210:     return undefined;
211:   }
212: 
213:   for (let index = lines.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
214:     const line = lines[index]?.trim();
215:     if (!line) continue;
216: 
217:     try {
218:       const entry = JSON.parse(line) as {
219:         type?: string;
220:         message?: {
221:           role?: string;
222:           content?: unknown;
223:           stopReason?: string;
224:           errorMessage?: string;
225:         };
226:       };
227: 
228:       if (entry.type !== 'message' || entry.message?.role !== 'assistant') continue;
229: 
230:       if (entry.message.errorMessage) {
231:         return summarizeAgentError(entry.message.errorMessage);
232:       }
233: 
234:       if (entry.message.stopReason === 'error') {
235:         return 'pi stopped with an error but did not record an error message';
236:       }
237: 
238:       // The newest assistant message was not an error; older errors are not the
239:       // cause of the empty stdout for this invocation.
240:       return undefined;
241:     } catch {
242:       // Ignore incomplete or malformed trailing JSONL lines.
243:     }
244:   }
245: 
246:   return undefined;
247: }
248: 
249: function summarizeAgentError(errorMessage: string): string {
250:   const codexJson = errorMessage.match(/Codex error:\s*(\{.*\})/su)?.[1];
251:   if (codexJson) {
252:     try {
253:       const parsed = JSON.parse(codexJson) as {
254:         error?: { type?: string; code?: string; message?: string };
255:       };
256:       const error = parsed.error;
257:       if (error?.message) {
258:         const code = error.code || error.type;
259:         return code ? `${code}: ${error.message}` : error.message;
260:       }
261:     } catch {
262:       // Fall back to the original error message below.
263:     }
264:   }
265: 
266:   return errorMessage;
267: }

304: interface RpcSessionStatsResponse {
305:   type: 'response';
306:   command: 'get_session_stats';
307:   success: boolean;
308:   data?: {
309:     tokens?: {
310:       input?: number;
311:       output?: number;
312:       cacheRead?: number;
313:       cacheWrite?: number;
314:       total?: number;
315:     };
316:     contextUsage?: {
317:       tokens?: number | null;
318:       contextWindow?: number | null;
319:       percent?: number | null;
320:     };
321:   };
322:   error?: string;
323: }
324: 
325: async function getSessionStatsViaRpc(
326:   sessionFile: string,
327:   cwd: string,
328: ): Promise<{ tokens: SessionTokenUsage; contextUsage?: SessionContextUsage }> {
329:   const args = ['--mode', 'rpc', '--session', sessionFile];
330:   const { bin: rpcBin, args: rpcArgs } = resolvePiSpawn(config.piBin, args);
331: 
332:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
333:     const proc = spawn(rpcBin, rpcArgs, {
334:       cwd,
335:       env: process.env,
336:       stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
337:     });
338: 
339:     const errChunks: Buffer[] = [];
340:     let stdout = '';
341:     let response: RpcSessionStatsResponse | undefined;
342:     let finished = false;
343: 
344:     const finish = (err?: Error) => {
345:       if (finished) return;
346:       finished = true;
347:       clearTimeout(timeout);
348:       if (err) {
349:         reject(err);
350:         return;
351:       }
352: 
353:       if (!response?.success || !response.data?.tokens) {
354:         reject(new Error(response?.error || 'pi did not return session stats'));
355:         return;
356:       }
357: 
358:       resolve({
359:         tokens: {
360:           input: toNumber(response.data.tokens.input),
361:           output: toNumber(response.data.tokens.output),
362:           cacheRead: toNumber(response.data.tokens.cacheRead),
363:           cacheWrite: toNumber(response.data.tokens.cacheWrite),
364:           total: toNumber(response.data.tokens.total),
365:         },
366:         contextUsage: response.data.contextUsage
367:           ? {
368:               tokens: toNullableNumber(response.data.contextUsage.tokens),
369:               contextWindow: toNullableNumber(response.data.contextUsage.contextWindow),
370:               percent: toNullableNumber(response.data.contextUsage.percent),
371:             }
372:           : undefined,
373:       });
374:     };
375: 
376:     const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
377:       if (process.platform === 'win32') {
378:         proc.kill();
379:       } else {
380:         proc.kill('SIGTERM');
381:         setTimeout(() => proc.kill('SIGKILL'), 1000);
382:       }
383:       finish(new Error('Timed out waiting for pi session stats'));
384:     }, 2500);
385: 
386:     proc.stdout.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
387:       stdout += chunk.toString('utf-8');
388: 
389:       let newlineIndex = stdout.indexOf('\n');
390:       while (newlineIndex !== -1) {
391:         const line = stdout.slice(0, newlineIndex).replace(/\r$/, '').trim();
392:         stdout = stdout.slice(newlineIndex + 1);
393: 
394:         if (line) {
395:           try {
396:             const message = JSON.parse(line) as RpcSessionStatsResponse | { type?: string };
397:             if (
398:               message.type === 'response' &&
399:               (message as RpcSessionStatsResponse).command === 'get_session_stats'
400:             ) {
401:               response = message as RpcSessionStatsResponse;
402:             }
403:           } catch {
404:             // Ignore non-JSON or partial lines from stdout.
405:           }
406:         }
407: 
408:         newlineIndex = stdout.indexOf('\n');
409:       }
410:     });
411: 
412:     proc.stderr.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => errChunks.push(chunk));
413:     proc.on('error', (err) => finish(err));
414:     proc.on('close', (code) => {
415:       const trailingLine = stdout.trim();
416:       if (trailingLine) {
417:         try {
418:           const message = JSON.parse(trailingLine) as RpcSessionStatsResponse | { type?: string };
419:           if (
420:             message.type === 'response' &&
421:             (message as RpcSessionStatsResponse).command === 'get_session_stats'
422:           ) {
423:             response = message as RpcSessionStatsResponse;
424:           }
425:         } catch {
426:           // Ignore malformed trailing output on shutdown.
427:         }
428:       }
429: 
430:       if (code !== 0) {
431:         const stderr = Buffer.concat(errChunks).toString('utf-8').trim();
432:         finish(new Error(stderr || `pi exited with code ${code}`));
433:         return;
434:       }
435: 
436:       finish();
437:     });
438: 
439:     proc.stdin.end('{"type":"get_session_stats"}\n');
440:   });
441: }

443: function readSessionTokensFromJsonl(sessionFile: string): SessionTokenUsage {
444:   const totals: SessionTokenUsage = { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0, total: 0 };
445:   const lines = readFileSync(sessionFile, 'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/u);
446: 
447:   for (const line of lines) {
448:     const trimmed = line.trim();
449:     if (!trimmed) continue;
450: 
451:     try {
452:       const entry = JSON.parse(trimmed) as {
453:         type?: string;
454:         message?: {
455:           role?: string;
456:           usage?: {
457:             input?: number;
458:             output?: number;
459:             cacheRead?: number;
460:             cacheWrite?: number;
461:             totalTokens?: number;
462:           };
463:         };
464:       };
465: 
466:       if (entry.type !== 'message' || entry.message?.role !== 'assistant' || !entry.message.usage) {
467:         continue;
468:       }
469: 
470:       const input = toNumber(entry.message.usage.input);
471:       const output = toNumber(entry.message.usage.output);
472:       const cacheRead = toNumber(entry.message.usage.cacheRead);
473:       const cacheWrite = toNumber(entry.message.usage.cacheWrite);
474: 
475:       totals.input += input;
476:       totals.output += output;
477:       totals.cacheRead += cacheRead;
478:       totals.cacheWrite += cacheWrite;
479:       totals.total +=
480:         toNumber(entry.message.usage.totalTokens) || input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite;
481:     } catch {
482:       // Ignore incomplete or malformed trailing JSONL lines.
483:     }
484:   }
485: 
486:   return totals;
487: }
488: 
489: function toNumber(value: number | undefined): number {
490:   return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0;
491: }
492: 
493: function toNullableNumber(value: number | null | undefined): number | null {
494:   return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null;
495: }
```
</details></tool-use>

Import via a supported subpath export if one is added","comments":[],"state":"OPEN","title":"bug: AuthStorage not exported from @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.84.x → piscord setup crashes"}
{"body":"## Bug\n\nOn `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` >= 0.83, every processed Discord message fails with:\n\n```\n{\"level\":50,...,\"err\":\"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getAvailableSnapshot')\",\"msg\":\"processMessage failed\"}\n```\n\nThe bot still sends an `⚠️ Internal error: ...` reply to Discord for each message.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`src/agent/model-catalog.ts` constructs the model registry like this:\n\n```ts\nfunction createModelRegistry(authStorage: AuthStorage): ModelRegistry {\n  const registryClass = ModelRegistry as unknown as {\n    create?: (authStorage: AuthStorage) => ModelRegistry;\n    new (authStorage: AuthStorage): ModelRegistry;\n  };\n  if (typeof registryClass.create === 'function') {\n    return registryClass.create(authStorage);\n  }\n  return new registryClass(authStorage);\n}\n```\n\npi-coding-agent 0.83 made two breaking changes that both break this path:\n\n1. **`ModelRegistry.create()` was removed.** The `ModelRegistry` constructor now takes a `ModelRuntime` (not an `AuthStorage`). So `new ModelRegistry(authStorage)` sets `this.runtime = undefined`, and the very next call `registry.getAvailable()` -> `this.runtime.getAvailableSnapshot()` throws the error above.\n2. **`AuthStorage` is no longer exported** from the package root (only `readStoredCredential` is). So `import { AuthStorage } from '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'` now throws a `SyntaxError` at module load — meaning a fresh process restart fails even earlier than the `getAvailableSnapshot` error (the currently-running error is from a process that still has the old, pre-upgrade modules cached in memory).\n\nA secondary issue: `loadModelCatalog` calls `registry.refresh()` fire-and-forget. With the new runtime, `ModelRuntime.refresh()` reloads config, rebuilds providers, and runs availability/auth checks against every provider (network calls). `ModelRuntime.create()` already does an initial refresh, so this is redundant, wasteful on a 30s cache TTL per cwd, and any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection.\n\n## Why CI didn't catch it\n\n`test/model-catalog.test.ts` mocks `vi.spyOn(ModelRegistry, 'create')` and `vi.spyOn(AuthStorage, 'create')`, so the tests exercise neither the real construction path nor the real exports.\n\n## Environment\n\n- piscord 1.7.0\n- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 0.83.0\n- Node v25.x\n\nI have a fix incoming in a linked PR.","comments":[],"state":"OPEN","title":"processMessage fails with \"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getAvailableSnapshot')\" on pi-coding-agent 0.83"}

Platform semantics confirm why a portable gateway cannot infer “the conversation” from a display surface: Slack threads use `thread_ts`; Telegram has topic IDs but no generic deletion event; Zulip topics are mutable and can move one message, a suffix, or an entire topic; Matrix models replies, threads, edits, reactions, and redactions as relations over immutable event IDs. The canonical gateway key therefore needs immutable provider/account/space/conversation/subconversation IDs, while names and topic titles remain mutable labels.

```text
## Discord thread/forum-post semantics

- **Channel identity:** A thread is represented as a channel object. Its `id` identifies the thread; `type` distinguishes public, announcement, private, or thread-only-channel posts. `guild_id` identifies the server, while `parent_id` identifies the containing text, announcement, forum, or media channel. `owner_id` identifies the creator.
- **Thread IDs:** A public thread started from a message uses the same ID as that starter message. In forum and media channels, creating a post also creates a message with the thread’s ID.
- **Parent and archive behavior:** Public threads inherit visibility from their parent. Private threads require explicit membership or `MANAGE_THREADS`. Threads may be active or archived; archived threads generally cannot be edited, joined, reacted to, or used for commands. Sending a message normally reactivates one unless it is locked. Locked threads require `MANAGE_THREADS` for moderator-restricted changes.
- **Message routing:** Thread activity is associated with the thread channel ID rather than the parent. Webhooks target a thread through the `thread_id` query parameter. Forum and media channels accept posts/threads only, not direct messages.
- **Gateway availability:** Threads require API v9 or newer for normal thread-related gateway behavior. API v8 clients may miss thread activity and messages occurring within threads. Gateway synchronization covers visible active threads, not archived threads initially. Newly accessible threads may arrive through `THREAD_CREATE` or `THREAD_LIST_SYNC`; losing channel access does not necessarily produce `THREAD_DELETE`.
- **Subscription caveat:** Gateway thread synchronization depends on guild subscription state. Official clients subscribe when a user visits a guild channel; apps are automatically subscribed to thread events and active threads after connecting.
- **Membership mapping:** Membership is explicit and keyed by thread ID plus user ID, with join time and flags. Current-user membership changes arrive through thread-member events; membership data for other users requires the `GUILD_MEMBERS` intent and the thread-member listing endpoint. For session mapping, retain `guild_id`, `parent_id`, thread `id`, visibility/type, archive/lock state, and relevant member status.
```
</details></tool-use>

### Gateway-relevant Message semantics

- `id` and `channel_id` are snowflakes identifying the message and its channel. The supplied text does not explicitly state that either value is immutable.
- Gateway `MESSAGE_CREATE` and `MESSAGE_UPDATE` may omit or blank content-bearing data when the app lacks the required message-content access. Specifically, content, embeds, attachments, and components can be empty; polls may be absent.
- `author` is “not guaranteed to be a valid user”; webhook-generated messages use webhook identity data and include `webhook_id`.
- `edited_timestamp` is null for messages never edited; otherwise it records the edit time.
- `message_reference` identifies related messages or channels. Replies use reference type `0`; forwards use type `1`.
- For replies, `referenced_message` may contain the resolved message. Its absence means resolution was not attempted or is unknown; null means the referenced message was deleted. This field applies only to message types 19, 21, and 23.
- Forwarding uses `message_snapshots`, containing a minimal copy of the source message. Snapshots are immutable, currently limited to one, and exclude the author. Supported fields include content, embeds, attachments, timestamps, flags, mentions, stickers, and components.
- Attachments include stable attachment IDs, metadata, URLs, dimensions where applicable, and optional duration or waveform data. When editing, each retained attachment must be listed by ID; description and spoiler state may be updated.
- Reactions are optional. Each entry reports total, normal, and burst counts, the emoji, and whether the current user reacted normally or with a burst reaction.
- Voice messages cannot be edited and permit only one audio attachment. Message deletability depends on message type; some system types are non-deletable, and auto-moderation messages require `MANAGE_MESSAGES`.
- Partial objects are expected: message snapshots are explicitly partial, webhook authors are identity representations rather than ordinary users, and some fields depend on intents or message type.
```
</details></tool-use>

## Delivery and recovery

- Gateway payloads include `op`, `d`, `s`, and `t`. The sequence number `s` is present for dispatch events (`op: 0`) and otherwise null.
- Store the latest received dispatch sequence. Heartbeats send that value, or `null` before any dispatch has arrived.
- To recover a disconnected session, send Resume with:
  - the authentication token,
  - the session ID,
  - the last received sequence number.
- Ready supplies the session ID and a gateway URL intended for resuming. Resumed confirms successful recovery.
- Reconnect instructs the client to reconnect and resume when possible.
- Invalid Session includes a boolean indicating whether the existing session can be resumed. If it cannot, the client must establish a new session.

The supplied material does **not** define guarantees about duplicate events, out-of-order delivery, or events being dropped. Therefore, it provides no authoritative basis for assuming exactly-once delivery, ordering, or automatic replay beyond the documented resume mechanism.

## Message events

- `MESSAGE_CREATE` delivers a newly created message, including optional guild context, member information, mentions, and channel type.
- `MESSAGE_UPDATE` delivers an updated message using the same additional fields as creation. Updates are partial message objects in the general sense of event updates; the excerpt specifically notes that `tts` is always false in updates.
- `MESSAGE_DELETE` contains the message ID, channel ID, and optional guild ID.
- The excerpt lists `MESSAGE_DELETE_BULK`, but does not provide its full semantics beyond identifying multiple deleted message IDs and their channel/guild context.
- The `MESSAGE_CONTENT` intent may affect whether message content is available; the supplied excerpt explicitly documents this requirement for auto-moderation content, but does not provide the complete message-content rules.

## Reactions

The receive-event index lists:

- `MESSAGE_REACTION_ADD`
- `MESSAGE_REACTION_REMOVE`
- `MESSAGE_REACTION_REMOVE_ALL`
- `MESSAGE_REACTION_REMOVE_EMOJI`

The supplied excerpt gives no field definitions, intent requirements, ordering rules, or recovery behavior for these events.

## Thread events

- `THREAD_CREATE` indicates a relevant new thread or that the current user was added to one. It may include `newly_created`; joining an existing private thread may include a thread-member object.
- `THREAD_UPDATE` carries a channel object. Changes to `last_message_id` are not reported through this event; track those through `MESSAGE_CREATE`.
- `THREAD_DELETE` contains only a subset of channel data: `id`, `guild_id`, `parent_id`, and `type`.
- `THREAD_LIST_SYNC` supplies active accessible threads, associated thread members, and parent-channel scope. Its `channel_ids` field may be absent, meaning guild-wide synchronization, and may include channels with no active threads so local state can be cleared.
- `THREAD_MEMBER_UPDATE` concerns the current user's thread membership and adds `guild_id`.
- `THREAD_MEMBERS_UPDATE` reports additions/removals, with member details for additions. Without the `GUILD_MEMBERS` intent, it is limited to changes involving the current user.

## Partial and changing payloads

- The documentation warns that undocumented fields are unsupported and may change.
- Some events intentionally carry partial resource objects, such as thread deletion and guild-unavailability notifications.
- Message-related guild/member fields can be absent for ephemeral messages, direct contexts, or webhook-authored messages.
- Channel updates may refer to roles or members that have already been removed, so consumers should not assume every referenced object remains resolvable.
- The excerpt does not identify any event as explicitly droppable. It only documents reconnection and session resumption as the recovery path.
```

Piscord’s operational strengths are real but narrower than its “never drops” slogan: SQLite provides durable pending work, per-channel serialization, global concurrency, and restart recovery; however, recovery is at-least-once without ingress/output dedup, so a crash after Discord send but before commit can duplicate, while send failure marks the item failed rather than retrying. It maps whole channels—not threads—to sessions, gives no user/role/guild allowlist, auto-registers every DM by default, inherits the full daemon environment, and has no sandbox or approval gate. Most decisively, v1.7.0 is confirmed broken on Pi 0.84.x (`AuthStorage` import crash) and on 0.83 processing (`ModelRegistry` API change).

```text
1: # Pi Discord Remote
2: 
3: A Pi extension that bridges your Pi coding sessions to Discord. Every project gets its own channel, every session gets its own thread — monitor, steer, and control Pi from Discord in real time.
4: 
5: ## Features
6: 
7: - **Per-project channels** — a dedicated Discord channel is created for each project (named after the working directory), keeping your server organized
8: - **Session threads** — each Pi session spawns a thread inside the project channel with a short, readable slug (`pi-a1b2c`)
9: - **Global config** — set your `.env` once in `~/.pi/.env`, works across all projects
10: - **Two-way control** — send messages in Discord to steer Pi, or react with 🛑 to abort
11: - **Tool call streaming** — optionally watch tool calls and results arrive live in Discord
12: - **Slash commands** — register bridge commands as native Discord slash commands
13: 
14: ## Prerequisites
15: 
16: - [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi)
17: - A [Discord bot](https://discord.com/developers/applications) in your server with these permissions:
18:   - Send Messages
19:   - Read Message History
20:   - Create Public Threads
21:   - Manage Threads
22:   - Add Reactions
23:   - Manage Channels *(needed for per-project channel creation)*
24: 
25: ## Installation
26: 
27: ### npm (recommended)
28: 
29: Inside Pi, run:
30: 
31: ```
32: /pi-install npm:pi-discord-bridge
33: ```
34: 
35: Or manually add to `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:
36: 
37: ```json
38: {
39:   "packages": [
40:     "npm:pi-discord-bridge"
41:   ]
42: }
43: ```
44: 
45: ### Local (from source)
46: 
47: ```bash
48: cp -r pi-discord-bridge ~/.pi/agent/extensions/discord-bridge
49: cd ~/.pi/agent/extensions/discord-bridge && npm install
50: ```
51: 
52: Then use `"ext:discord-bridge"` in settings.json instead.
53: 
54: ### Config
55: 
56: Either way, set up your environment:
57: 
58: ```bash
59: cp .env.example ~/.pi/.env
60: # Edit ~/.pi/.env with your bot token, channel IDs, etc.
61: ```
62: 
63: Restart Pi.
64: 
65: ## Configuration
66: 
67: All settings go in `~/.pi/.env`. See [`.env.example`](.env.example) for the full list.
68: 
69: | Variable | Default | Description |
70: | --- | --- | --- |
71: | `PI_DISCORD_ENABLED` | `false` | Master switch |
72: | `PI_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` | — | Discord bot token |
73: | `PI_DISCORD_USER_IDS` | — | Allowed Discord user IDs (comma-separated) |
74: | `PI_DISCORD_CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT` | `true` | `true` = auto-create a channel per project (requires `PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID`); `false` = send everything to `PI_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` |
75: | `PI_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` | — | Target channel when `CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT=false` |
76: | `PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID` | — | Guild for per-project channel creation (required when toggle is `true`) |
77: | `PI_DISCORD_STREAM_MESSAGES` | `false` | Live-edit messages as the assistant streams |
78: | `PI_DISCORD_CREATE_THREAD_PER_SESSION` | `true` | One thread per Pi session |
79: | `PI_DISCORD_THREAD_NAME_PREFIX` | `pi` | Thread name prefix |
80: | `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_CALLS` | `true` | Show tool calls in Discord |
81: | `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_RESULTS` | `true` | Show tool results in Discord |
82: | `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_USER_INPUT` | `true` | Echo user messages to Discord |
83: | `PI_DISCORD_RENDER_REASONING` | `false` | Show chain-of-thought |
84: 
85: ## How it works
86: 
87: ```
88: Server
89: ├── #general              (your existing channel)
90: ├── #my-app               (auto-created for ~/projects/my-app)
91: │   ├── pi-a1b2c          (session thread)
92: │   └── pi-f3d4e          (another session thread)
93: └── #api-server           (auto-created for ~/projects/api-server)
94:     └── pi-b7c8d          (session thread)
95: ```
96: 
97: Each time you start Pi in a project directory, the extension:
98: 
99: 1. Creates (or reuses) a text channel named after the project directory
100: 2. Creates a session thread with a 5-character slug inside that channel
101: 3. Sends all assistant messages, tool calls, and results to that thread
102: 
103: ## Discord commands
104: 
105: | Command | Description |
106: | --- | --- |
107: | `/session` | Current session and thread info |
108: | `/abort` | Abort the current turn (or react 🛑) |
109: | `/compact` | Trigger context compaction |
110: | `/new [args]` | Start a new Pi session |
111: | `/mute` / `/unmute` | Suppress/resume Discord output |
112: | `/discord-status` | Full status and config dump |
113: | `/discord-test [msg]` | Send a test message |
114: | `/discord-reconnect` | Reconnect the bot |
115: 
116: You can also just type naturally — messages are forwarded to Pi as input.
117: 
118: ## Pi commands
119: 
120: | Command | Description |
121: | --- | --- |
122: | `/discord-status` | Connection status, channels, config |
123: | `/discord-test [msg]` | Send a test message |
124: | `/discord-reconnect` | Reconnect the bot |
125: | `/discord-mute` / `/discord-unmute` | Mute/unmute Discord output |
126: | `/discord-arm` | Arm in-process session replacement |
127: | `/discord-launcher-status` | HTTP launcher info |
128:

```text
# ── Required ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable the extension.
PI_DISCORD_ENABLED=true

# Your Discord bot token (from https://discord.com/developers/applications).
PI_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=your-bot-token-here

# Comma-separated list of Discord user IDs allowed to control Pi.
PI_DISCORD_USER_IDS=your-user-id-here

# ── Channel mode ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Two mutually exclusive modes:
#
#   per-project (default)  — bot creates a dedicated channel for every
#                             project directory inside the configured guild.
#                             Requires PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID.
#
#   single-channel          — bot sends everything to one static channel.
#                             Requires PI_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID.

# Toggle between per-project channel creation (true) or single-channel mode (false).
PI_DISCORD_CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT=true

# ── Per-project mode (required when PI_DISCORD_CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT=true)

# Guild (server) ID where per-project channels will be created.
PI_DISCORD_GUILD_ID=your-guild-id-here

# ── Single-channel mode (required when PI_DISCORD_CREATE_CHANNEL_PER_PROJECT=false)

# Discord channel ID the bot should use for all messages.
# PI_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID=your-channel-id-here

# ── Threads ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Create a dedicated thread per Pi session (default: true).
PI_DISCORD_CREATE_THREAD_PER_SESSION=true

# Prefix for thread names. Final name: {prefix}-{5-char-slug}
PI_DISCORD_THREAD_NAME_PREFIX=pi

# Thread auto-archive duration in minutes. Options: 60, 1440 (1 day), 4320 (3 days), 10080 (1 week).
PI_DISCORD_THREAD_AUTO_ARCHIVE_MINUTES=10080

# ── Streaming ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable live message streaming (edits messages as the assistant generates).
# Default: false (sends one message per response).
PI_DISCORD_STREAM_MESSAGES=false

# ── Rendering ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Show user input in Discord (default: true).
PI_DISCORD_RENDER_USER_INPUT=true

# Show tool calls in Discord (default: true).
PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_CALLS=true

# Show tool results in Discord (default: true).
PI_DISCORD_RENDER_TOOL_RESULTS=true

# Show chain-of-thought / reasoning in Discord (default: false).
PI_DISCORD_RENDER_REASONING=false

# ── Formatting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Interval between stream edits in ms (only when streaming is enabled).
PI_DISCORD_EDIT_INTERVAL_MS=1100

# Interval between new message sends in ms.
PI_DISCORD_CREATE_INTERVAL_MS=600

# Max characters per message (Discord limit is 2000, we use 1990 to be safe).
PI_DISCORD_MAX_CHARS=1900

# Max characters for tool argument summaries.
PI_DISCORD_TOOL_ARGS_MAX_CHARS=800

# Max characters for tool result summaries.
PI_DISCORD_TOOL_RESULT_MAX_CHARS=1000

# Optional prefix prepended to every Discord message.
PI_DISCORD_PREFIX=

# Label shown when messages arrive from Discord, e.g. "[discord]".
PI_DISCORD_STEER_LABEL=[discord]

# ── Slash commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Register bridge commands as guild-scoped slash commands.
PI_DISCORD_REGISTER_SLASH_COMMANDS=false
PI_DISCORD_SLASH_COMMAND_GUILD_IDS=your-guild-id-here

# ── Session launcher (HTTP server) ────────────────────────────────────────

# Enable the /new-session HTTP endpoint.
PI_DISCORD_LAUNCHER_ENABLED=false

# Port for the launcher server.
PI_DISCORD_LAUNCHER_PORT=8765

# Secret to restrict /new-session access. Leave empty for no auth.
PI_DISCORD_LAUNCHER_SECRET=

# Command and args used to spawn new Pi sessions.
PI_DISCORD_SPAWN_COMMAND=pi
PI_DISCORD_SPAWN_ARGS=

# ── Overrides ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Path to a custom .env file. Default: ~/.pi/.env
# PI_DISCORD_ENV_FILE=/path/to/custom/.env

112386	/**

112388	 */
112389	export function loadConfig(): MsgBridgeConfig {
112390	  const config: MsgBridgeConfig = {};
112391	
112392	  if (fs.existsSync(CONFIG_PATH)) {
112393	    try {
112394	      const stats = fs.statSync(CONFIG_PATH);
112395	      const mode = stats.mode & 0o777;
112396	      if ((mode & 0o077) !== 0) {
112397	        console.warn(`⚠️  Config file ${CONFIG_PATH} has insecure permissions (${mode.toString(8)}). Should be 0600.`);
112398	      }
112399	
112400	      const fileConfig = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(CONFIG_PATH, "utf-8"));
112401	      Object.assign(config, fileConfig);
112402	    } catch (err) {
112403	      console.error("Failed to load config file:", err);
112404	    }
112405	  }
112406	
112407	  // Environment variables override file config (higher priority)
112408	  if (process.env.PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN) {
112409	    config.telegram = { token: process.env.PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN };
112410	  }
112411	  if (process.env.PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH) {
112412	    config.whatsapp = { authPath: process.env.PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH };
112413	  }
112414	  if (process.env.PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN && process.env.PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN) {
112415	    config.slack = {
112416	      botToken: process.env.PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN,
112417	      appToken: process.env.PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN,
112418	    };
112419	  }
112420	  if (process.env.PI_DISCORD_TOKEN) {
112421	    config.discord = { token: process.env.PI_DISCORD_TOKEN };
112422	  }
112423	  if (process.env.PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER && process.env.PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN) {
112424	    config.matrix = {
112425	      homeserverUrl: process.env.PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER,
112426	      accessToken: process.env.PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN,
112427	    };
112428	  }
112429	
112430	  return config;
112431	}

112433	/**
112434	 * Save config to file with secure permissions.
112435	 */
112436	export function saveConfig(config: MsgBridgeConfig): void {
112437	  if (!fs.existsSync(CONFIG_DIR)) {
112438	    fs.mkdirSync(CONFIG_DIR, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
112439	  }
112440	  fs.writeFileSync(CONFIG_PATH, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });
112441	  try {
112442	    fs.chmodSync(CONFIG_DIR, 0o700);
112443	  } catch (err) {
112444	    console.warn("Failed to set directory permissions:", err);
112445	  }
112446	}

112676	# Changelog
112677	
112678	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
112679	
112680	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
112681	and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
112682	
112683	## [Unreleased]
112684	
112685	## [0.4.0] - 2026-05-09
112686	
112687	### Added
112688	- Matrix transport via `matrix-bot-sdk` — works with Element X, Element Web, FluffyChat, any Matrix client. Auto-joins rooms, group chat support with mention detection, optional E2EE (Rust SDK crypto store). Set `"encryption": false` in the `matrix` config to disable E2EE (thanks @jchidley)
112689	- `hideToolCalls` config option, `/msg-bridge toggletools` pi command, and matching `/toggletools` DM admin command — trusted users can hide/show tool call summaries in their replies from either side
112690	- Empty-message guard in all transports (Discord, Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Matrix) to prevent provider errors on whitespace-only payloads
112691	
112692	### Changed
112693	- Tool call summaries now wrap the tool name in inline-code backticks (`🔧 \`hud_canvas\` (...)`), rendering as code across all 5 transports and avoiding Telegram's underscore-escape backslashes leaking into messages
112694	- Migrated peer dependencies from deprecated `@mariozechner/pi-{ai,coding-agent,tui}` to `@earendil-works/pi-{ai,coding-agent,tui}` (>=0.74). The `@mariozechner` packages were deprecated upstream with the message "please use @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent instead going forward"
112695	- Tightened peer constraints from `*` to `>=0.74` and removed the duplicated entries from devDependencies (npm auto-installs peers in dev)
112696	- Bumped devDependency floors: `@biomejs/biome` ^2.4.14, `@types/node` ^25.6.2, `typescript` ^6.0.3, `vitest` ^4.1.5
112697	
112698	### Fixed
112699	- `sendUserMessage` crash when a remote message arrives mid-turn — messages are now queued via `{ deliverAs: "followUp" }` so each remote message gets its own turn after the current one finishes, instead of being interleaved into it (fixes #10)
112700	- `pendingRemoteChat` no longer cleared on tool-call-only turns, so the next response reaches the right chat
112701	- Whitespace-only assistant responses no longer trigger Discord's "Cannot send an empty message" error
112702	- Telegram MarkdownV1 parse errors on stray special chars (e.g. snake_case tool names like `hud_canvas` triggering `400 Bad Request: can't parse entities`). `formatForTelegram` now lifts valid markdown patterns into sentinel placeholders, escapes literal `_*[\``, then restores
112703	
112704	## [0.3.0] - 2026-03-25
112705	
112706	### Added
112707	- Interactive menu (`/msg-bridge` with no args) — configure, connect, widget, help via `ui.select()`
112708	- Single-instance connection guard to prevent duplicate polling / 409 conflicts (fixes #2)
112709	  - Layer 1: global flag for same-process re-entrant calls (sub-agents)
112710	  - Layer 2: PID lock file (`~/.pi/msg-bridge.lock`) for cross-process duplicates
112711	- Session shutdown handler — releases lock and disconnects transports on exit
112712	- Lock check on `/msg-bridge configure` connect calls to prevent bypassing the guard
112713	- Test suite (vitest): config, lock, and formatting modules
112714	- CI workflow (GitHub Actions: lint + typecheck + test)
112715	- Biome linter configuration
112716	
112717	### Fixed
112718	- Discord DM messages not received — added required `Partials.Channel` and `Partials.Message` to client options (fixes #5, thanks @chr15m)
112719	- Transport errors now show clean messages instead of full stack traces
112720	
112721	### Changed
112722	- Extracted `config.ts`, `lock.ts`, `formatting.ts`, `ui/main-menu.ts` from index.ts
112723	- Moved `@mariozechner/pi-*` packages to peerDependencies
112724	- Updated devDependencies: typescript ^6.0.2, @types/node ^25.3.0, @biomejs/biome ^2.4.8, vitest ^4.1.1
112725	- `prepublishOnly` now runs lint and typecheck before build
112726	- Applied `npm audit fix` for transitive dependency vulnerabilities
112727	
112728	## [0.2.1] - 2026-02-11
112729	
112730	### Changed
112731	- Package renamed from `pi-msg-bridge` to `pi-messenger-bridge` for better clarity
112732	- Updated all repository URLs and documentation to reflect new package name
112733	- Command remains `/msg-bridge` for brevity and ease of use
112734	
112735	## [0.2.0] - 2026-02-11
112736	
112737	### Added
112738	- WhatsApp integration via Baileys library with QR code authentication
112739	- Slack integration with Socket Mode support
112740	- Discord integration with Message Content intent support
112741	- Debug mode for troubleshooting (config.debug or MSG_BRIDGE_DEBUG env var)
112742	- Non-blocking async transport initialization for faster startup
112743	- Widget toggle command (`/msg-bridge widget`)
112744	- Help command with full command reference
112745	- Automatic invalid session cleanup (WhatsApp 401 handling)
112746	- Session detection to prevent QR spam on startup
112747	
112748	### Changed
112749	- Renamed from "remote-pilot" to "msg-bridge" throughout codebase
112750	- Command changed from `/remote` to `/msg-bridge`
112751	- Config file moved from `~/.pi/msg-bridge/config.json` to `~/.pi/msg-bridge.json`
112752	- WhatsApp auth directory: `~/.pi/msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth/`
112753	- All debug output now behind debug flag (no spam by default)
112754	- Status widget only shows connected transports
112755	- Environment variables now override config file settings
112756	
112757	### Security
112758	- Config file permissions enforced: chmod 600 for files, 700 for directories
112759	- Config directory permissions validated on startup with warnings
112760	- WhatsApp auth directory created with secure permissions (700)
112761	- Invalid WhatsApp sessions automatically cleared on 401 errors
112762	
112763	### Fixed
112764	- QR code display for WhatsApp (using qrcode-terminal instead of Baileys built-in)
112765	- Tool call formatting now shows actual parameters instead of speculation
112766	- Username extraction from WhatsApp messages
112767	- Connection state tracking for accurate widget display
112768	- Startup performance (transports load in background)
112769	
112770	### Dependencies
112771	- Added: @whiskeysockets/baileys, qrcode-terminal, @slack/bolt, discord.js
112772	- Known vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies (node-telegram-bot-api, discord.js) - low impact for this use case
112773	
112774	## [0.1.0] - 2026-02-10
112775	
112776	### Added
112777	- Initial MVP release
112778	- Event-driven architecture using `pi.sendUserMessage()` and `turn_end` events
112779	- Telegram bot integration with polling support
112780	- Challenge-based authentication (6-digit codes)
112781	- Trusted user management
112782	- Admin commands for user and channel management
112783	- Status widget showing connection status
112784	- Commands: `/remote`, `/remote connect`, `/remote disconnect`, `/remote configure`
112785	- Environment variable and file-based configuration
112786	- Support for group chats with mention detection
112787	- Channel authorization modes: all, mentions, trusted-only
112788	
112789	### Security
112790	- 6-digit challenge codes with 2-minute expiry
112791	- 3-attempt limit with 5-minute blocking
112792	- First authenticated user becomes admin
112793	- Trusted user validation on all messages

# Channel and Group Conversation Chat for Agents - Teams | Microsoft Learn

To enable users to install an agent in a team or group chat, add the `teams` or `groupchat` scope. This allows all members of the conversation to interact with your agent. After the agent is installed, it has access to metadata about the conversation, such as the list of conversation members. Also, when it's installed in a team, the agent has access to details about that team and the full list of channels.

By default, agents in group chats and channels only receive messages when they're directly @mentioned. They don't receive other messages sent to the conversation. For example, your agent doesn't receive a message when the team or channel is mentioned, or when someone replies to a message from your agent without @mentioning it. The Teams SDK provides a dedicated `mention` activity route to handle @mention events.

Note

- Using resource-specific consent (RSC), an agent can receive all channel and group chat messages in conversations where it's installed without being @mentioned. For more information, see [receive all messages for agents](channel-messages-for-bots-and-agents).
- Private channel support for agent apps is limited. You can add agent-enabled apps in private channels where private channel app support is enabled, but agents can't post messages or Adaptive Cards in private channel conversations. For private and shared channel app support details, see [apps for shared and private channels](../../../build-apps-for-shared-private-channels).

## Design guidelines

In group chats and channels, design your agent for collaborative conversations with clear value, concise responses, and minimal noise.

## Threaded conversations

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-csharp"

In Teams channels, messages can be organized into threads. When your agent receives a message in a thread, the conversation context already carries the thread ID. Use `Send()` to send a message in the same thread without quoting, or `Reply()` to send with a visual quote of the inbound message.

```csharp
app.OnMessage(async (context, cancellationToken) =>
{
    // Send in the same thread, no quote
    await context.Send("Acknowledged", cancellationToken);

    // Send in the same thread with a visual quote of the inbound message
    await context.Reply("Got it!", cancellationToken);
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-typescript"

When your agent receives a message in a thread, the conversation context already carries the thread ID. Use `send()` to send a message in the same thread without quoting, or `reply()` to send with a visual quote of the inbound message.

```typescript
app.on('message', async ({ send, reply }) => {
  // Send in the same thread, no quote
  await send('Acknowledged');

  // Send in the same thread with a visual quote of the inbound message
  await reply('Got it!');
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-python"

When your agent receives a message in a thread, the conversation context already carries the thread ID. Use `send()` to send a message in the same thread without quoting, or `reply()` to send with a visual quote of the inbound message.

```python
@app.on_message
async def handle_message(ctx: ActivityContext[MessageActivity]):
    # Send in the same thread, no quote
    await ctx.send("Acknowledged")

    # Send in the same thread with a visual quote of the inbound message
    await ctx.reply("Got it!")
```

::: zone-end

For sending messages into a thread proactively, see [Proactive messages](send-proactive-messages).

## Send a message on installation

When your agent is first added to a group or team, you can send an introduction message by using the `install.add` lifecycle route. For more information, see [proactive messaging](/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/teams-sdk/essentials/sending-messages/proactive-messaging).

If you send an introduction message, include a brief description of the agent's features and how to use them.

You can also store the `conversationId` during installation to enable [proactive messaging](/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/teams-sdk/essentials/sending-messages/proactive-messaging) later.

The following code shows an example of sending welcome messages on installation:

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-csharp"

```csharp
app.OnInstall(async context => 
{ 
    await context.Send("Hello! I'm your agent. Here's what I can do..."); 
}); 
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-typescript"

```typescript
app.on('install.add', async ({ send }) => 
{ 
    await send('Hello! I\'m your agent. Here\'s what I can do...'); 
}); 
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-python"

```python
@app.on_install_add 
async def handle_install_add(ctx: ActivityContext[InstalledActivity]): 
    await ctx.send("Hello! I'm your agent. Here's what I can do...") 
```

::: zone-end

Don't send proactive welcome messages to users individually when the agent is installed in a team or group chat. If you send a welcome message, post it in the installed conversation and mention the person who added the agent.

Note

Ensure that the message sent by the agent is relevant and adds value to the initial message and doesn't spam the users.

Don't send a message in the following cases:

- When the team is large, for example, larger than 100 members. Your agent can be seen as spam and the person who added it can get complaints. You must clearly communicate your agent's value proposition to everyone who sees the welcome message.
- Your agent is first mentioned in a group or channel instead of being first added to a team.
- A group or channel is renamed.
- A team member is added to a group or channel.

## Work with mentions

In group chats and channels, messages that @mention your agent include a mention entity in the message text. If your agent is configured to receive all messages, such as with RSC, some incoming messages might not include an @mention. Your agent can retrieve other users mentioned in a message and add mentions to messages it sends. Agents in group chats enable user mentions using `@mention`; however, they don’t support `@everyone` for mentions.

For messages that include @mentions, the message text contains mention markup such as `<at>@agentname</at>`.

### Retrieve mentions

Mentions are returned in the `entities` object in the activity payload and contain both the unique ID of the user and the name of the user mentioned. The text of the message also includes the mention, such as `<at>@John Smith<at>`. However, don't rely on the text in the message to retrieve any information about the user. It's possible for the person sending the message to alter it. Therefore, use the `entities` object.

You can retrieve all mentions in the message by filtering the `entities` array in the activity for entries with `type` set to `mention`.

The following code shows an example of retrieving mentions:

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-csharp"

```csharp
app.OnMessage(async context =>
{
    var mentions = context.Activity.Entities?
        .Where(e => e.Type == "mention")
        .ToList();

    if (mentions != null && mentions.Any())
    {
        var firstMention = mentions[0].Properties["mentioned"]?["name"]?.ToString();
        await context.Send($"Hello {firstMention}");
    }
    else
    {
        await context.Send("Aw, no one was mentioned.");
    }
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-typescript"

```typescript
app.on('message', async ({ activity, send }) => {
    const mentions = activity.entities?.filter(e => e.type === 'mention');

    if (mentions && mentions.length > 0) {
        const firstMention = mentions[0].mentioned;
        await send(`Hello ${firstMention.name}.`);
    } else {
        await send('Aw, no one was mentioned.');
    }
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-python"

```python
@app.on_message
async def handle_message(ctx: ActivityContext[MessageActivity]):
    mentions = [e for e in (ctx.activity.entities or []) if e.type == "mention"]

    if mentions:
        first_mention = mentions[0].mentioned
        await ctx.send(f"Hello {first_mention.name}")
    else:
        await ctx.send("Aw, no one was mentioned.")
```

::: zone-end

```json

#### Check for and strip @mention

In channels and group chats, users typically address an agent or app with an @mention. Before interpreting the message, check that the mention targets your agent or app, then remove the mention text and trim whitespace. This leaves only the user’s command or prompt for processing.

Removing the mention prevents the agent or app name from interfering with command matching, intent recognition, search, or natural-language processing. It also lets the same handler process messages consistently across personal chats, group chats, and channels. Preserve other mentions when they are part of the user’s request.

Note

The TypeScript and Python versions for Teams SDK include built-in functions to remove @mention.

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-csharp"

```csharp
string StripMentions(MessageActivity msg)
{
    var text = msg.Text ?? "";
    if (msg.Entities == null) return text;

    foreach (var entity in msg.Entities)
    {
        if (entity is MentionEntity mention && mention.Text != null)
        {
            text = text.Replace(mention.Text, "");
        }
    }

    return text.Trim();
}
```

This code snippet demonstrates how to clean a Teams message before command parsing:

- `msg.Entities` contains structured metadata such as mentions.
- `Replace(mention.Text, "")` removes the visible mention such as `@contoso` from the message.
- `Trim()` removes leftover spaces.

For example, `@contoso summarize this thread` becomes `summarize this thread`.

The function removes **all mentions**, not only the agent's or bot’s mention. If other mentions are meaningful input, verify that a mention refers to the current bot before removing it.

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-typescript"

```typescript
app.on('message', async ({ activity, send }) => {
  const clean = activity.stripMentionsText().text;
  await send(`You said: ${clean}`);
});
```

This code snippet demonstrates listening for incoming message activities and removing the @mention text before processing the user’s message.

- `activity.stripMentionsText()` removes mention text such as @contoso from the activity.
- `.text` retrieves the cleaned message content.
- `send()` echoes the cleaned text back to the user.

For example, `@contoso summarize this chat` becomes `summarize this chat`, so the agent can parse the command.

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-python"

```python
@app.on_message
async def handle_message(ctx: ActivityContext[MessageActivity]):
    clean = ctx.activity.strip_mentions_text().text
    await ctx.send(f"You said: {clean}")
```

This code snippets shows how to listen for incoming messages and remove @mention text before processing them.

- `ctx.activity.strip_mentions_text()` removes mention text such as @contoso.
- `.text` returns the cleaned message.
- `ctx.send()` replies with the cleaned text.

For example, `@contoso summarize this chat` becomes `summarize this chat`, making the message easier to parse as a command or prompt.

::: zone-end

### Add mentions to your messages

Your agent can mention other users in messages posted in channels. To include a mention inline in your message, place the mention in the message text and add the mention details to the entities array. The `text` field in the mention entity must match the exact text in the message body.

The following code shows an example of adding mentions to your messages:

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-csharp"

```csharp
app.OnMessage(async context =>
{
    var user = context.Activity.From;
    var message = new MessageActivity($"Hello <at>{user.Name}</at>!").AddMention(user);
    await context.Send(message);
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-typescript"

```typescript
app.on('message', async ({ send, activity }) => {
    const user = activity.from;
    const message = new MessageActivity(`Hello <at>${user.name}</at>!`).addMention(user);
    await send(message);
});
```

::: zone-end

::: zone pivot="teams-sdk-python"

```python
@app.on_message 
async def handle_message(ctx: ActivityContext[MessageActivity]): 
    await ctx.send(MessageActivityInput(text="Hello!").add_mention(account=ctx.activity.from_))
```

::: zone-end
