401	function publicSourceMetadata(metadata: InternalFileMetadata): RuntimeSourceFile {
402	  return {
403	    sha256: metadata.sha256,
404	    executable: metadata.executable,
405	    mode: metadata.mode,
406	    size: metadata.size,
407	  };
408	}
409	
410	function publicTargetMetadata(metadata: InternalFileMetadata): RuntimeTargetFile {
411	  return {
412	    sha256: metadata.sha256,
413	    executable: metadata.executable,
414	    mode: metadata.actualMode,
415	    size: metadata.size,
416	  };
417	}
418	
419	function manifestMetadata(metadata: RuntimeSourceFile): RuntimeManifestFile {
420	  return {
421	    sha256: metadata.sha256,
422	    executable: metadata.executable,
423	    mode: desiredMode(metadata.executable),
424	  };
425	}
426	
427	function sameLogicalFile(
428	  left: Pick<RuntimeManifestFile, 'sha256' | 'executable'> | null,
429	  right: Pick<RuntimeManifestFile, 'sha256' | 'executable'> | null,
430	): boolean {
431	  return (
432	    left !== null &&
433	    right !== null &&
434	    left.sha256 === right.sha256 &&
435	    left.executable === right.executable
436	  );
437	}
438	
439	function targetMatchesManifest(
440	  target: InternalFileMetadata | null,
441	  manifest: RuntimeManifestFile | null,
442	): boolean {
443	  return (
444	    target !== null &&
445	    manifest !== null &&
446	    target.sha256 === manifest.sha256 &&
447	    observedModeMatches(target.actualMode, manifest.mode)
448	  );
449	}
450	
451	function targetMatchesSource(target: InternalFileMetadata | null, source: RuntimeSourceFile | null): boolean {
452	  return (
453	    target !== null &&
454	    source !== null &&
455	    target.sha256 === source.sha256 &&
456	    observedModeMatches(target.actualMode, source.mode)
457	  );
458	}
459	
460	function targetContentMatchesSource(
461	  target: InternalFileMetadata | null,
462	  source: RuntimeSourceFile | null,
463	): boolean {
464	  return target !== null && source !== null && target.sha256 === source.sha256;
465	}
466	
467	function digestFileEntries(files: Readonly<Record<string, RuntimeSourceFile>>): string {
468	  const digest = createHash('sha256');
469	  for (const [relativePath, metadata] of Object.entries(files).sort(([left], [right]) => sortStrings(left, right))) {
470	    digest.update(relativePath);
471	    digest.update('\0');
472	    digest.update(metadata.sha256);
473	    digest.update('\0');
474	    digest.update(metadata.executable ? 'x' : '-');
475	    digest.update('\0');
476	  }
477	  return digest.digest('hex');
478	}
479	
480	function digestFileContents(files: Readonly<Record<string, RuntimeSourceFile>>): string {
481	  const normalized = Object.fromEntries(
482	    Object.entries(files).map(([relativePath, metadata]) => [
483	      relativePath,
484	      { ...metadata, executable: false },
485	    ]),
486	  );
487	  return digestFileEntries(normalized);
488	}

490	/**
491	 * Scan a declarative agent tree without following links or accepting runtime state.
492	 */
493	export async function scanTree(root: string): Promise<ScannedRuntimeTree> {
494	  const absoluteRoot = resolveInputPath(root, 'source root');
495	  const rootStat = await lstatMaybe(absoluteRoot);
496	  if (rootStat === null) fail('PIA_SOURCE_MISSING', `Source directory does not exist: ${absoluteRoot}`);
497	  if (rootStat.isSymbolicLink()) {
498	    fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Source directory is a symbolic link: ${absoluteRoot}`);
499	  }
500	  if (!rootStat.isDirectory()) {
501	    fail('PIA_NOT_DIRECTORY', `Source root is not a directory: ${absoluteRoot}`);
502	  }
503	
504	  const entries: Array<[string, RuntimeSourceFile]> = [];
505	
506	  async function visit(directory: string, prefix: string): Promise<void> {
507	    const children = await fs.readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true });
508	    children.sort((left: Dirent, right: Dirent) => sortStrings(left.name, right.name));
509	
510	    for (const child of children) {
511	      const relativePath = prefix === '' ? child.name : `${prefix}/${child.name}`;
512	      validateRelativePath(relativePath, 'source path');
513	      const childPath = path.join(directory, child.name);
514	      const stat = await fs.lstat(childPath);
515	      if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
516	        fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Source path is a symbolic link: ${relativePath}`);
517	      }
518	      if (stat.isDirectory()) {
519	        await visit(childPath, relativePath);
520	        continue;
521	      }
522	      if (!stat.isFile()) {
523	        fail('PIA_NON_FILE_REJECTED', `Source path is not an ordinary file: ${relativePath}`);
524	      }
525	
526	      const { metadata } = await readOrdinaryFile(childPath, 'source path');
527	      entries.push([relativePath, publicSourceMetadata(metadata)]);
528	    }
529	  }
530	
531	  await visit(absoluteRoot, '');
532	  entries.sort(([left], [right]) => sortStrings(left, right));
533	  const files = Object.fromEntries(entries);
534	  return {
535	    root: absoluteRoot,
536	    digest: digestFileEntries(files),
537	    files,
538	  };
539	}
540	
541	export async function treeDigest(root: string): Promise<string> {
542	  return (await scanTree(root)).digest;
543	}
544	
545	/** Portable lineage digest: Git executable bits are not observable on Windows. */
546	export async function treeContentDigest(root: string): Promise<string> {
547	  return digestFileContents((await scanTree(root)).files);
548	}
549	
550	function validateManifest(
551	  rawManifest: unknown,
552	  expectedTarget: string,
553	  manifestPath: string,
554	): RuntimeManifest {
555	  if (!isPlainObject(rawManifest) || rawManifest.schemaVersion !== MANIFEST_VERSION) {
556	    fail('PIA_INVALID_MANIFEST', `Unsupported or malformed runtime manifest: ${manifestPath}`);
557	  }
558	  if (typeof rawManifest.target !== 'string' || rawManifest.target !== expectedTarget) {
559	    fail('PIA_MANIFEST_TARGET_MISMATCH', `Runtime manifest belongs to a different target: ${manifestPath}`, {
560	      expected: expectedTarget,
561	      actual: rawManifest.target,
562	    });
563	  }
564	  if (!isPlainObject(rawManifest.files)) {
565	    fail('PIA_INVALID_MANIFEST', `Runtime manifest files must be an object: ${manifestPath}`);
566	  }
567	
568	  const entries: Array<[string, RuntimeManifestFile]> = [];
569	  for (const [relativePath, metadata] of Object.entries(rawManifest.files)) {
570	    validateRelativePath(relativePath, 'manifest path');
571	    if (
572	      !isPlainObject(metadata) ||
573	      typeof metadata.sha256 !== 'string' ||
574	      !/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(metadata.sha256) ||
575	      typeof metadata.executable !== 'boolean' ||
576	      metadata.mode !== desiredMode(metadata.executable)
577	    ) {
578	      fail('PIA_INVALID_MANIFEST', `Invalid file metadata in runtime manifest: ${relativePath}`);
579	    }
580	    entries.push([
581	      relativePath,
582	      {
583	        sha256: metadata.sha256,
584	        executable: metadata.executable,
585	        mode: metadata.mode,
586	      },
587	    ]);
588	  }
589	  entries.sort(([left], [right]) => sortStrings(left, right));
590	  return {
591	    schemaVersion: MANIFEST_VERSION,
592	    target: expectedTarget,
593	    files: Object.fromEntries(entries),
594	  };
595	}
596	
597	async function loadManifest(manifestPath: string, targetDir: string): Promise<LoadedManifest> {
598	  const absoluteManifestPath = resolveInputPath(manifestPath, 'manifest path');
599	  const stat = await lstatMaybe(absoluteManifestPath);
600	  if (stat === null) return { exists: false, manifest: null, path: absoluteManifestPath };
601	  if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
602	    fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Runtime manifest is a symbolic link: ${absoluteManifestPath}`);
603	  }
604	  if (!stat.isFile()) {
605	    fail('PIA_INVALID_MANIFEST', `Runtime manifest is not an ordinary file: ${absoluteManifestPath}`);
606	  }
607	
608	  const { data } = await readOrdinaryFile(absoluteManifestPath, 'runtime manifest');
609	  let parsed: unknown;
610	  try {
611	    parsed = JSON.parse(data.toString('utf8'));
612	  } catch (error) {
613	    fail('PIA_INVALID_MANIFEST', `Runtime manifest is not valid JSON: ${absoluteManifestPath}`, {
614	      cause: errorMessage(error),
615	    });
616	  }
617	  return {
618	    exists: true,
619	    manifest: validateManifest(parsed, path.resolve(targetDir), absoluteManifestPath),
620	    path: absoluteManifestPath,
621	  };
622	}
623	
624	async function inspectTarget(targetDir: string, relativePath: string): Promise<TargetInspection> {
625	  const absoluteTarget = resolveInputPath(targetDir, 'runtime target');
626	  const components = validateRelativePath(relativePath, 'target path');
627	  const targetRoot = await inspectTargetRoot(absoluteTarget);
628	  if (!targetRoot.exists) return { kind: 'missing', metadata: null };
629	
630	  let current = absoluteTarget;
631	  for (let index = 0; index < components.length; index += 1) {
632	    current = path.join(current, components[index]);
633	    const stat = await lstatMaybe(current);
634	    if (stat === null) return { kind: 'missing', metadata: null };
635	    if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
636	      fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Managed runtime path is a symbolic link: ${relativePath}`);
637	    }
638	
639	    const isLeaf = index === components.length - 1;
640	    if (!isLeaf) {
641	      if (!stat.isDirectory()) {
642	        return {
643	          kind: 'obstruction',
644	          metadata: null,
645	          obstruction: components.slice(0, index + 1).join('/'),
646	        };
647	      }
648	      continue;
649	    }
650	
651	    if (stat.isDirectory()) {
652	      return { kind: 'directory', metadata: null, obstruction: relativePath };
653	    }
654	    if (!stat.isFile()) {
655	      fail('PIA_NON_FILE_REJECTED', `Managed runtime path is not an ordinary file: ${relativePath}`);
656	    }
657	    const { metadata } = await readOrdinaryFile(current, 'managed runtime path');
658	    return { kind: 'file', metadata };
659	  }
660	
661	  fail('PIA_INVALID_PATH', `Target path did not contain a file name: ${relativePath}`);
662	}
663	
664	async function inspectTargetRoot(targetDir: string): Promise<TargetRootInspection> {
665	  const absoluteTarget = resolveInputPath(targetDir, 'runtime target');
666	  const stat = await lstatMaybe(absoluteTarget);
667	  if (stat === null) return { exists: false, mode: null };
668	  if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
669	    fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Runtime target is a symbolic link: ${absoluteTarget}`);
670	  }
671	  if (!stat.isDirectory()) {
672	    fail('PIA_NOT_DIRECTORY', `Runtime target is not a directory: ${absoluteTarget}`);
673	  }
674	  return { exists: true, mode: stat.mode & 0o777 };
675	}
676	
677	function classifyFile(
678	  relativePath: string,
679	  source: RuntimeSourceFile | null,
680	  base: RuntimeManifestFile | null,
681	  targetInspection: TargetInspection,
682	): RuntimeFileStatus {
683	  const target = targetInspection.kind === 'file' ? targetInspection.metadata : null;
684	  let status: RuntimeClassification;
685	  let reason: RuntimeFileReason;
686	  let blocking = false;
687	
688	  if (base === null) {
689	    if (targetInspection.kind === 'missing') {
690	      status = 'new';
691	      reason = 'not-yet-applied';
692	    } else if (targetContentMatchesSource(target, source)) {
693	      // A first apply may be interrupted after its atomic target write but before
694	      // the manifest write. Matching bytes are safe to adopt; buildActions still
695	      // rewrites the file when its final private mode is not yet correct.
696	      status = 'source-only-update';
697	      reason = 'unowned-target-matches-source';
698	    } else {
699	      status = 'conflict';
700	      reason = targetInspection.kind === 'file' ? 'unowned-target-file' : 'unowned-target-obstruction';
701	      blocking = true;
702	    }
703	  } else if (targetInspection.kind !== 'file' && targetInspection.kind !== 'missing') {
704	    status = source !== null && sameLogicalFile(source, base) ? 'runtime-drift' : 'conflict';
705	    reason = 'target-is-not-a-file';
706	    blocking = true;
707	  } else if (source === null) {
708	    if (target === null || targetMatchesManifest(target, base)) {
709	      status = 'stale';
710	      reason = target === null ? 'already-absent' : 'source-removed';
711	    } else {
712	      status = 'conflict';
713	      reason = 'source-removed-runtime-changed';
714	    }
715	  } else if (target === null) {
716	    if (sameLogicalFile(source, base)) {
717	      status = 'runtime-drift';
718	      reason = 'runtime-file-missing';
719	    } else {
720	      status = 'conflict';
721	      reason = 'source-changed-runtime-file-missing';
722	    }
723	  } else {
724	    const sourceUnchanged = sameLogicalFile(source, base);
725	    const runtimeUnchanged = targetMatchesManifest(target, base);
726	    if (sourceUnchanged && runtimeUnchanged) {
727	      status = 'clean';
728	      reason = 'unchanged';
729	    } else if (!sourceUnchanged && runtimeUnchanged) {
730	      status = 'source-only-update';
731	      reason = 'source-changed';
732	    } else if (sourceUnchanged && !runtimeUnchanged) {
733	      status = 'runtime-drift';
734	      reason = 'runtime-changed';
735	    } else if (targetMatchesSource(target, source)) {
736	      status = 'source-only-update';
737	      reason = 'source-and-runtime-converged';
738	    } else {
739	      status = 'conflict';
740	      reason = 'source-and-runtime-diverged';
741	    }
742	  }
743	
744	  return {
745	    path: relativePath,
746	    status,
747	    classification: status,
748	    label: status.replaceAll('-', ' '),
749	    reason,
750	    owned: base !== null,
751	    blocking,
752	    source,
753	    applied: base,
754	    target: target === null ? null : publicTargetMetadata(target),
755	    targetKind: targetInspection.kind,
756	    obstruction: targetInspection.obstruction ?? null,
757	  };
758	}
759	
760	function dominantClassification(counts: RuntimeClassificationCounts): RuntimeClassification {
761	  if (counts.conflict > 0) return 'conflict';
762	  if (counts['runtime-drift'] > 0) return 'runtime-drift';
763	  if (counts['source-only-update'] > 0) return 'source-only-update';
764	  if (counts.new > 0) return 'new';
765	  if (counts.stale > 0) return 'stale';
766	  return 'clean';
767	}
768	
769	export async function getRuntimeStatus({
770	  sourceDir,
771	  targetDir,
772	  manifestPath,
773	}: RuntimeStatusOptions): Promise<RuntimeStatus> {
774	  if (sourceDir === undefined || targetDir === undefined || manifestPath === undefined) {
775	    fail('PIA_INVALID_ARGUMENT', 'sourceDir, targetDir, and manifestPath are required');
776	  }
777	
778	  const source = await scanTree(sourceDir);
779	  const absoluteTarget = resolveInputPath(targetDir, 'runtime target');
780	  const targetRoot = await inspectTargetRoot(absoluteTarget);
781	  const loadedManifest = await loadManifest(manifestPath, absoluteTarget);
782	  const manifestFiles = loadedManifest.manifest?.files ?? {};
783	  const relativePaths = [...new Set([...Object.keys(source.files), ...Object.keys(manifestFiles)])].sort(sortStrings);
784	  const files: RuntimeFileStatus[] = [];
785	
786	  for (const relativePath of relativePaths) {
787	    const sourceMetadata = source.files[relativePath] ?? null;
788	    const baseMetadata = manifestFiles[relativePath] ?? null;
789	    const targetInspection = await inspectTarget(absoluteTarget, relativePath);
790	    files.push(classifyFile(relativePath, sourceMetadata, baseMetadata, targetInspection));
791	  }
792	
793	  const counts: RuntimeClassificationCounts = {
794	    clean: 0,
795	    'source-only-update': 0,
796	    'runtime-drift': 0,
797	    conflict: 0,
798	    new: 0,
799	    stale: 0,
800	    total: files.length,
801	  };
802	  for (const file of files) counts[file.status] += 1;
803	  const hasRuntimeDrift = counts['runtime-drift'] > 0;
804	  const hasConflicts = counts.conflict > 0;
805	  const hasBlockingConflict = files.some((file) => file.blocking);
806	  const targetNeedsInitialization =
807	    !targetRoot.exists ||
808	    (targetRoot.mode !== null && !observedModeMatches(targetRoot.mode, DIRECTORY_MODE));
809	  const hasChanges =
810	    targetNeedsInitialization || !loadedManifest.exists || files.some((file) => file.status !== 'clean');
811	
812	  return {
813	    sourceDir: source.root,
814	    sourceDigest: source.digest,
815	    targetDir: absoluteTarget,
816	    targetExists: targetRoot.exists,
817	    targetMode: targetRoot.mode,
818	    targetNeedsInitialization,
819	    manifestPath: loadedManifest.path,
820	    manifestExists: loadedManifest.exists,
821	    manifest: loadedManifest.manifest,
822	    state: hasRuntimeDrift || hasConflicts ? 'blocked' : hasChanges ? 'changes' : 'clean',
823	    classification: dominantClassification(counts),
824	    counts,
825	    hasChanges,
826	    hasRuntimeDrift,
827	    hasConflicts,
828	    hasBlockingConflict,
829	    canApply: !hasRuntimeDrift && !hasConflicts,
830	    canForceApply: !hasBlockingConflict,
831	    files,
832	  };
833	}

835	async function mkdirPrivate(directory: string): Promise<boolean> {
836	  const stat = await lstatMaybe(directory);
837	  if (stat !== null) {
838	    if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Directory is a symbolic link: ${directory}`);
839	    if (!stat.isDirectory()) fail('PIA_NOT_DIRECTORY', `Expected a directory: ${directory}`);
840	    return false;
841	  }
842	  await fs.mkdir(directory, { recursive: true, mode: DIRECTORY_MODE });
843	  return true;
844	}
845	
846	async function ensureTargetParent(targetDir: string, relativePath: string): Promise<void> {
847	  const absoluteTarget = resolveInputPath(targetDir, 'runtime target');
848	  const components = validateRelativePath(relativePath, 'target path');
849	  await mkdirPrivate(absoluteTarget);
850	  await fs.chmod(absoluteTarget, DIRECTORY_MODE);
851	
852	  let current = absoluteTarget;
853	  for (const component of components.slice(0, -1)) {
854	    current = path.join(current, component);
855	    const stat = await lstatMaybe(current);
856	    if (stat === null) {
857	      await fs.mkdir(current, { mode: DIRECTORY_MODE });
858	    } else {
859	      if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) fail('PIA_SYMLINK_REJECTED', `Target directory is a symbolic link: ${current}`);
860	      if (!stat.isDirectory()) fail('PIA_NOT_DIRECTORY', `Target parent is not a directory: ${current}`);
861	    }
862	    await fs.chmod(current, DIRECTORY_MODE);
863	  }
864	}
865	
866	async function fsyncDirectory(directory: string): Promise<void> {
867	  if (process.platform === 'win32') return;
868	  let handle: FileHandle | undefined;
869	  try {
870	    handle = await fs.open(directory, fsConstants.O_RDONLY);
871	    await handle.sync();
872	  } catch (error) {
873	    if (!['EINVAL', 'ENOTSUP', 'EBADF'].includes(errorCode(error) ?? '')) throw error;
874	  } finally {
875	    await handle?.close();
876	  }
877	}
878	
879	async function atomicWrite(
880	  filePath: string,
881	  data: string | Uint8Array,
882	  mode: number,
883	  { noReplace = false }: { noReplace?: boolean } = {},
884	): Promise<void> {
885	  const directory = path.dirname(filePath);
886	  const temporaryPath = path.join(
887	    directory,
888	    `.pia-${path.basename(filePath)}-${process.pid}-${randomBytes(8).toString('hex')}`,
889	  );
890	  let handle: FileHandle | null = null;
891	  try {
892	    handle = await fs.open(temporaryPath, fsConstants.O_WRONLY | fsConstants.O_CREAT | fsConstants.O_EXCL, mode);
893	    await handle.writeFile(data);
894	    await handle.chmod(mode);
895	    await handle.sync();
896	    await handle.close();
897	    handle = null;
898	
899	    if (noReplace) {
900	      await fs.link(temporaryPath, filePath);
901	      await fs.unlink(temporaryPath);
902	    } else {
903	      await fs.rename(temporaryPath, filePath);
904	    }
905	    await fs.chmod(filePath, mode);
906	    await fsyncDirectory(directory);
907	  } catch (error) {
908	    await handle?.close().catch(() => {});
909	    await fs.unlink(temporaryPath).catch(() => {});
910	    throw error;
911	  }
912	}
913	
914	function sameTargetSnapshot(currentInspection: TargetInspection, priorFile: RuntimeFileStatus): boolean {
915	  if (priorFile.targetKind === 'missing') return currentInspection.kind === 'missing';
916	  if (priorFile.targetKind !== 'file' || currentInspection.kind !== 'file') return false;
917	  if (currentInspection.metadata === null || priorFile.target === null) return false;
918	  return (
919	    currentInspection.metadata.sha256 === priorFile.target.sha256 &&
920	    observedModeMatches(currentInspection.metadata.actualMode, priorFile.target.mode)
921	  );
922	}

924	function nextManifestFromStatus(status: RuntimeStatus): RuntimeManifest {

941	function buildActions(

951	    if (file.status === 'clean') continue;
952	    if ((file.status === 'runtime-drift' || file.status === 'conflict') && !force) {
953	      actions.push({ path: file.path, action: 'blocked', classification: file.status, reason: file.reason });

956	    if (file.blocking) {

958	      continue;

960	    if (file.source !== null) {
961	      if (
962	        file.target !== null &&
963	        file.target.sha256 === file.source.sha256 &&
964	        observedModeMatches(file.target.mode, file.source.mode)

966	        actions.push({ path: file.path, action: 'adopt', classification: file.status });
967	      } else {

969	      }
970	    } else if (file.target !== null) {

1133	function compareParentTrees(source: ScannedRuntimeTree, parent: ScannedRuntimeTree): ParentTreeDiff {
1134	  const paths = [...new Set([...Object.keys(source.files), ...Object.keys(parent.files)])].sort(sortStrings);
1135	  const files: ParentTreeFileStatus[] = paths.map((relativePath) => {
1136	    const sourceMetadata = source.files[relativePath] ?? null;
1137	    const parentMetadata = parent.files[relativePath] ?? null;
1138	    let status: ParentTreeClassification;
1139	    if (parentMetadata === null) status = 'added';
1140	    else if (sourceMetadata === null) status = 'removed';
1141	    else if (sameLogicalFile(sourceMetadata, parentMetadata)) status = 'unchanged';
1142	    else status = 'modified';
1143	    return {
1144	      path: relativePath,
1145	      status,
1146	      source: sourceMetadata,
1147	      parent: parentMetadata,
1148	    };
1149	  });
1150	  const counts: ParentTreeDiff['counts'] = {
1151	    added: 0,
1152	    removed: 0,
1153	    modified: 0,
1154	    unchanged: 0,
1155	    total: files.length,
1156	  };
1157	  for (const file of files) counts[file.status] += 1;
1158	  return {
1159	    directory: parent.root,
1160	    digest: parent.digest,
1161	    counts,
1162	    files,
1163	  };
1164	}

186	/** Stable, filesystem-safe key: a bounded project basename plus a canonical-path hash. */
187	export function projectKey(cwd: string): string {
188	  const canonical = canonicalCwd(cwd);
189	  const rawBase = path.basename(canonical) || 'root';
190	  const sanitized = rawBase
191	    .normalize('NFKD')
192	    .replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+/g, '-')
193	    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '') || 'project';
194	  const base = sanitized.slice(0, PROJECT_BASENAME_MAX_CHARS);
195	  const digest = createHash('sha256').update(canonical).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
196	  return `${base}-${digest}`;

323	  return {
324	    engine: inferredEngine,
325	    title,
326	    titleSlot,
327	    header,
328	    id: header.id,
329	    cwd: header.cwd,
330	    entries,
331	    activeBranch: branch,

371	export async function listSessions({
372	  sessionDir,
373	  engine,
374	}: ListSessionsOptions = {}): Promise<ParsedSessionFile[]> {
375	  if (typeof sessionDir !== 'string' || sessionDir.trim() === '') {
376	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_PATH', 'sessionDir must be a non-empty path');
377	  }
378	  const directory = path.resolve(sessionDir);
379	  let children: Dirent<string>[];
380	  try {
381	    children = await fs.readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true, encoding: 'utf8' });
382	  } catch (error) {
383	    if (hasErrorCode(error, 'ENOENT')) return [];
384	    throw error;
385	  }
386	
387	  const files = children
388	    .filter((entry) => entry.isFile() && entry.name.endsWith('.jsonl'))
389	    .map((entry) => path.join(directory, entry.name))
390	    .sort();
391	  const sessions = await Promise.all(files.map((filePath) => parseSessionFile(filePath, { engine })));
392	  sessions.sort((left, right) => right.mtimeMs - left.mtimeMs || left.path.localeCompare(right.path));
393	  return sessions;

397	export async function resolveSession({
398	  sessionDir,
399	  selector,
400	  latest = false,
401	  engine,
402	}: ResolveSessionOptions = {}): Promise<ParsedSessionFile> {
403	  if (selector !== undefined && (typeof selector !== 'string' || selector.trim() === '')) {
404	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_SELECTOR', 'Session selector must be a non-empty string');
405	  }
406	  if (latest && selector !== undefined && selector !== 'latest') {
407	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_SELECTOR', 'Choose either a selector or latest, not both');
408	  }
409	  if (selector && path.isAbsolute(selector)) {
410	    return await parseSessionFile(selector, { engine });
411	  }
412	
413	  const wantsLatest = latest || selector === 'latest';
414	  if (!wantsLatest && selector === undefined) {
415	    fail('PIA_SESSION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED', 'Specify an absolute session path, ID prefix, or latest');
416	  }
417	  const sessions = await listSessions({ sessionDir, engine });
418	  if (sessions.length === 0) {
419	    fail('PIA_SESSION_NOT_FOUND', `No sessions found under ${path.resolve(sessionDir || '')}`);
420	  }
421	  if (wantsLatest) return sessions[0];
422	
423	  const prefix = selector!.toLowerCase();
424	  const matches = sessions.filter((session) => session.id.toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix));
425	  if (matches.length === 0) fail('PIA_SESSION_NOT_FOUND', `No session ID starts with ${selector}`);
426	  if (matches.length > 1) {
427	    fail('PIA_AMBIGUOUS_SESSION', `Session ID prefix ${selector} matches ${matches.length} sessions`, {
428	      matches: matches.map((session) => ({ id: session.id, path: session.path })),
429	    });
430	  }
431	  return matches[0];
432	}

437	export function assertForkCompatible(
438	  sourceOrOptions: Engine | ForkCompatibilityOptions,
439	  maybeTargetEngine?: Engine,
440	): true {
441	  const objectOptions = typeof sourceOrOptions === 'object' ? sourceOrOptions : undefined;
442	  const sourceEngine = objectOptions
443	    ? objectOptions.sourceEngine || objectOptions.source?.engine
444	    : sourceOrOptions;
445	  const targetEngine = objectOptions ? objectOptions.targetEngine : maybeTargetEngine;
446	  if (!sourceEngine || !targetEngine) {
447	    fail('PIA_INVALID_ENGINE', 'Both sourceEngine and targetEngine are required for a raw fork');
448	  }
449	  const validSourceEngine = requireEngine(sourceEngine);
450	  const validTargetEngine = requireEngine(targetEngine);
451	  if (validSourceEngine !== validTargetEngine) {
452	    fail(
453	      'PIA_FOREIGN_SESSION',
454	      `Raw session fork cannot cross harness formats (${validSourceEngine} -> ${validTargetEngine}); use handoff instead`,
455	    );
456	  }
457	  return true;
458	}

273	export function validateLineage(combos: readonly Combo[]): Map<string, Combo> {
274	  const byId = new Map<string, Combo>(combos.map((combo) => [combo.id, combo]));
275	  for (const combo of combos) {
276	    const parentId = combo.metadata.derivedFrom;
277	    if (!parentId) continue;
278	    const parent = byId.get(parentId);
279	    if (!parent) throw new Error(`${combo.id}: parent combo ${parentId} does not exist`);
280	    if (parent.engine !== combo.engine) throw new Error(`${combo.id}: parent must use the same engine`);

285	    if (visiting.has(id)) throw new Error(`Lineage cycle detected at ${id}`);
286	    if (visited.has(id)) return;
287	    visiting.add(id);
288	    const parent = byId.get(id)?.metadata.derivedFrom;
289	    if (parent) visit(parent);

291	    visited.add(id);

297	export async function comboDigest(combo: Combo): Promise<string> {
298	  const metadata: Partial<ComboMetadata> = { ...combo.metadata };
299	  delete metadata.$schema;
300	  delete metadata.derivedFrom;
301	  delete metadata.parentDigest;
302	  const agentDigest = await treeContentDigest(combo.agentDir);
303	  const hash = createHash("sha256");
304	  hash.update(JSON.stringify(stable(metadata)));
305	  hash.update("\0");
306	  hash.update(agentDigest);
307	  return `sha256:${hash.digest("hex")}`;
308	}

390	    next.forEach((child, index) => {
391	      const last = index === next.length - 1;
392	      lines.push(`${prefix}${last ? "└─ " : "├─ "}${child.id} [${child.metadata.maturity}]`);
393	      walkChildren(child, `${prefix}${last ? "   " : "│  "}`);
394	    });
395	  };
396	  const roots = children.get(null) || [];
397	  roots.forEach((root) => {
398	    lines.push(`${root.id} [${root.metadata.maturity}]`);
399	    walkChildren(root, "");
400	  });
401	  return lines.join("\n");
402	}
403

49	  const direct = env[name];

63	function windowsPathEntries(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string[] {
64	  return (envValue(env, "PATH") || "")
65	    .split(";")
66	    .map((entry) => entry.trim().replace(/^"|"$/g, ""))
67	    .filter(Boolean);
68	}
69	
70	function hasPathSeparator(command: string): boolean {
71	  return command.includes("/") || command.includes("\\");
72	}

74	function findWindowsCommand(
75	  command: string,
76	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
77	  extensions: readonly string[],
78	): string | undefined {
79	  const extension = path.extname(command).toLowerCase();
80	  const names = extension ? [command] : extensions.map((suffix) => `${command}${suffix}`);
81	  if (hasPathSeparator(command)) return names.find(isRegularFile);
82	
83	  for (const directory of windowsPathEntries(env)) {
84	    for (const name of names) {
85	      const candidate = path.join(directory, name);
86	      if (isRegularFile(candidate)) return candidate;
87	    }
88	  }
89	  return undefined;
90	}

92	function findPowerShell(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string {
93	  for (const command of ["pwsh", "powershell"]) {
94	    const resolved = findWindowsCommand(command, env, [".exe"]);
95	    if (resolved) return resolved;
96	  }
97	
98	  const systemRoot = envValue(env, "SystemRoot");
99	  if (systemRoot) {
100	    const bundled = path.join(systemRoot, "System32", "WindowsPowerShell", "v1.0", "powershell.exe");
101	    if (isRegularFile(bundled)) return bundled;

108	 * npm always creates a PowerShell shim alongside its cmd shim; invoking that
109	 * file through `-File` keeps every forwarded value as a distinct argv item.
110	 */
111	export function resolveCommandInvocation(
112	  command: string,
113	  args: readonly string[] = [],
114	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,
115	  platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform,
116	): CommandInvocation {
117	  if (platform !== "win32") return { command, args: [...args] };
118	
119	  const requestedExtension = path.extname(command).toLowerCase();
120	  let resolved = findWindowsCommand(command, env, [".exe", ".com", ".ps1", ".cmd", ".bat"]);
121	  if (!resolved && (requestedExtension === ".cmd" || requestedExtension === ".bat")) {
122	    const siblingCommand = command.slice(0, -requestedExtension.length) + ".ps1";
123	    resolved = findWindowsCommand(siblingCommand, env, [".ps1"]);
124	  }
125	  if (!resolved) {
126	    if (requestedExtension === ".cmd" || requestedExtension === ".bat") {
127	      throw new Error(
128	        `Windows command shim ${command} is unsupported without a same-basename .ps1 sibling; pia never enables shell parsing`,
129	      );
130	    }
131	    return { command, args: [...args] };
132	  }
133	
134	  const resolvedExtension = path.extname(resolved).toLowerCase();
135	  if (resolvedExtension === ".cmd" || resolvedExtension === ".bat") {
136	    const sibling = resolved.slice(0, -resolvedExtension.length) + ".ps1";
137	    if (!isRegularFile(sibling)) {
138	      throw new Error(
139	        `Windows command shim ${resolved} is unsupported without a same-basename .ps1 sibling; pia never enables shell parsing`,
140	      );
141	    }
142	    resolved = sibling;
143	  }
144	  if (path.extname(resolved).toLowerCase() !== ".ps1") {
145	    return { command: resolved, args: [...args] };
146	  }
147	
148	  return {
149	    command: findPowerShell(env),
150	    args: [
151	      "-NoLogo",
152	      "-NoProfile",
153	      "-NonInteractive",
154	      "-ExecutionPolicy",
155	      "Bypass",
156	      "-File",
157	      resolved,
158	      ...args,
159	    ],
160	  };
161	}
162	
163	export function commandResult(
164	  command: string,
165	  args: readonly string[] = [],
166	  options: ProcessOptions = {},
167	): ProcessResult {
168	  const env = options.env || process.env;
169	  const invocation = resolveCommandInvocation(command, args, env);
170	  const result = spawnSync(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
171	    encoding: "utf8",
172	    stdio: [options.input === undefined ? "ignore" : "pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
173	    input: options.input,
174	    env,
175	    cwd: options.cwd,
176	    maxBuffer: options.maxBuffer || 8 * 1024 * 1024,
177	  });
178	  if (result.error) {
179	    return { ok: false, status: null, stdout: "", stderr: result.error.message, error: result.error };
180	  }
181	  return {
182	    ok: result.status === 0,
183	    status: result.status,
184	    stdout: result.stdout || "",
185	    stderr: result.stderr || "",
186	  };
187	}
188	
189	export async function runInherited(
190	  command: string,
191	  args: readonly string[],
192	  options: InheritedProcessOptions = {},
193	): Promise<number> {
194	  return await new Promise<number>((resolve, reject) => {
195	    const env = options.env || process.env;
196	    const invocation = resolveCommandInvocation(command, args, env);
197	    const child = spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
198	      cwd: options.cwd,
199	      env,
200	      stdio: "inherit",
201	    });
202	    child.on("error", reject);
203	    child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
204	      if (signal) {
205	        process.kill(process.pid, signal);
206	        return;
207	      }
208	      resolve(code ?? 1);
209	    });
210	  });
211	}

214	  const probe = commandResult(command, ["--version"]);
215	  return probe.ok ? probe.stdout.trim() || probe.stderr.trim() : undefined;

```text
1	# Sessions and handoff
2	
3	Configuration can be copied safely; live session files cannot. `pia` therefore
4	separates normal history, same-engine forks, and cross-harness handoffs into
5	three explicit operations.
6	
7	## Session isolation
8	
9	An isolated combo stores history below:
10	
11	```text
12	${PIA_STATE_HOME:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents}/
13	  sessions/<engine>/<combo-name>/<project-key>/
14	```
15	
16	With `history.mode: shared`, the leaf instead uses:
17	
18	```text
19	sessions/<engine>/shared/<group>/<project-key>/
20	```
21	
22	The project key is derived from the canonical working directory. Thus two
23	projects do not accidentally resume one another, and a shared group never
24	crosses the Pi/OMP boundary. Use `pia sessions <combo>` to inspect the sessions
25	available under the combo's effective policy.
26	
27	## Same-engine forks
28	
29	```sh
30	pia fork pi/base pi/research --latest -- <target arguments>
31	pia fork pi/base pi/research --session <id-or-path> -- <target arguments>
32	```
33	
34	The first two arguments are source and target combo IDs. Forking is allowed
35	only when both use the same engine. `--latest` selects the newest source session;
36	`--session` accepts an unambiguous session-ID prefix from the source combo's
37	effective session root, or an explicit absolute path.
38	
39	`pia` delegates to the target harness's native `--fork` behavior and creates a
40	new target session; it does not append to or byte-copy the source session. Use a
41	fork when the target should retain the native conversation tree and both sides
42	understand exactly the same session format.
43	
44	Although both snapshots use a session format identified as version 3, they are
45	not wire-compatible. OMP includes a title slot and additional entry types, so
46	raw cross-harness session sharing is prohibited. See the pinned
47	[Pi session loader](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/853a80d26c90a14c1886f0ebb8ffaae133ca2185/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts#L548-L553)
48	and [OMP session format](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/51f03804476c3fd3c15748ae07e4849d1efc883b/docs/session.md#L61-L66).
49	
50	## Deterministic handoff
51	
52	```sh
53	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --latest \
54	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" -- <target arguments>
55	```
56	
57	Handoff supports same- or cross-engine transfer. It reads the selected source
58	session without changing it and produces a private Markdown artifact under
59	`$PIA_STATE_HOME/handoffs/`. Generation is local and deterministic; it does not
60	ask another model to summarise the transcript.
61	
62	The extractor:
63	
64	1. Prefers the newest compaction summary; if none exists, keeps the first user
65	   goal and a bounded set of recent messages.
66	2. Adds source, target, and session provenance, canonical working directory,
67	   Git branch, `HEAD`, status, and diff-stat.
68	3. Excludes hidden thinking, images, tool arguments, and successful tool
69	   output. Failed tool output is capped at 2 KiB.
70	4. Caps the document at 128 KiB and reports omitted or truncated blocks.
71	5. Runs the agent-history-hygiene redactor, then validates with `gitleaks`.
72	   Any redaction or validation failure aborts the handoff.
73	6. Writes the artifact with mode `0600` on POSIX (or the containing user ACL on
74	   Windows) and starts a fresh target session with it as the first attachment.
75	
76	Use `--session <id-or-absolute-path>` instead of `--latest` to select
77	explicitly. `--max-bytes N` can lower or raise the 128 KiB default (minimum
78	4096). Use `--no-run` to generate the document without launching the target:
79	
80	```sh
81	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --session <id-or-path> \
82	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" --no-run
83	```
84	
85	Review the generated file before sharing it outside the machine. Redaction is a
86	fail-closed safety boundary, not a promise that arbitrary prose contains no
87	sensitive business context.
88	
89	Malformed session data, a missing source session, Git provenance failure in the
90	current project, an unavailable redactor or `gitleaks`, and an oversized/unsafe
91	artifact all fail before target launch. `pia doctor` checks the required helper
92	commands.
93
```

1	# Discord OpenCode Remote
2	
3	This directory pins and deploys a managed Kimaki bot. Discord project channels
4	map to local working directories and threads map to isolated OpenCode sessions.
5	
6	## 架構與程式碼導覽
7	
8	這套服務不是從零重寫 Discord bot，而是以固定版本的
9	`kimaki@0.26.0` 作為 Discord／OpenCode 協調核心，再由本目錄補上可重現的
10	patch、安全隔離、常駐服務、健康檢查、部署與回滾。這個責任邊界很重要：
11	
12	- 本專案維護的是整合與營運層：`start-kimaki.sh`、`patch-kimaki.mjs`、
13	  `deploy.sh`、`healthcheck.mjs`、launchd 設定及資料庫整理工具。
14	- Discord 事件、OpenCode session 與回應分派的核心來自 Kimaki，安裝後位於
15	  `node_modules/kimaki/dist/`。
16	- 不直接手改安裝後的 `dist`；所有必要變更集中在 `patch-kimaki.mjs`，並在
17	  `npm install` 的 `postinstall` 階段重播。
18	- patch 只接受 `0.26.0`。上游版本不符時直接失敗，避免把舊 patch 靜默套到
19	  不相容的新程式碼。
20	
21	### 主要程式碼
22	
23	```text
24	Discord bot/
25	├── package.json                    # 鎖定 Kimaki 版本與 postinstall patch
26	├── start-kimaki.sh                 # 乾淨環境、驗證、隔離與啟動參數
27	├── patch-kimaki.mjs                # 本機功能及安全修補的唯一來源
28	├── deploy.sh / rollback.sh         # 原子部署與回滾
29	├── healthcheck.mjs / watchdog.sh   # 功能健康檢查與故障恢復
30	├── com.solomon.kimaki.plist        # macOS launchd 常駐服務
31	└── node_modules/kimaki/dist/
32	    ├── discord-bot.js              # Discord MessageCreate 與 thread 路由
33	    ├── opencode.js                 # 啟動 opencode serve、建立 SDK client
34	    ├── session-handler/
35	    │   ├── thread-session-runtime.js   # prompt、session、queue、event 分派
36	    │   └── global-event-listener.js    # OpenCode SSE 全域事件流
37	    └── discord-utils.js            # Discord Markdown 與 2,000 字分段
38	```
39	
40	### 執行拓樸
41	
42	```text
43	macOS launchd
44	  └─ start-kimaki.sh
45	      └─ Kimaki Node.js process
46	          ├─ discord.js Gateway / REST
47	          ├─ ~/.kimaki/discord-sessions.db
48	          ├─ localhost Hrana DB bridge
49	          └─ opencode serve（localhost 隨機 port）
50	              ├─ OpenCode HTTP JSON API
51	              ├─ /global/event SSE stream
52	              ├─ Kimaki OpenCode plugins
53	              └─ 隔離的 OpenCode XDG／SQLite 狀態
54	```
55	
56	所有專案共用一個本機 `opencode serve` process，但每次 SDK request 都帶入
57	工作目錄；Discord project channel 對應本機目錄，Discord thread 則對應一個
58	OpenCode session。
59	
60	### 一次訊息的完整路徑
61	
62	1. Discord Gateway 送出 `MessageCreate`，入口是
63	   `node_modules/kimaki/dist/discord-bot.js:331`。
64	2. Bot 依序檢查 guild allowlist、自己的訊息、channel 是否綁定本機專案，
65	   以及使用者的 owner／admin／Manage Server／`Kimaki` role 權限。
66	3. Project channel 的新訊息會建立 Discord thread；既有 thread 則載入原本的
67	   OpenCode session。對應關係持久化在 `discord-sessions.db`。
68	4. 前處理階段解析回覆內容、mention、文字附件、圖片、PDF 與語音訊息。
69	5. `thread-session-runtime.js:2291-2368` 將使用者文字、Discord metadata、
70	   system prompt、附件、agent 與 model 組成 OpenCode request。
71	6. `session.promptAsync(request)` 透過 OpenCode SDK 發出 HTTP request：
72	   `POST /session/{sessionID}/prompt_async`。
73	7. OpenCode 執行模型及工具，再由 `/global/event` 以 Server-Sent Events
74	   推送 session、文字與工具事件。
75	8. `global-event-listener.js:130-210` 維持一條全域 SSE 連線；每個 thread
76	   runtime 再依 session ID 過濾屬於自己的事件。
77	9. 完成的文字交給 `discord-utils.js:486-534`，保留 Markdown/code fence，
78	   並依 Discord 的 2,000 字限制分段送回原 thread。
79	
80	```text
81	Discord MessageCreate
82	        │
83	        ▼
84	guild／role／channel 權限檢查
85	        │
86	        ▼
87	Discord channel → 本機專案目錄
88	Discord thread  → OpenCode session
89	        │
90	        ▼
91	session.promptAsync() ── HTTP + JSON ──► opencode serve
92	        ▲                                      │
93	        │                                      │ model / tools
94	        └──── session events ◄──── SSE ─────────┘
95	        │
96	        ▼
97	Markdown 整理、2,000 字分段、送回 Discord thread
98	```
99	
100	### 關鍵程式片段
101	
102	Discord 訊息入口先做 admission control，而不是收到訊息就直接交給模型：
103	
104	```js
105	discordClient.on(Events.MessageCreate, async (message) => {
106	  if (!isAllowedGuildId(message.guildId)) return
107	  if (isSelfBotMessage && !isCliInjectedPrompt) return
108	
109	  const channelConfig = await getChannelDirectory(owningChannelId)
110	  if (!channelConfig) return
111	
112	  const member = await resolveGuildMessageMember(message)
113	  if (!hasKimakiBotPermission(member, message.guild)) return
114	
115	  // 通過檢查後才交給對應的 thread/session runtime。
116	})
117	```
118	
119	Kimaki 在本機啟動一個共用 OpenCode server，並以 project directory 建立 SDK
120	client。實作入口是 `node_modules/kimaki/dist/opencode.js:639-790`：
121	
122	```js
123	const serverProcess = spawn(spawnCommand, spawnArgs, {
124	  cwd: os.homedir(),
125	  env: {
126	    ...process.env,
127	    OPENCODE_CONFIG: opencodeConfigPath,
128	    OPENCODE_PORT: port.toString(),
129	    KIMAKI: "1",
130	  },
131	})
132	
133	const client = createOpencodeClient({
134	  baseUrl,
135	  directory,
136	  headers: getOpencodeServerAuthHeaders(),
137	})
138	```
139	
140	送給 OpenCode 的資料不只有聊天文字，也包含這次 Discord turn 的執行上下文：
141	
142	```js
143	const parts = [
144	  { type: "text", text: promptWithImagePaths },
145	  { type: "text", text: syntheticContext, synthetic: true },
146	  ...images,
147	]
148	
149	const request = {
150	  sessionID: session.id,
151	  directory: this.sdkDirectory,
152	  parts,
153	  system: getOpencodeSystemMessage({
154	    sessionId: session.id,
155	    channelId,
156	    guildId: this.thread.guildId,
157	    threadId: this.thread.id,
158	  }),
159	  ...(resolvedAgent ? { agent: resolvedAgent } : {}),
160	  ...(modelField ? { model: modelField } : {}),
161	}
162	
163	await waitForGlobalEventListener()
164	await getClient().session.promptAsync(request)
165	```
166	
167	回應不是解析 CLI stdout，而是訂閱 OpenCode 的 typed event stream：
168	
169	```js
170	const subscribeResult = await client.global.event({ signal })
171	
172	for await (const event of subscribeResult.stream) {
173	  dispatchEvent(event)
174	}
175	```
176	
177	SSE 中斷時會以 exponential backoff 重連，從 500 ms 增加至最多 30 秒。
178	
179	### Session、狀態與並行
180	
181	- 一個 Discord thread 通常對應一個 OpenCode session，因此對話可以跨訊息延續。
182	- 不同 thread 有獨立 runtime，可以並行執行；同一 thread 的狀態變更會序列化，
183	  避免 event、queue 與 session transition 互相踩資料。
184	- 完整 OpenCode 對話存放在隔離的 OpenCode SQLite；thread/session mapping、
185	  model 選擇及已送出的 part mapping 存放在 Kimaki SQLite。
186	- 已送出的 OpenCode part 會記錄其 Discord message mapping，重連後可避免重複傳送。
187	- 顯式的本機 per-thread queue 是記憶體狀態，process restart 後不保留；這是目前
188	  已知的恢復邊界。
189	
190	### 安全邊界
191	
192	- `start-kimaki.sh` 使用 `env -i` 建立環境變數白名單，避免 launchd 或互動 shell
193	  的任意變數滲入服務。
194	- OpenCode API 只監聽 localhost 隨機 port，並要求私有 Basic Auth credential。
195	- Bot 使用固定 Discord guild allowlist，channel 還必須存在本機 project mapping。
196	- `--restrict-directories` 讓模型離開目前專案前必須取得額外許可。
197	- Bot 的 OpenCode XDG 目錄與桌面／Tailscale OpenCode 完全分離；啟動器拒絕
198	  symlink，並檢查 `opencode.db`、WAL、SHM 是否與共用實例指向相同 inode。
199	- `umask 077`、目錄 `0700` 及 credential `0600` 限制其他本機帳號讀取狀態。
200	- `--no-analytics`、`--no-critique` 與 `--no-auto-upgrade` 分別關閉產品分析、
201	  外部 diff critique，以及未經測試的自動升級。
202	
203	這不是 sandbox。獲授權的 Discord 使用者能透過 `!` 或 `/run-shell-command`
204	執行此 macOS 帳號可執行的 shell command；因此 Discord 帳號、server role 與
205	bot token 都必須視為主機存取憑證。
206	
207	### 給工程師的一句話
208	
209	這是一個以 Kimaki 作為 transport 與 session orchestration core 的 Discord
210	遠端 OpenCode runtime：本專案釘死上游版本，透過可重播 patch 客製行為，再補上
211	guild allowlist、XDG／SQLite 隔離、localhost Basic Auth、launchd supervision、
212	functional health check、原子部署與 rollback。
213	
214	## Runtime
215	
216	- Kimaki: `0.26.0`
217	- Sharp security override: `0.35.3`
218	- Node.js: `24.15.0`
219	- Bun: `1.3.12`
220	- OpenCode: `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`
221	- Kimaki state and Discord credentials: `~/.kimaki/`
222	- Kimaki OpenCode state: `~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/opencode/`
223	- Default Discord model: `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol`
224	
225	The launcher uses `umask 077`, so newly created credentials and logs default to
226	owner-only access.
227	
228	Install dependencies:
229	
230	```sh
231	npm install
232	```
233	
234	Start the interactive setup or run the configured bot:
235	
236	```sh
237	./start-kimaki.sh
238	```
239	
240	The launcher intentionally enables:
241	
242	- `--restrict-directories`: ask before leaving the active project.
243	- `--no-critique`: do not upload diffs to an external review service.
244	- `--no-analytics`: disable Kimaki product analytics.
245	- `--no-auto-upgrade`: keep the tested version pinned.
246	
247	It does not enable `--allow-all-users`. Initially, only the owner of the private
248	Discord server should have access.
249	
250	The runtime also enforces a fixed guild allowlist. Being a Discord server owner
251	or administrator is not sufficient unless the server ID is explicitly allowed.
252	The health endpoint becomes unhealthy when no allowlisted server is connected.
253	The localhost OpenCode API requires a private Basic Auth credential, and its
254	database retains only sessions referenced by Discord threads or scheduled work.
255	
256	## Discord Setup
257	
258	1. Create a private Discord server used only for this bot.
259	2. Open <https://discord.com/developers/applications> and create an application.
260	3. In **Bot**, enable **Message Content Intent**.
261	4. Reset and copy the bot token when the Kimaki setup wizard requests it.
262	5. Never paste the token into Discord, this repository, or an OpenCode prompt.
263	6. Use the install URL printed by Kimaki to add the bot to the private server.
264	
265	## Projects
266	
267	Register the two initial project directories after onboarding:
268	
269	```sh
270	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/Skill training"
271	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/every thing can be quant/第一性原理/不再被騙系統"
272	```
273	
274	Kimaki creates one Discord channel per directory. Switch project by switching
275	channel; start a separate task by posting a new channel message. Continue a task
276	inside its thread.
277	
278	This installation applies a version-checked local patch after `npm install`.
279	Discord's `/add-project` can accept an absolute path, browse a path prefix, or
280	search folder names under the home directory and mounted volumes. Projects are
281	created only when requested; subfolders are not pre-created as channels.
282	The command and its autocomplete can be used from any channel in the allowed
283	private server, including a channel that is not yet linked to a project.
284	
285	Examples in Discord's `/add-project` field:
286	
287	- `TOEIC`: search matching folder names.
288	- `/Users/solomon/`: browse folders in the home directory.
289	- `/Volumes/`: browse mounted disks.
290	- `/absolute/path/to/folder`: use an exact directory as the project root.
291	
292	Folder choices end in `/`. Select a folder, then reopen the `project` field to
293	browse its children. Submit at any level to create that folder's project channel.
294	One- or two-character searches use fast top-level matching; longer searches add
295	Spotlight results. If deep search times out, top-level matches remain available.
296	
297	## Background Service
298	
299	`com.solomon.kimaki.plist` is installed under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It
300	starts Kimaki when this macOS user logs in and restarts it after failures. Logs
301	are written to `~/.kimaki/launchd.log` and `~/.kimaki/launchd-error.log`.
302	
303	The deployed runtime is isolated from this Git working tree under
304	`~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/releases/`. `current` points at the active
305	release and `previous` provides rollback. Deploy a verified release with:
306	
307	```sh
308	./deploy.sh
309	```
310	
311	The watchdog checks Kimaki, Discord, and OpenCode every five minutes. It only
312	restarts after two consecutive failures and rotates each service log at 10 MB.
313	The OpenCode check performs a real session query instead of trusting the shallow
314	global health endpoint.
315	
316	Management commands:
317	
318	```sh
319	kimaki-remote status
320	kimaki-remote restart
321	kimaki-remote logs
322	kimaki-remote doctor
323	kimaki-remote deploy
324	kimaki-remote rollback
325	```
326	
327	Switch from the shared Gateway bot to your own Discord application with:
328	
329	```sh
330	kimaki-remote setup-self-hosted
331	```
332	
333	The command validates the Bot token before downtime, backs up the database,
334	accepts the token using hidden terminal input, opens the authorization URL, and
335	verifies functional health before finishing. `kimaki-remote use-gateway` only
336	stops the current Bot after confirming that saved Gateway credentials exist.
337	
338	Do not run two writing sessions concurrently against `Skill training`: its
339	workflow pulls, commits, and pushes at the end of each training round.
340	
341	## Security Boundary
342	
343	A user who can operate Kimaki can run shell commands on this Mac through `!` or
344	`/run-shell-command`. Treat the Discord account, server owner role, `Kimaki`
345	role, and bot token as machine-access credentials.
346	
347	Keep the existing Tailscale OpenCode service as a fallback. Kimaki starts its
348	own localhost OpenCode server on a separate random port and separate XDG data
349	directory. It never shares `opencode.db`, WAL, or SHM files with the desktop or
350	Tailscale service on port `4096`.
351
```

# Executive conclusion

Use a **Pi-authoritative, durable session-router model** as the default MVP.

“IM as ingress” should mean:

- IM transports provide authenticated events, reply/attachment metadata, and a return address.
- The gateway decides authorization, routing, ordering, approvals, and delivery.
- **Pi’s persisted session is the only authoritative model-visible conversation history.**
- The gateway does **not** replay the surrounding room/channel history on every prompt.
- The IM platform remains authoritative for native message facts such as edits, deletes, reactions, membership, and attachment availability, but those facts do not retroactively rewrite Pi history.

This is slightly richer than a simple bridge: a minimal durable control-plane database is still required. Without it, multi-chat attribution and restart safety fail, as the current `pi-messenger-bridge` demonstrates.

I would not make a broad multi-platform gateway part of `pia`’s core yet. First document this contract; if an MVP is built, make it a separately supervised companion service/package using Pi’s public SDK or RPC surface.

---

# 1. What the repository and Pi already establish

## Repository constraints

The repository explicitly distinguishes version-controlled configuration from live mutable state:

- Git is the source of truth for combo definitions, not the agent’s live home: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/architecture.md:3-5`.
- Sessions, credentials, databases, blobs, and caches belong outside Git: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/architecture.md:38-50`.
- Session routing is already scoped by engine, combo/history group, and canonical working directory: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/sessions-and-handoff.md:7-25` and `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/src/sessions.ts:186-223`.
- Wrapper-owned session flags are intentionally excluded from declarative `launchArgs`: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/architecture.md:83-100` and `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/schema/combo.schema.json:15-27`.

A gateway should preserve that division. Its event journal, queue, bindings, credentials, attachment cache, and delivery receipts are runtime state, never combo content.

Also, `history.mode: shared` means sharing history among compatible combos for the same engine/project. It is **not** a multi-user authorization or IM conversation policy. The code removes only the combo-name component while retaining engine and canonical-project scope: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/src/sessions.ts:199-223`.

## Discord/OpenCode baseline

The supplied baseline is successful partly because Discord supplies a convenient object boundary:

- Project channel maps to working directory and Discord thread maps to one OpenCode session: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/.specstory/references/Discord-OpenCode-Remote.md:56-58`.
- A new root message creates a thread; subsequent thread messages load its mapped session: `:62-78`.
- Each thread has an independent runtime, while operations within one thread are serialized: `:179-188`.
- OpenCode stores the full conversation; Kimaki separately stores thread/session, model, and delivered-part mappings: `:181-186`.
- Its per-thread pending queue is memory-only and is explicitly a restart boundary: `:186-188`.
- It is not a sandbox; authorized users have the host account’s command authority: `:190-205`.

Those assumptions are safe only because Discord threads provide a stable, visible task boundary. They are not a portable definition of “conversation.”

## Pi 0.84.4 session properties

The installed package is exactly 0.84.4: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/package.json:1-4`.

Relevant behavior:

- Pi persists sessions as JSONL trees and supports continue, resume, explicit session selection, and native fork: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/sessions.md:3-20`.
- Entries are linked by stable `id` and `parentId`; branching does not rewrite previous entries: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/session-format.md:174-185` and `:306-342`.
- Session history can include messages, model changes, compactions, branch summaries, and extension entries: `.../docs/session-format.md:203-304`.
- Extension `custom` entries persist metadata without entering model context, while `custom_message` entries can carry metadata and participate in context: `.../docs/session-format.md:263-284`.
- `AgentSessionRuntime` is the public session-replacement layer for new/resume/fork/import; the active `AgentSession` object changes and subscriptions must be rebound: `.../docs/sdk.md:114-178`.
- RPC exposes `new_session`, `switch_session`, `fork`, and `clone`: `.../docs/rpc.md:160-181` and `:620-715`.
- RPC `get_entries(since)` explicitly treats a stable entry ID as a durable cursor across restarts and returns the current leaf: `.../docs/rpc.md:717-745`.
- `agent_settled`, not `agent_end`, is the boundary after retries, compaction recovery, and queued continuations have all stopped: `.../docs/rpc.md:855-911` and `.../docs/extensions.md:567-580`.
- Pi supports images directly in SDK/RPC prompts, but not a general arbitrary-file attachment type in `PromptOptions`: `.../docs/sdk.md:180-215` and `.../docs/rpc.md:41-78`.
- Pi’s own steering/follow-up queues are in-memory fields on `AgentSession`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.d.ts:197-215`.
- The session writer directly rewrites/appends the JSONL file; there is no documented concurrent-writer contract: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.js:695-760`.

Therefore, **only one gateway worker may own a writable Pi session at a time**. A room lock alone is insufficient if two rooms can bind the same Pi session.

# 2. Source-of-truth model

There should not be one database pretending to own every kind of truth. Assign one authority per domain:

| Domain | Authority | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Native message existence, revision, sender, membership, attachment reference | IM provider | Do not infer current IM state from Pi history. |
| Model-visible work history, tool calls/results, branches, compaction | Pi session | Do not replay or reconstruct it from the IM timeline every turn. |
| Project/session binding, identity authorization, queue ownership, approvals, cursors, outbound receipts | Gateway database | Do not encode this only in display text or an in-memory callback. |
| Files and repository state | Workspace/Git/filesystem | Neither deleting an IM message nor deleting a Pi transcript reverses tool effects. |

The central invariant is:

> Every accepted IM invocation is projected into exactly one selected Pi session; later Pi turns use the Pi session, not a fresh copy of IM history.

This avoids two competing conversational histories while still acknowledging that provider-side edits and deletion are provider facts.

---

# 3. Portable conversation taxonomy

A gateway should distinguish these concepts rather than reducing all of them to `chatId`:

1. **Installation/account** — the bot identity or tenant installation.
2. **Space** — guild, workspace, tenant, realm, homeserver/account boundary.
3. **Conversation** — DM, multiparty DM, group, room, or channel.
4. **Subconversation** — thread, forum topic, Teams channel thread, Matrix thread root.
5. **Message** — immutable provider-issued message/event ID.
6. **Reply edge** — a relationship to one prior message; not necessarily a thread.
7. **Quote** — a copied excerpt that may be stale, partial, manually selected, or forged.
8. **Actor** — canonical provider user ID, separate from display name.
9. **Project binding** — approved `(Pi combo, canonical cwd, tool policy)`.
10. **Pi session binding** — transport context to Pi session ID/file and active leaf.
11. **Execution lane** — the current exclusive writer and queued jobs for that Pi session.
12. **Response route** — immutable destination captured for one admitted job.

The canonical transport key must include provider, bot account/installation, tenant or equivalent, conversation ID, and optional subcontext kind/ID. Names, channel titles, usernames, and topic strings are labels, never primary keys.

## Platform mapping

| Surface | Recommended boundary | Important caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Discord | Guild/account + thread channel ID. Parent project channel can select the project; thread selects the Pi session. | A Discord thread is itself a channel. Forum posts also create threads. Archived/visibility state is separate from identity. |
| Slack | Team/context team + conversation ID + root `thread_ts`. | Shared channels cross workspace boundaries; include installation/account context. `thread_ts` is absent for ordinary channel or DM messages. |
| Telegram | Bot account + chat ID + `message_thread_id` or direct-message topic ID where present. | Ordinary chats have no thread. Generic message-deletion updates are absent from the Bot API update union. |
| Matrix | Account/homeserver + room ID + `m.thread` root event ID. | A rich reply via `m.in_reply_to` is not automatically a thread. Edits and reactions are separate relation events. |
| Zulip | Realm + channel/stream ID, with a gateway-maintained topic binding. | A topic is a mutable label: it can be renamed or messages can be moved individually, from a point onward, or all at once. |
| Teams | Tenant + conversation/thread identity carried by the activity. | Bots receive only mentions by default unless broader resource-specific consent is granted. |
| Flat group/DM systems | Account + conversation ID; use an explicit current binding and reply-to-bot lookup. | There is no safe automatic way to support several simultaneous tasks in one flat room. |

Discord’s official documentation confirms that threads have channel IDs and parent IDs. Slack defines thread membership with `thread_ts`. Telegram exposes `message_thread_id` and explicit reply/quote metadata. Matrix’s `m.thread` always references the thread root, whereas a reply uses `m.in_reply_to`. Zulip’s own update API demonstrates that topics are mutable and movable.

## Platforms without usable threads

For a flat room, apply this resolution order:

1. A reply to a known bot output resolves through the stored outbound-message-to-Pi-session mapping.
2. An explicit session handle in a gateway command resolves that session.
3. A unique active room binding may be used.
4. If zero or multiple candidates remain, reject as ambiguous and ask for `/new`, `/resume`, or `/bind`.

Do not invent a session from reply-chain topology. A reply identifies a relation, not necessarily a persistent task.

For DMs, default to a session per **account + provider + peer + project binding**. Never merge all users’ DMs into one “main” session. OpenClaw’s current documentation explicitly warns that its personal-agent `main` default lets Alice and Bob share context and recommends `per-channel-peer` for multi-user inboxes.

# 4. Model taxonomy

## Model A — Active-session remote pilot

**Definition:** All admitted IM messages are injected into whichever Pi session is currently active; responses return to a mutable “last chat.”

**Invariants**

- Exactly one trusted operator.
- Exactly one active Pi task.
- No meaningful concurrent inbound traffic.
- Local TUI state decides the current session.

**Benefits**

- Very small extension.
- Native interactive Pi remains the user interface.
- Little new persistent state.

**Failure modes**

- Cross-chat context leakage.
- A later message overwrites the response destination of an earlier turn.
- No durable chat/session association.
- Restart loses pending attribution.
- `/new` or local resume can silently redirect future remote messages.
- Multiple users share host authority and transcript context.

**Storage**

- Credentials and allowlists only.
- Possibly one lock file and transient pending destination.

**Pi fit**

- Good fit for extension `sendUserMessage()` and `turn_end`.
- Poor fit for an actual multi-context gateway.

This is exactly the shape of current `pi-messenger-bridge`: one `pendingRemoteChat` variable at [src/index.ts:24-27](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-messenger-bridge/blob/8b0c1da19c930225b15ec971f9225241a82b381d/src/index.ts#L24-L27), overwritten for every incoming message before forwarding it to the active session at [src/index.ts:178-188](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-messenger-bridge/blob/8b0c1da19c930225b15ec971f9225241a82b381d/src/index.ts#L178-L188), then reused for delivery at [src/index.ts:200-250](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-messenger-bridge/blob/8b0c1da19c930225b15ec971f9225241a82b381d/src/index.ts#L200-L250). Its open issues request session management and attachments and report cross-contact message pollution.

**Verdict:** supportable as an explicitly single-user “remote console,” but not a general gateway.

---

## Model B — Pi-authoritative durable session router

**Definition:** The gateway maps each admitted transport context to a persistent Pi session. Only explicitly directed messages and explicitly selected reply/attachment context enter Pi.

**Invariants**

- Pi session history is the canonical model context.
- Every binding names one project/combo and zero or one current Pi session.
- Every admitted inbound event has one durable gateway job and immutable response route.
- Only one execution lease may mutate a Pi session.
- Normal messages are FIFO follow-ups, not implicit steering.
- No ambient room history is automatically copied.
- A given external event/revision is never deliberately projected twice.
- Session commands are parsed by the gateway and never forwarded as model text.

**Benefits**

- Minimal privacy and token footprint.
- Native Pi resume, branching, compaction, tool history, and model state remain correct.
- Natural fit for Discord threads and still deterministic on flat chats.
- Easy to explain: “the agent knows what you sent to the agent.”
- Much smaller semantic surface than mirroring each provider.

**Failure modes**

- Users may assume the agent saw nearby messages that were never sent to it.
- Provider edits/deletes cannot retroactively change an already-used Pi prompt.
- Exactly-once execution cannot be guaranteed across a crash spanning the gateway DB, Pi JSONL, and remote delivery.
- Shared-room users still share the session’s tool authority unless isolated operationally.
- A session opened concurrently in a local TUI can violate the single-writer invariant.

**Storage**

A small durable gateway database containing:

- canonical identities and allowlists;
- project and session bindings;
- inbound event IDs, revisions, states, and payload digests;
- per-session FIFO jobs, leases, and attempt state;
- Pi entry/leaf cursors;
- outbound message/chunk receipts;
- reply-to-session mappings;
- pending approvals;
- attachment metadata and cleanup deadlines.

It does not need to retain a complete room transcript.

**Pi fit**

Excellent through the public SDK; good through one RPC worker per active session. Public Pi APIs already cover persistent sessions, replacement, fork/clone, event subscriptions, compaction, images, and stable entry cursors.

**Verdict:** recommended MVP.

---

## Model C — Bounded incremental IM-history projection

**Definition:** Model B plus a deterministic, bounded selection of recent room events or a reply chain is attached to an invocation.

**Invariants**

- Pi remains authoritative for prior projected work.
- Every projected IM event carries immutable origin, actor, timestamp, and revision provenance.
- The gateway records which external events have already entered each Pi session.
- Only unseen deltas or an explicitly requested older reference are included.
- Bot outputs already present in Pi history are excluded from the projection.
- The projection has hard event, byte, and token limits.
- Untrusted participants’ content is visibly separated from the invoking user’s instruction.

**Benefits**

- Handles “summarize the discussion above” and threadless collaborative rooms.
- Better conversational continuity where mention-only ingress is too sparse.
- Less operational burden than a complete event mirror.

**Failure modes**

- Duplicate context unless inclusion watermarks are exact.
- Edits/deletes create stale snapshots.
- Pagination gaps and inaccessible history make the projection incomplete.
- Other users’ content becomes indirect prompt-injection input.
- Token usage and compaction frequency increase.
- A naïve last-N window can cut causally important messages or include unrelated simultaneous discussions.

**Storage**

Everything in Model B, plus:

- bounded normalized message cache;
- revision/tombstone records;
- per-Pi-session projection watermark;
- projection manifest/digest;
- author and reply/thread edges.

**Pi fit**

Best with SDK custom messages and metadata. RPC can pass flattened text/images, but its prompt command does not expose a documented persistent metadata field for external event IDs.

**Verdict:** useful second-stage model, not the default.

---

## Model D — Event-sourced IM-native mirror

**Definition:** The gateway persists the normalized IM event stream—including revisions, tombstones, membership, reactions, relation edges, and attachments—and derives Pi context projections from it.

**Invariants**

- The normalized gateway event log is append-only.
- Provider event identity plus source identifies a distinct event.
- Edits and deletes append revisions/tombstones; they never silently mutate audit history.
- Context projections are versioned and reproducible.
- Model execution and tool side effects are kept in a separate execution ledger so replay never reruns them.
- Pi sessions are projections/execution histories, not the authoritative representation of the IM room.

**Benefits**

- Rich audit, replay, migration, compliance, cross-channel views, and alternative projections.
- Correct handling of topic moves, edits, reactions, membership changes, and offline catch-up where providers expose those events.
- Supports multiple agents or re-projection strategies.

**Failure modes**

- Very high adapter and migration burden.
- “Complete mirror” is impossible on platforms that omit events, such as ordinary Telegram deletion notifications.
- Provider retention/permission changes create irreparable gaps.
- Deletion obligations conflict with append-only audit logs.
- Rebuilding model context cannot reproduce already executed filesystem or network side effects.
- Pi’s append-only session cannot be treated as a mutable mirror; re-projection generally requires a new/forked session.
- Considerably greater breach impact because the gateway retains all chat content.

**Storage**

Full normalized event log, raw-payload quarantine, relation graph, revision/tombstone history, membership snapshots, attachment object store, projection checkpoints, execution ledger, outbox, retention/legal-hold metadata, and schema migrations.

**Pi fit**

Weak as a Pi extension; reasonable only as a standalone service using SDK/RPC. Pi remains the execution engine, not the event store.

**Verdict:** only justified by product-level collaborative or compliance requirements.
