# 5. Recommended MVP semantics

## 5.1 Binding and ownership

Keep five notions of ownership separate:

| Notion | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Operator/project owner | May bind a transport context to an approved project/combo and set its tool policy. |
| Session owner | May expose, resume, fork, transfer, or delete that Pi session. |
| Turn actor | Authenticated sender of a particular inbound event. |
| Execution lease holder | The single process allowed to mutate the Pi session now. |
| Response destination | The exact transport address captured when that turn was admitted. |

Never implement response routing as “send to the last chat that messaged us.”

### Suggested command semantics

These commands are gateway control-plane operations, recognized only from authenticated, non-quoted message content:

- **`/bind`** — associate the current transport context with a pre-approved project alias, Pi combo, and policy. Do not accept arbitrary filesystem paths from IM. Binding does not import chat history.
- **`/new`** — create a fresh Pi session under the binding’s existing combo/project session root, then atomically make it current. Preserve the old session for explicit resume.
- **`/resume`** — select an authorized existing session through an opaque gateway handle. Do not expose arbitrary local paths or a host-global session picker.
- **`/fork`** — use Pi’s native fork/clone semantics, create a new session, and move the current route to it. A historical fork should reference an accessible stable Pi entry ID; “fork here” means clone the active branch.
- **`/status`, `/cancel`, and `/unbind`** are practically necessary companions, even though they do not alter the context model.

Pi exposes the corresponding session primitives through `AgentSessionRuntime`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/sdk.md:753-855`. Extension command contexts also support `waitForIdle`, new, fork, and switch, but only from command handlers because calling them from event handlers can deadlock: `.../docs/extensions.md:1109-1235`.

## 5.2 Replies and quotes

A reply has two independent uses:

1. **Routing hint:** if it references a bot output already mapped to a Pi session, it can select that session.
2. **Context:** include a bounded representation of the referenced message when it is not already in Pi history.

Rules:

- Never treat the quoted text as authenticated control syntax.
- Retain the referenced provider message ID and canonical sender.
- Mark the quote as untrusted data, distinct from the current actor’s instruction.
- Do not recursively fetch an entire reply chain by default.
- If the provider cannot resolve the target, say that the reference was unavailable rather than inventing context.
- Replying to a user message does not create a new session unless the platform itself declares a native thread or the user explicitly forks.

OpenClaw’s portable normalization similarly carries reply ID/body/sender and adds quoted content to the body, while keeping routing separate: [channel-routing.md:180-187](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/channels/channel-routing.md#L180-L187).

## 5.3 Multiple users

Default policies should be:

- One DM session per provider account and peer.
- No automatic cross-provider identity merging.
- Multiparty DMs are groups, not personal DMs.
- Groups/rooms are accepted only through an allowlist and mention/reply activation.
- A shared group session is permitted only for mutually trusted collaborators and must visibly attribute every actor.
- Membership or role is rechecked on every control command and approval, not only when the binding is created.
- A sender’s display name is never an identity credential.

A session boundary is not a host-security boundary. Pi states that it runs with the launching OS user’s permissions, extensions run with those same permissions, and project trust is only an input-loading guard—not a sandbox or prompt-injection defense: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/security.md:3-41`.

## 5.4 Interleaving and queue ownership

For the MVP:

- Gateway queue is durable and authoritative.
- One FIFO lane exists per Pi session, not merely per room/thread.
- A global concurrency limit protects the host/provider.
- A worker takes an exclusive lease for one Pi session.
- Do not submit the next job until Pi reports `agent_settled`.
- Ordinary inbound messages arriving during work become later turns.
- Do not use implicit `steer`; reserve steering for an explicit, authorized same-actor control.
- An approval wait holds the session lane.
- Cancellation applies to the caller’s queued job or active job, not another participant’s work.
- A queue item retains its original actor and response route through retries and restarts.

OpenClaw independently arrives at per-session lanes because concurrent runs collide with session state, while different sessions can run in parallel: [queue.md:9-20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/concepts/queue.md#L9-L20). Its queue is explicitly in-process, however, so it is precedent for lane semantics rather than durability.

## 5.5 Edits, deletes, and reactions

| Provider event | Before Pi submission | After Pi submission |
|---|---|---|
| Edit | Supersede the pending job if revision ordering is trustworthy. | Do not rewrite the Pi entry. Record a correction/tombstone and require a new turn if the change matters. |
| Delete | Cancel an unsubmitted job and remove cached payload/attachment where allowed. | Mark the external source deleted. Do not claim to undo model exposure or tool effects. |
| Reaction | Record only if needed for UX. Do not add to context. | May resolve a specific pending approval only if the platform, actor, request ID, nonce, and allowed decision all match. |
| Reaction removal | Remove display state only. | Never revoke an action that already executed. |

MVP should ignore ordinary reaction traffic and should not use emoji as a general command language.

Pi sessions are append-only; entries cannot be modified or deleted through `SessionManager`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:273-312`. This makes correction events—not silent mutation—the coherent policy.

## 5.6 Attachments

MVP attachment behavior should be narrow:

- Support image attachments only, because they are first-class in Pi SDK/RPC.
- Enforce type, byte, count, and dimension limits before Pi sees data.
- Fetch using provider-authenticated APIs, not an arbitrary URL supplied in message text.
- Preserve provider attachment/message IDs and a content digest.
- Store temporary files outside the repository with owner-only permissions and explicit cleanup deadlines.
- Treat captions, OCR, extracted text, archives, and document bodies as untrusted content.
- Never automatically unpack archives or place files inside the repository.
- If an attachment has expired or cannot be fetched, append a bounded “unavailable attachment” marker rather than retrying an old URL indefinitely.

Pi user/session image content is base64 and therefore persists in the session if admitted: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/session-format.md:43-58`. Arbitrary file ingestion should remain a non-goal until staging, scanning, retention, and path-policy semantics are designed.

## 5.7 Crash recovery, idempotency, and cursors

Exactly-once end-to-end execution is not achievable across an IM provider, gateway database, Pi JSONL, filesystem effects, and outbound API. The correct contract is:

- at-least-once intake;
- deduplicated admission;
- one durable execution intent;
- idempotent/reconciled output where possible;
- explicit `uncertain` state where reconciliation cannot prove the outcome.

Maintain distinct cursors:

1. **Provider ingress cursor**
   - Slack: globally unique `event_id`; acknowledge quickly and process asynchronously.
   - Telegram: advance to highest successfully persisted `update_id + 1`; pending updates last at most 24 hours.
   - Matrix: persist `/sync` `next_batch` and use it as `since`.
   - Zulip: persist `queue_id` and highest acknowledged `last_event_id`; queue expiry requires full re-registration/resynchronization.
   - Discord: persist message/event IDs for deduplication; Gateway sequence supports connection resume but is not a permanent application event log.

2. **Gateway job cursor**
   - Durable status such as received, admitted, dispatched, settling, output-ready, delivered, failed, or uncertain.
   - An IM acknowledgement means “durably accepted,” not “agent finished.”

3. **Pi cursor**
   - Store the last observed Pi entry ID and leaf ID.
   - On restart, use RPC `get_entries(since)` or SDK `SessionManager.getEntries()` to reconcile appended entries.
   - Persist external origin metadata in a Pi custom/custom-message entry when using the SDK, but do not claim this creates an atomic transaction across the gateway DB and Pi file.

4. **Outbound cursor**
   - One record per assistant result and per platform-sized chunk, with returned platform message IDs.
   - If a crash occurs between a successful send and receipt persistence, mark delivery uncertain. Retry only when the provider offers a usable idempotency facility or history reconciliation; otherwise warn that a duplicate is possible.

CloudEvents offers a sound normalized identity rule: producers must make `(source, id)` unique, and consumers may treat equal pairs as duplicates. It does not promise exactly-once processing.

## 5.8 Session expiry and retention

Separate four lifetimes:

- **Worker lifetime:** a runtime can be detached when idle without changing the binding.
- **Binding lifetime:** the transport context still points to a Pi session.
- **Pi session retention:** the persisted JSONL remains resumable.
- **Gateway event/attachment retention:** governed by independent privacy policy.

Recommended default:

- Dedicated DM/thread/topic bindings do not automatically expire.
- `/new` or explicit policy rotates the session.
- Optional idle expiry is a **soft unbind/rotation evaluated on the next real inbound user message**, not deletion.
- Queues, heartbeats, retries, and maintenance must not extend human-activity freshness.
- Never expire while a run or approval is pending.
- Purging is a separate administrative operation and must account for both gateway storage and Pi session files.

Pi compaction is not retention deletion. It changes the active LLM context while the append-only session still contains the old entries. Pi session totals explicitly include compacted-away history: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.d.ts:640-645`.

## 5.9 Compaction and avoiding duplicate history

Let Pi own normal context-window management:

- Pi compacts before/within runs near the model limit and rebuilds context as summary plus retained recent messages: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/compaction.md:27-81`.
- It avoids cutting between a tool call and result: `.../docs/compaction.md:83-120`.
- Compaction and branch summaries are persisted session events.

For Model B:

- Never load “the last N IM messages” on each turn.
- Every accepted IM prompt is already in Pi history after submission.
- Only the new inbound message, one explicit reply/quote, and its new attachments are sent.

For Model C:

- Keep a per-session projection watermark and manifest.
- Include only previously unseen external events.
- Exclude bot output already represented by Pi assistant messages.
- Append corrections for later edits rather than re-including the whole window.
- Keep user attribution and trust classification through compaction.

The repository’s existing handoff policy is a useful precedent for deliberate transfer rather than implicit replay: it prefers the newest compaction summary, otherwise takes the first goal plus bounded recent messages; it excludes hidden thinking, images, tool arguments, and successful tool output; and it caps output at 128 KiB: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/sessions-and-handoff.md:50-87`.

## 5.10 Cross-device and cross-channel handoff

- Multiple devices viewing the same native DM or room naturally share the same transport key.
- Similar display names across channels do not establish identity.
- Cross-provider identity linking must be explicit and verified.
- `/resume` from another channel may attach that channel to the existing Pi session only after authorization and a warning that prior session context becomes visible there.
- Default handoff should **move** the writable binding, not silently create two active routes.
- If shared bindings are later supported, they must share one Pi-session execution lane, while each job still returns only to its captured origin.
- Cross-harness continuation should continue to use the repository’s deterministic handoff rather than raw session sharing; Pi and OMP version-3 files are intentionally not considered wire-compatible: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/sessions-and-handoff.md:27-48`.

---

# 6. Trust, prompt injection, approvals, and attribution

## Trust boundary

The MVP should support:

- one operator; or
- one mutually trusting team using an isolated gateway host/runtime.

It should not claim hostile multi-tenant isolation. OpenClaw’s current security model reaches the same conclusion: one trust boundary per gateway, and separate gateway/credentials/OS user or host for mutually adversarial users: [security/index.md:17-34](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/gateway/security/index.md#L17-L34).

## Prompt treatment

- Current actor text, quoted text, ambient history, attachments, links, repository content, and tool output are all untrusted data.
- Never concatenate transport metadata or quoted history into a privileged system instruction.
- Strip or neutralize provider formatting only for parsing safety; do not claim sanitization solves prompt injection.
- The gateway authorization layer, not the model, decides project access, session access, tools, paths, outbound recipients, and approval validity.
- Ordinary IM messages must not automatically invoke Pi extension commands or expand arbitrary skills/templates. Pi RPC explicitly expands skill/template commands and executes extension commands immediately, even while streaming: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/rpc.md:56-76`. Gateway commands need their own authenticated namespace.

OWASP and NIST both treat indirect instructions in documents, web content, email, and files as an agent-hijacking risk; the important mitigations are structural separation, least privilege, independent tool authorization, sandboxing, and human approval—not a text filter alone.

## Approval contract

For mutating or consequential tools:

- Tool policy is checked before approval; approval cannot override a forbidden capability.
- Bind approval to the exact Pi session, originating job, tool-call ID, tool name, normalized arguments, cwd/project, actor, and policy revision.
- Default to allow-once.
- Expire pending approvals and deny on timeout, disconnect, session switch, cancellation, or parameter change.
- Only a project-authorized approver may resolve it; membership in a chat is insufficient.
- Quoted text, forwarded messages, bot-authored content, and ordinary reactions cannot grant approval.
- Record initiator and approver separately.
- A late approval never revives an aborted run.
- If the gateway cannot surface a confirmation UI, block the tool.

Pi provides a stable interception point: `tool_call` fires before execution and can block: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/extensions.md:776-817`. RPC translates extension confirmations into correlated `extension_ui_request`/`extension_ui_response` messages and blocks while waiting: `.../docs/rpc.md:1184-1205` and `:1207-1374`. The bundled permission example fails closed when no UI exists: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts:13-29`.

## Attribution

Every accepted invocation should retain:

- canonical actor ID and display label at receipt time;
- provider/account/tenant/conversation/subconversation IDs;
- provider message/event ID and revision;
- reply/quote source;
- project binding and Pi session/leaf;
- gateway job ID;
- Pi entry IDs produced by the job;
- tool-call initiator and separate approver;
- outbound route and resulting platform message IDs.

The model should see enough sender attribution to reason about a shared conversation, while sensitive routing identifiers can live in `CustomMessageEntry.details`, which Pi documents as metadata not sent to the model: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:85-103`.

---

# 7. Privacy and deletion expectations

The gateway creates additional copies even in the router model:

- provider-side message;
- short-lived gateway inbox payload;
- Pi session entry;
- possibly base64 image content;
- model-provider request;
- logs and outbound receipts;
- tool-created files.

Therefore:

- Collect only explicitly admitted messages.
- Keep full raw inbound payloads only as long as required for retry/reconciliation.
- Encrypt state at rest where practical and use owner-only filesystem permissions.
- Never put tokens or credentials in prompts, session metadata, or logs.
- Do not send hidden thinking or full tool output back into IM.
- Use separate data-retention settings for events, attachments, audit metadata, and Pi sessions.
- Expose a clear distinction between “delete the IM message,” “forget gateway copy,” and “delete the Pi session.”
- Warn that deletion cannot undo model-provider exposure, repository changes, shell commands, network calls, or messages already sent elsewhere.
- Treat end-to-end encryption as terminating at the gateway: once decrypted for Pi, plaintext exists inside the gateway/Pi trust boundary.

Pi itself says that project trust is not sandboxing and recommends OS/container isolation, minimal mounts/credentials, and restricted networking for untrusted or unattended work: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/security.md:31-53`.

---

# 8. Pi API fit

| Surface | Fit | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Public SDK** | Best default for this TypeScript repository | Direct `AgentSession`, `AgentSessionRuntime`, `SessionManager`, custom messages/details, event subscriptions, and tool hooks. The SDK docs explicitly prefer it for Node/TypeScript, type safety, direct state, and programmatic customization: `.../docs/sdk.md:1145-1165`. |
| **RPC mode** | Strong isolation alternative | Language-neutral/process-isolated; has request correlation, new/switch/fork/clone, images, `get_entries(since)`, `agent_settled`, queue clearing, and UI dialogs. One worker should own one active writable session. |
| **Pi extension alone** | Only for a remote-console model or policy hooks | Good for tool interception and UI integration, but lifecycle is attached to an active Pi runtime and session replacement requires careful rebinding. It is the wrong primary owner for many simultaneous IM contexts. |
| **JSON event mode** | Diagnostics/one-shot output | Streams events but lacks the bidirectional lifecycle/control contract required by a gateway. |
| **Raw session JSONL manipulation** | Reject | The format is documented, but direct concurrent appends, rewrites, or synthetic edits bypass runtime invariants. Read for diagnostics/migration only. |
| **Experimental Pi Client/CBOR remote protocol** | Promising future path | It already has authoritative snapshots, multiple attached sessions, and exclusive/shared leases: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-client/README.md:26-34`. But the protocol explicitly has no compatibility guarantees: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-protocol/README.md:1-10` and `:69`. |

Pin Pi exactly and isolate it behind a small adapter. Pi is still pre-1.0 and has made documented breaking session-runtime changes; 0.65.0 moved replacement operations from `AgentSession` to `AgentSessionRuntime`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md:2116-2129`.

---

# 9. Explicit MVP non-goals

1. No full IM history synchronization.
2. No automatic inclusion of messages merely because they are nearby in a room.
3. No automatic cross-channel or cross-account identity linking.
4. No shared global DM session.
5. No hostile multi-tenant isolation on one host.
6. No simultaneous local-TUI and gateway writers to the same Pi session.
7. No implicit steering by later messages; normal arrivals queue as separate turns.
8. No retroactive mutation of Pi history after IM edits/deletes.
9. No promise of exactly-once tool execution or outbound delivery.
10. No reaction-based approvals initially.
11. No arbitrary archive/document ingestion; images only until file policy is designed.
12. No streaming partial assistant messages into IM initially; deliver authoritative completed messages.
13. No exposure of hidden thinking, secrets, complete tool output, raw session paths, or unrestricted session listings.
14. No replacement of Pi’s compaction logic with gateway-generated summaries.
15. No assumption that a channel, topic name, reply, mention, or display username is a stable identity.

---

# 10. Promotion triggers

Promote from Model B to **bounded history projection** when measured use shows:

- frequent “you missed the discussion above” failures;
- a material share of traffic comes from threadless collaborative rooms;
- users routinely reference messages the bot was not sent;
- reply payloads often omit enough source text to understand the request;
- a strict, testable context-visibility policy exists;
- the added token/privacy cost is accepted.

Promote to an **event-sourced mirror** only when requirements include:

- durable audit/replay of edits, deletions, reactions, and topic moves;
- legal hold or precise deletion/export workflows;
- high-availability gateways and long offline catch-up;
- multiple downstream agents or re-projection of the same conversation;
- cross-channel unified inbox semantics;
- deterministic migration of conversation projections;
- provider event loss must be detected and repaired.

Adopt Pi’s remote client/protocol only when it loses the explicit experimental/no-compatibility status and documents reconnect/replay and durable operation semantics suitable for gateway recovery.

If users are mutually untrusted, do **not** “promote” the context model. Split gateway, credentials, workspace, and preferably OS/container boundaries.

---

# Repository-level recommendation

1. Treat the current Discord/OpenCode document as a useful deployment baseline, not a portable context contract.
2. Document the Pi-authoritative session-router semantics before implementing adapters.
3. If implementation is approved, make the gateway an optional standalone service/package that consumes existing combo/session resolution; keep `pia`’s core focused on declarative configurations and explicit launch/session operations.
4. Use extensions only for Pi-side policy hooks and approval UI, not as the durable multi-session router.
5. Treat `pi-messenger-bridge` as a useful single-session remote-control reference, not a production multi-user foundation.
6. Do not begin with an IM-native mirror.

No repository files were modified.

Decision:
{"verdict":"docs-first","confidence":"high","executive_summary":"Choose docs/research first. Do not add an IM gateway, daemon command, transport configuration, runtime dependency, or even a committed gateway combo yet. Remote IM control is a separate Pi-specific security and operations product, while pia is a dependency-free, foreground, Pi/OMP-neutral configuration launcher. The repository should record the dated decision and promotion contract, then test existing external projects out of tree. 1	# pi-agents
2	
3	`pi-agents` keeps multiple [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) and
4	[Oh My Pi](https://omp.sh/) harness combinations in one Git repository. Its
5	`pia` CLI selects a combo, safely materialises its configuration into private
6	runtime state, and launches the matching agent without putting credentials or
7	session history in Git.
8	
9	The design stays deliberately small: each combo contains a complete config
10	tree, derived combos are normal copies with explicit lineage metadata, and
11	parent changes are reviewed rather than merged implicitly.
12	
13	`pia` is written in [Node-native TypeScript](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.21.0/docs/api/typescript.html).
14	Node 22.19+ executes the erasable
15	`.ts` sources directly, so deployed checkouts need no build step or runtime
16	packages; TypeScript and Node type definitions are development-only tools used
17	by `npm run typecheck` and CI.
18	
19	## Quick start
20	
21	Requirements: Node.js 22.19 or newer, plus `pi` and/or `omp` for the combos you
22	want to run.
23	
24	```sh
25	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/pi-agents.git
26	cd pi-agents
27	
28	# Optional for a development checkout; chezmoi deployments put bin/ on PATH.
29	npm link
30	
31	pia doctor
32	pia list --tree
33	pia apply pi/base --dry-run
34	pia run pi/base --
35	```
36	
37	No link is required to run directly from a checkout:
38	
39	```sh
40	./bin/pia --version              # macOS/Linux
41	```
42	
43	```powershell
44	.\bin\pia.ps1 --version         # Windows PowerShell
45	```
46	
47	```bat
48	bin\pia.cmd --version           # Windows cmd.exe
49	```
50	
51	When `bin/` is on `PATH`, all three environments use the command name `pia`.
52	The PowerShell launcher preserves literal argument boundaries and the child
53	exit code. The cmd launcher follows cmd.exe's normal quoting rules and is for
54	trusted interactive commands; programmatic callers with arbitrary input should
55	invoke `pia.ps1` through PowerShell. If an npm-installed harness is exposed as
56	a shim such as `pi.ps1`, `pia` invokes it through a fixed `PowerShell -File`
57	command and never enables child-process shell parsing.
58	
59	`pia run` safely applies the selected source before launch and stops on runtime
60	drift or an unowned collision. You can also save a default instead of naming
61	the combo every time:
62	
63	```sh
64	pia use pi/base
65	pia current
66	pia run -- --model provider/model
67	```
68	
69	Selection precedence is an explicit argument, then `PIA_COMBO`, then the value
70	saved by `pia use`.
71	
72	`pia` can generate native completion for every managed shell:
73	
74	```sh
75	pia completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_pia
76	pia completion bash > "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/pia"
77	```
78	
79	```powershell
80	pia completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
81	```
82	
83	Completion discovers combo directories directly, so `pia use <Tab>` reflects
84	newly derived or pulled combos without launching another Node process. The
85	provided chezmoi integrations generate/cache these scripts automatically.
86	
87	Human-readable output uses semantic terminal colours when the selected stream
88	supports them. `NO_COLOR` and `NODE_DISABLE_COLORS` disable colour;
89	`FORCE_COLOR` and non-zero `CLICOLOR_FORCE` can force it through a pipe. JSON,
90	completion code, versions, selected combo ids, and artifact paths always stay
91	plain for scripts.
92	
93	The compatibility snapshot for the current implementation is **Pi 0.84.4**
94	and **OMP 18.0.11**. Tests cover the wrapper's behavior and pinned session
95	fixtures; run `pia doctor` and a smoke launch when using a different upstream
96	version.
97	
98	## What is included
99	
100	- `combos/pi/base`: neutral upstream Pi configuration.
101	- `combos/pi/vanilla`: Pi with project/global resource discovery disabled by
102	  launch flags.
103	- `combos/omp/base`: neutral OMP native profile configuration.
104	- Strict source-to-runtime synchronisation with drift detection and dry runs.
105	- Per-combo or explicitly shared session storage, same-engine forks, and
106	  deterministic redacted handoffs across harnesses.
107	
108	Start with [combo authoring](docs/combos.md), then read
109	[architecture](docs/architecture.md),
110	[sessions and handoff](docs/sessions-and-handoff.md), the
111	[ecosystem snapshot](docs/ecosystem.md), and the optional
112	[chezmoi integration](docs/chezmoi.md).
113	
114	```sh
115	npm install --ignore-scripts   # development/type-check dependencies only
116	npm test
117	npm run typecheck
118	npm run check
119	```
120	
121	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap -->

123	
124	Future work is indexed in [TODO.md](TODO.md), with longer research under
125	[backlog/](backlog/). Past traps and their workarounds live under
126	[pitfalls/](pitfalls/).
127	<!-- project-knowledge-harness:readme-roadmap (end) -->
128
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Architecture
2	
3	`pia` separates version-controlled intent from mutable agent state. The Git
4	repository is the source of truth for combo definitions; it is never an agent's
5	live home directory.
6	
7	## Data layout
8	
9	```text
10	pi-agents/
11	  combos/<pi|omp>/<name>/
12	    combo.json             declarative metadata
13	    agent/                 complete managed config tree
14	  schema/combo.schema.json
15	  bin/pia
16	  src/*.ts                 Node-native erasable TypeScript
17	
18	${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/pi-agents/
19	  selection.json           value saved by `pia use`
20	
21	${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents/
22	  manifests/               last-applied managed-file hashes and modes
23	  runtime/pi/<name>/agent/ Pi configuration runtime
24	  sessions/                isolated/shared session roots
25	  handoffs/                generated private Markdown artifacts
26	```
27	
28	`PIA_SOURCE_ROOT` can point the CLI at another checkout. `PIA_STATE_HOME`
29	replaces the entire state root. These overrides are useful for tests and
30	advanced setups; normal users should let the CLI derive both paths.
31	
32	For Pi, `pia` launches with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to the combo's runtime
33	directory. For OMP, it uses a native profile named `pia-<combo-name>` and asks
34	`omp --profile ... config path` for the real location instead of assuming a
35	home or XDG layout. `PIA_PI_BIN` and `PIA_OMP_BIN` can override the executable
36	names.
37	
38	## Source and runtime contract
39	
40	Only files below a combo's `agent/` directory are managed. Downloaded packages,
41	credentials, sessions, caches, blobs, databases, and any other runtime-created
42	files stay outside Git or remain unowned in the runtime tree.
43	
44	The source tree must not contain credentials, `.env` files, session/package/
45	cache stores, or symlinks. On POSIX systems runtime directories are created
46	with mode `0700`; managed files use `0600` or `0700` according to their
47	executable bit. Windows does not expose equivalent POSIX mode enforcement
48	through Node, so runtime files inherit the user's profile ACL and drift checks
49	compare content rather than synthetic mode bits there. Writes and manifest
50	replacement are atomic.
51	
52	The source uses only TypeScript syntax that Node can erase without code
53	generation. Runtime execution therefore stays build-free; `tsconfig.json` and
54	the development dependencies exist solely for strict `tsc --noEmit` checking.
55	
56	Known runtime/credential paths are rejected structurally. `npm run check` also
57	runs gitleaks over combo content when the binary is available, while CI and the
58	existing pre-commit stack enforce the same secret scan before source is shared.
59	
60	Each manifest records its exact absolute target and, for every managed relative
61	path, the content hash, executable bit, and mode. `pia apply` classifies paths
62	as follows:
63	
64	| Source/runtime state | Result |
65	|---|---|
66	| New source path, unused target | Create it |
67	| Source changed, runtime still at last applied value | Update it |
68	| Runtime changed independently | Refuse the whole apply |
69	| Source and runtime both changed | Refuse the whole apply |
70	| Source removed, runtime unchanged | Remove the stale managed path |
71	| Source removed, runtime changed | Refuse unless forced |
72	| Target-only path never owned by `pia` | Preserve and omit from normal diff |
73	| New source collides with an unowned path or non-file obstruction | Always refuse |
74	
75	`--dry-run` returns the same plan without writing. `--force` makes source win
76	for previously managed drift and conflicts, including modified stale files; it
77	does not overwrite unowned collisions. This keeps force bounded by the prior
78	manifest instead of turning it into a recursive replacement operation.
79	
80	Use `pia status <combo>` for a summary and `pia diff <combo> --runtime` for
81	managed path details before applying.
82	
83	## Selection and launch
84	
85	A combo is selected in this order:
86	
87	1. The combo argument passed to the command.
88	2. `PIA_COMBO`.
89	3. The persistent value written by `pia use`.
90	
91	`pia run [combo] -- <agent arguments>` first performs the same safe apply, then
92	combines the combo's checked-in `launchArgs` with trailing arguments and
93	forwards the child process's exit code. Drift, conflicts, unsafe source files,
94	or unowned collisions abort before launch. A stale parent digest emits a warning
95	but does not block a standalone child combo.
96	
97	Wrapper-owned routing/session flags and secret-bearing flags are rejected from
98	`launchArgs`; runtime invocation remains explicit. Session storage is resolved
99	from engine, combo history policy, and canonical working directory. See
100	[sessions and handoff](sessions-and-handoff.md).
101	
102	## Why copies instead of inheritance
103	
104	Pi does not expose a stable, general-purpose config inheritance contract, and
105	OMP's layers do not cover every harness asset uniformly. `pia derive` therefore
106	copies a complete combo and records its parent digest. The child remains usable
107	and understandable on its own. Parent changes produce a lineage warning and a
108	review workflow, never an implicit merge at launch time.
109	
110	Declarative inheritance and three-way sync are intentionally deferred until
111	real usage demonstrates enough repeated maintenance to justify their conflict
112	rules. The research checkpoint is tracked in
113	[the backlog](../backlog/declarative-inheritance-three-way-sync.md).
114

```text
1	# Pi harness ecosystem snapshot
2	
3	This page records the assumptions behind `pia`, not a permanent verdict on fast
4	moving upstream projects. The compatibility snapshot reviewed and represented
5	by the test fixtures is **Pi 0.84.4** and **Oh My Pi 18.0.11**, as of
6	2026-08-30.
7	
8	## Upstream Pi
9	
10	Pi supports a global agent directory, project-local `.pi` configuration, and
11	the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` override. These primitives are sufficient for `pia`
12	to launch isolated full configurations, while repo-local settings and resources
13	can still participate according to Pi's trust and discovery rules. See Pi's
14	[settings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md),
15	[environment variables](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md),
16	and [packages](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages) documentation.
17	
18	Pi does not provide a single stable first-class abstraction that composes all
19	settings, skills, extensions, package references, prompts, and session policy as
20	a named inheritable profile. That is why `pia` switches the complete agent
21	directory and keeps combo inheritance explicit and copy-based.
22	
23	Two issue pages are easy to misread:
24	
25	- [#3590, layered config](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3590)
26	- [#7813, multiple settings profiles](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7813)
27	
28	Their closed status is easy to over-interpret, but each timeline contains the
29	GitHub Actions message that issues from new contributors are auto-closed
30	pending maintainer review. They are evidence that users asked
31	for these capabilities, **not** an explicit maintainer roadmap rejection. Any
32	future design review should re-check upstream rather than preserving either
33	interpretation as fact.
34	
35	## Oh My Pi
36	
37	OMP exposes named profiles through `omp --profile <name>` and has broader
38	configuration discovery and overlay behavior. A named profile relocates native
39	configuration and runtime resources, so `pia` uses an OMP profile named
40	`pia-<combo>` and resolves its actual path with OMP itself. See the upstream
41	[configuration and profile guide](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/config-usage.md).
42	
43	OMP's richer configuration system does not remove the need for a repository
44	contract: different resource types have different discovery rules, runtime
45	state must still stay out of Git, and a Pi combo should remain understandable
46	without translating it into OMP concepts. `pia` therefore presents the same
47	simple combo/source/runtime workflow for both engines and lets OMP own only its
48	native profile resolution.
49	
50	## MCP is an extension choice
51	
52	Do not describe `pi.mcp` as a Pi core package-manifest feature. The manifest
53	shape discussed in the original research belongs to an adapter/integration,
54	not upstream Pi's package contract. MCP support for a combo should identify the
55	specific extension it uses—for example the community
56	[`pi-mcp-adapter`](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter)—and keep that
57	adapter's configuration inside the combo like any other harness dependency.
58	
59	This distinction matters for portability: a combo that depends on an adapter
60	must pin and test that adapter rather than assuming another Pi installation can
61	interpret an undocumented `pi.mcp` field.
62	
63	## Why maintain another thin layer?
64	
65	There are many ready-made harnesses and profile managers. Use one of them when
66	its opinionated defaults already match the job. This repository is justified
67	when the goal is to:
68	
69	- keep experimental, learning, and production combos together;
70	- switch Pi and OMP through one predictable interface;
71	- review the exact Git-managed configuration before it reaches runtime;
72	- keep auth, sessions, packages, and caches private and mutable;
73	- reproduce selected behaviors from other harnesses without adopting all of
74	  their machinery.
75	
76	Research into [Claude Code](../backlog/claude-code-harness-to-pi.md),
77	[Codex](../backlog/codex-harness-to-pi.md), and
78	[OpenCode](../backlog/opencode-harness-to-pi.md) is intentionally deferred until
79	the base workflow has real usage data. Re-check upstream versions, docs, CLI
80	flags, and session formats before promoting any result to a production combo.
81
```
</details></tool-use>

57	  return engine === "pi" ? env.PIA_PI_BIN || "pi" : env.PIA_OMP_BIN || "omp";
58	}

60	function assertNoOwnedFlags(args: readonly string[]): void {
61	  let literal = false;
62	  for (const arg of args) {
63	    if (arg === "--") {
64	      literal = true;
65	      continue;
66	    }
67	    if (literal) continue;
68	    const flag = arg.includes("=") ? arg.slice(0, arg.indexOf("=")) : arg;
69	    if (WRAPPER_OWNED_FLAGS.has(flag)) {
70	      throw new Error(`Pass ${flag} through combo metadata is not allowed; pia owns runtime isolation and credentials`);
71	    }
72	  }

79	export async function resolveRuntimeTarget(
80	  combo: Combo,
81	  stateRoot: string,
82	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,
83	  runner: CommandRunner = commandResult,
84	): Promise<string> {
85	  if (combo.engine === "pi") return getPiRuntimeDir(stateRoot, combo);
86	  const binary = binaryFor("omp", env);
87	  const profile = getOmpProfileName(combo);
88	  const result = runner(binary, [`--profile=${profile}`, "config", "path"], { env });
89	  if (!result.ok) {
90	    const detail = (result.stderr || result.stdout || "OMP is not installed or could not resolve its profile").trim();
91	    throw new Error(`Unable to resolve OMP profile ${profile}: ${detail}`);
92	  }
93	  const target = result.stdout.trim().split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).at(-1);
94	  if (!target || !path.isAbsolute(target)) throw new Error(`OMP returned an invalid profile path: ${JSON.stringify(target)}`);
95	  const resolved = path.resolve(target);
96	  if (path.basename(resolved) !== "agent" || path.basename(path.dirname(resolved)) !== profile) {
97	    throw new Error(`OMP profile path is outside the expected ${profile}/agent shape: ${resolved}`);
98	  }
99	  for (const candidate of [path.dirname(resolved), resolved]) {
100	    try {
101	      const stat = await lstat(candidate);
102	      if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`OMP profile path contains a symbolic link: ${candidate}`);
103	      if (!stat.isDirectory()) throw new Error(`OMP profile path component is not a directory: ${candidate}`);
104	    } catch (error) {
105	      if (!isNodeError(error) || error.code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
106	    }
107	  }
108	  return resolved;
109	}

111	export async function runtimeContext({
112	  combo,
113	  stateRoot,
114	  cwd = process.cwd(),
115	  env = process.env,
116	  commandRunner,
117	}: RuntimeContextOptions): Promise<RuntimeContext> {
118	  const targetDir = await resolveRuntimeTarget(combo, stateRoot, env, commandRunner ?? commandResult);
119	  const manifestPath = getManifestPath(stateRoot, combo);
120	  const sessionOptions: SessionLeafOptions = {
121	    stateRoot,
122	    engine: combo.engine,
123	    comboName: combo.name,
124	    cwd,
125	    history: combo.metadata.history,
126	  };
127	  const sessionDir = sessionLeafDir(sessionOptions);
128	  return { targetDir, manifestPath, sessionDir };
129	}

132	  const context = await runtimeContext(options);
133	  return {
134	    ...context,
135	    status: await getRuntimeStatus({
136	      sourceDir: options.combo.agentDir,

139	    }),

144	  const context = await runtimeContext(options);
145	  return {
146	    ...context,
147	    result: await applyRuntime({
148	      sourceDir: options.combo.agentDir,
149	      targetDir: context.targetDir,
150	      manifestPath: context.manifestPath,
151	      dryRun: options.dryRun || false,
152	      force: options.force || false,
153	    }),
154	  };
155	}
156	
157	export async function runCombo({
158	  combo,
159	  stateRoot,
160	  cwd = process.cwd(),
161	  env = process.env,
162	  userArgs = [],
163	  commandRunner,
164	  spawnRunner = runInherited,
165	}: RunComboOptions): Promise<RunComboResult> {
166	  assertNoOwnedFlags(userArgs);
167	  const applied = await applyCombo({ combo, stateRoot, cwd, env, commandRunner });
168	  if (!applied.result.ok) {
169	    const reason = applied.result.reason || "runtime configuration has unresolved drift";
170	    throw new Error(`Refusing to launch ${combo.id}: ${reason}`);
171	  }
172	  await ensurePrivateDir(applied.sessionDir);
173	
174	  const childEnv = { ...env };
175	  delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR;
176	  const args = [];
177	  if (combo.engine === "pi") {
178	    childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR = applied.targetDir;
179	  } else {
180	    delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR;
181	    delete childEnv.OMP_PROFILE;
182	    delete childEnv.PI_PROFILE;
183	    args.push(`--profile=${getOmpProfileName(combo)}`);
184	  }
185	  args.push(...combo.metadata.launchArgs, "--session-dir", applied.sessionDir, ...userArgs);
186	  const exitCode = await spawnRunner(binaryFor(combo.engine, env), args, { cwd, env: childEnv });
187	  return { exitCode, args, command: binaryFor(combo.engine, env), ...applied };
188	}

187	export function projectKey(cwd: string): string {

190	  const sanitized = rawBase

196	  return `${base}-${digest}`;

232	  const byId = new Map<string, ActiveSessionEntry>();
233	  let leaf: ActiveSessionEntry | undefined;
234	  for (const rawEntry of entries) {
235	    if (!isRecord(rawEntry) || typeof rawEntry.id !== 'string' || rawEntry.id === '') continue;

237	    if (byId.has(entry.id)) {

246	  const visited = new Set<string>();
247	  let current: ActiveSessionEntry | undefined = leaf;

250	      fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_TREE', `Cycle in session entry parents at ${current.id}`);
251	    }
252	    visited.add(current.id);
253	    reverse.push(current);

255	    if (typeof current.parentId !== 'string' || current.parentId === '') {

258	    const parent = byId.get(current.parentId);
259	    if (!parent) {
260	      fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_TREE', `Missing parent ${current.parentId} for session entry ${current.id}`);

263	  }
264	  return reverse.reverse();

272	  if (engine !== undefined) requireEngine(engine);
273	  if (typeof content !== 'string' || content === '') {

276	
277	  const physicalLines = content.split('\n');
278	  if (physicalLines.at(-1) === '') physicalLines.pop();
279	  if (physicalLines.length === 0) fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION', `Empty session file: ${filePath}`);
280	
281	  let logicalIndex = 0;
282	  let titleSlot: OmpTitleSlot | undefined;
283	  const first = parseLine(physicalLines[0], 1, filePath);
284	  if (first.type === 'title') {
285	    if (engine === 'pi') {

287	    }
288	    if (!isTitleSlot(first)) {

290	    }
291	    if (Buffer.byteLength(`${physicalLines[0]}\n`, 'utf8') !== OMP_TITLE_SLOT_BYTES) {
292	      fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION', `OMP title slot is not ${OMP_TITLE_SLOT_BYTES} bytes in ${filePath}`);
293	    }
294	    titleSlot = first;
295	    logicalIndex = 1;
296	  }
297	
298	  if (logicalIndex >= physicalLines.length) {
299	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION', `Session header is missing from ${filePath}`);
300	  }
301	  const headerRecord = parseLine(physicalLines[logicalIndex], logicalIndex + 1, filePath);
302	  if (

304	    typeof headerRecord.id !== 'string' ||

306	    typeof headerRecord.cwd !== 'string'

309	  }
310	  const header = headerRecord as SessionHeader;

312	  const entries: SessionEntry[] = [];

315	  }

323	  return {

325	    title,
326	    titleSlot,
327	    header,
328	    id: header.id,
329	    cwd: header.cwd,
330	    entries,

390	    .sort();
391	  const sessions = await Promise.all(files.map((filePath) => parseSessionFile(filePath, { engine })));

397	export async function resolveSession({
398	  sessionDir,

401	  engine,
402	}: ResolveSessionOptions = {}): Promise<ParsedSessionFile> {
403	  if (selector !== undefined && (typeof selector !== 'string' || selector.trim() === '')) {
404	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_SELECTOR', 'Session selector must be a non-empty string');
405	  }
406	  if (latest && selector !== undefined && selector !== 'latest') {
407	    fail('PIA_INVALID_SESSION_SELECTOR', 'Choose either a selector or latest, not both');
408	  }
409	  if (selector && path.isAbsolute(selector)) {
410	    return await parseSessionFile(selector, { engine });
411	  }
412	
413	  const wantsLatest = latest || selector === 'latest';
414	  if (!wantsLatest && selector === undefined) {
415	    fail('PIA_SESSION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED', 'Specify an absolute session path, ID prefix, or latest');
416	  }
417	  const sessions = await listSessions({ sessionDir, engine });
418	  if (sessions.length === 0) {
419	    fail('PIA_SESSION_NOT_FOUND', `No sessions found under ${path.resolve(sessionDir || '')}`);
420	  }
421	  if (wantsLatest) return sessions[0];
422	
423	  const prefix = selector!.toLowerCase();
424	  const matches = sessions.filter((session) => session.id.toLowerCase().startsWith(prefix));
425	  if (matches.length === 0) fail('PIA_SESSION_NOT_FOUND', `No session ID starts with ${selector}`);
426	  if (matches.length > 1) {
427	    fail('PIA_AMBIGUOUS_SESSION', `Session ID prefix ${selector} matches ${matches.length} sessions`, {
428	      matches: matches.map((session) => ({ id: session.id, path: session.path })),
429	    });
430	  }
431	  return matches[0];

440	): true {
441	  const objectOptions = typeof sourceOrOptions === 'object' ? sourceOrOptions : undefined;
442	  const sourceEngine = objectOptions

290	    visiting.delete(id);
291	    visited.add(id);
292	  };
293	  for (const combo of combos) visit(combo.id);
294	  return byId;
295	}
296	
297	export async function comboDigest(combo: Combo): Promise<string> {
298	  const metadata: Partial<ComboMetadata> = { ...combo.metadata };
299	  delete metadata.$schema;
300	  delete metadata.derivedFrom;
301	  delete metadata.parentDigest;
302	  const agentDigest = await treeContentDigest(combo.agentDir);
303	  const hash = createHash("sha256");
304	  hash.update(JSON.stringify(stable(metadata)));
305	  hash.update("\0");
306	  hash.update(agentDigest);
307	  return `sha256:${hash.digest("hex")}`;
308	}
309	
310	export async function lineageInfo(sourceRoot: string, comboId: string): Promise<LineageInfo> {
311	  const combos = await listCombos(sourceRoot);
312	  const byId = new Map(combos.map((combo) => [combo.id, combo]));
313	  const combo = byId.get(comboId);
314	  if (!combo) throw new Error(`Unknown combo ${comboId}`);
315	  const ancestors: LineageAncestor[] = [];
316	  let cursor = combo;
317	  while (cursor.metadata.derivedFrom) {
318	    const parent = byId.get(cursor.metadata.derivedFrom);
319	    if (!parent) throw new Error(`${cursor.id}: parent combo ${cursor.metadata.derivedFrom} does not exist`);
320	    const digest = await comboDigest(parent);
321	    ancestors.push({
322	      id: parent.id,
323	      digest,
324	      reviewed: cursor.metadata.parentDigest === digest,
325	      recordedDigest: cursor.metadata.parentDigest as string,
326	    });
327	    cursor = parent;
328	  }
329	  const descendants = combos.filter((item) => item.metadata.derivedFrom === comboId).map((item) => item.id);
330	  return { combo, ancestors, descendants };
331	}
332	
333	export async function acknowledgeParent(sourceRoot: string, comboId: string): Promise<string> {
334	  const combos = await listCombos(sourceRoot);
335	  const byId = new Map(combos.map((combo) => [combo.id, combo]));
336	  const combo = byId.get(comboId);
337	  if (!combo) throw new Error(`Unknown combo ${comboId}`);
338	  const parentId = combo.metadata.derivedFrom;
339	  if (!parentId) throw new Error(`${comboId} has no parent`);
340	  const parent = byId.get(parentId);
341	  if (!parent) throw new Error(`${comboId}: parent combo ${parentId} does not exist`);
342	  const digest = await comboDigest(parent);
343	  const metadata = { ...combo.metadata, parentDigest: digest };
344	  await writeSourceJsonAtomic(combo.metadataPath, metadata);
345	  return digest;
346	}
347	
348	export async function deriveCombo(
349	  sourceRoot: string,
350	  parentId: string,
351	  childId: string,
352	  description?: string,
353	): Promise<Combo> {
354	  const parent = await loadCombo(sourceRoot, parentId);
355	  const childParts = parseComboId(childId);
356	  if (childParts.engine !== parent.engine) throw new Error("A derived combo must use the same engine as its parent");
357	  const childDir = path.join(sourceRoot, "combos", childParts.engine, childParts.name);
358	  try {
359	    await lstat(childDir);
360	    throw new Error(`Target combo ${childId} already exists`);
361	  } catch (error) {
362	    if (!isNodeError(error) || error.code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
363	  }
364	  await scanTree(parent.agentDir);
365	  await mkdir(path.dirname(childDir), { recursive: true });
366	  await cp(parent.comboDir, childDir, { recursive: true, errorOnExist: true, force: false });
367	  const parentDigest = await comboDigest(parent);
368	  const metadata = {
369	    ...parent.metadata,
370	    description: description || `Derived from ${parentId}.`,
371	    derivedFrom: parentId,
372	    parentDigest,
373	  };
374	  await writeSourceJsonAtomic(path.join(childDir, "combo.json"), metadata);
375	  return await loadCombo(sourceRoot, childId);
376	}
377	
378	export function renderComboTree(combos: readonly Combo[]): string {
379	  const children = new Map<string | null, Combo[]>();
380	  for (const combo of combos) {
381	    const parent = combo.metadata.derivedFrom || null;
382	    const list = children.get(parent) || [];
383	    list.push(combo);
384	    children.set(parent, list);
385	  }
386	  for (const list of children.values()) list.sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
387	  const lines: string[] = [];
388	  const walkChildren = (combo: Combo, prefix: string): void => {
389	    const next = children.get(combo.id) || [];
390	    next.forEach((child, index) => {
391	      const last = index === next.length - 1;
392	      lines.push(`${prefix}${last ? "└─ " : "├─ "}${child.id} [${child.metadata.maturity}]`);
393	      walkChildren(child, `${prefix}${last ? "   " : "│  "}`);
394	    });
395	  };
396	  const roots = children.get(null) || [];
397	  roots.forEach((root) => {
398	    lines.push(`${root.id} [${root.metadata.maturity}]`);
399	    walkChildren(root, "");
400	  });
401	  return lines.join("\n");
402	}
403
```

```text
1	# Combos
2	
3	A combo is one complete, selectable agent setup. Its identifier is
4	`<engine>/<name>`, where the engine is `pi` or `omp`. Names are 1–60 characters,
5	start with a lowercase letter or digit, use lowercase letters, digits, dots,
6	underscores, or hyphens, and do not end in a dot. The shared restriction keeps
7	the generated `pia-<name>` value valid as an OMP profile.
8	
9	## Directory and metadata
10	
11	```text
12	combos/pi/research/
13	  combo.json
14	  agent/
15	    settings.json
16	    AGENTS.md
17	    skills/
18	    extensions/
19	```
20	
21	`agent/` mirrors the configuration files that should be managed at runtime. It
22	must be a complete, readable setup rather than a delta against another combo.
23	
24	A minimal `combo.json` is:
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "$schema": "../../../schema/combo.schema.json",
29	  "schemaVersion": 1,
30	  "description": "Research-oriented upstream Pi harness.",
31	  "maturity": "experimental",
32	  "launchArgs": [],
33	  "history": {
34	    "mode": "isolated"
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	The fields are:
40	
41	- `schemaVersion`: currently `1`.
42	- `description`: a short human explanation of the combo's purpose.
43	- `maturity`: `experimental`, `learning`, or `production`.
44	- `launchArgs`: non-secret agent arguments applied on every launch.
45	- `history`: `isolated`, or `shared` with a named same-engine group.
46	- `derivedFrom` and `parentDigest`: a paired lineage reference written by
47	  `pia derive`.
48	
49	Example shared history policy:
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "history": {
54	    "mode": "shared",
55	    "group": "daily-coding"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Sharing is still separated by engine and canonical project directory. It does
61	not make Pi and OMP JSONL files interchangeable. Group names follow the same
62	1–60 character/no-trailing-dot safety rule as combo names.
63	
64	Do not put auth tokens, API keys, `.env` files, sessions, blobs, package stores,
65	or caches in `agent/`. Reference packages from configuration; let the harness
66	install or cache them in runtime state.
67	
68	## Derive and maintain a combo
69	
70	Create a child from an existing combo:
71	
72	```sh
73	pia derive pi/base pi/research
74	```
75	
76	This makes a full copy, sets `derivedFrom`, and records a digest of the reviewed
77	parent. There is no live inheritance. Edit the child normally and commit it as
78	a standalone configuration.
79	
80	When a parent changes:
81	
82	```sh
83	pia lineage pi/research
84	pia diff pi/research --parent
85	# manually copy or adapt only the changes you want
86	pia lineage pi/research --ack
87	```
88	
89	`--ack` only records the current parent digest. It must be run after the review,
90	not as a way to hide an unresolved warning. Lineage must remain within one
91	engine and cycles are rejected.
92	
93	## Inspect and use combos
94	
95	```sh
96	pia list
97	pia list --tree
98	pia list --json
99	
100	pia use pi/research
101	pia current
102	
103	pia status pi/research
104	pia diff pi/research --runtime
105	pia apply pi/research --dry-run
106	pia apply pi/research
107	pia run pi/research -- <pi arguments>
108	```
109	
110	`pia run` can omit its combo after `pia use` or `PIA_COMBO`; an explicit run
111	argument always wins. The management command signatures shown here require
112	explicit combo IDs so mutations and diagnostics have an unambiguous target.
113	
114	If a managed runtime file was edited directly, normal apply fails without
115	changing anything. Review the diff and either carry the intended edit back to
116	`agent/`, or use `pia apply <combo> --force` to discard drift on paths that
117	`pia` previously owned. Unmanaged runtime files are preserved.
118	
119	`launchArgs` cannot contain wrapper-owned options such as profile, session,
120	cwd, config, resume/fork routing, or API-key flags. Put one-off agent options
121	after `--`; keep secrets in the harness's private auth mechanism or environment.
122	
123	## Command map
124	
125	In the table, `<session-selector>` means either `--latest` or
126	`--session <id-or-absolute-path>`.
127	
128	| Command | Purpose |
129	|---|---|
130	| `pia list [--tree|--json]` | Discover combos and lineage |
131	| `pia use <combo>` / `pia current` | Save or print the default selection |
132	| `pia derive <parent> <child> [--description TEXT]` | Copy a combo and record lineage |
133	| `pia lineage <combo> [--ack]` | Inspect or acknowledge a parent digest |
134	| `pia status <combo>` | Summarise source/runtime health |
135	| `pia diff <combo> [--runtime|--parent]` | Show managed runtime or lineage differences |
136	| `pia apply <combo> [--dry-run|--force]` | Safely materialise source configuration |
137	| `pia run [combo] -- <args>` | Safely apply, then launch the selected harness |
138	| `pia sessions <combo>` | List sessions visible to that combo |
139	| `pia fork <from> <to> <session-selector> -- <args>` | Native same-engine session fork |
140	| `pia handoff <from> <to> <session-selector> --goal TEXT [--no-run] -- <args>` | Redacted context transfer |
141	| `pia doctor [--json]` | Check binaries, versions, source safety, and helpers |
142	| `pia completion <zsh\|bash\|powershell>` | Emit native shell completion code |
143
```

```text
- **Settings declaration:** Pi settings use a `packages` array. Entries may be package-source strings or objects with filtering rules. For example:  
  > `"packages": ["npm:simple-pkg"]`

  An object can select resource subsets:  
  > `"source": "npm:my-package",`  
  > `"extensions": ["extensions/*.ts", "!extensions/legacy.ts"],`

- **Package manifest:** A package may declare resources under the `pi` field in `package.json`; paths are relative to the package root. For example:  
  > `"extensions": ["./extensions"],`  
  > `"skills": ["./skills"],`

  If no manifest exists, Pi conventionally discovers `.ts`/`.js` extensions under `extensions/`, skills under `skills/`, Markdown prompts under `prompts/`, and JSON themes under `themes/`.

- **Pinning references:** npm specs with explicit versions are pinned and skipped by package-update operations. Git references are pinned to tags or commits. Examples:  
  > `npm:@scope/pkg@1.2.3`  
  > `git:github.com/user/repo@v1`

  Git updates reconcile the clone to the configured ref but do not move it to a newer ref. Installing the same repository with a new ref changes the configured pin.

- **Install locations:** User-level npm packages are placed under `~/.pi/agent/npm/`, while project-level npm packages use `.pi/npm/`. Git packages are cloned under `~/.pi/agent/git/<host>/<path>` globally or `.pi/git/<host>/<path>` for projects. Local-path packages are not copied.

- **Extensions:** Packages can include extensions through manifest paths or the conventional `extensions/` directory. They can also include skills, prompts, and themes.

- **Git-managed project implications:** Project settings are stored in `.pi/settings.json` when installed with `-l`; these settings can be committed and shared. Once the project is trusted, Pi automatically installs missing project packages at startup. When a Git package’s checkout is reconciled, Pi resets and cleans it, then runs `npm install` when its package contains `package.json`.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
## Install and enable

- Install as a local Pi extension/package:
  - `pi install /path/to/pi-chat`
  - or load it for a session with `pi -e /path/to/pi-chat`
- The README describes it as a Pi extension. It does not provide a registry package name or a separate service installer.
- After installation, use `/chat-config` to create accounts, configure channels, and add secrets.

## Prerequisites

- QEMU; macOS users are given `brew install qemu` as an example.
- A Gondolin guest image, fetched automatically on the first connection.
- A Discord or Telegram bot token.
- `tmux` for managing multiple channel workers.

## Guided setup and supported transports

Setup is partly guided through `/chat-config`, but external provider steps remain manual:

- **Discord:** create a bot, enable Message Content Intent, enter its token, invite it to a server using the setup-provided URL, then select and configure server channels.
- **Telegram:** create a bot with BotFather, enter its token, then add direct messages or groups through the setup flow.

The README lists Discord server channels and Telegram DMs/groups. It does not describe other transports.

## Running it

- `/chat-connect` connects the current channel.
- `/chat-disconnect` disconnects it.
- `/chat-status` reports connection, model, usage, and context information.
- `/chat-list` lists configured channels.
- `/chat-new` starts a fresh Pi session while retaining the chat connection.

For multiple channels:

- `/chat-spawn-all` starts configured channels in detached `tmux`/Pi sessions.
- `/chat-spawn-all --restart` restarts those sessions.
- `/chat-workers` displays worker status.
- `/chat-open-all` opens active workers in a tiled `tmux` dashboard.
- `/chat-kill-all` stops managed workers.

Workers write status snapshots every 15 seconds under `~/.pi/agent/chat/worker-status/`; the `chat_workers` tool exposes equivalent information. The README does not document a system service, boot-time startup, automatic recovery, or production deployment model.

## Runtime model

- Each connected channel gets its own Gondolin micro-VM.
- The VM provides Alpine Linux, Bash, Pi file tools, `/workspace`, and account-level `/shared` storage.
- Workspace, shared storage, memory, skills, chat logs, and VM state persist under `~/.pi/agent/chat/`.
- Outbound HTTP/TLS is open by default.
- Chat users can remotely stop, inspect, compact, or reset a session with `stop`, `status`, `compact`, and `new`.
- Files can be exchanged through attachments; older messages can be searched with `chat_history`.

## Security and other limitations

- Configuration secrets are scoped globally, per account, or per channel, and are restricted by allowed host patterns.
- For those secrets, Gondolin substitutes protected environment values only for permitted outbound hosts; the agent is not shown the underlying value.
- Runtime credentials use an encrypted browser exchange and are stored in the channel workspace. The temporary private key is held in Pi-chat memory, so the returned encrypted blob alone is unusable.
- Memory and skills are persistent and may be account-wide or channel-specific; skills are automatically discovered and injected into the prompt.
- The README does not provide backup, rotation, access-control, network-hardening, monitoring, or availability guidance.

## Official or companion status

The README links Gondolin, the Agent Skills standard, and Vercel Chat SDK. It says some rendering logic is vendored or adapted from the Vercel project, but does not describe Pi-chat as an official companion or integration.
```

```text
### Extension registration

The default export registers the pi extension and adds:

- Flag: `--chat-conversation <id>`
- Tools: `chat_workers`, `chat_history`, `chat_attach`, `chat_request_secret`
- Delegated standard tools: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`
- Commands:
  - `/chat-config`
  - `/chat-list`
  - `/chat-spawn-all [--restart]`
  - `/chat-workers`
  - `/chat-open-all`
  - `/chat-kill-all`
  - `/chat-connect <account/channel>`
  - `/chat-new`
  - `/chat-disconnect`
  - `/chat-status`

### Startup behavior

On `session_start`, the extension:

1. Loads or initializes the chat home.
2. Registers its tools and activates them.
3. Checks for `--chat-conversation`.
4. If absent, checks for a persisted conversation ID.
5. Connects only if one of those IDs exists.

Therefore, an ordinary Pi startup with neither a flag nor persisted connection state does not automatically connect, spawn workers, or create tmux sessions.

A persisted connection can reconnect automatically when that session resumes. The flag can also initiate connection explicitly.

### How setup and workers start

- `/chat-config` opens the configuration UI for Discord and Telegram accounts/channels.
- `/chat-connect` connects the current Pi session to a configured conversation.
- `/chat-spawn-all` explicitly creates detached tmux workers for all configured conversations.
- `/chat-open-all` only creates a dashboard for workers that are already running.
- Connection startup prepares QEMU/Gondolin assets and starts a sandbox.

### Effect of a combo package reference alone

A package reference alone does not activate the extension’s runtime behavior. Pi must load this extension so its default export executes. Even then, loading it only registers flags, tools, commands, and hooks; it does not automatically configure accounts, connect a channel, or spawn workers unless a persisted conversation or startup flag supplies a conversation ID.

## Document-grounded facts

- **Installation:**  
  - npm: “pi install npm:@gamalan/pi-gateway”  
  - Manual build: “git clone https://github.com/gamalan/pi-gateway.git”, then “cd pi-gateway”, “npm install && npm run build”, and “pi install .”
- **Initial setup:** Configure “~/.pi/gateway/config.json”. On first launch without that file, the package copies in its default configuration. The documented default listener is `http://localhost:3847`.
- **Startup commands:** “/gateway start”, “/gateway status”, and “/gateway stop”. Detached operation is available through “/gateway start -d” or “pi-gateway start -d”.
- **Compatibility:** Requires pi coding agent version `>= 0.80.3` and `@sinclair/typebox` version `>= 0.32.0`. The project identifies itself as an MIT-licensed fork.
- **Supported adapters:** “Discord, Telegram, Slack, Twitch, WhatsApp, WebSocket.”

## Architecture and session topology

The described topology is:

1. Platform adapters normalize messages from chat services.
2. The gateway routes them to pi through RPC.
3. Each chat receives an isolated conversation session.
4. HTTP/WebSocket clients can also submit prompts and receive events.
5. Background work runs in separate child sessions and reports results to the originating chat.
6. Security, session storage, and background-task management are gateway subsystems.

Sessions use daily, inactivity-based, or combined reset rules. Session data is persisted in “~/.pi/gateway/gateway-sessions.db”. Configuration defaults are shipped at “node_modules/pi-gateway/config/config.default.json”.

## Access-control defaults

- The documented default is `security.allowAll: true`; therefore, access is open unless changed.
- Pairing is disabled by default with `requirePairing: false`.
- Configured UID lists begin empty. Setting `allowAll` to false enables allowlist enforcement.
- An empty token array means API bearer-token authentication is not required.
- External users receive a restricted, read-oriented tool set by default.
- Administrative UIDs bypass tool restrictions; the document states, “Admin users have full unrestricted access”.
- Rate limiting defaults to 60 requests per 60,000 milliseconds.
- Pairing codes can be required for users not already approved.
- Tool permissions resolve from most-specific user rules to platform and global rules, with denial winning ties.

## Service behavior and warnings

- Responses are presented incrementally through message updates.
- Telegram selects webhooks when `webhookUrl` exists; otherwise it uses persistent long polling. Webhooks require a publicly reachable URL.
- Detached mode is claimed to continue after pi exits, with pi’s footer reflecting daemon state.
- HTTP and WebSocket interfaces are optional configuration features and expose status, sessions, background tasks, allowlists, and pairing data.
- Configuration examples contain placeholder credentials; real platform tokens and secrets must be supplied.
- The documented defaults are unsafe for an exposed deployment: open access, wildcard CORS, and no API tokens.
- Admin privileges intentionally permit high-impact tools such as shell execution and file modification.
- The material gives no deployment guidance for TLS, secret storage, backups, process supervision, high availability, observability, or database recovery.

## Claims versus demonstrated facts

The page **claims** real-time streaming, persistent sessions, background execution, security enforcement, multi-platform support, and daemon persistence. It also describes the project as “Multi-platform chat bridge for pi — connect your AI agent to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more.”

What is **demonstrated by the supplied material** is only the documented command set, configuration schema, file locations, endpoint descriptions, version requirements, and stated design. There are no test results, execution logs, benchmarks, security audits, uptime guarantees, or evidence of production deployment.

## Production and maturity wording

The only positive installation guidance is the label “Install from npm (recommended)”. The text does not explicitly call the software production-ready, mature, stable, enterprise-grade, or supported by an SLA. Its functional descriptions are product claims rather than independently verified maturity evidence.

## Source facts

- **Defaults apply globally** (`platform = null`, `userId = null`).
- **Allowed by default:** `gateway_*`, plus read/search/navigation tools such as `read`, `web_search`, `fetch_content`, `fffind`, `ffgrep`, `module_report`, symbol readers, AST inspection, LSP diagnostics/navigation, and `image_generate`.
- **Denied by default:** `bash`, `write`, `edit`, `subagent`, `todo`, `goal_complete`, `mcp`, `ast_grep_replace`, `agent_browser`, `wait`, `intercom`, `wiki_*`, and `lens_diagnostics`.
- Any tool with no matching rule is rejected.
- Tool patterns support `*` for multiple characters and `?` for one character.

### Admin bypass

- `isToolAllowed()` immediately returns true when `isAdmin(platform, userId)` succeeds.
- Admins also receive a guard stating that all tools are available.
- The shown code does not define how administrators are designated.

### Policy precedence

For matching rules, selection proceeds by:

1. Most specific scope.
2. Larger numeric priority within that scope.
3. A denial wins when scope and priority are tied.

Specificity is calculated from exact platform and user matches: platform contributes one level and user contributes two. A rule with both exact values therefore outranks platform-only, user-only, and global rules.

Explicit rules are stored in the database and replace an existing rule with the same `(platform, userId, toolName)` tuple. A null platform applies across platforms; a null user applies across users.

### Guard behavior

The guard is inserted into the prompt sent to `pi`; it does not enforce tool access at the RPC or execution layer. The effective-policy summary shown to `pi` merely collects allow and deny patterns; it does not resolve conflicts using the same specificity and priority algorithm as `isToolAllowed()`.

## Security judgments

- The evaluator fails closed for unrecognized tools, which is a sensible restrictive default.
- The prompt-based guard is not a hardened security boundary because prompt injection may cause `pi` to disregard it.
- The default gateway allowance is not absolute in practice: a more specific or higher-priority explicit denial can override it.
- **Remote approvals are not implemented** in the shown code. There is no approval request, approval response, expiration, or approval-audit flow; only policy creation, deletion, listing, and reset are provided.

```text
## Task persistence and recovery

- Uses a lazily initialized SQLite database at `~/.pi/gateway/gateway-background-tasks.db`, with WAL enabled.
- Persists task identity, parent/background session IDs, command, status, progress, result/error, and timestamps.
- A task row is inserted before the Pi process starts.
- `started_at` is never written, and there is no persisted process ID, attempt number, heartbeat, or lease.
- On process restart, previously running rows remain `running`; there is no reattachment, reconciliation, retry, or recovery pass.
- The declared `timeout` status is never assigned, and no timeout mechanism exists.
- Cleanup can delete old rows regardless of whether they are still marked running.

## Pi session integration

- Each task creates a background session through `createBackgroundSession("background", id, "system", parentSessionId)`.
- The resulting session ID is persisted with the task.
- Execution launches a separate process using:

  `pi --mode json --print <command>`

- Environment variables are inherited.
- Standard output is collected and inspected for JSON objects containing progress fields.
- Standard error becomes the failure message for nonzero termination.
- The created session is not otherwise used in this module for input, event handling, result storage, or restoration.

## Terminal-event semantics

- Completion is driven by the child-process `close` event, not by agent lifecycle events.
- A zero exit code produces a completed task; a nonzero code produces failure.
- The `error` event also marks the task failed.
- There is no handling for `agent_end` or `agent_settled`; neither event exists in this implementation.
- There is no once-only terminal transition guard, so close/error, cancellation, and completion can race and overwrite one another.
- Output parsing is inconsistent with line-oriented JSON: progress is parsed line by line, while final output is parsed as one complete JSON value.

## Deduplication and idempotency

- Every invocation creates a new ID from the current timestamp plus random bytes.
- There is no caller-provided idempotency key, command hash, uniqueness constraint, or duplicate detection.
- `completeTask`, `failTask`, and delivery updates do not verify the prior status or affected-row count.
- Repeated completion, late process events, and cancellation can therefore mutate an already-terminal task.
- Progress callbacks remain registered after completion or failure, creating a potential in-memory leak.

## Queueing

- There is no queue, scheduler, concurrency limit, priority, or backpressure.
- Each call to `startBackgroundTask` immediately spawns a process.
- The child’s stdin is piped but never written to or closed.
- Cancellation only works while the process is present in the in-memory process map.

## Delivery and restart behavior

- Pending results are selected for a parent session when status is completed or failed and delivery has not been recorded.
- Delivery changes the status to delivered and records a timestamp.
- Delivery is not transactional with result consumption, so multiple consumers could observe the same pending result.
- The in-memory process and callback maps are lost on restart; persisted tasks cannot be cancelled or monitored afterward.

## Compatibility-sensitive APIs

- Exported types: `BackgroundStatus`, `BackgroundTask`.
- Exported functions: `initBackgroundTasks`, `startBackgroundTask`, `updateTaskProgress`, `completeTask`, `failTask`, `markTaskDelivered`, `getTask`, `getPendingResultsForSession`, `listTasks`, `cancelTask`, and `cleanupOldTasks`.
- Consumers depend on the status values `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `timeout`, and `delivered`.
- Consumers also depend on the SQLite path, table columns, parent-session filtering, callback signature, and the external `pi` invocation format.
```
</details></tool-use>
