1	# Discord OpenCode Remote
2	
3	This directory pins and deploys a managed Kimaki bot. Discord project channels
4	map to local working directories and threads map to isolated OpenCode sessions.
5	
6	## 架構與程式碼導覽
7	
8	這套服務不是從零重寫 Discord bot，而是以固定版本的
9	`kimaki@0.26.0` 作為 Discord／OpenCode 協調核心，再由本目錄補上可重現的
10	patch、安全隔離、常駐服務、健康檢查、部署與回滾。這個責任邊界很重要：
11	
12	- 本專案維護的是整合與營運層：`start-kimaki.sh`、`patch-kimaki.mjs`、
13	  `deploy.sh`、`healthcheck.mjs`、launchd 設定及資料庫整理工具。
14	- Discord 事件、OpenCode session 與回應分派的核心來自 Kimaki，安裝後位於
15	  `node_modules/kimaki/dist/`。
16	- 不直接手改安裝後的 `dist`；所有必要變更集中在 `patch-kimaki.mjs`，並在
17	  `npm install` 的 `postinstall` 階段重播。
18	- patch 只接受 `0.26.0`。上游版本不符時直接失敗，避免把舊 patch 靜默套到
19	  不相容的新程式碼。
20	
21	### 主要程式碼
22	
23	```text
24	Discord bot/
25	├── package.json                    # 鎖定 Kimaki 版本與 postinstall patch
26	├── start-kimaki.sh                 # 乾淨環境、驗證、隔離與啟動參數
27	├── patch-kimaki.mjs                # 本機功能及安全修補的唯一來源
28	├── deploy.sh / rollback.sh         # 原子部署與回滾
29	├── healthcheck.mjs / watchdog.sh   # 功能健康檢查與故障恢復
30	├── com.solomon.kimaki.plist        # macOS launchd 常駐服務
31	└── node_modules/kimaki/dist/
32	    ├── discord-bot.js              # Discord MessageCreate 與 thread 路由
33	    ├── opencode.js                 # 啟動 opencode serve、建立 SDK client
34	    ├── session-handler/
35	    │   ├── thread-session-runtime.js   # prompt、session、queue、event 分派
36	    │   └── global-event-listener.js    # OpenCode SSE 全域事件流
37	    └── discord-utils.js            # Discord Markdown 與 2,000 字分段
38	```
39	
40	### 執行拓樸
41	
42	```text
43	macOS launchd
44	  └─ start-kimaki.sh
45	      └─ Kimaki Node.js process
46	          ├─ discord.js Gateway / REST
47	          ├─ ~/.kimaki/discord-sessions.db
48	          ├─ localhost Hrana DB bridge
49	          └─ opencode serve（localhost 隨機 port）
50	              ├─ OpenCode HTTP JSON API
51	              ├─ /global/event SSE stream
52	              ├─ Kimaki OpenCode plugins
53	              └─ 隔離的 OpenCode XDG／SQLite 狀態
54	```
55	
56	所有專案共用一個本機 `opencode serve` process，但每次 SDK request 都帶入
57	工作目錄；Discord project channel 對應本機目錄，Discord thread 則對應一個
58	OpenCode session。
59	
60	### 一次訊息的完整路徑
61	
62	1. Discord Gateway 送出 `MessageCreate`，入口是
63	   `node_modules/kimaki/dist/discord-bot.js:331`。
64	2. Bot 依序檢查 guild allowlist、自己的訊息、channel 是否綁定本機專案，
65	   以及使用者的 owner／admin／Manage Server／`Kimaki` role 權限。
66	3. Project channel 的新訊息會建立 Discord thread；既有 thread 則載入原本的
67	   OpenCode session。對應關係持久化在 `discord-sessions.db`。
68	4. 前處理階段解析回覆內容、mention、文字附件、圖片、PDF 與語音訊息。
69	5. `thread-session-runtime.js:2291-2368` 將使用者文字、Discord metadata、
70	   system prompt、附件、agent 與 model 組成 OpenCode request。
71	6. `session.promptAsync(request)` 透過 OpenCode SDK 發出 HTTP request：
72	   `POST /session/{sessionID}/prompt_async`。
73	7. OpenCode 執行模型及工具，再由 `/global/event` 以 Server-Sent Events
74	   推送 session、文字與工具事件。
75	8. `global-event-listener.js:130-210` 維持一條全域 SSE 連線；每個 thread
76	   runtime 再依 session ID 過濾屬於自己的事件。
77	9. 完成的文字交給 `discord-utils.js:486-534`，保留 Markdown/code fence，
78	   並依 Discord 的 2,000 字限制分段送回原 thread。
79	
80	```text
81	Discord MessageCreate
82	        │
83	        ▼
84	guild／role／channel 權限檢查
85	        │
86	        ▼
87	Discord channel → 本機專案目錄
88	Discord thread  → OpenCode session
89	        │
90	        ▼
91	session.promptAsync() ── HTTP + JSON ──► opencode serve
92	        ▲                                      │
93	        │                                      │ model / tools
94	        └──── session events ◄──── SSE ─────────┘
95	        │
96	        ▼
97	Markdown 整理、2,000 字分段、送回 Discord thread
98	```
99	
100	### 關鍵程式片段
101	
102	Discord 訊息入口先做 admission control，而不是收到訊息就直接交給模型：
103	
104	```js
105	discordClient.on(Events.MessageCreate, async (message) => {
106	  if (!isAllowedGuildId(message.guildId)) return
107	  if (isSelfBotMessage && !isCliInjectedPrompt) return
108	
109	  const channelConfig = await getChannelDirectory(owningChannelId)
110	  if (!channelConfig) return
111	
112	  const member = await resolveGuildMessageMember(message)
113	  if (!hasKimakiBotPermission(member, message.guild)) return
114	
115	  // 通過檢查後才交給對應的 thread/session runtime。
116	})
117	```
118	
119	Kimaki 在本機啟動一個共用 OpenCode server，並以 project directory 建立 SDK
120	client。實作入口是 `node_modules/kimaki/dist/opencode.js:639-790`：
121	
122	```js
123	const serverProcess = spawn(spawnCommand, spawnArgs, {
124	  cwd: os.homedir(),
125	  env: {
126	    ...process.env,
127	    OPENCODE_CONFIG: opencodeConfigPath,
128	    OPENCODE_PORT: port.toString(),
129	    KIMAKI: "1",
130	  },
131	})
132	
133	const client = createOpencodeClient({
134	  baseUrl,
135	  directory,
136	  headers: getOpencodeServerAuthHeaders(),
137	})
138	```
139	
140	送給 OpenCode 的資料不只有聊天文字，也包含這次 Discord turn 的執行上下文：
141	
142	```js
143	const parts = [
144	  { type: "text", text: promptWithImagePaths },
145	  { type: "text", text: syntheticContext, synthetic: true },
146	  ...images,
147	]
148	
149	const request = {
150	  sessionID: session.id,
151	  directory: this.sdkDirectory,
152	  parts,
153	  system: getOpencodeSystemMessage({
154	    sessionId: session.id,
155	    channelId,
156	    guildId: this.thread.guildId,
157	    threadId: this.thread.id,
158	  }),
159	  ...(resolvedAgent ? { agent: resolvedAgent } : {}),
160	  ...(modelField ? { model: modelField } : {}),
161	}
162	
163	await waitForGlobalEventListener()
164	await getClient().session.promptAsync(request)
165	```
166	
167	回應不是解析 CLI stdout，而是訂閱 OpenCode 的 typed event stream：
168	
169	```js
170	const subscribeResult = await client.global.event({ signal })
171	
172	for await (const event of subscribeResult.stream) {
173	  dispatchEvent(event)
174	}
175	```
176	
177	SSE 中斷時會以 exponential backoff 重連，從 500 ms 增加至最多 30 秒。
178	
179	### Session、狀態與並行
180	
181	- 一個 Discord thread 通常對應一個 OpenCode session，因此對話可以跨訊息延續。
182	- 不同 thread 有獨立 runtime，可以並行執行；同一 thread 的狀態變更會序列化，
183	  避免 event、queue 與 session transition 互相踩資料。
184	- 完整 OpenCode 對話存放在隔離的 OpenCode SQLite；thread/session mapping、
185	  model 選擇及已送出的 part mapping 存放在 Kimaki SQLite。
186	- 已送出的 OpenCode part 會記錄其 Discord message mapping，重連後可避免重複傳送。
187	- 顯式的本機 per-thread queue 是記憶體狀態，process restart 後不保留；這是目前
188	  已知的恢復邊界。
189	
190	### 安全邊界
191	
192	- `start-kimaki.sh` 使用 `env -i` 建立環境變數白名單，避免 launchd 或互動 shell
193	  的任意變數滲入服務。
194	- OpenCode API 只監聽 localhost 隨機 port，並要求私有 Basic Auth credential。
195	- Bot 使用固定 Discord guild allowlist，channel 還必須存在本機 project mapping。
196	- `--restrict-directories` 讓模型離開目前專案前必須取得額外許可。
197	- Bot 的 OpenCode XDG 目錄與桌面／Tailscale OpenCode 完全分離；啟動器拒絕
198	  symlink，並檢查 `opencode.db`、WAL、SHM 是否與共用實例指向相同 inode。
199	- `umask 077`、目錄 `0700` 及 credential `0600` 限制其他本機帳號讀取狀態。
200	- `--no-analytics`、`--no-critique` 與 `--no-auto-upgrade` 分別關閉產品分析、
201	  外部 diff critique，以及未經測試的自動升級。
202	
203	這不是 sandbox。獲授權的 Discord 使用者能透過 `!` 或 `/run-shell-command`
204	執行此 macOS 帳號可執行的 shell command；因此 Discord 帳號、server role 與
205	bot token 都必須視為主機存取憑證。
206	
207	### 給工程師的一句話
208	
209	這是一個以 Kimaki 作為 transport 與 session orchestration core 的 Discord
210	遠端 OpenCode runtime：本專案釘死上游版本，透過可重播 patch 客製行為，再補上
211	guild allowlist、XDG／SQLite 隔離、localhost Basic Auth、launchd supervision、
212	functional health check、原子部署與 rollback。
213	
214	## Runtime
215	
216	- Kimaki: `0.26.0`
217	- Sharp security override: `0.35.3`
218	- Node.js: `24.15.0`
219	- Bun: `1.3.12`
220	- OpenCode: `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`
221	- Kimaki state and Discord credentials: `~/.kimaki/`
222	- Kimaki OpenCode state: `~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/opencode/`
223	- Default Discord model: `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol`
224	
225	The launcher uses `umask 077`, so newly created credentials and logs default to
226	owner-only access.
227	
228	Install dependencies:
229	
230	```sh
231	npm install
232	```
233	
234	Start the interactive setup or run the configured bot:
235	
236	```sh
237	./start-kimaki.sh
238	```
239	
240	The launcher intentionally enables:
241	
242	- `--restrict-directories`: ask before leaving the active project.
243	- `--no-critique`: do not upload diffs to an external review service.
244	- `--no-analytics`: disable Kimaki product analytics.
245	- `--no-auto-upgrade`: keep the tested version pinned.
246	
247	It does not enable `--allow-all-users`. Initially, only the owner of the private
248	Discord server should have access.
249	
250	The runtime also enforces a fixed guild allowlist. Being a Discord server owner
251	or administrator is not sufficient unless the server ID is explicitly allowed.
252	The health endpoint becomes unhealthy when no allowlisted server is connected.
253	The localhost OpenCode API requires a private Basic Auth credential, and its
254	database retains only sessions referenced by Discord threads or scheduled work.
255	
256	## Discord Setup
257	
258	1. Create a private Discord server used only for this bot.
259	2. Open <https://discord.com/developers/applications> and create an application.
260	3. In **Bot**, enable **Message Content Intent**.
261	4. Reset and copy the bot token when the Kimaki setup wizard requests it.
262	5. Never paste the token into Discord, this repository, or an OpenCode prompt.
263	6. Use the install URL printed by Kimaki to add the bot to the private server.
264	
265	## Projects
266	
267	Register the two initial project directories after onboarding:
268	
269	```sh
270	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/Skill training"
271	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/every thing can be quant/第一性原理/不再被騙系統"
272	```
273	
274	Kimaki creates one Discord channel per directory. Switch project by switching
275	channel; start a separate task by posting a new channel message. Continue a task
276	inside its thread.
277	
278	This installation applies a version-checked local patch after `npm install`.
279	Discord's `/add-project` can accept an absolute path, browse a path prefix, or
280	search folder names under the home directory and mounted volumes. Projects are
281	created only when requested; subfolders are not pre-created as channels.
282	The command and its autocomplete can be used from any channel in the allowed
283	private server, including a channel that is not yet linked to a project.
284	
285	Examples in Discord's `/add-project` field:
286	
287	- `TOEIC`: search matching folder names.
288	- `/Users/solomon/`: browse folders in the home directory.
289	- `/Volumes/`: browse mounted disks.
290	- `/absolute/path/to/folder`: use an exact directory as the project root.
291	
292	Folder choices end in `/`. Select a folder, then reopen the `project` field to
293	browse its children. Submit at any level to create that folder's project channel.
294	One- or two-character searches use fast top-level matching; longer searches add
295	Spotlight results. If deep search times out, top-level matches remain available.
296	
297	## Background Service
298	
299	`com.solomon.kimaki.plist` is installed under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It
300	starts Kimaki when this macOS user logs in and restarts it after failures. Logs
301	are written to `~/.kimaki/launchd.log` and `~/.kimaki/launchd-error.log`.
302	
303	The deployed runtime is isolated from this Git working tree under
304	`~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/releases/`. `current` points at the active
305	release and `previous` provides rollback. Deploy a verified release with:
306	
307	```sh
308	./deploy.sh
309	```
310	
311	The watchdog checks Kimaki, Discord, and OpenCode every five minutes. It only
312	restarts after two consecutive failures and rotates each service log at 10 MB.
313	The OpenCode check performs a real session query instead of trusting the shallow
314	global health endpoint.
315	
316	Management commands:
317	
318	```sh
319	kimaki-remote status
320	kimaki-remote restart
321	kimaki-remote logs
322	kimaki-remote doctor
323	kimaki-remote deploy
324	kimaki-remote rollback
325	```
326	
327	Switch from the shared Gateway bot to your own Discord application with:
328	
329	```sh
330	kimaki-remote setup-self-hosted
331	```
332	
333	The command validates the Bot token before downtime, backs up the database,
334	accepts the token using hidden terminal input, opens the authorization URL, and
335	verifies functional health before finishing. `kimaki-remote use-gateway` only
336	stops the current Bot after confirming that saved Gateway credentials exist.
337	
338	Do not run two writing sessions concurrently against `Skill training`: its
339	workflow pulls, commits, and pushes at the end of each training round.
340	
341	## Security Boundary
342	
343	A user who can operate Kimaki can run shell commands on this Mac through `!` or
344	`/run-shell-command`. Treat the Discord account, server owner role, `Kimaki`
345	role, and bot token as machine-access credentials.
346	
347	Keep the existing Tailscale OpenCode service as a fallback. Kimaki starts its
348	own localhost OpenCode server on a separate random port and separate XDG data
349	directory. It never shares `opencode.db`, WAL, or SHM files with the desktop or
350	Tailscale service on port `4096`.
351

53020	- Integrates as a Pi extension rather than a standalone agent.

53026	- Pairing uses expiring, single-use links, QR flows, or PIN commands.

53035	- Multiple live sessions can share one local broker; users can list, select, or target sessions individually.
53036	- Session labels, one-shot prompts, offline-session cleanup, and same-workspace supersession are supported.
53037	- Continuing a session with `pi --continue` normally preserves non-secret binding metadata when the state directory remains unchanged.
53038	- Remote disconnect affects only the requesting conversation; local disconnect removes all bindings for the current session.
53039	- Remote session replacement works only for an eligible online, idle route and does not start offline Pi processes.
53040	
53041	## Streaming and concurrency
53042	- Concurrent sessions are supported through a broker scoped by state directory, bot-token hash, and broker namespace.
53043	- Busy-session prompts default to queued follow-ups; explicit steering is also available.
53044	- Progress modes range from quiet to verbose and completion-only.
53045	- Progress is coalesced, deduplicated, and updated in place where supported rather than forwarding every Pi event.
53046	- Shared progress cards expose bounded tool summaries and counts, not tool output, transcripts, file contents, or raw arguments.
53047	- Final responses are chunked by platform limits, with file or Markdown fallbacks where supported.
53048	
53049	## Process lifecycle
53050	- PiRelay keeps Pi running locally and does not create a hidden standalone agent.
53051	- A supervised local broker is shared by same-scope Pi sessions.
53052	- Clients reconnect and reconcile routes after broker restarts or transient transport failures.
53053	- `/relay restart` replaces the shared broker while clients retry connection autonomously.
53054	- Broker state and non-secret bindings are stored under `~/.pi/agent/pirelay/`.
53055	
53056	## Security characteristics
53057	- Bot tokens and app secrets are expected through environment variables; configuration stores variable names rather than resolved secrets.
53058	- Pairing codes expire and cannot be reused.
53059	- State excludes raw tokens, signing secrets, hidden prompts, tool internals, and transcripts.
53060	- Workspace file and image delivery requires explicit commands and path validation.
53061	- Redaction can remove common secret patterns before remote delivery.
53062	- Approval gates can block sensitive operations on timeout, revoked access, offline routes, or failed delivery.
53063	
53064	## Limitations
53065	- Messenger bot/app traffic is not end-to-end encrypted by PiRelay.
53066	- Slack lacks native typing bubbles and uses reactions or ephemeral fallback messages.
53067	- Discord and Slack file delivery is less capable than Telegram support.
53068	- Telegram group chats are not the default mode.
53069	- Structured-answer detection is deliberately conservative.
53070	- Image prompts require a vision-capable Pi model; image transfer is size- and MIME-limited.
53071	- `/images` only discovers captured outputs and obvious image paths from the latest Pi turn.
53072	- Native Slack and Discord slash commands may lag platform synchronization; text command prefixes are the reliable fallback.
53073	```

53096	## Purpose
53097	
53098	This is an **agent-to-agent delegation bridge**: one Pi session sends work to another Pi instance running on a peer’s machine. It is not described as a general human remote-desktop or shell-access tool. A human can initiate delegation through `/ask-agent`, while the local LLM can invoke `ask_remote_agent` automatically.
53099	
53100	## Architecture and Pi integration
53101	
53102	- The remote machine runs Pi with bridge mode and RPC port `18777`.
53103	- The local extension connects to the peer’s `/rpc` endpoint.
53104	- Peer URLs come from `REMOTE_AGENT_URL` or `~/.pi/agent/remote-agents.json`.
53105	- Pi integration consists of:
53106	  - The `/ask-agent` command for manual delegation.
53107	  - The `ask_remote_agent` tool for model-driven delegation.
53108	  - A single TypeScript extension entry point, `index.ts`.
53109	- The README says remote activity can expose tools such as reading, shell commands, editing, and writing.
53110

53112

53116	- The remote endpoint is represented as an HTTPS Tailscale hostname ending in `/rpc`.

53119

168169	## Model B — Pi-authoritative durable session router
168170	
168171	**Definition:** The gateway maps each admitted transport context to a persistent Pi session. Only explicitly directed messages and explicitly selected reply/attachment context enter Pi.
168172	
168173	**Invariants**
168174	
168175	- Pi session history is the canonical model context.
168176	- Every binding names one project/combo and zero or one current Pi session.
168177	- Every admitted inbound event has one durable gateway job and immutable response route.
168178	- Only one execution lease may mutate a Pi session.
168179	- Normal messages are FIFO follow-ups, not implicit steering.
168180	- No ambient room history is automatically copied.
168181	- A given external event/revision is never deliberately projected twice.
168182	- Session commands are parsed by the gateway and never forwarded as model text.
168183	
168184	**Benefits**
168185	
168186	- Minimal privacy and token footprint.
168187	- Native Pi resume, branching, compaction, tool history, and model state remain correct.
168188	- Natural fit for Discord threads and still deterministic on flat chats.
168189	- Easy to explain: “the agent knows what you sent to the agent.”
168190	- Much smaller semantic surface than mirroring each provider.
168191	
168192	**Failure modes**
168193	
168194	- Users may assume the agent saw nearby messages that were never sent to it.
168195	- Provider edits/deletes cannot retroactively change an already-used Pi prompt.
168196	- Exactly-once execution cannot be guaranteed across a crash spanning the gateway DB, Pi JSONL, and remote delivery.
168197	- Shared-room users still share the session’s tool authority unless isolated operationally.
168198	- A session opened concurrently in a local TUI can violate the single-writer invariant.
168199	
168200	**Storage**
168201	
168202	A small durable gateway database containing:
168203	
168204	- canonical identities and allowlists;
168205	- project and session bindings;
168206	- inbound event IDs, revisions, states, and payload digests;
168207	- per-session FIFO jobs, leases, and attempt state;
168208	- Pi entry/leaf cursors;
168209	- outbound message/chunk receipts;
168210	- reply-to-session mappings;
168211	- pending approvals;
168212	- attachment metadata and cleanup deadlines.
168213	
168214	It does not need to retain a complete room transcript.
168215	
168216	**Pi fit**
168217	
168218	Excellent through the public SDK; good through one RPC worker per active session. Public Pi APIs already cover persistent sessions, replacement, fork/clone, event subscriptions, compaction, images, and stable entry cursors.
168219	
168220	**Verdict:** recommended MVP.
168221	
168222	---
168223	
168224	## Model C — Bounded incremental IM-history projection
168225	
168226	**Definition:** Model B plus a deterministic, bounded selection of recent room events or a reply chain is attached to an invocation.
168227	
168228	**Invariants**
168229	
168230	- Pi remains authoritative for prior projected work.
168231	- Every projected IM event carries immutable origin, actor, timestamp, and revision provenance.
168232	- The gateway records which external events have already entered each Pi session.
168233	- Only unseen deltas or an explicitly requested older reference are included.
168234	- Bot outputs already present in Pi history are excluded from the projection.
168235	- The projection has hard event, byte, and token limits.
168236	- Untrusted participants’ content is visibly separated from the invoking user’s instruction.
168237	
168238	**Benefits**
168239	
168240	- Handles “summarize the discussion above” and threadless collaborative rooms.
168241	- Better conversational continuity where mention-only ingress is too sparse.
168242	- Less operational burden than a complete event mirror.
168243	
168244	**Failure modes**
168245	
168246	- Duplicate context unless inclusion watermarks are exact.
168247	- Edits/deletes create stale snapshots.
168248	- Pagination gaps and inaccessible history make the projection incomplete.
168249	- Other users’ content becomes indirect prompt-injection input.
168250	- Token usage and compaction frequency increase.
168251	- A naïve last-N window can cut causally important messages or include unrelated simultaneous discussions.
168252	
168253	**Storage**
168254	
168255	Everything in Model B, plus:
168256	
168257	- bounded normalized message cache;
168258	- revision/tombstone records;
168259	- per-Pi-session projection watermark;
168260	- projection manifest/digest;
168261	- author and reply/thread edges.
168262	
168263	**Pi fit**
168264	
168265	Best with SDK custom messages and metadata. RPC can pass flattened text/images, but its prompt command does not expose a documented persistent metadata field for external event IDs.
168266	
168267	**Verdict:** useful second-stage model, not the default.
168268

168270	
168271	## Model D — Event-sourced IM-native mirror
168272	
168273	**Definition:** The gateway persists the normalized IM event stream—including revisions, tombstones, membership, reactions, relation edges, and attachments—and derives Pi context projections from it.
168274	
168275	**Invariants**
168276	
168277	- The normalized gateway event log is append-only.
168278	- Provider event identity plus source identifies a distinct event.
168279	- Edits and deletes append revisions/tombstones; they never silently mutate audit history.
168280	- Context projections are versioned and reproducible.
168281	- Model execution and tool side effects are kept in a separate execution ledger so replay never reruns them.
168282	- Pi sessions are projections/execution histories, not the authoritative representation of the IM room.
168283	
168284	**Benefits**
168285	
168286	- Rich audit, replay, migration, compliance, cross-channel views, and alternative projections.
168287	- Correct handling of topic moves, edits, reactions, membership changes, and offline catch-up where providers expose those events.
168288	- Supports multiple agents or re-projection strategies.
168289	
168290	**Failure modes**
168291	
168292	- Very high adapter and migration burden.
168293	- “Complete mirror” is impossible on platforms that omit events, such as ordinary Telegram deletion notifications.
168294	- Provider retention/permission changes create irreparable gaps.
168295	- Deletion obligations conflict with append-only audit logs.
168296	- Rebuilding model context cannot reproduce already executed filesystem or network side effects.
168297	- Pi’s append-only session cannot be treated as a mutable mirror; re-projection generally requires a new/forked session.
168298	- Considerably greater breach impact because the gateway retains all chat content.
168299	
168300	**Storage**
168301	
168302	Full normalized event log, raw-payload quarantine, relation graph, revision/tombstone history, membership snapshots, attachment object store, projection checkpoints, execution ledger, outbox, retention/legal-hold metadata, and schema migrations.
168303	
168304	**Pi fit**
168305	
168306	Weak as a Pi extension; reasonable only as a standalone service using SDK/RPC. Pi remains the execution engine, not the event store.
168307	
168308	**Verdict:** only justified by product-level collaborative or compliance requirements.

168311	
168312	# 5. Recommended MVP semantics
168313	
168314	## 5.1 Binding and ownership
168315	
168316	Keep five notions of ownership separate:
168317	
168318	| Notion | Meaning |
168319	|---|---|
168320	| Operator/project owner | May bind a transport context to an approved project/combo and set its tool policy. |
168321	| Session owner | May expose, resume, fork, transfer, or delete that Pi session. |
168322	| Turn actor | Authenticated sender of a particular inbound event. |
168323	| Execution lease holder | The single process allowed to mutate the Pi session now. |
168324	| Response destination | The exact transport address captured when that turn was admitted. |
168325	
168326	Never implement response routing as “send to the last chat that messaged us.”
168327	
168328	### Suggested command semantics
168329	
168330	These commands are gateway control-plane operations, recognized only from authenticated, non-quoted message content:
168331	
168332	- **`/bind`** — associate the current transport context with a pre-approved project alias, Pi combo, and policy. Do not accept arbitrary filesystem paths from IM. Binding does not import chat history.
168333	- **`/new`** — create a fresh Pi session under the binding’s existing combo/project session root, then atomically make it current. Preserve the old session for explicit resume.
168334	- **`/resume`** — select an authorized existing session through an opaque gateway handle. Do not expose arbitrary local paths or a host-global session picker.
168335	- **`/fork`** — use Pi’s native fork/clone semantics, create a new session, and move the current route to it. A historical fork should reference an accessible stable Pi entry ID; “fork here” means clone the active branch.
168336	- **`/status`, `/cancel`, and `/unbind`** are practically necessary companions, even though they do not alter the context model.
168337	
168338	Pi exposes the corresponding session primitives through `AgentSessionRuntime`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/sdk.md:753-855`. Extension command contexts also support `waitForIdle`, new, fork, and switch, but only from command handlers because calling them from event handlers can deadlock: `.../docs/extensions.md:1109-1235`.
168339	
168340	## 5.2 Replies and quotes
168341	
168342	A reply has two independent uses:
168343	
168344	1. **Routing hint:** if it references a bot output already mapped to a Pi session, it can select that session.
168345	2. **Context:** include a bounded representation of the referenced message when it is not already in Pi history.
168346	
168347	Rules:
168348	
168349	- Never treat the quoted text as authenticated control syntax.
168350	- Retain the referenced provider message ID and canonical sender.
168351	- Mark the quote as untrusted data, distinct from the current actor’s instruction.
168352	- Do not recursively fetch an entire reply chain by default.
168353	- If the provider cannot resolve the target, say that the reference was unavailable rather than inventing context.
168354	- Replying to a user message does not create a new session unless the platform itself declares a native thread or the user explicitly forks.
168355	
168356	OpenClaw’s portable normalization similarly carries reply ID/body/sender and adds quoted content to the body, while keeping routing separate: [channel-routing.md:180-187](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/channels/channel-routing.md#L180-L187).
168357	
168358	## 5.3 Multiple users
168359	
168360	Default policies should be:
168361	
168362	- One DM session per provider account and peer.
168363	- No automatic cross-provider identity merging.
168364	- Multiparty DMs are groups, not personal DMs.
168365	- Groups/rooms are accepted only through an allowlist and mention/reply activation.
168366	- A shared group session is permitted only for mutually trusted collaborators and must visibly attribute every actor.
168367	- Membership or role is rechecked on every control command and approval, not only when the binding is created.
168368	- A sender’s display name is never an identity credential.
168369	
168370	A session boundary is not a host-security boundary. Pi states that it runs with the launching OS user’s permissions, extensions run with those same permissions, and project trust is only an input-loading guard—not a sandbox or prompt-injection defense: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/security.md:3-41`.
168371	
168372	## 5.4 Interleaving and queue ownership
168373	
168374	For the MVP:
168375	
168376	- Gateway queue is durable and authoritative.
168377	- One FIFO lane exists per Pi session, not merely per room/thread.
168378	- A global concurrency limit protects the host/provider.
168379	- A worker takes an exclusive lease for one Pi session.
168380	- Do not submit the next job until Pi reports `agent_settled`.
168381	- Ordinary inbound messages arriving during work become later turns.
168382	- Do not use implicit `steer`; reserve steering for an explicit, authorized same-actor control.
168383	- An approval wait holds the session lane.
168384	- Cancellation applies to the caller’s queued job or active job, not another participant’s work.
168385	- A queue item retains its original actor and response route through retries and restarts.
168386	
168387	OpenClaw independently arrives at per-session lanes because concurrent runs collide with session state, while different sessions can run in parallel: [queue.md:9-20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/concepts/queue.md#L9-L20). Its queue is explicitly in-process, however, so it is precedent for lane semantics rather than durability.
168388	
168389	## 5.5 Edits, deletes, and reactions
168390	
168391	| Provider event | Before Pi submission | After Pi submission |
168392	|---|---|---|
168393	| Edit | Supersede the pending job if revision ordering is trustworthy. | Do not rewrite the Pi entry. Record a correction/tombstone and require a new turn if the change matters. |
168394	| Delete | Cancel an unsubmitted job and remove cached payload/attachment where allowed. | Mark the external source deleted. Do not claim to undo model exposure or tool effects. |
168395	| Reaction | Record only if needed for UX. Do not add to context. | May resolve a specific pending approval only if the platform, actor, request ID, nonce, and allowed decision all match. |
168396	| Reaction removal | Remove display state only. | Never revoke an action that already executed. |
168397	
168398	MVP should ignore ordinary reaction traffic and should not use emoji as a general command language.
168399	
168400	Pi sessions are append-only; entries cannot be modified or deleted through `SessionManager`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:273-312`. This makes correction events—not silent mutation—the coherent policy.
168401	
168402	## 5.6 Attachments
168403	
168404	MVP attachment behavior should be narrow:
168405	
168406	- Support image attachments only, because they are first-class in Pi SDK/RPC.
168407	- Enforce type, byte, count, and dimension limits before Pi sees data.
168408	- Fetch using provider-authenticated APIs, not an arbitrary URL supplied in message text.
168409	- Preserve provider attachment/message IDs and a content digest.
168410	- Store temporary files outside the repository with owner-only permissions and explicit cleanup deadlines.
168411	- Treat captions, OCR, extracted text, archives, and document bodies as untrusted content.
168412	- Never automatically unpack archives or place files inside the repository.
168413	- If an attachment has expired or cannot be fetched, append a bounded “unavailable attachment” marker rather than retrying an old URL indefinitely.
168414	
168415	Pi user/session image content is base64 and therefore persists in the session if admitted: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/session-format.md:43-58`. Arbitrary file ingestion should remain a non-goal until staging, scanning, retention, and path-policy semantics are designed.
168416	
168417	## 5.7 Crash recovery, idempotency, and cursors
168418	
168419	Exactly-once end-to-end execution is not achievable across an IM provider, gateway database, Pi JSONL, filesystem effects, and outbound API. The correct contract is:
168420	
168421	- at-least-once intake;
168422	- deduplicated admission;
168423	- one durable execution intent;
168424	- idempotent/reconciled output where possible;
168425	- explicit `uncertain` state where reconciliation cannot prove the outcome.
168426	
168427	Maintain distinct cursors:
168428	
168429	1. **Provider ingress cursor**
168430	   - Slack: globally unique `event_id`; acknowledge quickly and process asynchronously.
168431	   - Telegram: advance to highest successfully persisted `update_id + 1`; pending updates last at most 24 hours.
168432	   - Matrix: persist `/sync` `next_batch` and use it as `since`.
168433	   - Zulip: persist `queue_id` and highest acknowledged `last_event_id`; queue expiry requires full re-registration/resynchronization.
168434	   - Discord: persist message/event IDs for deduplication; Gateway sequence supports connection resume but is not a permanent application event log.
168435	
168436	2. **Gateway job cursor**
168437	   - Durable status such as received, admitted, dispatched, settling, output-ready, delivered, failed, or uncertain.
168438	   - An IM acknowledgement means “durably accepted,” not “agent finished.”
168439	
168440	3. **Pi cursor**
168441	   - Store the last observed Pi entry ID and leaf ID.
168442	   - On restart, use RPC `get_entries(since)` or SDK `SessionManager.getEntries()` to reconcile appended entries.
168443	   - Persist external origin metadata in a Pi custom/custom-message entry when using the SDK, but do not claim this creates an atomic transaction across the gateway DB and Pi file.
168444	
168445	4. **Outbound cursor**
168446	   - One record per assistant result and per platform-sized chunk, with returned platform message IDs.
168447	   - If a crash occurs between a successful send and receipt persistence, mark delivery uncertain. Retry only when the provider offers a usable idempotency facility or history reconciliation; otherwise warn that a duplicate is possible.
168448	
168449	CloudEvents offers a sound normalized identity rule: producers must make `(source, id)` unique, and consumers may treat equal pairs as duplicates. It does not promise exactly-once processing.
168450	
168451	## 5.8 Session expiry and retention
168452	
168453	Separate four lifetimes:
168454	
168455	- **Worker lifetime:** a runtime can be detached when idle without changing the binding.
168456	- **Binding lifetime:** the transport context still points to a Pi session.
168457	- **Pi session retention:** the persisted JSONL remains resumable.
168458	- **Gateway event/attachment retention:** governed by independent privacy policy.
168459	
168460	Recommended default:
168461	
168462	- Dedicated DM/thread/topic bindings do not automatically expire.
168463	- `/new` or explicit policy rotates the session.
168464	- Optional idle expiry is a **soft unbind/rotation evaluated on the next real inbound user message**, not deletion.
168465	- Queues, heartbeats, retries, and maintenance must not extend human-activity freshness.
168466	- Never expire while a run or approval is pending.
168467	- Purging is a separate administrative operation and must account for both gateway storage and Pi session files.
168468	
168469	Pi compaction is not retention deletion. It changes the active LLM context while the append-only session still contains the old entries. Pi session totals explicitly include compacted-away history: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/agent-session.d.ts:640-645`.
168470	
168471	## 5.9 Compaction and avoiding duplicate history
168472	
168473	Let Pi own normal context-window management:
168474	
168475	- Pi compacts before/within runs near the model limit and rebuilds context as summary plus retained recent messages: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/compaction.md:27-81`.
168476	- It avoids cutting between a tool call and result: `.../docs/compaction.md:83-120`.
168477	- Compaction and branch summaries are persisted session events.
168478	
168479	For Model B:
168480	
168481	- Never load “the last N IM messages” on each turn.
168482	- Every accepted IM prompt is already in Pi history after submission.
168483	- Only the new inbound message, one explicit reply/quote, and its new attachments are sent.
168484	
168485	For Model C:
168486	
168487	- Keep a per-session projection watermark and manifest.
168488	- Include only previously unseen external events.
168489	- Exclude bot output already represented by Pi assistant messages.
168490	- Append corrections for later edits rather than re-including the whole window.
168491	- Keep user attribution and trust classification through compaction.
168492	
168493	The repository’s existing handoff policy is a useful precedent for deliberate transfer rather than implicit replay: it prefers the newest compaction summary, otherwise takes the first goal plus bounded recent messages; it excludes hidden thinking, images, tool arguments, and successful tool output; and it caps output at 128 KiB: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/sessions-and-handoff.md:50-87`.
168494	
168495	## 5.10 Cross-device and cross-channel handoff
168496	
168497	- Multiple devices viewing the same native DM or room naturally share the same transport key.
168498	- Similar display names across channels do not establish identity.
168499	- Cross-provider identity linking must be explicit and verified.
168500	- `/resume` from another channel may attach that channel to the existing Pi session only after authorization and a warning that prior session context becomes visible there.
168501	- Default handoff should **move** the writable binding, not silently create two active routes.
168502	- If shared bindings are later supported, they must share one Pi-session execution lane, while each job still returns only to its captured origin.
168503	- Cross-harness continuation should continue to use the repository’s deterministic handoff rather than raw session sharing; Pi and OMP version-3 files are intentionally not considered wire-compatible: `/Users/david/Worktrees/pi-agents/feat-im-gateway/docs/sessions-and-handoff.md:27-48`.
168504	
168505	---
168506	
168507	# 6. Trust, prompt injection, approvals, and attribution
168508	
168509	## Trust boundary
168510	
168511	The MVP should support:
168512	
168513	- one operator; or
168514	- one mutually trusting team using an isolated gateway host/runtime.
168515	
168516	It should not claim hostile multi-tenant isolation. OpenClaw’s current security model reaches the same conclusion: one trust boundary per gateway, and separate gateway/credentials/OS user or host for mutually adversarial users: [security/index.md:17-34](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/92ca6fbe6b84892a3c6ce0cb1803bd7dde387ba8/docs/gateway/security/index.md#L17-L34).
168517	
168518	## Prompt treatment
168519	
168520	- Current actor text, quoted text, ambient history, attachments, links, repository content, and tool output are all untrusted data.
168521	- Never concatenate transport metadata or quoted history into a privileged system instruction.
168522	- Strip or neutralize provider formatting only for parsing safety; do not claim sanitization solves prompt injection.
168523	- The gateway authorization layer, not the model, decides project access, session access, tools, paths, outbound recipients, and approval validity.
168524	- Ordinary IM messages must not automatically invoke Pi extension commands or expand arbitrary skills/templates. Pi RPC explicitly expands skill/template commands and executes extension commands immediately, even while streaming: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/rpc.md:56-76`. Gateway commands need their own authenticated namespace.
168525	
168526	OWASP and NIST both treat indirect instructions in documents, web content, email, and files as an agent-hijacking risk; the important mitigations are structural separation, least privilege, independent tool authorization, sandboxing, and human approval—not a text filter alone.
168527	
168528	## Approval contract
168529	
168530	For mutating or consequential tools:
168531	
168532	- Tool policy is checked before approval; approval cannot override a forbidden capability.
168533	- Bind approval to the exact Pi session, originating job, tool-call ID, tool name, normalized arguments, cwd/project, actor, and policy revision.
168534	- Default to allow-once.
168535	- Expire pending approvals and deny on timeout, disconnect, session switch, cancellation, or parameter change.
168536	- Only a project-authorized approver may resolve it; membership in a chat is insufficient.
168537	- Quoted text, forwarded messages, bot-authored content, and ordinary reactions cannot grant approval.
168538	- Record initiator and approver separately.
168539	- A late approval never revives an aborted run.
168540	- If the gateway cannot surface a confirmation UI, block the tool.
168541	
168542	Pi provides a stable interception point: `tool_call` fires before execution and can block: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/extensions.md:776-817`. RPC translates extension confirmations into correlated `extension_ui_request`/`extension_ui_response` messages and blocks while waiting: `.../docs/rpc.md:1184-1205` and `:1207-1374`. The bundled permission example fails closed when no UI exists: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts:13-29`.
168543	
168544	## Attribution
168545	
168546	Every accepted invocation should retain:
168547	
168548	- canonical actor ID and display label at receipt time;
168549	- provider/account/tenant/conversation/subconversation IDs;
168550	- provider message/event ID and revision;
168551	- reply/quote source;
168552	- project binding and Pi session/leaf;
168553	- gateway job ID;
168554	- Pi entry IDs produced by the job;
168555	- tool-call initiator and separate approver;
168556	- outbound route and resulting platform message IDs.
168557	
168558	The model should see enough sender attribution to reason about a shared conversation, while sensitive routing identifiers can live in `CustomMessageEntry.details`, which Pi documents as metadata not sent to the model: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:85-103`.
168559	
168560	---
168561	
168562	# 7. Privacy and deletion expectations
168563	
168564	The gateway creates additional copies even in the router model:
168565	
168566	- provider-side message;
168567	- short-lived gateway inbox payload;
168568	- Pi session entry;
168569	- possibly base64 image content;
168570	- model-provider request;
168571	- logs and outbound receipts;
168572	- tool-created files.
168573	
168574	Therefore:
168575	
168576	- Collect only explicitly admitted messages.
168577	- Keep full raw inbound payloads only as long as required for retry/reconciliation.
168578	- Encrypt state at rest where practical and use owner-only filesystem permissions.
168579	- Never put tokens or credentials in prompts, session metadata, or logs.
168580	- Do not send hidden thinking or full tool output back into IM.
168581	- Use separate data-retention settings for events, attachments, audit metadata, and Pi sessions.
168582	- Expose a clear distinction between “delete the IM message,” “forget gateway copy,” and “delete the Pi session.”
168583	- Warn that deletion cannot undo model-provider exposure, repository changes, shell commands, network calls, or messages already sent elsewhere.
168584	- Treat end-to-end encryption as terminating at the gateway: once decrypted for Pi, plaintext exists inside the gateway/Pi trust boundary.
168585	
168586	Pi itself says that project trust is not sandboxing and recommends OS/container isolation, minimal mounts/credentials, and restricted networking for untrusted or unattended work: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/security.md:31-53`.
168587	
168588	---
168589	
168590	# 8. Pi API fit
168591	
168592	| Surface | Fit | Assessment |
168593	|---|---|---|
168594	| **Public SDK** | Best default for this TypeScript repository | Direct `AgentSession`, `AgentSessionRuntime`, `SessionManager`, custom messages/details, event subscriptions, and tool hooks. The SDK docs explicitly prefer it for Node/TypeScript, type safety, direct state, and programmatic customization: `.../docs/sdk.md:1145-1165`. |
168595	| **RPC mode** | Strong isolation alternative | Language-neutral/process-isolated; has request correlation, new/switch/fork/clone, images, `get_entries(since)`, `agent_settled`, queue clearing, and UI dialogs. One worker should own one active writable session. |
168596	| **Pi extension alone** | Only for a remote-console model or policy hooks | Good for tool interception and UI integration, but lifecycle is attached to an active Pi runtime and session replacement requires careful rebinding. It is the wrong primary owner for many simultaneous IM contexts. |
168597	| **JSON event mode** | Diagnostics/one-shot output | Streams events but lacks the bidirectional lifecycle/control contract required by a gateway. |
168598	| **Raw session JSONL manipulation** | Reject | The format is documented, but direct concurrent appends, rewrites, or synthetic edits bypass runtime invariants. Read for diagnostics/migration only. |
168599	| **Experimental Pi Client/CBOR remote protocol** | Promising future path | It already has authoritative snapshots, multiple attached sessions, and exclusive/shared leases: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-client/README.md:26-34`. But the protocol explicitly has no compatibility guarantees: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-protocol/README.md:1-10` and `:69`. |
168600	
168601	Pin Pi exactly and isolate it behind a small adapter. Pi is still pre-1.0 and has made documented breaking session-runtime changes; 0.65.0 moved replacement operations from `AgentSession` to `AgentSessionRuntime`: `/Users/david/.local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md:2116-2129`.
168602	
168603	---
168604	
168605	# 9. Explicit MVP non-goals
168606	
168607	1. No full IM history synchronization.
168608	2. No automatic inclusion of messages merely because they are nearby in a room.
168609	3. No automatic cross-channel or cross-account identity linking.
168610	4. No shared global DM session.
168611	5. No hostile multi-tenant isolation on one host.
168612	6. No simultaneous local-TUI and gateway writers to the same Pi session.
168613	7. No implicit steering by later messages; normal arrivals queue as separate turns.
168614	8. No retroactive mutation of Pi history after IM edits/deletes.
168615	9. No promise of exactly-once tool execution or outbound delivery.
168616	10. No reaction-based approvals initially.
168617	11. No arbitrary archive/document ingestion; images only until file policy is designed.
168618	12. No streaming partial assistant messages into IM initially; deliver authoritative completed messages.
168619	13. No exposure of hidden thinking, secrets, complete tool output, raw session paths, or unrestricted session listings.
168620	14. No replacement of Pi’s compaction logic with gateway-generated summaries.
168621	15. No assumption that a channel, topic name, reply, mention, or display username is a stable identity.
168622	
168623	---
168624	
168625	# 10. Promotion triggers
168626	
168627	Promote from Model B to **bounded history projection** when measured use shows:
168628	
168629	- frequent “you missed the discussion above” failures;
168630	- a material share of traffic comes from threadless collaborative rooms;
168631	- users routinely reference messages the bot was not sent;
168632	- reply payloads often omit enough source text to understand the request;
168633	- a strict, testable context-visibility policy exists;
168634	- the added token/privacy cost is accepted.
168635	
168636	Promote to an **event-sourced mirror** only when requirements include:
168637	
168638	- durable audit/replay of edits, deletions, reactions, and topic moves;
168639	- legal hold or precise deletion/export workflows;
168640	- high-availability gateways and long offline catch-up;
168641	- multiple downstream agents or re-projection of the same conversation;
168642	- cross-channel unified inbox semantics;
168643	- deterministic migration of conversation projections;
168644	- provider event loss must be detected and repaired.
168645	
168646	Adopt Pi’s remote client/protocol only when it loses the explicit experimental/no-compatibility status and documents reconnect/replay and durable operation semantics suitable for gateway recovery.
168647	
168648	If users are mutually untrusted, do **not** “promote” the context model. Split gateway, credentials, workspace, and preferably OS/container boundaries.
168649	
168650	---
168651	
168652	# Repository-level recommendation
168653	
168654	1. Treat the current Discord/OpenCode document as a useful deployment baseline, not a portable context contract.
168655	2. Document the Pi-authoritative session-router semantics before implementing adapters.
168656	3. If implementation is approved, make the gateway an optional standalone service/package that consumes existing combo/session resolution; keep `pia`’s core focused on declarative configurations and explicit launch/session operations.
168657	4. Use extensions only for Pi-side policy hooks and approval UI, not as the durable multi-session router.
168658	5. Treat `pi-messenger-bridge` as a useful single-session remote-control reference, not a production multi-user foundation.
168659	6. Do not begin with an IM-native mirror.

Adopt a docs-first outcome for the selected **session-router** model:

- Pi sessions remain authoritative for model-visible history.
- IM provides identity, admission, routing, and delivery.
- Do not replay ambient room history; only explicitly directed messages and optionally bounded reply/quote context enter Pi.
- A production gateway still requires durable bindings, per-session FIFO/leases, deduplication, approvals, and delivery receipts.
- Keep `pia` transport-neutral. Do not add gateway, daemon, or service guarantees now.

Preserve the existing untracked files exactly as-is; do not edit, move, stage, or make committed documentation depend on them:

# Context

本次調研要判斷：Pi 的 extension／SDK／RPC 與既有 IM gateway 專案，是否適合直接納入 `pi-agents`，或目前只應留下可驗證的文件決策。以 **Pi 0.84.4** 與 **2026-08-31** 的來源快照為準，結論是 **docs-first**：`pia` 維持小型、無 runtime dependency、前景執行且同時支援 Pi／OMP 的 combo launcher；不在核心加入 gateway、daemon、transport schema 或 service lifecycle。

採用使用者選定的 **session-router context contract**：

- Pi session 是模型可見對話、tool history、branch 與 compaction 的唯一真相來源。
- IM provider 負責原生 message／reply／edit／delete／membership 事實；不把整個 room history 每輪重播進 prompt。
- Gateway 若日後實作，另以 durable state 負責 identity/admission、conversation↔project/combo↔Pi-session binding、per-session FIFO／single-writer lease、inbound dedup、approval 與 outbound receipt。
- Reply-to-bot 可作 routing hint；額外 quote/context 必須顯式、bounded、帶 attribution。沒有 thread 且 session 不唯一時拒絕猜測，要求明確 `/new`、`/resume` 或 `/bind`。

這不排除日後加入 Pi-only `maturity: experimental` combo；但外部候選尚未在 `pia` 隔離環境實跑 Pi 0.84.4，因此本階段不提交 package pin、extension 或 combo。

# project-knowledge-harness

A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.

Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:

| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |

Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
Hard invariants when serious enough — see
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

## When to use this skill

Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:

- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
  scattered across docs/")
- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
  `LESSONS.md` files

Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
documentation (use `docs/`).

## How to apply this skill (default workflow)

The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.

```
scripts/
  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
```

### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo

```sh
scripts/init.sh \
  --target /path/to/project \
  --project-name "My Project" \
  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
```

The script:

1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
   override with `--agent-contract`).
3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
   caught immediately.
5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
   not edit ignore files — see
   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).

`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.

### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea

Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".

1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
   doc is worth scaffolding.

   ```sh
   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
   ```

3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:

   ```sh
   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
   ```

   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.

4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.

5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.

### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky

Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.

1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item

In the same commit:

1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
   than one active item.
2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.

## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc

Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.

## Tag schema

Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.

## Anti-patterns

Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).

## Deployment exclusion

`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.

## Templates and bundled assets

- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
  table for traps documented elsewhere
- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`

## Reference implementation

A live example of this harness is at
[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):

- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section

# Evaluate an external Pi IM gateway

**Status**: P?
**Effort**: L
**Related**: `TODO.md` · `docs/ecosystem.md` · `docs/architecture.md` · `docs/combos.md`

## Context

Research completed on 2026-08-31 against Pi 0.84.4. The question is
whether remote messaging should become part of `pia`, a Pi combo, or remain an
external integration.

`pia` is currently a foreground, dependency-free Pi/OMP configuration launcher.
It can mechanically start Pi RPC with:

```sh
pia run pi/base -- --mode rpc
```

The existing passthrough in `src/cli.ts` and `src/harness.ts` safely applies the
combo and supplies its private session directory. `src/process.ts` then launches
one child with inherited stdio and returns only its exit code. This is a useful
process boundary for an external supervisor, but it is not an authenticated
network API, a multi-session scheduler, or a durable gateway.

The immediate decision is therefore **docs-first**. Keep `pia` core
transport-neutral, record the intended context contract and evidence, then test
an existing project outside this repository before committing any package,
extension, or combo.

All candidate assessments below are **source-reviewed, not runtime-verified**,
unless a row explicitly says otherwise. A permissive version range or the
continued presence of an API does not prove Pi 0.84.4 compatibility.

## Selected context model

Use a **Pi-authoritative session router**, not an IM-history mirror.

### Sources of truth

| Domain | Authority | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Native message identity, sender, revision, deletion, membership, and attachment availability | IM provider | Do not infer current IM state from a Pi transcript. |
| Model-visible conversation, tool history, branches, and compaction | Pi session | Do not replay the surrounding room history on each prompt. |
| Admission, project/session binding, execution lease, queue, approvals, cursors, and delivery receipts | Gateway state | These need durable service state outside a combo. |
| Repository and tool side effects | Workspace, filesystem, and Git | Editing or deleting an IM message cannot undo an executed action. |

Every admitted IM invocation is projected into exactly one selected Pi session.
Later turns continue from that Pi session rather than reconstructing context from
the IM timeline.

A canonical transport key must use stable IDs: provider, bot
account/installation, tenant or equivalent, conversation ID, and an optional
thread/topic/subconversation ID. Display names, channel titles, usernames, and
mutable topic labels are not identity keys. A binding additionally selects an
approved project alias, Pi combo, canonical working directory, tool policy, and
current Pi session.

### Thread and flat-room routing

Discord threads provide a convenient visible task boundary, but the portable
contract cannot assume they exist. For a flat room, resolve a message in this
order:

1. A reply to a known bot output uses the durable outbound-message-to-session
   mapping.
2. An authenticated gateway command names an authorized session handle.
3. A unique active binding for the conversation may be used.
4. If zero or multiple candidates remain, reject the message as ambiguous and
   require an explicit `/new`, `/resume`, or `/bind`.

A reply edge is a routing hint, not automatically a new conversation. Quoted
text is untrusted data, never authenticated control syntax. If referenced text
is needed and is not already in Pi history, include only that explicit, bounded
reference with its provider message ID and actor attribution; do not recursively
fetch a reply chain or ambient room window.

### Ordering and context lifetime

- Use one durable FIFO execution lane and one writable owner per **Pi session**,
  not merely per room. Two rooms bound to one session still share one lane.
- Ordinary messages arriving while work is active become later turns. Steering
  must be an explicit, authorized control rather than an implicit consequence
  of arrival time.
- Treat Pi's `agent_settled` event as the terminal boundary after retries,
  compaction recovery, and queued continuations; `agent_end` alone is not final.
- Let Pi own normal context-window compaction. Do not maintain a second gateway
  summary of the same accepted conversation.
- Before Pi submission, a trustworthy edit may replace a pending job. After
  submission, edits and deletions become corrections or tombstones; they do not
  mutate an earlier Pi entry or reverse tool effects.
- Default DMs to a distinct binding per provider account and peer. Shared rooms
  may share a session only for mutually trusted collaborators, with every turn
  attributed to its authenticated actor.

The router still needs a small durable control plane. At minimum it must retain
bindings, inbound provider IDs and job states, per-session ownership, the
original actor and response route, Pi entry/leaf cursors, pending approvals, and
outbound message/chunk receipts. It does not need a complete room transcript.

## Pi integration surfaces

| Surface | Appropriate use | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Pi extension | Foreground single-session remote control, policy hooks, tool interception, and approval UI | Session-scoped; long-lived resources must start/stop with session lifecycle; runs with the host user's permissions. |
| `AgentSession` / `AgentSessionRuntime` SDK | Preferred TypeScript embedding surface for a future companion service | The host owns admission, trust, disposal, replacement rebinding, queues, persistence, and multi-session coordination. |
| JSONL RPC over stdin/stdout | Process-isolated worker controlled by another service | One active replaceable runtime; no network listener, authentication, global scheduler, or documented multi-process JSONL writer safety. |
| Experimental CBOR protocol/client/server | Possible future multi-session substrate | No compatibility guarantee, no bundled network transport, and no turnkey coding-agent service today. |
| Raw session JSONL mutation | Diagnostics and migration only | Do not use as a live event bus or concurrent writer. |

Pi project trust only controls project resource loading. It is not tool approval
or a sandbox. Pi tools and extensions run as the launching OS user; a remote
identity that may drive them must therefore be treated as a machine-access
credential unless a separately verified OS/VM boundary limits that authority.

## Operational baseline

A resident production gateway would have to own all of the following outside
`pia`:

- deny-by-default account, tenant, guild, channel/thread/topic, actor, and admin
  admission;
- project and session binding, one-writer fencing, per-session queues, and
  bounded global concurrency;
- provider event cursors, durable deduplication, accepted/active/uncertain job
  states, and an outbound receipt or outbox strategy;
- restart reconciliation without concurrently mutating one Pi JSONL file;
- approval requests bound to actor, session, turn, tool, arguments, project,
  generation, and expiry, with timeout/disconnect failing closed;
- attachment type/size/path controls, temporary owner-only storage, retention,
  and safe handling of unavailable or expired media;
- credentials and mutable state outside Git-managed combo trees, with a minimal
  environment and redacted logs;
- functional health checks, bounded reconnect/backoff, process supervision,
  resource limits, backup/migration, reproducible deployment, and rollback.

These criteria were informed by a managed Kimaki/OpenCode deployment review and
by the public [Kimaki](https://github.com/remorses/kimaki) architecture. They are
requirements for any comparable production claim, not claims that upstream
Kimaki or an existing Pi candidate implements every item.

End-to-end exactly-once execution is not realistic across an IM provider, a
gateway database, Pi JSONL, filesystem side effects, and outbound APIs. A
truthful design should promise durable admission and reconciliation where
implemented, expose an `uncertain` outcome when it cannot prove completion, and
state the bounded circumstances in which duplicate execution or delivery may
occur.

## Candidate snapshot

### Shortlist

| Candidate | Observed fit | Source-reviewed gaps | Current decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`@zylab/pirelay@0.10.0`](https://github.com/zikolach/pirelay/releases/tag/v0.10.0) | Pi extension plus local broker; exact requester/conversation/thread binding; multiple live Pi sessions; pairing, progress, files, and optional remote approval gates; MIT release and substantial tests | CI/lockfile target Pi 0.73.1 rather than 0.84.4; host authority remains; approval coverage is opt-in; state rewrite is locked but not fully atomic; prompt queues and uniform ingress dedup are not durable | **First external spike** for the selected session-router model |
| [`earendil-works/pi-chat` at `9adbd29`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-chat/tree/9adbd29b40ee27ff1decf0fc87cbe180b40924f5) | Same organization as Pi and linked from Pi's README; Discord/Telegram; one worker and Gondolin micro-VM per configured conversation; persistent workspace and channel log | Do not infer an official support contract; current Discord mapping is channel-level, not thread-level; pending jobs are memory-only; open outbound network; QEMU/tmux footprint; no release/test/service unit; legacy Pi package scope and no 0.84.4 run; `LICENSE`/package say Apache-2.0 while README says MIT | Test second **only when per-conversation VM isolation is required** |
| [`TelePi` at `de6369e`](https://github.com/benedict2310/TelePi/tree/de6369e7e202e737498025d5f7ad5bfa35e86fce) | Telegram-focused standalone SDK daemon; per-chat/topic sessions, streaming, images/voice, dialogs, handoff, launchd/systemd, and current source near Pi 0.84.4 | Published v0.4.2 is materially stale; exact 0.84.4 not tested; chat/topic-to-session mapping and busy state are memory-only; no durable ingress cursor/queue or built-in tool gate | Consider only for a **Telegram-first** requirement, using pinned current source |

### Useful references, not adoption candidates

| Project | Reusable lesson | Reason not to adopt now |
|---|---|---|
| [`pi-messenger-bridge` at `8b0c1da`](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-messenger-bridge/tree/8b0c1da19c930225b15ec971f9225241a82b381d) | Small Pi extension and broad Telegram/WhatsApp/Slack/Discord/Matrix transport adapters | Every transport controls one active Pi session; one mutable pending reply destination is unsafe under concurrent senders; no durable routing, queue, dedup, attachments, or approval flow |
| [`Piscord` v1.7.0](https://github.com/Crokily/pi-discord-gateway/releases/tag/v1.7.0) | SQLite ingress queue, per-channel serialization, global concurrency, service setup, and retention | Confirmed broken by Pi 0.83/0.84 API changes; channel rather than actor admission; DMs can auto-register; no threads, streaming, or approval gate; replay and outbound failure semantics can duplicate or lose work |
| [`notdezzi/pi-discord-bridge` at `14c2572`](https://github.com/notdezzi/pi-discord-bridge/tree/14c2572b00b319c255e8c2036ee69f1618ac5470) | Desired project-channel to Pi-session-thread shape and direct extension streaming | Slash-command authorization bypass, shared project-channel fan-out, optional unauthenticated launcher, no durable queue, license conflict, and no tests/releases |
| [`tasercake/pi-connect` at `9982be6`](https://github.com/tasercake/pi-connect/tree/9982be694f547e4bbb702958f208ad6476498d8e) | Broad transport normalization, persistent RPC workers, crash `outcome-unknown` semantics, and optional Unix-user separation | No reliable license grant file, misleading npm name collision, Pi approval is not implemented, incompatible approval/yolo behavior, volatile queues, and no exact 0.84.4 proof |
| [`Dwsy/pi-gateway` at `953b1b0`](https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway/tree/953b1b0c857fdab22a39247320b891d8bde9e79c) | Deterministic Discord-thread/Telegram-topic session keys, worker pool, and bounded queues | Treats nonterminal `agent_end` as completion, auto-confirms unattended dialogs, has a configured but unenforced sandbox, and lacks current releases/test CI/durable queues |

Architecture comparators worth revisiting only after a concrete candidate fails a
documented gate:

- [remote-pi](https://github.com/jacobaraujo7/remote_pi) for device identity,
  keyring storage, relay trust disclosure, Unix-socket leadership, and service
  supervision;
- [pi-agent-web](https://github.com/leon-zym/pi-agent-web) for per-session process
  generations, controller leases, fencing, snapshot resynchronization, and exact
  Pi-version gates;
- [pi-rpc-bridge](https://github.com/CaptCanadaMan/pi-rpc-bridge) for a minimal
  loopback/private-network authentication boundary around one RPC process.

The reviewed [`@gamalan/pi-gateway`](https://github.com/gamalan/pi-gateway) is
not added to the spike order: its one global RPC process/current-channel model,
nonterminal completion handling, open/no-token defaults, missing event dedup, and
license/provenance questions do not fit this contract.

## Non-goals

For the current repository phase:

- no `pia gateway`, `pia serve`, network listener, broker, worker pool, provider
  adapter, service installer, or transport-aware combo schema;
- no full room transcript synchronization, automatic last-N history projection,
  cross-provider identity merge, or IM-native event mirror;
- no raw Pi RPC exposure as a secure public API and no dependency on the
  experimental CBOR stack;
- no Pi/OMP feature-parity promise for a Pi-specific integration;
- no exactly-once, never-lost, never-duplicated, sandbox, E2E-encryption, or
  universal-permission claim;
- no simultaneous local and gateway writers to one Pi session;
- no bot token, pairing secret, transport cursor, mapping database, queue,
  attachment cache, or outbox in a Git-managed combo tree;
- no committed gateway combo until an immutable external candidate passes the
  experimental gate.

## Promotion gates

The gates deliberately distinguish an experiment from a production service.
Failure at a higher tier does not prevent a clearly labelled lower-tier test.

### 1. Documentation decision

- Preserve this dated source review and session-router contract.
- Keep stable product-boundary language in `docs/ecosystem.md`; keep moving
  versions, rankings, and defects here.

### 2. Out-of-tree executable spike

- Name one operator, transport, topology, project-binding policy, concurrency
  target, attachment scope, target OS, and host-authority decision.
- Pin an immutable artifact and verify integrity, license/provenance, package
  scopes, install behavior, state paths, and required binaries.
- Run the real candidate with Pi 0.84.4 in a disposable account or VM and
  isolated `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`PIA_STATE_HOME`.
- Exercise authorized and unauthorized ingress, destination binding, same-session
  serialization, different-session concurrency, abort/new/resume/compact,
  `agent_settled`, approval allow/deny/timeout, attachments, disconnect, and
  process restart.
- Keep credentials and mutable state outside the repository and record every
  patch as a minimal, version-checked change.

### 3. Pi-only experimental combo

Passing this gate permits a `maturity: experimental` Pi combo without changing
`pia` core or its schema:

- immutable, licensed package/commit pin with an accountable maintainer;
- exact Pi 0.84.4 load and an authorized/unauthorized round trip;
- correct destination under the declared single-session or multi-session
  concurrency model;
- explicit service-state root outside combo source, with no secret in Git;
- no unattended auto-confirm and no authorization bypass for alternate command
  paths;
- documentation that promises only the behavior actually tested and states
  best-effort delivery, no sandbox, no service supervision, and no OMP support;
- dedicated typecheck/runtime coverage for any combo-local extension, because the
  current project TypeScript check does not compile `combos/**`.

### 4. Supported optional adapter

- maintained compatibility CI against the declared Pi versions;
- upgrade and security-response owner;
- authorization, routing, lifecycle, provider-limit, and restart regression
  tests;
- documented state migration, support matrix, failure semantics, and removal
  path.

### 5. Production resident service

- durable provider cursors, ingress uniqueness, queue state machine, outcome
  reconciliation, and transactional/idempotent outbound strategy where possible;
- generation fencing, one authoritative session writer, and crash injection at
  every admission/execution/delivery boundary;
- deny-by-default admission, auditable approvals, bounded media/network inputs,
  credential rotation, environment isolation, and an explicit VM/container/UID
  boundary when chat users must not receive host authority;
- functional transport and Pi health checks, supervised restart/backoff,
  resource limits, log rotation/redaction, database backup/migration, immutable
  or reproducible deployment, atomic activation, rollback, and recovery drills.

## Verification matrix

Runtime cells start as **unverified**. Update them only from a repeatable spike;
do not convert source inference into a pass.

| Candidate/ref | Artifact and license | Pi 0.84.4 load | State-root isolation | Admission | Binding/concurrency | Restart/dedup | Approval | Attachments | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pirelay 0.10.0 | Source-reviewed | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | First spike |
| pi-chat `9adbd29` | License conflict recorded | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | N/A until designed | Unverified | Conditional on VM requirement |
| TelePi `de6369e` | Source-reviewed | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Telegram-only fallback |

A spike report should also capture the exact Node/Pi versions, package tarball or
Git digest, mutable files created, environment variables consumed, process tree,
provider event IDs, Pi entry IDs, outbound message IDs, fault-injection point,
and whether the outcome was completed, failed, or uncertain.

## Open questions

- Is the first real deployment Discord, Telegram, or multi-transport?
- Is it a foreground personal remote control or an always-on service?
- Does one trusted operator have host-user authority, or is VM/container/UID
  isolation mandatory?
- What exact channel/thread/topic-to-project policy and concurrency are needed?
- Which attachments and approval interactions are required?
- Who owns upgrades, credentials, provider setup, recovery, and incident response?
