# project-knowledge-harness

A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.

Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:

| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |

Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
Hard invariants when serious enough — see
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

## When to use this skill

Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:

- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
  scattered across docs/")
- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
  `LESSONS.md` files

Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
documentation (use `docs/`).

## How to apply this skill (default workflow)

The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.

```
scripts/
  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
```

### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo

```sh
scripts/init.sh \
  --target /path/to/project \
  --project-name "My Project" \
  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
```

The script:

1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
   override with `--agent-contract`).
3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
   caught immediately.
5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
   not edit ignore files — see
   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).

`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.

### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea

Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".

1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
   doc is worth scaffolding.

   ```sh
   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
   ```

3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:

   ```sh
   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
   ```

   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.

4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.

5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.

### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky

Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.

1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).

### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item

In the same commit:

1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
   than one active item.
2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.

## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc

Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.

## Tag schema

Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.

## Anti-patterns

Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).

## Deployment exclusion

`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.

## Templates and bundled assets

- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
  table for traps documented elsewhere
- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`

## Reference implementation

A live example of this harness is at
[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):

- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section

100	function takeFlag(args: string[], name: string): boolean {
101	  const index = args.indexOf(name);
102	  if (index === -1) return false;
103	  args.splice(index, 1);
104	  return true;

106	
107	function takeOption(args: string[], name: string): string | undefined {
108	  const equalsIndex = args.findIndex((arg) => arg.startsWith(`${name}=`));
109	  if (equalsIndex !== -1) {
110	    const value = args.splice(equalsIndex, 1)[0];
111	    return value?.slice(name.length + 1);
112	  }
113	  const index = args.indexOf(name);
114	  if (index === -1) return undefined;
115	  if (index + 1 >= args.length) throw new Error(`${name} requires a value`);
116	  const [, value] = args.splice(index, 2);
117	  return value;
118	}

123	  return { own: args.slice(0, index), passthrough: args.slice(index + 1) };

126	function assertNoTargetSessionRouting(args: string[], operation: string): void {
127	  const reserved = new Set(["--continue", "-c", "--resume", "-r", "--session", "--fork", "--session-dir", "--no-session"]);
128	  for (const arg of args) {
129	    if (arg === "--") break;
130	    const flag = arg.includes("=") ? arg.slice(0, arg.indexOf("=")) : arg;
131	    if (reserved.has(flag)) {
132	      throw new Error(`${operation} owns target session creation; remove conflicting native flag ${flag}`);
133	    }
134	  }

404	async function cmdDoctor(sourceRoot: string, stateRoot: string, args: string[], env: Env): Promise<void> {

409	    checks.push({ name, ok, detail, severity });
410	  };
411	  const [major, minor] = process.versions.node.split(".").map(Number);
412	  add("node", major > 22 || (major === 22 && minor >= 19), process.versions.node);
413	  add("git", Boolean(commandExists("git")), commandExists("git") || "not found");
414	  add("python3", Boolean(commandExists("python3")), commandExists("python3") || "not found", "warning");
415	  add("gitleaks", Boolean(commandExists("gitleaks")), commandExists("gitleaks") || "not found", "warning");
416	  for (const engine of ["pi", "omp"]) {
417	    const binary = engine === "pi" ? env.PIA_PI_BIN || "pi" : env.PIA_OMP_BIN || "omp";
418	    const probe = commandResult(binary, ["--version"], { env });
419	    add(engine, probe.ok, probe.ok ? (probe.stdout || probe.stderr).trim() : "not installed", "warning");
420	  }
421	  try {
422	    const combos = await listCombos(sourceRoot);
423	    for (const combo of combos) await scanTree(combo.agentDir);
424	    add("combos", true, `${combos.length} valid`);
425	  } catch (error) {
426	    add("combos", false, errorMessage(error));
427	  }
428	  try {
429	    const selected = env.PIA_COMBO || (await readSelection(env));
430	    if (selected) await loadCombo(sourceRoot, selected);
431	    add("selection", true, selected || "none", "warning");
432	  } catch (error) {
433	    add("selection", false, errorMessage(error));
434	  }
435	  add("sourceRoot", true, sourceRoot);
436	  add("stateRoot", true, stateRoot);
437	  add("configRoot", true, getConfigRoot(env));
438	  if (json) printJson({ checks });
439	  else {
440	    for (const check of checks) {
441	      const label = check.ok ? "ok" : check.severity === "warning" ? "warn" : "error";
442	      process.stdout.write(
443	        `${tone(stateTone(label), label)}\t${ui.accent(check.name, stdoutStyle)}\t` +
444	        `${ui.muted(check.detail, stdoutStyle)}\n`,
445	      );
446	    }
447	  }
448	  if (checks.some((check) => !check.ok && check.severity === "error")) process.exitCode = 1;
449	}

451	export async function main(argv: string[], env: Env = process.env): Promise<void> {
452	  const sourceRoot = getSourceRoot(env);

461	    process.stdout.write(`${pkg.version}\n`);
462	    return;
463	  }
464	  const command = args.shift();
465	  if (!command) return await cmdRun(sourceRoot, stateRoot, [], env);
466	  if (command === "run") return await cmdRun(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
467	  if (command === "use") {
468	    if (args.length !== 1) throw new Error("Usage: pia use <combo>");
469	    const file = await saveSelection(sourceRoot, args[0], env);
470	    process.stdout.write(`${args[0]}\n${file}\n`);
471	    return;
472	  }
473	  if (command === "current") {
474	    const selected = env.PIA_COMBO || (await readSelection(env));
475	    if (!selected) throw new Error("No combo selected");
476	    await loadCombo(sourceRoot, selected);
477	    process.stdout.write(`${selected}\n`);

479	  }
480	  if (command === "list") return await cmdList(sourceRoot, args);
481	  if (command === "derive") {
482	    const description = takeOption(args, "--description");

484	    const combo = await deriveCombo(sourceRoot, args[0], args[1], description);
485	    process.stdout.write(`${combo.id}\n`);

487	  }
488	  if (command === "lineage") return await cmdLineage(sourceRoot, args);
489	  if (command === "status") return await cmdStatus(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
490	  if (command === "diff") return await cmdDiff(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
491	  if (command === "apply") return await cmdApply(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
492	  if (command === "sessions") return await cmdSessions(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args);
493	  if (command === "fork") return await cmdFork(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
494	  if (command === "handoff") return await cmdHandoff(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
495	  if (command === "doctor") return await cmdDoctor(sourceRoot, stateRoot, args, env);
496	  if (command === "completion") {

498	    process.stdout.write(await renderCompletion(args[0]));

87	  const profile = getOmpProfileName(combo);
88	  const result = runner(binary, [`--profile=${profile}`, "config", "path"], { env });

104	    } catch (error) {
105	      if (!isNodeError(error) || error.code !== "ENOENT") throw error;
106	    }
107	  }
108	  return resolved;
109	}

159	  stateRoot,
160	  cwd = process.cwd(),
161	  env = process.env,
162	  userArgs = [],
163	  commandRunner,
164	  spawnRunner = runInherited,
165	}: RunComboOptions): Promise<RunComboResult> {
166	  assertNoOwnedFlags(userArgs);
167	  const applied = await applyCombo({ combo, stateRoot, cwd, env, commandRunner });
168	  if (!applied.result.ok) {
169	    const reason = applied.result.reason || "runtime configuration has unresolved drift";
170	    throw new Error(`Refusing to launch ${combo.id}: ${reason}`);
171	  }
172	  await ensurePrivateDir(applied.sessionDir);
173	
174	  const childEnv = { ...env };
175	  delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR;
176	  const args = [];
177	  if (combo.engine === "pi") {
178	    childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR = applied.targetDir;
179	  } else {
180	    delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR;
181	    delete childEnv.OMP_PROFILE;
182	    delete childEnv.PI_PROFILE;
183	    args.push(`--profile=${getOmpProfileName(combo)}`);
184	  }
185	  args.push(...combo.metadata.launchArgs, "--session-dir", applied.sessionDir, ...userArgs);
186	  const exitCode = await spawnRunner(binaryFor(combo.engine, env), args, { cwd, env: childEnv });
187	  return { exitCode, args, command: binaryFor(combo.engine, env), ...applied };
188	}

48	function envValue(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, name: string): string | undefined {
49	  const direct = env[name];
50	  if (direct !== undefined) return direct;
51	  const match = Object.keys(env).find((key) => key.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase());
52	  return match ? env[match] : undefined;
53	}
54	
55	function isRegularFile(filePath: string): boolean {
56	  try {
57	    return statSync(filePath).isFile();
58	  } catch {
59	    return false;
60	  }
61	}
62	
63	function windowsPathEntries(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string[] {
64	  return (envValue(env, "PATH") || "")
65	    .split(";")
66	    .map((entry) => entry.trim().replace(/^"|"$/g, ""))
67	    .filter(Boolean);
68	}
69	
70	function hasPathSeparator(command: string): boolean {
71	  return command.includes("/") || command.includes("\\");
72	}
73	
74	function findWindowsCommand(
75	  command: string,
76	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,
77	  extensions: readonly string[],
78	): string | undefined {
79	  const extension = path.extname(command).toLowerCase();
80	  const names = extension ? [command] : extensions.map((suffix) => `${command}${suffix}`);
81	  if (hasPathSeparator(command)) return names.find(isRegularFile);
82	
83	  for (const directory of windowsPathEntries(env)) {
84	    for (const name of names) {
85	      const candidate = path.join(directory, name);
86	      if (isRegularFile(candidate)) return candidate;
87	    }
88	  }
89	  return undefined;
90	}

92	function findPowerShell(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): string {
93	  for (const command of ["pwsh", "powershell"]) {
94	    const resolved = findWindowsCommand(command, env, [".exe"]);
95	    if (resolved) return resolved;
96	  }
97	
98	  const systemRoot = envValue(env, "SystemRoot");
99	  if (systemRoot) {
100	    const bundled = path.join(systemRoot, "System32", "WindowsPowerShell", "v1.0", "powershell.exe");
101	    if (isRegularFile(bundled)) return bundled;
102	  }
103	  return "powershell.exe";
104	}

106	/**
107	 * Resolve Windows executables without enabling child_process shell parsing.
108	 * npm always creates a PowerShell shim alongside its cmd shim; invoking that
109	 * file through `-File` keeps every forwarded value as a distinct argv item.
110	 */
111	export function resolveCommandInvocation(
112	  command: string,
113	  args: readonly string[] = [],
114	  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,
115	  platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform,
116	): CommandInvocation {
117	  if (platform !== "win32") return { command, args: [...args] };
118	
119	  const requestedExtension = path.extname(command).toLowerCase();
120	  let resolved = findWindowsCommand(command, env, [".exe", ".com", ".ps1", ".cmd", ".bat"]);
121	  if (!resolved && (requestedExtension === ".cmd" || requestedExtension === ".bat")) {
122	    const siblingCommand = command.slice(0, -requestedExtension.length) + ".ps1";
123	    resolved = findWindowsCommand(siblingCommand, env, [".ps1"]);
124	  }
125	  if (!resolved) {
126	    if (requestedExtension === ".cmd" || requestedExtension === ".bat") {
127	      throw new Error(
128	        `Windows command shim ${command} is unsupported without a same-basename .ps1 sibling; pia never enables shell parsing`,
129	      );
130	    }
131	    return { command, args: [...args] };
132	  }
133	
134	  const resolvedExtension = path.extname(resolved).toLowerCase();
135	  if (resolvedExtension === ".cmd" || resolvedExtension === ".bat") {
136	    const sibling = resolved.slice(0, -resolvedExtension.length) + ".ps1";
137	    if (!isRegularFile(sibling)) {
138	      throw new Error(
139	        `Windows command shim ${resolved} is unsupported without a same-basename .ps1 sibling; pia never enables shell parsing`,
140	      );
141	    }
142	    resolved = sibling;
143	  }
144	  if (path.extname(resolved).toLowerCase() !== ".ps1") {
145	    return { command: resolved, args: [...args] };
146	  }
147	
148	  return {
149	    command: findPowerShell(env),
150	    args: [
151	      "-NoLogo",
152	      "-NoProfile",
153	      "-NonInteractive",
154	      "-ExecutionPolicy",
155	      "Bypass",
156	      "-File",
157	      resolved,
158	      ...args,
159	    ],
160	  };
161	}
162	
163	export function commandResult(
164	  command: string,
165	  args: readonly string[] = [],
166	  options: ProcessOptions = {},
167	): ProcessResult {
168	  const env = options.env || process.env;
169	  const invocation = resolveCommandInvocation(command, args, env);
170	  const result = spawnSync(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
171	    encoding: "utf8",
172	    stdio: [options.input === undefined ? "ignore" : "pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
173	    input: options.input,
174	    env,
175	    cwd: options.cwd,
176	    maxBuffer: options.maxBuffer || 8 * 1024 * 1024,
177	  });
178	  if (result.error) {
179	    return { ok: false, status: null, stdout: "", stderr: result.error.message, error: result.error };
180	  }
181	  return {
182	    ok: result.status === 0,
183	    status: result.status,
184	    stdout: result.stdout || "",
185	    stderr: result.stderr || "",
186	  };
187	}
188	
189	export async function runInherited(
190	  command: string,
191	  args: readonly string[],
192	  options: InheritedProcessOptions = {},
193	): Promise<number> {
194	  return await new Promise<number>((resolve, reject) => {
195	    const env = options.env || process.env;
196	    const invocation = resolveCommandInvocation(command, args, env);
197	    const child = spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
198	      cwd: options.cwd,
199	      env,
200	      stdio: "inherit",
201	    });
202	    child.on("error", reject);
203	    child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
204	      if (signal) {
205	        process.kill(process.pid, signal);
206	        return;
207	      }
208	      resolve(code ?? 1);
209	    });
210	  });
211	}
212	
213	export function commandExists(command: string): string | undefined {
214	  const probe = commandResult(command, ["--version"]);
215	  return probe.ok ? probe.stdout.trim() || probe.stderr.trim() : undefined;
216	}

```text
1	# Architecture
2	
3	`pia` separates version-controlled intent from mutable agent state. The Git
4	repository is the source of truth for combo definitions; it is never an agent's
5	live home directory.
6	
7	## Data layout
8	
9	```text
10	pi-agents/
11	  combos/<pi|omp>/<name>/
12	    combo.json             declarative metadata
13	    agent/                 complete managed config tree
14	  schema/combo.schema.json
15	  bin/pia
16	  src/*.ts                 Node-native erasable TypeScript
17	
18	${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/pi-agents/
19	  selection.json           value saved by `pia use`
20	
21	${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents/
22	  manifests/               last-applied managed-file hashes and modes
23	  runtime/pi/<name>/agent/ Pi configuration runtime
24	  sessions/                isolated/shared session roots
25	  handoffs/                generated private Markdown artifacts
26	```
27	
28	`PIA_SOURCE_ROOT` can point the CLI at another checkout. `PIA_STATE_HOME`
29	replaces the entire state root. These overrides are useful for tests and
30	advanced setups; normal users should let the CLI derive both paths.
31	
32	For Pi, `pia` launches with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to the combo's runtime
33	directory. For OMP, it uses a native profile named `pia-<combo-name>` and asks
34	`omp --profile ... config path` for the real location instead of assuming a
35	home or XDG layout. `PIA_PI_BIN` and `PIA_OMP_BIN` can override the executable
36	names.
37	
38	## Source and runtime contract
39	
40	Only files below a combo's `agent/` directory are managed. Downloaded packages,
41	credentials, sessions, caches, blobs, databases, and any other runtime-created
42	files stay outside Git or remain unowned in the runtime tree.
43	
44	The source tree must not contain credentials, `.env` files, session/package/
45	cache stores, or symlinks. On POSIX systems runtime directories are created
46	with mode `0700`; managed files use `0600` or `0700` according to their
47	executable bit. Windows does not expose equivalent POSIX mode enforcement
48	through Node, so runtime files inherit the user's profile ACL and drift checks
49	compare content rather than synthetic mode bits there. Writes and manifest
50	replacement are atomic.
51	
52	The source uses only TypeScript syntax that Node can erase without code
53	generation. Runtime execution therefore stays build-free; `tsconfig.json` and
54	the development dependencies exist solely for strict `tsc --noEmit` checking.
55	
56	Known runtime/credential paths are rejected structurally. `npm run check` also
57	runs gitleaks over combo content when the binary is available, while CI and the
58	existing pre-commit stack enforce the same secret scan before source is shared.
59	
60	Each manifest records its exact absolute target and, for every managed relative
61	path, the content hash, executable bit, and mode. `pia apply` classifies paths
62	as follows:
63	
64	| Source/runtime state | Result |
65	|---|---|
66	| New source path, unused target | Create it |
67	| Source changed, runtime still at last applied value | Update it |
68	| Runtime changed independently | Refuse the whole apply |
69	| Source and runtime both changed | Refuse the whole apply |
70	| Source removed, runtime unchanged | Remove the stale managed path |
71	| Source removed, runtime changed | Refuse unless forced |
72	| Target-only path never owned by `pia` | Preserve and omit from normal diff |
73	| New source collides with an unowned path or non-file obstruction | Always refuse |
74	
75	`--dry-run` returns the same plan without writing. `--force` makes source win
76	for previously managed drift and conflicts, including modified stale files; it
77	does not overwrite unowned collisions. This keeps force bounded by the prior
78	manifest instead of turning it into a recursive replacement operation.
79	
80	Use `pia status <combo>` for a summary and `pia diff <combo> --runtime` for
81	managed path details before applying.
82	
83	## Selection and launch
84	
85	A combo is selected in this order:
86	
87	1. The combo argument passed to the command.
88	2. `PIA_COMBO`.
89	3. The persistent value written by `pia use`.
90	
91	`pia run [combo] -- <agent arguments>` first performs the same safe apply, then
92	combines the combo's checked-in `launchArgs` with trailing arguments and
93	forwards the child process's exit code. Drift, conflicts, unsafe source files,
94	or unowned collisions abort before launch. A stale parent digest emits a warning
95	but does not block a standalone child combo.
96	
97	Wrapper-owned routing/session flags and secret-bearing flags are rejected from
98	`launchArgs`; runtime invocation remains explicit. Session storage is resolved
99	from engine, combo history policy, and canonical working directory. See
100	[sessions and handoff](sessions-and-handoff.md).
101	
102	## Why copies instead of inheritance
103	
104	Pi does not expose a stable, general-purpose config inheritance contract, and
105	OMP's layers do not cover every harness asset uniformly. `pia derive` therefore
106	copies a complete combo and records its parent digest. The child remains usable
107	and understandable on its own. Parent changes produce a lineage warning and a
108	review workflow, never an implicit merge at launch time.
109	
110	Declarative inheritance and three-way sync are intentionally deferred until
111	real usage demonstrates enough repeated maintenance to justify their conflict
112	rules. The research checkpoint is tracked in
113	[the backlog](../backlog/declarative-inheritance-three-way-sync.md).
114
```

```text
1	# Combos
2	
3	A combo is one complete, selectable agent setup. Its identifier is
4	`<engine>/<name>`, where the engine is `pi` or `omp`. Names are 1–60 characters,
5	start with a lowercase letter or digit, use lowercase letters, digits, dots,
6	underscores, or hyphens, and do not end in a dot. The shared restriction keeps
7	the generated `pia-<name>` value valid as an OMP profile.
8	
9	## Directory and metadata
10	
11	```text
12	combos/pi/research/
13	  combo.json
14	  agent/
15	    settings.json
16	    AGENTS.md
17	    skills/
18	    extensions/
19	```
20	
21	`agent/` mirrors the configuration files that should be managed at runtime. It
22	must be a complete, readable setup rather than a delta against another combo.
23	
24	A minimal `combo.json` is:
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "$schema": "../../../schema/combo.schema.json",
29	  "schemaVersion": 1,
30	  "description": "Research-oriented upstream Pi harness.",
31	  "maturity": "experimental",
32	  "launchArgs": [],
33	  "history": {
34	    "mode": "isolated"
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	The fields are:
40	
41	- `schemaVersion`: currently `1`.
42	- `description`: a short human explanation of the combo's purpose.
43	- `maturity`: `experimental`, `learning`, or `production`.
44	- `launchArgs`: non-secret agent arguments applied on every launch.
45	- `history`: `isolated`, or `shared` with a named same-engine group.
46	- `derivedFrom` and `parentDigest`: a paired lineage reference written by
47	  `pia derive`.
48	
49	Example shared history policy:
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "history": {
54	    "mode": "shared",
55	    "group": "daily-coding"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Sharing is still separated by engine and canonical project directory. It does
61	not make Pi and OMP JSONL files interchangeable. Group names follow the same
62	1–60 character/no-trailing-dot safety rule as combo names.
63	
64	Do not put auth tokens, API keys, `.env` files, sessions, blobs, package stores,
65	or caches in `agent/`. Reference packages from configuration; let the harness
66	install or cache them in runtime state.
67	
68	## Derive and maintain a combo
69	
70	Create a child from an existing combo:
71	
72	```sh
73	pia derive pi/base pi/research
74	```
75	
76	This makes a full copy, sets `derivedFrom`, and records a digest of the reviewed
77	parent. There is no live inheritance. Edit the child normally and commit it as
78	a standalone configuration.
79	
80	When a parent changes:
81	
82	```sh
83	pia lineage pi/research
84	pia diff pi/research --parent
85	# manually copy or adapt only the changes you want
86	pia lineage pi/research --ack
87	```
88	
89	`--ack` only records the current parent digest. It must be run after the review,
90	not as a way to hide an unresolved warning. Lineage must remain within one
91	engine and cycles are rejected.
92	
93	## Inspect and use combos
94	
95	```sh
96	pia list
97	pia list --tree
98	pia list --json
99	
100	pia use pi/research
101	pia current
102	
103	pia status pi/research
104	pia diff pi/research --runtime
105	pia apply pi/research --dry-run
106	pia apply pi/research
107	pia run pi/research -- <pi arguments>
108	```
109	
110	`pia run` can omit its combo after `pia use` or `PIA_COMBO`; an explicit run
111	argument always wins. The management command signatures shown here require
112	explicit combo IDs so mutations and diagnostics have an unambiguous target.
113	
114	If a managed runtime file was edited directly, normal apply fails without
115	changing anything. Review the diff and either carry the intended edit back to
116	`agent/`, or use `pia apply <combo> --force` to discard drift on paths that
117	`pia` previously owned. Unmanaged runtime files are preserved.
118	
119	`launchArgs` cannot contain wrapper-owned options such as profile, session,
120	cwd, config, resume/fork routing, or API-key flags. Put one-off agent options
121	after `--`; keep secrets in the harness's private auth mechanism or environment.
122	
123	## Command map
124	
125	In the table, `<session-selector>` means either `--latest` or
126	`--session <id-or-absolute-path>`.
127	
128	| Command | Purpose |
129	|---|---|
130	| `pia list [--tree|--json]` | Discover combos and lineage |
131	| `pia use <combo>` / `pia current` | Save or print the default selection |
132	| `pia derive <parent> <child> [--description TEXT]` | Copy a combo and record lineage |
133	| `pia lineage <combo> [--ack]` | Inspect or acknowledge a parent digest |
134	| `pia status <combo>` | Summarise source/runtime health |
135	| `pia diff <combo> [--runtime|--parent]` | Show managed runtime or lineage differences |
136	| `pia apply <combo> [--dry-run|--force]` | Safely materialise source configuration |
137	| `pia run [combo] -- <args>` | Safely apply, then launch the selected harness |
138	| `pia sessions <combo>` | List sessions visible to that combo |
139	| `pia fork <from> <to> <session-selector> -- <args>` | Native same-engine session fork |
140	| `pia handoff <from> <to> <session-selector> --goal TEXT [--no-run] -- <args>` | Redacted context transfer |
141	| `pia doctor [--json]` | Check binaries, versions, source safety, and helpers |
142	| `pia completion <zsh\|bash\|powershell>` | Emit native shell completion code |
143

7	## Context
8	
9	Research completed on 2026-08-31 against Pi 0.84.4. The question is
10	whether remote messaging should become part of `pia`, a Pi combo, or remain an
11	external integration.
12	
13	`pia` is currently a foreground, dependency-free Pi/OMP configuration launcher.
14	It can mechanically start Pi RPC with:
15	
16	```sh
17	pia run pi/base -- --mode rpc
18	```
19	
20	The existing passthrough in `src/cli.ts` and `src/harness.ts` safely applies the
21	combo and supplies its private session directory. `src/process.ts` then launches
22	one child with inherited stdio and returns only its exit code. This is a useful
23	process boundary for an external supervisor, but it is not an authenticated
24	network API, a multi-session scheduler, or a durable gateway.
25	
26	The immediate decision is therefore **docs-first**. Keep `pia` core
27	transport-neutral, record the intended context contract and evidence, then test
28	an existing project outside this repository before committing any package,
29	extension, or combo.
30	
31	All candidate assessments below are **source-reviewed, not runtime-verified**,
32	unless a row explicitly says otherwise. A permissive version range or the
33	continued presence of an API does not prove Pi 0.84.4 compatibility.
34	
35	## Selected context model
36	
37	Use a **Pi-authoritative session router**, not an IM-history mirror.
38	
39	### Sources of truth
40	
41	| Domain | Authority | Consequence |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| Native message identity, sender, revision, deletion, membership, and attachment availability | IM provider | Do not infer current IM state from a Pi transcript. |
44	| Model-visible conversation, tool history, branches, and compaction | Pi session | Do not replay the surrounding room history on each prompt. |
45	| Admission, project/session binding, execution lease, queue, approvals, cursors, and delivery receipts | Gateway state | These need durable service state outside a combo. |
46	| Repository and tool side effects | Workspace, filesystem, and Git | Editing or deleting an IM message cannot undo an executed action. |
47	
48	Every admitted IM invocation is projected into exactly one selected Pi session.
49	Later turns continue from that Pi session rather than reconstructing context from
50	the IM timeline.
51	
52	A canonical transport key must use stable IDs: provider, bot
53	account/installation, tenant or equivalent, conversation ID, and an optional
54	thread/topic/subconversation ID. Display names, channel titles, usernames, and
55	mutable topic labels are not identity keys. A binding additionally selects an
56	approved project alias, Pi combo, canonical working directory, tool policy, and
57	current Pi session.
58	
59	### Thread and flat-room routing
60	
61	Discord threads provide a convenient visible task boundary, but the portable
62	contract cannot assume they exist. For a flat room, resolve a message in this
63	order:
64	
65	1. A reply to a known bot output uses the durable outbound-message-to-session
66	   mapping.
67	2. An authenticated gateway command names an authorized session handle.
68	3. A unique active binding for the conversation may be used.
69	4. If zero or multiple candidates remain, reject the message as ambiguous and
70	   require an explicit `/new`, `/resume`, or `/bind`.
71	
72	A reply edge is a routing hint, not automatically a new conversation. Quoted
73	text is untrusted data, never authenticated control syntax. If referenced text
74	is needed and is not already in Pi history, include only that explicit, bounded
75	reference with its provider message ID and actor attribution; do not recursively
76	fetch a reply chain or ambient room window.
77	
78	### Ordering and context lifetime
79	
80	- Use one durable FIFO execution lane and one writable owner per **Pi session**,
81	  not merely per room. Two rooms bound to one session still share one lane.
82	- Ordinary messages arriving while work is active become later turns. Steering
83	  must be an explicit, authorized control rather than an implicit consequence
84	  of arrival time.
85	- Treat Pi's `agent_settled` event as the terminal boundary after retries,
86	  compaction recovery, and queued continuations; `agent_end` alone is not final.
87	- Let Pi own normal context-window compaction. Do not maintain a second gateway
88	  summary of the same accepted conversation.
89	- Before Pi submission, a trustworthy edit may replace a pending job. After
90	  submission, edits and deletions become corrections or tombstones; they do not
91	  mutate an earlier Pi entry or reverse tool effects.
92	- Default DMs to a distinct binding per provider account and peer. Shared rooms
93	  may share a session only for mutually trusted collaborators, with every turn
94	  attributed to its authenticated actor.
95	
96	The router still needs a small durable control plane. At minimum it must retain
97	bindings, inbound provider IDs and job states, per-session ownership, the
98	original actor and response route, Pi entry/leaf cursors, pending approvals, and
99	outbound message/chunk receipts. It does not need a complete room transcript.
100	
101	## Pi integration surfaces
102	
103	| Surface | Appropriate use | Boundary |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| Pi extension | Foreground single-session remote control, policy hooks, tool interception, and approval UI | Session-scoped; long-lived resources must start/stop with session lifecycle; runs with the host user's permissions. |
106	| `AgentSession` / `AgentSessionRuntime` SDK | Preferred TypeScript embedding surface for a future companion service | The host owns admission, trust, disposal, replacement rebinding, queues, persistence, and multi-session coordination. |
107	| JSONL RPC over stdin/stdout | Process-isolated worker controlled by another service | One active replaceable runtime; no network listener, authentication, global scheduler, or documented multi-process JSONL writer safety. |
108	| Experimental CBOR protocol/client/server | Possible future multi-session substrate | No compatibility guarantee, no bundled network transport, and no turnkey coding-agent service today. |
109	| Raw session JSONL mutation | Diagnostics and migration only | Do not use as a live event bus or concurrent writer. |
110	
111	Pi project trust only controls project resource loading. It is not tool approval
112	or a sandbox. Pi tools and extensions run as the launching OS user; a remote
113	identity that may drive them must therefore be treated as a machine-access
114	credential unless a separately verified OS/VM boundary limits that authority.
115	
116	## Operational baseline
117	
118	A resident production gateway would have to own all of the following outside
119	`pia`:
120	
121	- deny-by-default account, tenant, guild, channel/thread/topic, actor, and admin
122	  admission;
123	- project and session binding, one-writer fencing, per-session queues, and
124	  bounded global concurrency;
125	- provider event cursors, durable deduplication, accepted/active/uncertain job
126	  states, and an outbound receipt or outbox strategy;
127	- restart reconciliation without concurrently mutating one Pi JSONL file;
128	- approval requests bound to actor, session, turn, tool, arguments, project,
129	  generation, and expiry, with timeout/disconnect failing closed;
130	- attachment type/size/path controls, temporary owner-only storage, retention,
131	  and safe handling of unavailable or expired media;
132	- credentials and mutable state outside Git-managed combo trees, with a minimal
133	  environment and redacted logs;
134	- functional health checks, bounded reconnect/backoff, process supervision,
135	  resource limits, backup/migration, reproducible deployment, and rollback.
136	
137	These criteria were informed by a managed Kimaki/OpenCode deployment review and
138	by the public [Kimaki](https://github.com/remorses/kimaki) architecture. They are
139	requirements for any comparable production claim, not claims that upstream
140	Kimaki or an existing Pi candidate implements every item.
141	
142	End-to-end exactly-once execution is not realistic across an IM provider, a
143	gateway database, Pi JSONL, filesystem side effects, and outbound APIs. A
144	truthful design should promise durable admission and reconciliation where
145	implemented, expose an `uncertain` outcome when it cannot prove completion, and
146	state the bounded circumstances in which duplicate execution or delivery may
147	occur.
148	
149	## Candidate snapshot
150	
151	### Shortlist
152	
153	| Candidate | Observed fit | Source-reviewed gaps | Current decision |
154	|---|---|---|---|
155	| [`@zylab/pirelay@0.10.0`](https://github.com/zikolach/pirelay/releases/tag/v0.10.0) | Pi extension plus local broker; exact requester/conversation/thread binding; multiple live Pi sessions; pairing, progress, files, and optional remote approval gates; MIT release and substantial tests | CI/lockfile target Pi 0.73.1 rather than 0.84.4; host authority remains; approval coverage is opt-in; state rewrite is locked but not fully atomic; prompt queues and uniform ingress dedup are not durable | **First external spike** for the selected session-router model |
156	| [`earendil-works/pi-chat` at `9adbd29`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-chat/tree/9adbd29b40ee27ff1decf0fc87cbe180b40924f5) | Same organization as Pi and linked from Pi's README; Discord/Telegram; one worker and Gondolin micro-VM per configured conversation; persistent workspace and channel log | Do not infer an official support contract; current Discord mapping is channel-level, not thread-level; pending jobs are memory-only; open outbound network; QEMU/tmux footprint; no release/test/service unit; legacy Pi package scope and no 0.84.4 run; `LICENSE`/package say Apache-2.0 while README says MIT | Test second **only when per-conversation VM isolation is required** |
157	| [`TelePi` at `de6369e`](https://github.com/benedict2310/TelePi/tree/de6369e7e202e737498025d5f7ad5bfa35e86fce) | Telegram-focused standalone SDK daemon; per-chat/topic sessions, streaming, images/voice, dialogs, handoff, launchd/systemd, and current source near Pi 0.84.4 | Published v0.4.2 is materially stale; exact 0.84.4 not tested; chat/topic-to-session mapping and busy state are memory-only; no durable ingress cursor/queue or built-in tool gate | Consider only for a **Telegram-first** requirement, using pinned current source |
158	
159	### Useful references, not adoption candidates
160	
161	| Project | Reusable lesson | Reason not to adopt now |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| [`pi-messenger-bridge` at `8b0c1da`](https://github.com/tintinweb/pi-messenger-bridge/tree/8b0c1da19c930225b15ec971f9225241a82b381d) | Small Pi extension and broad Telegram/WhatsApp/Slack/Discord/Matrix transport adapters | Every transport controls one active Pi session; one mutable pending reply destination is unsafe under concurrent senders; no durable routing, queue, dedup, attachments, or approval flow |
164	| [`Piscord` v1.7.0](https://github.com/Crokily/pi-discord-gateway/releases/tag/v1.7.0) | SQLite ingress queue, per-channel serialization, global concurrency, service setup, and retention | Confirmed broken by Pi 0.83/0.84 API changes; channel rather than actor admission; DMs can auto-register; no threads, streaming, or approval gate; replay and outbound failure semantics can duplicate or lose work |
165	| [`notdezzi/pi-discord-bridge` at `14c2572`](https://github.com/notdezzi/pi-discord-bridge/tree/14c2572b00b319c255e8c2036ee69f1618ac5470) | Desired project-channel to Pi-session-thread shape and direct extension streaming | Slash-command authorization bypass, shared project-channel fan-out, optional unauthenticated launcher, no durable queue, license conflict, and no tests/releases |
166	| [`tasercake/pi-connect` at `9982be6`](https://github.com/tasercake/pi-connect/tree/9982be694f547e4bbb702958f208ad6476498d8e) | Broad transport normalization, persistent RPC workers, crash `outcome-unknown` semantics, and optional Unix-user separation | No reliable license grant file, misleading npm name collision, Pi approval is not implemented, incompatible approval/yolo behavior, volatile queues, and no exact 0.84.4 proof |
167	| [`Dwsy/pi-gateway` at `953b1b0`](https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway/tree/953b1b0c857fdab22a39247320b891d8bde9e79c) | Deterministic Discord-thread/Telegram-topic session keys, worker pool, and bounded queues | Treats nonterminal `agent_end` as completion, auto-confirms unattended dialogs, has a configured but unenforced sandbox, and lacks current releases/test CI/durable queues |
168	
169	Architecture comparators worth revisiting only after a concrete candidate fails a
170	documented gate:
171	
172	- [remote-pi](https://github.com/jacobaraujo7/remote_pi) for device identity,
173	  keyring storage, relay trust disclosure, Unix-socket leadership, and service
174	  supervision;
175	- [pi-agent-web](https://github.com/leon-zym/pi-agent-web) for per-session process
176	  generations, controller leases, fencing, snapshot resynchronization, and exact
177	  Pi-version gates;
178	- [pi-rpc-bridge](https://github.com/CaptCanadaMan/pi-rpc-bridge) for a minimal
179	  loopback/private-network authentication boundary around one RPC process.
180	
181	The reviewed [`@gamalan/pi-gateway`](https://github.com/gamalan/pi-gateway) is
182	not added to the spike order: its one global RPC process/current-channel model,
183	nonterminal completion handling, open/no-token defaults, missing event dedup, and
184	license/provenance questions do not fit this contract.
185	
186	## Non-goals
187	
188	For the current repository phase:
189	
190	- no `pia gateway`, `pia serve`, network listener, broker, worker pool, provider
191	  adapter, service installer, or transport-aware combo schema;
192	- no full room transcript synchronization, automatic last-N history projection,
193	  cross-provider identity merge, or IM-native event mirror;
194	- no raw Pi RPC exposure as a secure public API and no dependency on the
195	  experimental CBOR stack;
196	- no Pi/OMP feature-parity promise for a Pi-specific integration;
197	- no exactly-once, never-lost, never-duplicated, sandbox, E2E-encryption, or
198	  universal-permission claim;
199	- no simultaneous local and gateway writers to one Pi session;
200	- no bot token, pairing secret, transport cursor, mapping database, queue,
201	  attachment cache, or outbox in a Git-managed combo tree;
202	- no committed gateway combo until an immutable external candidate passes the
203	  experimental gate.
204	
205	## Promotion gates
206	
207	The gates deliberately distinguish an experiment from a production service.
208	Failure at a higher tier does not prevent a clearly labelled lower-tier test.
209	
210	### 1. Documentation decision
211	
212	- Preserve this dated source review and session-router contract.
213	- Keep stable product-boundary language in `docs/ecosystem.md`; keep moving
214	  versions, rankings, and defects here.
215	
216	### 2. Out-of-tree executable spike
217	
218	- Name one operator, transport, topology, project-binding policy, concurrency
219	  target, attachment scope, target OS, and host-authority decision.
220	- Pin an immutable artifact and verify integrity, license/provenance, package
221	  scopes, install behavior, state paths, and required binaries.
222	- Run the real candidate with Pi 0.84.4 in a disposable account or VM and
223	  isolated `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`PIA_STATE_HOME`.
224	- Exercise authorized and unauthorized ingress, destination binding, same-session
225	  serialization, different-session concurrency, abort/new/resume/compact,
226	  `agent_settled`, approval allow/deny/timeout, attachments, disconnect, and
227	  process restart.
228	- Keep credentials and mutable state outside the repository and record every
229	  patch as a minimal, version-checked change.
230	
231	### 3. Pi-only experimental combo
232	
233	Passing this gate permits a `maturity: experimental` Pi combo without changing
234	`pia` core or its schema:
235	
236	- immutable, licensed package/commit pin with an accountable maintainer;
237	- exact Pi 0.84.4 load and an authorized/unauthorized round trip;
238	- correct destination under the declared single-session or multi-session
239	  concurrency model;
240	- explicit service-state root outside combo source, with no secret in Git;
241	- no unattended auto-confirm and no authorization bypass for alternate command
242	  paths;
243	- documentation that promises only the behavior actually tested and states
244	  best-effort delivery, no sandbox, no service supervision, and no OMP support;
245	- dedicated typecheck/runtime coverage for any combo-local extension, because the
246	  current project TypeScript check does not compile `combos/**`.
247	
248	### 4. Supported optional adapter
249	
250	- maintained compatibility CI against the declared Pi versions;
251	- upgrade and security-response owner;
252	- authorization, routing, lifecycle, provider-limit, and restart regression
253	  tests;
254	- documented state migration, support matrix, failure semantics, and removal
255	  path.
256	
257	### 5. Production resident service
258	
259	- durable provider cursors, ingress uniqueness, queue state machine, outcome
260	  reconciliation, and transactional/idempotent outbound strategy where possible;
261	- generation fencing, one authoritative session writer, and crash injection at
262	  every admission/execution/delivery boundary;
263	- deny-by-default admission, auditable approvals, bounded media/network inputs,
264	  credential rotation, environment isolation, and an explicit VM/container/UID
265	  boundary when chat users must not receive host authority;
266	- functional transport and Pi health checks, supervised restart/backoff,
267	  resource limits, log rotation/redaction, database backup/migration, immutable
268	  or reproducible deployment, atomic activation, rollback, and recovery drills.
269	
270	## Verification matrix
271	
272	Runtime cells start as **unverified**. Update them only from a repeatable spike;
273	do not convert source inference into a pass.
274	
275	| Candidate/ref | Artifact and license | Pi 0.84.4 load | State-root isolation | Admission | Binding/concurrency | Restart/dedup | Approval | Attachments | Result |
276	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
277	| Pirelay 0.10.0 | Source-reviewed | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | First spike |
278	| pi-chat `9adbd29` | License conflict recorded | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | N/A until designed | Unverified | Conditional on VM requirement |
279	| TelePi `de6369e` | Source-reviewed | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Unverified | Telegram-only fallback |
280	
281	A spike report should also capture the exact Node/Pi versions, package tarball or
282	Git digest, mutable files created, environment variables consumed, process tree,
283	provider event IDs, Pi entry IDs, outbound message IDs, fault-injection point,
284	and whether the outcome was completed, failed, or uncertain.
285	
286	## Open questions
287	
288	- Is the first real deployment Discord, Telegram, or multi-transport?
289	- Is it a foreground personal remote control or an always-on service?
290	- Does one trusted operator have host-user authority, or is VM/container/UID
291	  isolation mandatory?
292	- What exact channel/thread/topic-to-project policy and concurrency are needed?
293	- Which attachments and approval interactions are required?
294	- Who owns upgrades, credentials, provider setup, recovery, and incident response?
295	
296	## Authoritative sources
297	
298	- [Pi v0.84.4 release](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v0.84.4)
299	- Pi v0.84.4:
300	  [extensions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md),
301	  [SDK](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md),
302	  [RPC](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md),

317	
318	2026-08-31: remain P?. Document the Pi-authoritative session-router contract and

```text
1	# pi-agents
2	
3	`pi-agents` keeps multiple [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) and
4	[Oh My Pi](https://omp.sh/) harness combinations in one Git repository. Its
5	`pia` CLI selects a combo, safely materialises its configuration into private
6	runtime state, and launches the matching agent without putting credentials or
7	session history in Git.
8	
9	The design stays deliberately small: each combo contains a complete config
10	tree, derived combos are normal copies with explicit lineage metadata, and
11	parent changes are reviewed rather than merged implicitly.
12	
13	`pia` is written in [Node-native TypeScript](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v22.21.0/docs/api/typescript.html).
14	Node 22.19+ executes the erasable
15	`.ts` sources directly, so deployed checkouts need no build step or runtime
16	packages; TypeScript and Node type definitions are development-only tools used
17	by `npm run typecheck` and CI.
18	
19	## Quick start
20	
21	Requirements: Node.js 22.19 or newer, plus `pi` and/or `omp` for the combos you
22	want to run.
23	
24	```sh
25	git clone https://github.com/daviddwlee84/pi-agents.git
26	cd pi-agents
27	
28	# Optional for a development checkout; chezmoi deployments put bin/ on PATH.
29	npm link
30	
31	pia doctor
32	pia list --tree
33	pia apply pi/base --dry-run
34	pia run pi/base --
35	```
36	
37	No link is required to run directly from a checkout:
38	
39	```sh
40	./bin/pia --version              # macOS/Linux
41	```
42	
43	```powershell
44	.\bin\pia.ps1 --version         # Windows PowerShell
45	```
46	
47	```bat
48	bin\pia.cmd --version           # Windows cmd.exe
49	```
50	
51	When `bin/` is on `PATH`, all three environments use the command name `pia`.
52	The PowerShell launcher preserves literal argument boundaries and the child
53	exit code. The cmd launcher follows cmd.exe's normal quoting rules and is for
54	trusted interactive commands; programmatic callers with arbitrary input should
55	invoke `pia.ps1` through PowerShell. If an npm-installed harness is exposed as
56	a shim such as `pi.ps1`, `pia` invokes it through a fixed `PowerShell -File`
57	command and never enables child-process shell parsing.
58	
59	`pia run` safely applies the selected source before launch and stops on runtime
60	drift or an unowned collision. You can also save a default instead of naming
61	the combo every time:
62	
63	```sh
64	pia use pi/base
65	pia current
66	pia run -- --model provider/model
67	```
68	
69	Selection precedence is an explicit argument, then `PIA_COMBO`, then the value
70	saved by `pia use`.
71	
72	`pia` can generate native completion for every managed shell:
73	
74	```sh
75	pia completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_pia
76	pia completion bash > "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/pia"
77	```
78	
79	```powershell
80	pia completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
81	```
82	
83	Completion discovers combo directories directly, so `pia use <Tab>` reflects
84	newly derived or pulled combos without launching another Node process. The
85	provided chezmoi integrations generate/cache these scripts automatically.
86	
87	Human-readable output uses semantic terminal colours when the selected stream
88	supports them. `NO_COLOR` and `NODE_DISABLE_COLORS` disable colour;
89	`FORCE_COLOR` and non-zero `CLICOLOR_FORCE` can force it through a pipe. JSON,
90	completion code, versions, selected combo ids, and artifact paths always stay
91	plain for scripts.
92	
93	The compatibility snapshot for the current implementation is **Pi 0.84.4**
94	and **OMP 18.0.11**. Tests cover the wrapper's behavior and pinned session
95	fixtures; run `pia doctor` and a smoke launch when using a different upstream
96	version.
97	
98	## What is included
99	
100	- `combos/pi/base`: neutral upstream Pi configuration.
101	- `combos/pi/vanilla`: Pi with project/global resource discovery disabled by
102	  launch flags.
103	- `combos/omp/base`: neutral OMP native profile configuration.
104	- Strict source-to-runtime synchronisation with drift detection and dry runs.
105	- Per-combo or explicitly shared session storage, same-engine forks, and
106	  deterministic redacted handoffs across harnesses.
107	
108	Start with [combo authoring](docs/combos.md), then read
109	[architecture](docs/architecture.md),
110	[sessions and handoff](docs/sessions-and-handoff.md), the
111	[ecosystem snapshot](docs/ecosystem.md), and the optional
112	[chezmoi integration](docs/chezmoi.md).
113	
114	```sh
115	npm install --ignore-scripts   # development/type-check dependencies only
116	npm test
117	npm run typecheck
118	npm run check
119	```
120

1	# Architecture
2	
3	`pia` separates version-controlled intent from mutable agent state. The Git
4	repository is the source of truth for combo definitions; it is never an agent's
5	live home directory.
6	
7	## Data layout
8	
9	```text
10	pi-agents/
11	  combos/<pi|omp>/<name>/
12	    combo.json             declarative metadata
13	    agent/                 complete managed config tree
14	  schema/combo.schema.json
15	  bin/pia
16	  src/*.ts                 Node-native erasable TypeScript
17	
18	${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/pi-agents/
19	  selection.json           value saved by `pia use`
20	
21	${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents/
22	  manifests/               last-applied managed-file hashes and modes
23	  runtime/pi/<name>/agent/ Pi configuration runtime
24	  sessions/                isolated/shared session roots
25	  handoffs/                generated private Markdown artifacts
26	```
27	
28	`PIA_SOURCE_ROOT` can point the CLI at another checkout. `PIA_STATE_HOME`
29	replaces the entire state root. These overrides are useful for tests and
30	advanced setups; normal users should let the CLI derive both paths.
31	
32	For Pi, `pia` launches with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to the combo's runtime
33	directory. For OMP, it uses a native profile named `pia-<combo-name>` and asks
34	`omp --profile ... config path` for the real location instead of assuming a
35	home or XDG layout. `PIA_PI_BIN` and `PIA_OMP_BIN` can override the executable
36	names.
37	
38	## Source and runtime contract
39	
40	Only files below a combo's `agent/` directory are managed. Downloaded packages,
41	credentials, sessions, caches, blobs, databases, and any other runtime-created
42	files stay outside Git or remain unowned in the runtime tree.
43	
44	The source tree must not contain credentials, `.env` files, session/package/
45	cache stores, or symlinks. On POSIX systems runtime directories are created
46	with mode `0700`; managed files use `0600` or `0700` according to their
47	executable bit. Windows does not expose equivalent POSIX mode enforcement
48	through Node, so runtime files inherit the user's profile ACL and drift checks
49	compare content rather than synthetic mode bits there. Writes and manifest
50	replacement are atomic.
51	
52	The source uses only TypeScript syntax that Node can erase without code
53	generation. Runtime execution therefore stays build-free; `tsconfig.json` and
54	the development dependencies exist solely for strict `tsc --noEmit` checking.
55	
56	Known runtime/credential paths are rejected structurally. `npm run check` also
57	runs gitleaks over combo content when the binary is available, while CI and the
58	existing pre-commit stack enforce the same secret scan before source is shared.
59	
60	Each manifest records its exact absolute target and, for every managed relative
61	path, the content hash, executable bit, and mode. `pia apply` classifies paths
62	as follows:
63	
64	| Source/runtime state | Result |
65	|---|---|
66	| New source path, unused target | Create it |
67	| Source changed, runtime still at last applied value | Update it |
68	| Runtime changed independently | Refuse the whole apply |
69	| Source and runtime both changed | Refuse the whole apply |
70	| Source removed, runtime unchanged | Remove the stale managed path |
71	| Source removed, runtime changed | Refuse unless forced |
72	| Target-only path never owned by `pia` | Preserve and omit from normal diff |
73	| New source collides with an unowned path or non-file obstruction | Always refuse |
74	
75	`--dry-run` returns the same plan without writing. `--force` makes source win
76	for previously managed drift and conflicts, including modified stale files; it
77	does not overwrite unowned collisions. This keeps force bounded by the prior
78	manifest instead of turning it into a recursive replacement operation.
79	
80	Use `pia status <combo>` for a summary and `pia diff <combo> --runtime` for
81	managed path details before applying.
82	
83	## Selection and launch
84	
85	A combo is selected in this order:
86	
87	1. The combo argument passed to the command.
88	2. `PIA_COMBO`.
89	3. The persistent value written by `pia use`.
90	
91	`pia run [combo] -- <agent arguments>` first performs the same safe apply, then
92	combines the combo's checked-in `launchArgs` with trailing arguments and
93	forwards the child process's exit code. Drift, conflicts, unsafe source files,
94	or unowned collisions abort before launch. A stale parent digest emits a warning
95	but does not block a standalone child combo.
96	
97	Wrapper-owned routing/session flags and secret-bearing flags are rejected from
98	`launchArgs`; runtime invocation remains explicit. Session storage is resolved
99	from engine, combo history policy, and canonical working directory. See
100	[sessions and handoff](sessions-and-handoff.md).
101	
102	## Why copies instead of inheritance
103	
104	Pi does not expose a stable, general-purpose config inheritance contract, and
105	OMP's layers do not cover every harness asset uniformly. `pia derive` therefore
106	copies a complete combo and records its parent digest. The child remains usable
107	and understandable on its own. Parent changes produce a lineage warning and a
108	review workflow, never an implicit merge at launch time.
109	
110	Declarative inheritance and three-way sync are intentionally deferred until
111	real usage demonstrates enough repeated maintenance to justify their conflict
112	rules. The research checkpoint is tracked in
113	[the backlog](../backlog/declarative-inheritance-three-way-sync.md).
114
```

```text
1	# Combos
2	
3	A combo is one complete, selectable agent setup. Its identifier is
4	`<engine>/<name>`, where the engine is `pi` or `omp`. Names are 1–60 characters,
5	start with a lowercase letter or digit, use lowercase letters, digits, dots,
6	underscores, or hyphens, and do not end in a dot. The shared restriction keeps
7	the generated `pia-<name>` value valid as an OMP profile.
8	
9	## Directory and metadata
10	
11	```text
12	combos/pi/research/
13	  combo.json
14	  agent/
15	    settings.json
16	    AGENTS.md
17	    skills/
18	    extensions/
19	```
20	
21	`agent/` mirrors the configuration files that should be managed at runtime. It
22	must be a complete, readable setup rather than a delta against another combo.
23	
24	A minimal `combo.json` is:
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "$schema": "../../../schema/combo.schema.json",
29	  "schemaVersion": 1,
30	  "description": "Research-oriented upstream Pi harness.",
31	  "maturity": "experimental",
32	  "launchArgs": [],
33	  "history": {
34	    "mode": "isolated"
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	The fields are:
40	
41	- `schemaVersion`: currently `1`.
42	- `description`: a short human explanation of the combo's purpose.
43	- `maturity`: `experimental`, `learning`, or `production`.
44	- `launchArgs`: non-secret agent arguments applied on every launch.
45	- `history`: `isolated`, or `shared` with a named same-engine group.
46	- `derivedFrom` and `parentDigest`: a paired lineage reference written by
47	  `pia derive`.
48	
49	Example shared history policy:
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "history": {
54	    "mode": "shared",
55	    "group": "daily-coding"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Sharing is still separated by engine and canonical project directory. It does
61	not make Pi and OMP JSONL files interchangeable. Group names follow the same
62	1–60 character/no-trailing-dot safety rule as combo names.
63	
64	Do not put auth tokens, API keys, `.env` files, sessions, blobs, package stores,
65	or caches in `agent/`. Reference packages from configuration; let the harness
66	install or cache them in runtime state.
67	
68	## Derive and maintain a combo
69	
70	Create a child from an existing combo:
71	
72	```sh
73	pia derive pi/base pi/research
74	```
75	
76	This makes a full copy, sets `derivedFrom`, and records a digest of the reviewed
77	parent. There is no live inheritance. Edit the child normally and commit it as
78	a standalone configuration.
79	
80	When a parent changes:
81	
82	```sh
83	pia lineage pi/research
84	pia diff pi/research --parent
85	# manually copy or adapt only the changes you want
86	pia lineage pi/research --ack
87	```
88	
89	`--ack` only records the current parent digest. It must be run after the review,
90	not as a way to hide an unresolved warning. Lineage must remain within one
91	engine and cycles are rejected.
92	
93	## Inspect and use combos
94	
95	```sh
96	pia list
97	pia list --tree
98	pia list --json
99	
100	pia use pi/research
101	pia current
102	
103	pia status pi/research
104	pia diff pi/research --runtime
105	pia apply pi/research --dry-run
106	pia apply pi/research
107	pia run pi/research -- <pi arguments>
108	```
109	
110	`pia run` can omit its combo after `pia use` or `PIA_COMBO`; an explicit run
111	argument always wins. The management command signatures shown here require
112	explicit combo IDs so mutations and diagnostics have an unambiguous target.
113	
114	If a managed runtime file was edited directly, normal apply fails without
115	changing anything. Review the diff and either carry the intended edit back to
116	`agent/`, or use `pia apply <combo> --force` to discard drift on paths that
117	`pia` previously owned. Unmanaged runtime files are preserved.
118	
119	`launchArgs` cannot contain wrapper-owned options such as profile, session,
120	cwd, config, resume/fork routing, or API-key flags. Put one-off agent options
121	after `--`; keep secrets in the harness's private auth mechanism or environment.
122	
123	## Command map
124	
125	In the table, `<session-selector>` means either `--latest` or
126	`--session <id-or-absolute-path>`.
127	
128	| Command | Purpose |
129	|---|---|
130	| `pia list [--tree|--json]` | Discover combos and lineage |
131	| `pia use <combo>` / `pia current` | Save or print the default selection |
132	| `pia derive <parent> <child> [--description TEXT]` | Copy a combo and record lineage |
133	| `pia lineage <combo> [--ack]` | Inspect or acknowledge a parent digest |
134	| `pia status <combo>` | Summarise source/runtime health |
135	| `pia diff <combo> [--runtime|--parent]` | Show managed runtime or lineage differences |
136	| `pia apply <combo> [--dry-run|--force]` | Safely materialise source configuration |
137	| `pia run [combo] -- <args>` | Safely apply, then launch the selected harness |
138	| `pia sessions <combo>` | List sessions visible to that combo |
139	| `pia fork <from> <to> <session-selector> -- <args>` | Native same-engine session fork |
140	| `pia handoff <from> <to> <session-selector> --goal TEXT [--no-run] -- <args>` | Redacted context transfer |
141	| `pia doctor [--json]` | Check binaries, versions, source safety, and helpers |
142	| `pia completion <zsh\|bash\|powershell>` | Emit native shell completion code |
143
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Sessions and handoff
2	
3	Configuration can be copied safely; live session files cannot. `pia` therefore
4	separates normal history, same-engine forks, and cross-harness handoffs into
5	three explicit operations.
6	
7	## Session isolation
8	
9	An isolated combo stores history below:
10	
11	```text
12	${PIA_STATE_HOME:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents}/
13	  sessions/<engine>/<combo-name>/<project-key>/
14	```
15	
16	With `history.mode: shared`, the leaf instead uses:
17	
18	```text
19	sessions/<engine>/shared/<group>/<project-key>/
20	```
21	
22	The project key is derived from the canonical working directory. Thus two
23	projects do not accidentally resume one another, and a shared group never
24	crosses the Pi/OMP boundary. Use `pia sessions <combo>` to inspect the sessions
25	available under the combo's effective policy.
26	
27	## Same-engine forks
28	
29	```sh
30	pia fork pi/base pi/research --latest -- <target arguments>
31	pia fork pi/base pi/research --session <id-or-path> -- <target arguments>
32	```
33	
34	The first two arguments are source and target combo IDs. Forking is allowed
35	only when both use the same engine. `--latest` selects the newest source session;
36	`--session` accepts an unambiguous session-ID prefix from the source combo's
37	effective session root, or an explicit absolute path.
38	
39	`pia` delegates to the target harness's native `--fork` behavior and creates a
40	new target session; it does not append to or byte-copy the source session. Use a
41	fork when the target should retain the native conversation tree and both sides
42	understand exactly the same session format.
43	
44	Although both snapshots use a session format identified as version 3, they are
45	not wire-compatible. OMP includes a title slot and additional entry types, so
46	raw cross-harness session sharing is prohibited. See the pinned
47	[Pi session loader](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/853a80d26c90a14c1886f0ebb8ffaae133ca2185/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts#L548-L553)
48	and [OMP session format](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/51f03804476c3fd3c15748ae07e4849d1efc883b/docs/session.md#L61-L66).
49	
50	## Deterministic handoff
51	
52	```sh
53	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --latest \
54	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" -- <target arguments>
55	```
56	
57	Handoff supports same- or cross-engine transfer. It reads the selected source
58	session without changing it and produces a private Markdown artifact under
59	`$PIA_STATE_HOME/handoffs/`. Generation is local and deterministic; it does not
60	ask another model to summarise the transcript.
61	
62	The extractor:
63	
64	1. Prefers the newest compaction summary; if none exists, keeps the first user
65	   goal and a bounded set of recent messages.
66	2. Adds source, target, and session provenance, canonical working directory,
67	   Git branch, `HEAD`, status, and diff-stat.
68	3. Excludes hidden thinking, images, tool arguments, and successful tool
69	   output. Failed tool output is capped at 2 KiB.
70	4. Caps the document at 128 KiB and reports omitted or truncated blocks.
71	5. Runs the agent-history-hygiene redactor, then validates with `gitleaks`.
72	   Any redaction or validation failure aborts the handoff.
73	6. Writes the artifact with mode `0600` on POSIX (or the containing user ACL on
74	   Windows) and starts a fresh target session with it as the first attachment.
75	
76	Use `--session <id-or-absolute-path>` instead of `--latest` to select
77	explicitly. `--max-bytes N` can lower or raise the 128 KiB default (minimum
78	4096). Use `--no-run` to generate the document without launching the target:
79	
80	```sh
81	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --session <id-or-path> \
82	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" --no-run
83	```
84	
85	Review the generated file before sharing it outside the machine. Redaction is a
86	fail-closed safety boundary, not a promise that arbitrary prose contains no
87	sensitive business context.
88	
89	Malformed session data, a missing source session, Git provenance failure in the
90	current project, an unavailable redactor or `gitleaks`, and an oversized/unsafe
91	artifact all fail before target launch. `pia doctor` checks the required helper
92	commands.
93
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Pi harness ecosystem snapshot
2	
3	This page records the assumptions behind `pia`, not a permanent verdict on fast
4	moving upstream projects. The compatibility snapshot reviewed and represented
5	by the test fixtures is **Pi 0.84.4** and **Oh My Pi 18.0.11**, as of
6	2026-08-30.
7	
8	## Upstream Pi
9	
10	Pi supports a global agent directory, project-local `.pi` configuration, and
11	the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` override. These primitives are sufficient for `pia`
12	to launch isolated full configurations, while repo-local settings and resources
13	can still participate according to Pi's trust and discovery rules. See Pi's
14	[settings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md),
15	[environment variables](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md),
16	and [packages](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages) documentation.
17	
18	Pi does not provide a single stable first-class abstraction that composes all
19	settings, skills, extensions, package references, prompts, and session policy as
20	a named inheritable profile. That is why `pia` switches the complete agent
21	directory and keeps combo inheritance explicit and copy-based.
22	
23	Two issue pages are easy to misread:
24	
25	- [#3590, layered config](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3590)
26	- [#7813, multiple settings profiles](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7813)
27	
28	Their closed status is easy to over-interpret, but each timeline contains the
29	GitHub Actions message that issues from new contributors are auto-closed
30	pending maintainer review. They are evidence that users asked
31	for these capabilities, **not** an explicit maintainer roadmap rejection. Any
32	future design review should re-check upstream rather than preserving either
33	interpretation as fact.
34	
35	## Oh My Pi
36	
37	OMP exposes named profiles through `omp --profile <name>` and has broader
38	configuration discovery and overlay behavior. A named profile relocates native
39	configuration and runtime resources, so `pia` uses an OMP profile named
40	`pia-<combo>` and resolves its actual path with OMP itself. See the upstream
41	[configuration and profile guide](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/config-usage.md).
42	
43	OMP's richer configuration system does not remove the need for a repository
44	contract: different resource types have different discovery rules, runtime
45	state must still stay out of Git, and a Pi combo should remain understandable
46	without translating it into OMP concepts. `pia` therefore presents the same
47	simple combo/source/runtime workflow for both engines and lets OMP own only its
48	native profile resolution.
49	
50	## MCP is an extension choice
51	
52	Do not describe `pi.mcp` as a Pi core package-manifest feature. The manifest
53	shape discussed in the original research belongs to an adapter/integration,
54	not upstream Pi's package contract. MCP support for a combo should identify the
55	specific extension it uses—for example the community
56	[`pi-mcp-adapter`](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter)—and keep that
57	adapter's configuration inside the combo like any other harness dependency.
58	
59	This distinction matters for portability: a combo that depends on an adapter
60	must pin and test that adapter rather than assuming another Pi installation can
61	interpret an undocumented `pi.mcp` field.
62	
63	## Remote messaging is an external integration
64	
65	Pi packages and extensions can connect a session to Discord, Telegram, or other
66	messaging systems, and a future Pi-only combo may pin one of those integrations.
67	That does not make remote messaging a `pia` core capability. `pia` does not
68	provide a messaging transport, authentication or admission, live session
69	orchestration, sandboxing, durable delivery, or service supervision.
70	
71	Apply the same rule as for MCP: name the specific integration, pin it, and test
72	its behavior against the selected Pi version instead of attributing third-party
73	behavior to Pi itself. The Pi README links to the separate
74	[`earendil-works/pi-chat`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-chat) project as
75	a chat-automation option; its shared organization and upstream link do not by
76	themselves establish a support contract or compatibility with this repository's
77	Pi snapshot.
78	
79	See the dated [IM gateway research](../backlog/pi-im-gateway.md) for the selected
80	session-router context contract, candidate evidence, and the gates for moving
81	from an external spike to an experimental combo or maintained service.
82	
83	## Why maintain another thin layer?
84	
85	There are many ready-made harnesses and profile managers. Use one of them when
86	its opinionated defaults already match the job. This repository is justified
87	when the goal is to:
88	
89	- keep experimental, learning, and production combos together;
90	- switch Pi and OMP through one predictable interface;
91	- review the exact Git-managed configuration before it reaches runtime;
92	- keep auth, sessions, packages, and caches private and mutable;
93	- reproduce selected behaviors from other harnesses without adopting all of
94	  their machinery.
95	
96	Research into [Claude Code](../backlog/claude-code-harness-to-pi.md),
97	[Codex](../backlog/codex-harness-to-pi.md), and
98	[OpenCode](../backlog/opencode-harness-to-pi.md) is intentionally deferred until
99	the base workflow has real usage data. Re-check upstream versions, docs, CLI
100	flags, and session formats before promoting any result to a production combo.
101
```
</details></tool-use>
