 # Pi harness ecosystem snapshot
 
 This page records the assumptions behind `pia`, not a permanent verdict on fast
 moving upstream projects. The compatibility snapshot reviewed and represented
 by the test fixtures is **Pi 0.84.4** and **Oh My Pi 18.0.11**, as of
 2026-08-30.
 
 ## Upstream Pi
 
 Pi supports a global agent directory, project-local `.pi` configuration, and
 the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` override. These primitives are sufficient for `pia`
 to launch isolated full configurations, while repo-local settings and resources
 can still participate according to Pi's trust and discovery rules. See Pi's
 [settings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md),
 [environment variables](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md),
 and [packages](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages) documentation.
 
 Pi does not provide a single stable first-class abstraction that composes all
 settings, skills, extensions, package references, prompts, and session policy as
 a named inheritable profile. That is why `pia` switches the complete agent
 directory and keeps combo inheritance explicit and copy-based.
 
 Two issue pages are easy to misread:
 
 - [#3590, layered config](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3590)
 - [#7813, multiple settings profiles](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7813)
 
 Their closed status is easy to over-interpret, but each timeline contains the
 GitHub Actions message that issues from new contributors are auto-closed
 pending maintainer review. They are evidence that users asked
 for these capabilities, **not** an explicit maintainer roadmap rejection. Any
 future design review should re-check upstream rather than preserving either
 interpretation as fact.
 
 ## Oh My Pi
 
 OMP exposes named profiles through `omp --profile <name>` and has broader
 configuration discovery and overlay behavior. A named profile relocates native
 configuration and runtime resources, so `pia` uses an OMP profile named
 `pia-<combo>` and resolves its actual path with OMP itself. See the upstream
 [configuration and profile guide](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/config-usage.md).
 
 OMP's richer configuration system does not remove the need for a repository
 contract: different resource types have different discovery rules, runtime
 state must still stay out of Git, and a Pi combo should remain understandable
 without translating it into OMP concepts. `pia` therefore presents the same
 simple combo/source/runtime workflow for both engines and lets OMP own only its
 native profile resolution.
 
 ## MCP is an extension choice
 
 Do not describe `pi.mcp` as a Pi core package-manifest feature. The manifest
 shape discussed in the original research belongs to an adapter/integration,
 not upstream Pi's package contract. MCP support for a combo should identify the
 specific extension it uses—for example the community
 [`pi-mcp-adapter`](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter)—and keep that
 adapter's configuration inside the combo like any other harness dependency.
 
 This distinction matters for portability: a combo that depends on an adapter
 must pin and test that adapter rather than assuming another Pi installation can
 interpret an undocumented `pi.mcp` field.
 
+## Remote messaging is an external integration
+
+Pi packages and extensions can connect a session to Discord, Telegram, or other
+messaging systems, and a future Pi-only combo may pin one of those integrations.
+That does not make remote messaging a `pia` core capability. `pia` does not
+provide a messaging transport, authentication or admission, live session
+orchestration, sandboxing, durable delivery, or service supervision.
+
+Apply the same rule as for MCP: name the specific integration, pin it, and test
+its behavior against the selected Pi version instead of attributing third-party
+behavior to Pi itself. The Pi README links to the separate
+[`earendil-works/pi-chat`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-chat) project as
+a chat-automation option; its shared organization and upstream link do not by
+themselves establish a support contract or compatibility with this repository's
+Pi snapshot.
+
+See the dated [IM gateway research](../backlog/pi-im-gateway.md) for the selected
+session-router context contract, candidate evidence, and the gates for moving
+from an external spike to an experimental combo or maintained service.
+
 ## Why maintain another thin layer?
 
 There are many ready-made harnesses and profile managers. Use one of them when
 its opinionated defaults already match the job. This repository is justified
 when the goal is to:
 
 - keep experimental, learning, and production combos together;
 - switch Pi and OMP through one predictable interface;
 - review the exact Git-managed configuration before it reaches runtime;
 - keep auth, sessions, packages, and caches private and mutable;
 - reproduce selected behaviors from other harnesses without adopting all of
   their machinery.
 
 Research into [Claude Code](../backlog/claude-code-harness-to-pi.md),
 [Codex](../backlog/codex-harness-to-pi.md), and
 [OpenCode](../backlog/opencode-harness-to-pi.md) is intentionally deferred until
 the base workflow has real usage data. Re-check upstream versions, docs, CLI
 flags, and session formats before promoting any result to a production combo.
```

1	# Evaluate declarative combo inheritance
2	
3	**Status**: P?
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · `docs/architecture.md` · `docs/combos.md`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Deferred on 2026-08-30 in favor of complete copied configs with lineage
10	metadata. Inheritance looks attractive for `base -> language -> domain`
11	families, but defining merge, deletion, ordering, validation, and conflict rules
12	before real usage would add a second configuration language without evidence it
13	is needed.
14	
15	## Current findings
16	
17	- `pia derive` copies a complete parent and records `derivedFrom` plus a parent
18	  digest. Parent changes warn; the child never changes until a human reviews it.
19	- `pia diff --parent` and `pia lineage --ack` provide a deliberately manual
20	  update loop with no hidden launch-time composition.
21	- OMP has native layers, while Pi and individual resource types expose
22	  different composition behavior. A wrapper-level merge could therefore be
23	  surprising even if it works for simple settings objects.
24	- Three-way sync could preserve child edits better than re-copying, but needs a
25	  durable base snapshot and precise treatment of arrays, renames, deletes,
26	  executable modes, and conflicts.
27	
28	## Options to compare
29	
30	| Option | Benefit | Cost/risk |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| Keep copy + digest acknowledgement | Explicit, portable, easy to debug | Repeated manual updates |
33	| Declarative `extends` materialised at apply | Compact child definitions | Merge semantics become a public API |
34	| Three-way sync command | Preserves independent child edits | Complex conflict/base storage and recovery |
35	
36	## Open questions
37	
38	- How often do parent changes need to propagate, and how many files are
39	  repeatedly copied in practice?
40	- Are conflicts mostly structured settings, or arbitrary prompts, skills, and
41	  executable assets?
42	- Should inheritance be engine-neutral or defer to each harness's native
43	  mechanisms?
44	- Can every effective combo still be inspected, exported, and reproduced
45	  without running an opaque merge?
46	
47	## Exit criteria
48	
49	- At least three meaningful derived combos and two parent-update events have
50	  been maintained with the copy workflow.
51	- The maintenance cost and conflict types are recorded with concrete examples.
52	- A decision note specifies merge/delete/array/mode/conflict behavior for any
53	  proposed alternative and includes migration/rollback steps.
54	- If complexity is justified, a throwaway prototype proves deterministic
55	  materialisation and conflict reporting before changing the public schema.
56	
57	## Decision
58	
59	2026-08-30: use complete copies and digest acknowledgements now. Do not add
60	declarative inheritance or three-way sync until the exit criteria show a real
61	maintenance problem.
62
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Anti-patterns to avoid
2	
3	When applying or maintaining this harness, avoid the following:
4	
5	- **Spawning new files** like `IDEAS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `WISHLIST.md`,
6	  `FUTURE.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `LESSONS.md`, `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`,
7	  `GOTCHAS.md` alongside `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/`. Three
8	  surfaces, always.
9	
10	- **Backlog or pitfall docs in `docs/`**. `docs/` is user-facing reference;
11	  these folders are maintainer-facing memory. Mixing them confuses readers.
12	
13	- **Pitfall docs titled by root cause** (e.g.
14	  `tmux-update-environment.md`) instead of symptom (e.g.
15	  `tmux-pane-loses-ssh-connection-var.md`). You'll search by what you're
16	  seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
17	
18	- **Paraphrasing error messages** in pitfall docs. Copy-paste the full
19	  error including stack/codes — paraphrasing throws away the searchable
20	  bits.
21	
22	- **Backlog or pitfall docs without dates**. A 6-month-old "we decided X"
23	  without a date loses meaning — re-validate or treat as stale.
24	
25	- **Bulk-migrating scattered historical pitfalls** into `pitfalls/` on day
26	  one. High risk of broken cross-links + lost context. Index them in the
27	  README's cross-reference table; physically migrate only when natural.
28	
29	- **Auto-redacting `backlog/` or `pitfalls/`** the way agent scratchpads
30	  are redacted. These are first-class docs you write deliberately; treat
31	  them like any other doc for secret review.
32	
33	- **TODO heading drift**. Keep the exact section order (`P1`, `P2`, `P3`,
34	  `P?`, `Done`) and item forms that `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates.
35	  If you need to evolve the format, update the validator and the
36	  documented format in the same change.
37	
38	- **Letting `## Done` grow unbounded**. Prune into a `CHANGELOG.md` (or
39	  similar) once prior-year items appear or the section grows past ~20
40	  entries, keeping recent entries for context.
41	
42	- **Overwriting an existing `TODO.md` with the template**. The bundled
43	  `scripts/init.sh` is conservative on purpose — pass `--force` only after
44	  preserving any real entries you want to keep.
45
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# When to add a backlog or pitfall doc, and the upgrade path
2	
3	## Backlog: when an entry needs `backlog/<slug>.md`
4	
5	Add a backlog doc when **any** apply:
6	
7	- `P?` priority (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
8	- Captures paused troubleshooting **that you intend to fix later** (preserve
9	  the error trace + root-cause analysis before context evaporates)
10	- Multiple options were considered (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
11	- `L` or `XL` effort (architectural; needs design before code)
12	
13	`S` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the TODO line is usually
14	enough.
15	
16	## Pitfalls: when a debugging session deserves `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
17	
18	Add a pitfall doc when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something that
19	wasn't googleable, AND any of:
20	
21	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (silent state, weird side
22	  effect, behaviour change without error)
23	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
24	  must come after process completion, etc.)
25	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
26	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
27	- A specific tool version is required or forbidden, and failure at the wrong
28	  version is silent / confusing
29	
30	Skip a pitfall doc when:
31	
32	- Trivially googleable (next person solves in 30 seconds)
33	- Already covered as part of normal config docs in `docs/<tool>.md` —
34	  cross-link from `pitfalls/README.md`'s "Cross-referenced pitfalls" table
35	  instead of duplicating
36	- Already a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` — those have higher enforcement
37	  (cross-link only)
38	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot)
39	
40	## Disambiguation: pitfall vs backlog vs TODO entry vs invariant
41	
42	| Situation | Goes in |
43	|---|---|
44	| "We hit X, debugged it, applied workaround, moving on" | `pitfalls/` |
45	| "We hit X, debugged it, but the real fix is queued" | `pitfalls/` (capture trace) AND `TODO.md` (queue the fix) — link both ways |
46	| "We thought about doing X but deferred" | `TODO.md` (P2/P3) |
47	| "We thought about doing X, did a 2-day spike, deferred" | `TODO.md` (P?) + `backlog/` |
48	| "X is a rule everyone must follow forever" | `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant |
49	
50	## Upgrade path: pitfall → Hard invariant
51	
52	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` (or the project's
53	agent contract file) when:
54	
55	- It recurs across machines / agents / sessions despite being documented
56	- The trap silently corrupts state (no error message, just wrong behaviour)
57	- The workaround is non-obvious enough that "remember to do X" is unsafe
58	
59	When graduating:
60	
61	1. Add the rule to `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants section
62	2. Link from the invariant back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for context
63	3. Leave the pitfall doc as historical record (don't delete — it explains
64	   *why* the invariant exists)
65
```
</details></tool-use>

404	async function cmdDoctor(sourceRoot: string, stateRoot: string, args: string[], env: Env): Promise<void> {
405	  const json = takeFlag(args, "--json");
406	  if (args.length) throw new Error(`Unknown doctor argument: ${args[0]}`);
407	  const checks: DoctorCheck[] = [];
408	  const add = (name: string, ok: boolean, detail: string, severity: Severity = "error") => {
409	    checks.push({ name, ok, detail, severity });
410	  };
411	  const [major, minor] = process.versions.node.split(".").map(Number);
412	  add("node", major > 22 || (major === 22 && minor >= 19), process.versions.node);
413	  add("git", Boolean(commandExists("git")), commandExists("git") || "not found");
414	  add("python3", Boolean(commandExists("python3")), commandExists("python3") || "not found", "warning");
415	  add("gitleaks", Boolean(commandExists("gitleaks")), commandExists("gitleaks") || "not found", "warning");
416	  for (const engine of ["pi", "omp"]) {
417	    const binary = engine === "pi" ? env.PIA_PI_BIN || "pi" : env.PIA_OMP_BIN || "omp";
418	    const probe = commandResult(binary, ["--version"], { env });
419	    add(engine, probe.ok, probe.ok ? (probe.stdout || probe.stderr).trim() : "not installed", "warning");
420	  }
421	  try {
422	    const combos = await listCombos(sourceRoot);
423	    for (const combo of combos) await scanTree(combo.agentDir);
424	    add("combos", true, `${combos.length} valid`);
425	  } catch (error) {
426	    add("combos", false, errorMessage(error));
427	  }
428	  try {
429	    const selected = env.PIA_COMBO || (await readSelection(env));
430	    if (selected) await loadCombo(sourceRoot, selected);
431	    add("selection", true, selected || "none", "warning");
432	  } catch (error) {
433	    add("selection", false, errorMessage(error));
434	  }
435	  add("sourceRoot", true, sourceRoot);
436	  add("stateRoot", true, stateRoot);
437	  add("configRoot", true, getConfigRoot(env));
438	  if (json) printJson({ checks });
439	  else {
440	    for (const check of checks) {
441	      const label = check.ok ? "ok" : check.severity === "warning" ? "warn" : "error";
442	      process.stdout.write(
443	        `${tone(stateTone(label), label)}\t${ui.accent(check.name, stdoutStyle)}\t` +
444	        `${ui.muted(check.detail, stdoutStyle)}\n`,
445	      );
446	    }
447	  }
448	  if (checks.some((check) => !check.ok && check.severity === "error")) process.exitCode = 1;
449	}

451	export async function main(argv: string[], env: Env = process.env): Promise<void> {
452	  const sourceRoot = getSourceRoot(env);
453	  const stateRoot = getStateRoot(env);
454	  const args = [...argv];
455	  if (args[0] === "--help" || args[0] === "-h" || args[0] === "help") {
456	    printHelp();
457	    return;
458	  }

```text
1	> pi can create extensions. Ask it to build one for your use case.
2	
3	# Extensions
4	
5	Extensions are TypeScript modules that extend pi's behavior. They can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, add commands, and more.
6	
7	> **Placement for /reload:** Put extensions in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (global) or `.pi/extensions/` (project-local) for auto-discovery. Use `pi -e ./path.ts` only for quick tests. Extensions in auto-discovered locations can be hot-reloaded with `/reload`.
8	
9	**Key capabilities:**
10	- **Custom tools** - Register tools the LLM can call via `pi.registerTool()`
11	- **Event interception** - Block or modify tool calls, inject context, customize compaction
12	- **User interaction** - Prompt users via `ctx.ui` (select, confirm, input, notify)
13	- **Custom UI components** - Full TUI components with keyboard input via `ctx.ui.custom()` for complex interactions
14	- **Custom commands** - Register commands like `/mycommand` via `pi.registerCommand()`
15	- **Session persistence** - Store state that survives restarts via `pi.appendEntry()`
16	- **Custom rendering** - Control how tool calls/results and messages appear in TUI
17	
18	**Example use cases:**
19	- Permission gates (confirm before `rm -rf`, `sudo`, etc.)
20	- Git checkpointing (stash at each turn, restore on branch)
21	- Path protection (block writes to `.env`, `node_modules/`)
22	- Custom compaction (summarize conversation your way)
23	- Conversation summaries (see `summarize.ts` example)
24	- Interactive tools (questions, wizards, custom dialogs)
25	- Stateful tools (todo lists, connection pools)
26	- External integrations (file watchers, webhooks, CI triggers)
27	- Games while you wait (see `snake.ts` example)
28	
29	See [examples/extensions/](../examples/extensions/) for working implementations.
