1548	  async function handleRelayDoctor(ctx: ExtensionContext): Promise<void> {
1549	    try {
1550	      const migrationPlan = await planRelayConfigMigrationForEnv();
1551	      if (migrationPlan) await promptAndApplyConfigMigration(ctx, migrationPlan);
1552	      const config = await ensureConfig(ctx, true);
1553	      const facts = await collectRelaySetupFacts(config);
1554	      const diagnostics = renderRelayStatusDiagnostics();
1555	      let brokerRepair: string | undefined;
1556	      const brokerState = runtime?.getBrokerSynchronizationState?.();
1557	      const authoritativeBinding = currentRoute ? await currentStatusBinding(config, "telegram") : undefined;
1558	      if (currentRoute && authoritativeBinding && brokerState?.routes[currentRoute.sessionKey] !== "synchronized") {
1559	        try {
1560	          const repaired = await runtime?.reconcileBrokerRoutes?.();
1561	          const routeHealth = repaired?.routes[currentRoute.sessionKey] ?? "unknown";
1562	          brokerRepair = routeHealth === "synchronized"
1563	            ? "Broker route repair: synchronized."
1564	            : `Broker route repair: ${routeHealth}; automatic retry remains active.`;
1565	        } catch {
1566	          brokerRepair = "Broker route repair: failed; automatic retry remains active. Check opt-in communication diagnostics locally for metadata-only details.";
1567	        }
1568	      } else if (currentRoute && brokerState) {
1569	        brokerRepair = `Broker route: ${brokerState.routes[currentRoute.sessionKey] ?? "unknown"}; transport: ${brokerState.transport}.`;
1570	      }
1571	      ctx.ui.notify([renderRelayDoctorReport(config, relaySetupDiagnostics(config, facts)), brokerRepair, diagnostics].filter(Boolean).join("\n\n"), "info");
1572	    } catch (error) {
1573	      const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
1574	      ctx.ui.notify(redactSecrets([
1575	        "Relay setup doctor",
1576	        "",
1577	        `Could not load relay config: ${message}`,
1578	        "Minimal Telegram setup: set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, then run /relay setup telegram and /relay connect telegram.",
1579	        "Discord and Slack are opt-in via discord.* / slack.* config or PI_RELAY_DISCORD_* / PI_RELAY_SLACK_* environment variables.",
1580	      ].join("\n")), "warning");

1582	  }

```text
1	# pi-chat
2	
3	A pi extension that bridges Discord and Telegram channels to a sandboxed pi session. Each connected channel gets its own [Gondolin](https://github.com/earendil-works/gondolin) micro-VM with persistent workspace, shared storage, memory, and skills.
4	
5	## Quick Start
6	
7	```bash
8	# Install
9	pi install /path/to/pi-chat
10	# or
11	pi -e /path/to/pi-chat
12	
13	# Configure accounts and channels
14	/chat-config
15	
16	# Connect
17	/chat-connect
18	```
19	
20	### Requirements
21	
22	- [QEMU](https://www.qemu.org/) installed (`brew install qemu` on macOS)
23	- Gondolin guest image (downloaded automatically on first connect)
24	- A Discord bot token or Telegram bot token
25	- `tmux` for multi-channel worker orchestration
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Features
30	
31	- **Discord server channels** and **Telegram DMs/groups**
32	- **Gondolin VM sandbox** per connection — tools run inside an isolated Alpine Linux micro-VM
33	- **Persistent workspace** and **shared storage** across sessions
34	- **Streamed preview** responses with edit-in-place
35	- **Reply-to-trigger** — bot replies are attached to the triggering message
36	- **Durable memory** — account-wide and channel-specific memory files
37	- **Skills** — agent-created reusable tools, auto-discovered and injected into the prompt
38	- **Encrypted secret exchange** — securely pass credentials via browser-based encryption
39	- **Remote control** — stop, compact, new session, and status via chat commands
40	- **Chat history** tool for searching older messages
41	- **File attachments** — send and receive files between chat and the VM
42	
43	---
44	
45	## Setup
46	
47	### Discord
48	
49	1. Create a bot at [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
50	2. Enable **Message Content Intent** under Bot settings
51	3. Run `/chat-config` → Create account → Discord
52	4. Enter your bot token
53	5. Invite the bot to a server (the setup flow provides the invite URL)
54	6. Select a server and configure channels
55	
56	### Telegram
57	
58	1. Create a bot via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)
59	2. Run `/chat-config` → Create account → Telegram
60	3. Enter your bot token
61	4. Add DMs or groups through the guided setup
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Commands
66	
67	| Command | Description |
68	|---------|-------------|
69	| `/chat-config` | Configure accounts, channels, and secrets |
70	| `/chat-connect` | Connect to a configured channel |
71	| `/chat-disconnect` | Disconnect the current channel |
72	| `/chat-status` | Show connection status, model, usage, context |
73	| `/chat-list` | List configured channels |
74	| `/chat-spawn-all` | Spawn every configured channel in detached tmux/pi sessions |
75	| `/chat-spawn-all --restart` | Restart those tmux/pi sessions |
76	| `/chat-workers` | Show managed tmux/pi worker status |
77	| `/chat-open-all` | Open running workers in a tiled tmux dashboard |
78	| `/chat-kill-all` | Kill all managed tmux/pi workers |
79	| `/chat-new` | Start a new pi session, keeping the chat connection |
80	
81	Workers also write status snapshots every 15 seconds under `~/.pi/agent/chat/worker-status/`. The `chat_workers` tool exposes the same status to an orchestrating pi agent.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## Remote Control
86	
87	Users in the connected chat can send these commands (with or without mentioning the bot):
88	
89	| Command | Effect |
90	|---------|--------|
91	| `stop` | Abort the current turn |
92	| `status` | Show model, usage, context stats |
93	| `compact` | Trigger context compaction |
94	| `new` | Start a new pi session |
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Storage Layout
99	
100	Everything lives under `~/.pi/agent/chat/`:
101	
102	```
103	~/.pi/agent/chat/
104	├── config.json                          # Accounts, channels, secrets
105	├── cache/                               # Discovery cache
106	└── accounts/<account>/
107	    ├── shared/                          # Mounted as /shared in VM
108	    │   ├── memory.md                    # Account-wide persistent memory
109	    │   └── skills/                      # Account-wide skills
110	    └── channels/<channel>/
111	        ├── channel.jsonl                # Chat log
112	        ├── .lock                        # Runtime lock
113	        ├── workspace/                   # Mounted as /workspace in VM
114	        │   ├── memory.md                # Channel-specific persistent memory
115	        │   ├── skills/                  # Channel-specific skills
116	        │   ├── incoming/                # Downloaded attachments
117	        │   ├── .secrets/                # Encrypted secrets
118	        │   └── SYSTEM.md                # Environment modification log
119	        └── gondolin/                    # VM state
120	            └── session.json
121	```
122	
123	---
124	
125	## VM Environment
126	
127	Each connection starts a Gondolin micro-VM with:
128	
129	- **Alpine Linux** with bash pre-installed
130	- `/workspace` → channel workspace directory
131	- `/shared` → account shared directory
132	- Tools: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`
133	- All outbound HTTP/TLS open by default
134	
135	The agent sees `/workspace` as its working directory.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Memory
140	
141	Two persistent memory files, injected into the system prompt on every turn:
142	
143	| File | VM Path | Scope |
144	|------|---------|-------|
145	| Account memory | `/shared/memory.md` | Shared across all channels for this account |
146	| Channel memory | `/workspace/memory.md` | Specific to this channel |
147	
148	The agent is instructed to write durable facts and preferences to these files when asked to remember something. Account-wide goes to `/shared/memory.md`, channel-specific to `/workspace/memory.md`.
149	
150	---
151	
152	## Skills
153	
154	The agent can create reusable tools as skills, following the [Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.io):
155	
156	- **Account-wide:** `/shared/skills/`
157	- **Channel-specific:** `/workspace/skills/`
158	
159	A skill is either a single `.md` file (e.g. `skills/foo.md`) or a directory with `SKILL.md` plus supporting files (e.g. `skills/foo/SKILL.md`, `skills/foo/run.sh`).
160	
161	Each skill needs YAML frontmatter:
162	
163	```yaml
164	---
165	name: skill-name
166	description: Short description of what this skill does
167	---
168	```
169	
170	Skills are automatically discovered and listed in the system prompt. The agent reads the full skill file before using it.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Secrets
175	
176	### Config Secrets (Gondolin HTTP hooks)
177	
178	Configure secrets at three levels via `/chat-config`:
179	
180	- **Global** — shared across all accounts
181	- **Per account** — shared across channels of that account
182	- **Per channel** — specific to one channel
183	
184	Each secret has a value and allowed host patterns. Gondolin replaces placeholder env vars with real values only for outbound HTTP requests to allowed hosts. The agent never sees the real secret value.
185	
186	### Runtime Secrets (encrypted exchange)
187	
188	For credentials the agent needs at runtime (API keys for skills, OAuth files, etc.):
189	
190	1. Agent calls the `chat_request_secret` tool
191	2. A link to `pi.dev/secret` is sent to the chat with an embedded public key
192	3. User clicks, pastes the secret, and gets an encrypted blob
193	4. User pastes the blob back into chat
194	5. pi-chat decrypts it (RSA-OAEP + AES-256-GCM) and stores it at `/workspace/.secrets/<name>`
195	6. Agent is notified and can use the file
196	
197	The encrypted blob is useless without the ephemeral private key held in pi-chat's memory.
198	
199	---
200	
201	## Tools
202	
203	| Tool | Description |
204	|------|-------------|
205	| `read` | Read files (routed through Gondolin VM) |
206	| `write` | Create/overwrite files |
207	| `edit` | Precise in-place edits |
208	| `bash` | Execute commands (runs `/bin/bash` in the VM) |
209	| `chat_history` | Search older messages from the chat log |
210	| `chat_attach` | Queue files to send with the next reply |
211	| `chat_request_secret` | Request a secret from the user via encrypted exchange |
212	
213	---
214	
215	## Credits
216	
217	pi-chat includes vendored/adapted logic inspired by [Vercel Chat SDK](https://github.com/vercel/ai) (MIT):
218	
219	- `src/render/format.ts`
220	- `src/render/streaming-markdown.ts`
221	- `src/render/streaming.ts`
222	
223	---
224	
225	## License
226	
227	MIT
228
```

22		readConversationLog,

25	
26	function isDMConversation(conversation: ResolvedConversation): boolean {
27		return conversation.channel.dm ?? false;

30	function toGuestDisplayPath(conversation: ResolvedConversation, localPath: string): string {
31		if (localPath === conversation.workspaceDir || localPath.startsWith(`${conversation.workspaceDir}/`)) {
32			const suffix = localPath.slice(conversation.workspaceDir.length).replace(/^\//, "");
33			return suffix ? `/workspace/${suffix}` : "/workspace";
34		}
35		if (localPath === conversation.sharedDir || localPath.startsWith(`${conversation.sharedDir}/`)) {
36			const suffix = localPath.slice(conversation.sharedDir.length).replace(/^\//, "");
37			return suffix ? `/shared/${suffix}` : "/shared";
38		}
39		return localPath;
40	}
41	
42	function formatTranscriptRecord(conversation: ResolvedConversation, record: ChatLogRecord): string[] {
43		if (record.type !== "inbound") return [];
44		const lines = [
45			`- [${record.timestamp}] [uid:${record.userId}] ${record.userName ?? "unknown"}: ${record.text || "(no text)"}`,
46		];
47		if (record.attachments.length > 0) {
48			lines.push("  attachments:");
49			for (const attachment of record.attachments)
50				lines.push(
51					`  - ${toGuestDisplayPath(conversation, attachment.localPath)}${attachment.mimeType ? ` (${attachment.mimeType})` : ""}`,
52				);
53		}
54		return lines;
55	}
56	
57	function getLatestTriggerRecord(records: ChatLogRecord[], job: PendingJob): InboundMessageRecord | undefined {
58		const triggerRecord = records.find((record) => record.recordId === job.triggerRecordId);
59		if (!triggerRecord || triggerRecord.type !== "inbound") return undefined;
60		return triggerRecord;
61	}
62	
63	function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
64		return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
65	}
66	
67	export class ConversationRuntime {
68		readonly conversation: ResolvedConversation;
69		private readonly ownerId: string;
70		private records: ChatLogRecord[] = [];
71		private nextRecordId = 1;
72		private pendingJobs: PendingJob[] = [];
73		private activeJob: PendingJob | undefined;
74		private armedAfterRecordId: number | undefined;
75	
76		constructor(conversation: ResolvedConversation, ownerId: string) {
77			this.conversation = conversation;
78			this.ownerId = ownerId;
79		}
80	
81		static async connect(conversation: ResolvedConversation, ownerId: string): Promise<ConversationRuntime> {
82			const runtime = new ConversationRuntime(conversation, ownerId);
83			await runtime.initialize();
84			return runtime;
85		}
86	
87		private async initialize(): Promise<void> {
88			await ensureConversationDirs(this.conversation);
89			await acquireConversationLock(this.conversation, this.ownerId);
90			this.records = await readConversationLog(this.conversation);
91			this.nextRecordId = this.records.reduce((max, record) => Math.max(max, record.recordId), 0) + 1;
92		}
93	
94		armAfterCurrentTail(): void {
95			this.armedAfterRecordId = this.records.at(-1)?.recordId ?? 0;
96		}
97	
98		isArmed(): boolean {
99			return this.armedAfterRecordId !== undefined;
100		}
101	
102		async disconnect(): Promise<void> {
103			await releaseConversationLock(this.conversation);
104		}
105	
106		private async appendRecord(record: ChatLogRecord): Promise<void> {
107			this.records.push(record);
108			this.nextRecordId = Math.max(this.nextRecordId, record.recordId + 1);
109			await appendConversationRecord(this.conversation, record);
110		}
111	
112		private getLastQueuedTriggerRecordId(): number {
113			let last = 0;
114			for (const record of this.records) {
115				if (record.type === "job_queued") last = Math.max(last, record.triggerRecordId);
116			}
117			return last;
118		}
119	
120		private getLastCompletedTriggerRecordId(): number {
121			let last = 0;
122			for (const record of this.records) {
123				if (record.type !== "job_completed") continue;
124				last = Math.max(last, record.triggerRecordId);
125			}
126			return last;
127		}
128	
129		private isAllowedInput(message: Pick<InboundMessageInput, "userId" | "roleIds" | "isBot">): boolean {
130			const access = this.conversation.access;
131			if ((message.isBot ?? false) && (access.ignoreBots ?? true)) return false;
132			if (access.allowedUserIds?.length && !access.allowedUserIds.includes(message.userId)) return false;
133			if (access.allowedRoleIds?.length) {
134				const roleIds = message.roleIds ?? [];
135				if (!roleIds.some((roleId) => access.allowedRoleIds?.includes(roleId))) return false;
136			}
137			return true;
138		}
139	
140		private isAllowedMessage(message: InboundMessageRecord): boolean {
141			return this.isAllowedInput(message);
142		}
143	
144		parseControlCommand(input: InboundMessageInput): "stop" | "new" | "compact" | "status" | undefined {
145			const normalized = normalizeInboundMessage(input, this.conversation.botName);
146			if (!this.isAllowedInput(normalized)) return undefined;
147			const account = this.conversation.account;
148			let text = normalized.text;
149			const botUserId = "botUserId" in account ? account.botUserId : undefined;
150			if (botUserId) text = text.replace(new RegExp(`<@!?${escapeRegExp(botUserId)}>`, "g"), " ");
151			const aliases = [this.conversation.botName, "botUsername" in account ? account.botUsername : undefined].filter(
152				Boolean,
153			);
154			for (const alias of aliases) text = text.replace(new RegExp(`@${escapeRegExp(alias || "")}\\b`, "ig"), " ");
155			const command = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().toLowerCase();
156			if (command === "stop" || command === "/stop") return "stop";
157			if (command === "new" || command === "/new") return "new";
158			if (command === "compact" || command === "/compact") return "compact";
159			if (command === "status" || command === "/status") return "status";
160			return undefined;
161		}
162	
163		matchesStopCommand(input: InboundMessageInput): boolean {
164			return this.parseControlCommand(input) === "stop";
165		}
166	
167		private shouldTriggerJob(message: InboundMessageRecord): false | "mention" | "dm" {
168			if (!this.isAllowedMessage(message)) return false;
169			if (isDMConversation(this.conversation)) return "dm";
170			if ((this.conversation.access.trigger ?? "mention") === "message") return "mention";
171			return message.mentionedBot ? "mention" : false;
172		}
173	
174		private shouldQueueTrigger(recordId: number): boolean {
175			if (this.armedAfterRecordId === undefined) return false;
176			return recordId > Math.max(this.armedAfterRecordId, this.getLastQueuedTriggerRecordId());
177		}
178	
179		getLastCheckpoint(): { cursor?: string; messageId?: string } {
180			for (let index = this.records.length - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
181				const record = this.records[index];
182				if (record?.type === "checkpoint") return { cursor: record.cursor, messageId: record.messageId };
183			}
184			return {};
185		}
186	
187		async noteCheckpoint(checkpoint: { cursor?: string; messageId?: string }): Promise<void> {
188			const previous = this.getLastCheckpoint();
189			if (previous.cursor === checkpoint.cursor && previous.messageId === checkpoint.messageId) return;
190			const record: CheckpointRecord = {
191				type: "checkpoint",
192				...buildBaseRecordFields(this.conversation, this.nextRecordId),
193				cursor: checkpoint.cursor,
194				messageId: checkpoint.messageId,
195			};
196			await this.appendRecord(record);
197		}
198	
199		async ingestInbound(
200			input: InboundMessageInput,
201			checkpoint?: { cursor?: string; messageId?: string },
202		): Promise<{ record: InboundMessageRecord; jobQueued: boolean }> {
203			const normalized = normalizeInboundMessage(input, this.conversation.botName);
204			const messageId = normalized.messageId || nextMessageId(this.conversation.service);
205			const attachments = await materializeAttachments(this.conversation, messageId, normalized.attachments);
206			const record: InboundMessageRecord = {
207				type: "inbound",
208				...buildBaseRecordFields(this.conversation, this.nextRecordId),
209				messageId,
210				userId: normalized.userId,
211				userName: normalized.userName,
212				roleIds: normalized.roleIds,
213				text: normalized.text,
214				mentionedBot: normalized.mentionedBot ?? false,
215				isBot: normalized.isBot ?? false,
216				attachments,
217			};
218			await this.appendRecord(record);
219			if (checkpoint) await this.noteCheckpoint(checkpoint);
220			const trigger = this.shouldTriggerJob(record);
221			if (!trigger || !this.shouldQueueTrigger(record.recordId)) return { record, jobQueued: false };
222			const queuedRecord: JobQueuedRecord = {
223				type: "job_queued",
224				...buildBaseRecordFields(this.conversation, this.nextRecordId),
225				jobId: randomUUID(),
226				trigger,
227				triggerRecordId: record.recordId,
228			};
229			await this.appendRecord(queuedRecord);
230			this.pendingJobs.push({
231				jobId: queuedRecord.jobId,
232				trigger: queuedRecord.trigger,
233				triggerRecordId: queuedRecord.triggerRecordId,
234				queuedRecordId: queuedRecord.recordId,
235			});
236			return { record, jobQueued: true };
237		}
238	
239		beginNextJob(): DispatchableJob | undefined {
240			if (this.activeJob || this.pendingJobs.length === 0) return undefined;
241			const job = this.pendingJobs.shift();
242			if (!job) return undefined;
243			this.activeJob = job;
244			const triggerRecord = getLatestTriggerRecord(this.records, job);
245			return { job, prompt: this.buildPrompt(job), triggerMessageId: triggerRecord?.messageId };
246		}
247	
248		private buildPrompt(job: PendingJob): string {
249			const completedBoundary = this.getLastCompletedTriggerRecordId();
250			const slice = this.records.filter(
251				(record) =>
252					record.recordId > completedBoundary && record.recordId <= job.triggerRecordId && record.type === "inbound",
253			);
254			const lines: string[] = [];
255			for (const record of slice) lines.push(...formatTranscriptRecord(this.conversation, record));
256			return lines.join("\n").trim();
257		}
258	
259		async completeActiveJob(text: string, remoteMessageId?: string, attachmentPaths?: string[]): Promise<void> {
260			const job = this.activeJob;
261			if (!job) return;
262			let outboundRecordId: number | undefined;
263			const trimmed = text.trim();
264			if (trimmed.length > 0 || (attachmentPaths?.length ?? 0) > 0) {
265				const triggerRecord = getLatestTriggerRecord(this.records, job);
266				const outbound = {
267					type: "outbound",
268					...buildBaseRecordFields(this.conversation, this.nextRecordId),
269					messageId: remoteMessageId || nextMessageId(this.conversation.service),
270					text: trimmed,

273					attachments: attachmentPaths?.length ? [...attachmentPaths] : undefined,

275				outboundRecordId = outbound.recordId;
276				await this.appendRecord(outbound);
277			}
278			await this.appendRecord({

280				...buildBaseRecordFields(this.conversation, this.nextRecordId),
281				jobId: job.jobId,
282				triggerRecordId: job.triggerRecordId,

305		findHistory(options: { query?: string; after?: string; before?: string; limit?: number }): Array<ChatLogRecord> {
306			const query = options.query?.toLowerCase();
307			const after = options.after ? Date.parse(options.after) : undefined;
308			const before = options.before ? Date.parse(options.before) : undefined;
309			const limit = Math.max(1, Math.min(options.limit ?? 20, 200));
310			const filtered = this.records.filter((record) => {
311				if (record.type !== "inbound" && record.type !== "outbound") return false;
312				const ts = Date.parse(record.timestamp);
313				if (after !== undefined && !(ts >= after)) return false;
314				if (before !== undefined && !(ts <= before)) return false;
315				if (!query) return true;
316				const speaker = record.type === "inbound" ? (record.userName ?? record.userId) : "assistant";
317				return `${speaker}\n${record.text}`.toLowerCase().includes(query);
318			});
319			return filtered.slice(Math.max(0, filtered.length - limit));
320		}
321	
322		getStatus(): ConversationStatus {
323			return {
324				conversationId: this.conversation.conversationId,
325				conversationName: this.conversation.conversationName,
326				logPath: this.conversation.logPath,
327				queueLength: this.pendingJobs.length,
328				hasActiveJob: this.activeJob !== undefined,
329				recordCount: this.records.length,
330				lastRecordId: this.records.at(-1)?.recordId ?? 0,
331			};
332		}

146				});
147				const data = (await response.json()) as { id?: string; message?: string };
148				if (!response.ok || !data.id) throw new Error(data.message || "Discord send failed");
149				firstMessageId ??= data.id;
150			} else {
151				const id = await postDiscordMessage(botToken, channelId, payload, signal);
152				firstMessageId ??= id;
153			}
154		}
155		return firstMessageId || "";
156	}
157	
158	async function catchUp(
159		client: Client<true>,
160		conversation: ResolvedConversation,
161		account: DiscordAccountConfig,
162		handlers: LiveConnectionHandlers,
163		afterId?: string,
164	): Promise<void> {
165		const channel = await resolveTextChannel(client, conversation);
166		const allMessages: Message[] = [];
167		let cursor = afterId;
168		while (true) {
169			const batch = await channel.messages.fetch(cursor ? { after: cursor, limit: 100 } : { limit: 25 });
170			if (batch.size === 0) break;
171			const sorted = [...batch.values()].sort((a, b) => a.createdTimestamp - b.createdTimestamp);
172			allMessages.push(...sorted);
173			cursor = sorted[sorted.length - 1].id;
174			if (batch.size < 100) break;
175		}
176		for (const message of allMessages) {
177			const input = await messageToInput(conversation, account, message);
178			if (!input) continue;
179			await handlers.onMessage(input, { messageId: input.messageId, cursor: input.messageId });
180		}
181	}
182	
183	export async function connectDiscordLive(
184		conversation: ResolvedConversation,
185		handlers: LiveConnectionHandlers,
186		lastMessageId?: string,
187	): Promise<LiveConnection> {
188		const account = conversation.account as DiscordAccountConfig;
189		const client = await withReadyClient(account.botToken);
190		await catchUp(client, conversation, account, handlers, lastMessageId);
191		await handlers.onCaughtUp();
192		const preview = new StreamingPreview(conversation.service, {
193			create: async (text, _parseMode, replyToMessageId) => {
194				return sendDiscordMessage(account.botToken, conversation.channel.id, text, [], undefined, replyToMessageId);
195			},
196			edit: async (id, text) => {
197				const channel = await resolveTextChannel(client, conversation);
198				const message = await channel.messages.fetch(id);
199				await message.edit({ content: text });
200			},
201			delete: async (id) => {
202				const channel = await resolveTextChannel(client, conversation);
203				const message = await channel.messages.fetch(id);
204				await message.delete();
205			},
206		});
207		const onMessageCreate = async (message: Message) => {
208			try {
209				const input = await messageToInput(conversation, account, message);
210				if (!input) return;
211				await handlers.onMessage(input, { messageId: input.messageId, cursor: input.messageId });
212			} catch (error) {
213				await handlers.onError(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)));
214			}
215		};
216		client.on(Events.MessageCreate, onMessageCreate);
217	
218		let disconnectFired = false;
219		const fireDisconnect = () => {
220			if (disconnectFired) return;
221			disconnectFired = true;
222			void handlers.onDisconnect?.();
223		};
224		client.on(Events.Error, (error) => {
225			void handlers.onError(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)));
226		});
227		client.on(Events.Invalidated, () => fireDisconnect());
228		client.on("disconnect", () => fireDisconnect());
229		client.ws.on("close" as any, () => {
230			setTimeout(() => {
231				if (!client.isReady()) fireDisconnect();
232			}, 30000);
233		});
234	
235		return {
236			conversation,
237			disconnect: async () => {
238				client.off(Events.MessageCreate, onMessageCreate);
239				client.destroy();
240			},
241			sendImmediate: async (text, replyToMessageId) => {
242				return sendDiscordMessage(account.botToken, conversation.channel.id, text, [], undefined, replyToMessageId);
243			},
244			send: async (text, attachmentPaths = [], signal, replyToMessageId) =>
245				sendDiscordMessage(account.botToken, conversation.channel.id, text, attachmentPaths, signal, replyToMessageId),
246			startTyping: async () => {
247				const channel = await resolveTextChannel(client, conversation);
248				await channel.sendTyping();
249			},
250			stopTyping: async () => {},
251			syncPreview: async (markdown, done = false) => preview.update(markdown, done),
252			clearPreview: async () => preview.clear(),
253			setReplyTo: (messageId) => preview.setReplyTo(messageId),
254		};
255	}

```text
1	# TelePi
2	
3	**Run your Pi coding agent from Telegram: voice prompts, screenshots, session handoff, and terminal handback.**
4	
5	TelePi is a Telegram bridge for the [Pi coding agent](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono). It runs locally on your machine, opens real Pi sessions in your repositories, lets you continue from your phone, and hands the exact same session back to the terminal when you return.
6	
7	**Who this is for:** developers already using Pi who want a safe mobile control surface for coding-agent work: reply from the train, send a screenshot, dictate a prompt, watch progress, then resume in the CLI without losing context.
8	
9	Early open-source release: **80+ stars, 13 forks, and hundreds of npm downloads**. Current npm release: `@futurelab-studio/telepi` **v0.4.2**, with macOS `launchd`, Linux `systemd --user`, image prompts, prompt inbox, local/cloud voice transcription, and Pi command bridging. Read the [Futurelab TelePi deep dive](https://futurelab.studio/blog/telepi-telegram-remote-control-for-pi/) for the longer story.
10	
11	> **Demo placeholder:** GIF coming soon. The core loop is: Pi CLI `/handoff` → Telegram text/voice/image prompt → `/handback` → resume the same Pi session in your terminal.
12	
13	## Try it in 5 minutes
14	
15	You need:
16	
17	- **Node.js 22.19+**
18	- A Telegram bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)
19	- Your numeric Telegram user ID for the allowlist
20	- Pi installed and authenticated locally (`~/.pi/agent/auth.json` exists after a working Pi login)
21	
22	Install the npm package and run the guided setup:
23	
24	```bash
25	npm install -g @futurelab-studio/telepi
26	telepi setup
27	telepi status
28	```
29	
30	`telepi setup` asks for your bot token, allowed Telegram user IDs, and default workspace. It installs the local service for your platform and the Pi `/handoff` extension.
31	
32	**Success checkpoint:** open Telegram and send `/start` to your bot. You should see your workspace/session status and voice backend status. If not, jump to [Troubleshooting activation blockers](#troubleshooting-activation-blockers).
33	
34	## Your first TelePi session
35	
36	1. Start or open a Pi session in a repository.
37	2. Run `/handoff` from Pi.
38	3. Open Telegram and find your bot.
39	4. Send a text prompt, voice message, or screenshot/photo.
40	5. Use `/handback` to resume the same session in your terminal.
41	
42	## Security model
43	
44	TelePi gives Telegram access to a coding agent, so it is designed to stay private by default:
45	
46	- **Telegram user allowlist:** only IDs in `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` can interact with the bot.
47	- **Workspace-scoped execution:** Pi tools are created for the active workspace and re-scoped when you switch sessions.
48	- **Local user service:** installed mode runs under your own macOS/Linux user account, not as a public server.
49	- **No public bot access when configured correctly:** anyone else who discovers the bot is rejected unless their Telegram user ID is allowlisted.
50	- **Docker support:** run TelePi in a non-root container with explicit read/write mounts if you want stronger filesystem isolation.
51	
52	## Features
53	
54	- **Bi-directional hand-off**: Move sessions CLI → Telegram (`/handoff`) and back (`/handback`)
55	- **Per-chat/topic sessions**: Every Telegram chat or forum topic gets its own Pi session, picker state, and retry history
56	- **Voice and image messages**: Send voice/audio for transcription, or photos/image documents as Pi image inputs
57	- **Local or cloud transcription**: [Parakeet CoreML](https://github.com/sebastian-software/parakeet-coreml) on Apple Silicon, [Sherpa-ONNX Parakeet](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/) for Intel Macs (and as a CPU fallback), or OpenAI Whisper in the cloud
58	- **Session tree navigation**: Browse, branch, and label your Pi session history with `/tree`, `/branch`, `/label`
59	- **Cross-workspace sessions**: Browse and switch between sessions from any project
60	- **Model switching**: Change AI models on the fly via `/model`
61	- **Workspace-aware `/new`**: Create sessions in any known project workspace
62	- **Pi slash-command bridge**: Run discovered Pi prompt templates, skills, and extension commands from Telegram, browse them with the paginated `/commands` picker, and surface Telegram-compatible ones in the native slash-command menu
63	- **External prompt inbox**: Let cron jobs, mail filters, webhooks, or log watchers drop `.txt` prompts into a watched directory
64	- **Helpful recovery commands**: `/help` for quick usage guidance and `/retry` to resend the last prompt in the current chat/topic
65	- **Extension dialog support**: Pi extension commands can ask for Telegram-native selects, confirms, and text input mid-command
66	- **Native Telegram UX**: Topic-safe inline keyboards, typing indicators, HTML-formatted responses, friendly user-facing errors, auto-retry on rate limits
67	- **Security**: Telegram user allowlist, workspace-scoped tools, Docker support
68	
69	## Full setup details
70	
71	The npm global install is the main path for TelePi on macOS (`launchd`) and Linux (`systemd --user`).
72	
73	1. Install TelePi globally:
74	   ```bash
75	   npm install -g @futurelab-studio/telepi
76	   ```
77	2. Run the installer using either flow:
78	   ```bash
79	   telepi setup
80	   ```
81	   When run in a terminal, `telepi setup` prompts for the three setup values TelePi currently cares about:
82	   - `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
83	   - `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS`
84	   - `TELEPI_WORKSPACE`
85	
86	   On a fresh config copied from `.env.example`, the example values are treated as placeholders, not saved defaults — pressing Enter still requires you to enter your real bot token, allowed user ID list, and workspace.
87	
88	   Or use the fast positional form:
89	   ```bash
90	   telepi setup <bot_token> <userids> <workspace>
91	   ```
92	   where `<userids>` uses the same comma-separated format as the config file, for example `123456789,987654321`.
93	
94	   `telepi setup` will:
95	   - create or update `~/.config/telepi/config.env`
96	   - preserve any existing optional config values already present in that file
97	   - on macOS, install/update `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.telepi.plist`
98	   - on Linux, install/update `~/.config/systemd/user/telepi.service` and run `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now telepi.service`
99	   - install the Pi `/handoff` extension at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/telepi-handoff.ts`
100	
101	   If you run setup non-interactively, you must either pass all three positional values or already have them configured; TelePi fails clearly instead of writing placeholder values.
102	3. Verify the installed config at `~/.config/telepi/config.env` with your real values:
103	   ```dotenv
104	   TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456789:AAFf_real_token_from_botfather
105	   TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS=111111111,222222222
106	   TELEPI_WORKSPACE=/Users/you/your-main-project
107	   ```
108	   Notes:
109	   - `TELEPI_WORKSPACE` is strongly recommended in installed mode so fresh Telegram sessions start in the right project
110	   - `PI_SESSION_PATH` is usually injected automatically by `/handoff`
111	   - `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR`, `PI_MODEL`, and `TOOL_VERBOSITY` are optional
112	4. Verify the install:
113	   ```bash
114	   telepi status
115	   ```
116	5. Open Telegram and send `/start` to your bot.
117	
118	Rerunning `telepi setup` after upgrades is safe; it refreshes the service unit and extension while preserving your config. After setup, `/handoff` automatically reuses the installed `launchd` service on macOS or `systemd --user` service on Linux by default.
119	
120	## Troubleshooting activation blockers
121	
122	### How do I get a Telegram bot token?
123	
124	Open [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather), send `/newbot`, choose a name and username, then copy the token into `telepi setup` as `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`.
125	
126	### How do I find my Telegram user ID?
127	
128	Message a helper bot such as [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot) and copy the numeric ID into `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS`. Use comma-separated IDs for multiple people, for example `123456789,987654321`.
129	
130	### Bot does not respond
131	
132	Run `telepi status` first. Then check that the token is correct, your numeric user ID is allowlisted, you messaged the right bot, and you do not have a second TelePi process polling the same token. On macOS, logs are in `~/Library/Logs/TelePi/`; on Linux, use `journalctl --user -u telepi.service -f`.
133	
134	### Pi auth missing
135	
136	Start Pi locally once and complete authentication before using TelePi. TelePi expects Pi credentials under `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` and sessions under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.
137	
138	### Service not running
139	
140	Run `telepi status`. On macOS, restart the LaunchAgent with `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.telepi`. On Linux, run `systemctl --user status telepi.service` and `systemctl --user restart telepi.service`; on headless systems you may also need `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"`.
141	
142	### Voice transcription not working
143	
144	Send `/start` and check the voice backend status. Local transcription needs `ffmpeg` plus either `parakeet-coreml` on Apple Silicon or `sherpa-onnx-node` with `SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR` for Intel/CPU fallback. Cloud transcription needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `~/.config/telepi/config.env`. See [Voice and Image Messages](#voice-and-image-messages) for setup details.
145	
146	## Development from Source
147	
148	Use a source checkout when you want to hack on TelePi or run the latest unreleased code.
149	
150	1. Install dependencies:
151	   ```bash
152	   npm install
153	   ```
154	2. Copy the example environment file and fill it in:
155	   ```bash
156	   cp .env.example .env
157	   ```
158	   Replace the example values from `.env.example` with your real settings. At minimum set:
159	   - `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
160	   - `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS`
161	   - `TELEPI_WORKSPACE` if you want fresh Telegram sessions rooted somewhere other than the repo directory
162	3. Start the bot in development mode:
163	   ```bash
164	   npm run dev
165	   ```
166	4. To test the installed-mode flow from a checkout, build first and use the built CLI entrypoint:
167	   ```bash
168	   npm run build
169	   node dist/cli.js setup
170	   # or: node dist/cli.js setup <bot_token> <userids> <workspace>
171	   node dist/cli.js status
172	   ```
173	
174	If you are working from a built checkout or GitHub Release artifact instead of a global npm install, install runtime dependencies first — the `dist/` files are not self-contained:
175	
176	```bash
177	npm install --omit=dev
178	# or: npm ci --omit=dev
179	node dist/cli.js setup
180	node dist/cli.js start
181	```
182	
183	
184	## Telegram Commands
185	
186	| Command | Description |
187	|---------|-------------|
188	| `/start` | Welcome message, session info, and voice backend status |
189	| `/help` | Quick command reference and usage tips |
190	| `/commands` | Open a paginated picker for TelePi commands plus discovered Pi prompt templates, skills, and extension commands |
191	| `/new` | Create a fresh session (shows workspace picker if multiple known) |
192	| `/retry` | Re-send the last prompt in the current chat/topic |
193	| `/handback` | Hand session back to Pi CLI (copies resume command to clipboard) |
194	| `/abort` | Cancel the current Pi operation |
195	| `/session` | Show current session details (ID, file, workspace, model) |
196	| `/sessions` | List all sessions across all workspaces with tap-to-switch buttons |
197	| `/sessions <path\|id>` | Switch directly to a specific session file or session ID/prefix |
198	| `/model` | Pick a different AI model from an inline keyboard |
199	| `/tree` | View the session entry tree; navigate with inline buttons |
200	| `/branch <id>` | Navigate to a specific entry ID (with confirmation) |
201	| `/label [args]` | Add or clear labels on entries for easy reference |
202	
203	Sessions, inline keyboards, and `/retry` state are isolated per Telegram chat/topic, so forum topics can be used independently without colliding with each other.
204	
205	`/commands` now opens a mobile-friendly inline picker with pagination plus `All`, `TelePi`, and `Pi` filters. Tapping a TelePi entry runs the built-in command immediately, and tapping a Pi entry forwards the slash command into the active Pi session. Telegram-compatible discovered Pi commands (for example `/review` or `/compact`) are also synced into Telegram's native slash-command interface for the current chat. Commands that Telegram cannot represent, such as `/skill:browser-tools`, stay available through the picker and by manual typing.
206	
207	Any non-TelePi slash command that matches the active Pi session's discovered commands is forwarded into Pi unchanged. That means Telegram can now trigger file-based prompt templates (for example `/review`), skills (`/skill:browser-tools`), and compatible extension commands. Interactive extension commands can also open Telegram-native select/confirm/input dialogs while the command is running.
208	
209	## External Prompt Inbox
210	
211	For cron jobs, mail filters, webhooks, or log watchers, keep the external trigger outside TelePi and write a `.txt` file into a prompt inbox instead:
212	
213	```env
214	TELEPI_PROMPT_INBOX_DIR=/absolute/path/to/prompt-inbox
215	TELEPI_PROMPT_INBOX_INTERVAL_MS=60000  # optional; default 60s, minimum 1s
216	```
217	
218	When enabled, TelePi polls the directory, processes one `.txt` file at a time, sends its trimmed contents to the root chat for the first `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` entry, and deletes the file after accepting it. If that chat is already busy, files stay queued for the next poll. Empty `.txt` files are deleted to avoid loops; subdirectories and non-`.txt` files are ignored.
219	
220	## Voice and Image Messages
221	
222	Send any Telegram **voice message** or **audio file** and TelePi will transcribe it and feed the transcript straight into Pi as a text prompt.
223	
224	```
225	[you send a voice message]
226	🎤 "How does the session hand-off work?" (via parakeet)
227	
228	[Pi responds normally]
229	```
230	
231	TelePi supports three transcription backends and picks the best available one automatically:
232	
233	| Backend | How to enable | Cost | Privacy |
234	|---------|---------------|------|---------|
235	| **Parakeet CoreML** (local) | `npm install parakeet-coreml` + `brew install ffmpeg` | Free | On-device |
236	| **Sherpa-ONNX Parakeet** (local, Intel Mac path) | `npm install sherpa-onnx-node` + download model + set `SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR` | Free | On-device |
237	| **Cloud transcription** | `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...` for OpenAI Whisper, or `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_URL`, `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL`, and `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_API_KEY` for a compatible provider | Provider-dependent | Cloud |
238	
239	TelePi tries backends in this order:
240	
241	1. **Parakeet CoreML** — best local path on Apple Silicon
242	2. **Sherpa-ONNX Parakeet** — the local/offline path for Intel Macs, where `parakeet-coreml` does not run (and a CPU fallback on Apple Silicon)
243	3. **OpenAI Whisper or a configured compatible provider** — cloud fallback
244	
245	The `/start` command shows which backends are currently active.
246	
247	Send a Telegram **photo** or **image document** to pass it to Pi as image input. Captions become the prompt; without a caption TelePi asks Pi to analyze the image.
248	
249	### Installing Parakeet CoreML (local transcription on Apple Silicon)
250	
251	Parakeet CoreML is an optional dependency (~1.5 GB download, macOS only with Apple Silicon):
252	
253	```bash
254	npm install parakeet-coreml
255	brew install ffmpeg   # required for audio decoding
256	```
257	
258	On first use the CoreML model is downloaded automatically. Subsequent calls use the cached model.
259	
260	### Installing Sherpa-ONNX Parakeet (local transcription for Intel Macs)
261	
262	This is the recommended local transcription path on Intel Macs, since `parakeet-coreml` is Apple-Silicon-only. It can also be used on Apple Silicon, but TelePi will still prefer Parakeet CoreML there when available.
263	
264	Install the optional Node binding:
265	
266	```bash
267	npm install sherpa-onnx-node
268	brew install ffmpeg   # required for audio decoding
269	```
270	
271	Download and extract the Parakeet model layout TelePi expects (`encoder.int8.onnx`, `decoder.int8.onnx`, `joiner.int8.onnx`, `tokens.txt`). The v3 multilingual model below is the intended Intel Mac setup:
272	
273	```bash
274	curl -LO https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/asr-models/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8.tar.bz2
275	tar xvf sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8.tar.bz2
276	```
277	
278	Point TelePi at the extracted directory:
279	
280	```bash
281	export SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR="$(pwd)/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8"
282	```
283	
284	If `SHERPA_ONNX_MODEL_DIR` is set, TelePi treats missing model files or a missing `sherpa-onnx-node` package as configuration errors and will not silently fall through to OpenAI.
285	
286	If the native module cannot find its shared libraries on macOS, start TelePi with:
287	
288	```bash
289	export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(pwd)/node_modules/sherpa-onnx-darwin-$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/x64/;s/arm64/arm64/'):${DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
290	```
291	
292	For the exact family of Sherpa Parakeet models TelePi currently supports, plus platform notes, see:
293	
294	- https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/pretrained_models/offline-transducer/nemo-transducer-models.html
295	
296	### Using OpenAI Whisper (cloud transcription)
297	
298	Add your key to your TelePi config file (`~/.config/telepi/config.env` in installed mode, or `.env` in a source checkout):
299	
300	```
301	OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
302	```
303	
304	No additional packages are required. Supports the same audio formats Telegram delivers (Ogg Opus, MP3, M4A, WAV, etc.).
305	
306	### Using an OpenAI-compatible transcription provider
307	
308	Set a custom full transcription endpoint when your provider accepts the OpenAI-compatible multipart `audio/transcriptions` request shape. Existing `OPENAI_API_KEY` setups remain unchanged when these values are unset.
309	
310	| Variable | Default | Purpose |
311	|----------|---------|---------|
312	| `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_API_KEY` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Credential sent to the provider |
313	| `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_URL` | OpenAI's `/v1/audio/transcriptions` endpoint | Full HTTP(S) endpoint |
314	| `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` | `whisper-1` | Value for the multipart `model` field |
315	| `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_AUTH_HEADER` | unset | Custom credential-header name; unset uses `Authorization: Bearer` |
316	| `TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_PROMPT` | unset | Optional recognition context for project-specific names and terms |
317	
318	For example:
319	
320	```bash
321	TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_API_KEY=...
322	TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_URL=https://provider.example/v1/audio/transcriptions
323	TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL=provider-whisper
324	TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_AUTH_HEADER=api-key
325	TELEPI_TRANSCRIPTION_PROMPT="Conversation about TelePi and Pi coding-agent sessions."
326	```
327	
328	TelePi removes URL credentials, queries, and fragments from endpoint details shown in errors.
329	
330	## Session Tree Navigation
331	
332	Every prompt and response in Pi is stored as a tree of entries. TelePi exposes this tree so you can review history and jump back to any point to create a new branch.
333	
334	### `/tree`
335	
336	Shows the session entry tree as a preformatted diagram with inline navigation buttons.
337	
338	```
339	/tree        — default view (last 10 entries, branch points highlighted)
340	/tree all    — full tree with navigation buttons on every entry
341	/tree user   — user messages only
342	```
343	
344	Inline buttons let you switch between filter modes without retyping the command.
345	
346	### `/branch <id>`
347	
348	Navigate to any entry by its short 4-character ID (shown in `/tree`). TelePi asks for confirmation and offers two options:
349	
350	- **Navigate here** — moves the session leaf to the selected entry; your next message creates a new branch from that point
351	- **Navigate + Summarize** — same, but first generates a concise summary of the branch you are leaving
352	
353	### `/label [args]`
354	
355	Attach human-readable labels to entries so you can find them easily in `/tree`.
356	
357	```
358	/label fix-auth          — label the current leaf "fix-auth"
359	/label <id> fix-auth     — label a specific entry
360	/label clear <id>        — remove a label
361	/label                   — list all labels in the session
362	```
363	
364	Labeled entries are highlighted in `/tree` output and shown in `/branch` confirmations.
365	
366	## Session Hand-off
367	
368	TelePi supports seamless bi-directional session hand-off between Pi CLI and Telegram. Both directions preserve the **full conversation context** — the JSONL session file is the single source of truth, and whichever side opens it gets the complete history, including any messages added by the other side.
369	
370	### CLI → Telegram (`/handoff`)
371	
372	You're working in Pi CLI on your laptop and want to continue from your phone:
373	
374	1. **In Pi CLI**, type `/handoff`
375	2. The extension hands off your current session to TelePi — in direct mode it starts TelePi immediately, and in `launchd` mode it restarts the installed LaunchAgent with the handed-off session. The default `auto` behavior picks `launchd` after `telepi setup`, otherwise direct mode — then shuts down Pi CLI
376	3. **Open Telegram** — TelePi is already running with your full conversation context. Just keep typing (or speak).
377	
378	**Extension installation**
379	
380	- If you used `telepi setup`, the extension is already installed at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/telepi-handoff.ts`
381	- If you are developing from a source checkout without `telepi setup`, symlink it manually:
382	
383	```bash
384	cd /path/to/TelePi
385	ln -s "$(pwd)/extensions/telepi-handoff.ts" ~/.pi/agent/extensions/telepi-handoff.ts
386	```
387	
388	Pi auto-discovers it after symlinking (or run `/reload` in Pi).
389	
390	The extension supports three hand-off mode settings, controlled via shell environment variables:
391	
392	- `TELEPI_HANDOFF_MODE=auto` *(default)* — if `telepi setup` assets are present, reuse `launchd` on macOS or `systemd --user` on Linux; otherwise use direct mode
393	- `TELEPI_HANDOFF_MODE=direct` — always start a fresh direct TelePi process; best for source-checkout development or when the installed service is unloaded
394	- `TELEPI_HANDOFF_MODE=launchd` — force macOS `launchd` hand-off by setting `PI_SESSION_PATH` in the `launchd` user environment and restarting the configured LaunchAgent
395	- `TELEPI_HANDOFF_MODE=systemd` — force Linux `systemd --user` hand-off by setting `PI_SESSION_PATH` in the user service manager and restarting `telepi.service`
396	- `TELEPI_LAUNCHD_LABEL` *(optional, default: `com.telepi`)* — LaunchAgent label/plist name to restart in `launchd` mode or auto-detect
397	
398	#### Direct mode
399	
400	Direct mode starts a separate TelePi process. That is the natural default for source-checkout development, where you typically export:
401	
402	```bash
403	export TELEPI_DIR="/path/to/TelePi"
404	```
405	
406	If a global `telepi` command is available and `~/.config/telepi/config.env` exists, direct mode can also launch the installed CLI explicitly. If the installed config is missing, `/handoff` now falls back to `TELEPI_DIR` when that source checkout path is available.
407	
408	#### launchd mode (default after `telepi setup` on macOS)
409	
410	If you installed TelePi with `telepi setup`, no extra shell exports are required: `/handoff` auto-detects the installed config + LaunchAgent plist and reuses the resident `launchd`-managed bot instead of starting a second direct polling process.
411	
412	If you are testing the installed flow from a source checkout, run the installer from the built checkout first:
413	
414	```bash
415	npm run build
416	node dist/cli.js setup
417	```
418	
419	You can still force launchd mode explicitly (or point at a non-default label) with:
420	
421	```bash
422	export TELEPI_HANDOFF_MODE=launchd
423	export TELEPI_LAUNCHD_LABEL=com.telepi
424	```
425	
426	In `launchd` mode, `/handoff` only does two things: set `PI_SESSION_PATH` in `launchd`, then restart the configured LaunchAgent. That keeps TelePi to a single bot process and avoids Telegram token conflicts.
427	
428	> **Note:** `launchctl setenv` does not persist across reboots. After a machine restart, `PI_SESSION_PATH` will be cleared and TelePi will start a fresh session until the next `/handoff`.
429	
430	> **Note:** `telepi setup` installs the plist with `KeepAlive`, so launchd will restart TelePi if it exits. To fully stop TelePi, unload the agent: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.telepi`.
431	
432	#### systemd mode (default after `telepi setup` on Linux)
433	
434	On Linux, `telepi setup` installs a user service at `~/.config/systemd/user/telepi.service`, reloads the user daemon, enables the service, and starts/restarts it. `/handoff` auto-detects that service and runs:
435	
436	```bash
437	systemctl --user set-environment PI_SESSION_PATH=/path/to/session.jsonl
438	systemctl --user restart telepi.service
439	```
440	
441	If `systemctl --user` is unavailable, make sure your distro has user systemd sessions enabled. On headless servers you may need lingering:
442	
443	```bash
444	loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
445	```
446	
447	Useful commands:
448	
449	```bash
450	systemctl --user status telepi.service
451	journalctl --user -u telepi.service -f
452	systemctl --user stop telepi.service
453	```
454	
455	### Telegram → CLI (`/handback`)
456	
457	You're on your phone and want to get back to your terminal:
458	
459	1. **In Telegram**, type `/handback`
460	2. TelePi disposes the session and sends you the exact command to resume, e.g.:
461	   ```
462	   cd '/Users/you/myproject' && pi --session '/Users/you/.pi/agent/sessions/.../session.jsonl'
463	   ```
464	3. On macOS and Linux desktops with `wl-copy`, `xclip`, or `xsel`, the command is **copied to your clipboard** automatically
465	4. **In your terminal**, paste and run — Pi CLI opens with the full conversation, including everything from Telegram
466	5. TelePi stays alive — send any message in Telegram to start a fresh session
467	
468	You can also resume with the shorthand:
469	
470	```bash
471	# Continue the most recent session in the project
472	cd /path/to/project && pi -c
473	```
474	
475	### Manual hand-off
476	
477	Without the extension, you can hand off manually:
478	
479	1. Note the session file path from Pi CLI (shown on startup)
480	2. Start TelePi with that session explicitly:
481	
482	```bash
483	TELEPI_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/telepi/config.env" PI_SESSION_PATH="/path/to/session.jsonl" telepi start
484	```
485	
486	From a source checkout, use the development entrypoint instead:
487	
488	```bash
489	cd /path/to/TelePi
490	PI_SESSION_PATH="/path/to/session.jsonl" npm run dev
491	```
492	
493	### How it works
494	
495	Both Pi CLI and TelePi use the same `SessionManager` from the Pi SDK to read/write session JSONL files stored under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`. When either side opens a session file:
496	
497	1. `SessionManager.open(path)` loads all entries from the JSONL file
498	2. `buildSessionContext()` walks the entry tree from the current leaf to the root
499	3. The full message history (including compaction summaries and branch context) is sent to the LLM
500	
501	This means hand-off is lossless — no context is dropped regardless of how many times you switch between CLI and Telegram.
502	
503	## Cross-Workspace Sessions
504	
505	TelePi discovers sessions from **all** project workspaces stored under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`. This means:
506	
507	- **`/sessions`** shows sessions from every project (OpenClawd, homepage, TelePi, etc.), grouped by workspace
508	- **`/new`** shows a workspace picker when multiple workspaces are known, so you can start a new session in any project
509	- **Switching sessions** automatically updates the workspace — coding tools are re-scoped to the correct project directory
510	
511	Sessions are stored under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<encoded-workspace-path>--/`.
512	
513	For a fuller module walkthrough after the bot/install refactors, see [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

613	## Docker
614	
615	For production use with Docker:
616	
617	```bash
618	docker compose up --build
619	```
620	
621	The compose file:
622	- Mounts `~/.pi/agent` read-only (for auth and settings)
623	- Mounts `~/.pi/agent/sessions` read-write (for session persistence)
624	- Mounts your workspace directory read-write
625	- Runs as non-root, drops capabilities, enables `no-new-privileges`
626	
627	## Security Notes
628	
629	- Only Telegram user IDs in `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` can interact with the bot
630	- Pi tools are scoped to the workspace via `createCodingTools(workspace)` and re-scoped on session switch
631	- The `/handoff` extension only shuts down Pi CLI if TelePi launches or restarts successfully
632	- URL sanitization blocks `javascript:` and other unsafe protocols in formatted output
633	- Shell commands in `/handback` use `spawnSync` (no shell interpretation) for clipboard copy
634	- Voice files are downloaded to a temporary directory and deleted immediately after transcription
635	
636	## Architecture
637	
638	```text
639	Telegram
640	  ↓
641	Grammy bot (`src/bot.ts`)
642	  ├── transport helpers         → `src/bot/telegram-transport.ts`
643	  ├── rendering helpers         → `src/bot/message-rendering.ts`
644	  ├── prompt lifecycle          → `src/bot/prompt-handler.ts`
645	  ├── chat-local busy/retry     → `src/bot/chat-state.ts`
646	  ├── extension dialogs         → `src/bot/extension-dialogs.ts`
647	  ├── grouped command handlers  → `src/bot/commands/*`
648	  └── voice route               → `src/voice.ts`
649	                                     └── ffmpeg decode + local/cloud transcription backends
650	        ↓
651	PiSessionRegistry / PiSessionService (`src/pi-session.ts`)
652	  ├── AgentSession / SessionManager → `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`
653	  ├── workspace + saved-session switching
654	  ├── model scope / registry integration
655	  ├── tree navigation + labels
656	  └── handback/session lifecycle
657	        ↓
658	Pi SDK + workspace-scoped coding tools
659	```
660	
661	The detailed module map, testing layout, and remaining large hotspots are documented in [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

668	npm run build          # TypeScript compilation

670	npm test               # Run tests

673	npm run ci:release     # Test + clean build + package release artifact

675	
676	## Release Automation
677	
678	GitHub Actions publishes npm and creates the GitHub Release automatically on tag pushes matching `v*.*.*`.
679	
680	Maintainer flow:
681	
682	```bash
683	npm version patch   # or minor / major
684	git push origin main --follow-tags
685	```
686	
687	The release workflow then:
688	- verifies the pushed tag matches `package.json`
689	- installs dependencies and runs release CI via `npx --yes npm@11.10.0`
690	- publishes `@futurelab-studio/telepi` to npm
691	- creates a GitHub Release with the packaged tarball and checksum
692	
693	Notes:
694	- prerelease tags like `v0.2.0-beta.1` are published to npm with the `next` dist-tag and marked as GitHub prereleases
695	- npm publishing uses Trusted Publishing from GitHub Actions; no `NPM_TOKEN` secret is required
696	- the trusted publisher must be configured on npm for repo `benedict2310/TelePi` and workflow `.github/workflows/release.yml`
697	- npm Trusted Publishing currently requires npm CLI `11.5.1+` and Node `22.14.0+`; TelePi keeps the runner's bundled npm unchanged and uses `npx --yes npm@11.10.0` for release steps because older npm versions can fail with misleading `E404 Not Found` publish errors even when OIDC is configured correctly
698	- the workflow has been verified end-to-end with release `v0.2.2`
699	- reusable setup details for this pattern live in `docs/npm-trusted-publishing.md`
700
```

1	import type { PiSessionContext } from "../pi-session.js";
2	import { getPiSessionContextKey } from "../pi-session.js";
3	
4	export interface ChatTaskRunner {
5	  tryStartPrompt(
6	    target: PiSessionContext,
7	    promptText: string,
8	    task: () => Promise<void>,
9	  ): "started" | "busy";
10	}
11	
12	export function createChatTaskRunner(deps: {
13	  beginProcessing: (target: PiSessionContext, promptText: string) => void;
14	  endProcessing: (target: PiSessionContext) => void;
15	  onTaskError: (error: unknown, target: PiSessionContext, promptText: string) => void;
16	}): ChatTaskRunner {
17	  const runningContexts = new Set<string>();
18	  const pendingTasks = new Set<Promise<void>>();
19	
20	  return {
21	    tryStartPrompt(target, promptText, task) {
22	      const contextKey = getPiSessionContextKey(target);
23	      if (runningContexts.has(contextKey)) {
24	        return "busy";
25	      }
26	
27	      runningContexts.add(contextKey);
28	      deps.beginProcessing(target, promptText);
29	
30	      let taskPromise!: Promise<void>;
31	      taskPromise = (async () => {
32	        try {
33	          await task();
34	        } catch (error) {
35	          deps.onTaskError(error, target, promptText);
36	        } finally {
37	          runningContexts.delete(contextKey);
38	          deps.endProcessing(target);
39	          pendingTasks.delete(taskPromise);
40	        }
41	      })();
42	
43	      pendingTasks.add(taskPromise);
44	      return "started";
45	    },
46	  };
47	}
48

160	function splitShellCommandSegments(command: string): string[] {

177			if (escaped) {

179				escaped = false;
180				continue;
181			}
182

187			}
188	
189			if (quote) {
190				current += character;
191				if (character === quote) {

195			}

667	): Promise<void> {
668		try {
669			if (images && images.length > 0) {
670				await session.prompt(text, { images });
671				return;
672			}
673	
674			await session.prompt(text);
675		} catch (error) {
676			throw wrapError("Pi session prompt failed", error);
677		}
678	}

769		async listSlashCommands(): Promise<SlashCommandInfo[]> {
770			const commands = this.getHandle().getSlashCommands();
771			const deduped = new Map<string, SlashCommandInfo>();
772	
773			for (const command of commands) {
774				const name = command.name.replace(/^\/+/, "").trim();
775				if (!name || deduped.has(name)) {
776					continue;
777				}
778				deduped.set(name, {
779					...command,
780					name,
781				});
782			}
783	
784			return [...deduped.values()].sort((left, right) =>
785				left.name.localeCompare(right.name),
786			);
787		}

839		async newSession(
840			request?: string | PiSessionNewSessionOptions,
841		): Promise<{ info: PiSessionInfo; created: boolean }> {
842			const options = normalizeNewSessionOptions(request);
843			const effectiveWorkspace = options.workspace ?? this.currentWorkspace;
844	
845			if (
846				(!this.handle || effectiveWorkspace !== this.currentWorkspace) &&
847				options.withSession
848			) {
849				throw new Error(
850					"TelePi only supports withSession callbacks for runtime-backed new-session replacements.",
851				);
852			}
853	
854			if (!this.handle || effectiveWorkspace !== this.currentWorkspace) {
855				const nextHandle = await createNewPiSession(
856					this.config,
857					effectiveWorkspace,
858					options,
859				);
860				await this.replaceHandle(nextHandle);
861				return { info: this.getInfo(), created: true };

863	
864			const previousSession = this.getSession();
865			const previousWorkspace = this.currentWorkspace;
866			const result = await this.getHandle().runtime.newSession({
867				parentSession: options.parentSession,
868				setup: options.setup,
869				withSession: options.withSession,
870			});
871			await this.rebindAfterRuntimeSessionReplacement(
872				previousSession,
873				previousWorkspace,
874			);
875			return { info: this.getInfo(), created: !result.cancelled };
876		}

878		async listModels(showAll = false): Promise<PiSessionModelOption[]> {
879			await this.getHandle().runtime.services.modelRuntime.getAvailable();
880			const session = this.getSession();
881			const currentModel = session.model;
882			const availableModels = this.getModelRegistry().getAvailable();
883			const availableKeys = new Set(
884				availableModels.map((model) => `${model.provider}/${model.id}`),
885			);
886			const scopedThinkingLevels = new Map(
887				session.scopedModels.map((scoped) => [
888					`${scoped.model.provider}/${scoped.model.id}`,
889					scoped.thinkingLevel,
890				]),
891			);
892			const available =
893				showAll || session.scopedModels.length === 0
894					? availableModels
895					: session.scopedModels
896							.map((scoped) => scoped.model)
897							.filter((model) =>
898								availableKeys.has(`${model.provider}/${model.id}`),
899							);
900	
901			return available.map((model) => ({
902				provider: model.provider,
903				id: model.id,
904				name: model.name,
905				current: currentModel
906					? model.provider === currentModel.provider &&
907						model.id === currentModel.id

909				thinkingLevel: scopedThinkingLevels.get(`${model.provider}/${model.id}`),
910			}));

951		async resolveSessionReference(
952			sessionReference: string,
953		): Promise<ResolvedSessionReference> {
954			const normalizedReference = sessionReference.trim();
955			if (!normalizedReference) {
956				throw new SessionReferenceResolutionError(
957					"Session reference cannot be empty.",
958				);
959			}
960	
961			const remappedReferencePath =
962				resolveSessionPathForRuntime(normalizedReference);
963			const looksLikePath =
964				normalizedReference.includes("/") ||
965				normalizedReference.includes("\\") ||
966				normalizedReference.endsWith(".jsonl") ||
967				normalizedReference.startsWith("~");
968			if (looksLikePath) {
969				if (!existsSync(remappedReferencePath)) {
970					throw new SessionReferenceResolutionError(
971						`Saved session not found: ${normalizedReference}`,
972					);
973				}
974	
975				const header = readSessionHeader(remappedReferencePath);
976	
977				let indexedWorkspace: string | undefined;
978				try {
979					const indexedMatch = (await this.listAllSessions()).find(
980						(session) =>
981							session.path === normalizedReference ||
982							session.path === remappedReferencePath ||
983							resolveSessionPathForRuntime(session.path) ===
984								remappedReferencePath,
985					);
986					indexedWorkspace = indexedMatch?.cwd;
987				} catch {
988					indexedWorkspace = undefined;
989				}
990	
991				const workspaceResolution = this.resolveSessionWorkspace(
992					indexedWorkspace ?? header?.cwd,
993				);
994				return {
995					id: header?.id ?? path.basename(remappedReferencePath),
996					path: remappedReferencePath,
997					cwd: workspaceResolution.cwd,
998					...(workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning
999						? { workspaceWarning: workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning }
1000						: {}),
1001					matchType: "path",
1002				};
1003			}
1004	
1005			const allSessions = await this.listAllSessions();
1006			const currentWorkspaceSessions = allSessions.filter(
1007				(session) => session.cwd === this.currentWorkspace,
1008			);
1009	
1010			const exactIdMatch =
1011				currentWorkspaceSessions.find(
1012					(session) => session.id === normalizedReference,
1013				) ?? allSessions.find((session) => session.id === normalizedReference);
1014			if (exactIdMatch) {
1015				const workspaceResolution = this.resolveSessionWorkspace(
1016					exactIdMatch.cwd,
1017				);
1018				return {
1019					id: exactIdMatch.id,
1020					path: exactIdMatch.path,
1021					cwd: workspaceResolution.cwd,
1022					...(workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning
1023						? { workspaceWarning: workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning }
1024						: {}),
1025					matchType: "id",
1026				};
1027			}
1028	
1029			const localPrefixMatches = currentWorkspaceSessions.filter((session) =>
1030				session.id.startsWith(normalizedReference),
1031			);
1032			if (localPrefixMatches.length === 1) {
1033				const [prefixMatch] = localPrefixMatches;
1034				const workspaceResolution = this.resolveSessionWorkspace(prefixMatch.cwd);
1035				return {
1036					id: prefixMatch.id,
1037					path: prefixMatch.path,
1038					cwd: workspaceResolution.cwd,
1039					...(workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning
1040						? { workspaceWarning: workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning }
1041						: {}),
1042					matchType: "prefix",
1043				};
1044			}
1045	
1046			if (localPrefixMatches.length > 1) {
1047				throw new SessionReferenceResolutionError(
1048					`Session ID prefix "${normalizedReference}" matches ${localPrefixMatches.length} saved sessions in the current workspace. Use more characters or /sessions to pick one.`,
1049				);
1050			}
1051	
1052			const prefixMatches = allSessions.filter((session) =>
1053				session.id.startsWith(normalizedReference),
1054			);
1055			if (prefixMatches.length === 1) {
1056				const [prefixMatch] = prefixMatches;
1057				const workspaceResolution = this.resolveSessionWorkspace(prefixMatch.cwd);
1058				return {
1059					id: prefixMatch.id,
1060					path: prefixMatch.path,
1061					cwd: workspaceResolution.cwd,
1062					...(workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning
1063						? { workspaceWarning: workspaceResolution.workspaceWarning }
1064						: {}),
1065					matchType: "prefix",
1066				};
1067			}
1068	
1069			if (prefixMatches.length > 1) {
1070				throw new SessionReferenceResolutionError(
1071					`Session ID prefix "${normalizedReference}" matches ${prefixMatches.length} saved sessions. Use more characters or /sessions to pick one.`,
1072				);
1073			}
1074	
1075			throw new SessionReferenceResolutionError(
1076				`No saved session matches "${normalizedReference}". Use /sessions to browse, or pass a full session path or session ID.`,
1077			);
1078		}

1080		/**
1081		 * Best-effort helper for UI flows that want a workspace hint before switching.
1082		 * Missing sessions and transient session-index failures should both surface as
1083		 * "no workspace available" so callers can safely fall back.
1084		 */
1085		async resolveWorkspaceForSession(
1086			sessionPath: string,
1087		): Promise<string | undefined> {
1088			try {
1089				return (await this.tryResolveSessionReference(sessionPath))?.cwd;
1090			} catch {
1091				return undefined;
1092			}
1093		}

1095		async switchSession(
1096			sessionPath: string,
1097			request?: string | PiSessionSwitchOptions,
1098		): Promise<PiSessionSwitchResult> {
1099			const options = normalizeSwitchSessionOptions(request);
1100			const resolvedReference =
1101				await this.tryResolveSessionReference(sessionPath);
1102			const runtimeSessionPath =
1103				resolvedReference?.path ?? resolveSessionPathForRuntime(sessionPath);
1104			const effectiveWorkspace =
1105				options.workspace ?? resolvedReference?.cwd ?? this.currentWorkspace;
1106	
1107			if (!this.handle && options.withSession) {
1108				throw new Error(
1109					"TelePi only supports withSession callbacks for runtime-backed session switches.",
1110				);
1111			}
1112	
1113			if (!this.handle) {
1114				const nextHandle = await createPiSession(
1115					this.config,
1116					runtimeSessionPath,
1117					effectiveWorkspace,
1118				);
1119				await this.replaceHandle(nextHandle);
1120				return {
1121					...this.getInfo(),
1122					cancelled: false,
1123				};
1124			}
1125	
1126			const previousSession = this.getSession();
1127			const previousWorkspace = this.currentWorkspace;
1128			const result = await this.getHandle().runtime.switchSession(
1129				runtimeSessionPath,
1130				{
1131					cwdOverride: effectiveWorkspace,
1132					withSession: options.withSession,
1133				},
1134			);
1135			await this.rebindAfterRuntimeSessionReplacement(
1136				previousSession,
1137				previousWorkspace,
1138			);
1139			return {
1140				...this.getInfo(),
1141				cancelled: result.cancelled,
1142			};
1143		}
1144	
1145		private async tryResolveSessionReference(
1146			sessionPath: string,
1147		): Promise<ResolvedSessionReference | undefined> {
1148			try {
1149				return await this.resolveSessionReference(sessionPath);
1150			} catch (error) {
1151				if (error instanceof SessionReferenceResolutionError) {
1152					return undefined;
1153				}
1154	
1155				throw error;
1156			}
1157		}
1158	
1159		private resolveSessionWorkspace(workspace: string | undefined): {
1160			cwd?: string;
1161			workspaceWarning?: string;
1162		} {
1163			const resolvedWorkspace = resolveWorkspacePathForRuntime(workspace);
1164			if (resolvedWorkspace) {
1165				return { cwd: resolvedWorkspace };
1166			}
1167	
1168			if (!workspace) {
1169				return {};
1170			}
1171	
1172			return {
1173				cwd: undefined,
1174				workspaceWarning: `Saved workspace ${workspace} is unavailable in this TelePi runtime. Continuing in the current workspace instead.`,
1175			};
1176		}
1177	
1178		private getUnavailableSavedWorkspace(
1179			sessionFile: string,
1180		): string | undefined {
1181			const header = readSessionHeader(sessionFile);
1182			if (!header?.cwd || header.cwd === this.currentWorkspace) {
1183				return undefined;
1184			}
1185	
1186			return resolveWorkspacePathForRuntime(header.cwd) ? undefined : header.cwd;
1187		}

1221			const previousSession = this.getSession();

1239		getLabels(): Array<{ id: string; label: string; description: string }> {
1240			const tree = this.getTree();
1241			const labels: Array<{ id: string; label: string; description: string }> =
1242				[];
1243	
1244			const walk = (node: SessionTreeNode): void => {
1245				if (node.label) {
1246					labels.push({
1247						id: node.entry.id,
1248						label: node.label,
1249						description: describeEntry(node.entry),
1250					});
1251				}
1252	
1253				for (const child of node.children) {
1254					walk(child);
1255				}
1256			};
1257	
1258			for (const root of tree) {
1259				walk(root);
1260			}
1261	
1262			return labels;
1263		}

1265		async handback(): Promise<{ sessionFile?: string; workspace: string }> {
1266			const info = {
1267				sessionFile: this.handle?.runtime.session.sessionFile,
1268				workspace: this.currentWorkspace,
1269			};
1270	
1271			const unavailableWorkspace = info.sessionFile
1272				? this.getUnavailableSavedWorkspace(info.sessionFile)
1273				: undefined;
1274			if (unavailableWorkspace) {
1275				throw new Error(
1276					`Cannot hand back this session while its saved workspace is unavailable (${unavailableWorkspace}). Reopen it from a valid workspace first.`,
1277				);
1278			}
1279	
1280			const previousHandle = this.handle;
1281			this.sessionUnsubscribe?.();
1282			this.sessionUnsubscribe = undefined;
1283			this.handle = undefined;
1284	
1285			try {
1286				await previousHandle?.dispose();
1287			} catch (error) {
1288				console.error("Failed to dispose session during handback:", error);
1289			}
1290	
1291			return info;
1292		}
1293	
1294		dispose(): void {
1295			this.sessionUnsubscribe?.();
1296			this.sessionUnsubscribe = undefined;
1297	
1298			const handle = this.handle;
1299			this.handle = undefined;
1300			if (!handle) {
1301				return;
1302			}
1303	
1304			void handle.dispose().catch((error) => {
1305				console.error("Failed to dispose Pi session:", error);
1306			});
1307		}

1309		private getHandle(): PiSessionHandle {
1310			if (!this.handle) {
1311				throw new Error("Pi session is not initialized");
1312			}
1313			return this.handle;
1314		}

1320		private async replaceHandle(nextHandle: PiSessionHandle): Promise<void> {
1321			const previousHandle = this.handle;
1322			const previousSession = previousHandle?.runtime.session;
1323			const previousWorkspace = this.currentWorkspace;
1324			this.handle = nextHandle;
1325	
1326			try {
1327				await this.rebindAfterSessionReplacement(previousSession);
1328			} catch (error) {
1329				await this.disposeHandleAfterRebindFailure(
1330					nextHandle,
1331					previousWorkspace,
1332					error,
1333				);
1334			} finally {
1335				try {
1336					await previousHandle?.dispose();
1337				} catch (error) {
1338					console.error("Failed to dispose previous session:", error);
1339				}
1340			}
1341		}
1342	
1343		private async bindExtensionsToCurrentSession(): Promise<void> {
1344			if (!this.extensionBindings || !this.handle) {
1345				return;
1346			}
1347	
1348			await this.getSession().bindExtensions(this.extensionBindings);
1349		}
1350	
1351		private rebindSessionSubscription(): void {
1352			this.sessionUnsubscribe?.();
1353			this.sessionUnsubscribe = undefined;
1354	
1355			if (!this.sessionCallbacks || !this.handle) {
1356				return;
1357			}

1359			this.sessionUnsubscribe = subscribeToSession(

1365		private async disposeHandleAfterRebindFailure(

1402		private async rebindAfterSessionReplacement(
1403			previousSession?: AgentSession,
1404		): Promise<void> {
1405			if (!this.handle) {
1406				return;
1407			}
1408	
1409			const currentSession = this.getSession();
1410			// AgentSessionRuntime replacements track the effective workspace on runtime.cwd.
1411			// TelePi treats runtime.cwd as the source of truth after every runtime-driven
1412			// session replacement while keeping these flows serialized through the service instance.
1413			this.currentWorkspace = this.handle.runtime.cwd;
1414			if (previousSession === currentSession) {
1415				return;
1416			}
1417	
1418			await this.bindExtensionsToCurrentSession();
1419			this.rebindSessionSubscription();
1420		}

1462		async getOrCreate(context: PiSessionContext): Promise<PiSessionService> {

1624	function normalizeResourceDiagnostics(

1644	function dedupeDiagnostics(

1692	function resolveModelOverride(
1693		modelRegistry: ModelRegistry,
1694		modelRef: string | undefined,
1695	): Model<Api> | undefined {
1696		if (!modelRef) {
1697			return undefined;
1698		}
1699	
1700		const normalized = modelRef.trim();
1701		const slashIndex = normalized.indexOf("/");
1702	
1703		if (slashIndex >= 0) {
1704			const provider = normalized.slice(0, slashIndex).trim();
1705			const rawModelId = normalized.slice(slashIndex + 1).trim();
1706			const modelId = rawModelId.split(":")[0]?.trim();
1707	
1708			if (!provider || !modelId) {
1709				throw new Error(`Invalid PI_MODEL value: ${modelRef}`);
1710			}
1711	
1712			const model = modelRegistry.find(provider, modelId);
1713			if (!model) {
1714				throw new Error(`Could not resolve PI_MODEL: ${modelRef}`);
1715			}
1716	
1717			return model;
1718		}
1719	
1720		const matches = modelRegistry
1721			.getAll()
1722			.filter((model) => model.id === normalized);
1723		if (matches.length === 0) {
1724			throw new Error(`Could not resolve PI_MODEL: ${modelRef}`);
1725		}
1726	
1727		if (matches.length > 1) {
1728			const providers = matches.map((model) => model.provider).join(", ");
1729			throw new Error(
1730				`PI_MODEL is ambiguous. Use provider/modelId instead. Matches: ${providers}`,
1731			);
1732		}
1733	
1734		return matches[0];
1735	}

572	export function createPromptHandler(
573		options: CreatePromptHandlerOptions,
574	): HandleUserPrompt {
575		const { isBusy, taskRunner, sendBusyReply, ...promptFlowDeps } = options;
576	
577		return async (
578			ctx: Context,
579			target: PiSessionContext,
580			userText: string,
581			preloadedSlashCommands?: SlashCommandInfo[],
582			images?: ImageContent[],
583		): Promise<boolean> => {
584			if (isBusy(target)) {
585				await sendBusyReply(ctx);
586				return false;
587			}
588	
589			const result = taskRunner.tryStartPrompt(target, userText, () =>
590				runPromptFlow(
591					promptFlowDeps,
592					ctx,
593					target,
594					userText,
595					preloadedSlashCommands,
596					images,
597				),
598			);
599			if (result === "busy") {
600				await sendBusyReply(ctx);
601				return false;
602			}
603	
604			return true;
605		};
606	}
