102	function selectPhotoFileId(
103		photos: Array<{ file_id: string; file_size?: number }> | undefined,
104	): string | undefined {
105		if (!photos || photos.length === 0) {
106			return undefined;
107		}
108	
109		let selected = photos[photos.length - 1];
110		for (const candidate of photos) {
111			if (
112				candidate.file_size !== undefined &&
113				(selected.file_size === undefined ||
114					candidate.file_size > selected.file_size)
115			) {
116				selected = candidate;
117			}
118		}
119	
120		return selected?.file_id;
121	}

123	function resolveImageMimeType(
124		filePath: string,
125		explicitMimeType?: string,
126	): string {
127		const normalizedMimeType = explicitMimeType?.trim().toLowerCase();
128		if (normalizedMimeType?.startsWith("image/")) {
129			return normalizedMimeType;
130		}
131	
132		const extensionIndex = filePath.lastIndexOf(".");
133		const extension =
134			extensionIndex >= 0 ? filePath.slice(extensionIndex).toLowerCase() : "";
135		return IMAGE_MIME_BY_EXTENSION[extension] ?? "image/jpeg";
136	}

```text
1	# Tag schema (priority × effort)
2	
3	Two orthogonal axes prevent the "important but unimplementable" trap:
4	
5	## Priority
6	
7	- `P1` — likely next batch (you'd reach for this if you sat down today)
8	- `P2` — worth doing, no rush
9	- `P3` — someday / nice-to-have
10	- `P?` — needs evaluation first; spike before committing to a priority
11	
12	## Effort
13	
14	- `S` — under an hour
15	- `M` — half day
16	- `L` — multi-day
17	- `XL` — architectural; design doc required before code
18	
19	## Useful combinations
20	
21	- `P?` + `[?/L]` — explicit "unknown of size L"; the most honest tag
22	- `P3` + `[S]` — "small enough to slip into any free moment"
23	- `P1` + `[XL]` — warns "you said this is urgent but it's actually huge — re-scope"
24	
25	## Heading and item syntax (validator-checked)
26	
27	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` enforces this exact form. If you change
28	the syntax, update the script in the same commit.
29	
30	- Section headings, in order: `## P1`, `## P2`, `## P3`, `## P?`, `## Done`
31	- Active items in `P1` / `P2` / `P3`:
32	  `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
33	- Active items in `P?`:
34	  `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
35	- Shipped items in `Done`:
36	  `- ✅ [YYYY-MM-DD] [P#/Effort] Title — one-line shipped summary`
37	- Optional trailing on active items:
38	  `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
39	
40	Anything that is NOT a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item — prose paragraphs,
41	blockquotes, HTML comments, `---` rules, indented sub-bullets — is ignored
42	by the validator. Use this room for explanatory text without breaking the
43	machine-readability of the lanes.
44

534	        saveConfig(cfg3);
535	        const toolState = cfg3.hideToolCalls ? "hidden" : "shown";
536	        context.ui.notify(`🔧 Tool calls ${toolState} in remote messages`, "info");
537	        break;
538	      }
539	      default:
540	        context.ui.notify(`Unknown subcommand: ${subcommand}. Run /msg-bridge help`, "warning");
541	        break;
542	    }
543	    },
544	  });
545	}
546
```

1	import type { ExternalMessage } from "../types.js";
2	import type { ITransportProvider } from "./interface.js";
3	
4	/**
5	 * Manages multiple transport providers and routes messages
6	 */
7	export class TransportManager {
8	  private transports = new Map<string, ITransportProvider>();
9	  private messageHandler?: (message: ExternalMessage) => void;
10	  private errorHandler?: (error: Error, transport: string) => void;
11	
12	  /**
13	   * Register a transport provider
14	   */
15	  addTransport(transport: ITransportProvider): void {
16	    this.transports.set(transport.type, transport);
17	
18	    // Forward messages from this transport
19	    transport.onMessage((msg) => {
20	      if (this.messageHandler) {
21	        this.messageHandler(msg);
22	      }
23	    });
24	
25	    // Forward errors from this transport
26	    transport.onError((err) => {
27	      if (this.errorHandler) {
28	        this.errorHandler(err, transport.type);
29	      }
30	    });
31	  }
32	
33	  /**
34	   * Get a specific transport by type
35	   */
36	  getTransport(type: string): ITransportProvider | undefined {
37	    return this.transports.get(type);
38	  }
39	
40	  /**
41	   * Get all registered transports
42	   */
43	  getAllTransports(): ITransportProvider[] {
44	    return Array.from(this.transports.values());
45	  }
46	
47	  /**
48	   * Connect all registered transports
49	   */
50	  async connectAll(): Promise<void> {
51	    const connections = Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) =>
52	      t.connect().catch((err) => {
53	        throw new Error(`${t.type} connection failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
54	      })
55	    );
56	    await Promise.all(connections);
57	  }
58	
59	  /**
60	   * Disconnect all transports
61	   */
62	  async disconnectAll(): Promise<void> {
63	    const disconnections = Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) =>
64	      t.disconnect()
65	    );
66	    await Promise.allSettled(disconnections);
67	  }
68	
69	  /**
70	   * Send a message to a specific chat via a specific transport
71	   */
72	  async sendMessage(
73	    chatId: string,
74	    transportType: string,
75	    text: string
76	  ): Promise<void> {
77	    const transport = this.transports.get(transportType);
78	    if (!transport) {
79	      throw new Error(`Transport ${transportType} not found`);
80	    }
81	    if (!transport.isConnected) {
82	      throw new Error(`Transport ${transportType} not connected`);
83	    }
84	    await transport.sendMessage(chatId, text);
85	  }
86	
87	  /**
88	   * Send typing indicator to a chat via a specific transport
89	   */
90	  async sendTyping(chatId: string, transportType: string): Promise<void> {
91	    const transport = this.transports.get(transportType);
92	    if (transport?.isConnected) {
93	      await transport.sendTyping(chatId);
94	    }
95	  }
96	
97	  /**
98	   * Register handler for incoming messages from all transports
99	   */
100	  onMessage(handler: (message: ExternalMessage) => void): void {
101	    this.messageHandler = handler;
102	  }
103	
104	  /**
105	   * Register handler for errors from all transports
106	   */
107	  onError(handler: (error: Error, transport: string) => void): void {
108	    this.errorHandler = handler;
109	  }
110	
111	  /**
112	   * Get connection status for all transports
113	   */
114	  getStatus(): Array<{ type: string; connected: boolean }> {
115	    return Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) => ({
116	      type: t.type,
117	      connected: t.isConnected,
118	    }));
119	  }
120	}
121

3	/**
4	 * Transport provider interface

6	 */
7	export interface ITransportProvider {
8	  /** Transport type identifier */
9	  readonly type: string;
10	
11	  /** Is the transport currently connected? */
12	  readonly isConnected: boolean;
13	
14	  /**
15	   * Connect to the messenger service
16	   * @throws Error if connection fails
17	   */
18	  connect(): Promise<void>;
19	
20	  /**
21	   * Disconnect from the messenger service
22	   */
23	  disconnect(): Promise<void>;
24	
25	  /**
26	   * Send a text message to a chat
27	   * @param chatId - Chat/channel identifier
28	   * @param text - Message content
29	   */
30	  sendMessage(chatId: string, text: string): Promise<void>;
31	
32	  /**
33	   * Send typing indicator to a chat
34	   * @param chatId - Chat/channel identifier
35	   */
36	  sendTyping(chatId: string): Promise<void>;
37	
38	  /**
39	   * Register callback for incoming messages
40	   * @param handler - Message handler function
41	   */
42	  onMessage(handler: (message: ExternalMessage) => void): void;
43	
44	  /**
45	   * Register callback for errors
46	   * @param handler - Error handler function
47	   */
48	  onError(handler: (error: Error) => void): void;
49	}

```text
1	# pi-messenger-bridge
2	
3	Bridge common messengers (Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Matrix) into pi.
4	
5	Remote users can interact with your pi coding agent via their messenger app.
6	
7	<img width="887" height="656" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d42a41e5-e7d5-420b-be8e-f2191facb190" />
8	
9	https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd64360e-e8cd-4820-a67f-bd127c5d6035
10	
11	## Features
12	
13	- 📱 Multi-messenger support (Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Matrix)
14	- 🔐 Challenge-based authentication (6-digit codes)
15	- 🎛️ Interactive menu (`/msg-bridge`) for setup and management
16	- 🔒 Single-instance guard — prevents duplicate bot polling with sub-agents
17	- 📊 Live status widget (toggleable)
18	- 💾 Persistent config (auth state, auto-connect, widget preference)
19	- 🔧 Tool call visibility for remote users
20	- 📝 Multi-turn conversation support
21	- 🔑 Secure permissions (chmod 600 for config files, 700 for directories)
22	
23	## Setup
24	
25	### 1. Install
26	
27	```bash
28	pi install npm:pi-messenger-bridge
29	```
30	
31	### 2. Configure Transports
32	
33	#### Telegram
34	
35	Create a bot via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) and get your token.
36	
37	```bash
38	/msg-bridge configure telegram <bot-token>
39	```
40	
41	Or set via environment variable:
42	```bash
43	export PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN="your-bot-token-here"
44	```
45	
46	#### WhatsApp
47	
48	Configure WhatsApp (requires QR code scan):
49	
50	```bash
51	/msg-bridge configure whatsapp
52	```
53	
54	Scan the QR code with your WhatsApp mobile app (**Linked Devices → Link a device**).
55	
56	> **Note:** After linking, **send a message to your own phone number** in WhatsApp to activate the bridge.
57	
58	Or set custom auth path:
59	```bash
60	export PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH="/path/to/whatsapp-auth"
61	```
62	
63	#### Slack
64	
65	Create a Slack app with Socket Mode enabled. You need both tokens:
66	
67	```bash
68	/msg-bridge configure slack <bot-token> <app-token>
69	```
70	
71	Or set via environment variables:
72	```bash
73	export PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-..."
74	export PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN="xapp-..."
75	```
76	
77	#### Discord
78	
79	1. Create a new application in the [Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
80	2. Go to **Bot** → **Reset Token** → copy the token
81	3. Enable **Message Content Intent** (under Privileged Gateway Intents on the same page)
82	4. Go to **OAuth2 → URL Generator** → select scope `bot` → select permissions `Send Messages` and `Read Message History` → open the generated URL to invite the bot to your server
83	
84	```bash
85	/msg-bridge configure discord <bot-token>
86	```
87	
88	Or set via environment variable:
89	```bash
90	export PI_DISCORD_TOKEN="your-bot-token"
91	```
92	
93	#### Matrix
94	
95	Works with any Matrix homeserver — Element X, Element Web, FluffyChat, etc. The bot auto-joins rooms it's invited to.
96	
97	1. Register a bot account on your homeserver (or reuse an existing user)
98	2. Get an access token: log in once via Element and copy from **Settings → Help & About → Advanced**, or POST to `/_matrix/client/v3/login`
99	3. Note your homeserver URL (e.g. `https://matrix.org`)
100	
101	```bash
102	/msg-bridge configure matrix <homeserver-url> <access-token>
103	```
104	
105	Or set via environment variables:
106	```bash
107	export PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER="https://matrix.org"
108	export PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN="syt_..."
109	```
110	
111	E2EE is **on by default**. Verify the bot's device once from another Matrix client (Element, etc.) — until verified, encrypted rooms can't be decrypted in either direction.
112	
113	Set `"encryption": false` in the `matrix` config to disable — useful for non-encrypted rooms only, or to bypass crypto-store/server desync (e.g. `M_UNKNOWN: One time key … already exists`). **Caveat:** with E2EE off, the homeserver sees plaintext, and the bot can't participate in encrypted rooms at all.
114	
115	### 3. Connect
116	
117	```bash
118	/msg-bridge connect
119	```
120	
121	### 4. Authenticate Users
122	
123	When a user messages your bot for the first time, they'll receive a 6-digit challenge code.
124	The code is displayed in your pi terminal. Share it with the user (e.g., via DM).
125	
126	The user enters the code in the bot chat to become a trusted user.
127	
128	## Commands
129	
130	| Command | Description |
131	|---|---|
132	| `/msg-bridge` | Open interactive menu (configure, connect, widget, help) |
133	| `/msg-bridge status` | Show connection and user status |
134	| `/msg-bridge connect` | Connect to all configured transports |
135	| `/msg-bridge disconnect` | Disconnect all transports |
136	| `/msg-bridge configure <platform> [token]` | Set transport credentials via CLI |
137	| `/msg-bridge widget` | Toggle status widget on/off |
138	| `/msg-bridge toggletools` | Toggle tool call visibility in remote messages |
139	| `/msg-bridge help` | Show command reference |
140	
141	### Admin commands (in DM with the bot)
142	
143	Trusted users can DM the bot directly to manage state. Reply with `/help` for the full list:
144	
145	| Command | Description |
146	|---|---|
147	| `/help` | Show admin command reference |
148	| `/trusted` | List trusted users |
149	| `/revoke <userId>` | Revoke trust for a user |
150	| `/channels` | List enabled channels |
151	| `/enable <chatId> <all\|mentions\|trusted-only>` | Enable a channel |
152	| `/disable <chatId>` | Disable a channel |
153	| `/toggletools` | Toggle tool call visibility in replies |
154	
155	## Configuration
156	
157	Config is stored at `~/.pi/msg-bridge.json` with secure permissions (chmod 600).
158	
159	Example config:
160	```json
161	{
162	  "telegram": { "token": "..." },
163	  "whatsapp": { "authPath": "..." },
164	  "slack": { "botToken": "...", "appToken": "..." },
165	  "discord": { "token": "..." },
166	  "matrix": { "homeserverUrl": "https://matrix.org", "accessToken": "syt_...", "encryption": true },
167	  "auth": {
168	    "trustedUsers": ["telegram:123", "whatsapp:456"],
169	    "adminUserId": "telegram:789"
170	  },
171	  "autoConnect": true,
172	  "showWidget": true,
173	  "debug": false
174	}
175	```
176	
177	## Environment Variables
178	
179	Environment variables override file config:
180	
181	- `PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` — Telegram bot token
182	- `PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH` — WhatsApp session directory (default: `~/.pi/msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth`)
183	- `PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` — Slack bot token (xoxb-...)
184	- `PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN` — Slack app token (xapp-...)
185	- `PI_DISCORD_TOKEN` — Discord bot token
186	- `PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER` — Matrix homeserver URL (e.g. `https://matrix.org`)
187	- `PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN` — Matrix access token
188	- `MSG_BRIDGE_DEBUG` — Enable debug logging (true/false)
189	
190	## Security
191	
192	- Config file: `~/.pi/msg-bridge.json` (chmod 600 - owner read/write only)
193	- Config directory: `~/.pi/` (chmod 700 - owner only)
194	- WhatsApp auth: `~/.pi/msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth/` (chmod 700 - owner only)
195	- Environment variables take precedence over config file
196	- Challenge-based authentication for all new users
197	- Transport-namespaced user IDs prevent impersonation
198	
199	## Troubleshooting
200	
201	Enable debug mode to see detailed logs:
202	
203	```json
204	{
205	  "debug": true
206	}
207	```
208	
209	Or:
210	```bash
211	export MSG_BRIDGE_DEBUG=true
212	```
213	
214	## Architecture
215	
216	Uses pi's native `sendUserMessage()` and `turn_end` events for two-way communication.
217	No tool-loop hacks needed — this is the pi-native way.
218	
219	Single-instance connection guard prevents duplicate polling when sub-agents spawn
220	(global flag + PID lock file at `~/.pi/msg-bridge.lock`).
221	
222	## Development
223	
224	```bash
225	npm install
226	npm run build        # compile TypeScript
227	npm run typecheck    # type-check without emitting
228	npm run test         # run tests
229	npm run lint         # biome lint
230	npm run lint:fix     # biome lint with auto-fix
231	```
232	
233	## License
234	
235	MIT
236
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
4	
5	## [1.7.0] - 2026-07-17
6	
7	### Changed
8	
9	- Discord `/pi model` now reads the model catalog from the configured pi binary (`PI_BIN --list-models`) and honors pi's configured `enabledModels` scope, including glob patterns and configured order. The bundled SDK catalog is used only as a fallback when the command fails.
10	- Model catalogs are prewarmed at startup for all registered channel working directories. `/pi model` autocomplete responds from the cache to stay inside Discord's response deadline and refreshes expired catalogs in the background.
11	- `PI_EXTRA_FLAGS` is now passed to model discovery as well, so models registered by pi extensions appear in the catalog.
12	
13	### Fixed
14	
15	- Model discovery via `pi --list-models` is bounded by a 15s timeout, so a hung pi install can no longer block gateway startup or slash commands.
16	- The model list parser now locates the table header instead of assuming it is the first output line, so banners printed by pi extensions no longer result in an empty catalog.
17	- `/pi model` autocomplete in unregistered channels returns no choices without spawning pi.
18	
19	## [1.6.1] - 2026-06-15
20	
21	### Fixed
22	
23	- Remove stale hardcoded README current-version text so npm/GitHub documentation does not show an outdated release number.
24	
25	## [1.6.0] - 2026-06-15
26	
27	### Changed
28	
29	- Discord attachments are now passed to `pi` by local file path instead of being injected with `@file`. This keeps binary and structured files such as DOCX, XLSX, PDFs, and images out of the model context while still letting the agent inspect or convert them with tools.
30	- Downloaded attachment media is retained for a configurable period so path-based agent workflows can continue after the initial message. New config: `MEDIA_RETENTION_HOURS` (default: `168`, one week).
31	
32	### Fixed
33	
34	- Empty stdout from `pi` no longer becomes an unhelpful `(empty response)` Discord reply. piscord now reports the recorded agent/session error when available, including context-window errors such as `context_length_exceeded`.
35	- Prevent large or binary attachments from flooding the model context and causing repeated empty responses in the affected channel session.

443	function readSessionTokensFromJsonl(sessionFile: string): SessionTokenUsage {

447	  for (const line of lines) {
448	    const trimmed = line.trim();
449	    if (!trimmed) continue;
450	
451	    try {
452	      const entry = JSON.parse(trimmed) as {
453	        type?: string;
454	        message?: {
455	          role?: string;
456	          usage?: {
457	            input?: number;
458	            output?: number;
459	            cacheRead?: number;
460	            cacheWrite?: number;
461	            totalTokens?: number;
462	          };
463	        };
464	      };

466	      if (entry.type !== 'message' || entry.message?.role !== 'assistant' || !entry.message.usage) {
467	        continue;

469	
470	      const input = toNumber(entry.message.usage.input);
471	      const output = toNumber(entry.message.usage.output);
472	      const cacheRead = toNumber(entry.message.usage.cacheRead);
473	      const cacheWrite = toNumber(entry.message.usage.cacheWrite);
474	
475	      totals.input += input;
476	      totals.output += output;
477	      totals.cacheRead += cacheRead;
478	      totals.cacheWrite += cacheWrite;
479	      totals.total +=
480	        toNumber(entry.message.usage.totalTokens) || input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite;
481	    } catch {
482	      // Ignore incomplete or malformed trailing JSONL lines.
483	    }
484	  }

487	}

127	      activeTaskControllers.delete(msg.rowid);
128	      activeChannelControllers.delete(jid);
129	      activeTaskPromises.delete(taskPromise);
130	
131	      if (running) {
132	        schedulePoll(0);
133	      }
134	    });
135	
136	    activeTaskPromises.add(taskPromise);
137	  }
138	}
139	
140	async function drainActiveTasks(timeoutMs: number): Promise<void> {
141	  if (activeTaskPromises.size === 0) {
142	    return;
143	  }
144	
145	  const initialDrain = Promise.allSettled([...activeTaskPromises]);
146	  const drainedGracefully = await waitForPromise(initialDrain, timeoutMs);
147	  if (drainedGracefully) {
148	    return;
149	  }
150	
151	  logger.warn(
152	    { timeoutMs, activeTasks: activeTaskPromises.size },
153	    'Shutdown timeout reached; aborting in-flight message processing',
154	  );
155	
156	  for (const controller of activeTaskControllers.values()) {
157	    controller.abort();
158	  }
159	
160	  if (activeTaskPromises.size > 0) {
161	    await Promise.race([
162	      Promise.allSettled([...activeTaskPromises]),
163	      new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5_000)),
164	    ]);
165	  }
166	}
167	
168	async function waitForPromise(promise: Promise<unknown>, timeoutMs: number): Promise<boolean> {
169	  if (timeoutMs === 0) {
170	    return false;
171	  }
172	
173	  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
174	
175	  try {
176	    await Promise.race([
177	      promise,
178	      new Promise((resolve) => {
179	        timer = setTimeout(resolve, timeoutMs);
180	      }),
181	    ]);
182	  } finally {
183	    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
184	  }
185	
186	  return activeTaskPromises.size === 0;
187	}
188	
189	async function processMessage(
190	  jid: string,
191	  rowid: number,
192	  senderName: string,
193	  content: string,
194	  signal: AbortSignal,
195	  attachments?: string | null,
196	): Promise<void> {
197	  const channel = getChannel(jid);
198	  if (!channel) {
199	    logger.warn({ jid }, 'Channel disappeared during processing');
200	    markMessageFailed(rowid);
201	    return;
202	  }
203	
204	  logger.info({ jid, senderName, len: content.length }, 'Processing message');
205	
206	  const typingLoop = createTypingLoop(jid);
207	
208	  try {
209	    const prompt = `[Discord user: ${senderName}]\n${content}`;
210	
211	    logMessage(jid, 'user', content);
212	
213	    const effective = computeEffectiveChannelSettings(channel);
214	
215	    const result = await invokeAgent(channel.folder, prompt, {
216	      model: effective.rawModelRef || undefined,
217	      thinking: effective.hasManagedThinking ? effective.effectiveThinking : undefined,
218	      cwd: effective.effectiveCwd,
219	      signal,
220	      attachments,
221	    });
222	
223	    if (signal.aborted) {
224	      markMessageFailed(rowid);
225	      logger.info({ jid, rowid }, 'Message abandoned: shutdown interrupted processing');
226	      return;
227	    }
228	
229	    if (result.ok) {
230	      const sent = await sendResponse(jid, result.text);
231	      if (!sent) {
232	        markMessageFailed(rowid);
233	        logger.warn({ jid }, 'Agent response generated but could not be delivered to Discord');
234	        return;
235	      }
236	
237	      logMessage(jid, 'assistant', result.text);
238	      markMessageDone(rowid);
239	      logger.info({ jid, responseLen: result.text.length }, 'Message processed');
240	      return;
241	    }
242	
243	    const errMsg = `⚠️ Agent error: ${result.error?.slice(0, 300) || 'unknown error'}`;
244	    await sendResponse(jid, errMsg);
245	    markMessageFailed(rowid);
246	    logger.warn({ jid, error: result.error }, 'Agent returned error');
247	  } catch (err: any) {
248	    if (signal.aborted) {
249	      markMessageFailed(rowid);
250	      logger.info({ jid, rowid }, 'Message abandoned: shutdown interrupted processing');
251	      return;
252	    }
253	
254	    logger.error({ jid, err: err.message }, 'processMessage failed');
255	    markMessageFailed(rowid);
256	    try {
257	      await sendResponse(jid, `⚠️ Internal error: ${err.message?.slice(0, 200)}`);
258	    } catch {
259	      // Nothing else to do here.
260	    }
261	  } finally {
262	    await typingLoop.stop();
263	  }
264	}
265	
266	function createTypingLoop(jid: string): { stop: () => Promise<void> } {
267	  let typingAlive = true;
268	  let cancelTypingDelay = () => {};
269	
270	  const loop = (async () => {
271	    while (typingAlive) {
272	      await setTyping(jid);
273	      if (!typingAlive) break;
274	
275	      const delay = cancellableSleep(8000);
276	      cancelTypingDelay = delay.cancel;
277	      await delay.promise;
278	      cancelTypingDelay = () => {};
279	    }
280	  })();
281	
282	  return {
283	    stop: async () => {
284	      typingAlive = false;
285	      cancelTypingDelay();
286	      await loop;
287	    },
288	  };
289	}
290	
291	function cancellableSleep(ms: number): { promise: Promise<void>; cancel: () => void } {
292	  let finished = false;
293	  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
294	  let resolvePromise: () => void = () => {};
295	
296	  const promise = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
297	    resolvePromise = () => {
298	      if (finished) return;
299	      finished = true;
300	      if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
301	      resolve();
302	    };
303	
304	    timer = setTimeout(resolvePromise, ms);
305	  });
306	
307	  return {
308	    promise,
309	    cancel: resolvePromise,
310	  };
311	}

2	import { config } from '../config.js';

11	const SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;
12	
13	let schedulerTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | undefined;
14	
15	export function computeNextRun(schedule: string, type: ScheduledTaskType): string | null {
16	  if (type === 'once') {
17	    const nextRun = new Date(schedule);
18	    if (Number.isNaN(nextRun.getTime()) || nextRun.getTime() <= Date.now()) {
19	      return null;
20	    }
21	
22	    return schedule;
23	  }
24	
25	  try {
26	    return new Cron(schedule).nextRun()?.toISOString() ?? null;
27	  } catch {
28	    return null;
29	  }
30	}
31	
32	export function startScheduler(): () => void {
33	  if (schedulerTimer) {
34	    return stopScheduler;
35	  }
36	
37	  const tick = () => {
38	    try {
39	      enqueueDueTasks();
40	    } catch (err) {
41	      logger.error(
42	        { err: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) },
43	        'Scheduler tick failed',
44	      );
45	    }
46	  };
47	
48	  tick();
49	  schedulerTimer = setInterval(tick, SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS);
50	
51	  logger.info(
52	    { intervalMs: SCHEDULER_INTERVAL_MS, maxPerTick: config.maxScheduledConcurrency },
53	    'Scheduler started',
54	  );
55	
56	  return stopScheduler;
57	}
58	
59	function stopScheduler(): void {
60	  if (!schedulerTimer) {
61	    return;
62	  }
63	
64	  clearInterval(schedulerTimer);
65	  schedulerTimer = undefined;
66	  logger.info('Scheduler stopped');
67	}
68	
69	function enqueueDueTasks(): void {
70	  const now = new Date().toISOString();
71	  const dueTasks = getDueScheduledTasks().slice(0, config.maxScheduledConcurrency);
72	
73	  for (const task of dueTasks) {
74	    enqueueDueTask(task, now);
75	  }
76	}
77	
78	function enqueueDueTask(task: ScheduledTaskRow, now: string): void {
79	  enqueueScheduledTask(
80	    task.id,
81	    {

83	      sender: 'scheduler',

85	      content: task.prompt,
86	      timestamp: now,

249	export async function sendResponse(jid: string, text: string): Promise<boolean> {

267	      const chunks = splitMessage(text, DISCORD_MAX_LENGTH);
268	      for (const chunk of chunks) {

270	      }
271	    }
272	    logger.info({ jid, length: text.length }, 'Response sent');

307	function splitMessage(text: string, max: number): string[] {
308	  const chunks: string[] = [];
309	  let remaining = text;
310	
311	  while (remaining.length > max) {
312	    // Try to split at last newline within limit
313	    let splitAt = remaining.lastIndexOf('\n', max);
314	    if (splitAt <= 0) splitAt = max; // hard split if no newline
315	    chunks.push(remaining.slice(0, splitAt));
316	    remaining = remaining.slice(splitAt).replace(/^\n/, '');
317	  }
318	  if (remaining) chunks.push(remaining);
319	  return chunks;
320	}

89	  ensureTableColumn('channels', 'thinking_override', "text not null default ''");
90	  ensureTableColumn('channels', 'cwd_override', "text not null default ''");
91	  ensureTableColumn('message_queue', 'attachments', 'text');
92	
93	  logger.info({ path: config.dbPath }, 'Database initialized');
94	}
95	
96	function ensureTableColumn(table: string, column: string, ddl: string): void {
97	  const rows = db.prepare(`pragma table_info(${table})`).all() as Array<{ name: string }>;
98	  if (rows.some((row) => row.name === column)) return;
99	  db.exec(`alter table ${table} add column ${column} ${ddl}`);
100	  logger.info({ table, column }, 'Database migrated: added column');
101	}
102	
103	function normalizeTimestamp(timestamp: string | null): string | null {
104	  if (timestamp === null) {
105	    return null;
106	  }
107	
108	  const parsed = new Date(timestamp);
109	  if (Number.isNaN(parsed.getTime())) {
110	    return timestamp;
111	  }
112	
113	  return parsed.toISOString().slice(0, 19).replace('T', ' ');
114	}
115	
116	// ── Channel registration ──
117	
118	export function registerChannel(ch: RegisteredChannel): void {
119	  db.prepare(
120	    `
121	    insert into channels (jid, name, folder, requires_trigger, is_main, model_override, thinking_override, cwd_override)
122	    values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
123	    on conflict(jid) do update set
124	      name = excluded.name,
125	      folder = excluded.folder,
126	      requires_trigger = excluded.requires_trigger,
127	      is_main = excluded.is_main,
128	      cwd_override = case
129	        when excluded.cwd_override != '' then excluded.cwd_override
130	        else channels.cwd_override
131	      end
132	  `,
133	  ).run(
134	    ch.jid,
135	    ch.name,
136	    ch.folder,
137	    ch.requiresTrigger ? 1 : 0,
138	    ch.isMain ? 1 : 0,
139	    ch.modelOverride || '',
140	    ch.thinkingOverride || '',
141	    ch.cwdOverride.trim(),
142	  );
143	  logger.info({ jid: ch.jid, name: ch.name }, 'Channel registered');
144	}
145	
146	export function unregisterChannel(jid: string): boolean {
147	  const result = db.prepare('delete from channels where jid = ?').run(jid);
148	  return result.changes > 0;
149	}
150	
151	export function getChannel(jid: string): RegisteredChannel | undefined {
152	  const row = db.prepare('select * from channels where jid = ?').get(jid) as any;
153	  return row ? rowToChannel(row) : undefined;
154	}
155	
156	export function getAllChannels(): RegisteredChannel[] {
157	  const rows = db.prepare('select * from channels order by created_at').all() as any[];
158	  return rows.map(rowToChannel);
159	}
160	
161	export function createDmChannel(
162	  jid: string,
163	  userId: string,
164	  displayName: string,
165	): RegisteredChannel {
166	  return {
167	    jid,
168	    name: `DM:${displayName}`,
169	    folder: `dm_${userId}`,
170	    requiresTrigger: false,
171	    isMain: false,
172	    modelOverride: '',
173	    thinkingOverride: '',
174	    cwdOverride: '',
175	  };
176	}
177	
178	export function setChannelModelOverride(jid: string, modelOverride: string): boolean {
179	  const result = db
180	    .prepare('update channels set model_override = ? where jid = ?')
181	    .run(modelOverride.trim(), jid);
182	  return result.changes > 0;
183	}
184	
185	export function clearChannelModelOverride(jid: string): boolean {
186	  const result = db.prepare("update channels set model_override = '' where jid = ?").run(jid);
187	  return result.changes > 0;
188	}
189	
190	export function setChannelThinkingOverride(jid: string, thinkingOverride: ThinkingLevel): boolean {
191	  const result = db
192	    .prepare('update channels set thinking_override = ? where jid = ?')
193	    .run(thinkingOverride, jid);
194	  return result.changes > 0;
195	}
196	
197	export function clearChannelThinkingOverride(jid: string): boolean {
198	  const result = db.prepare("update channels set thinking_override = '' where jid = ?").run(jid);
199	  return result.changes > 0;
200	}
201	
202	function rowToChannel(row: any): RegisteredChannel {
203	  return {
204	    jid: row.jid,
205	    name: row.name,
206	    folder: row.folder,
207	    requiresTrigger: row.requires_trigger === 1,
208	    isMain: row.is_main === 1,
209	    modelOverride: row.model_override || '',
210	    thinkingOverride: (row.thinking_override || '') as ThinkingLevel | '',
211	    cwdOverride: row.cwd_override || '',
212	  };
213	}
214	
215	// ── Message queue ──
216	
217	export function enqueueMessage(msg: {
218	  channelJid: string;
219	  sender: string;
220	  senderName: string;
221	  content: string;
222	  timestamp: string;
223	  attachments?: string | null;
224	}): void {
225	  db.prepare(
226	    `
227	    insert into message_queue (channel_jid, sender, sender_name, content, timestamp, attachments)
228	    values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
229	  `,
230	  ).run(
231	    msg.channelJid,
232	    msg.sender,
233	    msg.senderName,
234	    msg.content,
235	    msg.timestamp,
236	    msg.attachments ?? null,
237	  );
238	}
239	
240	export function claimNextMessage(channelJid: string): QueuedMessage | undefined {
241	  const row = db
242	    .prepare(
243	      `
244	    with next_message as (
245	      select rowid
246	      from message_queue
247	      where status = 'pending' and channel_jid = ?
248	      order by rowid asc
249	      limit 1
250	    )
251	    update message_queue
252	    set status = 'processing'
253	    where rowid = (select rowid from next_message)
254	      and status = 'pending'
255	    returning rowid, channel_jid, sender, sender_name, content, timestamp, status, attachments
256	  `,
257	    )
258	    .get(channelJid) as QueuedMessage | undefined;
259	
260	  return row;
261	}
262	
263	export function markMessageDone(rowid: number): void {
264	  db.prepare(
265	    "update message_queue set status = 'done', processed_at = datetime('now') where rowid = ?",
266	  ).run(rowid);
267	}
268	
269	export function markMessageFailed(rowid: number): void {
270	  db.prepare(
271	    "update message_queue set status = 'failed', processed_at = datetime('now') where rowid = ?",
272	  ).run(rowid);
273	}
274	
275	export function clearPendingMessages(channelJid: string): number {
276	  const result = db
277	    .prepare("delete from message_queue where channel_jid = ? and status = 'pending'")
278	    .run(channelJid);
279	  return result.changes;
280	}
281	
282	export function recoverStuckMessages(): number {
283	  const result = db
284	    .prepare("update message_queue set status = 'pending' where status = 'processing'")
285	    .run();
286	  return result.changes;
287	}
288	
289	/** Get channels that have pending messages */
290	export function channelsWithPending(): string[] {
291	  const rows = db
292	    .prepare(
293	      `
294	    select channel_jid
295	    from message_queue
296	    where status = 'pending'
297	    group by channel_jid
298	    order by min(rowid) asc
299	  `,
300	    )
301	    .all() as any[];
302	  return rows.map((r) => r.channel_jid);
303	}
304	
305	// ── Scheduled tasks ──
306	
307	export function addScheduledTask(task: {
308	  name: string;
309	  type: ScheduledTaskType;
310	  schedule: string;
311	  channelJid: string;
312	  prompt: string;
313	  createdBy?: string;
314	  nextRunAt: string;
315	}): number {
316	  const result = db
317	    .prepare(
318	      `
319	    insert into scheduled_tasks (name, type, schedule, channel_jid, prompt, created_by, next_run_at)
320	    values (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
321	  `,
322	    )
323	    .run(
324	      task.name,
325	      task.type,
326	      task.schedule,
327	      task.channelJid,
328	      task.prompt,
329	      task.createdBy ?? '',
330	      normalizeTimestamp(task.nextRunAt),
331	    );
332	
333	  return Number(result.lastInsertRowid);
334	}
335	
336	export function removeScheduledTask(id: number): boolean {
337	  const result = db.prepare('delete from scheduled_tasks where id = ?').run(id);
338	  return result.changes > 0;
339	}
340	
341	export function enableScheduledTask(id: number): boolean {
342	  const result = db.prepare('update scheduled_tasks set enabled = 1 where id = ?').run(id);
343	  return result.changes > 0;
344	}
345	
346	export function disableScheduledTask(id: number): boolean {
347	  const result = db.prepare('update scheduled_tasks set enabled = 0 where id = ?').run(id);
348	  return result.changes > 0;
349	}
350	
351	export function listScheduledTasks(): ScheduledTaskRow[] {
352	  return db
353	    .prepare(
354	      `
355	    select id, name, type, schedule, channel_jid, prompt, enabled, last_run_at, next_run_at, created_at, created_by
356	    from scheduled_tasks
357	    order by id asc
358	  `,
359	    )
360	    .all() as ScheduledTaskRow[];
361	}
362	
363	export function getDueScheduledTasks(): ScheduledTaskRow[] {
364	  return db
365	    .prepare(
366	      `
367	    select id, name, type, schedule, channel_jid, prompt, enabled, last_run_at, next_run_at, created_at, created_by
368	    from scheduled_tasks
369	    where enabled = 1
370	      and next_run_at is not null
371	      and next_run_at <= datetime('now')
372	    order by next_run_at asc, id asc
373	  `,
374	    )
375	    .all() as ScheduledTaskRow[];
376	}

378	export function updateTaskAfterRun(id: number, lastRunAt: string, nextRunAt: string | null): void {
379	  db.prepare(
380	    `
381	    update scheduled_tasks
382	    set last_run_at = ?,
383	        next_run_at = ?,
384	        enabled = case when ? is null then 0 else enabled end
385	    where id = ?
386	  `,
387	  ).run(normalizeTimestamp(lastRunAt), normalizeTimestamp(nextRunAt), nextRunAt, id);
388	}
389	
390	export function enqueueScheduledTask(
391	  taskId: number,
392	  msg: {
393	    channelJid: string;
394	    sender: string;
395	    senderName: string;
396	    content: string;
397	    timestamp: string;
398	  },
399	  lastRunAt: string,
400	  nextRunAt: string | null,
401	): void {
402	  db.transaction(() => {
403	    enqueueMessage(msg);
404	    updateTaskAfterRun(taskId, lastRunAt, nextRunAt);
405	  })();
406	}

415	  );

 `./.specstory/references/Discord-OpenCode-Remote.md`

```text
1	# Discord OpenCode Remote
2	
3	This directory pins and deploys a managed Kimaki bot. Discord project channels
4	map to local working directories and threads map to isolated OpenCode sessions.
5	
6	## 架構與程式碼導覽
7	
8	這套服務不是從零重寫 Discord bot，而是以固定版本的
9	`kimaki@0.26.0` 作為 Discord／OpenCode 協調核心，再由本目錄補上可重現的
10	patch、安全隔離、常駐服務、健康檢查、部署與回滾。這個責任邊界很重要：
11	
12	- 本專案維護的是整合與營運層：`start-kimaki.sh`、`patch-kimaki.mjs`、
13	  `deploy.sh`、`healthcheck.mjs`、launchd 設定及資料庫整理工具。
14	- Discord 事件、OpenCode session 與回應分派的核心來自 Kimaki，安裝後位於
15	  `node_modules/kimaki/dist/`。
16	- 不直接手改安裝後的 `dist`；所有必要變更集中在 `patch-kimaki.mjs`，並在
17	  `npm install` 的 `postinstall` 階段重播。
18	- patch 只接受 `0.26.0`。上游版本不符時直接失敗，避免把舊 patch 靜默套到
19	  不相容的新程式碼。
20	
21	### 主要程式碼
22	
23	```text
24	Discord bot/
25	├── package.json                    # 鎖定 Kimaki 版本與 postinstall patch
26	├── start-kimaki.sh                 # 乾淨環境、驗證、隔離與啟動參數
27	├── patch-kimaki.mjs                # 本機功能及安全修補的唯一來源
28	├── deploy.sh / rollback.sh         # 原子部署與回滾
29	├── healthcheck.mjs / watchdog.sh   # 功能健康檢查與故障恢復
30	├── com.solomon.kimaki.plist        # macOS launchd 常駐服務
31	└── node_modules/kimaki/dist/
32	    ├── discord-bot.js              # Discord MessageCreate 與 thread 路由
33	    ├── opencode.js                 # 啟動 opencode serve、建立 SDK client
34	    ├── session-handler/
35	    │   ├── thread-session-runtime.js   # prompt、session、queue、event 分派
36	    │   └── global-event-listener.js    # OpenCode SSE 全域事件流
37	    └── discord-utils.js            # Discord Markdown 與 2,000 字分段
38	```
39	
40	### 執行拓樸
41	
42	```text
43	macOS launchd
44	  └─ start-kimaki.sh
45	      └─ Kimaki Node.js process
46	          ├─ discord.js Gateway / REST
47	          ├─ ~/.kimaki/discord-sessions.db
48	          ├─ localhost Hrana DB bridge
49	          └─ opencode serve（localhost 隨機 port）
50	              ├─ OpenCode HTTP JSON API
51	              ├─ /global/event SSE stream
52	              ├─ Kimaki OpenCode plugins
53	              └─ 隔離的 OpenCode XDG／SQLite 狀態
54	```
55	
56	所有專案共用一個本機 `opencode serve` process，但每次 SDK request 都帶入
57	工作目錄；Discord project channel 對應本機目錄，Discord thread 則對應一個
58	OpenCode session。
59	
60	### 一次訊息的完整路徑
61	
62	1. Discord Gateway 送出 `MessageCreate`，入口是
63	   `node_modules/kimaki/dist/discord-bot.js:331`。
64	2. Bot 依序檢查 guild allowlist、自己的訊息、channel 是否綁定本機專案，
65	   以及使用者的 owner／admin／Manage Server／`Kimaki` role 權限。
66	3. Project channel 的新訊息會建立 Discord thread；既有 thread 則載入原本的
67	   OpenCode session。對應關係持久化在 `discord-sessions.db`。
68	4. 前處理階段解析回覆內容、mention、文字附件、圖片、PDF 與語音訊息。
69	5. `thread-session-runtime.js:2291-2368` 將使用者文字、Discord metadata、
70	   system prompt、附件、agent 與 model 組成 OpenCode request。
71	6. `session.promptAsync(request)` 透過 OpenCode SDK 發出 HTTP request：
72	   `POST /session/{sessionID}/prompt_async`。
73	7. OpenCode 執行模型及工具，再由 `/global/event` 以 Server-Sent Events
74	   推送 session、文字與工具事件。
75	8. `global-event-listener.js:130-210` 維持一條全域 SSE 連線；每個 thread
76	   runtime 再依 session ID 過濾屬於自己的事件。
77	9. 完成的文字交給 `discord-utils.js:486-534`，保留 Markdown/code fence，
78	   並依 Discord 的 2,000 字限制分段送回原 thread。
79	
80	```text
81	Discord MessageCreate
82	        │
83	        ▼
84	guild／role／channel 權限檢查
85	        │
86	        ▼
87	Discord channel → 本機專案目錄
88	Discord thread  → OpenCode session
89	        │
90	        ▼
91	session.promptAsync() ── HTTP + JSON ──► opencode serve
92	        ▲                                      │
93	        │                                      │ model / tools
94	        └──── session events ◄──── SSE ─────────┘
95	        │
96	        ▼
97	Markdown 整理、2,000 字分段、送回 Discord thread
98	```
99	
100	### 關鍵程式片段
101	
102	Discord 訊息入口先做 admission control，而不是收到訊息就直接交給模型：
103	
104	```js
105	discordClient.on(Events.MessageCreate, async (message) => {
106	  if (!isAllowedGuildId(message.guildId)) return
107	  if (isSelfBotMessage && !isCliInjectedPrompt) return
108	
109	  const channelConfig = await getChannelDirectory(owningChannelId)
110	  if (!channelConfig) return
111	
112	  const member = await resolveGuildMessageMember(message)
113	  if (!hasKimakiBotPermission(member, message.guild)) return
114	
115	  // 通過檢查後才交給對應的 thread/session runtime。
116	})
117	```
118	
119	Kimaki 在本機啟動一個共用 OpenCode server，並以 project directory 建立 SDK
120	client。實作入口是 `node_modules/kimaki/dist/opencode.js:639-790`：
121	
122	```js
123	const serverProcess = spawn(spawnCommand, spawnArgs, {
124	  cwd: os.homedir(),
125	  env: {
126	    ...process.env,
127	    OPENCODE_CONFIG: opencodeConfigPath,
128	    OPENCODE_PORT: port.toString(),
129	    KIMAKI: "1",
130	  },
131	})
132	
133	const client = createOpencodeClient({
134	  baseUrl,
135	  directory,
136	  headers: getOpencodeServerAuthHeaders(),
137	})
138	```
139	
140	送給 OpenCode 的資料不只有聊天文字，也包含這次 Discord turn 的執行上下文：
141	
142	```js
143	const parts = [
144	  { type: "text", text: promptWithImagePaths },
145	  { type: "text", text: syntheticContext, synthetic: true },
146	  ...images,
147	]
148	
149	const request = {
150	  sessionID: session.id,
151	  directory: this.sdkDirectory,
152	  parts,
153	  system: getOpencodeSystemMessage({
154	    sessionId: session.id,
155	    channelId,
156	    guildId: this.thread.guildId,
157	    threadId: this.thread.id,
158	  }),
159	  ...(resolvedAgent ? { agent: resolvedAgent } : {}),
160	  ...(modelField ? { model: modelField } : {}),
161	}
162	
163	await waitForGlobalEventListener()
164	await getClient().session.promptAsync(request)
165	```
166	
167	回應不是解析 CLI stdout，而是訂閱 OpenCode 的 typed event stream：
168	
169	```js
170	const subscribeResult = await client.global.event({ signal })
171	
172	for await (const event of subscribeResult.stream) {
173	  dispatchEvent(event)
174	}
175	```
176	
177	SSE 中斷時會以 exponential backoff 重連，從 500 ms 增加至最多 30 秒。
178	
179	### Session、狀態與並行
180	
181	- 一個 Discord thread 通常對應一個 OpenCode session，因此對話可以跨訊息延續。
182	- 不同 thread 有獨立 runtime，可以並行執行；同一 thread 的狀態變更會序列化，
183	  避免 event、queue 與 session transition 互相踩資料。
184	- 完整 OpenCode 對話存放在隔離的 OpenCode SQLite；thread/session mapping、
185	  model 選擇及已送出的 part mapping 存放在 Kimaki SQLite。
186	- 已送出的 OpenCode part 會記錄其 Discord message mapping，重連後可避免重複傳送。
187	- 顯式的本機 per-thread queue 是記憶體狀態，process restart 後不保留；這是目前
188	  已知的恢復邊界。
189	
190	### 安全邊界
191	
192	- `start-kimaki.sh` 使用 `env -i` 建立環境變數白名單，避免 launchd 或互動 shell
193	  的任意變數滲入服務。
194	- OpenCode API 只監聽 localhost 隨機 port，並要求私有 Basic Auth credential。
195	- Bot 使用固定 Discord guild allowlist，channel 還必須存在本機 project mapping。
196	- `--restrict-directories` 讓模型離開目前專案前必須取得額外許可。
197	- Bot 的 OpenCode XDG 目錄與桌面／Tailscale OpenCode 完全分離；啟動器拒絕
198	  symlink，並檢查 `opencode.db`、WAL、SHM 是否與共用實例指向相同 inode。
199	- `umask 077`、目錄 `0700` 及 credential `0600` 限制其他本機帳號讀取狀態。
200	- `--no-analytics`、`--no-critique` 與 `--no-auto-upgrade` 分別關閉產品分析、
201	  外部 diff critique，以及未經測試的自動升級。
202	
203	這不是 sandbox。獲授權的 Discord 使用者能透過 `!` 或 `/run-shell-command`
204	執行此 macOS 帳號可執行的 shell command；因此 Discord 帳號、server role 與
205	bot token 都必須視為主機存取憑證。
206	
207	### 給工程師的一句話
208	
209	這是一個以 Kimaki 作為 transport 與 session orchestration core 的 Discord
210	遠端 OpenCode runtime：本專案釘死上游版本，透過可重播 patch 客製行為，再補上
211	guild allowlist、XDG／SQLite 隔離、localhost Basic Auth、launchd supervision、
212	functional health check、原子部署與 rollback。
213	
214	## Runtime
215	
216	- Kimaki: `0.26.0`
217	- Sharp security override: `0.35.3`
218	- Node.js: `24.15.0`
219	- Bun: `1.3.12`
220	- OpenCode: `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`
221	- Kimaki state and Discord credentials: `~/.kimaki/`
222	- Kimaki OpenCode state: `~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/opencode/`
223	- Default Discord model: `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol`
224	
225	The launcher uses `umask 077`, so newly created credentials and logs default to
226	owner-only access.
227	
228	Install dependencies:
229	
230	```sh
231	npm install
232	```
233	
234	Start the interactive setup or run the configured bot:
235	
236	```sh
237	./start-kimaki.sh
238	```
239	
240	The launcher intentionally enables:
241	
242	- `--restrict-directories`: ask before leaving the active project.
243	- `--no-critique`: do not upload diffs to an external review service.
244	- `--no-analytics`: disable Kimaki product analytics.
245	- `--no-auto-upgrade`: keep the tested version pinned.
246	
247	It does not enable `--allow-all-users`. Initially, only the owner of the private
248	Discord server should have access.
249	
250	The runtime also enforces a fixed guild allowlist. Being a Discord server owner
251	or administrator is not sufficient unless the server ID is explicitly allowed.
252	The health endpoint becomes unhealthy when no allowlisted server is connected.
253	The localhost OpenCode API requires a private Basic Auth credential, and its
254	database retains only sessions referenced by Discord threads or scheduled work.
255	
256	## Discord Setup
257	
258	1. Create a private Discord server used only for this bot.
259	2. Open <https://discord.com/developers/applications> and create an application.
260	3. In **Bot**, enable **Message Content Intent**.
261	4. Reset and copy the bot token when the Kimaki setup wizard requests it.
262	5. Never paste the token into Discord, this repository, or an OpenCode prompt.
263	6. Use the install URL printed by Kimaki to add the bot to the private server.
264	
265	## Projects
266	
267	Register the two initial project directories after onboarding:
268	
269	```sh
270	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/Skill training"
271	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/every thing can be quant/第一性原理/不再被騙系統"
272	```
273	
274	Kimaki creates one Discord channel per directory. Switch project by switching
275	channel; start a separate task by posting a new channel message. Continue a task
276	inside its thread.
277	
278	This installation applies a version-checked local patch after `npm install`.
279	Discord's `/add-project` can accept an absolute path, browse a path prefix, or
280	search folder names under the home directory and mounted volumes. Projects are
281	created only when requested; subfolders are not pre-created as channels.
282	The command and its autocomplete can be used from any channel in the allowed
283	private server, including a channel that is not yet linked to a project.
284	
285	Examples in Discord's `/add-project` field:
286	
287	- `TOEIC`: search matching folder names.
288	- `/Users/solomon/`: browse folders in the home directory.
289	- `/Volumes/`: browse mounted disks.
290	- `/absolute/path/to/folder`: use an exact directory as the project root.
291	
292	Folder choices end in `/`. Select a folder, then reopen the `project` field to
293	browse its children. Submit at any level to create that folder's project channel.
294	One- or two-character searches use fast top-level matching; longer searches add
295	Spotlight results. If deep search times out, top-level matches remain available.
296	
297	## Background Service
298	
299	`com.solomon.kimaki.plist` is installed under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It
300	starts Kimaki when this macOS user logs in and restarts it after failures. Logs
301	are written to `~/.kimaki/launchd.log` and `~/.kimaki/launchd-error.log`.
302	
303	The deployed runtime is isolated from this Git working tree under
304	`~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/releases/`. `current` points at the active
305	release and `previous` provides rollback. Deploy a verified release with:
306	
307	```sh
308	./deploy.sh
309	```
310	
311	The watchdog checks Kimaki, Discord, and OpenCode every five minutes. It only
312	restarts after two consecutive failures and rotates each service log at 10 MB.
313	The OpenCode check performs a real session query instead of trusting the shallow
314	global health endpoint.
315	
316	Management commands:
317	
318	```sh
319	kimaki-remote status
320	kimaki-remote restart
321	kimaki-remote logs
322	kimaki-remote doctor
323	kimaki-remote deploy
324	kimaki-remote rollback
325	```
326	
327	Switch from the shared Gateway bot to your own Discord application with:
328	
329	```sh
330	kimaki-remote setup-self-hosted
331	```
332	
333	The command validates the Bot token before downtime, backs up the database,
334	accepts the token using hidden terminal input, opens the authorization URL, and
335	verifies functional health before finishing. `kimaki-remote use-gateway` only
336	stops the current Bot after confirming that saved Gateway credentials exist.
337	
338	Do not run two writing sessions concurrently against `Skill training`: its
339	workflow pulls, commits, and pushes at the end of each training round.
340	
341	## Security Boundary
342	
343	A user who can operate Kimaki can run shell commands on this Mac through `!` or
344	`/run-shell-command`. Treat the Discord account, server owner role, `Kimaki`
345	role, and bot token as machine-access credentials.
346	
347	Keep the existing Tailscale OpenCode service as a fallback. Kimaki starts its
348	own localhost OpenCode server on a separate random port and separate XDG data
349	directory. It never shares `opencode.db`, WAL, or SHM files with the desktop or
350	Tailscale service on port `4096`.
351
```

```text
1	# pi-chat
2	
3	A pi extension that bridges Discord and Telegram channels to a sandboxed pi session. Each connected channel gets its own [Gondolin](https://github.com/earendil-works/gondolin) micro-VM with persistent workspace, shared storage, memory, and skills.
4	
5	## Quick Start
6	
7	```bash
8	# Install
9	pi install /path/to/pi-chat
10	# or
11	pi -e /path/to/pi-chat
12	
13	# Configure accounts and channels
14	/chat-config
15	
16	# Connect
17	/chat-connect
18	```
19	
20	### Requirements
21	
22	- [QEMU](https://www.qemu.org/) installed (`brew install qemu` on macOS)
23	- Gondolin guest image (downloaded automatically on first connect)
24	- A Discord bot token or Telegram bot token
25	- `tmux` for multi-channel worker orchestration
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Features
30	
31	- **Discord server channels** and **Telegram DMs/groups**
32	- **Gondolin VM sandbox** per connection — tools run inside an isolated Alpine Linux micro-VM
33	- **Persistent workspace** and **shared storage** across sessions
34	- **Streamed preview** responses with edit-in-place
35	- **Reply-to-trigger** — bot replies are attached to the triggering message
36	- **Durable memory** — account-wide and channel-specific memory files
37	- **Skills** — agent-created reusable tools, auto-discovered and injected into the prompt
38	- **Encrypted secret exchange** — securely pass credentials via browser-based encryption
39	- **Remote control** — stop, compact, new session, and status via chat commands
40	- **Chat history** tool for searching older messages
41	- **File attachments** — send and receive files between chat and the VM
42	
43	---
44	
45	## Setup
46	
47	### Discord
48	
49	1. Create a bot at [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
50	2. Enable **Message Content Intent** under Bot settings
51	3. Run `/chat-config` → Create account → Discord
52	4. Enter your bot token
53	5. Invite the bot to a server (the setup flow provides the invite URL)
54	6. Select a server and configure channels
55	
56	### Telegram
57	
58	1. Create a bot via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)
59	2. Run `/chat-config` → Create account → Telegram
60	3. Enter your bot token
61	4. Add DMs or groups through the guided setup
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Commands
66	
67	| Command | Description |
68	|---------|-------------|
69	| `/chat-config` | Configure accounts, channels, and secrets |
70	| `/chat-connect` | Connect to a configured channel |
71	| `/chat-disconnect` | Disconnect the current channel |
72	| `/chat-status` | Show connection status, model, usage, context |
73	| `/chat-list` | List configured channels |
74	| `/chat-spawn-all` | Spawn every configured channel in detached tmux/pi sessions |
75	| `/chat-spawn-all --restart` | Restart those tmux/pi sessions |
76	| `/chat-workers` | Show managed tmux/pi worker status |
77	| `/chat-open-all` | Open running workers in a tiled tmux dashboard |
78	| `/chat-kill-all` | Kill all managed tmux/pi workers |
79	| `/chat-new` | Start a new pi session, keeping the chat connection |
80	
81	Workers also write status snapshots every 15 seconds under `~/.pi/agent/chat/worker-status/`. The `chat_workers` tool exposes the same status to an orchestrating pi agent.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## Remote Control
86	
87	Users in the connected chat can send these commands (with or without mentioning the bot):
88	
89	| Command | Effect |
90	|---------|--------|
91	| `stop` | Abort the current turn |
92	| `status` | Show model, usage, context stats |
93	| `compact` | Trigger context compaction |
94	| `new` | Start a new pi session |
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Storage Layout
99	
100	Everything lives under `~/.pi/agent/chat/`:
101	
102	```
103	~/.pi/agent/chat/
104	├── config.json                          # Accounts, channels, secrets
105	├── cache/                               # Discovery cache
106	└── accounts/<account>/
107	    ├── shared/                          # Mounted as /shared in VM
108	    │   ├── memory.md                    # Account-wide persistent memory
109	    │   └── skills/                      # Account-wide skills
110	    └── channels/<channel>/
111	        ├── channel.jsonl                # Chat log
112	        ├── .lock                        # Runtime lock
113	        ├── workspace/                   # Mounted as /workspace in VM
114	        │   ├── memory.md                # Channel-specific persistent memory
115	        │   ├── skills/                  # Channel-specific skills
116	        │   ├── incoming/                # Downloaded attachments
117	        │   ├── .secrets/                # Encrypted secrets
118	        │   └── SYSTEM.md                # Environment modification log
119	        └── gondolin/                    # VM state
120	            └── session.json
121	```
122	
123	---
124	
125	## VM Environment
126	
127	Each connection starts a Gondolin micro-VM with:
128	
129	- **Alpine Linux** with bash pre-installed
130	- `/workspace` → channel workspace directory
131	- `/shared` → account shared directory
132	- Tools: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`
133	- All outbound HTTP/TLS open by default
134	
135	The agent sees `/workspace` as its working directory.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Memory
140	
141	Two persistent memory files, injected into the system prompt on every turn:
142	
143	| File | VM Path | Scope |
144	|------|---------|-------|
145	| Account memory | `/shared/memory.md` | Shared across all channels for this account |
146	| Channel memory | `/workspace/memory.md` | Specific to this channel |
147	
148	The agent is instructed to write durable facts and preferences to these files when asked to remember something. Account-wide goes to `/shared/memory.md`, channel-specific to `/workspace/memory.md`.
149	
150	---
151	
152	## Skills
153	
154	The agent can create reusable tools as skills, following the [Agent Skills standard](https://agentskills.io):
155	
156	- **Account-wide:** `/shared/skills/`
157	- **Channel-specific:** `/workspace/skills/`
158	
159	A skill is either a single `.md` file (e.g. `skills/foo.md`) or a directory with `SKILL.md` plus supporting files (e.g. `skills/foo/SKILL.md`, `skills/foo/run.sh`).
160	
161	Each skill needs YAML frontmatter:
162	
163	```yaml
164	---
165	name: skill-name
166	description: Short description of what this skill does
167	---
168	```
169	
170	Skills are automatically discovered and listed in the system prompt. The agent reads the full skill file before using it.
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Secrets
175	
176	### Config Secrets (Gondolin HTTP hooks)
177	
178	Configure secrets at three levels via `/chat-config`:
179	
180	- **Global** — shared across all accounts
181	- **Per account** — shared across channels of that account
182	- **Per channel** — specific to one channel
183	
184	Each secret has a value and allowed host patterns. Gondolin replaces placeholder env vars with real values only for outbound HTTP requests to allowed hosts. The agent never sees the real secret value.
185	
186	### Runtime Secrets (encrypted exchange)
187	
188	For credentials the agent needs at runtime (API keys for skills, OAuth files, etc.):
189	
190	1. Agent calls the `chat_request_secret` tool
191	2. A link to `pi.dev/secret` is sent to the chat with an embedded public key
192	3. User clicks, pastes the secret, and gets an encrypted blob
193	4. User pastes the blob back into chat
194	5. pi-chat decrypts it (RSA-OAEP + AES-256-GCM) and stores it at `/workspace/.secrets/<name>`
195	6. Agent is notified and can use the file
196	
197	The encrypted blob is useless without the ephemeral private key held in pi-chat's memory.
198	
199	---
200	
201	## Tools
202	
203	| Tool | Description |
204	|------|-------------|
205	| `read` | Read files (routed through Gondolin VM) |
206	| `write` | Create/overwrite files |
207	| `edit` | Precise in-place edits |
208	| `bash` | Execute commands (runs `/bin/bash` in the VM) |
209	| `chat_history` | Search older messages from the chat log |
210	| `chat_attach` | Queue files to send with the next reply |
211	| `chat_request_secret` | Request a secret from the user via encrypted exchange |
212	
213	---
214	
215	## Credits
216	
217	pi-chat includes vendored/adapted logic inspired by [Vercel Chat SDK](https://github.com/vercel/ai) (MIT):
218	
219	- `src/render/format.ts`
220	- `src/render/streaming-markdown.ts`
221	- `src/render/streaming.ts`
222	
223	---
224	
225	## License
226	
227	MIT
228
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `/tmp/pi-im-doc-review/piscord/README.md`

```text
1	<p align="center">
2	  <img src="https://img.coly.cc/obs-img/2025/10/a3a76006fd9279cc3559b6854f9335fc.png" width="600" alt="piscord">
3	</p>
4	
5	<h1 align="center">Piscord</h1>
6	
7	<p align="center">
8	  <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/piscord"><img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/v/piscord" alt="npm version"></a>
9	  <img src="https://img.shields.io/npm/l/piscord" alt="license">
10	  <img src="https://img.shields.io/node/v/piscord" alt="node version">
11	  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-linux%20%7C%20macos%20%7C%20windows-blue" alt="platform">
12	</p>
13	
14	A lightweight Discord gateway for [pi coding agent](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono). SQLite-backed queue, per-channel session isolation, crash recovery, abort support. One command to set up, runs as a daemon, never drops a message.
15	
16	**Latest release:** see the npm version badge above and [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md) for details.
17	
18	```bash
19	npm install -g piscord
20	piscord setup                 # interactive wizard -- walks you through everything
21	```
22	
23	That's it. The setup wizard checks prerequisites, asks for your Discord bot token, lets you pick a channel policy, and optionally installs + starts a background service. Your bot is live in under a minute.
24	
25	## Prerequisites
26	
27	- **Node.js** ≥ 20
28	- **Linux, macOS, or Windows**
29	- **[pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono)** ≥ 0.74.0 installed and on `PATH`, with login completed (`~/.pi/agent/auth.json`)
30	- **Discord bot token** — [create one here](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
31	  - Enable **Message Content Intent** under Privileged Gateway Intents
32	  - Bot permissions: `Send Messages`, `Read Message History`, `View Channels`, `Attach Files`
33	
34	## Features
35	
36	- **Bridges to your existing `pi`** — shells out to the `pi` binary and reuses your login + model access
37	- **Per-channel sessions** — each Discord channel gets its own persistent conversation history
38	- **Per-channel working directories** — optionally override `PI_CWD` for specific channels without changing the global default
39	- **Channel access policy** — `open` (all channels), `open-trigger` (all channels, @mention required), or `allowlist` (manual registration only)
40	- **SQLite message queue** — survives crashes, auto-recovers stuck messages
41	- **Concurrency control** — per-channel serial processing + configurable global limit
42	- **DM auto-registration** — direct messages work out of the box
43	- **Discord slash commands** — `/pi status`, `/pi model`, `/pi thinking`, `/pi new`, `/pi stop`
44	- **Abort command** — `/pi stop` terminates the running task and clears queued messages
45	- **Attachment relay** — Discord file uploads are downloaded and passed to `pi` by local path so agents can inspect or convert any supported file type without flooding context
46	- **Message and file sending** — `piscord send` lets pi send plain text, files, or both to any Discord channel
47	- **Scheduled tasks** — cron or one-time tasks that trigger pi sessions on schedule
48	- **Archive auto-cleanup** — archived sessions are cleaned up after a configurable retention period
49	- **Cross-platform** — runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows with platform-aware defaults
50	- **Typing indicators** — shows "bot is typing" while `pi` processes
51	- **Message splitting** — handles Discord's 2000-character limit automatically
52	- **Daemon management** — systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS
53	- **Platform-aware paths** — XDG on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows
54	
55	## How It Works
56	
57	```
58	Discord ──discord.js──→ Gateway ──pi subprocess──→ Pi Agent
59	                           │                          │
60	                         SQLite                  Session dirs
61	                      (message queue)           (per channel)
62	```
63	
64	The gateway **does not embed or replace `pi`**. It finds and runs your installed `pi`:
65	
66	1. **Binary discovery** — uses `PI_BIN` config or finds `pi` in `PATH`
67	2. **Auth reuse** — `pi` reads its own `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` when invoked
68	3. **Model catalog** — the gateway imports the pi SDK to populate slash command autocomplete
69	4. **Invocation** — each message is processed as `pi --session-dir <dir> --continue -p <message>`
70	
71	## Channel Policy
72	
73	During setup you pick one of three policies. This controls how the bot interacts with server channels:
74	
75	| Policy         | Behavior                                                               |
76	| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
77	| `open`         | All guild channels auto-register on first message. No @mention needed. |
78	| `open-trigger` | All guild channels auto-register, but only respond when @mentioned.    |
79	| `allowlist`    | Only manually registered channels are active.                          |
80	
81	- DMs always auto-register when `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS=true` (the default).
82	- Use `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS` to block specific channels from auto-registration in `open` / `open-trigger` mode.
83	
84	If you chose `allowlist`, register channels manually:
85	
86	```bash
87	piscord register [REDACTED:discord-client-id] "my-server #general" --no-trigger
88	piscord register [REDACTED:discord-client-id] "my-server #general" --cwd /srv/repos/app
89	```
90	
91	Re-running `piscord register` with `--cwd` updates that channel's working directory override. If no override is set, the gateway uses the global `PI_CWD`.
92	
93	## Slash Commands
94	
95	The gateway registers a global `/pi` command on Discord:
96	
97	| Subcommand        | Description                                                        |
98	| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
99	| `/pi status`      | Show model, thinking, working directory, session info, token usage |
100	| `/pi model`       | Set the channel's model (autocomplete from pi's available models)  |
101	| `/pi reset-model` | Clear the channel's model override                                 |
102	| `/pi thinking`    | Set thinking level: off / minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh    |
103	| `/pi new`         | Start a fresh session for this channel                             |
104	| `/pi stop`        | Abort the current task and clear queued messages                   |
105	
106	`/pi model` reads the catalog from the configured `PI_BIN`, so it stays in sync when pi adds or removes models. It also honors pi's `enabledModels` setting (configured through `/scoped-models`), including model order and glob patterns. If no scope is configured, it shows all available models.
107	
108	## Tools for Pi
109	
110	The gateway exposes two capabilities through its CLI that **pi itself can invoke**. You don't type these commands in your terminal — you just tell pi in Discord, and it handles the rest.
111	
112	For example, you can say to pi:
113	
114	> _"Create a daily task at 9am UTC that generates a summary report"_
115	> _"Send me report.pdf with a message saying here you go"_
116	> _"Set a one-time reminder for the 2pm meeting today"_
117	
118	pi will run the appropriate `piscord task` or `piscord send` command behind the scenes.
119	
120	### Scheduled tasks
121	
122	pi can schedule cron-based or one-time prompts through the gateway's scheduler. Tasks are injected into the normal message queue, so they use the channel's configured model, thinking level, and working directory.
123	
124	Under the hood, pi runs commands like:
125	
126	```bash
127	piscord task add \
128	  --name "daily-report" \
129	  --schedule "0 9 * * *" \
130	  --channel dc:123456789 \
131	  --prompt "Generate today's summary report"
132	
133	piscord task add \
134	  --name "meeting-reminder" \
135	  --schedule "2026-04-05T14:00:00Z" \
136	  --channel dc:123456789 \
137	  --prompt "Remind Colin about the 2pm meeting" \
138	  --once
139	```
140	
141	The `--schedule` value uses standard 5-field cron syntax (`minute hour day month weekday`). For one-time tasks, add `--once` and pass an ISO 8601 datetime.
142	
143	**Task management** — also available via pi:
144	
145	```bash
146	piscord task list              # List all tasks
147	piscord task disable <id>      # Pause
148	piscord task enable <id>       # Resume
149	piscord task remove <id>       # Delete
150	```
151	
152	### Sending messages and files to Discord
153	
154	pi can send plain text messages, files, or both to any Discord channel using the gateway's built-in relay.
155	
156	When you ask pi to send something, it runs commands like:
157	
158	```bash
159	piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --text "hello"
160	piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --file /path/to/report.pdf --text "Here's the report"
161	piscord send --channel dc:123456789 --file chart.png --file data.csv
162	```
163	
164	- `--text` works on its own
165	- Up to 10 files per message (Discord limit)
166	- Respects `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` per file
167	- Works independently — no running gateway daemon required
168	
169	## Daemon Management
170	
171	The setup wizard offers to install a background service automatically. You can also manage it manually:
172	
173	```bash
174	piscord daemon install   # Generate + enable service
175	piscord daemon start     # Start
176	piscord daemon status    # Check status
177	piscord daemon logs      # Tail log output
178	piscord daemon stop      # Stop
179	piscord daemon uninstall # Remove the service
180	```
181	
182	- **Linux** — uses a systemd user service
183	- **macOS** — uses a launchd user agent
184	- **Windows** — daemon management is not yet supported; run `piscord start` in a terminal or use Task Scheduler manually
185	
186	> **Headless Linux servers**: enable user lingering so the service runs without an active login session:
187	>
188	> ```bash
189	> sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER
190	> ```
191	
192	## Configuration Reference
193	
194	Config file location depends on your OS (see Data Locations). On Linux: `~/.config/pi-discord-gateway/config.env`
195	
196	Most users won't need to edit this file directly — `piscord setup` generates it for you. If you do want to tweak advanced settings, you can edit the file manually, or ask your pi to configure it for you. Run `piscord status` to see the config path on your system.
197	
198	| Variable                     | Default                         | Description                                                                |
199	| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
200	| `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`          | _(required)_                    | Discord bot token                                                          |
201	| `PI_BIN`                     | `pi`                            | Path to pi binary                                                          |
202	| `PI_MODEL`                   | _(none)_                        | Default model override                                                     |
203	| `PI_THINKING`                | _(none)_                        | Default thinking level                                                     |
204	| `PI_CWD`                     | `$HOME`                         | Default working directory for pi; can be overridden per registered channel |
205	| `PI_EXTRA_FLAGS`             | _(none)_                        | Extra flags passed to pi                                                   |
206	| `TRIGGER_NAME`               | `pi`                            | Bot trigger name for @mentions                                             |
207	| `CHANNEL_POLICY`             | `open`                          | Channel access: `open`, `open-trigger`, or `allowlist`                     |
208	| `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS`          | _(none)_                        | Comma-separated channel IDs to exclude from auto-registration              |
209	| `MAX_CONCURRENCY`            | `3`                             | Max parallel pi invocations                                                |
210	| `MAX_SCHEDULED_CONCURRENCY`  | `1`                             | Max scheduled tasks enqueued per tick                                      |
211	| `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`           | `1000`                          | Queue poll interval (ms)                                                   |
212	| `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS`        | `15000`                         | Graceful shutdown timeout (ms)                                             |
213	| `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS`          | `true`                          | Auto-register DM channels                                                  |
214	| `ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS`     | `30`                            | Days to keep archived sessions (0 = never clean)                           |
215	| `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`       | `26214400`                      | Max size per attachment (0 = no limit)                                     |
216	| `MAX_TOTAL_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` | `52428800`                      | Max combined attachment size (0 = no limit)                                |
217	| `MEDIA_RETENTION_HOURS`      | `168`                           | Hours to keep downloaded attachment files for path-based agent access      |
218	| `SESSIONS_DIR`               | _(platform default)_/sessions   | Session storage directory (see Data Locations)                             |
219	| `DB_PATH`                    | _(platform default)_/gateway.db | SQLite database path (see Data Locations)                                  |
220	| `LOG_LEVEL`                  | `info`                          | Log level: debug/info/warn/error                                           |
221	
222	After changing config, restart the service: `piscord daemon stop && piscord daemon start`
223	
224	## CLI Reference
225	
226	```
227	piscord setup [token]                         Interactive setup wizard
228	piscord start                                 Start gateway (foreground)
229	piscord status                                Show diagnostics
230	
231	piscord channels                              List registered channels
232	piscord register <id> <name> [options]        Register a channel
233	piscord unregister <id>                       Unregister a channel
234	
235	piscord send --channel <jid> [--text <msg>] [--file <path> ...]
236	
237	piscord task add --name <n> --schedule <cron|iso> --channel <jid> --prompt <text> [--once]
238	piscord task list | remove <id> | enable <id> | disable <id>
239	
240	piscord archive list                          List archived sessions
241	piscord archive cleanup [--dry-run]           Clean up expired archived sessions
242	
243	piscord daemon install | uninstall | start | stop | status | logs
244	
245	piscord help                                  Show help
246	```
247	
248	### Register options
249	
250	| Flag              | Effect                                        |
251	| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
252	| `--no-trigger`    | Respond to all messages (not just @mentions)  |
253	| `--main`          | Mark as main channel (implies `--no-trigger`) |
254	| `--folder <name>` | Custom session folder name                    |
255	| `--cwd <path>`    | Override `PI_CWD` for this channel only       |
256	
257	## Data Locations
258	
259	Paths are platform-aware. Defaults by OS:
260	
261	| Item     | Linux                                       | macOS                                                      | Windows                                     |
262	| -------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
263	| Config   | `~/.config/pi-discord-gateway/config.env`   | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/config.env` | `%APPDATA%\piscord-gateway\config.env`      |
264	| Database | `~/.local/share/piscord-gateway/gateway.db` | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/gateway.db` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\piscord-gateway\gateway.db` |
265	| Sessions | `~/.local/share/piscord-gateway/sessions/`  | `~/Library/Application Support/piscord-gateway/sessions/`  | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\piscord-gateway\sessions\`  |
266	| pi auth  | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                     | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                                    | `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`                     |
267	
268	## Alternative Installation
269	
270	### npx (quick trial, no global install)
271	
272	```bash
273	npx piscord@latest setup
274	```
275	
276	### From source
277	
278	```bash
279	git clone https://github.com/Crokily/pi-discord-gateway.git
280	cd pi-discord-gateway
281	npm install && npm run build
282	node dist/cli/index.js setup
283	```
284	
285	## Troubleshooting
286	
287	<details>
288	<summary><strong>pi not found in PATH</strong></summary>
289	
290	`piscord status` shows "Pi binary: not found".
291	
292	- Check `pi --version` works in the same shell
293	- Set `PI_BIN=/full/path/to/pi` in config.env
294	- Restart: `piscord daemon stop && piscord daemon start`
295	</details>
296	
297	<details>
298	<summary><strong>Missing auth.json</strong></summary>
299	
300	`piscord status` shows "Pi auth: missing".
301	
302	- Run `pi` and complete the login flow
303	- Confirm `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` exists for the same user running the gateway
304	</details>
305	
306	<details>
307	<summary><strong>Daemon service won't start</strong></summary>
308	
309	- `piscord daemon status` — check for errors
310	- `piscord daemon logs` — see log output
311	- **Linux**: for headless servers, run `sudo loginctl enable-linger $USER`
312	- **macOS**: check `~/Library/Logs/piscord-gateway/` for launchd output
313	</details>
314	
315	<details>
316	<summary><strong>Bot is online but doesn't respond</strong></summary>
317	
318	- `open` policy: check `EXCLUDED_CHANNELS` doesn't include your channel
319	- `allowlist` policy: run `piscord channels` — at least one channel must be registered
320	- For trigger-only channels: mention the bot by name or use `@TriggerName`
321	- DMs auto-register when `AUTO_REGISTER_DMS=true`
322	</details>
323	
324	## Development
325	
326	```bash
327	npm install
328	npm run dev          # Start with tsx (no build needed)
329	npm run build        # Compile TypeScript
330	npm test             # Run Vitest suite
331	```
332	
333	## Security
334	
335	- Protect `config.env` — it contains your Discord bot token
336	- Anyone who can message a registered channel can spend your pi usage
337	- Review attachment size limits before exposing the bot
338	- Run the service as a normal user, not root
