```text
1	# Sessions and handoff
2	
3	Configuration can be copied safely; live session files cannot. `pia` therefore
4	separates normal history, same-engine forks, and cross-harness handoffs into
5	three explicit operations.
6	
7	## Session isolation
8	
9	An isolated combo stores history below:
10	
11	```text
12	${PIA_STATE_HOME:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents}/
13	  sessions/<engine>/<combo-name>/<project-key>/
14	```
15	
16	With `history.mode: shared`, the leaf instead uses:
17	
18	```text
19	sessions/<engine>/shared/<group>/<project-key>/
20	```
21	
22	The project key is derived from the canonical working directory. Thus two
23	projects do not accidentally resume one another, and a shared group never
24	crosses the Pi/OMP boundary. Use `pia sessions <combo>` to inspect the sessions
25	available under the combo's effective policy.
26	
27	## Same-engine forks
28	
29	```sh
30	pia fork pi/base pi/research --latest -- <target arguments>
31	pia fork pi/base pi/research --session <id-or-path> -- <target arguments>
32	```
33	
34	The first two arguments are source and target combo IDs. Forking is allowed
35	only when both use the same engine. `--latest` selects the newest source session;
36	`--session` accepts an unambiguous session-ID prefix from the source combo's
37	effective session root, or an explicit absolute path.
38	
39	`pia` delegates to the target harness's native `--fork` behavior and creates a
40	new target session; it does not append to or byte-copy the source session. Use a
41	fork when the target should retain the native conversation tree and both sides
42	understand exactly the same session format.
43	
44	Although both snapshots use a session format identified as version 3, they are
45	not wire-compatible. OMP includes a title slot and additional entry types, so
46	raw cross-harness session sharing is prohibited. See the pinned
47	[Pi session loader](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/853a80d26c90a14c1886f0ebb8ffaae133ca2185/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts#L548-L553)
48	and [OMP session format](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/51f03804476c3fd3c15748ae07e4849d1efc883b/docs/session.md#L61-L66).
49	
50	## Deterministic handoff
51	
52	```sh
53	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --latest \
54	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" -- <target arguments>
55	```
56	
57	Handoff supports same- or cross-engine transfer. It reads the selected source
58	session without changing it and produces a private Markdown artifact under
59	`$PIA_STATE_HOME/handoffs/`. Generation is local and deterministic; it does not
60	ask another model to summarise the transcript.
61	
62	The extractor:
63	
64	1. Prefers the newest compaction summary; if none exists, keeps the first user
65	   goal and a bounded set of recent messages.
66	2. Adds source, target, and session provenance, canonical working directory,
67	   Git branch, `HEAD`, status, and diff-stat.
68	3. Excludes hidden thinking, images, tool arguments, and successful tool
69	   output. Failed tool output is capped at 2 KiB.
70	4. Caps the document at 128 KiB and reports omitted or truncated blocks.
71	5. Runs the agent-history-hygiene redactor, then validates with `gitleaks`.
72	   Any redaction or validation failure aborts the handoff.
73	6. Writes the artifact with mode `0600` on POSIX (or the containing user ACL on
74	   Windows) and starts a fresh target session with it as the first attachment.
75	
76	Use `--session <id-or-absolute-path>` instead of `--latest` to select
77	explicitly. `--max-bytes N` can lower or raise the 128 KiB default (minimum
78	4096). Use `--no-run` to generate the document without launching the target:
79	
80	```sh
81	pia handoff pi/research omp/base --session <id-or-path> \
82	  --goal "Continue the provider comparison" --no-run
83	```
84	
85	Review the generated file before sharing it outside the machine. Redaction is a
86	fail-closed safety boundary, not a promise that arbitrary prose contains no
87	sensitive business context.
88	
89	Malformed session data, a missing source session, Git provenance failure in the
90	current project, an unavailable redactor or `gitleaks`, and an oversized/unsafe
91	artifact all fail before target launch. `pia doctor` checks the required helper
92	commands.
93
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Evaluate declarative combo inheritance
2	
3	**Status**: P?
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` · `docs/architecture.md` · `docs/combos.md`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Deferred on 2026-08-30 in favor of complete copied configs with lineage
10	metadata. Inheritance looks attractive for `base -> language -> domain`
11	families, but defining merge, deletion, ordering, validation, and conflict rules
12	before real usage would add a second configuration language without evidence it
13	is needed.
14	
15	## Current findings
16	
17	- `pia derive` copies a complete parent and records `derivedFrom` plus a parent
18	  digest. Parent changes warn; the child never changes until a human reviews it.
19	- `pia diff --parent` and `pia lineage --ack` provide a deliberately manual
20	  update loop with no hidden launch-time composition.
21	- OMP has native layers, while Pi and individual resource types expose
22	  different composition behavior. A wrapper-level merge could therefore be
23	  surprising even if it works for simple settings objects.
24	- Three-way sync could preserve child edits better than re-copying, but needs a
25	  durable base snapshot and precise treatment of arrays, renames, deletes,
26	  executable modes, and conflicts.
27	
28	## Options to compare
29	
30	| Option | Benefit | Cost/risk |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| Keep copy + digest acknowledgement | Explicit, portable, easy to debug | Repeated manual updates |
33	| Declarative `extends` materialised at apply | Compact child definitions | Merge semantics become a public API |
34	| Three-way sync command | Preserves independent child edits | Complex conflict/base storage and recovery |
35	
36	## Open questions
37	
38	- How often do parent changes need to propagate, and how many files are
39	  repeatedly copied in practice?
40	- Are conflicts mostly structured settings, or arbitrary prompts, skills, and
41	  executable assets?
42	- Should inheritance be engine-neutral or defer to each harness's native
43	  mechanisms?
44	- Can every effective combo still be inspected, exported, and reproduced
45	  without running an opaque merge?
46	
47	## Exit criteria
48	
49	- At least three meaningful derived combos and two parent-update events have
50	  been maintained with the copy workflow.

```text
1	# Tag schema (priority × effort)
2	
3	Two orthogonal axes prevent the "important but unimplementable" trap:
4	
5	## Priority
6	
7	- `P1` — likely next batch (you'd reach for this if you sat down today)
8	- `P2` — worth doing, no rush
9	- `P3` — someday / nice-to-have
10	- `P?` — needs evaluation first; spike before committing to a priority
11	
12	## Effort
13	
14	- `S` — under an hour
15	- `M` — half day
16	- `L` — multi-day
17	- `XL` — architectural; design doc required before code
18	
19	## Useful combinations
20	
21	- `P?` + `[?/L]` — explicit "unknown of size L"; the most honest tag
22	- `P3` + `[S]` — "small enough to slip into any free moment"
23	- `P1` + `[XL]` — warns "you said this is urgent but it's actually huge — re-scope"
24	
25	## Heading and item syntax (validator-checked)
26	
27	The bundled `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` enforces this exact form. If you change
28	the syntax, update the script in the same commit.
29	
30	- Section headings, in order: `## P1`, `## P2`, `## P3`, `## P?`, `## Done`
31	- Active items in `P1` / `P2` / `P3`:
32	  `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
33	- Active items in `P?`:
34	  `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
35	- Shipped items in `Done`:
36	  `- ✅ [YYYY-MM-DD] [P#/Effort] Title — one-line shipped summary`
37	- Optional trailing on active items:
38	  `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
39	
40	Anything that is NOT a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item — prose paragraphs,
41	blockquotes, HTML comments, `---` rules, indented sub-bullets — is ignored
42	by the validator. Use this room for explanatory text without breaking the
43	machine-readability of the lanes.
44
```
</details></tool-use>

 `/Users/david/.claude/skills/project-knowledge-harness/references/when-to-add-docs.md`

```text
1	# When to add a backlog or pitfall doc, and the upgrade path
2	
3	## Backlog: when an entry needs `backlog/<slug>.md`
4	
5	Add a backlog doc when **any** apply:
6	
7	- `P?` priority (record what was tried so it doesn't need re-investigation)
8	- Captures paused troubleshooting **that you intend to fix later** (preserve
9	  the error trace + root-cause analysis before context evaporates)
10	- Multiple options were considered (record trade-offs, not only the winner)
11	- `L` or `XL` effort (architectural; needs design before code)
12	
13	`S` items rarely need a backlog doc — a file path in the TODO line is usually
14	enough.
15	
16	## Pitfalls: when a debugging session deserves `pitfalls/<slug>.md`
17	
18	Add a pitfall doc when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something that
19	wasn't googleable, AND any of:
20	
21	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (silent state, weird side
22	  effect, behaviour change without error)
23	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
24	  must come after process completion, etc.)
25	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
26	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
27	- A specific tool version is required or forbidden, and failure at the wrong
28	  version is silent / confusing
29	
30	Skip a pitfall doc when:
31	
32	- Trivially googleable (next person solves in 30 seconds)
33	- Already covered as part of normal config docs in `docs/<tool>.md` —
34	  cross-link from `pitfalls/README.md`'s "Cross-referenced pitfalls" table
35	  instead of duplicating
36	- Already a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` — those have higher enforcement
37	  (cross-link only)
38	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot)
39	
40	## Disambiguation: pitfall vs backlog vs TODO entry vs invariant
41	
42	| Situation | Goes in |
43	|---|---|
44	| "We hit X, debugged it, applied workaround, moving on" | `pitfalls/` |
45	| "We hit X, debugged it, but the real fix is queued" | `pitfalls/` (capture trace) AND `TODO.md` (queue the fix) — link both ways |
46	| "We thought about doing X but deferred" | `TODO.md` (P2/P3) |
47	| "We thought about doing X, did a 2-day spike, deferred" | `TODO.md` (P?) + `backlog/` |
48	| "X is a rule everyone must follow forever" | `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant |
49	
50	## Upgrade path: pitfall → Hard invariant
51	
52	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` (or the project's
53	agent contract file) when:
54	
55	- It recurs across machines / agents / sessions despite being documented
56	- The trap silently corrupts state (no error message, just wrong behaviour)
57	- The workaround is non-obvious enough that "remember to do X" is unsafe
58	
59	When graduating:
60	
61	1. Add the rule to `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants section
62	2. Link from the invariant back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for context
63	3. Leave the pitfall doc as historical record (don't delete — it explains
64	   *why* the invariant exists)
65
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Anti-patterns to avoid
2	
3	When applying or maintaining this harness, avoid the following:
4	
5	- **Spawning new files** like `IDEAS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `WISHLIST.md`,
6	  `FUTURE.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `LESSONS.md`, `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`,
7	  `GOTCHAS.md` alongside `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/`. Three
8	  surfaces, always.
9	
10	- **Backlog or pitfall docs in `docs/`**. `docs/` is user-facing reference;
11	  these folders are maintainer-facing memory. Mixing them confuses readers.
12	
13	- **Pitfall docs titled by root cause** (e.g.
14	  `tmux-update-environment.md`) instead of symptom (e.g.
15	  `tmux-pane-loses-ssh-connection-var.md`). You'll search by what you're
16	  seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
17	
18	- **Paraphrasing error messages** in pitfall docs. Copy-paste the full
19	  error including stack/codes — paraphrasing throws away the searchable
20	  bits.
21	
22	- **Backlog or pitfall docs without dates**. A 6-month-old "we decided X"
23	  without a date loses meaning — re-validate or treat as stale.
24	
25	- **Bulk-migrating scattered historical pitfalls** into `pitfalls/` on day
26	  one. High risk of broken cross-links + lost context. Index them in the
27	  README's cross-reference table; physically migrate only when natural.
28	
29	- **Auto-redacting `backlog/` or `pitfalls/`** the way agent scratchpads
30	  are redacted. These are first-class docs you write deliberately; treat
31	  them like any other doc for secret review.
32	
33	- **TODO heading drift**. Keep the exact section order (`P1`, `P2`, `P3`,
34	  `P?`, `Done`) and item forms that `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` validates.
35	  If you need to evolve the format, update the validator and the
36	  documented format in the same change.
37	
38	- **Letting `## Done` grow unbounded**. Prune into a `CHANGELOG.md` (or
39	  similar) once prior-year items appear or the section grows past ~20
40	  entries, keeping recent entries for context.
41	
42	- **Overwriting an existing `TODO.md` with the template**. The bundled
43	  `scripts/init.sh` is conservative on purpose — pass `--force` only after
44	  preserving any real entries you want to keep.
45
```
</details></tool-use>

20	/**
21	 * pi-remote-pilot extension
22	 * Bridges messenger apps (Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord) into pi
23	 */
24	export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI): void {
25	  const transportManager = new TransportManager();
26	  let pendingRemoteChat: PendingRemoteChat | null = null;
27	  let auth: ChallengeAuth;
28	  let ctx: ExtensionContext;
29	
30	  /**
31	   * Update status widget
32	   */
33	  function updateWidget(): void {
34	    const config = loadConfig();
35	
36	    if (config.showWidget === false) {
37	      ctx.ui.setWidget("msg-bridge-status", undefined);
38	      return;
39	    }
40	
41	    const stats = auth.getStats();
42	    const transports: TransportStatus[] = transportManager
43	      .getStatus()
44	      .map((s) => ({
45	        type: s.type,
46	        connected: s.connected,
47	      }));
48	
49	    const widget = createStatusWidget(transports, stats.usersByTransport);
50	    if (widget) {
51	      ctx.ui.setWidget("msg-bridge-status", [widget]);
52	    } else {
53	      ctx.ui.setWidget("msg-bridge-status", undefined);
54	    }
55	  }
56	
57	  /**
58	   * Save auth state to config
59	   */
60	  function saveAuthState(): void {
61	    const config = loadConfig();
62	    config.auth = auth.exportConfig();
63	    saveConfig(config);
64	  }
65	
66	  /**
67	   * Initialize extension
68	   */
69	  pi.on("session_start", async (_event, context) => {
70	    ctx = context;
71	
72	    const config = loadConfig();
73	
74	    auth = new ChallengeAuth(
75	      (code, username) => {
76	        ctx.ui.notify(
77	          `🔐 Challenge code for @${username}: ${code}`,
78	          "info"
79	        );
80	      },
81	      (message, level) => {
82	        ctx.ui.notify(message, level);
83	      },
84	      async (_chatId, _message) => {
85	        // Challenge notifications are sent via the transport's sendMessage
86	      },
87	      saveAuthState
88	    );
89	
90	    if (config.auth) {
91	      auth.loadFromConfig(config.auth);
92	    }
93	
94	    // Initialize transports in the background (non-blocking)
95	    (async () => {
96	      const transportPromises: Promise<void>[] = [];
97	
98	      if (config.telegram?.token) {
99	        transportPromises.push(
100	          Promise.resolve().then(() => {
101	            const telegramProvider = new TelegramProvider(config.telegram!.token, auth);
102	            transportManager.addTransport(telegramProvider);
103	          })
104	        );
105	      }
106	
107	      if (config.whatsapp) {
108	        const whatsappAuthPath = config.whatsapp.authPath || path.join(
109	          os.homedir(),

111	          "msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth"
112	        );
113	
114	        const credsPath = path.join(whatsappAuthPath, "creds.json");
115	        if (fs.existsSync(credsPath)) {
116	          transportPromises.push(
117	            Promise.resolve().then(() => {
118	              const whatsappConfig = { ...config.whatsapp!, debug: config.debug };
119	              const whatsappProvider = new WhatsAppProvider(whatsappConfig, auth);
120	              transportManager.addTransport(whatsappProvider);
121	            })
122	          );
123	        } else {
124	          delete config.whatsapp;
125	          saveConfig(config);
126	        }
127	      }
128	
129	      if (config.slack?.botToken && config.slack?.appToken) {
130	        transportPromises.push(
131	          Promise.resolve().then(() => {
132	            const slackProvider = new SlackProvider(config.slack!, auth);
133	            transportManager.addTransport(slackProvider);
134	          })
135	        );
136	      }
137	
138	      if (config.discord?.token) {
139	        transportPromises.push(
140	          Promise.resolve().then(() => {
141	            const discordProvider = new DiscordProvider(config.discord!, auth);
142	            transportManager.addTransport(discordProvider);
143	          })
144	        );
145	      }
146	
147	      if (config.matrix?.homeserverUrl && config.matrix?.accessToken) {
148	        transportPromises.push(
149	          Promise.resolve().then(() => {
150	            const matrixProvider = new MatrixProvider(config.matrix!, auth);
151	            transportManager.addTransport(matrixProvider);
152	          })
153	        );
154	      }
155	
156	      await Promise.all(transportPromises);
157	
158	      // Auto-connect if configured
159	      const transports = transportManager.getAllTransports();
160	      if (transports.length > 0 && config.autoConnect !== false) {
161	        if (!acquireLock()) {
162	          ctx.ui.notify("ℹ️ msg-bridge: another instance is already connected — skipping auto-connect", "info");
163	        } else {
164	          try {
165	            await transportManager.connectAll();
166	            updateWidget();
167	          } catch (err) {
168	            releaseLock();
169	            ctx.ui.notify(`⚠️ Some transports failed to connect: ${(err as Error).message}`, "warning");
170	          }
171	        }
172	      }
173	    })().catch(err => {
174	      console.error("Transport initialization error:", err);
175	      ctx.ui.notify(`❌ Transport initialization failed: ${err.message}`, "error");
176	    });
177	
178	    transportManager.onMessage((msg) => {
179	      pendingRemoteChat = {
180	        chatId: msg.chatId,
181	        transport: msg.transport,
182	        username: msg.username,
183	        messageId: msg.messageId,
184	      };
185	
186	      const taggedMessage = `[📱 @${msg.username} via ${msg.transport}]: ${msg.content}`;
187	      pi.sendUserMessage(taggedMessage, { deliverAs: "followUp" });
188	    });
189	
190	    transportManager.onError((err, transport) => {
191	      ctx.ui.notify(`❌ ${transport} error: ${err.message}`, "error");
192	    });
193	
194	    updateWidget();
195	  });

197	  /**
198	   * Handle turn start - send typing indicator
199	   */
200	  pi.on("turn_start", async (_event, _context) => {
201	    if (pendingRemoteChat) {
202	      try {
203	        await transportManager.sendTyping(
204	          pendingRemoteChat.chatId,
205	          pendingRemoteChat.transport
206	        );
207	      } catch (_err) {
208	        // Ignore typing indicator errors
209	      }
210	    }
211	  });
212	
213	  /**
214	   * Handle turn end - send response back to messenger
215	   */
216	  pi.on("turn_end", async (event, _context) => {
217	    if (!pendingRemoteChat) return;
218	
219	    try {
220	      const message = event.message as AssistantMessage;
221	      const responseText = extractTextFromMessage(message);
222	      const toolCallsText = formatToolCalls(message);
223	      const hasPendingTools = hasToolCalls(message);
224	      const config = loadConfig();
225	
226	      const parts: string[] = [];
227	      const trimmedResponse = responseText.trim();
228	      if (trimmedResponse) parts.push(trimmedResponse);
229	      if (toolCallsText && !config.hideToolCalls) parts.push(toolCallsText);
230	
231	      if (parts.length === 0) {
232	        // Nothing to send this turn — don't touch pendingRemoteChat;
233	        // a future turn_end may have the actual response text.
234	        return;
235	      }
236	
237	      const fullText = parts.join("\n\n");
238	
239	      // Split long messages for Telegram's 4096 char limit
240	      const chunks = splitMessage(fullText, 4000);
241	      for (const chunk of chunks) {
242	        await transportManager.sendMessage(
243	          pendingRemoteChat.chatId,
244	          pendingRemoteChat.transport,
245	          chunk
246	        );
247	      }
248	
249	      if (!hasPendingTools) {
250	        pendingRemoteChat = null;
251	      }
252	    } catch (err) {
253	      const transport = pendingRemoteChat?.transport ?? "unknown";
254	      ctx.ui.notify(
255	        `Failed to send response to ${transport}: ${(err as Error).message}`,
256	        "error"
257	      );
258	      pendingRemoteChat = null;
259	    }
260	  });
261	
262	  /**
263	   * Cleanup on session exit — release lock and disconnect transports
264	   */

266	    await transportManager.disconnectAll();
267	    releaseLock();
268	  });

272	   */
273	  pi.registerCommand("msg-bridge", {
274	    description: "Manage remote messenger connections (help|status|connect|disconnect|configure|widget)",
275	    handler: async (args: string, context) => {

```text
## Context construction

The pinned page does **not include source code**, so it cannot establish the exact implementation. It lists `src/`, `index.ts`, and `types.ts`, but provides no code descriptions for them.

What `README.md` documents is:

- Each connected channel has its own sandboxed Pi/Gondolin environment.
- Channel state includes `gondolin/session.json`, suggesting persistent VM state.
- `/chat-new` explicitly starts a new Pi session; `compact` operates on the current context.
- Account and channel memory files are injected into the system prompt on every turn.
- Skills are discovered and listed in the system prompt.
- `channel.jsonl` stores chat history, but `chat_history` is exposed as a tool for searching older messages.

Therefore, the documented behavior is **one ongoing Pi session per connected channel**, augmented each turn with memory and skills. The page does **not** document replaying the entire channel log into every prompt. It also does not prove whether a worker restart resumes the native Pi conversation or reconstructs it from persisted state.

## Discord routing and session sharing

- The documented Discord routing unit is a **server channel**: setup asks the user to select a server and configure channels, and each connected channel gets its own environment.
- Threads and actors are not described, so the page provides no basis for claiming either is a routing/session boundary.
- Multiple turns in the same connected channel appear to share one Pi session until a new session, disconnect, or other lifecycle event occurs.

Relevant documented paths/sections: `README.md` sections **Features**, **Commands**, **Storage Layout**, **Memory**, **Skills**, and **Tools**; the repository file listing identifies `src/`, `index.ts`, and `types.ts` but does not expose their contents here.
```

1	# Context
2	
3	本次調研要判斷：Pi 的 extension／SDK／RPC 與既有 IM gateway 專案，是否適合直接納入 `pi-agents`，或目前只應留下可驗證的文件決策。以 **Pi 0.84.4** 與 **2026-08-31** 的來源快照為準，結論是 **docs-first**：`pia` 維持小型、無 runtime dependency、前景執行且同時支援 Pi／OMP 的 combo launcher；不在核心加入 gateway、daemon、transport schema 或 service lifecycle。
4	
5	採用使用者選定的 **session-router context contract**：
6	
7	- Pi session 是模型可見對話、tool history、branch 與 compaction 的唯一真相來源。
8	- IM provider 負責原生 message／reply／edit／delete／membership 事實；不把整個 room history 每輪重播進 prompt。
9	- Gateway 若日後實作，另以 durable state 負責 identity/admission、conversation↔project/combo↔Pi-session binding、per-session FIFO／single-writer lease、inbound dedup、approval 與 outbound receipt。
10	- Reply-to-bot 可作 routing hint；額外 quote/context 必須顯式、bounded、帶 attribution。沒有 thread 且 session 不唯一時拒絕猜測，要求明確 `/new`、`/resume` 或 `/bind`。
11	
12	這不排除日後加入 Pi-only `maturity: experimental` combo；但外部候選尚未在 `pia` 隔離環境實跑 Pi 0.84.4，因此本階段不提交 package pin、extension 或 combo。
13	
14	# Recommended changes
15	
16	## 1. 建立 `backlog/pi-im-gateway.md`
17	
18	沿用 `backlog/opencode-harness-to-pi.md` 等既有格式，加入 `Status: P?`、`Effort: L` 與 related links，並集中保存會隨時間變動的調研證據：
19	
20	1. **Context / decision snapshot**
21	   - 標記版本與日期（Pi 0.84.4、2026-08-31）。

23	   - 記錄立即決策：docs-first、核心不變；下一個 executable step 是 time-boxed、repo 外的相容性 spike。

26	   - 寫明上述四個 authority 與「accepted IM invocation 只投影至一個 Pi session」的不變量。
27	   - 記錄 threadless routing 順序、per-Pi-session FIFO／single writer、顯式 session control，以及不隱式匯入 ambient history。
28	   - 說明 edit/delete 不回寫既有 Pi history，也不能撤銷已發生的 filesystem/network side effects。

3	This directory pins and deploys a managed Kimaki bot. Discord project channels

29	├── healthcheck.mjs / watchdog.sh   # 功能健康檢查與故障恢復

40	### 執行拓樸
41

43	macOS launchd
44	  └─ start-kimaki.sh
45	      └─ Kimaki Node.js process
46	          ├─ discord.js Gateway / REST
47	          ├─ ~/.kimaki/discord-sessions.db
48	          ├─ localhost Hrana DB bridge
49	          └─ opencode serve（localhost 隨機 port）
50	              ├─ OpenCode HTTP JSON API
51	              ├─ /global/event SSE stream
52	              ├─ Kimaki OpenCode plugins
53	              └─ 隔離的 OpenCode XDG／SQLite 狀態
54	```

56	所有專案共用一個本機 `opencode serve` process，但每次 SDK request 都帶入
57	工作目錄；Discord project channel 對應本機目錄，Discord thread 則對應一個
58	OpenCode session。

60	### 一次訊息的完整路徑
61	
62	1. Discord Gateway 送出 `MessageCreate`，入口是
63	   `node_modules/kimaki/dist/discord-bot.js:331`。
64	2. Bot 依序檢查 guild allowlist、自己的訊息、channel 是否綁定本機專案，
65	   以及使用者的 owner／admin／Manage Server／`Kimaki` role 權限。
66	3. Project channel 的新訊息會建立 Discord thread；既有 thread 則載入原本的
67	   OpenCode session。對應關係持久化在 `discord-sessions.db`。
68	4. 前處理階段解析回覆內容、mention、文字附件、圖片、PDF 與語音訊息。
69	5. `thread-session-runtime.js:2291-2368` 將使用者文字、Discord metadata、
70	   system prompt、附件、agent 與 model 組成 OpenCode request。
71	6. `session.promptAsync(request)` 透過 OpenCode SDK 發出 HTTP request：
72	   `POST /session/{sessionID}/prompt_async`。
73	7. OpenCode 執行模型及工具，再由 `/global/event` 以 Server-Sent Events
74	   推送 session、文字與工具事件。
75	8. `global-event-listener.js:130-210` 維持一條全域 SSE 連線；每個 thread
76	   runtime 再依 session ID 過濾屬於自己的事件。
77	9. 完成的文字交給 `discord-utils.js:486-534`，保留 Markdown/code fence，
78	   並依 Discord 的 2,000 字限制分段送回原 thread。
79	
80	```text
81	Discord MessageCreate
82	        │
83	        ▼
84	guild／role／channel 權限檢查
85	        │
86	        ▼
87	Discord channel → 本機專案目錄
88	Discord thread  → OpenCode session
89	        │
90	        ▼
91	session.promptAsync() ── HTTP + JSON ──► opencode serve
92	        ▲                                      │
93	        │                                      │ model / tools
94	        └──── session events ◄──── SSE ─────────┘
95	        │
96	        ▼
97	Markdown 整理、2,000 字分段、送回 Discord thread
98	```
99	
100	### 關鍵程式片段
101	
102	Discord 訊息入口先做 admission control，而不是收到訊息就直接交給模型：
103	
104	```js
105	discordClient.on(Events.MessageCreate, async (message) => {
106	  if (!isAllowedGuildId(message.guildId)) return
107	  if (isSelfBotMessage && !isCliInjectedPrompt) return
108	
109	  const channelConfig = await getChannelDirectory(owningChannelId)
110	  if (!channelConfig) return
111	
112	  const member = await resolveGuildMessageMember(message)
113	  if (!hasKimakiBotPermission(member, message.guild)) return
114	
115	  // 通過檢查後才交給對應的 thread/session runtime。
116	})
117	```
118	
119	Kimaki 在本機啟動一個共用 OpenCode server，並以 project directory 建立 SDK
120	client。實作入口是 `node_modules/kimaki/dist/opencode.js:639-790`：
121	
122	```js
123	const serverProcess = spawn(spawnCommand, spawnArgs, {
124	  cwd: os.homedir(),
125	  env: {
126	    ...process.env,
127	    OPENCODE_CONFIG: opencodeConfigPath,
128	    OPENCODE_PORT: port.toString(),
129	    KIMAKI: "1",
130	  },
131	})
132	
133	const client = createOpencodeClient({
134	  baseUrl,
135	  directory,
136	  headers: getOpencodeServerAuthHeaders(),
137	})
138	```
139	
140	送給 OpenCode 的資料不只有聊天文字，也包含這次 Discord turn 的執行上下文：
141	
142	```js
143	const parts = [
144	  { type: "text", text: promptWithImagePaths },
145	  { type: "text", text: syntheticContext, synthetic: true },
146	  ...images,
147	]
148	
149	const request = {
150	  sessionID: session.id,
151	  directory: this.sdkDirectory,
152	  parts,
153	  system: getOpencodeSystemMessage({
154	    sessionId: session.id,
155	    channelId,
156	    guildId: this.thread.guildId,
157	    threadId: this.thread.id,
158	  }),
159	  ...(resolvedAgent ? { agent: resolvedAgent } : {}),
160	  ...(modelField ? { model: modelField } : {}),
161	}
162	
163	await waitForGlobalEventListener()
164	await getClient().session.promptAsync(request)
165	```
166	
167	回應不是解析 CLI stdout，而是訂閱 OpenCode 的 typed event stream：
168	
169	```js
170	const subscribeResult = await client.global.event({ signal })
171	
172	for await (const event of subscribeResult.stream) {
173	  dispatchEvent(event)
174	}
175	```
176	
177	SSE 中斷時會以 exponential backoff 重連，從 500 ms 增加至最多 30 秒。
178	
179	### Session、狀態與並行
180	
181	- 一個 Discord thread 通常對應一個 OpenCode session，因此對話可以跨訊息延續。
182	- 不同 thread 有獨立 runtime，可以並行執行；同一 thread 的狀態變更會序列化，
183	  避免 event、queue 與 session transition 互相踩資料。
184	- 完整 OpenCode 對話存放在隔離的 OpenCode SQLite；thread/session mapping、
185	  model 選擇及已送出的 part mapping 存放在 Kimaki SQLite。
186	- 已送出的 OpenCode part 會記錄其 Discord message mapping，重連後可避免重複傳送。
187	- 顯式的本機 per-thread queue 是記憶體狀態，process restart 後不保留；這是目前
188	  已知的恢復邊界。
189	
190	### 安全邊界
191	
192	- `start-kimaki.sh` 使用 `env -i` 建立環境變數白名單，避免 launchd 或互動 shell
193	  的任意變數滲入服務。
194	- OpenCode API 只監聽 localhost 隨機 port，並要求私有 Basic Auth credential。
195	- Bot 使用固定 Discord guild allowlist，channel 還必須存在本機 project mapping。
196	- `--restrict-directories` 讓模型離開目前專案前必須取得額外許可。
197	- Bot 的 OpenCode XDG 目錄與桌面／Tailscale OpenCode 完全分離；啟動器拒絕
198	  symlink，並檢查 `opencode.db`、WAL、SHM 是否與共用實例指向相同 inode。
199	- `umask 077`、目錄 `0700` 及 credential `0600` 限制其他本機帳號讀取狀態。
200	- `--no-analytics`、`--no-critique` 與 `--no-auto-upgrade` 分別關閉產品分析、
201	  外部 diff critique，以及未經測試的自動升級。
202	
203	這不是 sandbox。獲授權的 Discord 使用者能透過 `!` 或 `/run-shell-command`
204	執行此 macOS 帳號可執行的 shell command；因此 Discord 帳號、server role 與
205	bot token 都必須視為主機存取憑證。
206	
207	### 給工程師的一句話
208	
209	這是一個以 Kimaki 作為 transport 與 session orchestration core 的 Discord
210	遠端 OpenCode runtime：本專案釘死上游版本，透過可重播 patch 客製行為，再補上
211	guild allowlist、XDG／SQLite 隔離、localhost Basic Auth、launchd supervision、
212	functional health check、原子部署與 rollback。
213	
214	## Runtime
215	
216	- Kimaki: `0.26.0`
217	- Sharp security override: `0.35.3`
218	- Node.js: `24.15.0`
219	- Bun: `1.3.12`
220	- OpenCode: `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode`
221	- Kimaki state and Discord credentials: `~/.kimaki/`
222	- Kimaki OpenCode state: `~/.local/share/solomon-kimaki/opencode/`
223	- Default Discord model: `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol`
224	
225	The launcher uses `umask 077`, so newly created credentials and logs default to
226	owner-only access.
227	
228	Install dependencies:
229	
230	```sh
231	npm install
232	```
233	
234	Start the interactive setup or run the configured bot:
235	
236	```sh
237	./start-kimaki.sh
238	```
239	
240	The launcher intentionally enables:
241	
242	- `--restrict-directories`: ask before leaving the active project.
243	- `--no-critique`: do not upload diffs to an external review service.
244	- `--no-analytics`: disable Kimaki product analytics.
245	- `--no-auto-upgrade`: keep the tested version pinned.
246	
247	It does not enable `--allow-all-users`. Initially, only the owner of the private
248	Discord server should have access.
249	
250	The runtime also enforces a fixed guild allowlist. Being a Discord server owner
251	or administrator is not sufficient unless the server ID is explicitly allowed.
252	The health endpoint becomes unhealthy when no allowlisted server is connected.
253	The localhost OpenCode API requires a private Basic Auth credential, and its
254	database retains only sessions referenced by Discord threads or scheduled work.
255	
256	## Discord Setup
257	
258	1. Create a private Discord server used only for this bot.
259	2. Open <https://discord.com/developers/applications> and create an application.
260	3. In **Bot**, enable **Message Content Intent**.
261	4. Reset and copy the bot token when the Kimaki setup wizard requests it.
262	5. Never paste the token into Discord, this repository, or an OpenCode prompt.
263	6. Use the install URL printed by Kimaki to add the bot to the private server.
264	
265	## Projects
266	
267	Register the two initial project directories after onboarding:
268	
269	```sh
270	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/Skill training"
271	./node_modules/.bin/kimaki project add "/Users/solomon/every thing can be quant/第一性原理/不再被騙系統"
272	```
273	
274	Kimaki creates one Discord channel per directory. Switch project by switching
275	channel; start a separate task by posting a new channel message. Continue a task
276	inside its thread.
277	
278	This installation applies a version-checked local patch after `npm install`.
279	Discord's `/add-project` can accept an absolute path, browse a path prefix, or
280	search folder names under the home directory and mounted volumes. Projects are
281	created only when requested; subfolders are not pre-created as channels.
282	The command and its autocomplete can be used from any channel in the allowed
283	private server, including a channel that is not yet linked to a project.
284	
285	Examples in Discord's `/add-project` field:
286	
287	- `TOEIC`: search matching folder names.
288	- `/Users/solomon/`: browse folders in the home directory.
289	- `/Volumes/`: browse mounted disks.
290	- `/absolute/path/to/folder`: use an exact directory as the project root.
291	
292	Folder choices end in `/`. Select a folder, then reopen the `project` field to
293	browse its children. Submit at any level to create that folder's project channel.
294	One- or two-character searches use fast top-level matching; longer searches add
295	Spotlight results. If deep search times out, top-level matches remain available.
296	
297	## Background Service
298	
299	`com.solomon.kimaki.plist` is installed under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`. It
300	starts Kimaki when this macOS user logs in and restarts it after failures. Logs

1	/**
2	 * Extension UI Forwarder
3	 *
4	 * Manages forwarding extension_ui_request from RPC agents to WebChat WS clients,
5	 * and routing responses back to the agent's stdin.
6	 *
7	 * Replaces the auto-cancel behavior in rpc-client.ts when WebChat clients are connected.
8	 */
9	
10	import type { ServerWebSocket } from "bun";
11	import type {
12	  ExtensionUIRequest,
13	  ExtensionUIResponse,
14	  ExtensionUIDismissed,
15	  PendingUIRequest,
16	  ExtensionUIMethod,
17	  SelectOption,
18	} from "./extension-ui-types.ts";
19	import { createLogger } from "./types.ts";
20	
21	const DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 60_000;
22	
23	export class ExtensionUIForwarder {
24	  /** Pending requests awaiting frontend response */
25	  private pending = new Map<string, PendingUIRequest>();
26	  private log = createLogger("extension-ui");
27	
28	  /**
29	   * Forward an extension_ui_request to all connected WS clients.
30	   * Returns a Promise that resolves when a client responds or TTL expires.
31	   */
32	  forward(
33	    data: Record<string, unknown>,
34	    wsClients: Map<string, ServerWebSocket<any>>,
35	    writeToRpc: (response: string) => void,
36	  ): boolean {
37	    const id = data.id as string;
38	    const method = data.method as string;
39	    if (!id || !method) return false;
40	
41	    // No WS clients connected — fall back to auto-cancel
42	    if (wsClients.size === 0) return false;
43	
44	    const request: ExtensionUIRequest = this.normalizeRequest(data);
45	
46	    const entry: PendingUIRequest = {
47	      id,
48	      request,
49	      resolved: false,
50	      createdAt: Date.now(),
51	      ttlTimer: setTimeout(() => {
52	        this.handleTimeout(id, writeToRpc);
53	      }, request.ttlMs),
54	      respond: (response: ExtensionUIResponse) => {
55	        writeToRpc(JSON.stringify({
56	          type: "extension_ui_response",
57	          id,
58	          value: response.value,
59	          confirmed: response.confirmed,
60	          cancelled: response.cancelled,
61	        }));
62	      },
63	      onTimeout: () => {
64	        writeToRpc(JSON.stringify({
65	          type: "extension_ui_response",
66	          id,
67	          cancelled: true,
68	        }));
69	      },
70	    };
71	
72	    this.pending.set(id, entry);
73	
74	    // Broadcast to all WS clients (first-win)
75	    const frame = JSON.stringify({
76	      type: "event",
77	      event: "extension_ui_request",
78	      payload: request,
79	    });
80	    for (const ws of wsClients.values()) {
81	      try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
82	    }
83	
84	    this.log.debug(`Forwarded extension_ui_request ${id} (${method}) to ${wsClients.size} client(s)`);
85	    return true;
86	  }
87	
88	  /**
89	   * Handle a response from a WS client.
90	   * First response wins; late responses are ignored + dismissed.
91	   */
92	  handleResponse(
93	    response: ExtensionUIResponse,
94	    wsClients: Map<string, ServerWebSocket<any>>,
95	    respondingClientId: string,
96	  ): boolean {
97	    const entry = this.pending.get(response.id);
98	    if (!entry) return false;
99	
100	    if (entry.resolved) {
101	      // Already resolved — send dismissed to this late client
102	      this.log.debug(`Late response for ${response.id} from ${respondingClientId}, ignoring`);
103	      return false;
104	    }
105	
106	    // First win — resolve
107	    entry.resolved = true;
108	    clearTimeout(entry.ttlTimer);
109	    entry.respond(response);
110	    this.pending.delete(response.id);
111	
112	    // Notify other clients that this prompt is dismissed
113	    const dismissed: ExtensionUIDismissed = {
114	      type: "extension_ui_dismissed",
115	      id: response.id,
116	    };
117	    const frame = JSON.stringify({ type: "event", event: "extension_ui_dismissed", payload: dismissed });
118	    for (const [clientId, ws] of wsClients) {
119	      if (clientId !== respondingClientId) {
120	        try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
121	      }
122	    }
123	
124	    this.log.debug(`Resolved extension_ui_request ${response.id} via ${respondingClientId}`);
125	    return true;
126	  }
127	
128	  /**
129	   * Re-send pending requests to a newly connected client (reconnect recovery).
130	   * Only re-sends requests with remaining TTL > 10s.
131	   */
132	  resendPending(ws: ServerWebSocket<any>): void {
133	    const now = Date.now();
134	    for (const entry of this.pending.values()) {
135	      if (entry.resolved) continue;
136	      const elapsed = now - entry.createdAt;
137	      const remaining = entry.request.ttlMs - elapsed;
138	      if (remaining <= 10_000) continue;
139	
140	      const frame = JSON.stringify({
141	        type: "event",
142	        event: "extension_ui_request",
143	        payload: { ...entry.request, ttlMs: remaining },
144	      });
145	      try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
146	    }
147	  }
148	
149	  /** Cancel all pending requests (gateway shutdown). */
150	  cancelAll(writeToRpc: (response: string) => void): void {
151	    for (const entry of this.pending.values()) {
152	      if (!entry.resolved) {
153	        clearTimeout(entry.ttlTimer);
154	        entry.onTimeout();
155	      }
156	    }
157	    this.pending.clear();
158	  }
159	
160	  get pendingCount(): number {
161	    return this.pending.size;
162	  }
163	
164	  // ==========================================================================
165	  // Internal
166	  // ==========================================================================
167	
168	  private handleTimeout(id: string, writeToRpc: (response: string) => void): void {
169	    const entry = this.pending.get(id);
170	    if (!entry || entry.resolved) return;
171	
172	    entry.resolved = true;
173	    entry.onTimeout();
174	    this.pending.delete(id);
175	    this.log.debug(`Extension UI request ${id} timed out (${entry.request.ttlMs}ms)`);
176	  }
177	
178	  private normalizeRequest(data: Record<string, unknown>): ExtensionUIRequest {
179	    const method = data.method as ExtensionUIMethod;
180	    const base = {
181	      type: "extension_ui_request" as const,
182	      id: data.id as string,
183	      method,
184	      title: data.title as string | undefined,
185	      ttlMs: (data.ttlMs as number) ?? DEFAULT_TTL_MS,
186	    };
187	
188	    switch (method) {
189	      case "select":
190	      case "multiselect":
191	        return {
192	          ...base,
193	          method,
194	          options: this.normalizeOptions(data.options),
195	          initialValue: data.initialValue as string | undefined,
196	          initialValues: data.initialValues as string[] | undefined,
197	        };
198	      case "text":
199	      case "editor":
200	        return {
201	          ...base,
202	          method,
203	          placeholder: data.placeholder as string | undefined,
204	          defaultValue: data.defaultValue as string | undefined,
205	        };
206	      case "confirm":
207	        return {
208	          ...base,
209	          method,
210	          message: data.message as string | undefined,
211	          initialValue: data.initialValue as boolean | undefined,
212	        };
213	      case "progress":
214	        return {
215	          ...base,
216	          method,
217	          current: data.current as number | undefined,
218	          total: data.total as number | undefined,
219	          label: data.label as string | undefined,
220	        };
221	      default:
222	        return { ...base, method: "confirm", message: `Unknown method: ${method}` };
223	    }
224	  }
225	
226	  /** Normalize options: accept string[] or {value,label,hint?}[] */
227	  private normalizeOptions(raw: unknown): SelectOption[] {
228	    if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
229	    return raw.map((item) => {
230	      if (typeof item === "string") return { value: item, label: item };
231	      if (item && typeof item === "object" && "value" in item) {
232	        return {
233	          value: String(item.value),
234	          label: String(item.label ?? item.value),
235	          hint: item.hint ? String(item.hint) : undefined,
236	        };
237	      }
238	      return { value: String(item), label: String(item) };
239	    });
240	  }
241	}

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md`

```text
In Pi v0.84.4:

- `agent_end` marks completion of one low-level agent run, not the whole operation. Another run may follow because of:
  - automatic retry, indicated by `willRetry: true`;
  - overflow compaction recovery, where successful compaction triggers a retry;
  - transient compaction or branch-summary retry handling;
  - queued steering or follow-up messages.
- Steering is processed after the current assistant turn’s tool calls and before the next LLM call. Its delivery mode may process one message or all pending messages.
- Follow-ups are processed after the agent otherwise finishes, with the same one-at-a-time/all choice. Therefore, they can produce additional turns after an `agent_end`.
- `agent_settled` is emitted only after the session-level operation has completely stopped. At that point, no retry, compaction retry, or queued continuation remains.

Therefore, `agent_settled` is the correct terminal boundary for an external session router. An `agent_end` event should be treated as an intermediate low-level completion, not as permission to finalize or route the session.
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md`

```text
## Conclusion

The docs present the **SDK** as the preferred in-process TypeScript embedding approach over RPC when the host needs type safety, direct agent state, or programmatic customization.

They distinguish the surfaces:

- **`AgentSession`**: the API for operating one session—prompting, streaming events, model control, compaction, abortion, and cleanup.
- **`AgentSessionRuntime`**: the API for replacing the active session through new, resume/switch, fork/clone, or import flows, while rebuilding cwd-dependent runtime state.

The docs do not explicitly call `AgentSession` or `AgentSessionRuntime` a universal “recommended surface.” The practical guidance is to use `AgentSession` for a stable session and add the runtime layer when session replacement is required.

## Host responsibilities documented by the SDK

- **Queues:** During streaming, the host must choose steering versus follow-up behavior. `prompt()` requires an explicit streaming behavior, while `steer()` and `followUp()` provide direct queueing APIs. Queue state is exposed through events.
- **Persistence:** The host selects the `SessionManager` strategy: in-memory, new persistent, recent-session continuation, or opening a specific file. Session trees and branching are managed through `SessionManager`.
- **Settings durability:** Settings mutations enqueue asynchronous writes. The host must call `flush()` when it needs a durability boundary and inspect `drainErrors()` for I/O failures.
- **Cleanup:** The host is responsible for calling `session.dispose()`.
- **Replacement rebinding:** Runtime replacement changes `runtime.session`. Existing subscriptions belong to the old session, so the host must unsubscribe and resubscribe. If extensions are used, the host must bind them again to the replacement session.
- **Failure handling:** Runtime creation or replacement throws on failure; the caller decides how to handle that failure.

## Multi-session coordination

The docs provide no multi-session coordinator or policy. By inference, an application hosting multiple sessions must manage their separate session/runtime objects, subscriptions, persistence choices, queue interactions, lifecycle cleanup, and any cross-session synchronization itself.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v0.84.4/packages/coding-agent/docs/security.md`

```text
For Pi v0.84.4:

- **Project trust** controls loading project-local settings, resources, packages, and extensions.
- It **does not sandbox execution**, restrict tool actions, or prevent prompt injection from repository content.
- Pi, its built-in tools, and TypeScript extensions run with the permissions of the OS account that starts Pi. Shells, package managers, tests, and language servers likewise run as ordinary local processes.
- Therefore, without OS-, container-, VM-, or micro-VM-level isolation, host-executed tool access effectively has the launching user’s authority, subject to that user’s filesystem, credentials, mounts, and network access.
- Containers or VMs reduce that authority only when access is deliberately limited. A read/write host-workspace mount still permits changes to host files.
```
</details></tool-use>

20	async function withDiscordClient<T>(token: string, work: (client: Client<true>) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
21		const client = new Client({
22			intents: [GatewayIntentBits.Guilds],
23			partials: [Partials.Channel],
24		});
25		try {
26			const readyPromise = once(client, "ready");
27			await client.login(token);
28			if (!client.isReady()) {
29				await Promise.race([
30					readyPromise,
31					new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("Discord client failed to become ready")), 10000)),
32				]);
33			}
34			if (!client.isReady()) throw new Error("Discord client failed to become ready");
35			return await work(client as Client<true>);
36		} finally {
37			client.destroy();
38		}
39	}
40	
41	export async function listDiscordServers(token: string): Promise<DiscordServerInfo[]> {
42		return withDiscordClient(token, async (client) =>
43			[...client.guilds.cache.values()]
44				.map((guild) => ({ id: guild.id, name: guild.name }))
45				.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name)),
46		);
47	}

49	export async function waitForDiscordServerJoin(
50		token: string,
51		knownServerIds: string[],
52		signal?: AbortSignal,
53	): Promise<DiscordServerInfo> {
54		return withDiscordClient(token, async (client) => {
55			const known = new Set(knownServerIds);
56			for (const guild of client.guilds.cache.values()) {
57				if (!known.has(guild.id)) return { id: guild.id, name: guild.name };
58			}
59			return await new Promise<DiscordServerInfo>((resolve, reject) => {
60				const onAbort = () => {
61					client.off("guildCreate", onGuildCreate);
62					reject(new Error("Cancelled Discord server invite wait"));
63				};
64				const onGuildCreate = (guild: { id: string; name: string }) => {
65					if (signal) signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
66					resolve({ id: guild.id, name: guild.name });
67				};
68				client.on("guildCreate", onGuildCreate);
69				signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
70			});
71		});
72	}

69		if (message.author.id === account.botUserId) return undefined;
70		const attachments: NonNullable<InboundMessageInput["attachments"]> = [];
71		let index = 0;
72		for (const attachment of message.attachments.values()) {
73			const response = await fetch(attachment.url);
74			if (!response.ok) continue;
75			const data = new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer());
76			attachments.push(
77				await storeDownloadedAttachment(
78					conversation,
79					message.id,
80					++index,
81					attachment.name || `attachment-${index}`,
82					data,
83					attachment.contentType || undefined,
84					attachment.url,
85				),
86			);
87		}
88		return {
89			messageId: message.id,
90			userId: message.author.id,
91			userName: message.member?.displayName || message.author.username,
92			roleIds: message.member?.roles.cache.map((role) => role.id),
93			text: message.content || "",
94			mentionedBot:
95				message.mentions.users.has(account.botUserId || "") ||
96				textMentionsBot(message.content || "", account.botUsername, account.botUserId),
97			isBot: message.author.bot,
98			attachments,
99		};
100	}

116: ## Operational baseline
117: 
118: A resident production gateway would have to own all of the following outside
119: `pia`:
120: 
121: - deny-by-default account, tenant, guild, channel/thread/topic, actor, and admin
122:   admission;
123: - project and session binding, one-writer fencing, per-session queues, and
124:   bounded global concurrency;
125: - provider event cursors, durable deduplication, accepted/active/uncertain job
126:   states, and an outbound receipt or outbox strategy;
127: - restart reconciliation without concurrently mutating one Pi JSONL file;
128: - approval requests bound to actor, session, turn, tool, arguments, project,
129:   generation, and expiry, with timeout/disconnect failing closed;
130: - attachment type/size/path controls, temporary owner-only storage, retention,
131:   and safe handling of unavailable or expired media;
132: - credentials and mutable state outside Git-managed combo trees, with a minimal
133:   environment and redacted logs;
134: - functional health checks, bounded reconnect/backoff, process supervision,
135:   resource limits, backup/migration, reproducible deployment, and rollback.
136: 
137: These criteria were informed by a managed Kimaki/OpenCode deployment review and
138: by the public [Kimaki](https://github.com/remorses/kimaki) architecture. They are
139: requirements for any comparable production claim, not claims that upstream
140: Kimaki or an existing Pi candidate implements every item.
141: 
142: End-to-end exactly-once execution is not realistic across an IM provider, a
143: gateway database, Pi JSONL, filesystem side effects, and outbound APIs. A
144: truthful design should promise durable admission and reconciliation where
145: implemented, expose an `uncertain` outcome when it cannot prove completion, and
146: state the bounded circumstances in which duplicate execution or delivery may
147: occur.

205: ## Promotion gates
206: 
207: The gates deliberately distinguish an experiment from a production service.
208: Failure at a higher tier does not prevent a clearly labelled lower-tier test.
209: 
210: ### 1. Documentation decision
211: 
212: - Preserve this dated source review and session-router contract.
213: - Keep stable product-boundary language in `docs/ecosystem.md`; keep moving
214:   versions, rankings, and defects here.

216: ### 2. Out-of-tree executable spike
217: 
218: - Name one operator, transport, topology, project-binding policy, concurrency
219:   target, attachment scope, target OS, and host-authority decision.
220: - Pin an immutable artifact and verify integrity, license/provenance, package
221:   scopes, install behavior, state paths, and required binaries.
222: - Run the real candidate with Pi 0.84.4 in a disposable account or VM and
223:   isolated `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`PIA_STATE_HOME`.
224: - Exercise authorized and unauthorized ingress, destination binding, same-session

226:   `agent_settled`, approval allow/deny/timeout, attachments, disconnect, and
227:   process restart.
228: - Keep credentials and mutable state outside the repository and record every
229:   patch as a minimal, version-checked change.
230: 
231: ### 3. Pi-only experimental combo
232: 
233: Passing this gate permits a `maturity: experimental` Pi combo without changing
234: `pia` core or its schema:
235: 
236: - immutable, licensed package/commit pin with an accountable maintainer;
237: - exact Pi 0.84.4 load and an authorized/unauthorized round trip;

240: - explicit service-state root outside combo source, with no secret in Git;

243: - documentation that promises only the behavior actually tested and states
244:   best-effort delivery, no sandbox, no service supervision, and no OMP support;
245: - dedicated typecheck/runtime coverage for any combo-local extension, because the
246:   current project TypeScript check does not compile `combos/**`.
247: 
248: ### 4. Supported optional adapter
249: 
250: - maintained compatibility CI against the declared Pi versions;

252: - authorization, routing, lifecycle, provider-limit, and restart regression

258: 
259: - durable provider cursors, ingress uniqueness, queue state machine, outcome

261: - generation fencing, one authoritative session writer, and crash injection at

377	    const legacyKey = legacyChannelBindingStorageKey(channel, sessionKey);

379	    await this.update((data) => {
380	      const existing = data.channelBindings[key] ?? (instanceId === "default" ? data.channelBindings[legacyKey] : undefined);

498	  async tryUpsertDelegationTask(task: DelegationTaskRecord, options: { maxAuditEntries?: number } = {}): Promise<{ applied: boolean; task: DelegationTaskRecord; reason?: "conflict" }> {
499	    const maxAuditEntries = Math.max(1, options.maxAuditEntries ?? 200);
500	    let result: { applied: boolean; task: DelegationTaskRecord; reason?: "conflict" } = { applied: true, task };
501	    await this.update((data) => {
502	      const current = data.delegationTasks[task.id];
503	      if (current && !delegationTaskIncludesAudit(task, current)) {
504	        result = { applied: false, task: current, reason: "conflict" };
505	        return;
506	      }
507	      saveDelegationTask(data, task, maxAuditEntries);
508	      result = { applied: true, task };
509	    });
510	    return result;
511	  }

513	  async getDelegationTask(taskId: string, options: { runningTimeoutMs?: number; now?: string } = {}): Promise<DelegationTaskRecord | undefined> {
514	    let task: DelegationTaskRecord | undefined;
515	    await this.update((data) => {
516	      const current = data.delegationTasks[taskId];
517	      if (!current) return;
518	      const next = normalizeDelegationTaskForRead(current, options);
519	      if (next !== current) {
520	        saveDelegationTask(data, next, 200);
521	      }
522	      task = next;
523	    });
524	    return task;
525	  }

527	  async listDelegationTasks(options: { room?: DelegationTaskRoomRef; roomConversationId?: string; sourceMachineId?: string; targetMachineId?: string; limit?: number; runningTimeoutMs?: number; now?: string } = {}): Promise<DelegationTaskRecord[]> {
528	    const limit = Math.max(1, options.limit ?? 50);
529	    const data = await this.update((draft) => {
530	      for (const [taskId, current] of Object.entries(draft.delegationTasks)) {
531	        const next = normalizeDelegationTaskForRead(current, options);
532	        if (next === current) continue;
533	        saveDelegationTask(draft, next, 200);
534	      }
535	    });
536	    return Object.values(data.delegationTasks)
537	      .filter((task) => !options.room || delegationRoomMatches(task.room, options.room))
538	      .filter((task) => !options.roomConversationId || task.room.conversationId === options.roomConversationId)
539	      .filter((task) => !options.sourceMachineId || task.sourceMachineId === options.sourceMachineId)
540	      .filter((task) => !options.targetMachineId || task.target.kind === "machine" && task.target.machineId === options.targetMachineId)
541	      .sort((left, right) => Date.parse(right.updatedAt) - Date.parse(left.updatedAt) || right.id.localeCompare(left.id))
542	      .slice(0, limit);
543	  }

642	  async cancelPendingApprovalsForSession(sessionKey: string, reason = "session cancelled", now = toIsoNow()): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord[]> {
643	    const cancelled: ApprovalRequestRecord[] = [];
644	    await this.update((data) => {
645	      for (const [approvalId, request] of Object.entries(data.approvalRequests)) {
646	        if (request.sessionKey !== sessionKey || request.status !== "pending") continue;
647	        const next: ApprovalRequestRecord = { ...request, status: "cancelled", resolvedAt: now, decision: "deny" };
648	        data.approvalRequests[approvalId] = next;
649	        cancelled.push(next);
650	        const audit: ApprovalAuditEvent = { eventId: `approval-cancel-${approvalId}-${now}`, kind: "cancelled", approvalId, sessionKey, sessionLabel: request.sessionLabel, toolName: request.toolName, category: request.category, matcherFingerprint: request.matcherFingerprint, requester: request.requester, summary: request.safeSummary, at: now, detail: reason };
651	        data.approvalAudit = [...data.approvalAudit, audit].slice(-200);
652	      }
653	    });
654	    return cancelled;
655	  }

657	  async markInFlightDelegationTasksStaleAfterRestart(now = toIsoNow()): Promise<DelegationTaskRecord[]> {

659	    await this.update((data) => {
660	      for (const [taskId, task] of Object.entries(data.delegationTasks)) {
661	        const next = markDelegationTaskStaleAfterRestart(task, now);
662	        if (next === task || next.status === task.status && next.updatedAt === task.updatedAt) continue;
663	        data.delegationTasks[taskId] = next;
664	        data.delegationAudit = [...data.delegationAudit, ...next.audit.slice(task.audit.length)].slice(-200);
665	        changed.push(next);
666	      }
667	    });
668	    return changed;
669	  }

671	  async recordLifecycleNotification(input: {
672	    channel: ChannelBinding["channel"];
673	    instanceId?: string;
674	    sessionKey: string;
675	    conversationId: string;
676	    userId: string;
677	    kind: RelayLifecycleEventKind;

679	    debounceMs?: number;
680	  }): Promise<RelayLifecycleNotificationDecision> {
681	    let decision: RelayLifecycleNotificationDecision | undefined;
682	    await this.update((data) => {
683	      const key = relayLifecycleStorageKey(input);
684	      const previous = data.lifecycleNotifications[key];
685	      decision = decideRelayLifecycleNotification({ ...input, previous });
686	      if (decision.shouldNotify && input.kind === "online") return;
687	      data.lifecycleNotifications[key] = {
688	        ...decision.record,
689	        lastNotifiedAt: previous?.lastNotifiedAt,
690	        lastEvent: previous?.lastEvent,
691	      };
692	    });
693	    return decision!;
694	  }

723	function activeTargetTelegramBindingConflicts(data: TunnelStoreData, input: SessionBindingMigrationInput, source: PersistedBindingRecord): boolean {
724	  const target = data.bindings[input.newSessionKey];
725	  return Boolean(target && (target.chatId !== source.chatId || target.userId !== source.userId));
726	}

728	function isMissingFileError(error: unknown): boolean {
729	  return typeof error === "object" && error !== null && "code" in error && (error as { code?: unknown }).code === "ENOENT";
730	}
731	
732	function lifecycleStateForNotification(kind: RelayLifecycleEventKind): "online" | "offline" | "disconnected" {
733	  if (kind === "online" || kind === "moved") return "online";
734	  if (kind === "offline") return "offline";
735	  return "disconnected";
736	}

738	function normalizePinLikeCode(value: string): string | undefined {
739	  const digits = value.replace(/[^0-9]/g, "");
740	  return digits.length === 6 ? `${digits.slice(0, 3)}-${digits.slice(3)}` : undefined;
741	}
742	
743	function pendingPairingLookupKeys(code: string): string[] {
744	  const keys = [sha256(code.trim())];
745	  const normalizedPin = normalizePinLikeCode(code);
746	  if (normalizedPin && normalizedPin !== code.trim()) keys.push(sha256(normalizedPin));
747	  return keys;
748	}
749	
750	function findPendingPairingEntryByCode(data: TunnelStoreData, code: string): { key: string; pairing: PendingPairingRecord } | undefined {
751	  for (const key of pendingPairingLookupKeys(code)) {
752	    const pairing = data.pendingPairings[key];
753	    if (pairing) return { key, pairing };
754	  }
755	  return undefined;
756	}
757	
758	function findPendingPairingByCode(data: TunnelStoreData, code: string): PendingPairingRecord | undefined {
759	  return findPendingPairingEntryByCode(data, code)?.pairing;
760	}

762	function trustedRelayUserStorageKey(channel: ChannelBinding["channel"], instanceId: string, userId: string): string {
763	  return `${channel}:${instanceId}:${userId}`;
764	}
765	
766	function channelSelectionStorageKey(channel: ChannelBinding["channel"], conversationId: string, userId: string): string {
767	  return `${channel}:${conversationId}:${userId}`;
768	}

770	function normalizeDelegationTaskForRead(task: DelegationTaskRecord, options: { runningTimeoutMs?: number; now?: string } = {}): DelegationTaskRecord {
771	  const now = options.now ?? toIsoNow();
772	  const expired = expireDelegationTaskIfNeeded(task, now);
773	  return options.runningTimeoutMs ? expireDelegationTaskIfRunningTimedOut(expired, options.runningTimeoutMs, now) : expired;
774	}
775	
776	function saveDelegationTask(data: TunnelStoreData, task: DelegationTaskRecord, maxAuditEntries: number): void {
777	  const existingEventIds = new Set(data.delegationTasks[task.id]?.audit.map((event) => event.eventId) ?? []);
778	  const newAuditEvents = task.audit.filter((event) => !existingEventIds.has(event.eventId));
779	  data.delegationTasks[task.id] = task;
780	  data.delegationAudit = [...data.delegationAudit, ...newAuditEvents].slice(-maxAuditEntries);
781	}
782	
783	function delegationTaskIncludesAudit(candidate: DelegationTaskRecord, current: DelegationTaskRecord): boolean {
784	  const candidateEventIds = new Set(candidate.audit.map((event) => event.eventId));
785	  return current.audit.every((event) => candidateEventIds.has(event.eventId));
786	}
787	
788	function delegationRoomMatches(left: DelegationTaskRoomRef, right: DelegationTaskRoomRef): boolean {
789	  return left.messenger === right.messenger
790	    && left.instanceId === right.instanceId
791	    && left.conversationId === right.conversationId
792	    && left.threadId === right.threadId;
793	}

795	function activeTelegramBindingFromData(data: TunnelStoreData, sessionKey: string, expected: { chatId?: number; userId?: number; includePaused?: boolean }): PersistedBindingRecord | undefined {
796	  const outcome = resolveTelegramBindingAuthority(bindingAuthorityStateFromData(data), { sessionKey, ...expected });
797	  return authorityOutcomeAllowsDelivery(outcome) && "status" in outcome.binding ? outcome.binding : undefined;
798	}
799	
800	function activeChannelBindingFromData(data: TunnelStoreData, channel: ChannelBinding["channel"], sessionKey: string, expected: { instanceId?: string; conversationId?: string; userId?: string; includePaused?: boolean }): ChannelPersistedBindingRecord | undefined {
801	  const outcome = resolveChannelBindingAuthority(bindingAuthorityStateFromData(data), { channel, sessionKey, ...expected });
802	  return authorityOutcomeAllowsDelivery(outcome) && "status" in outcome.binding ? outcome.binding : undefined;
803	}
804	
805	function revokeChannelBindingRecord(binding: ChannelPersistedBindingRecord, revokedAt: string): ChannelPersistedBindingRecord {
806	  return { ...binding, revokedAt, lastSeenAt: revokedAt, status: "revoked" };
807	}
808	
809	function clearSelectionForBinding(data: TunnelStoreData, binding: ChannelBinding, sessionKey: string): void {
810	  const selectionKey = channelSelectionStorageKey(binding.channel, binding.conversationId, binding.userId);
811	  if (data.activeChannelSelections[selectionKey]?.sessionKey === sessionKey) delete data.activeChannelSelections[selectionKey];
812	}
