```text
1	# Pi harness ecosystem snapshot
2	
3	This page records the assumptions behind `pia`, not a permanent verdict on fast
4	moving upstream projects. The compatibility snapshot reviewed and represented
5	by the test fixtures is **Pi 0.84.4** and **Oh My Pi 18.0.11**, as of
6	2026-08-30.
7	
8	## Upstream Pi
9	
10	Pi supports a global agent directory, project-local `.pi` configuration, and
11	the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` override. These primitives are sufficient for `pia`
12	to launch isolated full configurations, while repo-local settings and resources
13	can still participate according to Pi's trust and discovery rules. See Pi's
14	[settings](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md),
15	[environment variables](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/environment-variables.md),
16	and [packages](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/packages) documentation.
17	
18	Pi does not provide a single stable first-class abstraction that composes all
19	settings, skills, extensions, package references, prompts, and session policy as
20	a named inheritable profile. That is why `pia` switches the complete agent
21	directory and keeps combo inheritance explicit and copy-based.
22	
23	Two issue pages are easy to misread:
24	
25	- [#3590, layered config](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3590)
26	- [#7813, multiple settings profiles](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7813)
27	
28	Their closed status is easy to over-interpret, but each timeline contains the
29	GitHub Actions message that issues from new contributors are auto-closed
30	pending maintainer review. They are evidence that users asked
31	for these capabilities, **not** an explicit maintainer roadmap rejection. Any
32	future design review should re-check upstream rather than preserving either
33	interpretation as fact.
34	
35	## Oh My Pi
36	
37	OMP exposes named profiles through `omp --profile <name>` and has broader
38	configuration discovery and overlay behavior. A named profile relocates native
39	configuration and runtime resources, so `pia` uses an OMP profile named
40	`pia-<combo>` and resolves its actual path with OMP itself. See the upstream
41	[configuration and profile guide](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/config-usage.md).
42	
43	OMP's richer configuration system does not remove the need for a repository
44	contract: different resource types have different discovery rules, runtime
45	state must still stay out of Git, and a Pi combo should remain understandable
46	without translating it into OMP concepts. `pia` therefore presents the same
47	simple combo/source/runtime workflow for both engines and lets OMP own only its
48	native profile resolution.
49	
50	## MCP is an extension choice
51	
52	Do not describe `pi.mcp` as a Pi core package-manifest feature. The manifest
53	shape discussed in the original research belongs to an adapter/integration,
54	not upstream Pi's package contract. MCP support for a combo should identify the
55	specific extension it uses—for example the community
56	[`pi-mcp-adapter`](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-mcp-adapter)—and keep that
57	adapter's configuration inside the combo like any other harness dependency.
58	
59	This distinction matters for portability: a combo that depends on an adapter
60	must pin and test that adapter rather than assuming another Pi installation can
61	interpret an undocumented `pi.mcp` field.
62	
63	## Remote messaging is an external integration
64	
65	Pi packages and extensions can connect a session to Discord, Telegram, or other
66	messaging systems, and a future Pi-only combo may pin one of those integrations.
67	That does not make remote messaging a `pia` core capability. `pia` does not
68	provide a messaging transport, authentication or admission, live session
69	orchestration, sandboxing, durable delivery, or service supervision.
70	
71	Apply the same rule as for MCP: name the specific integration, pin it, and test
72	its behavior against the selected Pi version instead of attributing third-party
73	behavior to Pi itself. The Pi README links to the separate
74	[`earendil-works/pi-chat`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi-chat) project as
75	a chat-automation option; its shared organization and upstream link do not by
76	themselves establish a support contract or compatibility with this repository's
77	Pi snapshot.
78	
79	See the dated [IM gateway research](../backlog/pi-im-gateway.md) for the selected
80	session-router context contract, candidate evidence, and the gates for moving
81	from an external spike to an experimental combo or maintained service.
82	
83	## Why maintain another thin layer?
84	
85	There are many ready-made harnesses and profile managers. Use one of them when
86	its opinionated defaults already match the job. This repository is justified
87	when the goal is to:
88	
89	- keep experimental, learning, and production combos together;
90	- switch Pi and OMP through one predictable interface;
91	- review the exact Git-managed configuration before it reaches runtime;
92	- keep auth, sessions, packages, and caches private and mutable;
93	- reproduce selected behaviors from other harnesses without adopting all of
94	  their machinery.
95	
96	Research into [Claude Code](../backlog/claude-code-harness-to-pi.md),
97	[Codex](../backlog/codex-harness-to-pi.md), and
98	[OpenCode](../backlog/opencode-harness-to-pi.md) is intentionally deferred until
99	the base workflow has real usage data. Re-check upstream versions, docs, CLI
100	flags, and session formats before promoting any result to a production combo.
101
```

157	export async function runCombo({
158	  combo,
159	  stateRoot,
160	  cwd = process.cwd(),
161	  env = process.env,
162	  userArgs = [],
163	  commandRunner,
164	  spawnRunner = runInherited,
165	}: RunComboOptions): Promise<RunComboResult> {
166	  assertNoOwnedFlags(userArgs);
167	  const applied = await applyCombo({ combo, stateRoot, cwd, env, commandRunner });
168	  if (!applied.result.ok) {
169	    const reason = applied.result.reason || "runtime configuration has unresolved drift";
170	    throw new Error(`Refusing to launch ${combo.id}: ${reason}`);
171	  }
172	  await ensurePrivateDir(applied.sessionDir);
173	
174	  const childEnv = { ...env };
175	  delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR;

178	    childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR = applied.targetDir;

180	    delete childEnv.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR;
181	    delete childEnv.OMP_PROFILE;

183	    args.push(`--profile=${getOmpProfileName(combo)}`);
184	  }
185	  args.push(...combo.metadata.launchArgs, "--session-dir", applied.sessionDir, ...userArgs);
186	  const exitCode = await spawnRunner(binaryFor(combo.engine, env), args, { cwd, env: childEnv });
187	  return { exitCode, args, command: binaryFor(combo.engine, env), ...applied };

171	    encoding: "utf8",
172	    stdio: [options.input === undefined ? "ignore" : "pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
173	    input: options.input,
174	    env,
175	    cwd: options.cwd,
176	    maxBuffer: options.maxBuffer || 8 * 1024 * 1024,
177	  });
178	  if (result.error) {
179	    return { ok: false, status: null, stdout: "", stderr: result.error.message, error: result.error };
180	  }
181	  return {
182	    ok: result.status === 0,
183	    status: result.status,
184	    stdout: result.stdout || "",
185	    stderr: result.stderr || "",
186	  };
187	}
188	
189	export async function runInherited(
190	  command: string,
191	  args: readonly string[],
192	  options: InheritedProcessOptions = {},
193	): Promise<number> {
194	  return await new Promise<number>((resolve, reject) => {
195	    const env = options.env || process.env;
196	    const invocation = resolveCommandInvocation(command, args, env);
197	    const child = spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, {
198	      cwd: options.cwd,
199	      env,
200	      stdio: "inherit",
201	    });
202	    child.on("error", reject);
203	    child.on("exit", (code, signal) => {
204	      if (signal) {
205	        process.kill(process.pid, signal);
206	        return;
207	      }
208	      resolve(code ?? 1);
209	    });
210	  });
211	}
212	
213	export function commandExists(command: string): string | undefined {
214	  const probe = commandResult(command, ["--version"]);
215	  return probe.ok ? probe.stdout.trim() || probe.stderr.trim() : undefined;
216	}
217
```

```text
1	# Architecture
2	
3	`pia` separates version-controlled intent from mutable agent state. The Git
4	repository is the source of truth for combo definitions; it is never an agent's
5	live home directory.
6	
7	## Data layout
8	
9	```text
10	pi-agents/
11	  combos/<pi|omp>/<name>/
12	    combo.json             declarative metadata
13	    agent/                 complete managed config tree
14	  schema/combo.schema.json
15	  bin/pia
16	  src/*.ts                 Node-native erasable TypeScript
17	
18	${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/pi-agents/
19	  selection.json           value saved by `pia use`
20	
21	${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pi-agents/
22	  manifests/               last-applied managed-file hashes and modes
23	  runtime/pi/<name>/agent/ Pi configuration runtime
24	  sessions/                isolated/shared session roots
25	  handoffs/                generated private Markdown artifacts
26	```
27	
28	`PIA_SOURCE_ROOT` can point the CLI at another checkout. `PIA_STATE_HOME`
29	replaces the entire state root. These overrides are useful for tests and
30	advanced setups; normal users should let the CLI derive both paths.
31	
32	For Pi, `pia` launches with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set to the combo's runtime
33	directory. For OMP, it uses a native profile named `pia-<combo-name>` and asks
34	`omp --profile ... config path` for the real location instead of assuming a
35	home or XDG layout. `PIA_PI_BIN` and `PIA_OMP_BIN` can override the executable
36	names.
37	
38	## Source and runtime contract
39	
40	Only files below a combo's `agent/` directory are managed. Downloaded packages,
41	credentials, sessions, caches, blobs, databases, and any other runtime-created
42	files stay outside Git or remain unowned in the runtime tree.
43	
44	The source tree must not contain credentials, `.env` files, session/package/
45	cache stores, or symlinks. On POSIX systems runtime directories are created
46	with mode `0700`; managed files use `0600` or `0700` according to their
47	executable bit. Windows does not expose equivalent POSIX mode enforcement
48	through Node, so runtime files inherit the user's profile ACL and drift checks
49	compare content rather than synthetic mode bits there. Writes and manifest
50	replacement are atomic.
51	
52	The source uses only TypeScript syntax that Node can erase without code
53	generation. Runtime execution therefore stays build-free; `tsconfig.json` and
54	the development dependencies exist solely for strict `tsc --noEmit` checking.
55	
56	Known runtime/credential paths are rejected structurally. `npm run check` also
57	runs gitleaks over combo content when the binary is available, while CI and the
58	existing pre-commit stack enforce the same secret scan before source is shared.
59	
60	Each manifest records its exact absolute target and, for every managed relative
61	path, the content hash, executable bit, and mode. `pia apply` classifies paths
62	as follows:
63	
64	| Source/runtime state | Result |
65	|---|---|
66	| New source path, unused target | Create it |
67	| Source changed, runtime still at last applied value | Update it |
68	| Runtime changed independently | Refuse the whole apply |
69	| Source and runtime both changed | Refuse the whole apply |
70	| Source removed, runtime unchanged | Remove the stale managed path |
71	| Source removed, runtime changed | Refuse unless forced |
72	| Target-only path never owned by `pia` | Preserve and omit from normal diff |
73	| New source collides with an unowned path or non-file obstruction | Always refuse |
74	
75	`--dry-run` returns the same plan without writing. `--force` makes source win
76	for previously managed drift and conflicts, including modified stale files; it
77	does not overwrite unowned collisions. This keeps force bounded by the prior
78	manifest instead of turning it into a recursive replacement operation.
79	
80	Use `pia status <combo>` for a summary and `pia diff <combo> --runtime` for
81	managed path details before applying.
82	
83	## Selection and launch
84	
85	A combo is selected in this order:
86	
87	1. The combo argument passed to the command.
88	2. `PIA_COMBO`.
89	3. The persistent value written by `pia use`.
90	
91	`pia run [combo] -- <agent arguments>` first performs the same safe apply, then
92	combines the combo's checked-in `launchArgs` with trailing arguments and
93	forwards the child process's exit code. Drift, conflicts, unsafe source files,
94	or unowned collisions abort before launch. A stale parent digest emits a warning
95	but does not block a standalone child combo.
96	
97	Wrapper-owned routing/session flags and secret-bearing flags are rejected from
98	`launchArgs`; runtime invocation remains explicit. Session storage is resolved
99	from engine, combo history policy, and canonical working directory. See
100	[sessions and handoff](sessions-and-handoff.md).
101	
102	## Why copies instead of inheritance
103	
104	Pi does not expose a stable, general-purpose config inheritance contract, and
105	OMP's layers do not cover every harness asset uniformly. `pia derive` therefore
106	copies a complete combo and records its parent digest. The child remains usable
107	and understandable on its own. Parent changes produce a lineage warning and a
108	review workflow, never an implicit merge at launch time.
109	
110	Declarative inheritance and three-way sync are intentionally deferred until
111	real usage demonstrates enough repeated maintenance to justify their conflict
112	rules. The research checkpoint is tracked in
113	[the backlog](../backlog/declarative-inheritance-three-way-sync.md).
114
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/combos.md`

```text
1	# Combos
2	
3	A combo is one complete, selectable agent setup. Its identifier is
4	`<engine>/<name>`, where the engine is `pi` or `omp`. Names are 1–60 characters,
5	start with a lowercase letter or digit, use lowercase letters, digits, dots,
6	underscores, or hyphens, and do not end in a dot. The shared restriction keeps
7	the generated `pia-<name>` value valid as an OMP profile.
8	
9	## Directory and metadata
10	
11	```text
12	combos/pi/research/
13	  combo.json
14	  agent/
15	    settings.json
16	    AGENTS.md
17	    skills/
18	    extensions/
19	```
20	
21	`agent/` mirrors the configuration files that should be managed at runtime. It
22	must be a complete, readable setup rather than a delta against another combo.
23	
24	A minimal `combo.json` is:
25	
26	```json
27	{
28	  "$schema": "../../../schema/combo.schema.json",
29	  "schemaVersion": 1,
30	  "description": "Research-oriented upstream Pi harness.",
31	  "maturity": "experimental",
32	  "launchArgs": [],
33	  "history": {
34	    "mode": "isolated"
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	The fields are:
40	
41	- `schemaVersion`: currently `1`.
42	- `description`: a short human explanation of the combo's purpose.
43	- `maturity`: `experimental`, `learning`, or `production`.
44	- `launchArgs`: non-secret agent arguments applied on every launch.
45	- `history`: `isolated`, or `shared` with a named same-engine group.
46	- `derivedFrom` and `parentDigest`: a paired lineage reference written by
47	  `pia derive`.
48	
49	Example shared history policy:
50	
51	```json
52	{
53	  "history": {
54	    "mode": "shared",
55	    "group": "daily-coding"
56	  }
57	}
58	```
59	
60	Sharing is still separated by engine and canonical project directory. It does
61	not make Pi and OMP JSONL files interchangeable. Group names follow the same
62	1–60 character/no-trailing-dot safety rule as combo names.
63	
64	Do not put auth tokens, API keys, `.env` files, sessions, blobs, package stores,
65	or caches in `agent/`. Reference packages from configuration; let the harness
66	install or cache them in runtime state.
67	
68	## Derive and maintain a combo
69	
70	Create a child from an existing combo:
71	
72	```sh
73	pia derive pi/base pi/research
74	```
75	
76	This makes a full copy, sets `derivedFrom`, and records a digest of the reviewed
77	parent. There is no live inheritance. Edit the child normally and commit it as
78	a standalone configuration.
79	
80	When a parent changes:
81	
82	```sh
83	pia lineage pi/research
84	pia diff pi/research --parent
85	# manually copy or adapt only the changes you want
86	pia lineage pi/research --ack
87	```
88	
89	`--ack` only records the current parent digest. It must be run after the review,
90	not as a way to hide an unresolved warning. Lineage must remain within one
91	engine and cycles are rejected.
92	
93	## Inspect and use combos
94	
95	```sh
96	pia list
97	pia list --tree
98	pia list --json
99	
100	pia use pi/research
101	pia current
102	
103	pia status pi/research
104	pia diff pi/research --runtime
105	pia apply pi/research --dry-run
106	pia apply pi/research
107	pia run pi/research -- <pi arguments>
108	```
109	
110	`pia run` can omit its combo after `pia use` or `PIA_COMBO`; an explicit run
111	argument always wins. The management command signatures shown here require
112	explicit combo IDs so mutations and diagnostics have an unambiguous target.
113	
114	If a managed runtime file was edited directly, normal apply fails without
115	changing anything. Review the diff and either carry the intended edit back to
116	`agent/`, or use `pia apply <combo> --force` to discard drift on paths that
117	`pia` previously owned. Unmanaged runtime files are preserved.
118	
119	`launchArgs` cannot contain wrapper-owned options such as profile, session,
120	cwd, config, resume/fork routing, or API-key flags. Put one-off agent options
121	after `--`; keep secrets in the harness's private auth mechanism or environment.
122	
123	## Command map
124	
125	In the table, `<session-selector>` means either `--latest` or
126	`--session <id-or-absolute-path>`.
127	
128	| Command | Purpose |
129	|---|---|
130	| `pia list [--tree|--json]` | Discover combos and lineage |
131	| `pia use <combo>` / `pia current` | Save or print the default selection |
132	| `pia derive <parent> <child> [--description TEXT]` | Copy a combo and record lineage |
133	| `pia lineage <combo> [--ack]` | Inspect or acknowledge a parent digest |
134	| `pia status <combo>` | Summarise source/runtime health |
135	| `pia diff <combo> [--runtime|--parent]` | Show managed runtime or lineage differences |
136	| `pia apply <combo> [--dry-run|--force]` | Safely materialise source configuration |
137	| `pia run [combo] -- <args>` | Safely apply, then launch the selected harness |
138	| `pia sessions <combo>` | List sessions visible to that combo |
139	| `pia fork <from> <to> <session-selector> -- <args>` | Native same-engine session fork |
140	| `pia handoff <from> <to> <session-selector> --goal TEXT [--no-run] -- <args>` | Redacted context transfer |
141	| `pia doctor [--json]` | Check binaries, versions, source safety, and helpers |
142	| `pia completion <zsh\|bash\|powershell>` | Emit native shell completion code |
143
```
</details></tool-use>

### protocol/README.md
1-# @earendil-works/pi-protocol
2-
3:Runtime-neutral schemas, types, CBOR encoding, and byte-stream framing for the experimental pi protocol.
4-
5-Protocol version `1` uses binary messages with this wire layout:
6-
7-1. A four-byte unsigned big-endian payload length.
8:2. One definite-length CBOR item containing the message.
9-
10:The first client message is always `hello`, containing `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. Subsequent messages use correlated request/response envelopes and server event envelopes. Session and server snapshots are authoritative. Progress events are transient UI hints and must not be reduced into authoritative state. Transports complete authentication before protocol bytes are exchanged.
11-
12:Session lists contain `SessionMetadata`, the normalized durable metadata available without acquiring a session runtime. Only `id` and `createdAt` are required; `updatedAt`, `parentSessionId`, `sessionName`, and `cwd` are included when supported by the backing store. Runtime state such as phase, model, thinking level, attachment, and locking appears only in an acquired `SessionSnapshot`.
13-
14-## Validated message API
15-
16:`encodeClientMessage()` and `encodeServerMessage()` validate a message and return a complete framed `Uint8Array`. The incremental decoders accept arbitrary fragmentation or coalescing, so they work with streams, sockets, and custom byte transports.
17-
18-```ts
19-import {
--
28-  version: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
29-};
30-
31:transport.send(encodeClientMessage(hello));
32-
33-const decoder = createServerMessageDecoder({ maxFrameLength: 1024 * 1024 });
34-for (const message of decoder.push(incomingChunk)) {
--
37-decoder.end(); // Call when the byte stream closes to detect truncation.
38-```
39-
40:`ClientMessageDecoder` and `ServerMessageDecoder` are also available directly. Schema violations, malformed CBOR, and invalid framing throw `ProtocolValidationError`. Validation errors do not retain rejected payloads.
41-
42-`parseClientMessage()` and `parseServerMessage()` only validate already-decoded values. They do not parse JSON strings.
43-
44-## Transport support
45-
46:Every transport carries the same complete bytes: `[uint32-be CBOR length][CBOR payload]`. Transports may split or coalesce those bytes arbitrarily.
47-
48:This package does not bundle a transport. Consumers provide a byte-stream transport that preserves byte order and reports stream closure. Custom transports must handle arbitrary frame fragmentation and coalescing.
49-
50:All transports are untrusted. Configure matching frame limits and enforce access controls appropriate for the transport before exposing a connection to the protocol. Unix sockets can use filesystem permissions, while network transports can authenticate during connection establishment.
51-
52-## Encoding and framing
53-
54:`encodeCbor()` and `decodeCbor()` implement the protocol's strict RFC 8949 subset. `encodeFrame()` and `FrameDecoder` handle framing independently of schemas and CBOR.
55-
56:The CBOR subset supports:
57-
58-- `null` and booleans
59-- finite numbers, with integers restricted to JavaScript's safe range and non-integers encoded as float64
--
62-- definite-length arrays
63-- definite-length maps represented by objects with unique string keys
64-
65:Undefined object properties are omitted. JSON-valued protocol fields reject CBOR byte strings and non-plain objects. Top-level undefined, undefined array entries, sparse arrays, non-finite or unsafe numbers, tags, indefinite-length items, malformed UTF-8, trailing data, excessive nesting, and oversized values are rejected.
66-
67:Default limits are 16 MiB per CBOR payload/frame, 1,000,000 array elements or map entries, and 64 nested item levels. Options can configure these limits. A frame decoder validates the declared length before buffering payload bytes.
68-
69:All schemas reject unknown object properties. The protocol is experimental and has no compatibility guarantees.

### client/README.md
1:# @earendil-works/pi-client
2-
3:Transport-neutral client for remote pi sessions. `PiClient` exchanges length-prefixed CBOR messages through a small `ByteTransport` interface. The package has no Node-specific imports.
4-
5-```ts
6:import { PiClient, type ByteTransportFactory } from "@earendil-works/pi-client";
7-
8:const transportFactory: ByteTransportFactory = async (handlers) => {
9:  // Connect using WebSocket, Unix socket, or another ordered byte transport.
10-  return {
11-    async send(chunk) {
12-      // Deliver chunks in invocation order and honor backpressure.
--
15-  };
16-};
17-
18:const client = new PiClient({ transportFactory });
19:await client.connect();
20:const session = await client.createSession({ cwd: "/workspace" });
21:const unsubscribe = session.subscribe((snapshot) => render(snapshot));
22:await session.prompt("Inspect this project");
23-unsubscribe();
24-```
25-
26:Call `handlers.onData(chunk)` for inbound bytes, `handlers.onClose()` for an orderly terminal close, and `handlers.onError(error)` for transport failures. A factory must create a fresh transport for every connection attempt and complete any transport-specific authentication before resolving. For example, a WebSocket factory can provide credentials in its upgrade request.
27-
28:`PiClient` does not reconnect automatically. Call `reconnect()` after disconnection. One connection can attach several sessions. Requests are correlated by ID. Server snapshots and successful response snapshots are authoritative, while progress events do not mutate snapshot state optimistically. Read cached session metadata from `client.snapshot?.sessions`; call `listSessions()` to request refreshed durable metadata from the server. Runtime state is available after acquiring a session.
29-
30:`acquireSession()` returns an independent `SessionLease`; leases cannot be constructed directly. Use `{ mode: "exclusive" }` for a lifecycle or mutation coordinator and `{ mode: "shared" }` when multiple low-level consumers intentionally share the session. Exclusive acquisition fails with `PiSessionOwnershipError` while any lease exists, and shared acquisition fails while an exclusive lease exists. `attachSession()` is a shared-acquisition convenience method. `createSession()` returns an exclusive lease for the newly created session.
31-
32:Calling `dispose()` or `detach()` releases only that lease. A lease rejects commands as soon as release begins. The client sends the protocol detach request after the final lease is released. If explicit `detach()` fails, the lease becomes active again for retry. If cleanup-oriented `dispose()` fails, it reports the protocol error but relinquishes local ownership; `PiClient` reconciles the failed protocol cleanup before the next acquisition. A released lease becomes unavailable without affecting other shared leases. Server removal or disconnection invalidates every lease for the affected attachment, and disposing an invalidated lease is a no-op. Commands fail with `PiDisconnectedError` while the client is disconnected and `PiSessionDetachedError` when the client is connected but a lease is releasing, released, or invalidated. Leases implement `AsyncDisposable`.
33-
34:`subscribe()` observes authoritative snapshots. `onEvent()` observes protocol events. Both return an unsubscribe function. Structured errors returned by the server are exposed as `PiServerError`.
35-
36-## Limits and security
37-
38:`PiClientOptions.maxFrameLength` bounds inbound and outbound CBOR payloads. Configure matching limits on the client and server. Transports should separately bound queued outbound bytes and preserve send order.
39-
40:Treat peers as untrusted. Use a secure transport with appropriate access controls and authenticate during transport establishment.
41-
42-Subscriber exceptions are isolated from protocol state. Set `onListenerError` in `PiClientOptions` to report them to application logging or diagnostics.
43-
44-## Unix-domain sockets
45-
46:Node.js and Bun consumers can use the separately exported Unix-domain socket transport:

50:import { createUnixTransportFactory } from "@earendil-works/pi-client/unix";
51-
52:const client = new PiClient({

54-    path: "/tmp/pi.sock",
55-  }),
56-});
57-
58:await client.connect();
59-```
60-
61:`maxPendingBytes` bounds queued outbound data. It defaults to four times the protocol frame limit. The transport preserves send order and waits for socket backpressure before resolving each send.
62-
63:The `@earendil-works/pi-client` root remains transport- and runtime-neutral. Importing the Node-compatible transport requires the explicit `@earendil-works/pi-client/unix` subpath.

35-
36:`PiServer` composes transport listeners through the `PiServerListener` interface. Each listener must complete any transport-specific authentication and authorization before passing a connection to `PiServer`. For example, a WebSocket listener can validate credentials during the HTTP upgrade, while the Unix listener relies on socket filesystem permissions. The Unix submodule exports the `createUnixListener()` building block and `createUnixServer()` preset, keeping the common case concise without coupling the primary server to Unix sockets. The listener uses length-prefixed CBOR messages from `@earendil-works/pi-protocol`.
37-
38-This package does not provide a standalone CLI or coding-agent service. Applications supply the `PiServerService` implementation.
39-
40:`PiServerService.listSessions()` returns protocol `SessionMetadata`, not acquired runtime state. Services should map the durable fields their storage supports and may omit `updatedAt`, `parentSessionId`, `sessionName`, and `cwd`. `PiServer` refreshes available metadata from live snapshots without requiring stored sessions to fabricate phase, model, thinking-level, attachment, or lock values.
41-
42-## Transport testing
43-
44:Custom transports can use `@earendil-works/pi-server/testing` for deterministic protocol conformance tests. It exports `createTestServer()`, `TestServerService`, `ProtocolTestClient`, and the transport-neutral `WireChannel` contract. `connectUnixTestClient()` is provided for Unix transport tests.
45-
46-## `pi-ai` protocol bridge
47-
48-`@earendil-works/pi-ai` domain objects and `@earendil-works/pi-protocol` wire DTOs remain independent. This package owns their boundary and exports `toProtocolModelMetadata()`, `toProtocolAssistantMessage()`, `toProtocolUserMessage()`, and `toProtocolToolResultMessage()`.
49-
50:The adapters reject invalid tool inputs, identifiers, timestamps, and mismatched tool results; `toProtocolToolResultMessage()` requires the original `ToolCall` so it can verify the association and convert its arguments itself. Diagnostic details are explicitly sanitized. Closed `pi-ai` unions are mapped exhaustively, and compile-time field manifests enumerate current `pi-ai` properties so additions require an explicit review. The protocol mirrors `pi-ai` vocabulary such as `toolCall` and `toolUse` where the semantics are identical. Protocol schemas enforce consistent lifecycle states, and tests encode adapter output through the runtime schemas so incompatible changes fail in the bridging package.
```

4-
5-Extensions are TypeScript modules that extend pi's behavior. They can subscribe to lifecycle events, register custom tools callable by the LLM, add commands, and more.
6-
7-> **Placement for /reload:** Put extensions in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` (global) or `.pi/extensions/` (project-local) for auto-discovery. Use `pi -e ./path.ts` only for quick tests. Extensions in auto-discovered locations can be hot-reloaded with `/reload`.
8-
9-**Key capabilities:**
10-- **Custom tools** - Register tools the LLM can call via `pi.registerTool()`
11-- **Event interception** - Block or modify tool calls, inject context, customize compaction
12:- **User interaction** - Prompt users via `ctx.ui` (select, confirm, input, notify)
13:- **Custom UI components** - Full TUI components with keyboard input via `ctx.ui.custom()` for complex interactions
14-- **Custom commands** - Register commands like `/mycommand` via `pi.registerCommand()`
15-- **Session persistence** - Store state that survives restarts via `pi.appendEntry()`
16-- **Custom rendering** - Control how tool calls/results and messages appear in TUI
17-
18-**Example use cases:**
19-- Permission gates (confirm before `rm -rf`, `sudo`, etc.)
20-- Git checkpointing (stash at each turn, restore on branch)
21-- Path protection (block writes to `.env`, `node_modules/`)

1-# RPC Mode
2-
3:RPC mode enables headless operation of the coding agent via a JSON protocol over stdin/stdout. This is useful for embedding the agent in other applications, IDEs, or custom UIs.
4-
5:**Note for Node.js/TypeScript users**: If you're building a Node.js application, consider using `AgentSession` directly from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` instead of spawning a subprocess. See [`src/core/agent-session.ts`](../src/core/agent-session.ts) for the API. For a subprocess-based TypeScript client, see [`src/modes/rpc/rpc-client.ts`](../src/modes/rpc/rpc-client.ts).
6-
7-## Starting RPC Mode
8-
9-```bash
10-pi --mode rpc [options]
11-```
12-
13-Common options:
14-- `--provider <name>`: Set the LLM provider (anthropic, openai, google, etc.)
15-- `--model <pattern>`: Model pattern or ID (supports `provider/id` and optional `:<thinking>`)
16:- `--name <name>` / `-n <name>`: Set the session display name at startup
17:- `--no-session`: Disable session persistence
18:- `--session-dir <path>`: Custom session storage directory
19-
20-## Protocol Overview
21-
22:- **Commands**: JSON objects sent to stdin, one per line
23-- **Responses**: JSON objects with `type: "response"` indicating command success/failure
24:- **Events**: Agent events streamed to stdout as JSON lines
25-
26-All commands support an optional `id` field for request/response correlation. If provided, the corresponding response will include the same `id`. `bash_execution_update` events also include the `id` of their originating `bash` command.
27-
28-### Framing
29-
30-RPC mode uses strict JSONL semantics with LF (`\n`) as the only record delimiter.
31-
32-This matters for clients:
33-- Split records on `\n` only
34-- Accept optional `\r\n` input by stripping a trailing `\r`
35-- Do not use generic line readers that treat Unicode separators as newlines
36-

113	
114	Session replacement APIs such as new-session, resume, fork, and import live on `AgentSessionRuntime`, not on `AgentSession`.
115	
116	### createAgentSessionRuntime() and AgentSessionRuntime
117	
118	Use the runtime API when you need to replace the active session and rebuild cwd-bound runtime state.
119	This is the same layer used by the built-in interactive, print, and RPC modes.
120	
121	`createAgentSessionRuntime()` takes a runtime factory plus the initial cwd/session target. The factory closes over process-global fixed inputs, recreates cwd-bound services for the effective cwd, resolves session options against those services, and returns a full runtime result.
122	
123	```typescript
124	import {
125	  type CreateAgentSessionRuntimeFactory,
126	  createAgentSessionFromServices,
127	  createAgentSessionRuntime,
128	  createAgentSessionServices,
129	  getAgentDir,
130	  SessionManager,
131	} from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
132	
133	const createRuntime: CreateAgentSessionRuntimeFactory = async ({ cwd, sessionManager, sessionStartEvent }) => {
134	  const services = await createAgentSessionServices({ cwd });
135	  return {
136	    ...(await createAgentSessionFromServices({
137	      services,
138	      sessionManager,
139	      sessionStartEvent,
140	    })),
141	    services,
142	    diagnostics: services.diagnostics,
143	  };
144	};
145	
146	const runtime = await createAgentSessionRuntime(createRuntime, {
147	  cwd: process.cwd(),
148	  agentDir: getAgentDir(),
149	  sessionManager: SessionManager.create(process.cwd()),
150	});
151	```
152	
153	`AgentSessionRuntime` owns replacement of the active runtime across:
154	
155	- `newSession()`
156	- `switchSession()`
157	- `fork()`
158	- clone flows via `fork(entryId, { position: "at" })`
159	- `importFromJsonl()`
160	
161	Important behavior:
162	
163	- `runtime.session` changes after those operations
164	- event subscriptions are attached to a specific `AgentSession`, so re-subscribe after replacement
165	- if you use extensions, call `runtime.session.bindExtensions(...)` again for the new session
166	- creation returns diagnostics on `runtime.diagnostics`
167	- if runtime creation or replacement fails, the method throws and the caller decides how to handle it
168	
169	```typescript
170	let session = runtime.session;
171	let unsubscribe = session.subscribe(() => {});
172	
173	await runtime.newSession();
174	
175	unsubscribe();
176	session = runtime.session;
177	unsubscribe = session.subscribe(() => {});
178	```

350	
351	### Startup Events
352	
353	#### project_trust
354	
355	Fired before pi decides whether to trust a project with dynamic configs (`.pi` or `.agents/skills`). It runs during startup and when session replacement (for example `/resume`) enters a cwd whose trust has not been resolved in the current process. Only user/global extensions and CLI `-e` extensions participate; project-local extensions are not loaded until after trust is resolved.
356	
357	```typescript
358	pi.on("project_trust", async (event, ctx) => {
359	  // event.cwd - current working directory
360	  // ctx has a limited trust context: cwd, mode, hasUI, and select/confirm/input/notify UI helpers
361	  if (await ctx.ui.confirm("Trust project?", event.cwd)) {
362	    return { trusted: "yes", remember: true };
363	  }
364	  return { trusted: "undecided" };
365	});
366	```
367	
368	A `project_trust` handler must return `{ trusted: "yes" | "no" | "undecided" }`. A user/global or CLI extension that returns `"yes"` or `"no"` owns the decision; the first yes/no decision wins and suppresses the built-in trust prompt. Use `remember: true` to persist a yes/no decision; otherwise it applies only to the current process. Return `"undecided"` to let later handlers or the built-in trust flow decide. Check `ctx.hasUI` before prompting. If no handler returns yes/no, normal trust resolution continues: saved `trust.json` decisions apply first, then `defaultProjectTrust` controls whether pi asks, trusts, or declines by default.
369	
370	### Resource Events
371	
372	#### resources_discover
373	
374	Fired after `session_start` so extensions can contribute additional skill, prompt, and theme paths.
375	The startup path uses `reason: "startup"`. Reload uses `reason: "reload"`.
376	
377	```typescript
378	pi.on("resources_discover", async (event, _ctx) => {
379	  // event.cwd - current working directory
380	  // event.reason - "startup" | "reload"
381	  return {
382	    skillPaths: ["/path/to/skills"],
383	    promptPaths: ["/path/to/prompts"],
384	    themePaths: ["/path/to/themes"],
385	  };
386	});
387	```

```text
1	# PiRelay
2	
3	![PiRelay logo](docs/logo.png)
4	
5	**PiRelay** is a messenger bridge for live Pi sessions.
6	
7	It pairs Telegram, Discord, or Slack chats with the exact Pi session you are using, then lets you monitor progress, receive completion notifications, and send prompts or control commands back into that same local Pi session.
8	
9	The npm package is `@zylab/pirelay`. The canonical Pi command family is `/relay ...`; the old `/telegram-tunnel ...` namespace has been removed.
10	
11	## What PiRelay does
12	
13	PiRelay keeps Pi local-first. It does not replace the terminal UI or start a hidden standalone agent. Instead, it registers the current Pi session with a local relay runtime and lets an authorized messenger chat steer that session remotely.
14	
15	Typical flow:
16	
17	1. start working in Pi locally
18	2. configure one messenger with `/relay setup <telegram|discord|slack>`
19	3. run `/relay connect <messenger>`
20	4. scan/open the QR/deep link or copy the pairing command
21	5. approve or trust the remote user locally if prompted
22	6. receive updates and send prompts while the Pi session stays usable locally
23	
24	## Supported messengers
25	
26	| Messenger | Current support | Reliable command form |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| Telegram | private bot chat, media bridge, inline actions, multi-session broker, BotCommand menu | `/status`, `/full`, `/progress verbose` |
29	| Discord | live DM-first bot runtime, optional explicit guild/channel control, best-effort native `/relay` | `relay status`, `relay full`, `relay progress verbose` |
30	| Slack | Socket Mode live runtime, App Home DM pairing, optional explicit channel/thread control, `/relay` manifest surface | `relay status`, `relay full`, `relay progress verbose` |
31	
32	Discord and Slack still document text prefixes first because native slash commands require platform sync/manifest delivery and can be stale or intercepted by another app.
33	
34	## Features
35	
36	### Pairing and session routing
37	
38	- pairs Telegram private chats, Discord DMs, Slack App Home DMs, or explicitly enabled Slack/Discord channels with the current Pi session
39	- uses expiring, single-use pairing payloads or mobile-friendly PIN commands
40	- closes the local pairing QR/dialog automatically when pairing completes
41	- shows local pairing completion notifications consistently across messengers
42	- restores non-secret binding metadata when a Pi session resumes with `pi --continue`
43	- supports multiple concurrently registered Pi sessions through one local broker per `{stateDir, bot token hash, brokerNamespace}` scope
44	- exposes session selection commands when more than one session is paired to the same chat and hides superseded same-workspace offline sessions by default
45	
46	### Remote prompting and control
47	
48	- plain authorized text becomes a Pi prompt when the session is idle
49	- while Pi is busy, prompts are queued as follow-ups by default or steered explicitly when configured
50	- Messenger image attachments become Pi image prompts when the selected model supports image input; GIF input is converted to its first frame
51	- Discord and Slack expose the same command semantics with platform-specific text prefixes
52	- Slack channel/thread prompts are gated by `slack.allowChannelMessages` and an explicit channel pairing
53	
54	### Progress and activity feedback
55	
56	- Telegram uses Bot API chat actions such as `typing...` where available
57	- Discord uses typing activity where available
58	- Slack uses a `:thinking_face:` reaction on accepted prompts when the app has `reactions:write`
59	- Slack falls back to a thread-aware ephemeral `Pi is working…` message when reactions are unavailable
60	- progress notifications support `quiet`, `normal`, `verbose`, and `completion-only`
61	- Telegram `/recent` and Discord/Slack `relay recent` show recent safe activity
62	
63	### Long-output and answer workflow
64	
65	- sends summaries, full output, and latest assistant text with platform-aware chunking/fallbacks
66	- detects structured choices and question sets in the latest completed assistant output
67	- supports Telegram inline buttons for recognized choices
68	- supports direct short option replies and explicit `answer` drafts
69	- adds one-click **Show in chat** and **Download .md** actions where Telegram supports them
70	- renders supported Markdown (bold, code, links, code blocks, and tables) for Telegram chat when it fits safe message limits, with plain-text fallback otherwise; table outputs also expose Markdown download actions
71	
72	### Image bridge
73	
74	- accepts Telegram photos plus messenger image documents/attachments after authorization: JPEG/PNG/WebP directly, and GIF by first-frame conversion
75	- uses the Telegram caption as prompt text, or a safe image-inspection fallback for image-only messages
76	- rejects image prompts when the selected Pi model does not support image input
77	- exposes latest tool-result image outputs and safe latest-turn workspace image references with `/images`
78	- supports `/send-image <relative-path>` for explicit delivery of validated workspace PNG/JPEG/WebP files; GIF conversion is inbound-only
79	- does not browse arbitrary workspace files or automatically echo local/remote input images
80	
81	### Safety and resilience
82	
83	- authorization happens before prompt injection, media download, callbacks, or control actions
84	- pairing links/PINs expire and are single-use
85	- raw bot tokens, signing secrets, app tokens, hidden prompts, tool internals, and transcripts are not persisted in relay state
86	- config writer stores secret env var names such as `tokenEnv`, `signingSecretEnv`, and `appTokenEnv`, not resolved secret values
87	- Telegram/Discord/Slack API limitations are handled with chunking, retry/backoff, explicit unsupported-feature messages, and offline/busy responses
88	
89	## Requirements
90	
91	- Pi installed and working
92	- Node.js compatible with this package (`>=20.6.0`)
93	- at least one configured messenger:
94	  - Telegram bot token from BotFather
95	  - Discord bot token and application id
96	  - Slack bot token, signing secret, and usually Socket Mode app token
97	
98	## Installation
99	
100	Install from npm when available:
101	
102	```bash
103	pi install npm:@zylab/pirelay
104	```
105	
106	Install from GitHub or a local checkout during development:
107	
108	```bash
109	pi install https://github.com/zikolach/pirelay
110	pi install /absolute/path/to/pirelay
111	```
112	
113	For a one-off run without adding it to settings:
114	
115	```bash
116	pi -e npm:@zylab/pirelay
117	```
118	
119	## Quick start
120	
121	### 1. Choose and configure a messenger
122	
123	Run the setup wizard inside Pi:
124	
125	```text
126	/relay setup telegram
127	/relay setup discord
128	/relay setup slack
129	```
130	
131	The setup wizard is secret-safe and tab-based. It shows diagnostics, env snippets, config snippets, links/QR guidance, troubleshooting, and for Slack a copyable app manifest that includes App Home, interactivity, scopes, events, and `/relay`.
132	
133	Useful setup actions:
134	
135	- `c` copies placeholder env exports to the system clipboard, with Pi editor fallback
136	- `w` writes/updates canonical config from currently defined env vars without storing secret values
137	- Slack-only `m` copies a secret-free Slack app manifest
138	
139	### 2. Pair the current session
140	
141	```text
142	/relay connect telegram [name]
143	/relay connect discord [name]
144	/relay connect slack [name]
145	```
146	
147	Then follow the messenger-specific instructions:
148	
149	- Telegram: scan/open the bot deep link and press **Start**
150	- Discord: DM the bot with `relay pair 123-456`
151	- Slack: open the App Home DM and send `relay pair 123-456`, or invite the app to a channel and paste the command there after enabling `slack.allowChannelMessages`
152	
153	If the remote identity is not already allow-listed or trusted, Pi asks locally whether to allow, trust, or deny the pairing.
154	
155	### 3. Check status remotely
156	
157	```text
158	/status               # Telegram
159	relay status          # Discord
160	relay status        # Slack
161	```
162	
163	## Messenger setup details
164	
165	### Telegram
166	
167	Create a bot with [BotFather](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather), then set one of:
168	
169	```bash
170	export PI_RELAY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="123456789:AA..."
171	# legacy alias still supported:
172	export TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="123456789:AA..."
173	```
174	
175	Optional allow-list:
176	
177	```bash
178	export PI_RELAY_TELEGRAM_ALLOW_USER_IDS="123456789"
179	```
180	
181	After startup validation, PiRelay best-effort registers Telegram's bot command menu from the same canonical command registry used by `/help`. Hyphenated commands use Telegram-safe aliases such as `/sendfile` and `/sendimage`; `/send-file` and `/send-image` text remain supported.
182	
183	### Discord
184	
185	Create an application/bot in the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/docs/quick-start/getting-started).
186	
187	Recommended env:
188	
189	```bash
190	export PI_RELAY_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN="..."
191	export PI_RELAY_DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID="[REDACTED:discord-client-id]"
192	export PI_RELAY_DISCORD_ALLOW_USER_IDS="[REDACTED:discord-client-id]"
193	```
194	
195	Enable **Message Content Intent** for plain DM prompts and `relay <command>` text controls. Invite with `bot applications.commands` scope and `permissions=0` for DM-first operation. PiRelay best-effort syncs one native `/relay` command with subcommands after login, but `relay <command>` text remains the reliable fallback, especially in shared rooms. Guild/channel control requires explicit config.
196	
197	### Slack
198	
199	Create a Slack app at <https://api.slack.com/apps>. `/relay setup slack` can copy a ready-to-paste app manifest including the `/relay` slash command. Reinstall/update the app after adding slash commands, scopes, events, or interactivity.
200	
201	Recommended Socket Mode env:
202	
203	```bash
204	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-..."
205	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET="..."
206	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_APP_TOKEN="xapp-..."
207	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_APP_ID="A0123456789"
208	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_WORKSPACE_ID="T0123456789"
209	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_ALLOW_USER_IDS="U0123456789"
210	```
211	
212	Slack app requirements:
213	
214	- Socket Mode enabled for local Pi usage
215	- App Home → Messages Tab enabled so users can DM the app
216	- `message.im` event for App Home DMs
217	- interactivity enabled and the `/relay` slash command installed for native slash-command discovery
218	- bot scopes including `chat:write`, `im:history`, `im:read`, `reactions:write`, and `files:write` for image/file delivery
219	- reinstall the app after scope, slash-command, interactivity, or App Home changes
220	
221	The `/relay <command>` native slash command is a discoverability layer and is requester-scoped when Slack provides a response URL. Plain `relay <command>` text remains the reliable fallback when the slash command has not been installed, synced, or delivered. Older Slack `pirelay <command>` examples are no longer accepted; use `relay <command>` for a single Discord/Slack text prefix.
222	
223	Slack channel/thread control is explicit:
224	
225	```bash
226	export PI_RELAY_SLACK_ALLOW_CHANNEL_MESSAGES=true
227	```
228	
229	Then invite the app to the channel and pair in that channel/thread with `relay pair <pin>`.
230	
231	## Local Pi commands
232	
233	| Command | Purpose |
234	|---|---|
235	| `/relay setup <telegram\|discord\|slack>` | open setup wizard or show headless setup guidance |
236	| `/relay connect <telegram\|discord\|slack> [name]` | create an expiring pairing flow for the current session |
237	| `/relay doctor` | diagnose configured relay channels, credentials, allow-lists, approval gates, and config/state permissions |
238	| `/relay approvals` | show recent non-secret approval-gate audit events for the current session |
239	| `/relay status` | show local relay status for the current session |
240	| `/relay send-file <telegram\|discord\|slack\|messenger:instance\|all> <relative-path> [caption]` | send an explicit safe workspace file/artifact to paired messenger chat(s) |
241	| `/relay trusted` | list locally trusted relay users |
242	| `/relay untrust <messenger> <userId>` | revoke local relay trust |
243	| `/relay disconnect` | locally disconnect the current Pi session from all paired messenger bindings |
244	
245	## Remote messenger commands
246	
247	| Purpose | Telegram | Discord/Slack text | Native slash (best-effort) |
248	|---|---|---|---|
249	| help | `/help` (also Telegram menu) | `relay help` | `/relay help` |
250	| status dashboard | `/status` | `relay status` | `/relay status` |
251	| list sessions | `/sessions` | `relay sessions` | `/relay sessions` |
252	| select session | `/use <session>` | `relay use <session>` | `/relay use <session>` |
253	| forget offline session | `/forget <session>` | `relay forget <session>` | `/relay forget <session>` |
254	| one-shot prompt | `/to <session> <prompt>` | `relay to <session> <prompt>` | `/relay to <session> <prompt>` |
255	| start replacement session | `/new` | `relay new` | `/relay new` |
256	| progress mode | `/progress <mode>` | `relay progress <mode>` | `/relay progress <mode>` |
257	| current progress mode | `/progress` | `relay progress` | `/relay progress` |
258	| alias current session | `/alias <name\|clear>` | `relay alias <name\|clear>` | `/relay alias <name\|clear>` |
259	| recent activity | `/recent` or `/activity` | `relay recent` or `relay activity` | `/relay recent` or `/relay activity` |
260	| latest summary | `/summary` | `relay summary` | `/relay summary` |
261	| full output | `/full` | `relay full` | `/relay full` |
262	| list allowed local skills | `/skills` | `relay skills` | `/relay skills` |
263	| invoke allowed local skill | `/skill <name> [input]` | `relay skill <name> [input]` | `/relay skill <name> [input]` |
264	| cancel pending skill input | `/cancel` or `/skill cancel` | `relay cancel` or `relay skill cancel` | `/relay cancel` |
265	| latest images | `/images` | `relay images` | `/relay images` |
266	| send workspace image | `/send-image <path>` | `relay send-image <path>` | `/relay send-image <path>` |
267	| send safe workspace file to requester | `/send-file <path> [caption]` | `relay send-file <path> [caption]` | `/relay send-file <path> [caption]` |
268	| steer active run | `/steer <text>` | `relay steer <text>` | `/relay steer <text>` |
269	| queue follow-up | `/followup <text>` | `relay followup <text>` | `/relay followup <text>` |
270	| abort current run | `/abort` | `relay abort` | `/relay abort` |
271	| compact context | `/compact` | `relay compact` | `/relay compact` |
272	| pause delivery | `/pause` | `relay pause` | `/relay pause` |
273	| resume delivery | `/resume` | `relay resume` | `/relay resume` |
274	| disconnect binding | `/disconnect` | `relay disconnect` | `/relay disconnect` |
275	| create delegation task (opt-in shared rooms) | `/delegate <machine\|#capability> <goal>` | `relay delegate <machine\|#capability> <goal>` | `/relay delegate <machine\|#capability> <goal>` |
276	| control delegation task | `/task@<bot_username> <claim\|decline\|cancel\|status\|history> [task-id]` (or `/task <claim\|decline\|cancel\|status\|history> [task-id]` in private/other clients) | `relay task <claim\|decline\|cancel\|status\|history> [task-id]` | `/relay task <claim\|decline\|cancel\|status\|history> [task-id]` |
277	
278	`quiet`, `normal`, `verbose`, and `completion-only` are valid progress modes. Progress mode controls non-terminal progress noise: quiet suppresses progress updates, completion-only sends final results plus safe compaction notifications, normal sends coalesced milestone progress, and verbose additionally includes safe visible model/tool snapshots at a shorter interval. Tool progress in normal/verbose modes is summarized as a bounded live card with safe intent labels such as `▶ bash: npm test`, `✓ read: extensions/relay/runtime/extension-runtime.ts`, or `✕ rg: pattern in extensions`, plus aggregate counts like `tools: bash×2 read×4`; it never includes tool output, file contents, replacement text, raw transcripts, or arbitrary custom-tool arguments. Progress updates are deduplicated/coalesced, and supported messengers update the same live progress message in place where possible instead of posting every raw Pi stream event. Terminal notifications still deliver the final assistant answer when it fits safe platform limits, splitting by paragraphs within platform limits and falling back to a Markdown document when an adapter supports files and the output is too large for a reasonable chat burst.
279	
280	Remote `/disconnect` is scoped to the requesting chat/conversation only: it revokes that Telegram, Discord, or Slack binding and suppresses future session output/buttons there, without disconnecting other messengers that remain paired to the same Pi session. Local `/relay disconnect` is broader and disconnects the current session from all paired messenger bindings.
281	
282	Remote `/new` starts a replacement session only for the selected online, idle Pi route; it does not start or resume an offline Pi process. Busy routes refuse the request and suggest waiting or using `/abort`. When Pi provides safe command-capable session control, eligible requester bindings and active selections move to the replacement session automatically; unsupported routes return an explicit limitation. Local `/new` uses the same short, strict same-machine/same-workspace handoff and otherwise falls back to normal offline/reconnect behavior.
283	
284	Remote `send-file` is requester-scoped: an authorized Telegram/Discord/Slack user may request a workspace-relative, validated path and PiRelay uploads it only back to that same conversation/thread. Targeted fan-out remains local-only via `/relay send-file <messenger|messenger:instance|all> <relative-path> [caption]`; remote forms must not include messenger targets such as `all` or `slack`.
285	
286	Remote skill invocation is opt-in via `skills.enabled`. When enabled, `/skills` lists allowed local Pi skills from the live session command registry, and `/skill <name> [input]` asks Pi to use that skill. If input is omitted, the next message from the same authorized requester is used as skill input; `/cancel` or `/skill cancel` cancels the pending input.
287	
288	Approval gates are disabled by default and act only as remote confirmation guardrails for sensitive Pi tool calls reached from remote messenger-owned turns, such as `git push`, package publishing, destructive shell commands, or protected file writes. Configure `approvalGates.enabled: true` plus explicit rules; matching remote operations pause and ask the active authorized requester to Approve once, Approve for session, or Deny. Local Pi prompts never require messenger approval. Timeout, stale/revoked/paused bindings, offline sessions, or delivery failures block remote gated operations by default. See `docs/config.md` for examples.
289	
290	Communication diagnostics are disabled by default. When troubleshooting missing final responses, broker routing, or messenger delivery, enable `communicationDiagnostics.enabled` temporarily and inspect the local JSONL log; see `docs/communication-diagnostics.md`. Remote commands do not upload these logs automatically.
291	
292	Agent delegation is disabled by default and only applies in explicitly enabled shared rooms. Delegation task cards are visible room messages; bot-authored ordinary output remains inert, peer-bot trust is configured separately from human allow-lists, and claimed work is injected as a bounded delegated-task prompt with completion/failure reported back to the room. For a concrete two-agent workflow, see `docs/agent-collaboration-playbooks.md`.
293	
294	## Prompt routing behavior
295	
296	### When Pi is idle
297	
298	A normal authorized message is delivered as a standard Pi prompt. For Slack channel/thread bindings, the sender must be the paired user, the current active selection, or must explicitly address the local machine bot depending on shared-room mode.
299	
300	Expected feedback:
301	
302	- Telegram: bot chat action such as `typing...`
303	- Discord: typing activity where supported
304	- Slack: `:thinking_face:` reaction, or ephemeral fallback if reactions are unavailable
305	
306	### When Pi is busy
307	
308	Prompts use the configured busy delivery mode. Default is `followUp`.
309	
310	Explicit controls:
311	
312	- Telegram: `/steer <text>` or `/followup <text>`
313	- Discord: `relay steer <text>` or `relay followup <text>`
314	- Slack: `relay steer <text>` or `relay followup <text>`
315	
316	## Guided answer flow
317	
318	PiRelay supports structured answering when the latest completed assistant output contains a reliable choice set or question set.
319	
320	Examples:
321	
322	```text
323	Choose:
324	1. sync specs now
325	2. archive without syncing
326	```
327	
328	Telegram can show inline options where available. All messengers can use short unambiguous replies or `answer` where supported by the command parser. Long or ambiguous messages are treated as normal prompts unless PiRelay can safely identify them as answers.
329	
330	Use `cancel` to leave an active answer flow.
331	
332	## Multi-session behavior
333	
334	PiRelay can track multiple live Pi sessions through a local broker. Pair sessions with labels when useful:
335	
336	```text
337	/relay connect telegram docs
338	/relay connect discord api
339	/relay connect slack release
340	```
341	
342	Use `/sessions` in Telegram or `relay sessions` in Discord/Slack to list targets. Use `/use` or `relay use` to select an active target. Use `/to` or `relay to` for one-shot prompts without switching sessions. Older offline pairings from the same machine/workspace are treated as superseded when a newer online session exists; use `/sessions all` or `relay sessions all` when you need to inspect or clean up those hidden stale entries, then run the messenger-appropriate forget command from the command table above.
343	
344	If the same bot/app is configured on multiple machines, use one ingress owner plus broker federation so other machines register routes instead of polling the same messenger concurrently.
345	
346	## Configuration
347	
348	Canonical config lives at:
349	
350	```text
351	~/.pi/agent/pirelay/config.json
352	```
353	
354	Example:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "relay": {
359	    "machineId": "laptop",
360	    "stateDir": "~/.pi/agent/pirelay",
361	    "brokerGroup": "personal"
362	  },
363	  "defaults": {
364	    "pairingExpiryMs": 300000,
365	    "busyDeliveryMode": "followUp"
366	  },
367	  "messengers": {
368	    "telegram": {
369	      "default": {
370	        "enabled": true,
371	        "tokenEnv": "PI_RELAY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN"
372	      }
373	    },
374	    "discord": {
375	      "default": {
376	        "enabled": true,
377	        "tokenEnv": "PI_RELAY_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN",
378	        "applicationId": "[REDACTED:discord-client-id]"
379	      }
380	    },
381	    "slack": {
382	      "default": {
383	        "enabled": true,
384	        "tokenEnv": "PI_RELAY_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN",
385	        "signingSecretEnv": "PI_RELAY_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET",
386	        "appTokenEnv": "PI_RELAY_SLACK_APP_TOKEN",
387	        "appId": "A0123456789",
388	        "workspaceId": "T0123456789"
389	      }
390	    }
391	  }
392	}
393	```
394	
395	Recommended permissions:
396	
397	```bash
398	chmod 600 ~/.pi/agent/pirelay/config.json
399	```
400	
401	Legacy Telegram tunnel config/state under `~/.pi/agent/telegram-tunnel` and `PI_TELEGRAM_TUNNEL_*` env vars are migration fallbacks only. Active non-secret bindings migrate to `telegram:default`; active pairing codes are not copied.
402	
403	For more detail, see [docs/config.md](docs/config.md).
404	
405	## Security notes
406	
407	Please treat PiRelay as a convenience/control channel, not a secret-safe transport.
408	
409	Important points:
410	
411	- Telegram Bot API traffic is not end-to-end encrypted
412	- Discord and Slack app/bot traffic follows their platform security model
413	- bot tokens and app secrets must stay in env vars or local config, never in session history
414	- pairing links/PINs are single-use and expire quickly
415	- allow-lists and local trust should be configured before broad remote control
416	- Slack/Discord channel control is disabled unless explicitly enabled
417	- redaction patterns can scrub common secret shapes before remote text/document delivery
418	- image files can contain visual secrets; PiRelay requires explicit image actions before sending latest image outputs/files remotely
419	
420	## Troubleshooting
421	
422	### Setup wizard cannot write config
423	
424	Use `c` to copy env snippets, export real values in your shell/profile, restart Pi or reload the environment, then run setup again and press `w`. Invalid boolean env values such as `sometimes` are rejected instead of silently skipped.
425	
426	### Telegram does not respond
427	
428	- run `/relay setup telegram`
429	- verify `PI_RELAY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` or `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`
430	- confirm the bot exists and the username resolves in Telegram
431	
432	### Discord does not receive messages
433	
434	- run `/relay setup discord`
435	- verify the bot token and application id
436	- enable Message Content Intent for DM text prompts
437	- ensure the bot and user can share a DM path, often by sharing a server
438	
439	### Slack says sending messages to the app is turned off
440	
441	- enable App Home → Messages Tab → Allow users to send messages to your app
442	- add the `message.im` event
443	- add `im:history`, `im:read`, `reactions:write`, and `files:write` scopes
444	- reinstall the Slack app after changing settings
445	
446	### Slack still shows `Pi is working…` instead of a reaction
447	
448	The Slack bot token likely lacks `reactions:write`/`files:write` or the app was not reinstalled after adding scopes. Add the needed scope, reinstall, then restart/reload PiRelay.
449	
450	### Pairing expired or points to the wrong session
451	
452	Run `/relay connect <messenger>` again from the Pi session you want to control. Pairing commands are single-use and scoped to the selected messenger/session.
453	
454	### `pi --continue` and pairing
455	
456	If you continue the same Pi session and PiRelay uses the same state directory, you usually do not need to pair again. Run the remote status command to verify. Reconnect only if the session key changed, state was deleted, or the binding was disconnected/revoked.
457	
458	### You changed code but behavior looks stale
459	
460	Restart the running Pi session/extension process. PiRelay normally supervises one local broker per `{stateDir, bot token hash, brokerNamespace}` scope and same-scope Pi sessions reconnect/register routes with that broker. If you are testing broker startup changes and need a hard reset, stop the detached broker before retesting:
461	
462	```bash
463	pkill -f 'extensions/relay/broker/process.js'
464	```
465	
466	Then restart Pi or reload the package from the updated checkout.
467	
468	### A running Pi session appears offline in `/sessions`
469	
470	PiRelay tracks binding authority, broker transport, and broker route synchronization separately. A live Pi process and active binding do not by themselves prove that remote routing is online. Broker clients reconcile their complete live route map after connection and periodically, so a missing in-memory route should repair automatically within about 30 seconds. Local `/relay status` reports `Broker transport` and `Broker route` separately; `/relay doctor` can request the same safe idempotent repair for a proven live route. If recovery remains pending, temporarily enable communication diagnostics and inspect metadata-only `broker.connect`, `broker.reconcile`, and `broker.retry` events without sharing tokens, destinations, socket paths, or route payloads.
471	
472	`/relay restart` replaces the broker shared by all same-scope local Pi sessions. Clients reconnect autonomously, and the command reports recovered client/route counts. A partial timeout leaves recovered sessions available while missing clients continue bounded retries; run `/relay doctor` in a missing live session rather than re-pairing it.
473	
474	### `/sessions` shows stale or offline duplicates
475	
476	When a newer online session exists for the same machine/workspace, PiRelay hides older offline same-workspace pairings from the default session list. Use `/sessions all` (or `relay sessions all` on Discord/Slack) to reveal hidden stale entries for diagnostics and cleanup, then run the appropriate forget command for your messenger to remove an offline pairing. PiRelay does not delete transcript files or automatically revoke live bindings when it hides superseded entries.
477	
478	## Architecture overview
479	
480	PiRelay consists of:
481	
482	- a Pi extension at `extensions/relay/`
483	- a companion skill at `skills/relay/`
484	- adapter runtimes for Telegram, Discord, and Slack
485	- a local broker process for multi-session routing
486	- persisted local state under `~/.pi/agent/pirelay/`
487	
488	The extension listens to Pi lifecycle events, tracks task state, publishes route updates, and injects authorized messenger input back into the session. Adapter modules own platform-specific I/O while shared core helpers own routing, authorization, formatting, media safety, redaction, progress, and setup metadata.
489	
490	## Development
491	
492	```bash
493	npm install
494	npm run typecheck
495	npm test
496	```
497	
498	OpenSpec validation for active changes:
499	
500	```bash
501	openspec validate <change> --strict
502	```
503	
504	Manual smoke-test steps and release notes live in:
505	
506	- [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)
507	- [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md)
508	
509	## Current limitations
510	
511	- native Slack typing bubbles are not available through supported Slack Web API / Socket Mode, so PiRelay uses reactions plus ephemeral fallback
512	- Slack/Discord file upload delivery is still limited compared with Telegram text/image support
513	- Telegram group-chat support is not the default runtime mode
514	- no end-to-end encryption beyond each messenger platform's bot/app transport
515	- answer workflow depends on conservative structured-output detection
516	- image prompts require a Pi model that supports image input
517	- image transfer is bounded by configured size and MIME-type limits; GIF source and converted first-frame PNG output are both checked
518	- `/images` only considers captured image outputs and obvious image file paths mentioned in the latest Pi turn
519	
520	## Related files
521	
522	- adapter/runtime details: [docs/adapters.md](docs/adapters.md)
523	- configuration reference: [docs/config.md](docs/config.md)
524	- manual testing checklist: [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md)
525	- Pi skill entrypoint: [skills/relay/SKILL.md](skills/relay/SKILL.md)
526

273	          || input.requester.userId !== binding.userId)) continue;
274	        const targetKey = channelBindingStorageKey(binding.channel, input.newSessionKey, binding.instanceId);
275	        const target = data.channelBindings[targetKey];
276	        if (target && (target.channel !== binding.channel
277	          || (target.instanceId ?? "default") !== (binding.instanceId ?? "default")
278	          || target.conversationId !== binding.conversationId
279	          || target.userId !== binding.userId)) continue;
280	        const moved: ChannelPersistedBindingRecord = {
281	          ...binding,
282	          sessionKey: input.newSessionKey,
283	          sessionId: input.newSessionId,
284	          sessionFile: input.newSessionFile,
285	          sessionLabel: input.newSessionLabel,
286	          lastSeenAt: now,
287	          status: "active",
288	          revokedAt: undefined,
289	          movedAt: undefined,
290	          movedToSessionKey: undefined,
291	        };
292	        data.channelBindings[key] = { ...binding, status: "revoked", revokedAt: now, movedAt: now, movedToSessionKey: input.newSessionKey };
293	        data.channelBindings[targetKey] = moved;
294	        result.channels.push(moved);
295	        movedAddresses.set(channelSelectionStorageKey(binding.channel, binding.conversationId, binding.userId), { channel: binding.channel, conversationId: binding.conversationId, userId: binding.userId });
296	      }
297	
298	      for (const [key, address] of movedAddresses) {
299	        const selection = data.activeChannelSelections[key];
300	        if (selection && selection.sessionKey !== input.oldSessionKey && selection.sessionKey !== input.newSessionKey) continue;
301	        data.activeChannelSelections[key] = { ...selection, ...address, sessionKey: input.newSessionKey, updatedAt: now };
302	        result.movedSelections += 1;
303	      }
304	    });
305	    return result;
306	  }

498	  async tryUpsertDelegationTask(task: DelegationTaskRecord, options: { maxAuditEntries?: number } = {}): Promise<{ applied: boolean; task: DelegationTaskRecord; reason?: "conflict" }> {
499	    const maxAuditEntries = Math.max(1, options.maxAuditEntries ?? 200);
500	    let result: { applied: boolean; task: DelegationTaskRecord; reason?: "conflict" } = { applied: true, task };
501	    await this.update((data) => {
502	      const current = data.delegationTasks[task.id];
503	      if (current && !delegationTaskIncludesAudit(task, current)) {
504	        result = { applied: false, task: current, reason: "conflict" };
505	        return;
506	      }
507	      saveDelegationTask(data, task, maxAuditEntries);
508	      result = { applied: true, task };
509	    });
510	    return result;
511	  }

513	  async getDelegationTask(taskId: string, options: { runningTimeoutMs?: number; now?: string } = {}): Promise<DelegationTaskRecord | undefined> {
514	    let task: DelegationTaskRecord | undefined;
515	    await this.update((data) => {
516	      const current = data.delegationTasks[taskId];
517	      if (!current) return;
518	      const next = normalizeDelegationTaskForRead(current, options);
519	      if (next !== current) {
520	        saveDelegationTask(data, next, 200);
521	      }
522	      task = next;
523	    });
524	    return task;
525	  }

527	  async listDelegationTasks(options: { room?: DelegationTaskRoomRef; roomConversationId?: string; sourceMachineId?: string; targetMachineId?: string; limit?: number; runningTimeoutMs?: number; now?: string } = {}): Promise<DelegationTaskRecord[]> {
528	    const limit = Math.max(1, options.limit ?? 50);
529	    const data = await this.update((draft) => {
530	      for (const [taskId, current] of Object.entries(draft.delegationTasks)) {
531	        const next = normalizeDelegationTaskForRead(current, options);
532	        if (next === current) continue;
533	        saveDelegationTask(draft, next, 200);
534	      }
535	    });
536	    return Object.values(data.delegationTasks)
537	      .filter((task) => !options.room || delegationRoomMatches(task.room, options.room))
538	      .filter((task) => !options.roomConversationId || task.room.conversationId === options.roomConversationId)
539	      .filter((task) => !options.sourceMachineId || task.sourceMachineId === options.sourceMachineId)
540	      .filter((task) => !options.targetMachineId || task.target.kind === "machine" && task.target.machineId === options.targetMachineId)
541	      .sort((left, right) => Date.parse(right.updatedAt) - Date.parse(left.updatedAt) || right.id.localeCompare(left.id))
542	      .slice(0, limit);
543	  }

671	  async recordLifecycleNotification(input: {
672	    channel: ChannelBinding["channel"];
673	    instanceId?: string;
674	    sessionKey: string;
675	    conversationId: string;
676	    userId: string;
677	    kind: RelayLifecycleEventKind;

679	    debounceMs?: number;
680	  }): Promise<RelayLifecycleNotificationDecision> {
681	    let decision: RelayLifecycleNotificationDecision | undefined;
682	    await this.update((data) => {
683	      const key = relayLifecycleStorageKey(input);
684	      const previous = data.lifecycleNotifications[key];
685	      decision = decideRelayLifecycleNotification({ ...input, previous });
686	      if (decision.shouldNotify && input.kind === "online") return;
687	      data.lifecycleNotifications[key] = {
688	        ...decision.record,
689	        lastNotifiedAt: previous?.lastNotifiedAt,
690	        lastEvent: previous?.lastEvent,
691	      };
692	    });
693	    return decision!;
694	  }

723	function activeTargetTelegramBindingConflicts(data: TunnelStoreData, input: SessionBindingMigrationInput, source: PersistedBindingRecord): boolean {
724	  const target = data.bindings[input.newSessionKey];
725	  return Boolean(target && (target.chatId !== source.chatId || target.userId !== source.userId));

728	function isMissingFileError(error: unknown): boolean {
729	  return typeof error === "object" && error !== null && "code" in error && (error as { code?: unknown }).code === "ENOENT";
730	}
731	
732	function lifecycleStateForNotification(kind: RelayLifecycleEventKind): "online" | "offline" | "disconnected" {
733	  if (kind === "online" || kind === "moved") return "online";
734	  if (kind === "offline") return "offline";
735	  return "disconnected";
736	}
737	
738	function normalizePinLikeCode(value: string): string | undefined {
739	  const digits = value.replace(/[^0-9]/g, "");
740	  return digits.length === 6 ? `${digits.slice(0, 3)}-${digits.slice(3)}` : undefined;
741	}
742	
743	function pendingPairingLookupKeys(code: string): string[] {
744	  const keys = [sha256(code.trim())];
745	  const normalizedPin = normalizePinLikeCode(code);
746	  if (normalizedPin && normalizedPin !== code.trim()) keys.push(sha256(normalizedPin));
747	  return keys;
748	}
749	
750	function findPendingPairingEntryByCode(data: TunnelStoreData, code: string): { key: string; pairing: PendingPairingRecord } | undefined {
751	  for (const key of pendingPairingLookupKeys(code)) {
752	    const pairing = data.pendingPairings[key];

216	export function inferApprovalCategory(toolName: string, input: unknown, summary = rawSearchText(input)): ApprovalRiskCategory {

221	  if (/\b(npm\s+publish|pnpm\s+publish|yarn\s+npm\s+publish|twine\s+upload|docker\s+push|cargo\s+publish)\b/.test(command)) return "publish";
222	  if (/\b(rm\s+-[^\n]*r|rm\s+-rf|sudo\b|chmod\s+777|chown\b|mkfs\b|dd\s+if=|killall\b|pkill\b)\b/.test(command)) return "destructive";
223	  return "shell";

235	export function parseApprovalTextCommand(command: string, args: string): { decision: ApprovalDecisionKind; approvalId: string } | undefined {
236	  if (command !== "approval" && command !== "approve") return undefined;
237	  const parts = args.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
238	  const verb = command === "approve" ? "approve" : parts.shift();
239	  const approvalId = parts.shift();
240	  if (!verb || !approvalId) return undefined;
241	  const decision = verb === "approve" ? "approve-once"
242	    : verb === "approve-session" || verb === "session" ? "approve-session"
243	    : verb === "approve-persistent" || verb === "persistent" ? "approve-persistent"
244	    : verb === "deny" ? "deny"
245	    : undefined;
246	  return decision ? { decision, approvalId } : undefined;
247	}

249	export function parseApprovalActionData(value: string): { decision: ApprovalDecisionKind; approvalId: string } | undefined {

251	  if (parts.length === 3 && parts[0] === COMPACT_ACTION_PREFIX) {
252	    const decision = APPROVAL_DECISION_BY_CODE[parts[1] ?? ""];
253	    const approvalId = parts[2]?.trim();
254	    return decision && approvalId ? { decision, approvalId } : undefined;
255	  }
256	  if (parts.length !== 4 || parts[0] !== "pirelay" || parts[1] !== "approval") return undefined;
257	  const decision = parts[2];

259	  const approvalId = parts[3]?.trim();

358	function ruleMatches(rule: ApprovalGateRule, input: { toolName: string; category: ApprovalRiskCategory; searchable: string; pathText: string; commandText: string }): boolean {
359	  const tools = [...(rule.tools ?? []), ...(rule.toolNames ?? [])].map((tool) => tool.toLowerCase());
360	  if (tools.length > 0 && !tools.includes(input.toolName.toLowerCase())) return false;
361	  if (rule.categories && rule.categories.length > 0 && !rule.categories.includes(input.category)) return false;
362	  const hasPatternConstraints = hasConfiguredPatterns(rule.commandPatterns) || hasConfiguredPatterns(rule.pathPatterns) || hasConfiguredPatterns(rule.textPatterns);
363	  const patternMatched = patternsMatch(rule.commandPatterns, input.commandText)
364	    || patternsMatch(rule.pathPatterns, input.pathText)
365	    || patternsMatch(rule.textPatterns, input.searchable);
366	  if (hasPatternConstraints) return patternMatched;
367	  return tools.length > 0 || Boolean(rule.categories && rule.categories.length > 0);
368	}

374	function patternsMatch(patterns: string[] | undefined, text: string): boolean {
375	  if (!patterns || patterns.length === 0) return false;
376	  return patterns.some((pattern) => {
377	    const normalized = pattern.trim().toLowerCase();
378	    if (!normalized) return false;
379	    if (normalized.startsWith("/") && normalized.endsWith("/") && normalized.length > 2) {
380	      try {
381	        return new RegExp(normalized.slice(1, -1), "i").test(text);
382	      } catch (error) {
383	        throw new Error(`Invalid approval pattern ${pattern}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);
384	      }
385	    }
386	    return text.includes(normalized);
387	  });
388	}
