326	// scanPiSession reads a pi session .jsonl file and extracts the session ID,
327	// a summary (first user message), and a message count.
328	func scanPiSession(path string) (sessionID, summary string, msgCount int) {
329		f, err := os.Open(path)
330		if err != nil {
331			return "", "", 0
332		}
333		defer f.Close()
334	
335		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(f)
336		scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), 1*1024*1024)
337	
338		for scanner.Scan() {
339			var entry map[string]any
340			if err := json.Unmarshal(scanner.Bytes(), &entry); err != nil {
341				continue
342			}
343			switch entry["type"] {
344			case "session":
345				if id, ok := entry["id"].(string); ok {
346					sessionID = id
347				}
348			case "message":
349				msg, _ := entry["message"].(map[string]any)
350				if msg == nil {
351					continue
352				}
353				role, _ := msg["role"].(string)
354				if role == "user" || role == "assistant" {
355					msgCount++
356				}
357				// Use first user message as summary.
358				if role == "user" && summary == "" {
359					content, _ := msg["content"].([]any)
360					for _, c := range content {
361						item, _ := c.(map[string]any)
362						if item != nil {
363							if text, ok := item["text"].(string); ok && text != "" {
364								summary = text
365								runes := []rune(summary)
366								if len(runes) > 80 {
367									summary = string(runes[:80]) + "..."
368								}
369								break
370							}
371						}
372					}
373				}
374			}
375		}
376		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
377			slog.Warn("pi: scan session error", "path", path, "error", err)
378		}
379		return
380	}

```text
1	# pi-gateway
2	
3	[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
4	[![Bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/Runtime-Bun-black?logo=bun)](https://bun.sh)
5	[![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Dwsy/pi-gateway?style=social)](https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway)
6	
7	The multi-channel AI gateway for pi coding agent. Connect your AI assistant to Telegram, Discord, Feishu, and WebChat with a single configuration.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Why pi-gateway?
12	
13	Direct use of OpenClaw requires managing RPC processes, message routing, and channel integrations yourself. pi-gateway handles all the infrastructure so you can focus on building intelligent agents.
14	
15	```
16	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
17	|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
18	|  Without         |     |  With            |     |  Your Benefit    |
19	|  pi-gateway      |     |  pi-gateway      |     |                  |
20	|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
21	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
22	| Manage RPC       |     |                  |     | Focus on agent   |
23	| processes        |     |  Automatic       |     | logic, not       |
24	|                  |     |  RPC Pool        |     | infrastructure   |
25	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
26	| Build message    |     |                  |     | Zero boilerplate |
27	| routing          |     |  Session Router  |     | for multi-user   |
28	|                  |     |                  |     | scenarios        |
29	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
30	| Handle channel   |     |                  |     | One config for   |
31	| differences      |     |  Unified API     |     | all platforms    |
32	|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
33	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
34	| Implement        |     |                  |     | Seamless pi      |
35	| from scratch     |     |  Plugin System   |     | skills support   |
36	|                  |     |                  |     |                  |
37	+------------------+     +------------------+     +------------------+
38	```
39	
40	### Key Differentiator: Seamless pi Skills
41	
42	pi-gateway is designed for pi users. All pi skills work out of the box:
43	
44	```
45	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
46	|                 |       |                 |       |                 |
47	|  pi skills      |       |  pi-gateway     |       |  Result         |
48	|                 |       |                 |       |                 |
49	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
50	| send_message    |  -->  | Auto-route to   |  -->  | Message sent    |
51	| send_media      |       | active channel  |       | to Telegram/    |
52	| session_status  |       |                 |       | Discord/WebChat |
53	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
54	| cron            |  -->  | Isolated        |  -->  | Scheduled       |
55	|                 |       | execution       |       | tasks work      |
56	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
57	| message         |  -->  | Channel-aware   |  -->  | Reactions,      |
58	|                 |       | adapters        |       | edits, pins     |
59	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
60	| All pi skills   |  -->  | Transparent     |  -->  | Works anywhere  |
61	|                 |       | integration     |       | pi runs         |
62	+-----------------+       +-----------------+       +-----------------+
63	```
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Architecture
68	
69	```
70	+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
71	|                           pi-gateway                                    |
72	|                                                                         |
73	|  Telegram ----+                                                         |
74	|               |     +------------+     +-------------+     +-------+    |
75	|  Discord ------+--> |  Plugin    | --> |  Session    | --> |  RPC  |    |
76	|               |     |  System    |     |  Router     |     |  Pool |    |
77	|  Feishu ------+     +------------+     +-------------+     +-------+    |
78	|               |           |                  |                |        |
79	|  WebChat -----+      Hooks/Tools       Message Queue    pi --mode rpc  |
80	|                           |                  |                |        |
81	|                     +-----+-----+            |           +----+----+   |
82	|                     |           |            |           |         |   |
83	|                  Auth       Transform    Backpressure   JSON     stdin  |
84	|                                          Handling       Lines    stdout |
85	|                                                                         |
86	+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
87	                                    |
88	                                    v
89	                            +--------------+
90	                            |              |
91	                            |  pi agent    |
92	                            |  + skills    |
93	                            |              |
94	                            +--------------+
95	```
96	
97	| Component | Purpose |
98	|-----------|---------|
99	| Plugin System | 14 hooks, 8 registration APIs. Extend without modifying core. |
100	| Session Router | Route to isolated agent instances: `agent:{id}:{channel}:{chat}` |
101	| Message Queue | Serialize per-session messages, prevent interleaving |
102	| RPC Pool | Manage subprocess pool with crash recovery and auto-scaling |
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Features
107	
108	**Multi-Channel**: Telegram, Discord, Feishu (Lark), WebChat
109	
110	**RPC Pool**: Isolated subprocess per session with configurable min/max/idle
111	
112	**Session Isolation**: Deterministic routing for per-user/group contexts
113	
114	**Message Queue**: Priority queue with backpressure handling
115	
116	**Model Failover**: Automatic fallback chain with exponential backoff
117	
118	**Cron Engine**: Scheduled tasks with isolated execution context
119	
120	**Security**: DM policies (pairing/allowlist/open/disabled), SSRF guard
121	
122	**Plugin Architecture**: Hot-reloadable plugins with full lifecycle management
123	
124	---
125	
126	## Quick Start
127	
128	```bash
129	# Clone and install
130	git clone https://github.com/Dwsy/pi-gateway.git
131	cd pi-gateway
132	bun install
133	
134	# Configure
135	cp pi-gateway.jsonc.example pi-gateway.jsonc
136	export TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="your-bot-token"
137	
138	# Start
139	bun run start
140	
141	# Open http://localhost:52134
142	```
143	
144	---
145	
146	## Configuration
147	
148	Minimal setup:
149	
150	```jsonc
151	{
152	  "gateway": { "port": 52134 },
153	  "agent": { "model": "claude-sonnet-4" },
154	  "channels": {
155	    "telegram": {
156	      "enabled": true,
157	      "botToken": "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"
158	    }
159	  }
160	}
161	```
162	
163	Key settings:
164	
165	| Section | Purpose | Required |
166	|---------|---------|----------|
167	| `gateway.port` | HTTP/WS listen port | No (default: 52134) |
168	| `agent.model` | LLM model for agent | Yes |
169	| `agent.pool` | RPC pool size (min/max) | No |
170	| `channels.*.botToken` | Platform bot token | If channel enabled |
171	
172	---
173	
174	## Plugin System
175	
176	```typescript
177	export default function myPlugin(api: GatewayPluginApi) {
178	  // Hook into agent lifecycle
179	  api.registerHook(["agent_end"], async (ctx) => {
180	    console.log(`Session ${ctx.sessionKey} completed`);
181	  });
182	
183	  // Add HTTP endpoint
184	  api.registerHttpRoute("GET", "/health", async (req, res) => {
185	    res.json({ status: "ok" });
186	  });
187	
188	  // Register slash command
189	  api.registerCommand("ping", async (ctx) => {
190	    await ctx.reply("Pong!");
191	  });
192	}
193	```
194	
195	Available hooks:
196	
197	| Hook | When |
198	|------|------|
199	| `before_agent_start` | Before agent starts |
200	| `agent_end` | After agent finishes |
201	| `message_received` | Message from channel |
202	| `message_sending` | Before sending (mutable) |
203	| `message_sent` | After sending |
204	| `before_tool_call` | Before tool execution |
205	| `after_tool_call` | After tool execution |
206	| `session_start` / `session_end` | Session lifecycle |
207	| `gateway_start` / `gateway_stop` | Gateway lifecycle |
208	
209	---
210	
211	## CLI Commands
212	
213	```bash
214	pi-gw gateway [--port N] [--verbose]   # Start gateway
215	pi-gw doctor                            # Health check
216	pi-gw send --to <target> --message <m>  # Send message
217	pi-gw config show                       # Show config
218	pi-gw onboard                           # Interactive setup
219	```
220	
221	Send command targets:
222	
223	```
224	telegram:<chatId>                           # DM
225	telegram:<accountId>:<chatId>               # Specific account
226	telegram:<accountId>:<chatId>:topic:<tid>   # Topic in group
227	discord:<channelId>                         # Discord channel
228	```
229	
230	---
231	
232	## Security
233	
234	| Policy | Behavior |
235	|--------|----------|
236	| `pairing` | Unknown sender gets 8-char code, admin approves |
237	| `allowlist` | Only configured user IDs can interact |
238	| `open` | Anyone can interact |
239	| `disabled` | Block all DMs |
240	
241	```bash
242	# Approve pairing request
243	pi-gw pairing approve telegram ABCD1234
244	```

263

266	- LLM provider (API key or OAuth via `pi /login`)

269	
270	## Common Issues
271	
272	**Cannot connect to Telegram**
273	
274	```bash
275	# Verify bot token
276	curl https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getMe
277	
278	# Check environment variable
279	echo $TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
280	```
281	
282	**RPC pool exhausted**
283	
284	```jsonc
285	{ "agent": { "pool": { "min": 2, "max": 8 } } }
286	```
287	
288	**Model rate limited**
289	
290	```jsonc
291	{
292	  "agent": {
293	    "modelFailover": {
294	      "primary": "claude-sonnet-4",
295	      "fallbacks": ["gpt-4o", "gemini-pro"]
296	    }
297	  }
298	}
299	```

469	        clearTimeout(timeout);

475	  private handleLine(line: string): void {

485	        this.pendingRequests.delete(data.id);
486	        clearTimeout(pending.timeout);
487	
488	        if (!data.success) {
489	          pending.reject(new Error(data.error ?? `RPC error for ${data.command}`));
490	        } else {

492	        }
493	        return;
494	      }

496	      // Auto-handle extension UI requests (headless mode)

499	      if (data.type === "extension_ui_request") {

502	      }
503	
504	      // Agent event
505	      for (const listener of this.eventListeners) {
506	        try {
507	          listener(data as AgentEvent);
508	        } catch (err) {
509	          this.log.error("Event listener error:", err);
510	        }
511	      }
512	    } catch {
513	      // Non-JSON line (e.g. pi startup output) — ignore
514	    }
515	  }

517	  /**

519	   *
520	   * pi extensions can emit these when they need user interaction:

522	   *   confirm  -> yes/no (auto: confirm)
523	   *   input    -> text input (auto: cancel)
524	   *   editor   -> text editor (auto: cancel)
525	   *   notify   -> notification (no response needed, but we ack anyway)
526	   *   setStatus/setWidget/setTitle/set_editor_text -> UI updates (no response needed)
527	   */
528	  private handleExtensionUIRequest(data: Record<string, unknown>): void {
529	    const id = data.id as string;
530	    const method = data.method as string;
531	
532	    if (!id || !method) return;
533	
534	    // Try external handler first (WS forwarding to WebChat frontend)
535	    if (this.extensionUIHandler && this.proc) {
536	      const writeToRpc = (msg: string) => { this.proc?.stdin.write(msg + "\n"); };
537	      if (this.extensionUIHandler(data, writeToRpc)) return;
538	    }
539	
540	    // Fallback: auto-respond in headless mode
541	    let response: Record<string, unknown> | null = null;

543	    switch (method) {
544	      case "select": {
545	        // Auto-select first option if available, otherwise cancel
546	        const options = data.options as string[] | undefined;
547	        if (options && options.length > 0) {
548	          response = { type: "extension_ui_response", id, value: options[0] };
549	          this.log.debug(`Extension UI auto-select: "${options[0]}" (from ${options.length} options)`);
550	        } else {
551	          response = { type: "extension_ui_response", id, cancelled: true };
552	          this.log.debug("Extension UI auto-cancel select (no options)");
553	        }
554	        break;
555	      }
556	      case "confirm":
557	        // Auto-confirm
558	        response = { type: "extension_ui_response", id, confirmed: true };
559	        this.log.debug(`Extension UI auto-confirm: "${data.title}"`);
560	        break;
561	      case "input":
562	        // Cancel text input (can't type in headless mode)
563	        response = { type: "extension_ui_response", id, cancelled: true };
564	        this.log.debug(`Extension UI auto-cancel input: "${data.title}"`);
565	        break;
566	      case "editor":
567	        // Cancel editor (can't edit in headless mode)
568	        response = { type: "extension_ui_response", id, cancelled: true };

570	        break;
571	      case "notify":
572	      case "setStatus":
573	      case "setWidget":
574	      case "setTitle":

601	      this.log.warn(`stdin write failed (process ${this.id} likely crashed): ${err}`);
602	      return false;
603	    }
604	  }
605	
606	  private startReadLoop(): void {
607	    if (!this.proc) return;
608	
609	    const decoder = new TextDecoder();
610	    let buffer = "";
611	    const stdout = this.proc.stdout;
612	
613	    this.readLoop = (async () => {
614	      const reader = (stdout as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>).getReader();
615	      try {
616	        while (true) {
617	          const { done, value } = await reader.read();
618	          if (done) break;
619	
620	          buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
621	          const lines = buffer.split("\n");
622	          buffer = lines.pop() ?? "";
623	
624	          for (const line of lines) {
625	            this.handleLine(line);
626	          }
627	        }
628	      } catch {
629	        // Stream closed
630	      }
631	
632	      if (buffer.trim()) {
633	        this.handleLine(buffer);
634	      }
635	    })();
636	  }
637	
638	  private collectStderr(): void {
639	    if (!this.proc) return;
640	
641	    const stderr = this.proc.stderr;
642	    (async () => {
643	      const reader = (stderr as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>).getReader();
644	      const decoder = new TextDecoder();
645	      try {
646	        while (true) {
647	          const { done, value } = await reader.read();
648	          if (done) break;
649	          this.stderr += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
650	          if (this.stderr.length > 10_000) {
651	            this.stderr = this.stderr.slice(-5_000);
652	          }
653	        }
654	      } catch {
655	        // Stream closed
656	      }
657	    })();
658	  }
659	}

1	/**
2	 * RPC Event type helpers — typed access to AgentEvent / RpcWireEvent fields.
3	 *
4	 * The upstream AgentEvent (from pi-agent-core) is a discriminated union
5	 * covering agent-loop events. RPC wire also emits session-level events
6	 * (auto_retry, auto_compaction, extension_error, before_agent_start)
7	 * defined as RpcSessionEvent in types.ts.
8	 *
9	 * This module provides:
10	 * 1. Narrowed Extract types for each AgentEvent variant
11	 * 2. Re-exports of RpcSessionEvent interfaces for direct use
12	 * 3. Helper functions for safe field extraction across camelCase/snake_case
13	 */
14	
15	import type { AgentEvent, AssistantMessageEvent, AgentMessage } from "./types.ts";
16	
17	// Re-export session-level event types for direct import
18	export type {
19	  RpcWireEvent,
20	  RpcSessionEvent,
21	  RpcAutoRetryStartEvent,
22	  RpcAutoRetryEndEvent,
23	  RpcAutoCompactionStartEvent,
24	  RpcAutoCompactionEndEvent,
25	  RpcBeforeAgentStartEvent,
26	  RpcExtensionErrorEvent,
27	} from "./types.ts";
28	
29	// ── Narrowed AgentEvent types (extract from the discriminated union) ────
30	
31	// Agent lifecycle
32	export type AgentStartEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "agent_start" }>;
33	export type AgentEndEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "agent_end" }>;
34	
35	// Turn lifecycle
36	export type TurnStartEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "turn_start" }>;
37	export type TurnEndEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "turn_end" }>;
38	
39	// Message lifecycle
40	export type MessageStartEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "message_start" }>;
41	export type MessageUpdateEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "message_update" }>;
42	export type MessageEndEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "message_end" }>;
43	
44	// Tool execution
45	export type ToolExecutionStartEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "tool_execution_start" }>;
46	export type ToolExecutionUpdateEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "tool_execution_update" }>;
47	export type ToolExecutionEndEvent = Extract<AgentEvent, { type: "tool_execution_end" }>;
48	
49	// ── Snake-case fallback for RPC transport ───────────────────────────────
50	
51	/** RPC-transported event may carry snake_case `assistant_message_event` */
52	interface SnakeCaseFallback {
53	  assistant_message_event?: AssistantMessageEvent;
54	}
55	
56	/**
57	 * Extract AssistantMessageEvent from a message_update event.
58	 * Handles both camelCase (native) and snake_case (RPC transport) keys.
59	 */
60	export function getAssistantMessageEvent(event: MessageUpdateEvent): AssistantMessageEvent | undefined {
61	  return event.assistantMessageEvent ?? (event as unknown as SnakeCaseFallback).assistant_message_event;
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Safely extract the `partial` field from an AssistantMessageEvent.
66	 * Not all AME variants carry `partial` (e.g., `done`, `error`).
67	 */
68	export function getAmePartial(ame: AssistantMessageEvent | undefined): unknown {
69	  if (!ame) return undefined;
70	  return "partial" in ame ? ame.partial : undefined;
71	}
72	
73	// ── Type guard for session-level events ─────────────────────────────────
74	
75	const SESSION_EVENT_TYPES = new Set([
76	  "auto_retry_start", "auto_retry_end",
77	  "auto_compaction_start", "auto_compaction_end",
78	  "before_agent_start", "extension_error",
79	]);
80	
81	/** Check if a wire event is a session-level event (not in AgentEvent). */
82	export function isSessionEvent(event: { type: string }): boolean {
83	  return SESSION_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.type);

1	/**
2	 * Extension UI Forwarder
3	 *
4	 * Manages forwarding extension_ui_request from RPC agents to WebChat WS clients,
5	 * and routing responses back to the agent's stdin.
6	 *
7	 * Replaces the auto-cancel behavior in rpc-client.ts when WebChat clients are connected.
8	 */
9	
10	import type { ServerWebSocket } from "bun";
11	import type {
12	  ExtensionUIRequest,
13	  ExtensionUIResponse,
14	  ExtensionUIDismissed,
15	  PendingUIRequest,
16	  ExtensionUIMethod,
17	  SelectOption,
18	} from "./extension-ui-types.ts";
19	import { createLogger } from "./types.ts";
20	
21	const DEFAULT_TTL_MS = 60_000;
22	
23	export class ExtensionUIForwarder {
24	  /** Pending requests awaiting frontend response */
25	  private pending = new Map<string, PendingUIRequest>();
26	  private log = createLogger("extension-ui");
27	
28	  /**
29	   * Forward an extension_ui_request to all connected WS clients.
30	   * Returns a Promise that resolves when a client responds or TTL expires.
31	   */
32	  forward(
33	    data: Record<string, unknown>,
34	    wsClients: Map<string, ServerWebSocket<any>>,
35	    writeToRpc: (response: string) => void,
36	  ): boolean {
37	    const id = data.id as string;
38	    const method = data.method as string;
39	    if (!id || !method) return false;
40	
41	    // No WS clients connected — fall back to auto-cancel
42	    if (wsClients.size === 0) return false;
43	
44	    const request: ExtensionUIRequest = this.normalizeRequest(data);
45	
46	    const entry: PendingUIRequest = {
47	      id,
48	      request,
49	      resolved: false,
50	      createdAt: Date.now(),
51	      ttlTimer: setTimeout(() => {
52	        this.handleTimeout(id, writeToRpc);
53	      }, request.ttlMs),
54	      respond: (response: ExtensionUIResponse) => {
55	        writeToRpc(JSON.stringify({
56	          type: "extension_ui_response",
57	          id,
58	          value: response.value,
59	          confirmed: response.confirmed,
60	          cancelled: response.cancelled,
61	        }));
62	      },
63	      onTimeout: () => {
64	        writeToRpc(JSON.stringify({
65	          type: "extension_ui_response",
66	          id,
67	          cancelled: true,
68	        }));
69	      },
70	    };
71	
72	    this.pending.set(id, entry);
73	
74	    // Broadcast to all WS clients (first-win)
75	    const frame = JSON.stringify({
76	      type: "event",
77	      event: "extension_ui_request",
78	      payload: request,
79	    });
80	    for (const ws of wsClients.values()) {
81	      try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
82	    }
83	
84	    this.log.debug(`Forwarded extension_ui_request ${id} (${method}) to ${wsClients.size} client(s)`);
85	    return true;
86	  }
87	
88	  /**
89	   * Handle a response from a WS client.
90	   * First response wins; late responses are ignored + dismissed.
91	   */
92	  handleResponse(
93	    response: ExtensionUIResponse,
94	    wsClients: Map<string, ServerWebSocket<any>>,
95	    respondingClientId: string,
96	  ): boolean {
97	    const entry = this.pending.get(response.id);
98	    if (!entry) return false;
99	
100	    if (entry.resolved) {
101	      // Already resolved — send dismissed to this late client
102	      this.log.debug(`Late response for ${response.id} from ${respondingClientId}, ignoring`);
103	      return false;
104	    }
105	
106	    // First win — resolve
107	    entry.resolved = true;
108	    clearTimeout(entry.ttlTimer);
109	    entry.respond(response);
110	    this.pending.delete(response.id);
111	
112	    // Notify other clients that this prompt is dismissed
113	    const dismissed: ExtensionUIDismissed = {
114	      type: "extension_ui_dismissed",
115	      id: response.id,
116	    };
117	    const frame = JSON.stringify({ type: "event", event: "extension_ui_dismissed", payload: dismissed });
118	    for (const [clientId, ws] of wsClients) {
119	      if (clientId !== respondingClientId) {
120	        try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
121	      }
122	    }
123	
124	    this.log.debug(`Resolved extension_ui_request ${response.id} via ${respondingClientId}`);
125	    return true;
126	  }
127	
128	  /**
129	   * Re-send pending requests to a newly connected client (reconnect recovery).
130	   * Only re-sends requests with remaining TTL > 10s.
131	   */
132	  resendPending(ws: ServerWebSocket<any>): void {
133	    const now = Date.now();
134	    for (const entry of this.pending.values()) {
135	      if (entry.resolved) continue;
136	      const elapsed = now - entry.createdAt;
137	      const remaining = entry.request.ttlMs - elapsed;
138	      if (remaining <= 10_000) continue;
139	
140	      const frame = JSON.stringify({
141	        type: "event",
142	        event: "extension_ui_request",
143	        payload: { ...entry.request, ttlMs: remaining },
144	      });
145	      try { ws.send(frame); } catch {}
146	    }
147	  }
148	
149	  /** Cancel all pending requests (gateway shutdown). */
150	  cancelAll(writeToRpc: (response: string) => void): void {
151	    for (const entry of this.pending.values()) {
152	      if (!entry.resolved) {
153	        clearTimeout(entry.ttlTimer);
154	        entry.onTimeout();
155	      }
156	    }
157	    this.pending.clear();
158	  }
159	
160	  get pendingCount(): number {
161	    return this.pending.size;
162	  }
163	
164	  // ==========================================================================
165	  // Internal
166	  // ==========================================================================
167	
168	  private handleTimeout(id: string, writeToRpc: (response: string) => void): void {
169	    const entry = this.pending.get(id);
170	    if (!entry || entry.resolved) return;
171	
172	    entry.resolved = true;
173	    entry.onTimeout();
174	    this.pending.delete(id);
175	    this.log.debug(`Extension UI request ${id} timed out (${entry.request.ttlMs}ms)`);
176	  }
177	
178	  private normalizeRequest(data: Record<string, unknown>): ExtensionUIRequest {
179	    const method = data.method as ExtensionUIMethod;
180	    const base = {
181	      type: "extension_ui_request" as const,
182	      id: data.id as string,
183	      method,
184	      title: data.title as string | undefined,
185	      ttlMs: (data.ttlMs as number) ?? DEFAULT_TTL_MS,
186	    };
187	
188	    switch (method) {
189	      case "select":
190	      case "multiselect":
191	        return {
192	          ...base,
193	          method,
194	          options: this.normalizeOptions(data.options),
195	          initialValue: data.initialValue as string | undefined,
196	          initialValues: data.initialValues as string[] | undefined,
197	        };
198	      case "text":
199	      case "editor":
200	        return {
201	          ...base,
202	          method,
203	          placeholder: data.placeholder as string | undefined,
204	          defaultValue: data.defaultValue as string | undefined,
205	        };
206	      case "confirm":
207	        return {
208	          ...base,
209	          method,
210	          message: data.message as string | undefined,
211	          initialValue: data.initialValue as boolean | undefined,
212	        };
213	      case "progress":
214	        return {
215	          ...base,
216	          method,
217	          current: data.current as number | undefined,
218	          total: data.total as number | undefined,
219	          label: data.label as string | undefined,
220	        };
221	      default:
222	        return { ...base, method: "confirm", message: `Unknown method: ${method}` };
223	    }
224	  }
225	
226	  /** Normalize options: accept string[] or {value,label,hint?}[] */
227	  private normalizeOptions(raw: unknown): SelectOption[] {
228	    if (!Array.isArray(raw)) return [];
229	    return raw.map((item) => {
230	      if (typeof item === "string") return { value: item, label: item };
231	      if (item && typeof item === "object" && "value" in item) {
232	        return {
233	          value: String(item.value),
234	          label: String(item.label ?? item.value),
235	          hint: item.hint ? String(item.hint) : undefined,
236	        };
237	      }
238	      return { value: String(item), label: String(item) };
239	    });
240	  }

1	/**
2	 * Per-session message queue — ensures serial processing per session.
3	 *
4	 * Aligned with OpenClaw's serial execution model and pi-mom's ChannelQueue:
5	 * - Messages for the same session are processed one at a time
6	 * - Different sessions can process concurrently
7	 * - Queue size is capped to prevent unbounded growth
8	 * - Priority-based ordering within each session queue
9	 */
10	
11	import { createLogger, type Logger, type SessionKey, type MessageSource, type ImageContent } from "./types.ts";
12	import type { MetricsCollector } from "./metrics.ts";
13	
14	// ============================================================================
15	// Types
16	// ============================================================================
17	
18	export type QueuedWork = () => Promise<void>;
19	
20	/** Prioritized work item with metadata for collect merge and drop summarization. */
21	export interface PrioritizedWork {
22	  work: QueuedWork;
23	  /** Numeric priority — higher = more urgent. DM=10, group=5, webhook=3, allowlist=+2 */
24	  priority: number;
25	  /** Enqueue timestamp for TTL and ordering */
26	  enqueuedAt: number;
27	  /** TTL in ms. 0 = no expiry */
28	  ttl: number;
29	  /** Original message source for collect grouping */
30	  source?: MessageSource;
31	  /** Original text for collect merge prompt */
32	  text?: string;
33	  /** Human-readable summary for drop policy. Fallback: text.slice(0, 140) */
34	  summaryLine?: string;
35	  /** Images attached to this message (for collect mode image concat) */
36	  images?: ImageContent[];
37	  /**
38	   * When set by collect mode, processMessage should use this text instead of msg.text.
39	   * Mutated by SessionQueue.drain() before calling work().
40	   */
41	  collectMergedText?: string;
42	  /**
43	   * Optional: called before merged work executes in collect mode.
44	   * Used by dispatch layer to trigger setTyping on first item, concat images, etc.
45	   */
46	  onBeforeCollectWork?: (batch: PrioritizedWork[]) => Promise<void>;
47	}
48	
49	export interface QueueStats {
50	  sessions: number;
51	  totalPending: number;
52	  dropCount: number;
53	  details: Array<{ sessionKey: SessionKey; pending: number; processing: boolean }>;
54	}
55	
56	// ============================================================================
57	// Session Queue (single session)
58	// ============================================================================
59	
60	/** Callback when an item is evicted due to queue full + lower priority. */
61	export type EvictionCallback = (item: PrioritizedWork) => void;
62	
63	/** Callback to execute a merged batch of items. */
64	export type CollectExecutor = (batch: PrioritizedWork[], mergedPrompt: string) => Promise<void>;
65	
66	/** Queue mode configuration. */
67	export interface QueueModeConfig {
68	  /** Queue processing mode. "collect" merges messages, "individual" processes one by one. */
69	  mode: "collect" | "individual";
70	  /** Debounce window in ms for collect mode. Default: 1500 */
71	  collectDebounceMs: number;
72	  /** Max dropped summaries to include in collect prompt overflow section. */
73	  maxDroppedSummaries: number;
74	}
75	
76	const DEFAULT_QUEUE_MODE: QueueModeConfig = {
77	  mode: "collect",
78	  collectDebounceMs: 1500,
79	  maxDroppedSummaries: 5,
80	};
81	
82	class SessionQueue {
83	  private queue: PrioritizedWork[] = [];
84	  private processing = false;
85	  private collectTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
86	  private droppedSummaries: string[] = [];
87	  private log: Logger;
88	  private onEvicted?: EvictionCallback;
89	  private modeConfig: QueueModeConfig;
90	  /** Metrics: total collect merges for this session. */
91	  collectMergeCount = 0;
92	
93	  constructor(
94	    readonly sessionKey: SessionKey,
95	    private maxSize: number,
96	    log: Logger,
97	    onEvicted?: EvictionCallback,
98	    modeConfig?: Partial<QueueModeConfig>,
99	  ) {
100	    this.log = log;
101	    this.onEvicted = onEvicted;
102	    this.modeConfig = { ...DEFAULT_QUEUE_MODE, ...modeConfig };
103	  }
104	
105	  get pending(): number {
106	    return this.queue.length;
107	  }
108	
109	  get isProcessing(): boolean {
110	    return this.processing;
111	  }
112	
113	  get isEmpty(): boolean {
114	    return this.queue.length === 0 && !this.processing;
115	  }
116	
117	  /** Get the lowest priority item in the queue (for global eviction). */
118	  get lowestPriorityItem(): PrioritizedWork | null {
119	    if (this.queue.length === 0) return null;
120	    return this.queue.reduce((min, x) => x.priority < min.priority ? x : min);
121	  }
122	
123	  /**
124	   * Clear all pending items, cancel collect debounce timer, and reset dropped summaries.
125	   * Used by interrupt mode to discard queued messages before redispatching.
126	   * Returns the number of items cleared.
127	   */
128	  clearCollectBuffer(): number {
129	    const cleared = this.queue.length;
130	    if (this.collectTimer) {
131	      clearTimeout(this.collectTimer);
132	      this.collectTimer = null;
133	    }
134	    this.queue.length = 0;
135	    this.droppedSummaries = [];
136	    if (cleared > 0) {
137	      this.log.info(`Cleared collect buffer for ${this.sessionKey}: ${cleared} items discarded`);
138	    }
139	    return cleared;
140	  }
141	
142	  enqueue(item: PrioritizedWork): boolean {
143	    if (this.queue.length >= this.maxSize) {
144	      // Evict lowest priority item if new item has higher priority
145	      const lowest = this.lowestPriorityItem;
146	      if (lowest && item.priority > lowest.priority) {
147	        this.queue.splice(this.queue.indexOf(lowest), 1);
148	        this.log.debug(`Evicted priority=${lowest.priority} item from ${this.sessionKey} for priority=${item.priority}`);
149	        this.recordDroppedSummary(lowest);
150	        this.onEvicted?.(lowest);
151	      } else {
152	        this.log.warn(`Queue full for ${this.sessionKey} (max ${this.maxSize}), dropping message`);
153	        return false;
154	      }
155	    }
156	    // Insert sorted by priority desc, FIFO within same priority
157	    const idx = this.queue.findIndex(x => x.priority < item.priority);
158	    this.queue.splice(idx === -1 ? this.queue.length : idx, 0, item);
159	    this.scheduleProcess();
160	    return true;
161	  }
162	
163	  /** Remove a specific item (for global eviction). */
164	  evict(item: PrioritizedWork): boolean {
165	    const idx = this.queue.indexOf(item);
166	    if (idx === -1) return false;
167	    this.queue.splice(idx, 1);
168	    this.onEvicted?.(item);
169	    return true;
170	  }
171	
172	  // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
173	  // Processing
174	  // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	
176	  private scheduleProcess(): void {
177	    // Don't schedule if already processing — new items will be picked up by the while loop
178	    if (this.processing) return;
179	
180	    if (this.modeConfig.mode === "individual") {
181	      // Individual mode: process immediately, no debounce
182	      void this.drain();
183	      return;
184	    }
185	
186	    // Collect mode: reset debounce timer on each new message
187	    if (this.collectTimer) clearTimeout(this.collectTimer);
188	    this.collectTimer = setTimeout(() => {
189	      this.collectTimer = null;
190	      void this.drain();
191	    }, this.modeConfig.collectDebounceMs);
192	  }
193	
194	  /**
195	   * Async while loop drain — processes batches until queue is empty
196	   * AND all dropped summaries have been flushed.
197	   * Not recursive to avoid stack overflow under high-frequency enqueue.
198	   *
199	   * Design note: collect debounce (1500ms) is handled here at the queue layer.
200	   * Channel plugins (e.g. Telegram) should set their own debounce to 0 to avoid
201	   * double-debouncing. The queue is the single source of truth for message coalescing.
202	   */
203	  private async drain(): Promise<void> {
204	    if (this.processing) return;
205	    this.processing = true;
206	
207	    try {
208	      // Also drain if there are pending dropped summaries (OpenClaw: droppedCount > 0)
209	      while (this.queue.length > 0 || this.droppedSummaries.length > 0) {
210	        const batch = this.queue.splice(0, this.queue.length);
211	
212	        if (batch.length === 0 && this.droppedSummaries.length > 0) {
213	          // No items but have dropped summaries — generate summary-only prompt
214	          // This can happen when all items were evicted but summaries remain
215	          this.log.info(`Flushing ${this.droppedSummaries.length} dropped summaries for ${this.sessionKey}`);
216	          this.droppedSummaries = []; // Clear to exit loop
217	          break;
218	        }
219	
220	        if (batch.length === 1 || this.modeConfig.mode === "individual") {
221	          // Single item or individual mode: process each separately
222	          for (const item of batch) {
223	            try {
224	              await item.work();
225	            } catch (err) {
226	              this.log.error(`Queue error for ${this.sessionKey}:`, err);
227	            }
228	          }
229	        } else {
230	          // Collect mode: merge batch into single prompt
231	          this.collectMergeCount++;
232	          const mergedPrompt = this.buildCollectPrompt(batch);
233	          this.log.info(`Collect merged ${batch.length} messages for ${this.sessionKey}`);
234	
235	          // Set merged text on the last item. The work closure captures this item
236	          // by reference, so processMessage will see collectMergedText.
237	          // Safe from races: processing=true prevents concurrent drain,
238	          // and finally ensures cleanup even on exception.
239	          const lastItem = batch[batch.length - 1];
240	          lastItem.collectMergedText = mergedPrompt;
241	          try {
242	            if (lastItem.onBeforeCollectWork) {
243	              await lastItem.onBeforeCollectWork(batch);
244	            }
245	            await lastItem.work();
246	          } catch (err) {
247	            this.log.error(`Queue collect error for ${this.sessionKey}:`, err);
248	          } finally {
249	            lastItem.collectMergedText = undefined;
250	          }
251	        }
252	        // Loop continues if new items arrived during execution
253	      }
254	    } finally {
255	      this.processing = false;
256	    }
257	  }
258	
259	  /**
260	   * Build a merged prompt from multiple queued messages.
261	   * Format aligned with OpenClaw buildCollectPrompt().
262	   */
263	  buildCollectPrompt(items: PrioritizedWork[]): string {
264	    const lines: string[] = ["[Queued messages while agent was busy]", ""];
265	
266	    for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i++) {
267	      lines.push("---");
268	      const imgTag = items[i].images?.length ? " (with image)" : "";
269	      lines.push(`Queued #${i + 1}${imgTag}`);
270	      lines.push(items[i].text ?? "(no text)");
271	      lines.push("");
272	    }
273	
274	    // Append overflow section for dropped messages
275	    if (this.droppedSummaries.length > 0) {
276	      lines.push("---");
277	      lines.push("[Dropped messages (summarized)]");
278	      const summaries = this.droppedSummaries.slice(-this.modeConfig.maxDroppedSummaries);
279	      const overflow = this.droppedSummaries.length - summaries.length;
280	      for (const s of summaries) {
281	        lines.push(s);
282	      }
283	      if (overflow > 0) {
284	        lines.push(`(and ${overflow} more dropped)`);
285	      }
286	      // Clear after including in prompt
287	      this.droppedSummaries = [];
288	    }
289	
290	    return lines.join("\n");
291	  }
292	
293	  /** Record a dropped message summary for inclusion in next collect prompt. */
294	  private recordDroppedSummary(item: PrioritizedWork): void {
295	    const summary = item.summaryLine ?? (item.text ?? "").slice(0, 140);
296	    const ellipsis = !item.summaryLine && (item.text?.length ?? 0) > 140 ? "..." : "";
297	    this.droppedSummaries.push(`[Dropped] ${summary}${ellipsis}`);
298	  }
299	}
300	
301	// ============================================================================
302	// Message Queue Manager (all sessions)
303	// ============================================================================
304	
305	export class MessageQueueManager {
306	  private queues = new Map<SessionKey, SessionQueue>();
307	  private log: Logger;
308	  private maxQueueSize: number;
309	  private globalMaxPending: number;
310	  private modeConfig: Partial<QueueModeConfig>;
311	  private _dropCount = 0;
312	  /** Sliding window for enqueue rate (timestamps of recent enqueues) */
313	  private enqueueTimestamps: number[] = [];
314	  private readonly RATE_WINDOW_MS = 10_000; // 10s sliding window
315	
316	  constructor(
317	    maxQueueSize = 15,
318	    modeConfig?: Partial<QueueModeConfig>,
319	    private metrics?: MetricsCollector,
320	    globalMaxPending = 100,
321	  ) {
322	    this.log = createLogger("queue");
323	    this.maxQueueSize = maxQueueSize;
324	    this.globalMaxPending = globalMaxPending;
325	    this.modeConfig = modeConfig ?? {};
326	  }
327	
328	  /**
329	   * Enqueue prioritized work for a session. Returns false if the queue is full.
330	   */
331	  enqueue(sessionKey: SessionKey, item: PrioritizedWork): boolean;
332	  /**
333	   * Enqueue work for a session (backward compat). Returns false if the queue is full.
334	   * Wraps into PrioritizedWork with default priority=5.
335	   */
336	  enqueue(sessionKey: SessionKey, work: QueuedWork): boolean;
337	  enqueue(sessionKey: SessionKey, itemOrWork: PrioritizedWork | QueuedWork): boolean {
338	    const item: PrioritizedWork = typeof itemOrWork === "function"
339	      ? { work: itemOrWork, priority: 5, enqueuedAt: Date.now(), ttl: 0 }
340	      : itemOrWork;
341	
342	    // Global pending cap: check total across all sessions
343	    if (this.getTotalPending() >= this.globalMaxPending) {
344	      const evicted = this.evictGlobalLowestPriority(item.priority);
345	      if (!evicted) {
346	        this._dropCount++;
347	        this.metrics?.incQueueDrop();
348	        this.log.warn(`Global pending cap reached (${this.globalMaxPending}), dropping priority=${item.priority} message`);
349	        return false;
350	      }
351	    }
352	
353	    let queue = this.queues.get(sessionKey);
354	    if (!queue) {
355	      queue = new SessionQueue(sessionKey, this.maxQueueSize, this.log, (evicted) => {
356	        this._dropCount++;
357	        this.metrics?.incQueueDrop();
358	        this.log.info(`Evicted item from ${sessionKey} (priority=${evicted.priority}, summary="${evicted.summaryLine ?? evicted.text?.slice(0, 50) ?? "?"}")`);
359	      }, this.modeConfig);
360	      this.queues.set(sessionKey, queue);
361	    }
362	    const ok = queue.enqueue(item);
363	    if (ok) {
364	      this.enqueueTimestamps.push(Date.now());
365	    } else {
366	      this._dropCount++;
367	      this.metrics?.incQueueDrop();
368	    }
369	    return ok;
370	  }
371	
372	  /**
373	   * Enqueue rate: messages/sec over the last 10s sliding window.
374	   */
375	  private getEnqueueRate(): number {
376	    const now = Date.now();
377	    const cutoff = now - this.RATE_WINDOW_MS;
378	    // Trim old entries
379	    while (this.enqueueTimestamps.length > 0 && this.enqueueTimestamps[0] < cutoff) {
380	      this.enqueueTimestamps.shift();
381	    }
382	    return this.enqueueTimestamps.length / (this.RATE_WINDOW_MS / 1000);
383	  }
384	
385	  /**
386	   * Get total pending items across all sessions.
387	   */
388	  private getTotalPending(): number {
389	    let total = 0;
390	    for (const queue of this.queues.values()) {
391	      total += queue.pending;
392	    }
393	    return total;
394	  }
395	
396	  /**
397	   * Find and evict the lowest priority item across all sessions.
398	   * Returns true if an item was evicted, false if all items have >= priority.
399	   */
400	  private evictGlobalLowestPriority(incomingPriority: number): boolean {
401	    let lowestQueue: SessionQueue | null = null;
402	    let lowestItem: PrioritizedWork | null = null;
403	
404	    for (const queue of this.queues.values()) {
405	      const candidate = queue.lowestPriorityItem;
406	      if (candidate && (!lowestItem || candidate.priority < lowestItem.priority)) {
407	        lowestItem = candidate;
408	        lowestQueue = queue;
409	      }
410	    }
411	
412	    if (!lowestQueue || !lowestItem || lowestItem.priority >= incomingPriority) {
413	      return false;
414	    }
415	
416	    return lowestQueue.evict(lowestItem);
417	  }
418	
419	  /**
420	   * Get queue stats for monitoring.
421	   */
422	  getStats(): QueueStats & { collectMergeCount: number; enqueueRate: number } {
423	    const details: QueueStats["details"] = [];
424	    let totalPending = 0;
425	    let collectMergeCount = 0;
426	
427	    for (const [key, queue] of this.queues) {
428	      details.push({
429	        sessionKey: key,
430	        pending: queue.pending,
431	        processing: queue.isProcessing,
432	      });
433	      totalPending += queue.pending;
434	      collectMergeCount += queue.collectMergeCount;
435	    }
436	
437	    return {
438	      sessions: this.queues.size,
439	      totalPending,
440	      dropCount: this._dropCount,
441	      collectMergeCount,
442	      enqueueRate: this.getEnqueueRate(),
443	      details,
444	    };
445	  }
446	
447	  /**
448	   * Clean up empty queues.
449	   */
450	  cleanup(): void {
451	    for (const [key, queue] of this.queues) {
452	      if (queue.isEmpty) {
453	        this.queues.delete(key);
454	      }
455	    }
456	  }
457	
458	  /**
459	   * Clear collect buffer for a specific session (interrupt mode).
460	   * Discards all pending items, cancels debounce timer, resets dropped summaries.
461	   * Returns the number of items cleared.
462	   */
463	  clearCollectBuffer(sessionKey: SessionKey): number {
464	    const queue = this.queues.get(sessionKey);
465	    if (!queue) return 0;
466	    return queue.clearCollectBuffer();
467	  }
468	}

```text
The authoritative definition in the **Message Structure** section is:

> “id of the channel the message was sent in”

For a message sent inside a thread, `channel_id` is the **thread’s ID**, because the thread is the channel where that message was sent—not the parent channel’s ID.

The parent channel appears separately in the thread starter’s `message_reference`; the **Thread starter messages** section says its `channel_id` points to the originating message in the parent channel.
```

```text
Yes. `ThreadChannel` is text-based: it inherits from `BaseChannel`, whose `isTextBased()` method identifies text-based channels.

Relevant documentation:

- `isTextBased()` — “Indicates whether this channel is text-based.”
- `send()` — “Sends a message to this channel.”
- `sendTyping()` — “Sends a typing indicator in the channel.”

It also exposes `messages`, a `GuildMessageManager` for messages sent in the thread.
```

```text
1	# pi-messenger-bridge
2	
3	Bridge common messengers (Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Matrix) into pi.
4	
5	Remote users can interact with your pi coding agent via their messenger app.
6	
7	<img width="887" height="656" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d42a41e5-e7d5-420b-be8e-f2191facb190" />
8	
9	https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd64360e-e8cd-4820-a67f-bd127c5d6035
10	
11	## Features
12	
13	- 📱 Multi-messenger support (Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, Matrix)
14	- 🔐 Challenge-based authentication (6-digit codes)
15	- 🎛️ Interactive menu (`/msg-bridge`) for setup and management
16	- 🔒 Single-instance guard — prevents duplicate bot polling with sub-agents
17	- 📊 Live status widget (toggleable)
18	- 💾 Persistent config (auth state, auto-connect, widget preference)
19	- 🔧 Tool call visibility for remote users
20	- 📝 Multi-turn conversation support
21	- 🔑 Secure permissions (chmod 600 for config files, 700 for directories)
22	
23	## Setup
24	
25	### 1. Install
26	
27	```bash
28	pi install npm:pi-messenger-bridge
29	```
30	
31	### 2. Configure Transports
32	
33	#### Telegram
34	
35	Create a bot via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) and get your token.
36	
37	```bash
38	/msg-bridge configure telegram <bot-token>
39	```
40	
41	Or set via environment variable:
42	```bash
43	export PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN="your-bot-token-here"
44	```
45	
46	#### WhatsApp
47	
48	Configure WhatsApp (requires QR code scan):
49	
50	```bash
51	/msg-bridge configure whatsapp
52	```
53	
54	Scan the QR code with your WhatsApp mobile app (**Linked Devices → Link a device**).
55	
56	> **Note:** After linking, **send a message to your own phone number** in WhatsApp to activate the bridge.
57	
58	Or set custom auth path:
59	```bash
60	export PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH="/path/to/whatsapp-auth"
61	```
62	
63	#### Slack
64	
65	Create a Slack app with Socket Mode enabled. You need both tokens:
66	
67	```bash
68	/msg-bridge configure slack <bot-token> <app-token>
69	```
70	
71	Or set via environment variables:
72	```bash
73	export PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="xoxb-..."
74	export PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN="xapp-..."
75	```
76	
77	#### Discord
78	
79	1. Create a new application in the [Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications)
80	2. Go to **Bot** → **Reset Token** → copy the token
81	3. Enable **Message Content Intent** (under Privileged Gateway Intents on the same page)
82	4. Go to **OAuth2 → URL Generator** → select scope `bot` → select permissions `Send Messages` and `Read Message History` → open the generated URL to invite the bot to your server
83	
84	```bash
85	/msg-bridge configure discord <bot-token>
86	```
87	
88	Or set via environment variable:
89	```bash
90	export PI_DISCORD_TOKEN="your-bot-token"
91	```
92	
93	#### Matrix
94	
95	Works with any Matrix homeserver — Element X, Element Web, FluffyChat, etc. The bot auto-joins rooms it's invited to.
96	
97	1. Register a bot account on your homeserver (or reuse an existing user)
98	2. Get an access token: log in once via Element and copy from **Settings → Help & About → Advanced**, or POST to `/_matrix/client/v3/login`
99	3. Note your homeserver URL (e.g. `https://matrix.org`)
100	
101	```bash
102	/msg-bridge configure matrix <homeserver-url> <access-token>
103	```
104	
105	Or set via environment variables:
106	```bash
107	export PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER="https://matrix.org"
108	export PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN="syt_..."
109	```
110	
111	E2EE is **on by default**. Verify the bot's device once from another Matrix client (Element, etc.) — until verified, encrypted rooms can't be decrypted in either direction.
112	
113	Set `"encryption": false` in the `matrix` config to disable — useful for non-encrypted rooms only, or to bypass crypto-store/server desync (e.g. `M_UNKNOWN: One time key … already exists`). **Caveat:** with E2EE off, the homeserver sees plaintext, and the bot can't participate in encrypted rooms at all.
114	
115	### 3. Connect
116	
117	```bash
118	/msg-bridge connect
119	```
120	
121	### 4. Authenticate Users
122	
123	When a user messages your bot for the first time, they'll receive a 6-digit challenge code.
124	The code is displayed in your pi terminal. Share it with the user (e.g., via DM).
125	
126	The user enters the code in the bot chat to become a trusted user.
127	
128	## Commands
129	
130	| Command | Description |
131	|---|---|
132	| `/msg-bridge` | Open interactive menu (configure, connect, widget, help) |
133	| `/msg-bridge status` | Show connection and user status |
134	| `/msg-bridge connect` | Connect to all configured transports |
135	| `/msg-bridge disconnect` | Disconnect all transports |
136	| `/msg-bridge configure <platform> [token]` | Set transport credentials via CLI |
137	| `/msg-bridge widget` | Toggle status widget on/off |
138	| `/msg-bridge toggletools` | Toggle tool call visibility in remote messages |
139	| `/msg-bridge help` | Show command reference |
140	
141	### Admin commands (in DM with the bot)
142	
143	Trusted users can DM the bot directly to manage state. Reply with `/help` for the full list:
144	
145	| Command | Description |
146	|---|---|
147	| `/help` | Show admin command reference |
148	| `/trusted` | List trusted users |
149	| `/revoke <userId>` | Revoke trust for a user |
150	| `/channels` | List enabled channels |
151	| `/enable <chatId> <all\|mentions\|trusted-only>` | Enable a channel |
152	| `/disable <chatId>` | Disable a channel |
153	| `/toggletools` | Toggle tool call visibility in replies |
154	
155	## Configuration
156	
157	Config is stored at `~/.pi/msg-bridge.json` with secure permissions (chmod 600).
158	
159	Example config:
160	```json
161	{
162	  "telegram": { "token": "..." },
163	  "whatsapp": { "authPath": "..." },
164	  "slack": { "botToken": "...", "appToken": "..." },
165	  "discord": { "token": "..." },
166	  "matrix": { "homeserverUrl": "https://matrix.org", "accessToken": "syt_...", "encryption": true },
167	  "auth": {
168	    "trustedUsers": ["telegram:123", "whatsapp:456"],
169	    "adminUserId": "telegram:789"
170	  },
171	  "autoConnect": true,
172	  "showWidget": true,
173	  "debug": false
174	}
175	```
176	
177	## Environment Variables
178	
179	Environment variables override file config:
180	
181	- `PI_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` — Telegram bot token
182	- `PI_WHATSAPP_AUTH_PATH` — WhatsApp session directory (default: `~/.pi/msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth`)
183	- `PI_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` — Slack bot token (xoxb-...)
184	- `PI_SLACK_APP_TOKEN` — Slack app token (xapp-...)
185	- `PI_DISCORD_TOKEN` — Discord bot token
186	- `PI_MATRIX_HOMESERVER` — Matrix homeserver URL (e.g. `https://matrix.org`)
187	- `PI_MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN` — Matrix access token
188	- `MSG_BRIDGE_DEBUG` — Enable debug logging (true/false)
189	
190	## Security
191	
192	- Config file: `~/.pi/msg-bridge.json` (chmod 600 - owner read/write only)
193	- Config directory: `~/.pi/` (chmod 700 - owner only)
194	- WhatsApp auth: `~/.pi/msg-bridge-whatsapp-auth/` (chmod 700 - owner only)
195	- Environment variables take precedence over config file
196	- Challenge-based authentication for all new users
197	- Transport-namespaced user IDs prevent impersonation
198	
199	## Troubleshooting
200	
201	Enable debug mode to see detailed logs:
202	
203	```json
204	{
205	  "debug": true
206	}
207	```
208	
209	Or:
210	```bash
211	export MSG_BRIDGE_DEBUG=true
212	```
213	
214	## Architecture
215	
216	Uses pi's native `sendUserMessage()` and `turn_end` events for two-way communication.
217	No tool-loop hacks needed — this is the pi-native way.
218	
219	Single-instance connection guard prevents duplicate polling when sub-agents spawn
220	(global flag + PID lock file at `~/.pi/msg-bridge.lock`).
221	
222	## Development
223	
224	```bash
225	npm install
226	npm run build        # compile TypeScript
227	npm run typecheck    # type-check without emitting
228	npm run test         # run tests
229	npm run lint         # biome lint
230	npm run lint:fix     # biome lint with auto-fix
231	```
232	
233	## License
234	
235	MIT
236
```

444	                await discordProvider.connect();
445	                context.ui.notify("✅ Discord configured and connected", "info");
446	              } catch (err) {
447	                releaseLock();

449	              }
450	            } else {
451	              context.ui.notify("✅ Discord configured (another instance is connected — run /msg-bridge connect later)", "info");
452	            }
453	            updateWidget();
454	            break;
455	          }
456	
457	          case "matrix": {
458	            const matrixParts = token.split(/\s+/);
459	            const homeserverUrl = matrixParts[0];
460	            const matrixAccessToken = matrixParts.slice(1).join(" ");
461	            if (!homeserverUrl || !matrixAccessToken) {
462	              context.ui.notify("Usage: /msg-bridge configure matrix <homeserver-url> <access-token>", "error");
463	              return;
464	            }
465	
466	            config.matrix = { homeserverUrl, accessToken: matrixAccessToken };
467	            saveConfig(config);
468	            const matrixProvider = new MatrixProvider(config.matrix, auth);
469	            transportManager.addTransport(matrixProvider);
470	            if (acquireLock()) {
471	              try {
472	                await matrixProvider.connect();
473	                context.ui.notify("✅ Matrix configured and connected", "info");
474	              } catch (err) {

480	            }

483	          }
484	
485	          default:
486	            context.ui.notify(`❌ Unknown platform: ${platform}`, "error");
487	        }
488	        break;
489	      }
490	
491	      case "widget": {
492	        const cfg2 = loadConfig();
493	        cfg2.showWidget = cfg2.showWidget === false;
494	        saveConfig(cfg2);
495	        const widgetState = cfg2.showWidget !== false ? "shown" : "hidden";
496	        context.ui.notify(`📊 Status widget ${widgetState}`, "info");
497	        updateWidget();
498	        break;
499	      }
500	
501	      case "status": {
502	        const stats = auth.getStats();
503	        const status = transportManager.getStatus();
504	        const lines = [

515	        if (stats.trustedUsers > 0) {

517	            if (userIds.length > 0) {

522	
523	        lines.push("");

525	        lines.push("━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━");
526	
527	        context.ui.notify(lines.join("\n"), "info");
528	        break;
529	      }
530	
531	      case "toggletools": {

541	        break;

1	import type { ExternalMessage } from "../types.js";
2	import type { ITransportProvider } from "./interface.js";
3	
4	/**
5	 * Manages multiple transport providers and routes messages
6	 */
7	export class TransportManager {
8	  private transports = new Map<string, ITransportProvider>();
9	  private messageHandler?: (message: ExternalMessage) => void;
10	  private errorHandler?: (error: Error, transport: string) => void;
11	
12	  /**
13	   * Register a transport provider
14	   */
15	  addTransport(transport: ITransportProvider): void {
16	    this.transports.set(transport.type, transport);
17	
18	    // Forward messages from this transport
19	    transport.onMessage((msg) => {
20	      if (this.messageHandler) {
21	        this.messageHandler(msg);
22	      }
23	    });
24	
25	    // Forward errors from this transport
26	    transport.onError((err) => {
27	      if (this.errorHandler) {
28	        this.errorHandler(err, transport.type);
29	      }
30	    });
31	  }
32	
33	  /**
34	   * Get a specific transport by type
35	   */
36	  getTransport(type: string): ITransportProvider | undefined {
37	    return this.transports.get(type);
38	  }
39	
40	  /**
41	   * Get all registered transports
42	   */
43	  getAllTransports(): ITransportProvider[] {
44	    return Array.from(this.transports.values());
45	  }
46	
47	  /**
48	   * Connect all registered transports
49	   */
50	  async connectAll(): Promise<void> {
51	    const connections = Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) =>
52	      t.connect().catch((err) => {
53	        throw new Error(`${t.type} connection failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
54	      })
55	    );
56	    await Promise.all(connections);
57	  }
58	
59	  /**
60	   * Disconnect all transports
61	   */
62	  async disconnectAll(): Promise<void> {
63	    const disconnections = Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) =>
64	      t.disconnect()
65	    );
66	    await Promise.allSettled(disconnections);
67	  }
68	
69	  /**
70	   * Send a message to a specific chat via a specific transport
71	   */
72	  async sendMessage(
73	    chatId: string,
74	    transportType: string,
75	    text: string
76	  ): Promise<void> {
77	    const transport = this.transports.get(transportType);
78	    if (!transport) {
79	      throw new Error(`Transport ${transportType} not found`);
80	    }
81	    if (!transport.isConnected) {
82	      throw new Error(`Transport ${transportType} not connected`);
83	    }
84	    await transport.sendMessage(chatId, text);
85	  }
86	
87	  /**
88	   * Send typing indicator to a chat via a specific transport
89	   */
90	  async sendTyping(chatId: string, transportType: string): Promise<void> {
91	    const transport = this.transports.get(transportType);
92	    if (transport?.isConnected) {
93	      await transport.sendTyping(chatId);
94	    }
95	  }
96	
97	  /**
98	   * Register handler for incoming messages from all transports
99	   */
100	  onMessage(handler: (message: ExternalMessage) => void): void {
101	    this.messageHandler = handler;
102	  }
103	
104	  /**
105	   * Register handler for errors from all transports
106	   */
107	  onError(handler: (error: Error, transport: string) => void): void {
108	    this.errorHandler = handler;
109	  }
110	
111	  /**
112	   * Get connection status for all transports
113	   */
114	  getStatus(): Array<{ type: string; connected: boolean }> {
115	    return Array.from(this.transports.values()).map((t) => ({
116	      type: t.type,
117	      connected: t.isConnected,
118	    }));
119	  }
120	}

```text
1	# pi-gateway
2	
3	Multi-platform chat bridge for pi — connect your AI agent to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. Real-time streaming, per-chat sessions, background tasks, and role-based access control.
4	
5	> Fork of [0xKobold/pi-gateway](https://github.com/0xKobold/pi-gateway) with config-based UID allowlisting.
6	
7	## Features
8	
9	- **Multi-platform adapters** — Discord, Telegram, Slack, Twitch, WhatsApp, WebSocket
10	- **Real-time streaming** — responses appear token-by-token via live message editing
11	- **Per-chat sessions** — isolated conversations with configurable reset policies (daily / idle)
12	- **Background tasks** — spawn async work from chats, results delivered when ready
13	- **Allowlist security** — DB-based and config-file pre-approved UIDs, admin roles, tool access policies
14	- **Detached daemon mode** — `/gateway start -d` or `pi-gateway start -d` keeps the gateway alive after pi closes
15	- **HTTP + WebSocket API** — connect external clients, send prompts, receive streaming responses
16	- **pi-native** — runs as a pi extension with `/gateway` slash commands and registered tools
17	
18	## Installation
19	
20	Install from npm (recommended):
21	
22	```bash
23	pi install npm:@gamalan/pi-gateway
24	```
25	
26	Or clone and build manually:
27	
28	```bash
29	git clone https://github.com/gamalan/pi-gateway.git
30	cd pi-gateway
31	npm install && npm run build
32	pi install .
33	```
34	
35	Requires pi coding agent (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent >= 0.80.3`) and `@sinclair/typebox >= 0.32.0`.
36	
37	## Quick Start
38	
39	```bash
40	# Start the gateway
41	/gateway start
42	
43	# Check status
44	/gateway status
45	
46	# Stop
47	/gateway stop
48	```
49	
50	The gateway starts on `http://localhost:3847` by default. See `/gateway config` for current settings. When detached mode is active, pi's footer shows `🟢 Gateway (daemon)` and automatically follows daemon start/stop changes.
51	
52	## Configuration
53	
54	Configuration lives at `~/.pi/gateway/config.json`:
55	
56	```jsonc
57	{
58	  "port": 3847,
59	  "host": "localhost",
60	  "tokens": [],                    // Bearer tokens for API auth (empty = allow all)
61	  "corsOrigins": ["*"],
62	  "enableWebSocket": true,
63	  "enableHttp": true,
64	  "security": {
65	    "allowAll": true,              // false = enforce allowlist
66	    "requirePairing": false,
67	    "allowedUids": {},             // pre-approved users (see Security)
68	    "adminUids": {},              // users with full access (see Admin Users)
69	    "rateLimit": {
70	      "maxRequests": 60,
71	      "windowMs": 60000
72	    }
73	  },
74	  "sessions": {
75	    "resetPolicy": "idle",         // "daily" | "idle" | "both"
76	    "dailyHour": 4,                // hour (0-23) for daily reset
77	    "idleMinutes": 1440            // minutes before idle reset
78	  },
79	  "platforms": {
80	    "discord": {
81	      "enabled": true,
82	      "botToken": "your-token",
83	      "guildId": "optional-guild-id"
84	    },
85	    "twitch": {
86	      "enabled": true,
87	      "clientId": "your-client-id",
88	      "clientSecret": "your-secret",
89	      "channels": ["channel-name"]
90	    },
91	    "telegram": {
92	      "enabled": true,
93	      "token": "your-bot-token",
94	      "webhookUrl": "https://..."  // omit for long polling
95	    },
96	    "slack": {
97	      "enabled": true,
98	      "webhookUrl": "https://...",
99	      "botToken": "optional-bot-token"
100	    },
101	    "whatsapp": {
102	      "enabled": true,
103	      "sessionPath": "~/.pi/whatsapp-session",
104	      "printQr": true
105	    }
106	  }
107	}
108	```
109	
110	When the gateway starts for the first time with no config file, it
111	automatically seeds `~/.pi/gateway/config.json` from the default
112	template shipped with the package.  You can also find it at
113	`node_modules/pi-gateway/config/config.default.json`.
114	
115	### Telegram: webhook vs long polling
116	
117	The gateway auto-detects the mode based on whether `webhookUrl` is set:
118	
119	| `webhookUrl` | Mode | How it works |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| Set | **Webhook** | Telegram POSTs updates to `/webhook/telegram` on the gateway's HTTP server. Lowest latency, requires a public URL. |
122	| Omitted | **Long polling** | The gateway opens a persistent connection to Telegram's `getUpdates` endpoint (30s timeout). Telegram holds it open and returns immediately when a message arrives — near-real-time, no public URL needed. |
123	
124	Both modes are real-time. Long polling is NOT interval-based — it keeps one connection alive at all times.
125	
126	## Security
127	
128	### Allowlist (DB)
129	
130	Manage users at runtime via `/gateway` commands:
131	
132	```bash
133	# List allowlisted users
134	/gateway allow
135	
136	# Add a user
137	/gateway allow discord 123456789
138	
139	# Revoke a user (via tool or directly)
140	```
141	
142	### Config-file pre-approved UIDs
143	
144	Skip pairing entirely by listing UIDs in the `security` block of `config.json`:
145	
146	```jsonc
147	{
148	  "security": {
149	    "allowAll": false,
150	    "allowedUids": {
151	      "discord": ["123456789", "987654321"],
152	      "telegram": ["1234567890"],
153	      "*": ["cross-platform-admin"]
154	    },
155	    "adminUids": {
156	      "discord": ["123456789"],
157	      "*": ["cross-platform-admin-uid"]
158	    },
159	    "rateLimit": {
160	      "maxRequests": 60,
161	      "windowMs": 60000
162	    }
163	  }
164	}
165	```
166	
167	- Platform-specific keys match that platform only
168	- The `"*"` wildcard matches any platform
169	- Users in this list are auto-allowed on first contact — no pairing code needed
170	- `adminUids` grants full unrestricted access (bypasses all tool policies)
171	- All security settings live in the main `config.json` — no separate security file
172	
173	### Admin Users
174	
175	Admin users have **full unrestricted access** — they bypass all tool policies and can use every tool pi offers (bash, write, edit, subagent, etc.).
176	
177	Admins can be set at runtime or via config's `security.adminUids` block:
178	
179	```jsonc
180	{
181	  "security": {
182	    "adminUids": {
183	      "discord": ["123456789"],
184	      "*": ["cross-platform-admin-uid"]
185	    }
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	```bash
191	# List all admins (DB + config)
192	/gateway admin list
193	
194	# Grant admin to a user on a specific platform
195	/gateway admin add discord 123456789
196	
197	# Grant admin on ALL platforms
198	/gateway admin add * 123456789
199	
200	# Revoke admin
201	/gateway admin remove discord 123456789
202	```
203	
204	Admin users are listed in the status panel and their messages carry a "FULL ACCESS" guard.
205	
206	### Tool Policy
207	
208	By default, external users are **restricted to read-only tools** when their messages reach pi: they can search code, inspect files, and ask questions, but cannot write files, execute shell commands, spawn subagents, or modify system state.
209	
210	The policy is enforced via a system directive prepended to every forwarded message. It is tunable per platform, per user, or globally.
211	
212	**Default allowed tools:** `read`, `web_search`, `fetch_content`, `fffind`, `ffgrep`, `module_report`, `read_symbol`, code search tools, `lsp_diagnostics`, `lsp_navigation`, `image_generate`, `gateway_*`
213	
214	**Default denied tools:** `bash`, `write`, `edit`, `subagent`, `todo`, `goal_complete`, `mcp`, `ast_grep_replace`, `agent_browser`, `wait`, `intercom`, `wiki_*`, `lens_diagnostics`
215	
216	#### Managing Policies
217	
218	```bash
219	# List all explicit policies
220	/gateway tool-policy list
221	
222	# See the default baseline
223	/gateway tool-policy defaults
224	
225	# Allow bash for a specific user
226	/gateway tool-policy set discord U123456 bash allow
227	
228	# Deny write for all users on Discord
229	/gateway tool-policy set discord * write deny
230	
231	# Allow everything for an admin user (glob)
232	/gateway tool-policy set * admin-uid * allow
233	
234	# Remove a policy by ID
235	/gateway tool-policy remove 3
236	
237	# Reset all custom policies to defaults
238	/gateway tool-policy reset
239	```
240	
241	Policies can also be managed from within pi sessions via the `gateway_tool_policy` tool.
242	
243	**Resolution order** (highest wins): user-specific > platform-specific > global. Ties break deny-first (secure by default). The `*` glob matches any tool name. Admin users always bypass all restrictions.
244	
245	> **Note:** All security configuration (allowlist, admin UIDs, rate limits)
246	> lives in the `security` block of `~/.pi/gateway/config.json`. There is
247	> no separate security config file. On first run, the gateway
248	> auto-seeds a complete default config so you don't have to write one
249	> from scratch.
250	
251	### Pairing Flow
252	
253	When `requirePairing` is enabled and a user is not in the allowlist:
254	
255	1. User sends a message → blocked, receives a pairing code
256	2. Admin approves with `/gateway pair <code>`
257	3. User is added to the DB allowlist
258	
259	## Commands
260	
261	| Command | Description |
262	|---------|-------------|
263	| `/gateway start [port]` | Start the gateway |
264	| `/gateway stop` | Stop the gateway |
265	| `/gateway restart` | Restart the gateway |
266	| `/gateway status` | Show running status, platforms, sessions |
267	| `/gateway pair [code]` | List pending codes or approve one |
268	| `/gateway allow [platform] [userId]` | List allowlist or add a user |
269	| `/gateway revoke <platform> <userId>` | Remove a user from the DB allowlist |
270	| `/gateway sessions` | List active chat sessions |
271	| `/gateway tasks` | List background tasks |
272	| `/gateway config` | Show current configuration |
273	| `/gateway admin list` | List admin users (DB + config) |
274	| `/gateway admin add <p\|*> <uid>` | Grant admin privileges |
275	| `/gateway admin remove <p\|*> <uid>` | Revoke admin |
276	| `/gateway admin list` | List admin users |
277	| `/gateway admin add <p\|*> <uid>` | Grant admin privileges |
278	| `/gateway admin remove <p\|*> <uid>` | Revoke admin |
279	| `/gateway tool-policy list` | List explicit tool policies |
280	| `/gateway tool-policy defaults` | Show default policy baseline |
281	| `/gateway tool-policy set <p> <u> <t> allow\|deny` | Add/update a tool policy |
282	| `/gateway tool-policy remove <id>` | Delete a policy |
283	| `/gateway tool-policy reset` | Clear all, back to defaults |
284	
285	## HTTP API
286	
287	Available when the gateway is running:
288	
289	| Endpoint | Method | Description |
290	|----------|--------|-------------|
291	| `/api/status` | GET | Gateway status (running, adapters, clients, sessions) |
292	| `/api/sessions` | GET | Active sessions |
293	| `/api/background` | GET | Background tasks |
294	| `/api/allowlist` | GET | Allowlisted users |
295	| `/api/pairing` | GET | Pending pairing codes |
296	
297	Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` if tokens are configured.
298	
299	## WebSocket API
300	
301	Connect to `ws://localhost:3847`. Messages are JSON:
302	
303	```jsonc
304	// Send a prompt
305	{ "type": "prompt", "data": { "message": "Hello" } }
306	
307	// Start a background task
308	{ "type": "background", "data": { "sessionId": "...", "command": "..." } }
309	
310	// Ping
311	{ "type": "ping" }
312	```
313	
314	Receive responses, background task updates, and agent events as server-pushed messages.
315	
316	## Registered Tools
317	
318	The extension registers these tools for use in pi sessions:
319	
320	- **`gateway_status`** — Check if gateway is running and which adapters are active
321	- **`gateway_sessions`** — List active chat sessions
322	- **`gateway_background_tasks`** — List and manage background tasks
323	- **`gateway_pairing`** — Generate or approve pairing codes
324	- **`gateway_tool_policy`** — Manage tool access policies for external users
325	
326	## Sessions
327	
328	Each chat gets an isolated session with configurable reset policies:
329	
330	- **daily** — Session resets at a specific hour each day (default: 4 AM)
331	- **idle** — Session resets after N minutes of inactivity
332	- **both** — Whichever triggers first
333	
334	Sessions persist across gateway restarts in `~/.pi/gateway/gateway-sessions.db`.
335	
336	## Background Tasks
337	
338	Long-running work is spawned in isolated background sessions. Results are delivered back to the parent chat when complete. Managed via `/gateway tasks`.
339	
340	## Architecture
341	
342	```
343	┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐
344	│  pi agent   │◄───►│        pi-gateway           │
345	│  (RPC)      │     │                             │
346	└─────────────┘     │  ┌─────────────────────┐    │
347	                    │  │ Platform Adapters    │    │
348	┌─────────────┐     │  │ Discord · Telegram   │    │
349	│ HTTP / WS   │────►│  │ Slack · Twitch       │    │
350	│ Clients     │     │  │ WhatsApp · WebSocket │    │
351	└─────────────┘     │  └─────────────────────┘    │
352	                    │                             │
353	                    │  ┌─────────────────────┐    │
354	                    │  │ Sessions Store      │    │
355	                    │  │ Background Manager  │    │
356	                    │  │ Security Layer      │    │
357	                    │  └─────────────────────┘    │
358	                    └─────────────────────────────┘
359	```
360	
361	- **Platform adapters** translate incoming platform messages into a unified format
362	- **Sessions store** (`SQLite`) persists per-chat state with reset policies
363	- **Background manager** spawns async child processes, delivers results via chat
364	- **Security layer** checks allowlists, manages pairing codes, and enforces rate limits
365	
366	## License
367	
368	MIT
369
```
</details></tool-use>

102	Discord 訊息入口先做 admission control，而不是收到訊息就直接交給模型：

104	```js
105	discordClient.on(Events.MessageCreate, async (message) => {
106	  if (!isAllowedGuildId(message.guildId)) return
107	  if (isSelfBotMessage && !isCliInjectedPrompt) return
108	
109	  const channelConfig = await getChannelDirectory(owningChannelId)
110	  if (!channelConfig) return
111	
112	  const member = await resolveGuildMessageMember(message)
113	  if (!hasKimakiBotPermission(member, message.guild)) return
114	
115	  // 通過檢查後才交給對應的 thread/session runtime。
116	})
117	```
118

133	const client = createOpencodeClient({
